books.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:1
verses.text: Homilies on the Acts of the Apostles: Homily I.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:2
verses.text: Acts I.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:3
verses.text: ,  "The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, concerning all things which Jesus began both to do and to teach, until the day on which, having given charge to the Apostles, whom He had chosen, by the Holy Spirit, He was taken up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:4
verses.text: To many persons this Book is so little known, both it and its author, that they are not even aware that there is such a book in existence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:5
verses.text: For this reason especially I have taken this narrative for my subject, that I may draw to it such as do not know it, and not let such a treasure as this remain hidden out of sight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:6
verses.text: For indeed it may profit us no less than even the Gospels; so replete is it with Christian wisdom and sound doctrine, especially in what is said concerning the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:7
verses.text: Then let us not hastily pass by it, but examine it closely.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:8
verses.text: Thus, the predictions which in the Gospels Christ utters, here we may see these actually come to pass; and note in the very facts the bright evidence of Truth which shines in them, and the mighty change which is taking place in the disciples now that the Spirit has come upon them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:9
verses.text: For example, they heard Christ say, "Whoso believeth on Me, the works that I do shall he do also, and greater works than these shall he do" (John xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:10
verses.text: ): and again, when He foretold to the disciples, that they should be brought before rulers and kings, and in their synagogues they should scourge them, and that they should suffer grievous things, and overcome all (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:11
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:12
verses.text: ): and that the Gospel should be preached in all the world (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:13
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:14
verses.text: ): now all this, how it came to pass exactly as it was said, may be seen in this Book, and more besides, which He told them while yet with them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:15
verses.text: Here again you will see the Apostles themselves, speeding their way as on wings over land and sea; and those same men, once so timorous and void of understanding, on the sudden become quite other than they were; men despising wealth, and raised above glory and passion and concupiscence, and in short all such affections: moreover, what unanimity there is among them now; nowhere any envying as there was before, nor any of the old hankering after the preeminence, but all virtue brought in them to its last finish, and shining through all, with surpassing lustre, that charity, concerning which the Lord had given so many charges saying, "In this shall all men know that ye are My disciples, if ye love one another".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:16
verses.text: (John xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:17
verses.text: ) And then, besides, there are doctrines to be found here, which we could not have known so surely as we now do, if this Book had not existed, but the very crowning point of our salvation would be hidden, alike for practice of life and for doctrine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:18
verses.text: The greater part, however, of this work is occupied with the acts of Paul, who "laboured more abundantly than they all".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:19
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:20
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:21
verses.text: ) And the reason is, that the author of this Book, that is, the blessed Luke, was his companion: a man, whose high qualities, sufficiently visible in many other instances, are especially shown in his firm adherence to his Teacher, whom he constantly followed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:22
verses.text: Thus at a time when all had forsaken him, one gone into Galatia, another into Dalmatia, hear what he says of this disciple: "Only Luke is with me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:23
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:24
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:25
verses.text: ) And giving the Corinthians a charge concerning him, he says, "Whose praise is in the Gospel throughout all the Churches".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:26
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:27
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:28
verses.text: ) Again, when he says, "He was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve," and, "according to the Gospel which ye received" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:29
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:30
verses.text: , ), he means the Gospel of this Luke.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:31
verses.text: So that there can be no mistake in attributing this work to him: and when I say, to him, I mean, to Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:32
verses.text: And why then did he not relate every thing, seeing he was with Paul to the end? We may answer, that what is here written, was sufficient for those who would attend, and that the sacred writers ever addressed themselves to the matter of immediate importance, whatever it might be at the time: it was no object with them to be writers of books: in fact, there are many things which they have delivered by unwritten tradition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:33
verses.text: Now while all that is contained in this Book is worthy of admiration, so is especially the way the Apostles have of coming down to the wants of their hearers: a condescension suggested by the Spirit who has so ordered it, that the subject on which they chiefly dwell is that which pertains to Christ as man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:34
verses.text: For so it is, that while they discourse so much about Christ, they have spoken but little concerning His Godhead; it was mostly of the Manhood that they discoursed, and of the Passion, and the Resurrection, and the Ascension.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:35
verses.text: For the thing required in the first instance was this, that it should be believed that He was risen, and ascended into heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:36
verses.text: As then the point on which Christ himself most insisted was, to have it known that He was come from the Father, so is it this writer's principal object to declare, that Christ was risen from the dead, and was received up into Heaven, and that He went to God, and came from God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:37
verses.text: For, if the fact of His coming from God were not first believed, much more, with the Resurrection and Ascension added thereto, would the Jews have found the entire doctrine incredible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:38
verses.text: Wherefore gently and by degrees he leads them on to higher truths.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:39
verses.text: Nay, at Athens Paul even calls Him man simply, without saying more (Acts xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:41
verses.text: For if, when Christ Himself spoke of His equality with the Father, they often attempted to stone Him, and called Him a blasphemer for this reason, it was little to be expected that they would receive this doctrine from the fishermen, and that too, with the Cross coming before it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:42
verses.text: But why speak of the Jews, seeing that even the disciples often upon hearing the more sublime doctrines were troubled and offended? Therefore also He told them, "I have many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:43
verses.text: (John xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:44
verses.text: ) If those could not, who had been so long time with Him, and had been admitted to so many secrets, and had seen so many wonders, how was it to be expected that men, but newly dragged away from altars, and idols, and sacrifices, and cats, and crocodiles (for such did the Gentiles worship), and from the rest of their evil ways, should all at once receive the more sublime matters of doctrine? And how in particular should Jews, hearing as they did every day of their lives, and having it ever sounded in their ears, "The Lord thy God is one Lord, and beside Him is none other" (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:45
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:46
verses.text: ): who also had seen Him hanging nailed on the Cross, nay, had themselves crucified and buried Him, and not seen Him even risen: when they were told that this same person was God and equal with the Father, how should they, of all men, be otherwise than shocked and revolted? Therefore it is that gently and little by little they carry them on, with much consideration and forbearance letting themselves down to their low attainments, themselves the while enjoying in more plentiful measure the grace of the Spirit, and doing greater works in Christ's name than Christ Himself did, that they may at once raise them up from their grovelling apprehensions, and confirm the saying, that Christ was raised from the dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:47
verses.text: For this, in fact, is just what this Book is: a Demonstration of the Resurrection:  this being once believed, the rest would come in due course.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:48
verses.text: The subject then and entire scope of this Book, in the main, is just what I have said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:49
verses.text: And now let us hear the Preface itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:50
verses.text: "The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and to teach".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:52
verses.text: ) Why does he put him in mind of the Gospel? To intimate how strictly he may be depended upon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:53
verses.text: For at the outset of the former work he says, "It seemed good to me also, having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first, to write unto thee in order".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:54
verses.text: (Luke i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:55
verses.text: ) Neither is he content with his own testimony, but refers the whole matter to the Apostles, saying, "Even as they delivered them unto us, which from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:56
verses.text: (Luke i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:57
verses.text: ) Having then accredited his account in the former instance, he has no need to put forth his credentials afresh for this treatise, seeing his disciple has been once for all satisfied, and by the mention of that former work he has reminded him of the strict reliance to be placed in him for the truth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:58
verses.text: For if a person has shown himself competent and trustworthy to write of things which he has heard, and moreover has obtained our confidence, much more will he have a right to our confidence when he has composed an account, not of things which he has received from others, but of things which he has seen and heard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:59
verses.text: For thou didst receive what relates to Christ; much more wilt thou receive what concerns the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:60
verses.text: What then, (it may be asked), is it a question only of history, with which the Holy Spirit has nothing to do? Not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:61
verses.text: For, if "those delivered it unto us, who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word;" then, what he says, is theirs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:62
verses.text: And why did he not say, 'As they who were counted worthy of the Holy Spirit delivered them unto us;' but "Those who were eyewitnesses?" Because, in matter of belief, the very thing that gives one a right to be believed, is the having learned from eyewitnesses: whereas the other appears to foolish persons mere parade and pretension.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:63
verses.text: And therefore John also speaks thus: "I saw, and bare record that this is the Son of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:64
verses.text: (John.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:65
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:66
verses.text: ) And Christ expresses Himself in the same way to Nicodemus, while he was dull of apprehension, "We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and no one receiveth our witness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:67
verses.text: (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:68
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:69
verses.text: ) Accordingly, He gave them leave to rest their testimony in many particulars on the fact of their having seen them, when He said, "And do ye bear witness concerning Me, because ye have been with Me from the beginning".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:70
verses.text: (John xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:71
verses.text: ) The Apostles themselves also often speak in a similar manner; "We are witnesses, and the Holy Spirit which God hath given to those that obey Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:72
verses.text: (Acts ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:73
verses.text: ); and on a subsequent occasion, Peter, still giving assurance of the Resurrection, said, "Seeing we did eat and drink with Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:74
verses.text: (Acts x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:75
verses.text: ) For they more readily received the testimony of persons who had been His companions, because the notion of the Spirit was as yet very much beyond them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:76
verses.text: Therefore John also at that time, in his Gospel, speaking of the blood and water, said, he himself saw it, making the fact of his having seen it equivalent, for them, to the highest testimony, although the witness of the Spirit is more certain than the evidence of sight, but not so with unbelievers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:77
verses.text: Now that Luke was a partaker of the Spirit, is abundantly clear, both from the miracles which even now take place; and from the fact that in those times even ordinary persons were gifted with the Holy Ghost; and again from the testimony of Paul, in these words, "Whose praise is in the Gospel" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:78
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:79
verses.text: ); and from the appointment to which he was chosen: for having said this, the Apostle adds, "But also appointed of the Churches to travel with us with this grace which is administered by us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:80
verses.text: Now mark how unassuming he is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:81
verses.text: He does not say, The former Gospel which I preached, but, "The former treatise have I made;" accounting the title of Gospel to be too great for him; although it is on the score of this that the Apostle dignifies him: "Whose praise," he says, "is in the Gospel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:82
verses.text: But he himself modestly says, "The former treatise have I made—O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and to teach:" not simply "of all," but from the beginning to the end; "until the day," he says, "in which He was taken up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:83
verses.text: And yet John says, that it was not possible to write all: for "were they written, I suppose," says he, "that even the world itself could not contain the books written".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:84
verses.text: (John xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:85
verses.text: ) How then does the Evangelist here say, "Of all?" He does not say "all," but "of all," as much as to say, "in a summary way, and in the gross;" and "of all that is mainly and pressingly important".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:86
verses.text: Then he tells us in what sense he says all, when he adds, "Which Jesus began both to do and to teach;" meaning His miracles and teaching; and not only so, but implying that His doing was also a teaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:87
verses.text: But now consider the benevolent and Apostolic feelings of the writer: that for the sake of a single individual he took such pains as to write for him an entire Gospel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:88
verses.text: "That thou mightest have," he says, "the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:89
verses.text: (Luke i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:90
verses.text: ) In truth, he had heard Christ say, "It is not the will of My Father that one of these little ones should perish".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:91
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:92
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:93
verses.text: ) And why did he not make one book of it, to send to one man Theophilus, but has divided it into two subjects? For clearness, and to give the brother a pause for rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:94
verses.text: Besides, the two treatises are distinct in their subject-matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:95
verses.text: But consider how Christ accredited his words by His deeds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:96
verses.text: Thus He saith, "Learn of Me, for I am meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:97
verses.text: (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:98
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:99
verses.text: ) He taught men to be poor,  and exhibited this by His actions: "For the Son of Man," He says, "hath not where to lay His head".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:100
verses.text: (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:101
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:102
verses.text: ) Again, He charged men to love their enemies; and He taught the same lesson on the Cross, when He prayed for those who were crucifying Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:103
verses.text: He said, "If any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also" (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:104
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:105
verses.text: ): now He not only gave His garments, but even His blood.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:106
verses.text: In this way He bade others teach.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:107
verses.text: Wherefore Paul also said, "So as ye have us for an example".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:108
verses.text: (Philip.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:109
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:110
verses.text: ) For nothing is more frigid than a teacher who shows his philosophy only in words: this is to act the part not of a teacher, but of a hypocrite.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:111
verses.text: Therefore the Apostles first taught by their conduct, and then by their words; nay rather they had no need of words, when their deeds spoke so loud.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:112
verses.text: Nor is it wrong to speak of Christ's Passion as action, for in suffering all He performed that great and wonderful act, by which He destroyed death, and effected all else that He did for us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:113
verses.text: "Until the day in which He was taken up, after that He, through the Holy Spirit, had given commandments unto the Apostles whom He had chosen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:114
verses.text: After He had given commandments through the Spirit" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:115
verses.text: ); i-e: they were spiritual words that He spake unto them, nothing human; either this is the meaning, or, that it was by the Spirit that He gave them commandments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:116
verses.text: Do you observe in what low terms he still speaks of Christ, as in fact Christ had spoken of Himself? "But if I by the Spirit of God cast out devils" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:117
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:118
verses.text: ); for indeed the Holy Ghost wrought in that Temple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:119
verses.text: Well, what did He command? "Go ye therefore," He says, "make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost; teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:120
verses.text: (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:121
verses.text: xxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:122
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:123
verses.text: ) A high encomium this for the Apostles; to have such a charge entrusted to them, I mean, the salvation of the world! words full of the Spirit! And this the writer hints at in the expression, "through the Holy Ghost" (and, "the words which I spake unto you," saith the Lord, "are Spirit") (John vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:124
verses.text: ); thus leading the hearer on to a desire of learning what the commands were, and establishing the authority of the Apostles, seeing it is the words of the Spirit they are about to speak, and the commandments of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:125
verses.text: "After He had given commandments," he says, "He was taken up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:126
verses.text: He does not say, 'ascended;' he still speaks as concerning a man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:127
verses.text: It appears then that He also taught the Disciples after His resurrection, but of this space of time no one has related to us the whole in detail.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:128
verses.text: St.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:129
verses.text: John indeed, as also does the present writer, dwells at greater length on this subject than the others; but none has clearly related every thing (for they hastened to something else); however, we have learnt these things through the Apostles, for what they heard, that did they tell.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:130
verses.text: "To whom also He shewed Himself alive".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:131
verses.text: Having first spoken of the Ascension, he adverts to the Resurrection; for since thou hast been told that "He was taken up," therefore, lest thou shouldest suppose Him to have been taken up by others, he adds, "To whom He shewed Himself alive".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:132
verses.text: For if He shewed Himself in the greater, surely He did in the minor circumstance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:133
verses.text: Seest thou, how casually and unperceived he drops by the way the seeds of these great doctrines?  "Being seen of them during forty days".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:134
verses.text: He was not always with them now, as He was before the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:135
verses.text: For the writer does not say "forty days," but, "during forty days".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:136
verses.text: He came, and again disappeared; by this leading them on to higher conceptions, and no longer permitting them to stand affected towards Him in the same way as before, but taking effectual measures to secure both these objects, that the fact of His Resurrection should be believed, and that He Himself should be ever after apprehended to be greater than man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:137
verses.text: At the same time, these were two opposite things; for in order to the belief in His Resurrection, much was to be done of a human character, and for the other object, just the reverse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:138
verses.text: Nevertheless, both results have been effected, each when the fitting time arrived.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:139
verses.text: But why did He appear not to all, but to the Apostles only? Because to the many it would have seemed a mere apparition, inasmuch as they understood not the secret of the mystery.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:140
verses.text: For if the disciples themselves were at first incredulous and were troubled, and needed the evidence of actual touch with the hand, and of His eating with them, how would it have fared in all likelihood with the multitude? For this reason therefore by the miracles wrought by the Apostles He renders the evidence of His Resurrection unequivocal, so that not only the men of those times—this is what would come of the ocular proof—but also all men thereafter, should be certain of the fact, that He was risen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:141
verses.text: Upon this ground also we argue with unbelievers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:142
verses.text: For if He did not rise again, but remains dead, how did the Apostles perform miracles in His name? But they did not, say you, perform miracles? How then was our religion (ἔθνος) instituted? For this certainly they will not controvert nor impugn what we see with our eyes: so that when they say that no miracles took place, they inflict a worse stab upon themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:143
verses.text: For this would be the greatest of miracles, that without any miracles, the whole world should have eagerly come to be taken in the nets of twelve poor and illiterate men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:144
verses.text: For not by wealth of money, not by wisdom of words, not by any thing else of this kind, did the fishermen prevail; so that objectors must even against their will acknowledge that there was in these men a Divine power, for no human strength could ever possibly effect such great results.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:145
verses.text: For this He then remained forty days on earth, furnishing in this length of time the sure evidence of their seeing Him in His own proper Person, that they might not suppose that what they saw was a phantom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:146
verses.text: And not content with this, He added also the evidence of eating with them at their board: as to signify this, the writer adds, "And being at table with them, He commanded".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:147
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:148
verses.text: ) And this circumstance the Apostles themselves always put forth as an fallible token of the Resurrection; as where they say, "Who did eat and drink with Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:149
verses.text: (Acts x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:150
verses.text: )  And what did He, when appearing unto them those forty days? Why, He conversed with them, says the writer, "concerning the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:151
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:152
verses.text: ) For, since the disciples both had been distressed and troubled at the things which already had taken place, and were about to go forth to encounter great difficulties, He recovered them by His discourses concerning the future.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:153
verses.text: "He commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:154
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:155
verses.text: ) First, He led them out to Galilee, afraid and trembling, in order that they might listen to His words in security.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:156
verses.text: Afterwards, when they had heard, and had passed forty days with Him, "He commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:157
verses.text: Wherefore? Just as when soldiers are to charge a multitude, no one thinks of letting them issue forth until they have armed themselves, or as horses are not suffered to start from the barriers until they have got their charioteer; so Christ did not suffer these to appear in the field before the descent of the Spirit, that they might not be in a condition to be easily defeated and taken captive by the many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:158
verses.text: Nor was this the only reason, but also there were many in Jerusalem who should believe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:159
verses.text: And then again that it might not be said, that leaving their own acquaintance, they had gone to make a parade among strangers, therefore among those very men who had put Christ to death do they exhibit the proofs of His Resurrection, among those who had crucified and buried Him, in the very town in which the iniquitous deed had been perpetrated; thereby stopping the mouths of all foreign objectors.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:160
verses.text: For when those even who had crucified Him appear as believers, clearly this proved both the fact of the crucifixion and the iniquity of the deed, and afforded a mighty evidence of the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:161
verses.text: Furthermore, lest the Apostles should say, How shall it be possible for us to live among wicked and bloody men, they so many in number, we so few and contemptible, observe how He does away their fear and distress, by these words, "But wait for the promise of the Father, which ye have heard of Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:162
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:163
verses.text: ) You will say, When had they heard this? When He said, "It is expedient for you that I go away; for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:164
verses.text: (John xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:165
verses.text: ) And again, "I will pray the Father, and He shall send you another Comforter, that He may abide with you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:166
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:167
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:168
verses.text: )  But why did the Holy Ghost come to them, not while Christ was present, nor even immediately after his departure, but, whereas Christ ascended on the fortieth day, the Spirit descended "when the day of Pentecost," that is, the fiftieth, "was fully come?" (Acts ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:169
verses.text: ) And how was it, if the Spirit had not yet come, that He said, "Receive ye the Holy Ghost?" (John xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:170
verses.text: ) In order to render them capable and meet for the reception of Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:171
verses.text: For if Daniel fainted at the sight of an Angel (Dan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:172
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:173
verses.text: ), much more would these when about to receive so great a grace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:174
verses.text: Either this then is to be said, or else that Christ spoke of what was to come, as if come already; as when He said, "Tread ye upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the devil".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:175
verses.text: (Luke x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:176
verses.text: ) But why had the Holy Ghost not yet come? It was fit that they should first be brought to have a longing desire for that event, and so receive the grace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:177
verses.text: For this reason Christ Himself departed, and then the Spirit descended.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:178
verses.text: For had He Himself been there, they would not have expected the Spirit so earnestly as they did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:179
verses.text: On this account neither did He come immediately after Christ's Ascension, but after eight or nine days.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:180
verses.text: It is the same with us also; for our desires towards God are then most raised, when we stand in need.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:181
verses.text: Accordingly, John chose that time to send his disciples to Christ when they were likely to feel their need of Jesus, during his own imprisonment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:182
verses.text: Besides, it was fit that our nature should be seen in heaven, and that the reconciliation should be perfected, and then the Spirit should come, and the joy should be unalloyed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:183
verses.text: For, if the Spirit being already come, Christ had then departed, and the Spirit remained; the consolation would not have been so great as it was.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:184
verses.text: For in fact they clung to Him, and could not bear to part with Him; wherefore also to comfort them He said, "It is expedient for you that I go away".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:185
verses.text: (John xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:186
verses.text: ) On this account He also waits during those intermediate days, that they might first despond for awhile, and be made, as I said, to feel their need of Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:187
verses.text: and then reap a full and unalloyed delight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:188
verses.text: But if the Spirit were inferior to the Son, the consolation would not have been adequate; and how could He have said, "It is expedient for you?" For this reason the greater matters of teaching were reserved for the Spirit, that the disciples might not imagine Him inferior.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:189
verses.text: Consider also how necessary He made it for them to abide in Jerusalem, by promising that the Spirit should be granted them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:190
verses.text: For lest they should again flee away after His Ascension, by this expectation, as by a bond, He keeps them to that spot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:191
verses.text: But having said, "Wait for the promise of the Father, which ye have heard of Me," He then adds, "For John truly baptized with water, but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:192
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:193
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:194
verses.text: ) For now indeed He gives them to see the difference there was betwixt Him and John, plainly, and not as heretofore in obscure hints; for in fact He had spoken very obscurely, when He said, "Notwithstanding, he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he:" but now He says plainly, "John baptized with water, but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:195
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:196
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:197
verses.text: ) And he no longer uses the testimony, but merely adverts to the person of John, reminding the disciples of what he had said, and shows them that they are now become greater than John; seeing they too are to baptize with the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:198
verses.text: Again, He did not say, I baptize you with the Holy Ghost, but, "Ye shall be baptized:" teaching us humility.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:199
verses.text: For this was plain enough from the testimonyof John, that it was Christ Himself Who should baptize: "He it is that shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire" (Luke iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:200
verses.text: ); wherefore also He made mention of John.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:201
verses.text: The Gospels, then, are a history of what Christ did and said; but the Acts, of what that "other Comforter" said and did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:202
verses.text: Not but that the Spirit did many things in the Gospels also; even as Christ here in the Acts still works in men as He did in the Gospels: only then the Spirit wrought through the Temple, now through the Apostles: then, He came into the Virgin's womb, and fashioned the Temple; now, into Apostolic souls: then in the likeness of a dove; now, in the likeness of fire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:203
verses.text: And wherefore? Showing there the gentleness of the Lord, but here His taking vengeance also, He now puts them in mind of the judgment likewise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:204
verses.text: For, when need was to forgive, need was there of much gentleness; but now we have obtained the gift, it is henceforth a time for judgment and examination.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:205
verses.text: But why does Christ say, "Ye shall be baptized," when in fact there was no water in the upper room? Because the more essential part of Baptism is the Spirit, through Whom indeed the water has its operation; in the same manner our Lord also is said to be anointed, not that He had ever been anointed with oil, but because He had received the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:206
verses.text: Besides, we do in fact find them receiving a baptism with water and a baptism with the Spirit, and these at different moments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:207
verses.text: In our case both take place under one act, but then they were divided.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:208
verses.text: For in the beginning they were baptized by John; since, if harlots and publicans went to that baptism, much rather would they who thereafter were to be baptized by the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:209
verses.text: Then, that the Apostles might not say, that they were always having it held out to them in promises (John xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:210
verses.text: , ), (for indeed Christ had already discoursed much to them concerning the Spirit, that they should not imagine It to be an impersonal Energy or Operation, (ἐνέργειαν ἀνυπόστατον) that they might not say this, then, He adds, "not many days hence".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:211
verses.text: And He did not explain when, that they might always watch: but, that it would soon take place, He told them, that they might not faint; yet the exact time He refrained from adding, that they might always be vigilant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:212
verses.text: Nor does He assure them by this alone; I mean, by the shortness of the time, but withal by saying, "The promise which ye have heard of Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:213
verses.text: For this is not, saith He, the only time I have told you, but already I have promised what I shall certainly perform.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:214
verses.text: What wonder then that He does not signify the day of the final consummation, when this day which was so near He did not choose to reveal? And with good reason; to the end they may be ever wakeful, and in a state of expectation and earnest heed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:215
verses.text: For it cannot, it cannot be, that a man should enjoy the benefit of grace except he watch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:216
verses.text: Seest thou not what Elias saith to his disciple? "If thou see me when I am taken up" ( Kings ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:217
verses.text: ), this that thou askest shall be done for thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:218
verses.text: Christ also was ever wont to say unto those that came unto Him, "Believest thou?" For if we be not appropriated and made over to the thing given, neither do we greatly feel the benefit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:219
verses.text: So it was also in the case of Paul; grace did not come to him immediately, but three days intervened, during which he was blind; purified the while, and prepared by fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:220
verses.text: For as those who dye the purple first season with other ingredients the cloth that is to receive the dye, that the bloom may not be fleeting; so in this instance God first takes order that the soul shall be thoroughly in earnest, and then pours forth His grace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:221
verses.text: On this account also, neither did He immediately send the Spirit, but on the fiftieth day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:222
verses.text: Now if any one ask, why we also do not baptize at that season of Pentecost? we may answer, that grace is the same now as then; but the mind becomes more elevated now, by being prepared through fasting.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:223
verses.text: And the season too of Pentecost furnishes a not unlikely reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:224
verses.text: What may that be? Our fathers held Baptism to be just the proper curb upon evil concupiscence, and a powerful lesson for teaching to be sober-minded even in a time of delights.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:225
verses.text: As if then we were banquetting with Christ Himself, and partaking of His table, let us do nothing at random, but let us pass our time in fastings, and prayers, and much sobriety of mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:226
verses.text: For if a man who is destined to enter upon some temporal government, prepares himself all his life long, and that he may obtain some dignity, lays out his money, spends his time, and submits to endless troubles; what shall we deserve, who draw near to the kingdom of heaven with such negligence, and both show no earnestness before we have received, and after having received are again negligent? Nay, this is the very reason why we are negligent after having received, that we did not watch before we had received.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:227
verses.text: Therefore many, after they have received, immediately have returned to their former vomit, and have become more wicked, and drawn upon themselves a more severe punishment; when having been delivered from their former sins, herein they have more grievously provoked the Judge, that having been delivered from so great a disease, still they did not learn sobriety, but that has happened unto them, which Christ threatened to the paralytic man, saying, "Behold thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee" (John v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:228
verses.text: ): and which He also predicted of the Jews, that "the last state shall be worse than the first".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:229
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:230
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:231
verses.text: ) For if, saith He, showing that by their ingratitude they should bring upon them the worst of evils, "if I had not come, and spoken unto them, they had not had sin" (John xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:232
verses.text: ); so that the guilt of sins committed after these benefits is doubled and quadrupled, in that, after the honour put upon us, we show ourselves ungrateful and wicked.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:233
verses.text: And the Laver of Baptism helps not a whit to procure for us a milder punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:234
verses.text: And consider: a man has gotten grievous sins by committing murder or adultery, or some other crime: these were remitted through Baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:235
verses.text: For there is no sin, no impiety, which does not yield and give place to this gift; for the Grace is Divine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:236
verses.text: A man has again committed adultery and murder; the former adultery is indeed done away, the murder forgiven, and not brought up again to his charge, "for the gifts and calling of God are without repentance" (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:237
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:238
verses.text: ); but for those committed after Baptism he suffers a punishment as great as he would if both the former sins were brought up again, and many worse than these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:239
verses.text: For the guilt is no longer simply equal, but doubled and tripled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:240
verses.text: Look: in proof that the penalty of these sins is greater, hear what St.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:241
verses.text: Paul says: "He that despised Moses' law died without mercy, under two or three witnesses: of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?" (Heb.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:242
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:243
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:244
verses.text: )  Perhaps we have now deterred many from receiving baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:245
verses.text: Not however with this intention have we so spoken, but on purpose that having received it, they may continue in temperance and much moderation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:246
verses.text: 'But I am afraid,' says one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:247
verses.text: If thou wert afraid, thou wouldest have received and guarded it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:248
verses.text: 'Nay,' saith he, 'but this is the very reason why I do not receive it,—that I am frightened.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:249
verses.text: ' And art thou not afraid to depart thus? 'God is merciful,' saith he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:250
verses.text: Receive baptism then, because He is merciful and ready to help.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:251
verses.text: But thou, where to be in earnest is the thing required, dost not allege this mercifulness; thou thinkest of this only where thou hast a mind to do so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:252
verses.text: And yet that was the time to resort to God's mercy, and we shall then be surest of obtaining it, when we do our part.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:253
verses.text: For he that has cast the whole matter upon God, and, after his baptism, sins, as being man it is likely, he may, and repents, shall obtain mercy; whereas he that prevaricates with God's mercy, and departs this life with no portion in that grace, shall have his punishment without a word to be said for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:254
verses.text: 'But how if he depart,' say you, 'after having had the grace vouchsafed to him?' He will depart empty again of all good works.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:255
verses.text: For it is impossible, yes, it is in my opinion impossible, that the man who upon such hopes dallied with baptism should have effected ought generous and good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:256
verses.text: And why dost thou harbor such fear, and presume upon the uncertain chance of the future? Why not convert this fear into labor and earnestness, and thou shalt be great and admirable? Which is best, to fear or to labor? Suppose some one to have placed thee, having nothing to do, in a tottering house, saying, Look for the decaying roof to fall upon thy head: for perhaps it will fall, perhaps not; but if thou hadst rather it should not, then work and inhabit the more secure apartment: which wouldest thou have rather chosen, that idle condition accompanied with fear, or this labor with confidence? Why then, act now in the same way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:257
verses.text: For the uncertain future is like a decayed house, ever threatening to fall; but this work, laborious though it be, ensures safety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:258
verses.text: Now God forbid that it should happen to us to fall into so great straits as to sin after baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:259
verses.text: However, even if aught such should happen, God is merciful, and has given us many ways of obtaining remission even after this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:260
verses.text: But just as those who sin after baptism are punished for this reason more severely than the Catechumens, so again, those who know that there are medicines in repentance, and yet will not make use of them, will undergo a more grievous chastisement.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:261
verses.text: For by how much the mercy of God is enlarged, by so much does the punishment increase, if we do not duly profit by that mercy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:262
verses.text: What sayest thou, O man? When thou wast full of such grievous evils, and given over, suddenly thou becamest a friend, and wast exalted to the highest honor, not by labors of thine own, but by the gift of God: thou didst again return to thy former misconduct; and though thou didst deserve to be sorely punished, nevertheless, God did not turn away, but gave unnumbered opportunities of salvation, whereby thou mayest yet become a friend: yet for all this, thou hast not the will to labor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:263
verses.text: What forgiveness canst thou deserve henceforth? Will not the Gentiles with good reason deride thee as a worthless drone? For if there be power in that doctrine of yours, say they, what means this multitude of uninitiated persons? If the mysteries be excellent and desirable, let none receive baptism at his last gasp.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:264
verses.text: For that is not the time for giving of mysteries but for making of wills; the time for mysteries is in health of mind and soundness of soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:265
verses.text: For, if a man would not prefer to make his will in such a condition; and if he does so make it, he gives a handle for subsequent litigation (and this is the reason why testators premise these words: "Alive, in my senses, and in health, I make this disposal of my property:"), how should it be possible for a person who is no longer master of his senses to go through the right course of preparation for the sacred mysteries? For if in the affairs of this life, the laws of the world would not permit a man who was not perfectly sound in mind to make a will, although it be in his own affairs that he would lay down the law; how, when thou art receiving instruction concerning the kingdom of heaven, and the unspeakable riches of that world, shall it be possible for thee to learn all clearly, when very likely too thou art beside thyself through the violence of thy malady? And when wilt thou say those words to Christ, in the act of being buried with Him when at the point to depart hence? For indeed both by works and by words must we show our good will towards Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:266
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:267
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:268
verses.text: ) Now what thou art doing is all one, as if a man should want to be enlisted as a soldier, when the war is just about to break up; or to strip for the contest in the arena, just when the spectators have risen from their seats.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:269
verses.text: For thou hast thine arms given thee, not that thou shouldest straightway depart hence, but that being equipped therewith, thou mayest raise a trophy over the enemy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:270
verses.text: Let no one think that it is out of season to discourse on this subject, because it is not Lent now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:271
verses.text: Nay, this it is that vexes me, that ye look to a set time in such matters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:272
verses.text: Whereas that Eunuch, barbarian as he was and on a journey, yea on the very highway, he did not seek for a set time (Acts viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:273
verses.text: ); no, nor the jailer, though he was in the midst of a set of prisoners, and the teacher he saw before him was a man scourged and in chains, and whom he was still to have in his custody.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:274
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:275
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:276
verses.text: ) But here, not being inmates of a jail, nor out on a journey, many are putting off their baptism even to their last breath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:277
verses.text: Now if thou still questionest that Christ is God, stand away from the Church: be not here, even as a hearer of the Divine Word, and as one of the catechumens: but if thou art sure of this, and knowest clearly this truth, why delay? Why shrink back and hesitate? For fear, say you, lest I should sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:278
verses.text: But dost thou not fear what is worse, to depart for the next world with such a heavy burden? For it is not equally excusable, not to have gotten a grace set before you, and to have failed in attempting to live uprightly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:279
verses.text: If thou be called to account, Why didst thou not come for it? what wilt thou answer? In the other case thou mayest allege the burden of thy passions, and the difficulty of a virtuous life: but nothing of the kind here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:280
verses.text: For here is grace, freely conveying liberty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:281
verses.text: But thou fearest lest thou shouldest sin? Let this be thy language after Baptism: and then entertain this fear, in order to hold fast the liberty thou hast received; not now, to prevent thy receiving such a gift.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:282
verses.text: Whereas now thou art wary before baptism, and negligent after it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:283
verses.text: But thou art waiting for Lent: and why? Has that season any advantage? Nay, it was not at the Passover that the Apostles received the grace, but at another season; and then three thousand (Luke says,) and five thousand were baptized: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:284
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:285
verses.text: ; iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:286
verses.text: , and ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:287
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:288
verses.text: ) and again Cornelius.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:289
verses.text: Let us then not wait for a set time, lest by hesitating and putting off we depart empty, and destitute of so great gifts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:290
verses.text: What do you suppose is my anguish when I hear that any person has been taken away unbaptized, while I reflect upon the intolerable punishments of that life, the inexorable doom! Again, how I am grieved to behold others drawing near to their last gasp, and not brought to their right mind even then.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:291
verses.text: Hence too it is that scenes take place quite unworthy of this gift.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:292
verses.text: For whereas there ought to be joy, and dancing, and exultation, and wearing of garlands, when another is christened; the wife of the sick man has no sooner heard that the physician has ordered this, than she is overcome with grief, as if it were some dire calamity; she sets up the greatest lamentation, and nothing is heard all over the house but crying and wailing, just as it is when condemned criminals are led away to their doom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:293
verses.text: The sick man again is then more sorely grieved; and if he recovers from his illness, is as vexed as if some great harm had been done to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:294
verses.text: For since he had not been prepared for a virtuous life, he has no heart for the conflicts which are to follow, and shrinks at the thought of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:295
verses.text: Do you see what devices the devil contrives, what shame, what ridicule? Let us rid ourselves of this disgrace; let us live as Christ has enjoined.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:296
verses.text: He gave us Baptism, not that we should receive and depart, but that we should show the fruits of it in our after life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:297
verses.text: How can one say to him who is departing and broken down, Bear fruit? Hast thou not heard that "the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace?" (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:298
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:299
verses.text: ) How comes it then that the very contrary takes place here? For the wife stands there mourning, when she ought to rejoice; the children weeping, when they ought to be glad together; the sick man himself lies there in darkness, and surrounded by noise and tumult, when he ought to be keeping high festival; full of exceeding despondency at the thought of leaving his children orphans, his wife a widow, his house desolate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:300
verses.text: Is this a state in which to draw near unto mysteries? answer me; is this a state in which to approach the sacred table? Are such scenes to be tolerated? Should the Emperor send letters and release the prisoners in the jails, there is joy and gladness: God sends down the Holy Ghost from Heaven to remit not arrears of money, but a whole mass of sins, and do ye all bewail and lament? Why, how grossly unsuitable is this! Not to mention that sometimes it is upon the dead that the water has been poured, and holy mysteries flung upon the ground.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:301
verses.text: However, not we are to blame for this, but men who are so perverse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 1:302
verses.text: I exhort you then to leave all, and turn and draw near to Baptism with all alacrity, that having given proof of great earnestness at this present time, we may obtain confidence for that which is to come; whereunto that we may attain, may it be granted unto us all by the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, to Whom be glory and power for ever and ever, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:1
verses.text: Homily II.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:2
verses.text: Acts I.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:3
verses.text: "When they therefore were come together, they asked of Him, saying, Lord, wilt Thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?"  When the disciples intend to ask anything, they approach Him together, that by dint of numbers they may abash Him into compliance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:4
verses.text: They well knew that in what He had said previously, "Of that day knoweth no man" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:5
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:6
verses.text: ), He had merely declined telling them: therefore they again drew near, and put the question.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:7
verses.text: They would not have put it had they been truly satisfied with that answer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:8
verses.text: For having heard that they were about to receive the Holy Ghost, they, as being now worthy of instruction, desired to learn.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:9
verses.text: Also they were quite ready for freedom: for they had no mind to address themselves to danger; what they wished was to breathe freely again; for they were no light matters that had happened to them, but the utmost peril had impended over them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:10
verses.text: And without saying any thing to Him of the Holy Ghost, they put this question: "Lord, wilt Thou at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?" They did not ask, when? but whether "at this time".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:11
verses.text: So eager were they for that day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:12
verses.text: Indeed, to me it appears that they had not any clear notion of the nature of that kingdom; for the Spirit had not yet instructed them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:13
verses.text: And they do not say, When shall these things be? but they approach Him with greater honour, saying, "Wilt Thou at this time restore again the kingdom," as being now already fallen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:14
verses.text: For there they were still affected towards sensible objects, seeing they were not yet become better than those who were before them; here they have henceforth high conceptions concerning Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:15
verses.text: Since then their minds are elevated, He also speaks to them in a higher strain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:16
verses.text: For He no longer tells them, "Of that day not even the Son of Man knoweth" (Mark xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:17
verses.text: ); but He says, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons which the Father hath put in His own power (Acts i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:18
verses.text: ) Ye ask things greater than your capacity, He would say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:19
verses.text: And yet even now they learned things that were much greater than this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:20
verses.text: And that you may see that this is strictly the case, look how many things I shall enumerate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:21
verses.text: What, I pray you, was greater than their having learned what they did learn? Thus, they learned that there is a Son of God, and that God has a Son equal with Himself in dignity (John v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:22
verses.text: –); they learned that there will be a resurrection (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:23
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:24
verses.text: ); that when He ascended He sat on the right hand of God (Luke xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:25
verses.text: ); and what is still more stupendous, that Flesh is seated in heaven, and adored by Angels, and that He will come again (Mark xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:26
verses.text: ); they learned what is to take place in the judgment (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:27
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:28
verses.text: ); learned that they shall then sit and judge the twelve tribes of Israel (Luke xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:29
verses.text: ); learned that the Jews would be cast out, and in their stead the Gentiles should come in (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:30
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:32
verses.text: For, tell me, which is greater? to learn that a person will reign, or to learn the time when? (Luke xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:34
verses.text: Paul learned "things which it is not lawful for a man to utter" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:35
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:36
verses.text: ); things that were before the world was made, he learned them all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:37
verses.text: Which is the more difficult, the beginning or the end? Clearly to learn the beginning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:38
verses.text: This, Moses learned, and the time when, and how long ago: and he enumerates the years.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:39
verses.text: And the wise Solomon saith, "I will make mention of things from the beginning of the world".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:40
verses.text: And that the time is at hand, they do know: as Paul saith, "The Lord is at hand, be careful for nothing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:41
verses.text: (Phil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:42
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:43
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:44
verses.text: These things they knew not then, and yet He mentions many signs (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:45
verses.text: ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:46
verses.text: xxiv).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:47
verses.text: But, as He has just said, "Not many days hence," wishing them to be vigilant, and did not openly declare the precise moment, so is it here also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:48
verses.text: However, it is not about the general Consummation that they now ask Him, but, "Wilt Thou at this time," say they, "restore the kingdom to Israel?" And not even this did He reveal to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:49
verses.text: They also asked this about the end of the world before: and as on that occasion He answered by leading them away from thinking that their deliverance was near and, on the contrary, cast them into the midst of perils, so likewise on this occasion but more mildly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:50
verses.text: For, that they may not imagine themselves to be wronged, and these things to be mere pretences, hear what He says: He immediately gives them that at which they rejoiced: for He adds: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you; and ye shall be witnesses unto Me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:51
verses.text: (Acts i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:52
verses.text: ) Then, that they may make no more enquiries, straightway He was received up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:53
verses.text: Thus, just as on the former occasion He had darkened their minds by awe, and by saying, "I know not;" here also He does so by being taken up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:54
verses.text: For great was their eagerness on the subject, and they would not have desisted; and yet it was very necessary that they should not learn this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:55
verses.text: For tell me, which do the Gentiles most disbelieve? that there will be a consummation of the world, or that God is become man, and issued from the Virgin? But I am ashamed of dwelling on this point, as if it were about some difficult matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:56
verses.text: Then again, that the disciples might not say, Why dost thou leave the matter in suspense? He adds, "Which the Father hath put in His own power".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:57
verses.text: And yet He declared the Father's power and His to be one: as in the saying, "For as the Father raiseth up the dead and quickeneth them, even so the Son quickeneth whom He will".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:58
verses.text: (John v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:59
verses.text: ) If where need is to work, Thou actest with the same power as the Father; where it behooves to know, dost Thou not know with the same power? Yet certainly to raise up the dead is much greater than to learn the day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:60
verses.text: If the greater be with power, much more the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:61
verses.text: But just as when we see a child crying, and pertinaciously wishing to get something from us that is not expedient for him, we hide the thing, and show him our empty hands, and say, "See, we have it not:" the like has Christ here done with the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:62
verses.text: But as the child, even when we show him our empty hands, persists with his crying, conscious he has been deceived, and then we leave him, and depart, saying, "Such an one calls me:" and we give him something else instead, in order to divert him from his desire, telling him it is a much finer thing than the other, and then hasten away; in like manner Christ acted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:63
verses.text: The disciples asked to have something, and He said He had it not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:64
verses.text: And on the first occasion he frightened them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:65
verses.text: Then again they asked to have it now: He said He had it not; and He did not frighten them now, but after having shown the empty hands, He has done this, and gives them a plausible reason: "Which the Father," He says, "hath put in his own power".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:66
verses.text: What? Thou not know the things of the Father! Thou knowest Him, and not what belongs to Him! And yet Thou hast said, "None knoweth the Father but the Son" (Luke x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:67
verses.text: ); and, "The Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:68
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:69
verses.text: ); and Thou not know this! But they feared to ask Him again, lest they should hear Him say, "Are ye also without understanding?" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:70
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:71
verses.text: ) For they feared Him now much more than before.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:72
verses.text: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:73
verses.text: As in the former instance He had not answered their question (for it is the part of a teacher to teach not what the disciple chooses, but what is expedient for him to learn), so in this, He tells them beforehand, for this reason, what they ought to know, that they may not be troubled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:74
verses.text: In truth, they were yet weak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:75
verses.text: But to inspire them with confidence, He raised up their souls, and concealed what was grievous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:76
verses.text: Since he was about to leave them very shortly, therefore in this discourse He says nothing painful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:77
verses.text: But how? He extols as great the things which would be painful: all but saying, "'Fear not': for ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you; and ye shall be witnesses unto Me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:78
verses.text: For since he had said, "Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not" (Matt.
