verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:79
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:80
verses.text: ), what there He left unsaid, He here adds, "And to the uttermost part of the earth;" and having spoken this, which was more fearful than all the rest, then that they may not again question Him, He held His peace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:81
verses.text: "And having this said, while they beheld, He was taken up; and a cloud received Him out of their sight" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:82
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:83
verses.text: Seest thou that they did preach and fulfil the Gospel? For great was the gift He had bestowed on them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:84
verses.text: In the very place, He says, where ye are afraid, that is, in Jerusalem, there preach ye first, and afterwards unto the uttermost part of the earth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:85
verses.text: Then for assurance of what He had said, "While they beheld, He was taken up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:86
verses.text: Not "while they beheld" did He rise from the dead, but "while they beheld, He was taken up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:87
verses.text: Inasmuch, however, as the sight of their eyes even here was not all-sufficient; for in the Resurrection they saw the end, but not the beginning, and in the Ascension they saw the beginning, but not the end: because in the former it had been superfluous to have seen the beginning, the Lord Himself Who spake these things being present, and the sepulchre showing clearly that He is not there; but in the latter, they needed to be informed of the sequel by word of others: inasmuch then as their eyes do not suffice to show them the height above, nor to inform them whether He is actually gone up into heaven, or only seemingly into heaven, see then what follows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:88
verses.text: That it was Jesus Himself they knew from the fact that He had been conversing with them (for had they seen only from a distance, they could not have recognized Him by sight), but that He is taken up into Heaven the Angels themselves inform them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:89
verses.text: Observe how it is ordered, that not all is done by the Spirit, but the eyes also do their part.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:90
verses.text: But why did "a cloud receive Him?" This too was a sure sign that He went up to Heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:91
verses.text: Not fire, as in the case of Elijah, nor fiery chariot, but "a cloud received Him;" which was a symbol of Heaven, as the Prophet says; "Who maketh the clouds His chariot" (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:92
verses.text: civ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:93
verses.text: ); it is of the Father Himself that this is said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:94
verses.text: Therefore he says, "on a cloud;" in the symbol, he would say, of the Divine power, for no other Power is seen to appear on a cloud.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:95
verses.text: For hear again what another Prophet says: "The Lord sitteth upon a light cloud" (Is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:96
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:97
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:98
verses.text: For it was while they were listening with great attention to what He was saying, and this in answer to a very interesting question, and with their minds fully aroused and quite awake, that this thing took place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:99
verses.text: Also on the mount Sinai the cloud was because of Him: since Moses also entered into the darkness, but the cloud there was not because of Moses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:100
verses.text: And He did not merely say, "I go," lest they should again grieve, but He said, "I send the Spirit" (John xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:101
verses.text: , ); and that He was going away into heaven they saw with their eyes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:102
verses.text: O what a sight they were granted! "And while they looked stedfastly," it is said, "toward heaven, as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel; which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? This same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven"—they used the expression "This" demonstratively, saying, "this Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall thus"—demonstratively, "in this way"—"come in like manner as ye have seen Him going into heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:103
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:104
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:105
verses.text: ) Again, the outward appearance is cheering "in white apparel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:106
verses.text: They were Angels, in the form of men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:107
verses.text: And they say, "Ye men of Galilee:" they showed themselves to be trusted by the disciples, by saying, "Ye men of Galilee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:108
verses.text: For this was the meaning: else, what needed they to be told of their country, who knew it well enough? By their appearance also they attracted their regard, and shewed that they were from heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:109
verses.text: But wherefore does not Christ Himself tell them these things, instead of the Angels? He had beforehand told them all things; "What if ye shall see the Son of Man going up where He was before?" (John vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:110
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:111
verses.text: Moreover the Angels did not say, 'whom you have seen taken up,' but, "going into heaven:" ascension is the word, not assumption; the expression "taken up," belongs to the flesh.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:112
verses.text: For the same reason they say, "He which is taken up from you shall thus come," not, "shall be sent," but, "shall come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:113
verses.text: He that ascended, the same is he also that descended" (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:114
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:116
verses.text: So again the expression, "a cloud received Him:" for He Himself mounted upon the cloud.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:117
verses.text: Of the expressions, some are adapted to the conceptions of the disciples, some agreeable with the Divine Majesty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:118
verses.text: Now, as they behold, their conceptions are elevated: He has given them no slight hint of the nature of His second coming.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:119
verses.text: For this, "Shall thus come," means, with the body; which thing they desired to hear; and, that he shall come again to judgment "thus" upon a cloud.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:120
verses.text: "And, behold, two men stood by them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:121
verses.text: Why is it said, "men?" Because they had fashioned themselves completely as such, that the beholders might not be overpowered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:122
verses.text: "Which also said:" their words moreover were calculated for soothing: "Why stand ye gazing up into heaven?" They would not let them any longer wait there for Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:123
verses.text: Here again, these tell what is greater, and leave the less unsaid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:124
verses.text: That "He will thus come," they say, and that "ye must look for Him from heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:125
verses.text: For the rest, they called them off from that spectacle to their saying, that they might not, because they could not see Him, imagine that He was not ascended, but even while they are conversing, would be present ere they were aware.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:126
verses.text: For if they said on a former occasion, "Whither goest Thou?" (John xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:127
verses.text: ) much more would they have said it now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:128
verses.text: "Wilt Thou at this time," say they, "restore the kingdom to Israel?" (Recapitulation).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:129
verses.text: They so well knew his mildness, that after His Passion also they ask Him, "Wilt thou restore?" And yet He had before said to them, "Ye shall hear of wars and rumors of wars, but the end is not yet," nor shall Jerusalem be taken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:130
verses.text: But now they ask Him about the kingdom, not about the end.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:131
verses.text: And besides, He does not speak at great length with them after the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:132
verses.text: They address then this question, as thinking that they themselves would be in high honor, if this should come to pass.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:133
verses.text: But He (for as touching this restoration, that it was not to be, He did not openly declare; for what needed they to learn this? hence they do not again ask, "What is the sign of Thy coming, and of the end of the world?" for they are afraid to say that: but, "Wilt Thou restore the kingdom to Israel?" for they thought there was such a kingdom), but He, I say, both in parables had shown that the time was not near, and here where they asked, and He answered thereto, "Ye shall receive power," says He, "when the Holy Ghost is come upon you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:134
verses.text: Is come upon you," not, "is sent," to shew the Spirit's coequal Majesty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:135
verses.text: How then darest thou, O opponent of the Spirit, to call Him a creature?.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:136
verses.text: "And ye shall be witnesses to Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:137
verses.text: He hinted at the Ascension.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:138
verses.text: "And when he had spoken these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:139
verses.text: Which they had heard before, and He now reminds them of.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:140
verses.text: "He was taken up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:141
verses.text: Already it has been shown, that He went up into heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:142
verses.text: "And a cloud, etc".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:143
verses.text: "Clouds and darkness are under His feet," (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:144
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:145
verses.text: ; xcvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:146
verses.text: ) saith the Scripture: for this is declared by the expression, "And a cloud received Him:" the Lord of heaven, it means.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:147
verses.text: For as a king is shown by the royal chariot, so was the royal chariot sent for Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:148
verses.text: "Behold, two men, etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:149
verses.text: That they may vent no sorrowful exclamations, and that it might not be with them as it was with Elisha, ( Kings ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:150
verses.text: ) who, when his master was taken up, rent his mantle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:151
verses.text: And what say they? "This Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall thus come".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:152
verses.text: And, "Behold, two men stood by them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:153
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:154
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:155
verses.text: ) With good reason: for "in the mouth of two witnesses shall every word be established" (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:156
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:157
verses.text: ): and these utter the same things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:158
verses.text: And it is said, that they were "in white apparel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:159
verses.text: In the same manner as they had already seen an Angel at the sepulchre, who had even told them their own thoughts; so here also an Angel is the preacher of His Ascension; although indeed the Prophets had frequently foretold it, as well as the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:160
verses.text: Everywhere it is Angels as at the Nativity, "for that which is conceived in her," saith one, "is by the Holy Ghost" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:161
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:162
verses.text: ): and again to Mary, "Fear not, Mary".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:163
verses.text: (Luke i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:164
verses.text: ) And at the Resurrection: "He is not here; He is risen, and goeth before you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:165
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:166
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:167
verses.text: ) "Come, and see!" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:168
verses.text: xxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:169
verses.text: ) And at the Second Coming.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:170
verses.text: For that they may not be utterly in amaze, therefore it is added, "Shall thus come".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:171
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:172
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:173
verses.text: ) They recover their breath a little; if indeed He shall come again, if also thus come, and not be unapproachable! And that expression also, that it is "from them" He is taken up, is not idly added.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:174
verses.text: And of the Resurrection indeed Christ Himself bears witness (because of all things this is, next to the Nativity, nay even above the Nativity, the most wonderful: His raising Himself to life again): for, "Destroy," He says, "this Temple, and in three days I will raise it up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:175
verses.text: (John ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:176
verses.text: ) "Shall thus come," say they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:177
verses.text: If any therefore desires to see Christ; if any grieves that he has not seen Him: having this heard, let him show forth an admirable life, and certainly he shall see Him, and shall not be disappointed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:178
verses.text: For Christ will come with greater glory, though "thus," in this manner, with a body; and much more wondrous will it be to see Him descending from heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:179
verses.text: But for what He will come, they do not add.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:180
verses.text: "Shall thus come," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:181
verses.text: This is a confirmation of the Resurrection; for if he was taken up with a body, much rather must He have risen again with a body.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:182
verses.text: Where are those who disbelieve the Resurrection? Who are they, I pray? Are they Gentiles, or Christians? for I am ignorant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:183
verses.text: But no, I know well: they are Gentiles, who also disbelieve the work of Creation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:184
verses.text: For the two denials go together: the denial that God creates any thing from nothing, and the denial that He raises up what has been buried.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:185
verses.text: But then, being ashamed to be thought such as "know not the power of God" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:186
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:187
verses.text: ), that we may not impute this to them, they allege: We do not say it with this meaning, but because there is no need of the body.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:188
verses.text: Truly it may be seasonably said, "The fool will speak foolishness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:189
verses.text: (Is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:190
verses.text: xxxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:191
verses.text: ) Are you not ashamed not to grant, that God can create from nothing? If he creates from matter already existing, wherein does He differ from men? But whence, you demand, are evils? Though you should not know whence, ought you for that to introduce another evil in the knowledge of evils? Hereupon two absurdities follow.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:192
verses.text: For if you do not grant, that from things which are not, God made the things which are, much more shall you be ignorant whence are evils: and then, again, you introduce another evil, the affirming that Evil (τὴν κακίαν) is uncreated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:193
verses.text: Consider now what a thing it is, when you wish to find the source of evils, to be both ignorant of it, and to add another to it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:194
verses.text: Search after the origin of evils, and do not blaspheme God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:195
verses.text: And how do I blaspheme? says he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:196
verses.text: When you make out that evils have a power equal to God's; a power uncreated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:197
verses.text: For, observe what Paul says; "For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:198
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:199
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:200
verses.text: ) But the devil would have both to be of matter, that there may be nothing left from which we may come to the knowledge of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:201
verses.text: For tell me, whether is harder: to take that which is by nature evil (if indeed there be ought such; for I speak upon your principles, since there is no such thing as evil by nature), and make it either good, or even coefficent of good? or, to make of nothing? Whether is easier (I speak of quality); to induce the non-existent quality; or to take the existing quality, and change it into its contrary? where there is no house, to make the house; or where it is utterly destroyed, to make it identically exist again? Why, as this is impossible, so is that: to make a thing into its opposite.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:202
verses.text: Tell me, whether is harder; to make a perfume, or to make filth have the effect of perfume? Say, whether of these is easier (since we subject God to our reasonings: nay, not we, but ye); to form eyes, or to make a blind man to see continuing blind, and yet more sharp-sighted, than one who does see? To make blindness into sight, and deafness into hearing? To me the other seems easier.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:203
verses.text: Say then do you grant God that which is harder, and not grant the easier? But souls also they affirm to be of His substance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:204
verses.text: Do you see what a number of impieties and absurdities are here! In the first place, wishing to show that evils are from God, they bring in another thing more impious than this, that they are equal with Him in majesty, and God prior in existence to none of them, assigning this great prerogative even to them! In the next place, they affirm evil to be indestructible: for if that which is uncreated can be destroyed, ye see the blasphemy! So that it comes to this, either that nothing is of God if not these; or that these are God! Thirdly, what I have before spoken of, in this point they defeat themselves, and prepare against themselves fresh indignation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:205
verses.text: Fourthly, they affirm unordered matter to possess such inherent (ἐπιτηδειότητα) power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:206
verses.text: Fifthly, that evil is the cause of the goodness of God, and that without this the Good had not been good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:207
verses.text: Sixthly, they bar against us the ways of attaining unto the knowledge of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:208
verses.text: Seventhly, they bring God down into men, yea plants and logs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:209
verses.text: For if our soul be of the substance of God, but the process of its transmigration into new bodies brings it at last into cucumbers, and melons, and onions, why then the substance of God will pass into cucumbers! And if we say, that the Holy Ghost fashioned the Temple of our Lord's body in the Virgin, they laugh us to scorn: and if, that He dwelt in that spiritual Temple, again they laugh; while they themselves are not ashamed to bring down God's substance into cucumbers, and melons, and flies, and caterpillars, and asses, thus excogitating a new fashion of idolatry: for let it not be as the Egyptians have it, "The onion is God;" but let it be, "God in the onion"! Why dost thou shrink from the notion of God's entering into a body? 'It is shocking,' says he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:210
verses.text: Why then this is much more shocking.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:211
verses.text: But, forsooth, it is not shocking—how should it be?—this same thing which is so, if it be into us! 'But thy notion is indeed shocking.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:212
verses.text: ' Do ye see the filthiness of their impiety?—But why do they not wish the body to be raised? And why do they say the body is evil? By what then, tell me, dost thou know God? by what hast thou the knowledge of existing things? The philosopher too: by means of what is he a philosopher, if the body does nothing towards it? Deaden the senses, and then learn something of the things one needs to know! What would be more foolish than a soul, if from the first it had the senses deadened? If the deadening of but a single part, I mean of the brain, becomes a marring of it altogether; if all the rest should be deadened, what would it be good for? Show me a soul without a body.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:213
verses.text: Do you not hear physicians say, The presence of disease sadly enfeebles the soul? How long will ye put off hanging yourselves? Is the body material? tell me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:214
verses.text: "To be sure, it is".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:215
verses.text: Then you ought to hate it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:216
verses.text: Why do you feed, why cherish it? You ought to get quit of this prison.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:217
verses.text: But besides: "God cannot overcome matter, unless he (συμπλακἥ) implicate himself with it: for he cannot issue orders to it (O feebleness!) until he close with it, and (σταθἥ) take his stand (say you) through the whole of it!" And a king indeed does all by commanding; but God, not by commanding the evil! In short, if it were unparticipant of all good, it could not subsist at all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:218
verses.text: For Evil cannot subsist, unless it lay hold upon somewhat of the accidents of Virtue: so that if it had been heretofore all unmixed with virtue, it would have perished long ago: for such is the condition of evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:219
verses.text: Let there be a profligate man, let him put upon himself no restraint whatever, will he live ten days? Let there be a robber, and devoid of all conscience in his dealings with every one, let him be such even to his fellow-robbers, will he be able to live? Let there be a thief, void of all shame, who knows not what blushing is, but steals openly in public.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:220
verses.text: It is not in the nature of evils to subsist, unless they get some small share at least in good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:221
verses.text: So that hereupon, according to these men, God gave them their subsistence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:222
verses.text: Let there be a city of wicked men; will it stand? But let them be wicked, not only with regard to the good, but towards each other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:223
verses.text: Why, it is impossible such a city should stand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:224
verses.text: Truly, "professing themselves to be wise, they became fools".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:225
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:226
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:227
verses.text: ) If bodily substance be evil, then all things visible exist idly, and in vain, both water and earth, and sun, and air; for air is also body, though not solid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:228
verses.text: It is in point then to say, "The wicked have told me foolish things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:229
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:230
verses.text: cxix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:231
verses.text: ) But let not us endure them, let us block up our ears against them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:232
verses.text: For there is, yea, there is, a resurrection of bodies.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:233
verses.text: This the sepulchre which is at Jerusalem declares, this the pillar to which He was bound, when He was scourged.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:234
verses.text: For, "We did eat and drink with Him," it is said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 2:235
verses.text: Let us then believe in the Resurrection, and do things worthy of it, that we may attain to the good things which are to come, through Christ Jesus our Lord, with Whom to the Father, and the Holy Ghost together, be power, honor, now and for ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:1
verses.text: Homily III.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:2
verses.text: Acts I.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:3
verses.text: "Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day's journey".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:4
verses.text: "Then returned they," it is said: namely, when they had heard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:5
verses.text: For they could not have borne it, if the angel had not (ὑπερέθετο) referred them to another Coming.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:6
verses.text: It seems to me, that it was also on a sabbath-day that these things took place; for he would not thus have specified the distance, saying, "from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day's journey," unless they were then going on the sabbath-day a certain definite distance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:7
verses.text: "And when they were come in," it says, "they went up into an upper room, where they were making their abode:" so they then remained in Jerusalem after the Resurrection: "both Peter, and James, and John:" no longer is only the latter together with his brother mentioned, but together with Peter the two: "and Andrew, and Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, and James (the son) of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas, (the brother) of James".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:8
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:9
verses.text: ) He has done well to mention the disciples: for since one had betrayed Christ, and another had been unbelieving, he thereby shows that, except the first, all of them were preserved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:10
verses.text: "These were all continuing with one accord in prayer together with the women".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:12
verses.text: ) For this is a powerful weapon in temptations; and to this they had been trained.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:13
verses.text: "Continuing with one accord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:14
verses.text: Good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:15
verses.text: (καλὥς).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:16
verses.text: Besides, the present temptation directed them to this: for they exceedingly feared the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:17
verses.text: "With the women," it is said: for he had said that they had followed Him: "and with Mary the mother of Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:18
verses.text: (Luke xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:19
verses.text: ) How then is it said, that "that disciple" took her to his own home" (John xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:20
verses.text: ), at that time? But then the Lord had brought them together again, and so returned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:21
verses.text: "And with His brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:22
verses.text: (John xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:23
verses.text: ) These also were before unbelieving.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:24
verses.text: "And in those days," it says, "Peter stood up in the midst of the disciples, and said".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:26
verses.text: ) Both as being ardent, and as having been put in trust by Christ with the flock, and as having precedence in honor, he always begins the discourse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:27
verses.text: ("The number of the names together were about an hundred and twenty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:28
verses.text: ) Men and brethren," he says, "this Scripture must needs have been fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost spake before," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:30
verses.text: ) Why did he not ask Christ to give him some one in the room of Judas? It is better as it is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:31
verses.text: For in the first place, they were engaged in other things; secondly, of Christ's presence with them, the greatest proof that could be given was this: as He had chosen when He was among them, so did He now being absent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:32
verses.text: Now this was no small matter for their consolation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:33
verses.text: But observe how Peter does everything with the common consent; nothing imperiously.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:34
verses.text: And he does not speak thus without a meaning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:35
verses.text: But observe how he consoles them concerning what had passed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:36
verses.text: In fact, what had happened had caused them no small consternation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:37
verses.text: For if there are many now who canvass this circumstance, what may we suppose they had to say then?  "Men and brethren," says Peter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:38
verses.text: For if the Lord called them brethren, much more may he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:39
verses.text: "Men," he says: they all being present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:40
verses.text: See the dignity of the Church, the angelic condition! No distinction there, "neither male nor female".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:41
verses.text: I would that the Churches were such now! None there had his mind full of some worldly matter, none was anxiously thinking about household concerns.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:42
verses.text: Such a benefit are temptations, such the advantage of afflictions!  "This Scripture," says he, "must needs have been fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost spake before".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:43
verses.text: Always he comforts them by the prophecies.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:44
verses.text: So does Christ on all occasions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:45
verses.text: In the very same way, he shows here that no strange thing had happened, but what had already been foretold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:46
verses.text: "This Scripture must needs have been fulfilled," he says, "which the Holy Ghost by the mouth of David spake before".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:47
verses.text: He does not say, David, but the Spirit through him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:48
verses.text: See what kind of doctrine the writer has at the very outset of the book.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:49
verses.text: Do you see, that it was not for nothing that I said in the beginning of this work, that this book is the Polity of the Holy Spirit? "Which the Holy Ghost spake before by the mouth of David".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:50
verses.text: Observe how he appropriates (οἰκειοὕται) him; and that it is an advantage to them, that this was spoken by David, and not by some other Prophet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:51
verses.text: "Concerning Judas," he says, "which was guide".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:52
verses.text: Here again mark the philosophical temper of the man: how he does not mention him with scorn, nor say, "that wretch," "that miscreant:" but simply states the fact; and does not even say, "who betrayed Him," but does what he can to transfer the guilt to others: nor does he animadvert severely even on these: "Which was guide," he says, "to them that took Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:53
verses.text: Furthermore, before he declares where David had spoken, he relates what had been the case with Judas, that from the things present he may fetch assurance of the things future, and show that this man had already received his due.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:54
verses.text: "For he was numbered," says he, "with us, and had obtained part of this ministry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:55
verses.text: Now this man acquired a field out of the reward of iniquity".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:56
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:57
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:58
verses.text: ) He gives his discourse a moral turn, and covertly mentions the cause of the wickedness, because it carried reproof with it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:59
verses.text: And he does not say, The Jews, but, "this man, acquired" it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:60
verses.text: For since the minds of weak persons do not attend to things future, as they do to things present, he discourses of the immediate punishment inflicted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:61
verses.text: "And falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:62
verses.text: He does well to dilate not upon the sin, but upon the punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:63
verses.text: "And," he says, "all his bowels gushed out".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:64
verses.text: This brought them consolation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:65
verses.text: "And it was known unto all the dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue Aceldama, that is to say, the field of blood".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:66
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:67
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:68
verses.text: Now the Jews gave it this name, not on this account, but because of Judas; here, however, Peter makes it to have this reference, and when he brings forward the adversaries as witnesses, both by the fact that they named it, and by saying, "in their proper tongue," this is what he means.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:69
verses.text: Then after the event, he appositely brings in the Prophet, saying, "For it is written in the Book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:70
verses.text: ) (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:71
verses.text: lxix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:72
verses.text: ): this is said of the field and the dwelling: "And his bishopric let another take; that is, his office, his priesthood.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:73
verses.text: So that this, he says, is not my counsel, but His who hath foretold these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:74
verses.text: For, that he may not seem to be undertaking a great thing, and just such as Christ had done, he adduces the Prophet as a witness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:75
verses.text: "Wherefore it behooves of these men which have companied with us all the time".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:76
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:77
verses.text: ) Why does he make it their business too? That the matter might not become an object of strife, and they might not fall into contention about it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:78
verses.text: For if the Apostles themselves once did this, much more might those.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:79
verses.text: This he ever avoids.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:80
verses.text: Wherefore at the beginning he said, "Men and brethren.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:81
verses.text: It behooves" to choose from among you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:82
verses.text: He defers the decision to the whole body, thereby both making the elected objects of reverence and himself keeping clear of all invidiousness with regard to the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:83
verses.text: For such occasions always give rise to great evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:84
verses.text: Now that some one must needs be appointed, he adduces the prophet as witness: but from among what persons: "Of these," he says, "which have companied with us all the time".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:85
verses.text: To have said, the worthy must present themselves, would have been to insult the others; but now he refers the matter to length of time; for he says not simply, "These who have companied with us," but, "all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, beginning from the baptism of John unto that same day that He was taken up from us, must one be ordained to be a witness with us of His resurrection" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:86
verses.text: ): that their college (ὁ χορὸς) might not be left mutilated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:87
verses.text: Then why did it not rest with Peter to make the election himself: what was the motive? This; that he might not seem to bestow it of favor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:88
verses.text: And besides, he was not yet endowed with the spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:89
verses.text: "And they appointed two, Joseph called Barsabus, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:90
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:91
verses.text: ) Not he appointed them: but it was he that introduced the proposition to that effect, at the same time pointing out that even this was not his own, but from old time by prophecy; so that he acted as expositor, not as preceptor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:92
verses.text: "Joseph called Barsabus, who was surnamed Justus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:93
verses.text: Perhaps both names are given, because there were others of the same name, for among the Apostles also there were several names alike; as James, and James (the son) of Alphaeus; Simon Peter, and Simon Zelotes; Judas (the brother) of James, and Judas Iscariot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:94
verses.text: The appellation, however, may have arisen from a change of life, and very likely also of the moral character.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:95
verses.text: "They appointed two," it is said, "Joseph called Barsabus, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:96
verses.text: And they prayed, and said; Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, show whether of these two thou hast chosen, that he may take part of this ministry and Apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:97
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:98
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:99
verses.text: ) They do well to mention the sin of Judas, thereby showing that it is a witness they ask to have; not increasing the number, but not suffering it to be diminished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:100
verses.text: "And they gave forth their lots" (for the spirit was not yet sent), "and the lot fell upon Matthias: and he was numbered with the eleven Apostles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:101
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:102
verses.text: )  "Then," it says, "returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet (Recapitulation), "which is nigh to Jerusalem, at the distance of a sabbath-day's journey:" so that there was no long way to go, to be a cause of alarm to them while yet trembling and fearful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:103
verses.text: "And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:104
verses.text: They durst not appear in the town.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:105
verses.text: They also did well to go up into an upper room, as it became less easy to arrest them at once.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:106
verses.text: "And they continued," it is said, "with one accord in prayer".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:107
verses.text: Do you see how watchful they were? "Continuing in prayer," and "with one accord," as it were with one soul, continuing therein: two things reported in their praise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:108
verses.text: "Where they were abiding," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:109
verses.text: , to, "And Mary the Mother of Jesus and His brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:110
verses.text: Now Joseph perhaps was dead: for it is not to be supposed that when the brethren had become believers, Joseph believed not; he who in fact had believed before any.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:111
verses.text: Certain it is that we nowhere find him looking upon Christ as man merely.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:112
verses.text: As where His mother said, "Thy father and I did seek thee sorrowing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:113
verses.text: (Luke ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:114
verses.text: ) And upon another occasion, it was said, "Thy mother and thy brethren seek thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:115
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:116
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:117
verses.text: ) So that Joseph knew this before all others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:118
verses.text: And to them the brethren Christ said, "The world cannot hate you, but Me it hateth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:119
verses.text: (John vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:120
verses.text: )  Again, consider the moderation of James.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:121
verses.text: He it was who received the Bishopric of Jerusalem, and here he says nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:122
verses.text: Mark also the great moderation of the other Apostles, how they concede the throne to him, and no longer dispute with each other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:123
verses.text: For that Church was as it were in heaven: having nothing to do with this world's affairs: and resplendent not with wails, no, nor with numbers, but with the zeal of them that formed the assembly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:124
verses.text: They were "about an hundred and twenty," it says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:125
verses.text: The seventy perhaps whom Christ Himself had chosen, and other of the more earnest-minded disciples, as Joseph and Matthias.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:126
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:127
verses.text: ) There were women, he says, many, who followed Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:128
verses.text: (Mark xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:129
verses.text: ) "The number of the names together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:130
verses.text: Together" they were on all occasions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:131
verses.text: "Men and brethren," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:132
verses.text: Here is forethought for providing a teacher; here was the first who ordained a teacher.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:133
verses.text: He did not say, 'We are sufficient.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:134
verses.text: ' So far was he beyond all vain-glory, and he looked to one thing alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:135
verses.text: And yet he had the same power to ordain as they all collectively.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:136
verses.text: But well might these things be done in this fashion, through the noble spirit of the man, and because prelacy then was not an affair of dignity, but of provident care for the governed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:137
verses.text: This neither made the elected to become elated, for it was to dangers that they were called, nor those not elected to make a grievance of it, as if they were disgraced.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:138
verses.text: But things are not done in this fashion now; nay, quite the contrary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:139
verses.text: —For observe, they were an hundred and twenty, and he asks for one out of the whole body: with good right, as having been put in charge of them: for to him had Christ said, "And when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:140
verses.text: (Luke xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:141
verses.text: , Ben.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:142
verses.text: )  "For he was numbered with us," (πρὥτος τοῦ πράγματος αὐθεντει absent from A.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:143
verses.text: B.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:144
verses.text: C ) says Peter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:145
verses.text: On this account it behooves to propose another; to be a witness in his place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:146
verses.text: And see how he imitates his Master, ever discoursing from the Scriptures, and saying nothing as yet concerning Christ; namely, that He had frequently predicted this Himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:147
verses.text: Nor does he mention where the Scripture speaks of the treachery of Judas; for instance, "The mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me" (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:148
verses.text: cix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:149
verses.text: ); but where it speaks only of his punishment; for this was most to their advantage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:150
verses.text: It shows again the benevolence of the Lord: "For he was numbered with us" (τοὕτο γὰρ αὐτοὺς μάλιστα ὡφέλει· Δείκνυσι πάλιν A.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:151
verses.text: B.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:152
verses.text: C ), he says, "and obtained his lot of this ministry".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:153
verses.text: He calls it everywhere "lot," showing that the whole is from God's grace and election, and reminding them of the old times, inasmuch as God chose him into His own lot or portion, as of old He took the Levites.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:154
verses.text: He also dwells upon the circumstances respecting Judas, showing that the reward of the treachery was made itself the herald of the punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:155
verses.text: For he "acquired," he says, "a field out of the reward of the iniquity".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:156
verses.text: Observe the divine economy in the event.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:157
verses.text: "Of the iniquity," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:158
verses.text: For there are many iniquities, but never was anything more iniquitous than this: so that the affair was one of iniquity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:159
verses.text: Now not only to those who were present did the event become known, but to all thereafter, so that without meaning or knowing what they were about, they gave it a name; just as Caiaphas had prophesied unconsciously.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:160
verses.text: God compelled them to call the field in Hebrew "Aceldama".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:161
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:162
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:163
verses.text: ) By this also the evils which were to come upon the Jews were declared: and Peter shows the prophecy to have been so far in part fulfilled, which says, "It had been good for that man if he had not been born".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:164
verses.text: We may with propriety apply this same to the Jews likewise; for if he who was guide suffered thus, much more they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:165
verses.text: Thus far however Peter says nothing of this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:166
verses.text: Then, showing that the term, "Aceldama," might well be applied to his fate, he introduces the prophet, saying, "Let his habitation be desolate".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:167
verses.text: For what can be worse desolation than to become a place of burial? And the field may well be called his.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:168
verses.text: For he who cast down the price, although others were the buyers, has a right to be himself reckoned owner of a great desolation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:169
verses.text: This desolation was the prelude to that of the Jews, as will appear on looking closely into the facts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:170
verses.text: For indeed they destroyed themselves by famine, and killed many, and the city became a burial-place of strangers, of soldiers, for as to those, they would not even have let them be buried, for in fact they were not deemed worthy of sepulture.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:171
verses.text: "Wherefore of these men which have companied with us," continues Peter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:172
verses.text: Observe how desirous he is they should be eye-witnesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:173
verses.text: It is true indeed that the Spirit would shortly come; and yet great care is shown with regard to this circumstance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:174
verses.text: "Of these men," he says, "which have companied with us, all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:175
verses.text: He shows that they had dwelt with Christ, not simply been present as disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:176
verses.text: In fact, from the very beginning there were many that then followed Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:177
verses.text: Observe, for instance, how this appears in these words: "One of the two which heard John speak, and followed Jesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:178
verses.text: —All the time," he says, "that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, beginning from the baptism of John".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:179
verses.text: (John i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:180
verses.text: ) True! for no one knew what preceded that event, though they did learn it by the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:181
verses.text: "Unto that same day that He was taken up from us, must one be ordained to be a witness with us of His resurrection".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:182
verses.text: He said not, a witness of the rest of his actions, but a witness of the resurrection alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:183
verses.text: For indeed that witness had a better right to be believed, who was able to declare, that He Who ate and drank, and was crucified, the same rose again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:184
verses.text: Wherefore it was needed that he should be a witness, not only of the time preceding this event, nor only of what followed it, and of the miracles; the thing required was, the resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:185
verses.text: For the other matters were manifest and acknowledged, but the resurrection took place in secret, and was manifest to these only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:186
verses.text: And they do not say, Angels have told us; but, We have seen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:187
verses.text: For this it was that was most needful at that time: that they should be men having a right to be believed, because they had seen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:188
verses.text: "And they appointed two," it is said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:189
verses.text: Why not many? That the feeling of disappointment might not reach further, extending to many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:190
verses.text: Again, it is not without reason that he puts Matthias last; he would show, that frequently he that is honourable among men, is inferior before God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:191
verses.text: And they all pray in common saying, "Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, show.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:192
verses.text: Thou," not "We".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:193
verses.text: And very seasonably they use the epithet, "heart-knowing:" for by Him Who is this must the choice be made.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:194
verses.text: So confident were they, that assuredly one of them must be appointed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:195
verses.text: They said not, Choose, but, "Show the chosen one;" knowing that all things were foreordained of God; "Whom Thou didst choose: one of these two," say they, "to have his lot in this ministry and apostleship".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:196
verses.text: For there was besides another ministry (διακονία).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:197
verses.text: "And they gave them their lots".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:198
verses.text: For they did not yet consider themselves to be worthy to be informed by some sign.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:199
verses.text: And besides, if in a case where neither prayer was made, nor men of worth were the agents, the casting of lots so much availed, because it was done of a right intention, I mean in the case of Jonah (Jonah i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:200
verses.text: ); much more did it here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:201
verses.text: Thus, did he, the designated, fill up the company, complete the order: but the other candidate was not annoyed; for the apostolic writers would not have concealed that or any other failings of their own, seeing they have told of the very chief Apostles, that on other occasions they had indignation (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:202
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:203
verses.text: ; Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:204
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:205
verses.text: ), and this not once only, but again and again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:206
verses.text: Let us then also imitate them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:207
verses.text: And now I address no longer every one, but those who aim at preferment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:208
verses.text: If thou believest that the election is with God, be not displeased.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:209
verses.text: (Mark x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:210
verses.text: , ; xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:211
verses.text: ) For it is with Him thou art displeased, and with Him thou art exasperated: it is He who has made the choice; thou doest the very thing that Cain did; because, forsooth, his brother's sacrifice was preferred, he was indignant, when he ought to have felt compunction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:212
verses.text: However, that is not what I mean here; but this, that God knows how to dispense things for the best.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:213
verses.text: In many cases, thou art in point of disposition more estimable than the other but not the fit person.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:214
verses.text: Besides, on the other hand, thy life is irreproachable, and thy habits those of a well-nurtured man, but in the Church this is not all that is wanted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:215
verses.text: Moreover, one man is adapted for one thing, another for another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:216
verses.text: Do you not observe, how much discourse the holy Scripture has made on this matter? But let me say why it is that the thing has become a subject of competition: it is because we come to the Episcopate not as unto a work of governing and superintending the brethren, but as to a post of dignity and repose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:217
verses.text: Did you but know that a Bishop is bound to belong to all, to bear the burden of all; that others, if they are angry, are pardoned, but he never; that others, if they sin, have excuses made for them, he has none; you would not be eager for the dignity, would not run after it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:218
verses.text: So it is, the Bishop is exposed to the tongues of all, to the criticism of all, whether they be wise or fools.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:219
verses.text: He is harassed with cares every day, nay, every night.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:220
verses.text: He has many to hate him, many to envy him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:221
verses.text: Talk not to me of those who curry favor with all, of those who desire to sleep, of those who advance to this office as for repose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:222
verses.text: We have nothing to do with these; we speak of those who watch for your souls, who consider the safety and welfare of those under them before their own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:223
verses.text: Tell me now: suppose a man has ten children, always living with him, and constantly under his control; yet is he solicitous about them; and a bishop, who has such numbers, not living under the same roof with him, but owing obedience to his authority—what does he not need to be! But he is honored, you will say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:224
verses.text: With what sort of honor, indeed! Why, the paupers and beggars abuse him openly in the market-place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:225
verses.text: And why does he not stop their mouths then? Yes, very proper work, this, for a bishop, is it not? Then again, if he do not give to all, the idle and the industrious alike, lo! a thousand complaints on all sides.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:226
verses.text: None is afraid to accuse him, and speak evil of him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:227
verses.text: In the case of civil governors, fear steps in; with bishops, nothing of the kind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:228
verses.text: As for the fear of God, it does not influence people, as regards them, in the least degree.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:229
verses.text: Why speak of the anxiety connected with the word and doctrine? the painful work in Ordinations? Either, perhaps, I am a poor wretched incompetent creature, or else, the case is as I say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:230
verses.text: The soul of a Bishop is for all the world like a vessel in a storm: lashed from every side, by friends, by foes, by one's own people, by strangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:231
verses.text: Does not the Emperor rule the whole world, the Bishop a single city? Yet a Bishop's anxieties are as much beyond those of the emperor, as the waters of a river simply moved, by the wind are surpassed in agitation by the swelling and raging sea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:232
verses.text: And why? because in the one case there are many to lend a hand, for all goes on by law and by rule; but in the other there is none of this, nor is there authority to command; but if one be greatly moved, then he is harsh; if the contrary, then he is cold! And in him these opposites must meet, that he may neither be despised, nor be hated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:233
verses.text: Besides, the very demands of business preoccupy him: how many is he obliged to offend, whether he will or not! How many to be severe with! I speak not otherwise than it is, but as I find it in my own actual experience.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:234
verses.text: I do not think there are many among Bishops that will be saved, but many more that perish: and the reason is, that it is an affair that requires a great mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:235
verses.text: Many are the exigencies which throw a man out of his natural temper; and he had need have a thousand eyes on all sides.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:236
verses.text: Do you not see what a number of qualifications the Bishop must have? to be apt to teach, patient, holding fast the faithful word in doctrine (see  Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:237
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:238
verses.text: –; Tit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:239
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:240
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:241
verses.text: What trouble and pains does this require! And then, others do wrong, and he bears all the blame.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:242
verses.text: To pass over every thing else: if one soul depart unbaptized, does not this subvert all his own prospect of salvation? The loss of one soul carries with it a penalty which no language can represent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:243
verses.text: For if the salvation of that soul was of such value, that the Son of God became man, and suffered so much, think how sore a punishment must the losing of it bring! And if in this present life he who is cause of another's destruction is worthy of death, much more in the next world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:244
verses.text: Do not tell me, that the presbyter is in fault, or the deacon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:245
verses.text: The guilt of all these comes perforce upon the head of those who ordained them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:246
verses.text: Let me mention another instance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:247
verses.text: It chances, that a bishop has inherited from his predecessor a set of persons of indifferent character.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:248
verses.text: What measures is it proper to take in respect of bygone transgressions (for here are two precipices) so as not to let the offender go unpunished, and not to cause scandal to the rest? Must one's first step be to cut him off? There is no actual present ground for that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:249
verses.text: But is it right to let him go unmarked? Yes, say you; for the fault rests with the bishop who ordained him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:250
verses.text: Well then? must one refuse to ordain him again, and to raise him to a higher degree of the ministry? That would be to publish it to all men, that he is a person of indifferent character, and so again one would cause scandal in a different way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:251
verses.text: But is one to promote him to a higher degree? That is much worse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:252
verses.text: If then there were only the responsibility of the office itself for people to run after in the episcopate, none would be so quick to accept it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:253
verses.text: But as things go, we run after this, just as we do after the dignities of the world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:254
verses.text: That we may have glory with men, we lose ourselves with God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:255
verses.text: What profit in such honor? How self-evident its nothingness is! When you covet the episcopal rank, put in the other scale, the account to be rendered after this life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:256
verses.text: Weigh against it, the happiness of a life free from toil, take into account the different measure of the punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:257
verses.text: I mean, that even if you have sinned, but in your own person merely, you will have no such great punishment, nothing like it: but if you have sinned as bishop, you are lost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:258
verses.text: Remember what Moses endured, what wisdom he displayed, what good deeds he exhibited: but, for committing one sin only, he was bitterly punished; and with good reason; for this fault was attended with injury to the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:259
verses.text: Not in regard that the sin was public, but because it was the sin of a spiritual Ruler (ίερέως) cf.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:260
verses.text: S.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:261
verses.text: ); for in truth we do not pay the same penalty for public and for hidden faults.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:262
verses.text: (Aug in Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:263
verses.text: xcix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:264
verses.text: ) The sin may be the same, but not the (ζημία) harm of it; nay, not the sin itself; for it is not the same thing to sin in secret and unseen, and to sin openly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:265
verses.text: But the bishop cannot sin unobserved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:266
verses.text: Well for him if he escape reproach, though he sin not; much less can he think to escape notice, if he do sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:267
verses.text: Let him be angry, let him laugh, or let him but dream of a moment's relaxation, many are they that scoff, many that are offended, many that lay down the law, many that bring to mind the former bishops, and abuse the present one; not that they wish to sound the praise of those; no, it is only to carp at him that they bring up the mention of fellow-bishops, of presbyters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:268
verses.text: Sweet, says the proverb, is war to the inexperienced; but it may rather be said now, that even after one has come out of it, people in general have seen nothing of it: for in their eyes it is not war, but like those shepherds in Ezekiel, we slay and devour.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:269
verses.text: (Ezek.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:270
verses.text: xxxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:271
verses.text: ) Which of us has it in his power to show that he has taken as much care for the flocks of Christ, as Jacob did for Laban's? (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:272
verses.text: xxxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:273
verses.text: ) Which of us can tell of the frost of the night? For talk not to me of vigils, and all that parade.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:274
verses.text: The contrary plainly is the fact.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:275
verses.text: Prefects, and governors (ὕπαρχοι καὶ τοπάρχαι) of provinces, do not enjoy such honour as he that governs the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:276
verses.text: If he enter the palace, who but he is first? If he go to see ladies, or visit the houses of the great, none is preferred to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:277
verses.text: The whole state of things is ruined and corrupt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:278
verses.text: I do not speak thus as wishing to put us bishops to shame, but to repress your hankering after the office.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:279
verses.text: For with what conscience, (even should you succeed in becoming a bishop, having made interest for it either in person or by another), with what eyes will you look the man in the face who worked with you to that end? What will you have to plead for your excuse? For he that unwillingly, by compulsion and not with his own consent, was raised to the office, may have something to say for himself, though for the most part even such an one has no pardon to expect, and yet truly he so far has something to plead in excuse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:280
verses.text: Think how it fared with Simon Magus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:281
verses.text: What signifies it that you give not money, if, in place of money, you pay court, you lay many plans, you set engines to work? "Thy money perish with thee!" (Acts viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:282
verses.text: ) Thus was it said to him, and thus will it be said to these: your canvassing perish with you, because you have thought to purchase the gift of God by human intrigue! But there is none such here? And God forbid there should be! For it is not that I wish any thing of what I have been saying to be applicable to you: but just now the connexion has led us on to these topics.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:283
verses.text: In like manner when we talk against covetousness, we are not preaching at you, no, nor against any one man personally.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:284
