verses.text: God grant it may be the case, that these remedies were prepared by us without necessity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:285
verses.text: The wish of the physician is, that after all his pains, his drugs may be thrown away because not wanted: and this is just what we desire, that our words may not have been needed, and so have been spoken to the wind, so as to be but words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:286
verses.text: I am ready to submit to anything, rather than be reduced to the necessity of using this language.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:287
verses.text: But if you like, we are ready to leave off; only let our silence be without bad effects.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:288
verses.text: No one, I imagine, though he were ever so vainglorious, would wish to make a display of severity, when there is nothing to call for it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:289
verses.text: I will leave the teaching to you: for that is the best teaching, which teaches by actions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:290
verses.text: For indeed the best physicians, although the sickness of their patients brings them in fees, would rather their friends were well.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:291
verses.text: And so we too wish all to be well.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:292
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:293
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:294
verses.text: ) It is not that we desire to be approved, and you reproved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:295
verses.text: I would gladly manifest, if it were possible, with my very eyes, the love which I bear to you: for then no one would be able to reproach me, though my language were ever so rough.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:296
verses.text: "For speech of friends, yea, were it insult, can be borne;" more "faithful are the wounds of a friend, rather than the ready kisses of an enemy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:297
verses.text: (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:298
verses.text: xxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:299
verses.text: ) There nothing I love more than you, no, not even light itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:300
verses.text: I would gladly have my eyes put out ten thousand times over, if it were possible by this means to convert your souls; so much is your salvation dearer to me than light itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:301
verses.text: For what profit to me in the rays of the sun, when despondency on your account makes it all thick darkness before my eyes? Light is good when it shines in cheerfulness, to a sorrowful heart it seems even to be a trouble.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:302
verses.text: How true this is, may you never learn by experience! However, if it happen to any of you to fall into sin, just stand by my bedside, when I am laid down to rest and should be asleep; see whether I am not like a palsied man, like one beside himself, and, in the language of the prophet, "the light of mine eyes, it also is gone from me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:303
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:304
verses.text: xxxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:305
verses.text: ) For where is our hope, if you do not make progress? where our despondency, if you do excellently? I seem to have wings, when I hear any thing good of you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:306
verses.text: "Fulfil ye my joy".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:307
verses.text: (Phil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:308
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:309
verses.text: ) This one thing is the burden of my prayers, that I long for your advancement.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:310
verses.text: But that in which I strive with all is this, that I love you, that I am wrapped up in you, that you are my all, father, mother, brethren, children.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:311
verses.text: Think not then that any thing that has been said was said in a hostile spirit, nay, it is for your amendment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:312
verses.text: It is written "A brother assisted by his brother is as a strong city".

verses.text: (Prov.

verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:315
verses.text: ) Then do not take it in disdain: for neither do I undervalue what you have to say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:316
verses.text: I should wish even to be set right by you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:317
verses.text: For all (Edd.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:318
verses.text: 'all we') ye are brethren, and One is our Master: yet even among brothers it is for one to direct, while the others obey.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 3:319
verses.text: Then disdain it not, but let us do all to the glory of God, for to Him belongs glory for ever and ever, Amen.

verses.text: Homily IV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:3
verses.text: ,  "And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:4
verses.text: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:5
verses.text: Dost thou perceive the type? What is this Pentecost? The time when the sickle was to be put to the harvest, and the ingathering was made.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:6
verses.text: See now the reality, when the time was come to put in the sickle of the word: for here, as the sickle, keen-edged, came the Spirit down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:7
verses.text: For hear the words of Christ: "Lift up your eyes," He said, "and look on the fields, for they are white already to harvest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:8
verses.text: (John iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:9
verses.text: ) And again, "The harvest truly is great, but the laborers are few".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:10
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:11
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:12
verses.text: ) But as the first-fruits of this harvest, He himself took our nature, and bore it up on high.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:13
verses.text: Himself first put in the sickle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:14
verses.text: Therefore also He calls the Word the Seed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:15
verses.text: "When," it says, "the day of Pentecost was fully come" (Luke viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:16
verses.text: , ): that is, when at the Pentecost, while about it, in short.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:17
verses.text: For it was essential that the present events likewise should take place during the feast, that those who had witnessed the crucifixion of Christ, might also behold these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:18
verses.text: "And suddenly there came a sound from heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:20
verses.text: ) Why did this not come to pass without sensible tokens? For this reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:21
verses.text: If even when the fact was such, men said, "They are full of new wine," what would they not have said, had it been otherwise? And it is not merely, "there came a sound," but, "from heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:22
verses.text: And the suddenness also startled them, and brought all together to the spot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:23
verses.text: "As of a rushing mighty wind:" this betokens the exceeding vehemence of the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:24
verses.text: "And it filled all the house:" insomuch that those present both believed, and (Edd.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:25
verses.text: τούτους) in this manner were shown to be worthy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:26
verses.text: Nor is this all; but what is more awful still, "And there appeared unto them," it says, "cloven tongues like as of fire".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:28
verses.text: ) Observe how it is always, "like as;" and rightly: that you may have no gross sensible notions of the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:29
verses.text: Also, "as it were of a blast:" therefore it was not a wind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:30
verses.text: "Like as of fire".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:31
verses.text: For when the Spirit was to be made known to John, then it came upon the head of Christ as in the form of a dove: but now, when a whole multitude was to be converted, it is "like as of fire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:32
verses.text: And it sat upon each of them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:33
verses.text: This means, that it remained and rested upon them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:34
verses.text: For the sitting is significant of settledness and continuance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:35
verses.text: Was it upon the twelve that it came? Not so; but upon the hundred and twenty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:36
verses.text: For Peter would not have quoted to no purpose the testimony of the prophet, saying, "And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith the Lord God, I will pour out of My spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:37
verses.text: (Joel ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:38
verses.text: ) "And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:40
verses.text: ) For, that the effect may not be to frighten only, therefore is it both "with the Holy Ghost, and with fire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:41
verses.text: And began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:42
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:43
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:44
verses.text: ) They receive no other sign, but this first; for it was new to them, and there was no need of any other sign.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:45
verses.text: "And it sat upon each of them," says the writer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:46
verses.text: Observe now, how there is no longer any occasion for that person to grieve, who was not elected as was Matthias, "And they were all filled," he says; not merely received the grace of the Spirit, but "were filled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:47
verses.text: And began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:48
verses.text: It would not have been said, All, the Apostles also being there present, unless the rest also were partakers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:49
verses.text: For were it not so, having above made mention of the Apostles distinctively and by name, he would not now have put them all in one with the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:50
verses.text: For if, where it was only to be mentioned that they were present, he makes mention of the Apostles apart, much more would he have done so in the case here supposed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:51
verses.text: Observe, how when one is continuing in prayer, when one is in charity, then it is that the Spirit draws near.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:52
verses.text: It put them in mind also of another vision: for as fire did He appear also in the bush.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:53
verses.text: "As the Spirit gave them utterance, ἀποφθέγγεσθαι (Exod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:54
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:55
verses.text: ) For the things spoken by them were ἀποφθέγματα, profound utterances.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:56
verses.text: "And," it says, "there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:57
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:58
verses.text: ) The fact of their dwelling there was a sign of piety: that being of so many nations they should have left country, and home, and relations, and be abiding there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:59
verses.text: For, it says, "There were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:60
verses.text: Now when this was noised abroad, the multitude came together, and were confounded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:61
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:62
verses.text: ) Since the event had taken place in a house, of course they came together from without.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:63
verses.text: The multitude was confounded: was all in commotion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:64
verses.text: They marvelled; "Because that every man heard them speak in his own language.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:65
verses.text: And they were amazed," it says, "and marvelled, saying one to another, Behold, are not all these which speak Galileans?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:66
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:67
verses.text: ) They immediately turned their eyes towards the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:68
verses.text: "And how" (it follows) "hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born? Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judea, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia, Phrygia, and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene:" mark how they run from east to west: "and strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes, Cretes and Arabians, we do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:69
verses.text: And, they were all amazed, and were in doubt, saying one to another, What meaneth this? Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:70
verses.text: O the excessive folly! O the excessive malignity! Why it was not even the season for that; for it was Pentecost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:71
verses.text: For this was what made it worse: that when those were confessing—men that were Jews, that were Romans, that were proselytes, yea perhaps that had crucified Him—yet these, after so great signs, say, "They are full of new wine!"  But let us look over what has been said from the beginning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:72
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:73
verses.text: ) "And when the day of Pentecost," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:74
verses.text: "It filled," he says, "the house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:75
verses.text: That wind πνοὴ was a very pool of water.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:76
verses.text: This betokened the copiousness, as the fire did the vehemence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:77
verses.text: This nowhere happened in the case of the Prophets: for to uninebriated souls such accesses are not attended with much disturbance; but "when they have well drunken," then indeed it is as here, but with the Prophets it is otherwise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:78
verses.text: (Ez.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:79
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:80
verses.text: ) The roll of a book is given him, and Ezekiel ate what he was about to utter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:81
verses.text: "And it became in his mouth," it is said, "as honey for sweetness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:82
verses.text: (And again the hand of God touches the tongue of another Prophet; but here it is the Holy Ghost Himself: (Jer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:83
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:84
verses.text: ) so equal is He in honor with the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:85
verses.text: ) And again, on the other hand, Ezekiel calls it "Lamentations, and mourning, and woe".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:86
verses.text: (Ez.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:87
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:88
verses.text: ) To them it might well be in the form of a book; for they still needed similitudes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:89
verses.text: Those had to deal with only one nation, and with their own people; but these with the whole world, and with men whom they never knew.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:90
verses.text: Also Elisha receives the grace through the medium of a mantle ( Kings xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:91
verses.text: ); another by oil, as David ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:92
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:93
verses.text: ); and Moses by fire, as we read of him at the bush.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:94
verses.text: (Exod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:95
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:96
verses.text: ) But in the present case it is not so; for the fire itself sat upon them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:97
verses.text: (But wherefore did the fire not appear so as to fill the house? Because they would have been terrified.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:98
verses.text: ) But the story shows, that it is the same here as there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:99
verses.text: For you are not to stop at this, that "there appeared unto them cloven tongues," but note that they were "of fire".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:100
verses.text: Such a fire as this is able to kindle infinite fuel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:101
verses.text: Also, it is well said, Cloven, for they were from one root; that you may learn, that it was an operation sent from the Comforter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:102
verses.text: But observe how those men also were first shown to be worthy, and then received the Spirit as worthy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:103
verses.text: Thus, for instance, David: what he did among the sheepfolds, the same he did after his victory and trophy; that it might be shown how simple and absolute was his faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:104
verses.text: Again, see Moses despising royalty, and forsaking all, and after forty years taking the lead of the people (Exod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:105
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:106
verses.text: ); and Samuel occupied there in the temple ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:107
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:108
verses.text: ); Elisha leaving all ( Kings xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:109
verses.text: ); Ezekiel again, made manifest by what happened thereafter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:110
verses.text: In this manner, you see, did these also leave all that they had.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:111
verses.text: They learnt also what human infirmity is, by what they suffered; they learnt that it was not in vain they had done these good works.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:112
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:113
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:114
verses.text: and xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:115
verses.text: ) Even Saul, having first obtained witness that he was good, thereafter received the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:116
verses.text: But in the same manner as here did none of them receive.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:117
verses.text: Thus Moses was the greatest of the Prophets, yet he, when others were to receive the Spirit, himself suffered diminution.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:118
verses.text: But here it is not so; but just as fire kindles as many flames as it will, so here the largeness of the Spirit was shown, in that each one received a fountain of the Spirit; as indeed He Himself had foretold, that those who believe in Him, should have "a well of water springing up into everlasting life".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:119
verses.text: (John iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:120
verses.text: ) And good reason that it should be so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:121
verses.text: For they did not go forth to argue with Pharaoh, but to wrestle with the devil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:122
verses.text: But the wonder is this, that when sent they made no objections; they said not, they were "weak in voice, and of a slow tongue".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:123
verses.text: (Exod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:124
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:125
verses.text: ) For Moses had taught them better.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:126
verses.text: They said not, they were too young.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:127
verses.text: (Jer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:128
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:129
verses.text: ) Jeremiah had made them wise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:130
verses.text: And yet they had heard of many fearful things, and much greater than were theirs of old time; but they feared to object.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:131
verses.text: —And because they were angels of light, and ministers of things above "Suddenly there came from heaven," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:132
verses.text: To them of old, no one "from heaven" appears, while they as yet follow after a vocation on earth; but now that Man has gone up on high, the Spirit also descends mightily from on high.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:133
verses.text: "As it were a rushing mighty wind;" making it manifest by this, that nothing shall be able to withstand them, but they shall blow away all adversaries like a heap of dust.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:134
verses.text: "And it filled all the house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:135
verses.text: The house also was a symbol of the world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:136
verses.text: "And it sat upon each of them," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:137
verses.text: and "the multitude came together, and were confounded".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:138
verses.text: Observe their piety; they pronounce no hasty judgment, but are perplexed: whereas those reckless ones pronounce at once, saying, "These men are full of new wine".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:139
verses.text: Now it was in order that they might have it in their power, in compliance with the Law, to appear thrice in the year in the Temple, that they dwelt there, these "devout men from all nations".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:140
verses.text: Observe here, the writer has no intention of flattering them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:141
verses.text: For he does not say that they pronounced any opinion: but what? "Now when this was noised abroad, the multitude came together, and were confounded".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:142
verses.text: And well they might be; for they supposed the matter was now coming to an issue against them, on account of the outrage committed against Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:143
verses.text: Conscience also agitated their souls, the very blood being yet upon their hands, and every thing alarmed them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:144
verses.text: "Behold, are not all these which speak Galileans?" For indeed this was confessed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:145
verses.text: "And how hear we" so much did the sound alarm them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:146
verses.text: "Every man in our own tongue," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:147
verses.text: for it found the greater part of the world assembled there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:148
verses.text: "Parthians and Medes," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:149
verses.text: This nerved the Apostles: for, what it was to speak in the Parthian tongue, they knew not but now learnt from what those said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:150
verses.text: Here is mention made of nations that were hostile to them, Cretans, Arabians, Egyptians, Persians: and that they would conquer them all was here made manifest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:151
verses.text: But as to their being in those countries, they were there in captivity, many of them: or else, the doctrines of the Law had become disseminated among the Gentiles in those countries.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:152
verses.text: So then the testimony comes from all quarters: from citizens, from foreigners, from proselytes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:153
verses.text: "We do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:154
verses.text: For it was not only that they spoke (in their tongues), but the things they spoke were wonderful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:155
verses.text: Well then might they be in doubt: for never had the like occurred.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:156
verses.text: Observe the ingenuousness of these men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:157
verses.text: They were amazed and were in doubt, saying, "What meaneth this?" But "others mocking said, 'These men are full of new wine'" (John viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:158
verses.text: ), and therefore mocked.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:159
verses.text: O the effrontery! And what wonder is it? Since even of the Lord Himself, when casting out devils, they said that He had a devil! For so it is; wherever impudent assurance exists, it has but one object in view, to speak at all hazards, it cares not what; not that the man should say something real and relevant to the matter of discourse, but that he should speak no matter what.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:160
verses.text: "They are full of new wine".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:161
verses.text: Quite a thing of course (is not it?), that men in the midst of such dangers, and dreading the worst, and in such despondency, have the courage to utter such things! And observe: since this was unlikely; because they would not have been drinking much at that early hour, they ascribe the whole matter to the quality (of the wine), and say, "They are full" of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:162
verses.text: "But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:163
verses.text: In a former place you saw his provident forethought, here you see his manly courage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:164
verses.text: For if they were astonished and amazed, was it not as wonderful that he should be able in the midst of such a multitude to find language, he, an unlettered and ignorant man? If a man is troubled when he speaks among friends, much more might he be troubled among enemies and bloodthirsty men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:165
verses.text: That they are not drunken, he shows immediately by his very voice, that they are not beside themselves, as the soothsayers: and this too, that they were not constrained by some compulsory force.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:166
verses.text: What is meant by, "with the eleven?" They expressed themselves through one common voice, and he was the mouth of all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:167
verses.text: The eleven stood by as witnesses to what he said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:168
verses.text: "He lifted up his voice," it is said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:169
verses.text: That is, he spoke with great confidence, that they might perceive the grace of the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:170
verses.text: He who had not endured the questioning of a poor girl, now in the midst of the people, all breathing murder, discourses with such confidence, that this very thing becomes an unquestionable proof of the Resurrection: in the midst of men who could deride and make a joke of such things as these! What effrontery, think you, must go to that! what impiety, what shamelessness! For wherever the Holy Spirit is present, He makes men of gold out of men of clay.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:171
verses.text: Look, I pray you, at Peter now: examine well that timid one, and devoid of understanding; as Christ said, "Are ye also yet without understanding?" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:172
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:173
verses.text: ) the man, who after that marvellous confession was called "Satan".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:174
verses.text: (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:175
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:176
verses.text: ) Consider also the unanimity of the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:177
verses.text: They themselves ceded to him the office of speaking; for it was not necessary that all should speak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:178
verses.text: "And he lifted up his voice," and spoke out to them with great boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:179
verses.text: Such a thing it is to be a spiritual man! Only let us also bring ourselves into a state meet for the grace from above, and all becomes easy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:180
verses.text: For as a man of fire falling into the midst of straw would take no harm, but do it to others: not he could take any harm, but they, in assailing him, destroy themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:181
verses.text: For the case here was just as if one carrying hay should attack one bearing fire: even so did the Apostles encounter these their adversaries with great boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:182
verses.text: For what did it harm them, though they were so great a multitude? Did they not spend all their rage? did they not turn the distress upon themselves? Of all mankind were ever any so possessed with both rage and terror, as those became possessed? Were they not in an agony, and were dismayed, and trembled? For hear what they say, "Do ye wish to bring this man's blood upon us?" (Acts v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:183
verses.text: ) Did they (the Apostles) not fight against poverty and hunger: against ignominy and infamy (for they were accounted deceivers): did they not fight against ridicule and wrath and mockery?—for in their case the contraries met: some laughed at them, others punished them;—were they not made a mark for the wrathful passions, and for the merriment, of whole cities? exposed to factions and conspiracies: to fire, and sword, and wild beasts? Did not war beset them from every quarter, in ten thousand forms? And were they any more affected in their minds by all these things, than they would have been at seeing them in a dream or in a picture? With bare body they took the field against all the armed, though against them all men had arbitrary power against them, were: terrors of rulers, force of arms, in cities and strong walls: without experience, without skill of the tongue, and in the condition of quite ordinary men, matched against juggling conjurors, against impostors, against the whole throng of sophists, of rhetoricians, of philosophers grown mouldy in the Academy and the walks of the Peripatetics, against all these they fought the battle out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:184
verses.text: And the man whose occupation had been about lakes, so mastered them, as if it cost him not so much ado as even a contest with dumb fishes: for just as if the opponents he had to outwit were indeed more mute than fishes, so easily did he get the better of them! And Plato, that talked a deal of nonsense in his day, is silent now, while this man utters his voice everywhere; not among his own countrymen alone, but also among Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and in India, and in every part of the earth, and to the extremities of the world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:185
verses.text: Where now is Greece, with her big pretentions? Where the name of Athens? Where the ravings of the philosophers? He of Galilee, he of Bethsaida, he, the uncouth rustic, has overcome them all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:186
verses.text: Are you not ashamed—confess it—at the very name of the country of him who has defeated you? But if you hear his own name too, and learn that he was called Cephas, much more will you hide your faces.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:187
verses.text: This, this has undone you quite; because you esteem this a reproach, and account glibness of tongue a praise, and want of glibness a disgrace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:188
verses.text: You have not followed the road you ought to have chosen, but leaving the royal road, so easy, so smooth, you have trodden one rough, and steep, and laborious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:189
verses.text: And therefore you have not attained unto the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:190
verses.text: Why then, it is asked, did not Christ exercise His influence upon Plato, and upon Pythagoras? Because the mind of Peter was much more philosophical than their minds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:191
verses.text: They were in truth children shifted about on all sides by vain glory; but this man was a philosopher, one apt to receive grace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:192
verses.text: If you laugh at these words, it is no wonder; for those aforetime laughed, and said, the men were full of new wine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:193
verses.text: But afterwards, when they suffered those bitter calamities, exceeding all others in misery; when they saw their city falling in ruins, and the fire blazing, and the walls hurled to the ground, and those manifold frantic horrors, which no one can find words to express, they did not laugh then.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:194
verses.text: And you will laugh then, if you have the mind to laugh, when the time of hell is close at hand, when the fire is kindled for your souls.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:195
verses.text: But why do I speak of the future? Shall I show you what Peter is, and what Plato, the philosopher? Let us for the present examine their respective habits, let us see what were the pursuits of each.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:196
verses.text: The one wasted his time about a set of idle and useless dogmas, and philosophical, as he says, that we may learn that the soul of our philosopher becomes a fly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:197
verses.text: Most truly said, a fly! not indeed changed into one, but a fly must have entered upon possession of the soul which dwelt in Plato; for what but a fly is worthy of such ideas! The man was full of irony, and of jealous feelings against every one else, as if he made it his ambition to introduce nothing useful, either out of his own head or other people's.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:198
verses.text: Thus he adopted the metempsychosis from another, and from himself produced the Republic, in which he enacted those laws full of gross turpitude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:199
verses.text: Let the women, he says, be in common, and let the virgins go naked, and let them wrestle before the eyes of their lovers, and let there also be common fathers, and let the children begotten be common.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:200
verses.text: But with us, not nature makes common fathers, but the philosophy of Peter does this; as for that other, it made away with all paternity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:201
verses.text: For Plato's system only tended to make the real father next to unknown, while the false one was introduced.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:202
verses.text: It plunged the soul into a kind of intoxication and filthy wallowing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:203
verses.text: Let all, he says, have intercourse with the women without fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:204
verses.text: The reason why I do not examine the maxims of poets, is, that I may not be charged with ripping up fables.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:205
verses.text: And yet I am speaking of fables much more ridiculous than even those.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:206
verses.text: Where have the poets devised aught so portentous as this? But (not to enter into the discussion of his other maxims), what say you to these—when he equips the females with arms, and helmets, and greaves, and says that the human race has no occasion to differ from the canine! Since dogs, he says, the female and the male, do just the same things in common, so let the women do the same works as the men, and let all be turned upside down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:207
verses.text: For the devil has always endeavored by their means to show that our race is not more honorable than that of brutes; and, in fact, some have gone to such a pitch of (κενοδοξίας) absurdity, as to affirm that the irrational creatures are endued with reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:208
verses.text: And see in how many various ways he has run riot in the minds of those men! For whereas their leading men affirmed that our soul passes into flies, and dogs, and brute creatures; those who came after them, being ashamed of this, fell into another kind of turpitude, and invested the brute creatures with all rational science, and made out that the creatures—which were called into existence on our account—are in all respects more honorable than we! They even attribute to them foreknowledge and piety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:209
verses.text: The crow, they say, knows God, and the raven likewise, and they possess gifts of prophecy, and foretell the future; there is justice among them, and polity, and laws.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:210
verses.text: Perhaps you do not credit the things I am telling you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:211
verses.text: And well may you not, nurtured as you have been with sound doctrine; since also, if a man were fed with this fare, he would never believe that there exists a human being who finds pleasure in eating dung.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:212
verses.text: The dog also among them is jealous, according to Plato.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:213
verses.text: But when we tell them that these things are fables, and are full of absurdity, 'You do not enter (ἐνοήσατε) into the higher meaning,' say they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:214
verses.text: No, we do not enter into this your surpassing nonsense, and may we never do so: for it requires (of course!) an excessively profound mind, to inform me, what all this impiety and confusion would be at.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:215
verses.text: Are you talking, senseless men, in the language of crows, as the children are wont (in play)? For you are in very deed children, even as they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:216
verses.text: But Peter never thought of saying any of these things: he uttered a voice, like a great light shining out in the dark, a voice which scattered the mist and darkness of the whole world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:217
verses.text: Again, his deportment, how gentle it was, how considerate (ἐπιεικὲς); how far above all vainglory; how he looked towards heaven without all self-elation, and this, even when raising up the dead! But if it had come to be in the power of any one of those senseless people (in mere fantasy of course) to do anything like it, would he not straightway have looked for an altar and a temple to be reared to him, and have wanted to be equal with the gods? since in fact when no such sign is forthcoming, they are forever indulging such fantastic conceits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:218
verses.text: And what, pray you, is that Minerva of theirs, and Apollo, and Juno? They are different kinds of demons among them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:219
verses.text: And there is a king of theirs, who thinks fit to die for the mere purpose of being accounted equal with the gods.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:220
verses.text: But not so the men here: no, just the contrary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:221
verses.text: Hear how they speak on the occasion of the lame man's cure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:222
verses.text: "Ye men of Israel, why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made him to walk? (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:223
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:224
verses.text: ) We also are men of like passions with you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:225
verses.text: (Ibid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:226
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:227
verses.text: ) But with those, great is the self-elation, great the bragging; all for the sake of men's honors, nothing for the pure love of truth and virtue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:228
verses.text: (φιλοσοφίας ἔνεκεν.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:229
verses.text: ) For where an action is done for glory, all is worthless.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:230
verses.text: For though a man possess all, yet if he have not the mastery over this (lust), he forfeits all claim to true philosophy, he is in bondage to the more tyrannical and shameful passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:231
verses.text: Contempt of glory; this it is that is sufficient to teach all that is good, and to banish from the soul every pernicious passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:232
verses.text: I exhort you therefore to use the most strenuous endeavors to pluck out this passion by the very roots; by no other means can you have good esteem with God, and draw down upon you the benevolent regard of that Eye which never sleepeth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 4:233
verses.text: Wherefore, let us use all earnestness to obtain the enjoyment of that heavenly influence, and thus both escape the trial of present evils, and attain unto the future blessings, through the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost be glory, power, honor, now and ever, and to all ages, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:1
verses.text: Homily V.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:2
verses.text: Acts II.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:3
verses.text: "Ye men of Judea, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:4
verses.text: "Ye men of Judea, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem," whom the writer above described as strangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:5
verses.text: Here he directs his discourse to those others, the mockers, and while he seems to reason with those, he sets these right.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:6
verses.text: For indeed it was divinely ordered that "some mocked," that he might have a starting-point for his defence, and by means of that defence, might teach.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:7
verses.text: "And all ye that dwell in Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:8
verses.text: It seems they accounted it a high encomium to dwell in Jerusalem too.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:9
verses.text: "Be this," says he, "known unto you, and hearken unto my words".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:10
verses.text: In the first instance he made them more disposed to attend to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:11
verses.text: "For not as ye suppose," says he, "are these drunken".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:12
verses.text: Do you observe the mildness of his defence? (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:13
verses.text: ) Although having the greater part of the people on his side, he reasons with those others gently; first he removes the evil surmise, and then he establishes his apology.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:14
verses.text: On this account, therefore, he does not say, "as ye mock," or, "as ye deride," but, "as ye suppose;" wishing to make it appear that they had not said this in earnest, and for the present taxing them with ignorance rather than with malice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:15
verses.text: "For these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:16
verses.text: And why this? Is it not possible at the third hour to be drunken? But he did not insist upon this to the letter; for there was nothing of the kind about them; the others said it only in mockery.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:17
verses.text: Hence we learn that on unessential points one must not spend many words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:18
verses.text: And besides, the sequel is enough to bear him out on this point: so now the discourse is for all in common.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:19
verses.text: "But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel, And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith the Lord God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:20
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:22
verses.text: Joel ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:23
verses.text: ) Nowhere as yet the name of Christ, nor His promises but the promise is that of the Father.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:24
verses.text: Observe the wisdom: observe the considerate forbearance: (συγκατάβασιν.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:25
verses.text: ) He did not pass on to speak at once of the things relating to Christ; that He had promised this after His Crucifixion; truly that would have been to upset all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:26
verses.text: And yet, you will say, here was sufficient to prove His divinity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:27
verses.text: True, it was, if believed (and the very point was that it should be believed); but if not believed, it would have caused them to be stoned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:28
verses.text: "And I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:29
verses.text: He offers even to them excellent hopes, if they would have them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:30
verses.text: And so far, he does not leave it to be regarded as the exclusive advantage of himself and his company; which would have made them be looked upon with an evil eye; thus cutting off all envious feeling.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:31
verses.text: "And your sons shall prophesy".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:32
verses.text: And yet, he says, not yours this achievement, this distinction; the gift has passed over to your children.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:33
verses.text: Himself and his company he calls their sons, and those whom he is addressing he calls his and their fathers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:34
verses.text: "And your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams; and on My servants and on My handmaidens I will pour out in those days of My Spirit; and they shall prophesy".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:35
verses.text: So far he shows that he and his have found favor, in that they had received (καταξιωθέντας) the Spirit; not so they whom he is addressing; for that they had crucified the Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:36
verses.text: So Christ also, willing to mitigate their wrath, said, "By whom do your sons cast out devils?" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:37
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:38
verses.text: ) He did not say, My disciples; for indeed it seemed a flattering mode of expression.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:39
verses.text: And so Peter also did not say, 'They are not drunk, but speak by the Spirit:' but he takes refuge with the prophet, and under shelter of him, so speaks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:40
verses.text: As for the accusation of drunkenness, he cleared himself of that by his own assertion; but for the grace, he fetches the prophet as witness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:41
verses.text: "I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:42
verses.text: "And your sons," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:43
verses.text: To some the grace was imparted through dreams, to others it was openly poured forth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:44
verses.text: For indeed by dreams the prophets saw, and received revelations.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:45
verses.text: Then he goes on with the prophecy, which has in it also something terrible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:46
verses.text: "And I will show wonders in heaven above, and signs" "in the earth beneath".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:48
verses.text: ) In these words he speaks both of the judgment to come, and of the taking of Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:49
verses.text: "Blood and fire, and vapor of smoke".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:50
verses.text: Observe how he describes the capture.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:51
verses.text: "The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:52
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:53
verses.text: ) This results from the (διαθέσεως) internal affection of the sufferers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:54
verses.text: It is said, indeed, that many such phenomena actually did occur in the sky, as Josephus attests.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:55
verses.text: At the same time the Apostle strikes fear into them, by reminding them of the darkness which had lately occurred, and leading them to expect things to come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:56
verses.text: "Before that great and notable day of the Lord come".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:57
verses.text: For be not confident, he means to say, because at present you sin with impunity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:58
verses.text: For these things are the prelude of a certain great and dreadful day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:59
verses.text: Do you see how he made their souls to quake and melt within them, and turned their laughter into pleading for acquittal? For if these things are the prelude of that day, it follows that the extreme of danger is impending.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:60
verses.text: But what next? He again lets them take breath, adding, "And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:61
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:62
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:63
verses.text: ) This is said concerning Christ, as Paul affirms, but Peter does not venture as yet to reveal this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:64
verses.text: Well, let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:65
verses.text: It is well managed, that as against men laughing and mocking, he starts up and begins with, "Be this known unto you all and hearken unto my words".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:66
verses.text: But he begins by saying, "Ye men of Judea".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:67
verses.text: By the expression ᾽Ιουδαἵοι, I take him to mean those that lived in Judea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:68
verses.text: —And, if you please, let us compare those expressions in the Gospel, that you may learn what a sudden change has taken place in Peter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:69
verses.text: "A damsel," it is written, "came out unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:70
verses.text: And, says he, "I know not the Man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:71
verses.text: And being again questioned, "he began to curse and to swear".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:72
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:73
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:74
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:75
verses.text: ) But see here his boldness, and his great freedom of speech.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:76
verses.text: —He did not praise those who had said, "We do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God;" but by his severity towards those others, he made these more earnest, and at the same time his address is clear from all appearance of adulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:77
verses.text: And it is well to remark, on all occasions, however the Apostles may condescend to the level of their hearers (συγκατάβασις), their language is clear from all appearance both of adulation and of insolence: which is a difficult point to manage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:78
verses.text: Now that these things should have occurred at "the third hour," was not without cause.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:79
verses.text: For the brightness of this fire is shown at the very time when people are not engaged in their works, nor at dinner; when it is bright day, when all are in the market-place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:80
verses.text: Do you observe also the freedom which fills his speech? "And hearken to my words".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:81
verses.text: And he added nothing, but, "This," says he, "is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel; And it shall come to pass in the last days".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:82
verses.text: He shows, in fact, that the consummation is nigh at hand, and the words, "In the last days," have a kind of emphasis.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:83
verses.text: "I will pour out," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:84
verses.text: And then, that he may not seem to limit the privilege to the sons only, he subjoins, "And your old men shall dream dreams".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:85
verses.text: Mark the sequence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:86
verses.text: First sons; just as David said, "Instead of thy fathers, were begotten thy sons".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:88

verses.text: ) And again Malachi; "They shall turn the hearts of the fathers to the children.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:90
verses.text: And on my handmaidens, and on my servants".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:91

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:93
verses.text: ) This also is a token of excellence, for we have become His servants, by being freed from sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:94
verses.text: And great is the gift, since the grace passes over to the other sex also, not as of old, it was limited to just one or two individuals, as Deborah and Huldah.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:95
verses.text: He did not say that it was the Holy Ghost, neither did he expound the words of the prophet; but he merely brings in the prophecy to fight its own battle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:96
verses.text: As yet also he has said nothing about Judas; and yet it was known to all what a doom and punishment he had undergone; for nothing was more forcible than to argue with them from prophecy: this was more forcible even than facts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:97
verses.text: For when Christ performed miracles, they often contradicted Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:98
verses.text: But when Christ brought forward the prophet, saying, "The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit Thou on my right hand," they were silent, and "no man," we read, "was able to answer Him a word".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:99
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:100
verses.text: xc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:101
verses.text: ) And on all occasions He Himself also appealed to the Scriptures; for instance, "If he called them gods to whom the word of God came".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:102
verses.text: (John x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:103
verses.text: ) And in many places one may find this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:104
verses.text: On this account here also Peter says, "I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh;" that is, upon the Gentiles also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:105
verses.text: But he does not yet reveal this, nor give interpretations; indeed, it was better not to do so (as also this obscure saying, "I will show wonders in heaven above," put them the more in fear because it was obscure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:106
verses.text: ) And it would have been more an offence, had it been interpreted from the very first.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:107
verses.text: Then besides, even as plain, he passes over it, wishing to make them regard it as such.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:108
verses.text: But after all, he does interpret to them anon, when he discourses to them upon the resurrection, and after he has paved the way by his discourse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:109
verses.text: (infra v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:110
verses.text: ) For since the good things were not sufficient to allure them, it is added, "And I will show wonders, etc".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:111
verses.text: Yet this has never been fulfilled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:112
verses.text: For none escaped then in that former judgment, but now the faithful did escape, in Vespasian's time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:113
verses.text: And this it is that the Lord speaks of, "Except those days had been shortened, not all flesh should be saved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:114
verses.text: —"Blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:115
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:117
verses.text: ) The worst to come first; namely, the inhabitants to be taken, and then the city to be razed and burnt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:118
verses.text: Then he dwelt upon the metaphor, bringing before the eyes of the hearers the overthrow and the taking.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:119
verses.text: "The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:120
verses.text: What means, the moon turned into blood? It denotes the excess of the slaughter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:121
verses.text: The language is fraught with helpless dismay.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:122
verses.text: (supra p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:123
verses.text: ) "And it shall come to pass, every one who shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:124
verses.text: Every one," he says: though he be priest (but he does not vet reveal the meaning), though bond, though free.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:125
verses.text: For there is no male nor female in Christ Jesus, no bond, no free.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:126

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:128
verses.text: ) Well may it be so, for all these are but shadow.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:129
verses.text: For if in king's palaces there is no high-born nor low-born, but each appears according to his deeds; and in art, each is shown by his works; much more in that school of wisdom (φιλοσοφια).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:130
verses.text: "Every one who shall invoke".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:131
verses.text: Invoke: not any how, for it is written, "Not every one that saith unto Me, Lord, Lord:" but with (διαθέσεως) inward earnest affection, with a life more than commonly good, with the confidence which is meet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:132
verses.text: Thus far, however, he makes the discourse light, by introducing that which relates to faith, and that terrible which relates to the punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:133
verses.text: For in the invocation is the salvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:134
verses.text: What, I pray you, is this you say? Do you talk of salvation for them after the Cross? Bear with me a little.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:135
verses.text: Great is the mercy of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:136
verses.text: And this very fact does, no less than the resurrection, prove him to be God, yea, no less than His miracles—the fact that He calls these to Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:137
verses.text: For surpassing goodness is, above all things, peculiarly God's own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:138
verses.text: Therefore also He says, "None is good save one, that is, God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:139
verses.text: (Luke xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:140
verses.text: ) Only let us not take this goodness for an occasion of negligence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:141
verses.text: For He also punishes as God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:142
verses.text: In fact, the very punishments here spoken of, He brought them to pass, even He who said, "Every one who shall call on the name of the Lord, shall be saved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:143
verses.text: I speak of the fate of Jerusalem; that intolerable punishment: of which I will tell you some few of the particulars, useful to us in our contest, both with the Marcionites and many other heretics.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:144
verses.text: For, since they distinguish between Christ a good God, and that evil God of the Old Testament, let us see who it was that effected these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:145
verses.text: The evil God, taking vengeance for Christ? or not so? How then alien to Him? But was it the good God? Nay, but it is demonstrated that both the Father and the Son did these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:146
verses.text: The Father in many places; for instance, when He says in the parable of the vineyard, "He will miserably destroy those wicked husbandmen" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:147
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:148
verses.text: ); again in the parable of the marriage feast, the King is said to send His armies (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:149
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:150
verses.text: ): and the Son, when He says, "But those Mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 5:151
verses.text: (Luke xix.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 8

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 8:1
verses.text: And they sent, saying, We will not have Thee to reign over us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 8:2
verses.text: Would you like then to hear the things which actually came to pass? Moreover, Christ Himself also speaks of the future tribulations, than which never any thing more dreadful came to pass; never any thing more ruthless, my beloved, than the deeds then done! And He Himself declared it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 8:3
verses.text: For what could you wish to see more grievous than these?.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 11

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 11:1
verses.text: —probed them with their daggers!—.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 14

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 14:1
verses.text: But shall I relate to you the shocking case of the woman, that tragic tale?.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:1
verses.text: (Joseph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:2
verses.text: B.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:3
verses.text: J.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:4
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:5
verses.text: ) Did not the actual events cast all misery into the shade? But shall I tell you of famines and pestilences? One might speak of horrors without number: nature was unknown; law unknown; they outdid wild beasts in ferocity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:6
verses.text: True, these miseries came by the fate of wars; but because God, because Christ so willed it to be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:7
verses.text: These facts will apply both against the Marcionites and against those who do not believe that there is a hell: for they are sufficient to silence their impudence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:8
verses.text: Are not these calamities more severe than the Babylonian? Are not these sufferings more grievous than the famines of that time? Yes, for "never was the like from the beginning of the world" "no, nor ever shall be such".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:9
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:10
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:11
verses.text: ) And this was Christ's own declaration.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:12
verses.text: In what sense then, think ye, is it said that Christ remitted them their sin? Perhaps it seems a commonplace question: but do ye solve it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:13
verses.text: —It is not possible to show anywhere, even in fiction, any thing like what the reality was here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:14
verses.text: And had it been a Christian that wrote this history, the matter might be regarded with suspicion: but if he was a Jew, and a Jewish zealot, and after the Gospel, how can the meaning of the facts be otherwise than palpable to all men? For you will see the man, how, everywhere, he always extols the concerns of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:15
verses.text: —There is therefore a hell, O man! and God is good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:16
verses.text: —Aye, did you shudder at hearing these horrors? But these, which take place here, are nothing in comparison with what shall be in that world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:17
verses.text: Once more I am compelled to seem harsh, disagreeable, stern.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:18
verses.text: But what can I do? I am set to this: just as a severe schoolmaster is set to be hated by his scholars: so are we.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:19
verses.text: For would it not be strange indeed, that, while those who have a certain post assigned them by kings do that which is appointed them, however disagreeable the task may be, we, for fear of your censure, should leave our appointed task undone? Another has a different work.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:20
verses.text: Of you, many have it for their work, to show mercy, to act humanely, to be pleasant and agreeable to the persons to whom you are benefactors.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:21
verses.text: But to those to whom we do good, we seem stern and severe, troublesome and disagreeable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:22
verses.text: For we do good, not by the pleasure we give, but by the pain we inflict.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:23
verses.text: So it is also with the physician: though he indeed is not excessively disagreeable, for the benefit afforded by his art is had immediately; ours hereafter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:24
verses.text: So again the magistrate is odious to the disorderly and seditious; so the legislator is vexatious to them for whom he makes laws.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:25
verses.text: But not so he that invites to enjoyment, not so he that prepares public festivities and entertainments, and puts all the people in garlands: no, these are men that win acceptance, feasting, as they do, whole cities with all sorts of spectacles; contributing largely, bearing all the cost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:26
verses.text: And therefore those whom they have treated, requite them for these enjoyments with words of welcome and benediction, with hanging (παραπετάσματα) of tapestries, and a blaze of lamps, and with wreaths, and boughs, and brilliant garments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:27
verses.text: Whereas, at the sight of the physician, the sick become sad and downcast: at sight of the magistrate, the rioters become subdued: no running riot then, no gambolling, except when he also goes over into their ranks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:28
verses.text: Let us see, then, which render the best service to their cities; those who provide these festivities, and banquetings, and expensive entertainments, and manifold rejoicings; or those who restrain all those doings, bearing before them stocks, scourges, executioners, dreaded soldiers, and a voice fraught with much terror: and issuing orders, and making men hang down their heads, and with the rod dispersing the idlers in the market-place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:29
verses.text: Let us see, I say; these are the disagreeable, those the beloved: let us see where the gain rests.
