verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:30
verses.text: (λήλει.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:31
verses.text: ) What comes then of your pleasure-givers? A kind of frigid enjoyment, lasting till the evening, and to-morrow vanished; mirth ungoverned, words unseemly and dissolute.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:32
verses.text: And what of these? Awe, sobriety, subdued thoughts; reasonableness of mind, an end of idleness; a curb on the passions within; a wall of defence, next to God, against assailants from without.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:33
verses.text: It is by means of these we have each our property but by those ruinous festivities we dissipate it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:34
verses.text: Robbers indeed have not invaded it, but vainglory together with pleasure acts the part of robber.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:35
verses.text: Each sees the robber carrying off everything before his eyes, and is delighted at it! A new fashion of robbery, this, to induce people to be glad when one is plundering them! On the other part, there is nothing of the kind: but God, as the common Father, has secured us as by a wall against all depredators, both seen and unseen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:36
verses.text: For, "Take heed," saith He, "that ye do not your alms before men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:37
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:38
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:39
verses.text: ) The soul learns from the one, excess; from the other to flee injustice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:40
verses.text: For injustice consists not merely in grasping at more wealth than belongs to us, but in giving to the belly more than its needful sustenance, in carrying mirth beyond its proper bounds, and causing it to run into frantic excesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:41
verses.text: From the one, it learns sobriety; from the other, unchastity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:42
verses.text: For it is unchastity, not merely to have carnal intercourse with women, but even to look upon a woman with unchaste eyes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:43
verses.text: From the one, it learns modesty; from the other, conceited self-importance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:44
verses.text: For, "All things," says the Apostle, "are lawful for me, but not all things expedient".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:45
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:46
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:47
verses.text: ) From the one, decent behavior; from the other unseemliness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:48
verses.text: For, as to the doings in the theatres, I pass these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:49
verses.text: But to let you see that it is not even a pleasure either, but a grief, show me, but a single day after the festival, both those who spent their money in giving it, and those who were feasted with spectacles: and you shall see them all looking dejected enough, but most of all him, your (ἔκεἵνον) famous man that has spent his money for it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:50
verses.text: And this is but fair: for, the day before, he delighted the common man, and the common man indeed was in high good humor and enjoyment, and rejoiced indeed in the splendid garment, but then not having the use of it, and seeing himself stripped of it, he was grieved and annoyed; and wanted to be the great man, seeing even his own enjoyment to be small compared with his.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:51
verses.text: Therefore, the day after, they change places, and now he, the great man, gets the larger share in the dejection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:52
verses.text: Now if in worldly matters, amusements are attended with such dissatisfaction, while disagreeable things are so beneficial, much more does this hold in things spiritual.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:53
verses.text: Why is it that no one quarrels with the laws, but on the contrary all account that matter a common benefit? For indeed not strangers from some other quarter, nor enemies of those for whom the laws are made, came and made these orders, but the citizens themselves, their patrons, their benefactors: and this very thing, the making of laws, is a token of beneficence and good-will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:54
verses.text: And yet the laws are full of punishment and restraint, and there is no such thing as law without penalty and coercion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:55
verses.text: Then is it not unreasonable, that while the expositors of those laws are called deliverers, benefactors, and patrons, we are considered troublesome and vexatious if we speak of the laws of God? When we discourse about hell, then we bring forward those laws: just as in the affairs of the world, people urge the laws of murder, highway robbery, and the like, so do we the penal laws: laws, which not man enacted, but the Only-Begotten Son of God Himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:56
verses.text: Let him that hath no mercy, He says, be punished (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:57
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:58
verses.text: ); for such is the import of the parable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:59
verses.text: Let him that remembereth injuries, pay the last penalty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:60
verses.text: Let him that is angry without cause, be cast into the fire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:61
verses.text: Let him that reviles, receive his due in hell.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:62
verses.text: If you think these laws which you hear strange, be not amazed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:63
verses.text: For if Christ was not intended to make new laws, why did He come? Those other laws are manifest to us; we know that the murderer and adulterer ought to be punished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:64
verses.text: If then we were meant only to be told the same things over again, where was the need of a heavenly Teacher? Therefore He does not say, Let the adulterer be punished, but, whoso looketh on with unchaste eyes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:65
verses.text: And where, and when, the man will receive punishment, He there tells us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:66
verses.text: And not in fine public monuments, nor yet somewhere out of sight, did He deposit His laws; not pillars of brass did He raise up, and engrave letters thereon, but twelve souls raised He up for us, the souls of the Apostles, and in their minds has He by the Spirit inscribed this writing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:67
verses.text: This cite we to you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:68
verses.text: If this was authorized to Jews, that none might take refuge in the plea of ignorance, much more is it to us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:69
verses.text: But should any say, "I do not hear, therefore have no guilt," on this very score he is most liable to punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:70
verses.text: For, were there no teacher, it would be possible to take refuge in this plea; but if there be, it is no longer possible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:71
verses.text: Thus see how, speaking of Jews, the Lord deprives them of all excuse; "If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin:" (John xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:72
verses.text: ): and Paul again, "But I say, have they not heard? Nay, but into all the earth went forth their sound".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:73
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:74
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:75
verses.text: ) For then there is excuse, when there is none to tell the man; but when the watchman sits there, having this as the business of his life, there is excuse no longer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:76
verses.text: Nay, rather, it was the will of Christ, not that we should look only upon these written pillars, but that we should ourselves be such.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:77
verses.text: But since we have made ourselves unworthy of the writing, at least let us look to those.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:78
verses.text: For just as the pillars threaten others, but are not themselves obnoxious to punishment, nor yet the laws, even so the blessed Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:79
verses.text: And observe; not in one place only stands this pillar, but its writing is carried round about in all the world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:80
verses.text: Whether you go among the Indians, you shall hear this: whether into Spain, or to the very ends of the earth, there is none without the hearing, except it be of his own neglect.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 17:81
verses.text: Then be not offended, but give heed to the things spoken, that ye may be able to lay hold upon the works of virtue, and attain unto the eternal blessings in Christ Jesus our Lord, with Whom to the Father and Holy Ghost together be glory, power, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:1
verses.text: Homily VI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:2
verses.text: Acts II.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:3
verses.text: "Ye men of Israel, hear these my words".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:4
verses.text: "Ye men of Israel": it is not for flattery that he uses this term; but, as he has borne hard upon them, he relaxes a little, and puts them in mind of their great ancestor Israel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:5
verses.text: Here again he begins with an introduction, that they may not become excited, now that he is going to make express mention to them of Jesus: for in what preceded, there was no reason why they should be excited, while the Prophet was the subject of discourse: but the name of Jesus would have given offence at the very outset.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:6
verses.text: —And he does not say, "Do as I bid you," but, Hear; as being not at all exacting.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:7
verses.text: And observe how he forbears to speak of the high matters, and begins with the very low: "Jesus," he says: and then straightway mentions the place He belonged to, being one which was held in mean estimation: "Jesus of Nazareth": and does not say anything great about Him, nor even such as one would say about a Prophet, so far: "Jesus," he says, "of Nazareth, a man proved (to be) from God among you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:8
verses.text: Observe; what great matter was this, to say that He was sent from God? For this was the point which on all occasions both He and John and the Apostles were studious to show.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:9
verses.text: Thus hear John saying: "The same said unto me On whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and abiding on him, this is He".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:10
verses.text: (John i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:11
verses.text: ) But Christ Himself does this to an extreme; Of Myself I am not come, He sent Me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:12
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:13
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:14
verses.text: ) And everywhere in the Scriptures this seems the point most studiously insisted upon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:15
verses.text: Therefore also this holy leader of the blessed company, the lover of Christ, the good shepherd, the man put in trust with the keys of heaven, the man who received the Spiritual Wisdom, when he has first subdued the Jews by fear; and has shown what great things have been vouchsafed to the disciples, and what a right they have to be believed, then first proceeds to speak concerning Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:16
verses.text: Only think what boldness it was to say it, in the midst of the murderers—that He is risen! And yet he does not all at once say, He is risen; but what?—"He came," says he, "from God: this is manifest by the signs which"—he does not yet say, Jesus Himself wrought: but what?—"which God wrought by Him in the midst of you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:17
verses.text: He calls themselves as witnesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:18
verses.text: "A man proved (to be sent) from God among you, by miracles and wonders and signs, which God wrought by him in the midst of you, as also ye yourselves know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:19
verses.text: Then, having fallen upon the mention of that their sacrilegious outrage, observe how he endeavors to quit them of the crime: "Him," he says, "being by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God delivered up": (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:20
verses.text: ) adding however, "ye have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain:" for though it was predetermined, still they were murderers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:21
verses.text: "By the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God:" all but using the same words as Joseph did; just as he said to his brethren; "Be not angry one with another by the way: God sent me hither".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:22
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:23
verses.text: xlv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:24
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:25
verses.text: ) It is God's doing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:26
verses.text: "What of us, then?" (it might be said,) "it was even well done on our part".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:27
verses.text: That they may not say this, therefore it is that he adds, "By wicked hands ye have crucified and slain".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:28
verses.text: Here then he hints at Judas; while at the same time he shows them that it was not from any strength of theirs, and would not have been, if He had not Himself permitted it: it was God that delivered Him up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:29
verses.text: He has transferred the evil entire upon the head of Judas, now already parted from them; for he it was that delivered Him over to them by the kiss.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:30
verses.text: Or, "By wicked hands," refers to the soldiers: for neither is it simply, "Ye have slain," but, By wicked men ye have done this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:31
verses.text: And observe how everywhere they make it of great importance that the Passion should first be confessed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:32
verses.text: Whom God Raised Up (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:33
verses.text: ), says he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:34
verses.text: This was the great thing; and observe how he sets it in the middle of his discourse: for the former matters had been confessed; both the miracles and the signs and the slaying—"Whom God," says he, "raised up, having loosed the pains of death, because it was not possible that He should be kept in its power".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:35
verses.text: It is something great and sublime that he has hinted at here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:36
verses.text: For the expression, "It was not possible," even itself is that of one assigning something.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:37
verses.text: It shows that death itself in holding Him had pangs as in travail, and was sore bestead: whereas, by pains, or, travail-pangs, of death, the Old Testament means danger and disaster: and that He so rose as never more to die.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:38
verses.text: For the assertion, "Seeing that it was not possible that He should be holden of it," means this, that His rising was not common to the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:39
verses.text: Then, however, before their thoughts can enter at all into his meaning, he brings David upon them, an authority which sets aside all human reasoning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:40
verses.text: "For David saith (with reference) to Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:42
verses.text: ) And observe how, once more, the testimony is lowly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:43
verses.text: For therefore he begins the citation further up, with the matters of lowlier import: therefore was death not in the number of grievous things because, says he, "I foresaw the Lord always before my face, that He is on my right hand that I should not be moved:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:44
verses.text: –) and, "that Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:45
verses.text: Then, having finished the citation from the Prophet, he adds; "Men and brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:47
verses.text: ) When he is about to say anything great, he uses this opening address, to rouse and to conciliate them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:48
verses.text: "Let me be allowed," he says, "to speak freely to you of the patriarch David".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:49
verses.text: Remarkable lowliness, in a case where he was giving no hurt, nor was there any reason why the hearers should be angry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:50
verses.text: For he did not say, This is not said concerning David, but concerning the Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:51
verses.text: But in another point of view: by his reverential expression towards the blessed David, he awed them; speaking of an acknowledged fact as if it were a bold thing to say, and therefore begging them to pardon him for saying it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:52
verses.text: And thereupon his expression is not simply "concerning David," but "concerning the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried:" he does not also say, "and is not risen again," but in another way (though this too would have been no great thing to say), "And his sepulchre is with us unto this day," he has said what comes to the same thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:53
verses.text: Then—and even so he does not come to the mention of Christ, but what next?—he goes on with his encomium upon David, "Being therefore a prophet, and knowing that with an oath God had sworn unto him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:55
verses.text: ) But this he says, that were it but on account of the honor shown to David, and the descent from him, they may accept what is said concerning Christ's resurrection, as seeing that it would be an injury to the prophecy, and a derogating from (τἥς εἰς αὐτοὺς τιμἥς) their honor, if this were not the fact.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:56
verses.text: "And knowing," he says, "that with an oath God had sworn unto him"—he does not say simply "promised"—"of the fruit of his loins after the flesh to raise up Christ, to seat Him upon his throne".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:57
verses.text: Observe how he has again only hinted at what is sublime.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:58
verses.text: For now that he has soothed them with his expression, he confidently adds this: The prophet saith it "of His resurrection, that neither was His soul left in hell, nor did His flesh see corruption".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:59
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:60
verses.text: ) This again is wonderful: it shows that His resurrection was not like that of other men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:61
verses.text: For though death laid hold on Him, yet it did not its own work then.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:62
verses.text: —And, as regards the sin, he has spoken of that, covertly and darkly; of the punishment, he forbore to add anything; but that they had slain Him, this he has spoken out; for the rest he now comes to the sign given by God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:63
verses.text: And when it is once proved, that He, the slain, was just, was dear to God, then, though thou be silent of the punishment, be sure that he which did the sin will condemn himself more than ever thou canst condemn him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:64
verses.text: So then, that he refers all to the Father, is in order that they may receive what is said: and that assertion, "Not possible," he fetches in from the prophecy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:65
verses.text: Well then, let us again look over what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:66
verses.text: "Jesus of Nazareth, a man proved (to be sent) from God unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:67
verses.text: (Recapitulation of v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:68
verses.text: –): one, of whom, by reason of His works, there can be no doubt; but who, on the contrary, is demonstrated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:69
verses.text: Thus also Nicodemus said, "No man can do these miracles which Thou doest—By miracles, and wonders, and signs which God wrought by Him in the midst of you" (John iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:70
verses.text: ): not secretly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:71
verses.text: Setting out from facts notorious to those whom he was addressing, he then comes to things hidden.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:72
verses.text: Thereupon in saying, "By the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:73
verses.text: ) he shows that it was not because they had the power to do it, and that there was a wisdom and a Divine arrangement in the event, seeing it was from God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:74
verses.text: He rapidly passes over the unpleasant part, adding, "Whom God raised up," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:75
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:76
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:77
verses.text: For it is always a point of great importance with them to show that He was once dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:78
verses.text: Though ye should deny it, says he, (ἐκεῖνοι) those (present) will bear witness to the fact.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:79
verses.text: "Having loosed the pangs of death".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:80
verses.text: He that gives Death trouble, may much more give trouble to them that crucified Him: however, nothing of the kind is here said, as that He had power to slay you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:81
verses.text: Meanwhile, let us also learn thus to hold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:82
verses.text: For one that is in pain like a woman in travail, does not hold the thing held, and is not active but passive; and makes haste to cast it off.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:83
verses.text: And it is well said: "For David saith in reference to him" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:84
verses.text: ); that you may not refer that saying to the Prophet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:85
verses.text: —"Therefore being a Prophet, and knowing," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:86
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:87
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:88
verses.text: ) Do you observe how he now interprets the prophecy, and does not give it bare of comment? How did He "seat Him upon" David's "throne?" For the kingdom after the Spirit is in heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:89
verses.text: Observe how, along with the resurrection, he has also declared the kingdom in the fact of His rising again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:90
verses.text: He shows that the Prophet was under constraint: for the prophecy was concerning Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:91
verses.text: Why does he say, not, Concerning His kingdom (it was a great matter), but "Concerning His resurrection?" And how did He seat Him upon his (David's) throne? Why, He reigns as King over Jews also, yea, what is much more, over them that crucified Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:92
verses.text: "For His flesh saw no corruption".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:93
verses.text: This seems to be less than resurrection, but it is the same thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:94
verses.text: "This Jesus"—observe how he does not call Him otherwise—"hath God raised up; whereof all we are witnesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:95
verses.text: Being therefore by the right hand of God exalted" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:96
verses.text: , ): again he takes refuge with the Father, and yet it had been enough to say what precedes: but he knows what a great point this is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:97
verses.text: Here he has hinted at the Ascension also, and that Christ is in heaven: but neither does he say this openly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:98
verses.text: "And having received," says he, "the promise of the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:99
verses.text: Observe how, in the beginning of his discourse, he does not say that Jesus Himself had sent It, but the Father: now, however, that he has mentioned His signs and the things done to Him by the Jews, and has spoken of His resurrection, he boldly introduces what he has to say about these matters, again adducing themselves as witnesses by both senses: "He hath shed forth this, which ye do see and hear".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:100
verses.text: And of the resurrection he has made continual mention, but of their outrageous deed he has spoken once for all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:101
verses.text: "And having received the promise of the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:102
verses.text: This again is great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:103
verses.text: "The promise," he says; because promised before His Passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:104
verses.text: Observe how he now makes it all His "He hath poured forth this", covertly making a great point.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:105
verses.text: For if it was He that poured it forth, it is of Him that the Prophet has spoken above, "In the last days I will pour forth of My Spirit on My Servants, and on Mine handmaids, and I will do wonders in the heaven above.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:106
verses.text: (supra, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:107
verses.text: ) Observe what he secretly puts into it! But then, because it was a great thing, he again veils it with the expression of "His having received of the Father".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:108
verses.text: He has spoken of the good things fulfilled, of the signs; has said, that He is king, the point that touched them; has said, that it is He that gives the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:109
verses.text: (Arist.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:110
verses.text: Rhet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:111
verses.text: ) (For, however much a person may say, if it does not issue in something advantageous, he speaks to no purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:112
verses.text: ) Just as John: "The same," says he, "shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:113
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:114
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:115
verses.text: ) And it shows that the Cross not only did not make Him less, but rendered Him even more illustrious, seeing that of old God promised it to Him, but now has given it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:116
verses.text: Or it may be, "the promise" which He promised to us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:117
verses.text: He so foreknew it about to be, and has given it to us greater after the resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:118
verses.text: And, "hath poured it out," he says; not requiring worthiness: and not simply gave, but with abundance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:119
verses.text: Whence does this appear? Henceforth after the mention of His giving the Spirit, he confidently speaks also of His ascension into heaven; and not only so, but again adducing the witness, and reminding them of that Person concerning Whom Christ once spake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:120
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:121
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:122
verses.text: ) "For not David," says he "ascended into the heavens.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:123
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:124
verses.text: ) Here he no longer speaks in lowly phrase, having the confidence which results from the things said; nor does he say, "Be it permitted me to speak," or the like: "But he saith himself; The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit Thou on My right hand, until I make Thine enemies Thy footstool".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:125
verses.text: Now if He be David's Lord, much more shall they not disdain Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:126
verses.text: "Sit thou on My right hand;" he has set the whole matter here; "until I make Thine enemies Thy footstool:" here also he has brought upon them a great terror, just as in the beginning he showed what He does to His friends, what to his enemies.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:127
verses.text: And again, as to the act of subjugation, not to provoke unbelief, he ascribes it to the Father.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:128
verses.text: Since then these are great things that he has uttered, he again brings his discourse down to lowly matters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:129
verses.text: "Let therefore," he says, "the whole house of Israel know assuredly: i-e: question ye not, nor doubt ye: then also in the tone of command it follows; "that God hath made Him both Lord"—this he says from David—"and Christ," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:130
verses.text: ), this from the Psalm: For when it would have been rightly concluded, "Let therefore the whole house of Israel know assuredly that" He sitteth on the right hand of God, this, which would have been great, he forbears, and brings in a different matter which is much more humble, and the expression "Hath made;" i-e: hath ordained: so that there is nothing about (οὐσίωσις) communication of substance here, but the expression relates to this which has been mentioned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:131
verses.text: "Even this Jesus, Whom ye crucified".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:132
verses.text: He does well to end with this, thereby agitating their minds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:133
verses.text: For when he has shown how great it is, he has then exposed their daring deed, so as to show it to be greater, and to possess them with terror.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:134
verses.text: For men are not so much attracted by benefits as they are chastened by fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:135
verses.text: But the admirable and great ones, and beloved of God, need none of these motives: men, such as was Paul: not of the kingdom, not of hell, made he account.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:136
verses.text: For this is indeed to love Christ, this to be no hireling, nor to reckon it a matter of trafficking and trading, but to be indeed virtuous, and to do all for the love of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:137
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:138
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:139
verses.text: ) Then what tears does it not deserve, when, owing so large a measure, we do not even like traders seek the kingdom of heaven! He promises us so great things, and not even so is He worthy to be heard? What can come up to this enmity! And yet, they are mad after money-making, though it be with enemies, though it be with slaves, though it be with persons most hostile to them, that they come in contact, though it be with persons utterly evil, if only they expect that they shall be enabled by their means to make money, they will do everything, will flatter, and be obsequious, and make themselves slaves, and will esteem them more to be revered than all men, to get some advantage out of them: for the hope of money does not allow them to give a thought to any such considerations as these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:140
verses.text: But the Kingdom is not so powerful as money is; nay, rather, not in the smallest proportion as powerful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:141
verses.text: For it is no ordinary Being that promises: but this is greater than even the Kingdom itself that we receive it from such a Giver! But now the case is the same as if a king, wishing, after ten thousand other benefits, to make us his heirs and coheirs with his son should be despised: while some captain of a band of robbers, who has done ten thousand wrongs to us and to our parents, and is himself fraught with ten thousand wickednesses, and has utterly marred our honor and our welfare, should, on presenting a single penny, receive our worship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:142
verses.text: God promises a Kingdom, and is despised: the Devil helps us to hell, and he is honored! Here God, there Devil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:143
verses.text: But let us see the difference of the tasks enjoined.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:144
verses.text: For if there were none of these considerations in the case: if it were not, here God, there Devil; not, here one helping to a kingdom, there to a hell: the nature itself of the tasks enjoined were sufficient to induce us to comply with the former.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:145
verses.text: For what does each enjoin? The one, the things which make glorious; the other the things which put to shame: one, the things which involve in ten thousand calamities and disgraces; the other, the things which have with them abundant refreshment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:146
verses.text: For look: the one saith, "Learn ye of Me, for I am meek and lowly of heart, and ye shall find rest unto your souls".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:147
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:148
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:149
verses.text: ): the other saith, Be thou savage, and ungentle, and passionate, and wrathful, and more a wild beast than a man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:150
verses.text: Let us see which is more useful, which, I pray you, more profitable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 18:151
verses.text: "Speak not of this," say you.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:1
verses.text: But consider that he is the devil: above all indeed, if that be shown: there is need also to undergo toils, and, on the other hand, the prize of victory will be greater.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:2
verses.text: For not he that enjoins easy tasks is the kind (κηδεμὼν) benefactor, but he that enjoins what is for our good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:3
verses.text: Since fathers also enjoin disagreeable tasks; but for this they are fathers: and so again do masters to slaves: but kidnappers and destroyers (λυμεὥνες) on the other hand, do just the reverse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:4
verses.text: And yet that the commands of Christ are attended with a pleasure, is manifest from that saying.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:5
verses.text: For to what sort do you take the passionate man to belong, and to what the forbearing and meek? Does not the soul of the (ἐκείνου) one seem to be in a kind of solitary retreat, enjoying exceeding quiet; while that of (τούτου) the other is like a market-place and tumult and the midst of cities, where great is the clamor of those going out, the noise of camels, mules, asses: of men shouting loud to those that meet them, that they may not be trodden under foot: and again, of silver-beaters, of braziers, of men thrusting and pushing this way and that and some overborne, some overbearing? But the soul of (τούτου) the former is like some mountain-top, with its delicate air, its pure sunshine, its limpid gushing fountains, its multitude of charming flowers, while the vernal meads and gardens put on their plumage of shrubs and flowers, and glance with rifling waters: and if any sound is heard there, it is sweet, and calculated to affect the ear with a sense of much delight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:6
verses.text: For either the warbling birds perch on the outermost spray of the branching trees, and cicadas, nightingales and swallows, blended in one harmony, perform a kind of concerted music; or the zephyr gently stirring the leaves, draws whistling tones from pines and firs, resembling oft the notes of the swan: and roses, violets, and other flowers, gently swayed, and (κυανίζοντα) dark-dimpling, show like a sea just rippled over with gentle undulations.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:7
verses.text: Nay, many are the images one might find.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:8
verses.text: Thus, when one looks at the roses, one shall fancy that he beholds in them the rainbow; in the violets a waving sea; in the lilies, the sky.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:9
verses.text: But not by the spectacle alone, and the beholding, does such an one then cause delight: but also in the very body of him that looks to the meadow, rather it refreshes him, and causes him to breathe freely, so that he thinks himself more in heaven than on earth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:10
verses.text: There is withal a sound of a different kind, when water from the mountain-steep, borne by its own force through ravines gently plashes over its pebbly bed with lulling noise, and so relaxes our frame with the pleasurable sensations, as quickly to draw over our eyes the soft languor of slumber.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:11
verses.text: You have heard the description with pleasure: perhaps also it has made you enamored of solitude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 21:12
verses.text: But sweeter far than this solitude is the soul.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:1
verses.text: of the long-suffering.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:2
verses.text: For it was not for the sake of describing a meadow, nor for the sake of making a display of language, that we have broached this similitude: but the object was, that, seeing how great is the delight of the long suffering, and how, by converse with a long suffering man, one would be far more both delighted and benefited, than by frequenting such spots, ye may follow after such men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:3
verses.text: For when not even a breath of violence proceeds from such a soul, but mild and engaging words, then indeed does that gentle softness of the zephyr find its counterpart: entreaties also, devoid of all arrogance, but forming the resemblance to those winged warblers,—how is not this far better? For not the body is fanned by the soft breeze of speech; no, it refreshes our souls heated and glowing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:4
verses.text: A physician, by ever so great attention, could not so speedily rid a man of the fever, as a patient man would cool, by the breath of his own words, a person who was passionate and burning with wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:5
verses.text: And why do I speak of a physician? Not even iron, made red-hot and dipped into water, so quickly parts with its heat, as does the passionate man when he comes in contact with the soul of the long-suffering.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:6
verses.text: But as, if it chance that singing birds find their way into the market, they go for nothing there, just so is it with our precepts when they light upon souls addicted to wrathful passions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:7
verses.text: Assuredly, sweeter is gentleness than bitterness and frowardness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:8
verses.text: —Well, but the one was God's bidding, the other the devil's.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:9
verses.text: Do you see that it was not for nothing that I said, even if there were no devil or God in the case, the things enjoined would be enough in themselves to (ἀποστἥσαι) revolt us? For the one is both agreeable to himself, and serviceable to others, the other displeasing to himself, and hurtful to others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:10
verses.text: Nothing is more unpleasant than a man in a passion, nothing more noisome, more odious, more shocking, as also nothing more pleasing than one who knows not what it is to be in a passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:11
verses.text: Better dwell with a wild beast than with a passionate man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:12
verses.text: For the beast, when once tamed, abides by its law; but the man, no matter how often you have tamed him, again turns wild, unless however he should of himself settle down into some such habit (of gentleness).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:13
verses.text: For as a bright sunny day and winter with all its gloom, so are the soul of the angry and that of the gentle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:14
verses.text: However, let us at present look not to the mischievous consequences resulting to others, but to those which affect the persons themselves: though indeed it is also no slight mischief (to one's self) to cause ill to another, for the present, however, let that be the consideration.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:15
verses.text: What executioner with his lash can so lacerate the ribs, what red-hot lancets (ὀβελίσκοι) ever so pierced the body, what madness can so dispossess a man of his natural reason, as anger and rage do? I know many instances of persons engendering diseases by giving loose to anger: and the worst of fevers are precisely these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:16
verses.text: But if they so injure the body, think of the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:17
verses.text: For do not argue that you do not see the mischief, but rather consider, if that which is the recipient of the malignant passion is so hurt, what must be the hurt sustained by that which engenders it! Many have lost their eyes, many have fallen into most grievous disease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:18
verses.text: Yet he that bears bravely, shall endure all things easily.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:19
verses.text: But, however, both such are the troublesome tasks the devil enjoins, and the wages he assigns us for these is hell.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:20
verses.text: He is both devil and foe to our salvation, and we rather do his bidding than Christ's, Saviour as He is, and Benefactor and Defender, and speaking as He does such words, which are both sweeter, and more reverend, and more profitable and beneficial, and are both to ourselves and to those who live in our company the greatest of blessings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:21
verses.text: Nothing worse than anger, my beloved, nothing worse than unseasonable wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:22
verses.text: It will not have any long delay; it is a quick, sharp passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:23
verses.text: Many a time has a mere word been blurted out in anger, which needs for its curing a whole lifetime, and a deed been done which was the ruin of the man for life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:24
verses.text: For the worst of it is this, that in a little moment, and by one act, and by a single word, full oft has it cast us out from the possession of eternal good, and brought to nought a world of pains.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:25
verses.text: Wherefore I beseech you to do all you can to curb this savage beast.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:26
verses.text: Thus far, however, I have spoken concerning meekness and wrath; if one should take in hand to treat of other opposites, as covetousness and the mad passion for glory, contrasted with contempt of wealth and of glory; intemperance with sobriety; envy with benevolence; and to marshal them each against its opposite, then one would know how great the difference.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 23:27
verses.text: Behold how from the very things enjoined it is plainly shown, that the one master is God, the other the devil! Why then, let us do God's bidding, and not cast ourselves into bottomless pits; but while there is time, let us wash off all that defiles the soul, that we may attain unto the eternal blessings, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and Holy Ghost together be glory, power, honor, now and ever, and world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:1
verses.text: Homily VII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:2
verses.text: Acts II.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:3
verses.text: "Now when they heard these words (E.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:4
verses.text: V.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:5
verses.text: 'this,') they were pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and to the rest of the Apostles, Men and brethren, what shall we do?"  Do you see what a great thing gentleness is? More than any vehemence, it pricks our hearts, inflicts a keener wound.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:6
verses.text: For as in the case of bodies which have become callous, the man that strikes upon them does not affect the sense so powerfully, but if he first mollify them and make them tender, then he pierces them effectually; so in this instance also, it is necessary first to mollify.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:7
verses.text: But that which softens, is not wrath, not vehement accusation, not personal abuse; it is gentleness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:8
verses.text: The former indeed rather aggravate the callousness, this last alone removes it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:9
verses.text: If then you are desirous to reprove any delinquent, approach him with all possible mildness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:10
verses.text: For see here; he gently reminds them of the outrages they have committed, adding no comment; he declares the gift of God, he goes on to speak of the grace which bore testimony to the event, and so draws out his discourse to a still greater length.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:11
verses.text: So they stood in awe of the gentleness of Peter, in that he, speaking to men who had crucified his Master, and breathed murder against himself and his companions, discoursed to them in the character of an affectionate father and teacher.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:12
verses.text: Not merely were they persuaded; they even condemned themselves, they came to a sense of their past behavior.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:13
verses.text: For he gave no room for their anger to be roused, and darken their judgment, but by means of humility he dispersed, as it were, the mist and darkness of their indignation, and then pointed out to them the daring outrage they had committed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:14
verses.text: For so it is; when we say of ourselves that we are injured, the opposite party endeavor to prove that they have not done the injury; but when we say, we have not been injured, but have rather done the wrong, the others take the contrary line.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:15
verses.text: If, therefore, you wish to place your enemy (εἰς ἀγώνα) in the wrong, beware of accusing him; nay (ἀγώνισαι), plead for him, he will be sure to find himself guilty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:16
verses.text: There is a natural spirit of opposition in man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:17
verses.text: Such was the conduct of Peter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:18
verses.text: He did not accuse them harshly; on the contrary, he almost endeavored to plead for them, as far as was possible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:19
verses.text: And this was the very reason that he penetrated into their souls.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:20
verses.text: You will ask, where is the proof that they were pricked? In their own words; for what say they? "Men and brethren, what shall we do?" Whom they had called deceivers, they call "brethren:" not that hereby they put themselves on an equality with them, but rather by way of attracting their brotherly affection and kindness: and besides, because the Apostles had deigned to call them by this title.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:21
verses.text: And, say they, "What shall we do?" They did not straightway say, Well then, we repent; but they surrendered themselves to the disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:22
verses.text: Just as a person on the point of shipwreck, upon seeing the pilot, or in sickness the physician, would put all into his hands, and do his bidding in everything; so have these also confessed that they are in extreme peril, and destitute of all hope of salvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:23
verses.text: They did not say, How shall we be saved? but, "What shall we do?" Here again Peter, though the question is put to all, is the man to answer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:24
verses.text: "Repent," says he, "and be baptized every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:26
verses.text: ) He does not yet say, Believe, but, "Be baptized every one of you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:27
verses.text: For this they received in baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:28
verses.text: Then he speaks of the gain; "For the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:29
verses.text: If you are to receive a gift, if baptism conveys remission, why delay? He next gives a persuasive turn to his address, adding, "For the promise is unto you" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:30
verses.text: ): for he had spoken of a promise above.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:31
verses.text: "And to your children," he says: the gift is greater, when these are to be heirs of the blessings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:32
verses.text: "And to all," he continues, "that are afar off:" if to those that are afar off, much more to you that are near: "even as many as the Lord our God shall call".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:33
verses.text: Observe the time he takes for saying, "To those that are afar off".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:34
verses.text: It is when he finds them conciliated and self-accusing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:35
verses.text: For when the soul pronounces sentence against itself, no longer can it feel envy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:36
verses.text: "And with many other words did he testify, and exhort, saying".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:38
verses.text: ) Observe how, throughout, the writer studies brevity, and how free he is from ambition and display.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:39
verses.text: "He testified and exhorted, saying".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:40
verses.text: This is the perfection of teaching, comprising something of fear and something of love.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:41
verses.text: "Save yourselves from this untoward generation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:42
verses.text: He says nothing of the future, all is about the present, by which indeed men are chiefly swayed; he shows that the Gospel releases from present evils as well.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:43
verses.text: "Then they that gladly received his word were baptized; and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:44
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:45
verses.text: ) Think you not this cheered the Apostles more than the miracle? "And they continued steadfastly and with one accord in the Apostles' doctrine and fellowship".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:47
verses.text: ) Here are two virtues, perseverance and concord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:48
verses.text: "In the Apostles' doctrine," he says: for they again taught them; "and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayer".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:49
verses.text: All in common, all with perseverance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:50
verses.text: "And fear came upon every soul" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:51
verses.text: ): of those that believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:52
verses.text: For they did not despise the Apostles, like common men, nor did they fix their regard on that which was visible merely.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:53
verses.text: Verily, their thoughts were kindled into a glow.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:54
verses.text: And as Peter had before spoken much, and declared the promises, and the things to come, well might they be beside themselves with fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:55
verses.text: The wonders also bore witness to the words: "Many wonders and signs were done by the Apostles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:56
verses.text: As was the case with Christ; first there were signs, then teaching, then wonders; so was it now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:57
verses.text: "And all that believed were together, and had all things common".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:59
verses.text: ) Consider what an advance was here immediately! For the fellowship was not only in prayers, nor in doctrine alone, but also in (πολιτεία) social relations.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:60
verses.text: "And sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men, as every man had need".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:61
verses.text: See what fear was wrought in them! "And they parted them," he says, showing the (τὸ οἰκονομικὸν) wise management: "As every man had need".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:62
verses.text: Not recklessly, like some philosophers among the Greeks, of whom some gave up their land, others cast into the sea great quantities of money; but this was no contempt of riches, but only folly and madness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:63
verses.text: For universally the devil has made it his endeavor to disparage the creatures of God, as if it were impossible to make good use of riches.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:64
verses.text: "And continuing daily with one accord in the temple" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:65
verses.text: ), they enjoyed the benefit of teaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:66
verses.text: Consider how these Jews did nothing else great or small, than assiduously attend at the temple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:67
verses.text: For, as having become more earnest, they had increased devotion also to the place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:68
verses.text: For the Apostles did not for the present pluck them away from this object, for fear of injuring them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:69
verses.text: "And breaking bread from house to house, did take their portion of food with gladness and singleness of heart, praising God, and having favor with all the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:70
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:71
verses.text: ) It seems to me that in mentioning "bread," he here signifies fasting and hard life; for they "took their portion of food," not of dainty fare.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:72
verses.text: "With gladness," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:73
verses.text: Seest thou that not the dainty fare, but the (τροφἥς οὐ τρυφἥς) food made the enjoyment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:74
verses.text: For they that fare daintily are under punishment and pain; but not so these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:75
verses.text: Do you see that the words of Peter contain this also, namely, the regulation of life? "And singleness of heart".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:76
verses.text: For no gladness can exist where there is no simplicity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:77
verses.text: How had they "favor with all the people?" On account of their alms deeds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:78
verses.text: For do not look to the fact, that the chief priests for envy and spite rose up against them, but rather consider that "they had favor with the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:79
verses.text: —"And the Lord added to the Church daily (ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό) together such as should be saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:80
verses.text: —And all that believed were together".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:81
verses.text: Once more, the unanimity, the charity, which is the cause of all good things!  "Now when they heard this," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:82
verses.text: "Then Peter said unto them," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:83
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:84
verses.text: ) What had been said was not enough.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:85
verses.text: For those sayings indeed were sufficient to bring them to faith; but these are to show what things the believer behooves to do.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:86
verses.text: And he said not, In the Cross, but, "In the name of Jesus Christ let every one of you be baptized".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:87
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:88
verses.text: ) And he does not put them continually in mind of the Cross, that he may not seem to reproach them, but he says simply, "Repent:" and why? That we may be punished? No: "And let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, for the remission of sins".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:89
verses.text: And yet quite other is the law; of this world's tribunals: but in the case of the Gospel proclamation (κηρύγματος); when the delinquent has confessed, then is he saved! Observe how Peter does not instantly hurry over this, but he specifies also the conditions, and adds, "Ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost;" an assertion accredited by the fact, that the Apostles themselves had received that gift.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:90
verses.text: "For the promise," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:91
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:92
verses.text: ) "The promise," i-e: the gift of the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:93
verses.text: So far, he speaks of the easy part, and that which has with it a great gift; and then he leads them to practice: for it will be to them a ground of earnestness, to have tasted already of those so great blessings "and with many other words did he testify," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:94
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:95
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:96
verses.text: Since, however, the hearer would desire to learn what was the sum and, substance of these further words, he tells us this: "Saying, save yourselves from this untoward generation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:97
verses.text: "They then, that gladly received his words," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:98
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:99
verses.text: ) they approved of what had been said, although fraught with terror, and after their assent given, proceed at once to baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:100
verses.text: "And they continued" it is written, "steadfastly in the doctrine" (or, "teaching") "of the Apostles" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:101
verses.text: ): for it was not for one day, no nor for two or three days that they were under teaching as being persons who had gone over to a different course of life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:102
verses.text: "And they continued with one accord in the Apostles' doctrine," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:103
verses.text: The expression is not, ὁμοὕ "together," but ὁμοθυμαδὸν, "with one accord;" ("and daily," he says afterwards, "they were continuing with one accord in the temple,") i-e: with one soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:104
verses.text: And here again in his conciseness, he does not relate the teaching given; for as young children, the Apostles nourished them with spiritual food.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:105
verses.text: "And fear came upon every soul" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:106
verses.text: ): clearly, of those, as well, who did not believe; namely, upon seeing so great a change all at once effected, and besides in consequence of the miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:107
verses.text: "And all that believed were together, and had all things in common," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:108
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:109
verses.text: ) They are all become angels on a sudden; all of them continuing in prayer and hearing, they saw that spiritual things are common, and no one there has more than other, and they speedily came together (ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ), to the same thing in common, even to the imparting to all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:110
verses.text: "And all the believing" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:111
verses.text: ), it says, were ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ: and to see that this does not mean that they were together in place, observe what follows "And had all things common".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:112
verses.text: "All," it says: not one with the exception of another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:113
verses.text: This was an angelic commonwealth, not to call anything of theirs their own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:114
verses.text: Forthwith the root of evils was cut out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:115
verses.text: By what they did, they showed what they had heard: this was that which he said, "Save yourselves from this untoward generation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:116
verses.text: —"And daily continuing with one accord in the temple".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:117
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:118
verses.text: ) Since they are become three thousand, they take them abroad now: and withal, the boldness imparted by the Spirit being great: and daily they went up as to a sacred place, as frequently we find Peter and John doing this: for at present they disturbed none of the Jewish observances.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:119
verses.text: And this honor too passed over to the place; the eating in the house.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:120
verses.text: In what house? In the Temple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:121
verses.text: Observe the increase of piety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:122
verses.text: They cast away their riches, and rejoiced, and had great gladness, for greater were the riches they received without labor (ἄπονα Cat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:123
verses.text: al.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:124
verses.text: ἀγαθά).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:125
verses.text: None reproached, none envied, none grudged; no pride, no contempt was there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:126
verses.text: As children they did indeed account themselves to be under teaching: as new born babes, such was their disposition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:127
verses.text: Yet why use this faint image? If you remember how it was when God shook our city with an earthquake, how subdued all men were.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:128
verses.text: (Infra, Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:129
verses.text: xli.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:130
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:131
verses.text: ) Such was the case then with those converts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:132
verses.text: No knavery, no villany then: such is the effect of fear, of affliction! No talk of "mine" and "thine" then.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:133
verses.text: Hence gladness waited at their table; no one seemed to eat of his own, or of another's;—I grant this may seem a riddle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:134
verses.text: Neither did they consider their brethren's property foreign to themselves; it was the property of a Master; nor again deemed they aught their own, all was the brethren's.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:135
verses.text: The poor man knew no shame, the rich no haughtiness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:136
verses.text: This is gladness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:137
verses.text: The latter deemed himself the obliged and fortunate party; the others felt themselves as honored herein, and closely were they bound together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:138
verses.text: For indeed, because when people make doles of money, there are apt to be insults, pride, grudging; therefore says the Apostle, "Not grudgingly, or of necessity".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:139
verses.text: —( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:140
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:141
verses.text: ) "With gladness and simplicity of heart," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:142
verses.text: See of how many things he bears witness to them! Genuine faith, upright conduct, perseverance in hearing, in prayers, in singleness, in cheerfulness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:143
verses.text: "Praising God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:144
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:145
verses.text: ) Two things there were which might deject them; their abstemious living, and the loss of their property.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:146
verses.text: Yet on both these accounts did they rejoice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:147
verses.text: "And having favor with all the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:148
verses.text: For who but must love men of this character, as common fathers? They conceived no malice toward each other; they committed all to the grace of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:149
verses.text: "With all the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:150
verses.text: Fear there was none; yea, though they had taken their position in the midst of dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:151
verses.text: By singleness, however, he denotes their entire virtue, far surpassing their contempt of riches, their abstinence, and their preseverance in prayer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:152
verses.text: For thus also they offered pure praise to God: this is to praise God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:153
verses.text: But observe also here how they immediately obtain their reward.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:154
verses.text: "Having favor with all the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:155
verses.text: They were engaging, and highly beloved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:156
verses.text: For who would not prize and admire their simplicity of character; who would not be linked to one in whom was nothing underhand? To whom too does salvation belong, but to these? To whom those great marvels? Was it not to shepherds that the Gospel was first preached? and to Joseph, being a man of simple mind, insomuch that he did not let a suspicion of adultery frighten him into doing wrong? Did not God elect rustics, those artless men? For it is written, "Blessed is every simple soul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:157
verses.text: (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:158
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:159
verses.text: ) And again, "He that walketh simply, walketh surely".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:160
verses.text: (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:161
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:162
verses.text: ) "True," you will say, "but prudence also is needed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:163
verses.text: Why, what is simplicity, I pray you, but prudence? For when you suspect no evil, neither can you fabricate any: when you have no annoyances, neither can you remember injuries.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:164
verses.text: Has any one insulted you? You were not pained.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:165
verses.text: Has any one reviled you? You were nothing hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:166
verses.text: Has he envied you? Still you had no hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:167
verses.text: Simplicity is a high road to true philosophy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:168
verses.text: None so beautiful in soul as the simple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:169
verses.text: For as in regard of personal appearance, he that is sullen, and downcast, and reserved (σύννους), even if he be good-looking, loses much of his beauty; while he that relaxes his countenance, and gently smiles, enhances his good looks; so in respect of the soul, he that is reserved, if he have ten thousand good points, disfigures them; but the frank and simple, just the reverse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:170
verses.text: A man of this last description may be safely made a friend, and when at variance easily reconciled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:171
