verses.text: No need of guards and outposts, no need of chains and fetters with such an one; but great is his own freedom, and that of those who associate with him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:172
verses.text: But what, you will say, will such a man do if he fall among wicked people? God, Who has commanded us to be simple-minded, will stretch out His hand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:173
verses.text: What was more guileless than David? What more wicked than Saul? Yet who triumphed? Again, in Joseph's case; did not he in simplicity approach his master's wife, she him with wicked art? Yet what, I pray, was he the worse? Furthermore, what more simple than was Abel? what more malicious than Cain? And Joseph again, had he not dealt artlessly with his brethren? Was not this the cause of his eminence, that he spoke out unsuspiciously, while they received his words in malice? He declared once and again his dreams unreservedly; and then again he set off to them carrying provisions; he used no caution; he committed all to God: nay, the more they held him in the light of an enemy, the more did he treat them as brothers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:174
verses.text: God had power not to have suffered him to fall into their hands; but that the wonder might be made manifest, how, though they do their worst, he shall be higher than they: though the blow do come upon him, it comes from another, not from himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:175
verses.text: On the contrary, the wicked man strikes himself first, and none other than himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:176
verses.text: "For alone," it is said, "shall he bear his troubles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:177
verses.text: (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:178
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:179
verses.text: ) Ever in him the soul is full of dejection, his thoughts being ever entangled: whether he must hear aught or say aught, he does all with complaints, with accusation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:180
verses.text: Far, very far from such do friendship and harmony make their abode: but fightings are there, and enmities, and all unpleasantness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:181
verses.text: They that are such suspect even themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:182
verses.text: To these not even sleep is sweet, nor anything else.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:183
verses.text: And have they a wife also, lo, they are enemies and at war with all: what endless jealousies, what unceasing fear! Aye, the wicked, πονηρὸς has his name from πονεἵν, "to have trouble".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:184
verses.text: And, indeed, thus the Scripture is ever calling "wickedness" by the name of labor; as, for instance, "Under his tongue is toil and labor;" and again, "In the midst of them is toil and labor".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:185
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:186
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:187
verses.text: ; xc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:188
verses.text: ; and lv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:189
verses.text: )  Now if any one should wonder, whence those who had at first been of this last class, now are so different, let him learn that affliction was the cause, affliction, that school-mistress of heavenly wisdom, that mother of piety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:190
verses.text: When riches were done away with, wickedness also disappeared.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:191
verses.text: True, say you, for this is the very thing I am asking about; but whence comes all the wickedness there is now? How is it that it came into the minds of those three thousand and five thousand straightway, to choose virtue, and that they simultaneously became Christian philosophers, whereas now hardly one is to be found? how was it that they then were in such harmony? What was it, that made them resolute and active? What was it that so suddenly inflamed them? The reason is, that they drew near with much piety; that honors were not so sought after as they are now; that they transferred their thoughts to things future, and looked for nothing of things present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:192
verses.text: This is the sign of an ardent mind, to encounter perils; this was their idea of Christianity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:193
verses.text: We take a different view, we seek our comfort here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:194
verses.text: The result is, that we shall not even obtain this, when the time is come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:195
verses.text: "What are we to do?" asked those men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:196
verses.text: We, just the contrary—"What shall we do?" What behooved to be done, they did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:197
verses.text: We, quite the reverse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:198
verses.text: Those men condemned themselves, despaired of saving themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:199
verses.text: This is what made them such as they were.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:200
verses.text: They knew what a gift they had received.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:201
verses.text: But how can you become like them, when you do everything in an opposite spirit? They heard, and were forthwith baptized.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:202
verses.text: They did not speak those cold words which we do now, nor did they contrive delays (p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:203
verses.text: , note ); and yet they had heard all the requirements: but that word, "Save yourselves from this generation," made them to be not sluggish; rather they welcomed the exhortation; and that they did welcome it, they proved by their deeds, they showed what manner of men they were.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:204
verses.text: They entered at once the lists, and took off the coat; whereas we do enter, but we intend to fight with our coat on.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:205
verses.text: This is the cause that our antagonist has so little trouble, for we get entangled in our own movements, and are continually thrown down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:206
verses.text: We do precisely the same thing as he who, having to cope with a man frantic, breathing fire; and seeing him, a professed wrestler, covered with dust, tawny, stripped, clotted with dirt from the sand and sun, and running down with sweat and oil and dirt; himself, smelling of perfumes, should put on his silken garments, and his gold shoes, and his robe hanging down to his heels, and his golden trinkets on the head, and so descend into the arena, and grapple with him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:207
verses.text: Such a one will not only be impeded, but being taken up with the sole idea of not staining or rending his fine clothes, will tumble at the very first onset, and withal will suffer that which he chiefly dreaded, the damage of those his fond delights.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:208
verses.text: The time for the contest is come, and say, are you putting on your silks? It is the time of exercise, the hour of the race, and are you adorning yourself as for a procession? Look not to outward things, but to the inward.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:209
verses.text: For by the thoughts about these things the soul is hampered on all sides, as if by strong cords, so that she cannot let you raise a hand, or contend against the adversary; and makes you soft and effeminate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:210
verses.text: One may think himself, even when released from all these ties, well off, to be enabled to conquer that impure power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:211
verses.text: And on this account Christ too did not allow the parting with riches alone to suffice, but what saith He? "Sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and come and follow Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:212
verses.text: (Mark x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:213
verses.text: ) Now if, even when we cast away our riches, we are not yet in a safe position, but stand still in need of some further art and close practice; much more, if we retain them, shall we fail to achieve great things, and, instead thereof, become a laughing-stock to the spectators, and to the evil one himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:214
verses.text: For even though there were no devil, though there were none to wrestle with us, yet ten thousand roads on all sides lead the lover of money to hell.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:215
verses.text: Where now are they who ask why the devil was made (διατί ὁ δ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:216
verses.text: γέγονεν;)? Behold here the devil has no hand in the work, we do it all ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:217
verses.text: Of a truth they of the hills might have a right to speak thus, who after they had given proof of their temperance, their contempt of wealth and disregard of all such things, have infinitely preferred to abandon father, and houses, and lands, and wife, and children.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:218
verses.text: Yet, they are the last to speak so: but the men who at no time ought to say it, these do say it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:219
verses.text: Those are indeed wrestlings with the devil; these he does not think worth entering into.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:220
verses.text: You will say, But it is the devil who instils this same covetousness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:221
verses.text: Well, flee from it, do not harbor it, O man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:222
verses.text: Suppose now, you see one flinging out filth from some upper story, and at the same time a person seeing it thrown out, yet standing there and receiving it all on his head: you not only do not pity him, but you are angry, and tell him it serves him right; and, "Do not be a fool," everyone cries out to him, and lays the blame not so much on the other for shooting out the filth, as on him for letting it come on him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:223
verses.text: But now, you know that covetousness is of the devil; you know that it is the cause of ten thousand evils; you see him flinging out, like filth, his noisome imaginations; and do you not see that you are receiving on your bare head his nastiness, when it needed but to turn aside a little to escape it altogether? Just as our man by shifting his position would have escaped; so, do you refuse to admit such imaginations, ward off the lust.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:224
verses.text: And how am I to do this? you will ask.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:225
verses.text: Were you a Gentile, and had eyes for things present alone, the matter perhaps might be one of considerable difficulty, and yet even the Gentiles have achieved as much; but you—a man in expectation of heaven and heavenly bliss—and you to ask, "How am I to repel bad thoughts?" Were I saying the contrary, then you might doubt: did I say, covet riches, "How shall I covet riches," you might answer, "seeing such things as I do?" Tell me, if gold and precious stones were set before you, and I were to say, Desire lead, would there not be reason for hesitation? For you would say, How can I? But if I said, Do not desire it; this had been plainer to understand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:226
verses.text: I do not marvel at those who despise, but at those who despise not riches.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:227
verses.text: This is the character of a soul exceeding full of stupidity, no better than flies and gnats, a soul crawling upon the earth, wallowing in filth, destitute of all high ideas.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:228
verses.text: What is it you say? Are you destined to inherit eternal life; and do you say, how shall I despise the present life for the future? What, can the things be put in competition? You are to receive a royal vest; and say you, How shall I despise these rags? You are going to be led into the king's palace; and do you say, How shall I despise this present hovel? Of a truth, we ourselves are to blame in every point, we who do not choose to let ourselves be stirred up ever so little.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:229
verses.text: For the willing have succeeded, and that with great zeal and facility.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 24:230
verses.text: Would that you might be persuaded by our exhortation, and succeed too, and become imitators of those who have been successful, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, and power, and honor, now and ever, and world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:1
verses.text: Homily VIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:2
verses.text: Acts III.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:3
verses.text: "Now Peter and John went up together into the temple, at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:4
verses.text: Everywhere we find these two Apostles in great harmony together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:5
verses.text: "To him Simon Peter beckoned".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:6
verses.text: (John xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:7
verses.text: ) These two also "came together to the sepulchre.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:8
verses.text: (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:9
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:10
verses.text: et seq.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:11
verses.text: ) And concerning John, Peter said unto Christ, "And what shall this man do?" (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:12
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:13
verses.text: ) Now as for the other miracles, the writer of this book omits them; but he mentions the miracle by which they were all put in commotion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:14
verses.text: Observe again that they do not come to them purposely; so clear were they of ambition, so closely did they imitate their Master.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:15
verses.text: Why now did they go up to the temple? Did they still live as Jews? No, but for expediency (χρησίμως).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:16
verses.text: A miraculous sign again takes place, which both confirms the converts, and draws over the rest; and such, as they were a sign for having wrought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:17
verses.text: The disease was in the nature of the man, and baffled the art of medicine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:18
verses.text: He had been forty years lame (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:19
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:20
verses.text: ), as the writer says afterwards, and no one during all that time had cured him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:21
verses.text: And the most obstinate diseases are those which are born with men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:22
verses.text: It was a great calamity, insomuch that even to provide for himself his necessary sustenance was impossible for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:23
verses.text: The man was conspicuous both from the place, and from his malady.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:24
verses.text: Hear how the matter is related.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:25
verses.text: "And a certain man, lame from his mother's womb, was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:27
verses.text: ) He sought to receive alms, and he did not know who the men were.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:28
verses.text: "Who seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple, asked an alms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:29
verses.text: And Peter, fastening his eyes upon him, with John, said, Look on us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:30
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:32
verses.text: ) Yet, not even so were the man's thoughts elevated, but he persisted in his importunity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:33
verses.text: For such is poverty; upon a refusal, it compels people still to persist.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:34
verses.text: Let this put us to shame who fall back in our prayers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:35
verses.text: But observe, I pray you, Peter's gentleness: for he said, "Look on us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:36
verses.text: So truly did their very bearing, of itself, betoken their character.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:37
verses.text: "And he gave heed unto them, expecting to receive something of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:38
verses.text: Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have I give thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:41
verses.text: ) He did not say, I give thee something much better than silver or gold: but what? "In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:42
verses.text: And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:43
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:44
verses.text: ) Such was also the way of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:45
verses.text: Often He healed by word, often by an act, often also He stretched forth the hand, where men were somewhat weak in faith, that the cure might not appear to be spontaneous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:46
verses.text: "And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:47
verses.text: This act made manifest the Resurrection, for it was an image of the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:48
verses.text: "And immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:49
verses.text: And he leaping up stood, and walked".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:50
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:51
verses.text: ) Perhaps it was by way of trying himself that he put it thus to further proof, whether perchance the thing done might not be to no purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:52
verses.text: His feet were weak; it was not that he had lost them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:53
verses.text: Some say that he did not even know how to walk.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:54
verses.text: "And entered with them into the temple".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:55
verses.text: Of a truth it was marvellous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:56
verses.text: The Apostles do not urge him; but of his own accord he follows, by the act of following pointing out his benefactors.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:57
verses.text: "And leaping and praising God;" not admiring them, but God that wrought by them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:58
verses.text: The man was grateful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:59
verses.text: "Now Peter and John went up together into the temple," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:60
verses.text: You observe how they continued in prayer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:61
verses.text: "The ninth hour:" there they prayed together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:62
verses.text: "And a certain man," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:63
verses.text: The man was in the act of being carried at that instant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:64
verses.text: "Whom they laid daily:" (his bearers carried him away:) "at the gate," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:65
verses.text: just when people went into the temple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:66
verses.text: And that you may not suppose that they carried him for some other purpose, but that it was in order that he might receive alms, hear what the writer says: "so that he might receive alms of those entering into the temple".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:67
verses.text: (Recapitulation of vv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:68
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:69
verses.text: ) And this is the reason why he also makes mention of the places, to give evidence of what he relates.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:70
verses.text: "And how was it," you may ask, "that they did not present him to Christ?" Perhaps they were certain unbelieving men, that haunted the temple, as in fact neither did they present him to the Apostles, when they saw them entering, after having done such great miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:71
verses.text: "He asked," it is written, "to receive an alms".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:72
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:73
verses.text: ) Their bearing marked them as certain devout and righteous men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:74
verses.text: "And Peter fastening his eyes upon him, with John, said," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:75
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:76
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:77
verses.text: ) And observe how John is everywhere silent, while Peter makes excuse for him also; "Silver and gold," he says, "have I none".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:78
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:79
verses.text: ) He does not say, I have none here, as we are wont to speak, but absolutely, I have none.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:80
verses.text: "What then?" he might say, "do you take no notice of me, your suppliant?" Not so, but of what I have, receive thou.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:81
verses.text: Do you remark how unassuming Peter is, how he makes no display even to the object of his beneficence? "In the name," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:82
verses.text: "And he took him by the hand," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:83
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:84
verses.text: ) And the mouth and the hand did all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:85
verses.text: Such sort of persons were the Jews; lame, and the right thing being to ask for health, these same ask for money, grovelling on the ground: for this it was that they beset the temple—to get money.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:86
verses.text: What then does Peter? He did not despise him; he did not look about for some rich subject; he did not say, If the miracle is not done to some great one (εἰς ἐκεἵνον), nothing great is done: he did not look for some honor from him, no, nor heal him in the presence of people; for the man was at the entrance, not where the multitude were, that is, within.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:87
verses.text: But Peter sought no such object; nor upon entering did he proclaim the matter: no, it was by his bearing that he attracted the lame man to ask.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:88
verses.text: And the wonder is, that he believed so readily.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:89
verses.text: For those who are set free from diseases of long standing, hardly believe their very eyesight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:90
verses.text: Once healed, he remains with the Apostles, giving thanks to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:91
verses.text: "And he entered," it is said, "with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:92
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:93
verses.text: ) Observe how restless he is, in the eagerness of his delight, at the same time shutting the mouths of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:94
verses.text: Also, that he leaped, was to prevent the suspicion of hypocrisy; for after all, this was beyond the possibility of deception.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:95
verses.text: For if previously he was totally unable to walk, even when hunger pressed hard (and indeed he would not have chosen to share with his bearers the proceeds of his begging, if he had been able to manage for himself), this holds still more in the present case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:96
verses.text: And how should he have feigned in behalf of those who had given him no alms? But the man was grateful, even after his recovery.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:97
verses.text: And thus on either side his faith is shown, both by his thankfulness, and by the recent event.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:98
verses.text: He was so well known to all, that "they recognized him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:99
verses.text: And all the people," it says, "saw him walking and praising God; and they recognized (ἐπεγίνωσκον) that it was he which sat for alms at the Beautiful gate of the temple".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:101
verses.text: ) It is well said, "they recognized," inasmuch as he was one unknown now by reason of what had happened: for we use this term with regard to objects, which we find a difficulty in recognizing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:102
verses.text: "And they were filled with wonder and amazement at that which had happened unto him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:103
verses.text: Needs must it be believed that the name of Christ remits sins, seeing it produces even such effects as this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:104
verses.text: ("And as he held Peter and John, all the people came together at the porch that is called Solomon's, greatly wondering".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:105
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:106
verses.text: ) From his good feelings and love towards the Apostles, the lame man would not leave them; perhaps he was thanking them openly, and praising them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:107
verses.text: "And all the people," it is said, "ran together unto them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:108
verses.text: And when Peter saw them, he answered".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:109
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:110
verses.text: ) Again it is he who acts, and addresses the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:111
verses.text: And in the former instance, it was the circumstance of the tongues that aroused them to hearing, now it was this miracle; then, he took occasion to speak from their accusations now, from their supposition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:112
verses.text: Let us then consider, in what this address differs from the former, and in what it agrees with that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:113
verses.text: The former was held in a house, before any one has come over, and before they themselves have wrought anything; this, when all are wondering, and the healed man is standing by; when none doubt, as in the other case where some said "These men are full of new wine".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:114
verses.text: (Acts xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:115
verses.text: ) At the one, he was surrounded by all the Apostles as he spoke; but at this, he has John alone; for by this time he is bold, and become more energetic.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:116
verses.text: Such is the nature of virtue; once started, it advances, and never stops.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:117
verses.text: Observe also how it was divinely ordered, that the miracle should take place in the temple, that others also might wax bold, while the Apostles work not in holes (εἰς καταδύσεις) and corners, and in secret: though not in the interior of the temple either, where the greater number were.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:118
verses.text: How then, I pray you, was it believed? The man himself who was healed proclaimed the benefit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:119
verses.text: For there was no reason why he should lie, nor why he should have joined a different set of people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:120
verses.text: Either then it was because of the spaciousness of the place, that he there wrought the miracle, or because the spot was retired.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:121
verses.text: And observe the event.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:122
verses.text: They went up for one object, and they accomplished another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 25:123
verses.text: Thus also did Cornelius: he prayed and fasted.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:1
verses.text: But hitherto they always call Him, "of Nazareth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:2
verses.text: "In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth," said Peter, walk.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:3
verses.text: For in the first instance, the thing required was, that He should be believed in.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:4
verses.text: Let us not, I pray you, give over at the beginning of the story: and if one has named some particular achievement of virtue, and then has dropped it for awhile, let us begin over again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:5
verses.text: If we get into the right mood (ἐν ἕξει), we shall soon arrive at the end, soon reach the summit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:6
verses.text: For earnestness, it is said, begets earnestness, and dulness begets dulness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:7
verses.text: He who has effected some little reformation, thereby receives encouragement to approach greater things, and thence again to go on something more than that; and just as it is with fire, the more wood it lays hold on, the more vehement it becomes, so likewise zeal, the more pious reflections it kindles, the more effectually is it armed against their opposites.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:8
verses.text: As, for example: There are set in us, like so many thorns, perjury, falsehood hypocrisy, deceit, dishonesty, abusiveness, scoffing, buffoonery, indecency, scurrility; again under another head, covetousness, rapacity, injustice, calumny, insidiousness; again, wicked lust, uncleanness, lewdness, fornication, adultery; again, envy, emulation, anger, wrath, rancor, revenge, blasphemy, and numberless others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:9
verses.text: If we effect a reformation in the first instances, not only in them will the success have been achieved, but through them in the following cases also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:10
verses.text: For reason has then gained more strength to overthrow those other vices.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:11
verses.text: For instance, if he, who has frequently sworn, once extirpates that satanic habit, he has not only gained this point, but a habit of piety in other respects will have been brought in.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:12
verses.text: For no one, I suppose, averse to swearing would easily consent to do any other wicked act; he will feel a reverence for the virtue already acquired.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:13
verses.text: Just as the man who wears a beautiful robe, will blush to roll himself in the mire; so is it also here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:14
verses.text: From this beginning he will come to learn not to be angry, not to strike, not to insult.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:15
verses.text: For if once he has come right in little matters, the whole affair is done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:16
verses.text: Often, however, something of this sort takes place, that a person has once reformed, and then again through carelessness falls back into the old sins but too readily, so that the case becomes irremediable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:17
verses.text: For instance, we have made it a law to ourselves not to swear; we have got on well, for some three, or even four days; after that being hard put to it, we scattered away the whole of our collected gain; we then fall into indolence and recklessness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:18
verses.text: Still it is not right to give over; one must set to work zealously again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:19
verses.text: For it is said, he that has built up a house, and then sees his building pulled down, will have less spirit for building again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:20
verses.text: Yes, but for all this, one must not be dispirited, but must once more set to work zealously.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:21
verses.text: Let us then lay down daily laws for ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:22
verses.text: For a time let us begin with the easier.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:23
verses.text: Let us retrench all that superfluity of paths, and put a bridle on our tongues; let no one swear by God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:24
verses.text: Here is no outlay, here is no fatigue, here is no cost of time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:25
verses.text: It is sufficient to will, and all is done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:26
verses.text: It is a matter of habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:27
verses.text: I beseech and entreat you, let us contribute thus much of zeal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:28
verses.text: Tell me, if I had bid you contribute your money, would not each one of you readily cast in according to his ability? If you saw me in extreme danger, would you not, if it had been possible, have cut off your own flesh to give me? Well, I am in danger now, and in great danger, such indeed that, were I withal confined to a dungeon, or had I received ten thousand stripes, or were a convict in the mines, I could not suffer more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:29
verses.text: Reach me then the hand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:30
verses.text: Consider how great is the danger, that I should not have been able to reform this which is least: I say "least" in regard to the labor required.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:31
verses.text: What shall I have to say hereafter, when thus called to account? "Why did you not remonstrate? why did you not enjoin? why did you not lay the law before them? why did you not check the disobedient?" It will not be enough for me to say, that I did admonish.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:32
verses.text: It will be answered, "You ought to have used more vehement rebuke; since Eli also admonished".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:33
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:34
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:35
verses.text: ) But God forbid I should compare you with Eli's sons.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:36
verses.text: Indeed, he did admonish them and say, "Nay, my sons, do not so; evil is the report that I hear of you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:37
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:38
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:39
verses.text: ) But subsequently the Scripture saith, that he did not admonish his sons: since he did not admonish them severely, or with threats.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:40
verses.text: For is it not strange indeed, that in the synagogues of the Jews the laws are in such force, and whatever the teacher enjoins is performed; while here we are thus despised and rejected? It is not my own glory that I care for (my glory is your good report), but it is for your salvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:41
verses.text: Every day we lift up our voice, and shout in your ears.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:42
verses.text: But there is none to hear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:43
verses.text: Still we take no strong measures.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:44
verses.text: I fear we shall have to give an account at the coming Day of this excessive and unseasonable leniency.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:45
verses.text: Wherefore, with a loud and clear voice, I proclaim to all and testify, that those who are notorious for this transgression, who utter words which come "of the evil one," (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:46
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:47
verses.text: ) (for such is swearing,) shall not step over the threshold of the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:48
verses.text: Let this present month be the time allowed you for reforming in this matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:49
verses.text: Talk not to me, "Necessity of business compels me to use oaths, else people do not believe me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:50
verses.text: To begin with this, retrench those oaths which come merely of habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:51
verses.text: I know many will laugh, but it is better to be laughed at now, than wept for hereafter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:52
verses.text: They will laugh, who are mad.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:53
verses.text: For who, I ask, in his right mind would laugh at the keeping of the commandment? But suppose they do; why, it will not be at us, but at Christ, that such men will laugh.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:54
verses.text: You shudder at the word! I knew you would.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:55
verses.text: Now if this law were of my making, at me would be the laughing; but if Another be the Lawgiver, the jeering passes over to Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:56
verses.text: Yes, and Christ was once spit upon, and smitten with the palm, smitten upon the face.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:57
verses.text: Now also He bears with this, and it is no wonder (οὐδὲν ἀπεικὸς)! For this, hell is prepared; for this, the worm that dieth not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:58
verses.text: Behold, again I say and testify; let him laugh that will, let him scoff that listeth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:59
verses.text: Hereunto are we set, to be laughed at and mocked, to suffer all things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:60
verses.text: We are "the offscouring" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:61
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:62
verses.text: ) or the world, as blessed Paul says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:63
verses.text: If any man refuse to conform to this order, that man I, by my word, as with a trumpet's blast, do prohibit to set foot over the Church's threshold, be he prince, be he even the crowned head.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:64
verses.text: Either depose me from this station, or if I am to remain, expose me not to danger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:65
verses.text: I cannot bear to ascend this throne, without effecting some great reformation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:66
verses.text: For if this be impossible, it is better to stand below.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:67
verses.text: Nothing more wretched than a ruler who does his people no good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:68
verses.text: Do exert yourselves, and attend to this, I entreat you; and let us strive, and of a surety more will come of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:69
verses.text: Fast, entreat God (and we will do the same with you) that this pernicious habit may be eradicated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:70
verses.text: It is no great matter, to become teachers to the world; no small honor to have it said everywhere, that really in this city there is not a man that swears.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:71
verses.text: If this come to pass, you will receive the reward not only of your own good works; indeed what I am to you, this you will become to the world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:72
verses.text: Assuredly others also will emulate you; assuredly you will be a candle set upon a candlestick.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:73
verses.text: And is this, you will say, the whole matter? No, this is not all, but this is a beginning of other virtues.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:74
verses.text: He who swears not, will certainly attain unto piety in other respects, whether he will or not, by dint of self-respect and awe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:75
verses.text: But you will urge that most men do not keep to it, but fall away.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:76
verses.text: Well, better one man that doeth the will of the Lord, than ten thousand transgressors.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:77
verses.text: In fact, hereby is everything subverted, everything turned upside down, I mean, because after the fashion of the Theatre we desire numbers not a select number.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:78
verses.text: For what indeed will a multitude be able to profit? Would you learn that it is the saints, not the numbers, which make the multitude? Lead out to war ten hundred thousand men, and one saint, and let us see who achieves the most? Joshua the son of Nun went out to war, and alone achieved all; the rest were of no use.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:79
verses.text: Wouldest thou see, beloved, that the great multitude, when it does not the will of God, is no better than a thing of naught? I wish indeed, and desire, and with pleasure would be torn in pieces, to adorn the Church with a multitude, yea, but a select multitude; yet if this be impossible, that the few should be select, is my desire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:80
verses.text: Do you not see, that it is better to possess one precious stone, than ten thousand farthing pieces? Do you not see that it is better to have the eye sound, than to be loaded with flesh, and yet deprived of sight? Do you not see that it is better to have one healthy sheep, than ten thousand with the murrain; that fine children, though few, are better than many children diseased withal; that in the Kingdom there will be few, but in hell many? What have I to do with a multitude? what profit therein? None.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:81
verses.text: Rather they are a plague to the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:82
verses.text: It is as if one who had the option of ten healthy persons or ten thousand sick folks, should take to himself the latter in addition to the ten.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:83
verses.text: The many who do nothing well, will avail us only for punishment hereafter, and disgrace for the time being.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:84
verses.text: For no one will urge it as a point in our favor that we are many; we shall be blamed for being unprofitable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:85
verses.text: In fact, this is what men always tell us, when we say, We are many; "aye, but bad," they answer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:86
verses.text: Behold again: I give warning, and proclaim with a loud voice, let no one think it a laughing matter: I will exclude and prohibit the disobedient; and as long as I sit on this throne, I will give up not one of its rights.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:87
verses.text: If any one depose me from it, then I am no longer responsible; as long as I am responsible, I cannot disregard them; on account not of my own punishment, but of your salvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:88
verses.text: For I do exceedingly long for your salvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:89
verses.text: To advance it, I endure pain and vexation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 28:90
verses.text: But yield your obedience, that both here and hereafter you may receive a plentiful reward, and that we may in common reap eternal blessings; through the grace and mercy of the only-begotten Son of God; to Whom with the Father and the Holy Ghost be glory, power, and honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:1
verses.text: Homily IX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:2
verses.text: Acts III.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:3
verses.text: "And when Peter saw it, he answered unto the people, Ye men of Israel, why marvel ye at this, or why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we have made this man to walk?"  There is greater freedom of speech in this harangue, than in the former.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:4
verses.text: Not that he was afraid on the former occasion, but the persons whom he addressed there, being jesters and scoffers, would not have borne it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:5
verses.text: Hence in the beginning of that address he also bespeaks their attention by his preamble; "Be this known unto you, and hearken to my words".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:6
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:7
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:8
verses.text: ) But here there is no need of this management.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:9
verses.text: (κατασκευἥς.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:10
verses.text: ) For his hearers were not in a state of indifference.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:11
verses.text: The miracle had aroused them all; they were even full of fear and amazement.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:12
verses.text: Wherefore also there was no need of beginning at that point, but rather with a different topic; by which, in fact, he powerfully conciliated them, namely, by rejecting the glory which was to be had from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:13
verses.text: For nothing is so advantageous, and so likely to pacify the hearers, as to say nothing about one's self of an honorable nature, but, on the contrary, to obviate all surmise of wishing to do so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:14
verses.text: And, in truth, much more did they increase their glory by despising glory, and showing that what had just taken place was no human act, but a Divine work; and that it was their part to join with the beholders in admiration, rather than to receive it from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:15
verses.text: Do you see how clear of all ambition he is, and how he repels the honor paid to him? In the same manner also did the ancient fathers; for instance, Daniel said, "Not for any wisdom that is in me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:16
verses.text: (Dan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:17
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:18
verses.text: ) And again Joseph, "Do not interpretations belong to God?" (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:19
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:20
verses.text: ) And David, "When the lion and the bear came, in the name of the Lord I rent them with my hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:21
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:22
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:23
verses.text: ) And so likewise here the Apostles, "Why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:24
verses.text: ) Nay, not even this; for not by our own merit did we draw down the Divine influence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:25
verses.text: "The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:26
verses.text: See how assiduously he thrusts himself (εἰσωθει) upon the fathers of old, lest he should appear to be introducing a new doctrine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:27
verses.text: In the former address he appealed to the patriarch David, here he appeals to Abraham and the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:28
verses.text: "Hath glorified His Servant Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:29
verses.text: Again a lowly expression, like as in the opening address.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:30
verses.text: But at this point he proceeds to enlarge upon the outrage, and exalts the heinousness of the deed, no longer, as before, throwing a veil over it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:31
verses.text: This he does, wishing to work upon them more powerfully.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:32
verses.text: For the more he proved them accountable, the better his purpose were effected.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:33
verses.text: "Hath glorified," he says, "His Servant Jesus, Whom ye delivered up, and denied Him in the presence of Pilate, when he was determined to let him go".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:34
verses.text: The charge is twofold: Pilate was desirous to let Him go; you would not, when he was willing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:35
verses.text: "But ye denied the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted unto you; and killed the Prince (or Author) of Life: Whom God hath raised from the dead; whereof we are witnesses".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:38
verses.text: ) Ye desired a robber instead of Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:39
verses.text: He shows the great aggravation of the act.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:40
verses.text: As he has them under his hand, he now strikes hard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:41
verses.text: "The Prince of Life," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:42
verses.text: In these words he establishes the doctrine of the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:43
verses.text: "Whom God hath raised from the dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:44
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:45
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:46
verses.text: ) "Whence doth this appear?" He no longer refers to the Prophets, but to himself, inasmuch as now he has a right to be believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:47
verses.text: Before, when he affirmed that He was risen, he adduced the testimony of David; now, having said it, he alleges the College of Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:48
verses.text: "Whereof we are witnesses," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:49
verses.text: "And His name, through faith in His name, hath made this man strong, whom ye see and know: yea, the faith which is by Him hath given him this perfect soundness in the presence of you all".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:50
verses.text: Seeking to declare the matter (ζητὥν τὸ πρἅγμα εὶπεἵν), he straightway brings forward the sign: "In the presence," he says, "of you all".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:51
verses.text: As he had borne hard upon them, and had shown that He Whom they crucified had risen, again he relaxes, by giving them the power of repentance; "And now, brethren, I wot that through ignorance ye did it, as did also your rulers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:52
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:53
verses.text: ) This is one ground of excuse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:54
verses.text: The second is of a different kind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:55
verses.text: As Joseph speaks to his brethren, "God did send me before you (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:56
verses.text: xlv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:57
verses.text: ); what in the former speech he had briefly said, in the words, "Him, being delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, ye have taken,"—this he here enlarges upon: "But what God before had showed by the mouth of all His Prophets, that His Christ should suffer, He hath so fulfilled".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:59
verses.text: ) At the same time showing, that it was not of their doing, if this be proved, that it took place after God's counsel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:60
verses.text: He alludes to those words with which they had reviled Him on the Cross, namely "Let Him deliver Him, if He will have Him; for He said, I am the Son of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:61
verses.text: If He trust in God, let Him now come down from the cross".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:62
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:63
verses.text: xxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:64
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:65
verses.text: ) O foolish men, were these idle words? It must needs so come to pass, and the prophets bear witness thereunto.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:66
verses.text: Therefore if He descended not, it was for no weakness of His own that He did not come down, but for very power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:67
verses.text: And Peter puts this by way of apology for the Jews, hoping that they may also close with what he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:68
verses.text: "He hath so fulfilled," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:69
verses.text: Do you see now how he refers everything to that source? "Repent ye therefore," he says, "and be converted".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:70
verses.text: He does not add, "from your sins;" but, "that your sins, may be blotted out," means the same thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:71
verses.text: And then he adds the gain: "So shall the times of refreshing come from the presence of the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:72
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:73
verses.text: ) This betokens them in a sad state, brought low by many wars.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:74
verses.text: For it is to the case of one on fire, and craving comfort, that the expression applies.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:75
verses.text: And see now how he advances.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:76
verses.text: In his first sermon, he but slightly hinted at the resurrection, and Christ's sitting in heaven; but here he also speaks of His visible advent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:77
verses.text: "And He shall send Jesus the Christ ordained (for you), "Whom the heaven must (i-e: must of necessity) receive, until the times of the restitution of all things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:78
verses.text: The reason why He does not now come is clear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:79
verses.text: "Which God hath spoken," he continues, "by the mouth of His holy prophets since the world began.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:80
verses.text: For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A Prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:81
verses.text: Before, he had spoken of David, here he speaks of Moses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:82
verses.text: "Of all things," he says, "which He hath spoken".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:83
verses.text: But he does not say, "which Christ," but, "which God hath spoken by the mouth of all His holy prophets since the world began".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:84
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:85
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:86
verses.text: ) Then he betakes him to the ground of credibility, saying, "A Prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; Him shall ye hear in all things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:87
verses.text: And then the greatness of the punishment: "And it shall come to pass, that every soul which will not hear that Prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:88
verses.text: Yea, and all the prophets, from Samuel and those that follow, after, as many as have spoken have likewise foretold of these days".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:89
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:90
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:91
verses.text: ) He has done well to set the distinction here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:92
verses.text: For whenever he says anything great, he appeals to them of old.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:93
verses.text: And he found a text which contained both truths; just as in the other discourse he said, "Until He put His foes under His feet".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:94
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:95
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:96
verses.text: ) The remarkable circumstance is, that the two things stand together; that is, subjection and disobedience, and the punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:97
verses.text: "Like unto me," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:98
verses.text: Then why are ye alarmed? "Ye are the children of the prophets" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:99
verses.text: ): so that to you they spake, and for your sakes have all these things come to pass.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:100
verses.text: For as they deemed that through their outrage they had become alienated (and indeed there is no parity of reason, that He Who now is crucified, should now cherish them as His own), he proves to them that both the one and the other are in accordance with prophecy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:101
verses.text: "Ye are the children," he says, "of the Prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, 'And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:102
verses.text: ' Unto you first," he continues, "God having raised up His Son (τόν Παἵδα) sent Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:103
verses.text: "To others indeed also, but to you first who crucified Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:104
verses.text: "To bless you," he adds, "in turning away every one of you from his iniquities".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:105
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:106
verses.text: )  Now let us consider again more minutely what has been read out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:107
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:108
verses.text: ) In the first place, he establishes the point that the miracle was performed by them; saying, "Why marvel ye?" And he will not let the assertion be disbelieved: and to give it more weight, he anticipates their judgment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:109
verses.text: "Why look ye," he says, "so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:110
verses.text: ) If this troubles and confounds you, learn Who was the Doer, and be not amazed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:111
verses.text: And observe how on all occasions when he refers to God, and says that all things are from Him, then he fearlessly chides them: as above where he said, "A man approved of God among you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:112
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:113
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:114
verses.text: ) And on all occasions he reminds them of the outrage they had committed, in order that the fact of the Resurrection may be established.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:115
verses.text: But here he also subjoins something else; for he no more says, "of Nazareth," but what? "The God of our fathers hath glorified His Servant Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:116
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:117
verses.text: ) Observe also the modesty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:118
verses.text: He reproached them not, neither did he say at once, "Believe then now: behold, a man that has been forty years lame, has been raised up through the name of Jesus Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:119
verses.text: This he did not say, for it would have excited opposition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:120
verses.text: On the contrary, he begins by commending them for admiring the deed, and again calls them after their ancestor: "Ye men of Israel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:121
verses.text: Moreover, he does not say, It was Jesus that healed him: but, "The God of our fathers hath glorified," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:122
verses.text: But then, lest they should say, How can this stand to reason—that God should glorify the transgressor? therefore he reminds them of the judgment before Pilate, showing that, would they but consider, He was no transgressor; else Pilate had not wished to release Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:123
verses.text: And he does not say, "when Pilate was desirous," but, "was determined to let Him go".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:124
verses.text: "But ye denied the Holy One," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:125
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:126
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:127
verses.text: ) Him who had killed others, ye asked to be released; Him Who quickeneth them that are killed, ye did not wish to have! And that they might not ask again, How should it be that God now glorifies Him, when before He gave no assistance? he brings forward the prophets, testifying that so it behooved to be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:128
verses.text: "But those things which God before had showed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:129
verses.text: , (infra v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:130
verses.text: ) Then, lest they should suppose that God's dispensation was their own apology, first he reproves them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:131
verses.text: Moreover, that the denying Him "to Pilate's face," was no ordinary thing; seeing that he wished to release Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:132
verses.text: And that ye cannot deny this, the man who was asked in preference to Him is witness against you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:133
verses.text: This also is part of a deep dispensation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:134
verses.text: Here it shows their shamelessness and effrontery; that a Gentile, one who saw Him for the first time, should have discharged Him, though he had heard nothing striking; while they who had been brought up among His miracles, have done the very opposite! For, as he has said, "When he (Pilate) had determined to let Him go," that it may not be imagined that he did this of favor, we read, "And he said, It is a custom with you to release one prisoner: will ye therefore that I release unto you this man? (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:135
verses.text: xxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:136
verses.text: ) "But ye denied the Holy One and the Just".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:137
verses.text: (Mark xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:138
verses.text: ) He does not say, "Ye delivered up;" but everywhere, "Ye denied".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:139
verses.text: For, said they, "We have no king but Caesar".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:140
verses.text: (John xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:141
verses.text: ) And he does not say only, Ye did not beg off the innocent, and, "Ye denied" Him but, "Ye slew" Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:142
verses.text: While they were hardened, he refrained from such language; but when their minds are most moved, then he strikes home, now that they are in a condition to feel it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:143
verses.text: For just as when men are drunk we say nothing to them, but when they are sober, and are recovered from their intoxication then we chide them; thus did Peter: when they were able to understand his words, then he also sharpened his tongue, alleging against them many charges; that, Whom God had glorified, they had delivered up; Whom Pilate would have acquitted they denied to his face; that they preferred the robber before Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:144
verses.text: Observe again how he speaks covertly concerning Christ's power, showing that He raised Himself: just as in his first discourse he had said, "Because it was not possible that He should be holden of it" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:145
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:146
verses.text: ), so here he says, "And killed the Prince of Life".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:147
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:148
verses.text: ) It follows that the Life He had was not from another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:149
verses.text: The prince (or author) of evil would be he that first brought forth evil; the prince or author of murder, he who first originated murder; so also the Prince (or Author) of Life must be He Who has Life from Himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:150
verses.text: "Whom God raised up," he continues: and now that he has uttered this, he adds, "And his name, upon faith in his name, hath made this man strong, whom ye see and know; yea, the faith which is by Him hath given Him this perfect soundness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:151
verses.text: The faith which is by Him ἡ δι᾽ αὐτοὕ πίστις.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:152
verses.text: And yet it was ἡ εἰς αὐτὸν πιστις, "the faith which is in Him" (as its object) that did all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:153
verses.text: For the Apostles did not say, "By the name," but, "In the name," and it was in Him (εἰς αὐτὸν) that the man believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:154
verses.text: But they did not yet make bold to use the expression, "The faith which is in Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:155
verses.text: For, that the phrase "By Him" should not be too low, observe that after saying, "Upon the faith of His name," he adds, "His name hath made him strong," and then it is that he says, "Yea, the faith which is by Him hath given him this perfect soundness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:156
verses.text: Observe how he implies, that in the καὶ ἐκεἵνο former expression also "Whom God raised up," he did but condescend to their low attainments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:157
verses.text: For that Person needed not Another's help for His rising again, Whose Name raised up a lame man, being all one as dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:158
verses.text: Mark how on all occasions he adduces their own testimony.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:159
verses.text: Thus above, he said, "As ye yourselves also know;" and, "In the midst of you:" and here again, "Whom ye see and know: in the presence of you all".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:160
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:161
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:162
verses.text: ) And yet that it was, "In His name," they knew not: but they did know that the man was lame, that he stands there whole.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:163
verses.text: They that had wrought the deed themselves confessed, that it was not by their own power, but by that of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:164
verses.text: And had this assertion been unfounded, had they not been truly persuaded themselves that Christ had risen again, they would not have sought to establish the honor of a dead man instead of their own, especially while the eyes of the multitude were upon them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:165
verses.text: Then, when their minds were alarmed, immediately he encourages them, by the appellation of Brethren, "And now, brethren, I wot, etc".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:166
verses.text: For in the former discourse he foretold nothing, but only says concerning Christ, "Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly:" here he adds an admonition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:167
verses.text: There he waited till the people spoke: here, he knew how much they had already effected, and that the present assembly was better disposed toward them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:168
verses.text: "That through ignorance ye did it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:169
verses.text: And yet the circumstances mentioned above were not to be put to the score of ignorance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:170
verses.text: To choose the robber, to reject Him Who had been adjudged to be acquitted, to desire even to destroy Him—how should this be referred to ignorance? Nevertheless, he gives them liberty to deny it, and to change their mind about what had happened.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:171
verses.text: "Now this indeed, that you put to death the innocent, ye knew: but that you were killing "the Prince of Life," this, belike, ye did not know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:172
verses.text: And he exculpated not them alone, but also the chief contrivers of the evil, "ye and your rulers:" for doubtless it would have roused their opposition, had he gone off into accusation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:173
verses.text: For the evil-doer, when you accuse him of some wickedness that he has done, in his endeavor to exonerate himself, grows more vehement.
