verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:174
verses.text: And he no longer says, "Ye crucified," "Ye killed," but, "Ye did it;" leading them to seek for pardon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:175
verses.text: If those rulers did it through ignorance, much more did these present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:176
verses.text: "But these things which God before had showed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:177
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:178
verses.text: ) But it is remarkable, that both in the first and in the second discourse, speaking to the same effect, that is, in the former, "By the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God;" and in this, "God before had showed that Christ should suffer;" in neither does he adduce any particular text in proof.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:179
verses.text: The fact is, that each one of such passages is accompanied with many accusations, and with mention of the punishment in store for them as; "I will deliver up," says one, "the wicked in requital for His grave, and the rich in return for His death".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:180
verses.text: (Is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:181
verses.text: liii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 29:182
verses.text: ) And again,.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:1
verses.text: "Those things," he says, "which God before had showed by the mouth of all His prophets, that Christ should suffer, He hath so fulfilled".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:2
verses.text: It shows the greatness of that "counsel," in that all spoke of it, and not one only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:3
verses.text: It does not follow, because the event was through ignorance, that it took place irrespectively of God's ordinance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:4
verses.text: See how great is the Wisdom of God, when it uses the wickedness of others to bring about that which must be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:5
verses.text: "He hath fulfilled," he says: that they may not imagine that anything at all is wanting; for whatsoever Christ must needs suffer, has been fulfilled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:6
verses.text: But do not think, that, because the Prophets said this, and because ye did it through ignorance, this sufficeth to your exculpation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:7
verses.text: However, he does not express himself thus, but in milder terms says, "Repent ye therefore".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:8
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:9
verses.text: ) "Why? For either it was through ignorance, or by the dispensation of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:10
verses.text: "That your sins may be blotted out".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:11
verses.text: I do not mean the crimes committed at the Crucifixion; perhaps they were through ignorance; but so that your other sins may be blotted out: this only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:12
verses.text: "So shall the times of refreshing come unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:13
verses.text: Here he speaks of the Resurrection, obscurely.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:14
verses.text: For those are indeed times of refreshing, which Paul also looked for, when he said, "We that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burthened".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:15
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:16
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:17
verses.text: ) Then to prove that Christ is the cause of the days of refreshing, he says, "And He shall send Jesus Christ, which before was for you ordained".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:19
verses.text: ) He said not, "That your sin may be blotted out," but, "your sins;" for he hints at that sin also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:20
verses.text: "He shall send".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:21
verses.text: And whence? "Whom the heaven must receive".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:23
verses.text: ) Still "must" "receive?" And why not simply, Whom the heaven hath received? This, as if discoursing of old times: so, he says, it is divinely ordered, so it is settled: not a word yet of His eternal subsistence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:24
verses.text: —"For Moses indeed said unto the fathers, A Prophet shall the Lord raise up for you:" "Him shall ye hear in all things that He shall speak unto you:" and having said, "All things which God hath spoken by the mouth of all His holy Prophets," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:25
verses.text: ) now indeed he brings in Christ Himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:26
verses.text: For, if He predicted many things and it is necessary to hear Him, one would not be wrong in saying that the Prophets have spoken these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:27
verses.text: But, besides, he wishes to show that the Prophets did predict the same things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:28
verses.text: And, if any one will look closely into the matter, he will find these things spoken in the Old Testament, obscurely indeed, but nevertheless spoken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:29
verses.text: "Who was purposely designed," says he: in Whom there is nothing novel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:30
verses.text: Here he also alarms them, by the thought that much remains to be fulfilled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:31
verses.text: But if so, how says he, "Hath fulfilled?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:32
verses.text: ) The things which it was necessary "that Christ should suffer," are fulfilled: the things which must come to pass, not yet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:33
verses.text: "A prophet shall the Lord God raise up for you from among your brethren, like unto me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:34
verses.text: This would most conciliate them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:35
verses.text: Do you observe the sprinkling of low matters and high, side by side,—that He Who was to go up into the heavens should be like unto Moses? And yet it was a great thing too.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:36
verses.text: For in fact He was not simply like unto Moses, if so be that "every soul which will not hear shall be destroyed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:37
verses.text: And one might mention numberless other things which show that He was not like unto Moses; so that it is a mighty text that he has handled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:38
verses.text: "God shall raise Him up unto you," says Moses, "from among your brethren," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:39
verses.text: : consequently Moses himself threatens those that should not hear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:40
verses.text: "Yea, and all the prophets," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:41
verses.text: : all this is calculated to attract "Yea, and all the prophets," says the Apostle, "from Samuel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:42
verses.text: He refrains from enumerating them singly, not to make his discourse too long; but having alleged that decisive testimony of Moses, he passes by the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:43
verses.text: "Ye," he says, "are the children of the Prophets, and of the covenant which God made".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:44
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:45
verses.text: ) "Children of the covenant;" that is, heirs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:46
verses.text: For lest they should think that they received this offer from the favor of Peter, he shows, that of old it was due to them, in order that they may the rather believe that such also is the will of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:47
verses.text: "Unto you first," he continues, "God having raised up His Son Jesus, sent Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:48
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:49
verses.text: ) He does not say simply, "Unto you He sent His Son," but also, after the resurrection, and when He had been crucified.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:50
verses.text: For that they may not suppose that he himself granted them this favor, and not the Father, he says, "To bless you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:51
verses.text: For if He is your Brother, and blesses you, the affair is a promise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:52
verses.text: "Unto you first".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:53
verses.text: That is, so far are you from having no share in these blessings, that He would have you become moreover promoters and authors of them to others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:54
verses.text: For you are not to feel like castaways.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:55
verses.text: "Having raised up": again, the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:56
verses.text: "In turning away," he says, "every one of you from his iniquities".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:57
verses.text: In this way He blesses you: not in a general way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:58
verses.text: And what kind of blessing is this? A great one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:59
verses.text: For of course not the turning a man away from his iniquities is itself sufficient to remit them also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:60
verses.text: And if it is not sufficient to remit, how should it be to confer a blessing? For it is not to be supposed that the transgressor becomes forthwith also blessed; he is simply released from his sins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:61
verses.text: But this, "Like unto me," would no wise apply.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:62
verses.text: "Hear ye Him," he says; and not this alone, but he adds, "And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that Prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:63
verses.text: When he has shown them that they had sinned, and has imparted forgiveness to them, and promised good things, then indeed, then he says, "Moses also says the same thing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:64
verses.text: What sort of connection is this: "Until the times of the restitution;" and then to introduce Moses, saying, that all that Christ said shall come to pass? Then also, on the other hand, he says, as matter of encomium (so that for this reason also ye ought to obey): "Ye are the children of the prophets and of the covenant:" i-e: heirs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:65
verses.text: Then why do you stand affected towards that which is your own, as if it were another's? True, you have done deeds worthy of condemnation; still you may yet obtain pardon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:66
verses.text: Having said this, with reason he is now able to say, "Unto you God sent his Son Jesus to bless you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:67
verses.text: He says not, To save you, but what is greater; that the crucified Jesus blessed His crucifiers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:68
verses.text: Let us then also imitate Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:69
verses.text: Let us cast out that spirit of murder and enmity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:70
verses.text: It is not enough not to retaliate (for even in the Old Dispensation this was exemplified); but let us do all as we would for bosom-friends, as we would for ourselves so for those who have injured us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:71
verses.text: We are followers of Him, we are His disciples, who after being crucified, sets everything in action in behalf of his murderers, and sends out His Apostles to this end.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:72
verses.text: And yet we have often suffered justly; but those acted not only unjustly, but impiously; for He was their Benefactor, He had done no evil, and they crucified Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:73
verses.text: And for what reason? For the sake of their reputation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:74
verses.text: But He Himself made them objects of reverence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:75
verses.text: "The scribes and the pharisees sit in Moses' seat; all therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that do ye, but after their works do ye not".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:76
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:77
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:78
verses.text: ) And again in another place, "Go thy way, show thyself to the priest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:79
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:80
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:81
verses.text: ) Besides, when He might have destroyed them, He saves them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:82
verses.text: Let us then imitate Him, and let no one be an enemy, no one a foe, except to the devil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:83
verses.text: Not a little does the habit of not swearing contribute to this end: I mean to the not giving way to wrath: and by not giving way to wrath, we shall not have an enemy either.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:84
verses.text: Lop off the oaths of a man, and you have clipt the wings of his anger, you have smothered all his passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:85
verses.text: Swearing, it is said, is as the wind to wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:86
verses.text: Lower the sails; no need of sails, when there is no wind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:87
verses.text: If then we do not clamor, and do not swear, we have cut the sinews of passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:88
verses.text: And if you doubt this, just put it to experiment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:89
verses.text: Impose it as a law upon the passionate man that he shall never swear, and you will have no necessity of preaching moderation to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:90
verses.text: So the whole business is finished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:91
verses.text: For even though you do not forswear yourselves yet, by swearing at all, do you not know in what absurd consequences you involve yourselves—binding yourselves to an absolute necessity and as with a cord, and putting yourselves to all manner of shifts, as men studying how to rescue their soul from an evil which there is no escaping, or, failing of that, obliged by that self-imposed necessity to spend your life thenceforth in vexation, in quarrels, and to curse your wrath? But all is in vain, and to no purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:92
verses.text: Threaten, be peremptory (διόρισαι), do all, whatever it be, without swearing; so: it is in your power to reverse (ἀναλὕσαι) both what you have said and what you have done if you have the mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:93
verses.text: Thus on the present day I must needs speak more gently to you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:94
verses.text: For since ye have heard me, and the greater part of the reformation is achieved by you, now then let us see for what purpose the taking of oaths was introduced, and why allowed to be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:95
verses.text: In relating to you their first origin, and when they were conceived, and how, and by whom we shall give you this account in requital for your obedience.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:96
verses.text: For it is fit that he who has made his practice right, should be taught the philosophy of the matter, but he who is not yet doing the right, is not worthy to be told the history.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:97
verses.text: They made many covenants in Abraham's time, and slew victims, and offered sacrifices, and as yet oaths were not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:98
verses.text: Whence then did they come in? When evil increased, when all was confusion, upside down, when men had turned aside to idolatry: then it was, then, when men appeared no longer worthy to be believed, that they called God as witness, as if thereby giving an adequate surety for what they said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:99
verses.text: Such in fact is the Oath: it is a security where men's principles cannot be trusted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:100
verses.text: So that in the indictment of the swearer the first charge is this,—that he is not to be trusted without a surety, and a great surety too: for such is the exceeding faithlessness, that they ask not man as surety, but will needs have God! Secondly, the same charge lies against him who receives the oath: that, in a question of compact, he must drag in God for warranty, and refuse to be satisfied unless he get Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:101
verses.text: O the excessive stupidity, the insolence of such conduct! Thou, a worm, earth and dust, and ashes, and vapor, to drag in thy Lord as the surety, and to compel the other to drag Him in likewise! Tell me, if your servants were disputing with each other, and exchanging assurances with each other, and the fellow-servant should declare that for his part he would not be satisfied till he had their common master given him for surety, would he not have stripes given him without number, and be made to know that the master is for other purposes, and not to be put to any such use as this? Why do I speak of a fellow-servant? For should he choose any respectable person, would not that person consider it an affront? But I do not wish to do this, say you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:102
verses.text: Well: then do not compel the other to do so either: since where men only are in question, this is done—if your party says, "I give such an one as my surety," you do not allow him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:103
verses.text: "What then," say you, "am I to lose what I have given?" I am not speaking of this; but that you allow him to insult God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:104
verses.text: For which reason greater shall be the inevitable punishment to him who forces the oath upon another, than to him who takes it: the same holds with regard to him who gives an oath when no one asks him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:105
verses.text: And what makes it worse, is, that every one is ready to swear, for one farthing, for some petty item, for his own injustice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:106
verses.text: All this may be said, when there is no perjury; but if perjury follow in the train, both he that imposes and he that takes the oath have turned everything upside down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:107
verses.text: "But there are some things," you will say, "which are unknown".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:108
verses.text: Well take these into account, and do nothing negligently; but, if you do act negligently, take the loss to yourself as your punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:109
verses.text: It is better to be the loser thus, than in a very different way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:110
verses.text: For tell me—you force a man to take an oath, with what expectation? That he will forswear himself? But this is utter insanity; and the judgment will fall upon your own head; better you should lose your money, than he be lost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:111
verses.text: Why act thus to your own detriment, and to the insulting of God? This is the spirit of a wild beast, and of an impious man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:112
verses.text: But you do this in the expectation that he will not forswear himself? Then trust him without the oath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:113
verses.text: "Nay, there are many," you reply, "who in the absence of an oath would presume to defraud; but, once the oath taken, would refrain".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:114
verses.text: You deceive yourself, man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:115
verses.text: A man having once learnt to steal, and to wrong his neighbor, will presume full oft to trample upon his oath; if on the contrary he shrinks from swearing, he will much more shrink from injustice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:116
verses.text: "But he is influenced against his will".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:117
verses.text: Well then, he deserves pardon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:118
verses.text: But why am I speaking of this kind of oaths, while I pass over those in the market-place? For as regards these last, you can urge none of these pleas.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:119
verses.text: For ten farthings you there have swearing and forswearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:120
verses.text: In fact, because the thunderbolt does not actually fall from heaven, because all things are not overthrown, you stand holding God in your bonds: to get a few vegetables, a pair of shoes, for a little matter of money, calling Him to witness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:121
verses.text: What is the meaning of this? Do not let us imagine, that because we are not punished, therefore we do not sin; this comes of God's mercy; not of our merit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:122
verses.text: Let your oath be an imprecation upon your own child, upon your own self: say, "Else let the hangman lash my ribs".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:123
verses.text: But you dare not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:124
verses.text: Is God less valuable than thy ribs? is He less precious than thy pate? Say "Else let me be struck blind".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:125
verses.text: But no.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:126
verses.text: Christ so spares us, that He will not let us swear even by our own head; and yet we so little spare the honor of God, that on all occasions we must drag Him in! Ye know not what God is, and with what sort of lips he behooves to be invoked.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:127
verses.text: Why, when we speak of any man of eminent worth, we say, "First wash your mouth, and then make mention of him:" and yet, that precious Name which is above every name, the Name which is marvellous in all the earth, the Name which devils hear and tremble, we haul about as we list! Oh! the force of habit! thereby has that Name become cheap.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:128
verses.text: No doubt, if you impose on any one the necessity of coming into the sacred edifice to take his oath there, you feel that you have made the oath an awful one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:129
verses.text: And yet how is it that it seems awful in this way, but because we have been in the habit of using that at random, but not this? For ought not a shudder of awe to be felt when God is but named? But now, whereas among the Jews His Name was held to be so reverend, that it was written upon plates, and none was allowed to wear the characters except the high-priest alone: we bandy about His Name like any ordinary word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:130
verses.text: If simply to name God was not allowed to all; to call Him to witness, what audacity is it! nay, what madness! For if need were (rather than this) to fling away all that you have, ought you not readily to part with all? Behold, I solemnly declare and testify; reform these oaths of the forum, these superfluous oaths, and bring to me all those who wish to take them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:131
verses.text: Behold, in the presence of this assembly, I charge those who are set apart for the tending of the Houses of Prayer, I exhort and issue this order to them, that no person be allowed to take such oaths at his own discretion: or rather, that none be allowed to swear in any other way, but that the person be brought to me, whosoever he be, since even for these matters less will not serve but they must needs come before us, just as if one had to do with little children.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:132
verses.text: May there be no occasion! It is a shame in some things still to need to be taught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:133
verses.text: Do you dare to touch the Holy Table, being a person unbaptized? No, but what is still worse, you the baptized dare to lay your hand upon the Holy Table, which not even all ordained persons are allowed to touch, and so to take your oath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:134
verses.text: Now you would not go and lay your hand upon the head of your child, and yet do you touch the Table, and not shudder, not feel afraid? Bring these men to me; I will judge, and send them away rejoicing, both the one and the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:135
verses.text: Do what you choose; I lay it down as a law that there be no swearing at all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:136
verses.text: What hope of salvation, while we thus make all to have been done in vain? Is this the end of your bills, and your bonds, that you should sacrifice your own soul? What gain do you get so great as the loss? Has he forsworn himself? You have undone both him and yourself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:137
verses.text: But has he not? even so still you have undone (both), by forcing him to transgress the commandment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:138
verses.text: Let us cast out this disease from the soul: at any rate let us drive it out of the forum, out of our shops, out of our other work-places; our profits will but be the greater.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:139
verses.text: Do not imagine that the success of your worldly plans is to be ensured by transgressions of the Divine laws.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:140
verses.text: "But he refuses to trust me," say you; and in fact I have sometimes heard this said by some: "Unless I swear oaths without number, the man will not trust me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:141
verses.text: Yes, and for this you may thank yourself, because you are so off-hand with your oaths.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:142
verses.text: For were it not so, but on the contrary were it clear to all men that you do not swear, take my word for it, you would be more readily believed upon your mere nod, than those are who swallow oaths by thousands.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:143
verses.text: For look now: which do you more readily believe? me who do not swear, or those that do swear? "Yes," say you, "but then you are ruler and bishop".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:144
verses.text: Then suppose I prove to you that it is not only for that reason? Answer me with truth, I beseech you; were I in the habit of perpetually swearing, would my office stand me in that stead? Not a whit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:145
verses.text: Do you see that it is not for this reason? And what do you gain at all? Answer me that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:146
verses.text: Paul endured hunger; do you then also choose to hunger rather than to transgress one of the commandments of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:147
verses.text: Why are you so unbelieving? Here are you, ready to do and suffer all things for the sake of not swearing: and shall not He reward you? Shall He, Who sustains day by day both takers and breakers of oaths, give you over to hunger, when you have obeyed Him? Let all men see, that of those who assemble in this Church not one is a swearer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:148
verses.text: By this also let us become manifest, and not by our creed alone; let us have this mark also to distinguish us both from the Gentiles and from all men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:149
verses.text: Let us receive it as a seal from heaven, that we may everywhere be seen to be the King's own flock.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:150
verses.text: By our mouth and tongue let us be known, in the first place, just as the barbarians are by theirs: even as those who speak Greek are distinguished from barbarians, so let us be known.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:151
verses.text: Answer me: the birds which are said to be parrots, how are they known to be parrots? is it not by speaking like men? Let us then be known by speaking like the Apostles; by speaking like the Angels.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:152
verses.text: If any one bid you swear tell him, "Christ has spoken, and I do not swear".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:153
verses.text: This is enough to make a way for all virtue to come in.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:154
verses.text: It is a gate to religion, a high road leading to the philosophy of piety; a kind of training-school.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 32:155
verses.text: These things let us observe, that we may obtain also the future blessings, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, to Whom with the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, power and honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:1
verses.text: Homily X.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:2
verses.text: Acts IV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:3
verses.text: "And as they spake unto the people, there came unto them the priests, and the captain of the temple".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:4
verses.text: Ere yet they had time to take breath after their first trials, straightway they enter into others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:5
verses.text: And observe how the events are disposed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:6
verses.text: First, they were all mocked together; this was no small trial: secondly, they enter into dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:7
verses.text: And these two things do not take place in immediate succession; but when first the Apostles have won admiration by their two discourses, and after that have performed a notable miracle, thereupon it is that, after they are waxen bold, through God's disposal, they enter the lists.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:8
verses.text: But I wish you to consider, how those same persons, who in the case of Christ must need look out for one to deliver Him up to them, now with their own hands arrest the Apostles, having become more audacious and more impudent since the Crucifixion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:9
verses.text: In truth, sin, while it is yet struggling to the birth, is attended with some sense of shame; but when once fully born, it makes those more shameless who practise it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:10
verses.text: "And the captain of the temple," it is said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:11
verses.text: The object again was to attach a public criminality to what was doing, and not to prosecute it as the act of private individuals: such in fact was constantly their plan of proceeding.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:12
verses.text: "Being grieved that they taught the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:13
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:14
verses.text: ) Not merely because they taught, but because they declared, not alone that Christ Himself was risen from the dead, but moreover, that we through Him do rise again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:15
verses.text: "Because they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection of the dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:16
verses.text: So mighty was His Resurrection, that to others also He is the cause of a resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:17
verses.text: "And they laid hands on them, and put them in hold unto the next day; for it was now eventide.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:19
verses.text: ) What impudence! They feared not the multitude; for this also the captain of the temple was with them: they had their hands still reeking with the blood of the former victim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:20
verses.text: "For it was now eventide," it is said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:21
verses.text: It was with the wish to abate their spirit that those men did this, and guarded them; but the delay only served to make the Apostles more intrepid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:22
verses.text: And consider who these are who are arrested.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:23
verses.text: They are the chiefs of the Apostles, who are now become a pattern to the rest, that they should no longer crave each other's support, nor want to be together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:24
verses.text: "Howbeit, many having heard the word, believed; and the number of the men was about five thousand".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:26
verses.text: ) How was this? Did they see them in honor? Did they not behold them put in bonds? How then did they believe? Do you see the evident efficacy? And yet even those that believed already might well have become weaker.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:27
verses.text: But no, it is no longer so: for Peter's sermon had laid the seed deep into them, and had taken a hold upon their understandings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:28
verses.text: Therefore were their enemies incensed, that they did not fear them, that they made no account of their present troubles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:29
verses.text: For, say they, if He that was crucified effects such great things, and makes the lame to walk, we fear not these men either.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:30
verses.text: This again is of God's ordering.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:31
verses.text: For those who now believe were more numerous than the former.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:32
verses.text: Therefore it was that in their presence they bound the Apostles, to make them also more fearful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:33
verses.text: But the reverse took place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:34
verses.text: And they examine them not before the people, but privately, that the hearers may not profit by their boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:35
verses.text: "And it came to pass on the morrow, that their rulers, and elders, and scribes, and Annas the High Priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kindred of the High Priest, were gathered together at Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:38
verses.text: ) For now along with the other evils (of the times), the Law was no longer observed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:39
verses.text: And again they set off the business with the form of a tribunal, to constitute them guilty by their iniquitous sentence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:40
verses.text: "And when they had set them in the midst, they asked, By what power, or by what name, have ye done this?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:41
verses.text: ) And yet they knew it well; for it was because they were "grieved that they preached through Jesus the resurrection" that they arrested them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:42
verses.text: Then for what purpose do they question them? They expected the numbers present would make them recant, and thought by this means to have put all right again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:43
verses.text: Observe then what they say: "And by what name have ye done this? Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:44
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:45
verses.text: ) And now, I pray you, call to mind Christ's saying; "When they deliver you up unto the synagogues, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall speak; for it is the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:46
verses.text: (Luke xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:48
verses.text: ) So that it was a mighty Power they enjoyed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:49
verses.text: What then says Peter? "Ye rulers of the people, and elders of Israel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:50
verses.text: Mark the Christian wisdom of the man; how full of confidence it is: he utters not a word of insult, but says with respect, "Ye rulers of the people, and elders of Israel, if we be this day called to account of the good deed done to the impotent man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:51
verses.text: He takes them in hand right valiantly; by the opening of his speech he exposes them, and reminds them of the former things: that it is for a work of beneficence they are calling them to account.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:52
verses.text: As if he had said, "In all fairness we ought to have been crowned for this deed, and proclaimed benefactors; but since "we are even put upon our trial for a good deed done to an impotent man," not a rich man, not powerful, not noble—and yet who would feel envy in a case like this?" It is a most forcible (ἀπαγγελια, al.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:53
verses.text: ἐπαγγελία) way of putting the case; and he shows that they are piercing their own selves:—"By what means this man is made whole: be it known unto you all, and to all the people Israel; that by the Name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth:"—this is what would vex them most.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:54
verses.text: For this was that which Christ had told the disciples, "What ye hear in the ear that preach ye upon the housetops.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:55
verses.text: —That in the name of Jesus Christ," he says, "of Nazareth, Whom ye crucified, Whom God raised from the dead, even by Him doth this man stand here before you whole".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:56
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:57
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:58
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:59
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:60
verses.text: ) Think not, he says that we conceal the country, or the nature of the death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:61
verses.text: "Whom ye crucified, Whom God raised from the dead, even by Him doth this man stand before you whole".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:62
verses.text: Again the death, again the resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:63
verses.text: "This is the stone," he says, "which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:64
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:65
verses.text: ) He reminds them also of a saying which was enough to frighten them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:66
verses.text: For it had been said, "Whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:67
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:68
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:69
verses.text: )—Neither is there salvation in any other, (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:70
verses.text: ) Peter says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:71
verses.text: What wounds, think you, must these words inflict on them! "For there is none other name," he continues, "under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:72
verses.text: Here he utters also lofty words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:73
verses.text: For when the object is, not to carry some point successfully, but only to show boldness he does not spare; for he was not afraid of striking too deep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:74
verses.text: Nor does he say simply, "By another;" but, "Neither is there salvation in any other:" that is, He is able to save us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:75
verses.text: In this way he subdued their threatening.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:76
verses.text: "Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:77
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:78
verses.text: ) The two unlearned men beat down with their rhetoric them and the chief priests.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:79
verses.text: For it was not they that spake, but the grace of the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:80
verses.text: "And beholding the man which was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:81
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:82
verses.text: ) Great was the boldness of the man; that even in the judgment-hall he has not left them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:83
verses.text: For had they said that the fact was not so, there was he to refute them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:84
verses.text: "But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they conferred among themselves, saying, What are we to do to these men?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:85
verses.text: ) See the difficulty they are in, and how the fear of men again does everything.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:86
verses.text: As in the case of Christ, they were not able (as the saying is) to undo what is done, nor to cast it into the shade, but for all their hindering, the Faith did but gain ground the more; so was it now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:87
verses.text: "What shall we do?" O the folly! to suppose that those who had tasted of the conflict, would now take fright at it: to expect, impotent as their efforts had proved in the beginning, to effect something new, after such a specimen of oratory as had been exhibited! The more they wished to hinder, the more the business grew upon their hands.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:88
verses.text: But what say they? "For that indeed a notable miracle hath been done by them is manifest to all them that dwell in Jerusalem; and we cannot deny it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:89
verses.text: But that it spread no further among the people, let us straightly threaten them, that they speak henceforth to no man in this name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:90
verses.text: And they called them, and commanded them not to speak at all, nor teach, in the name of Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:91
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:92
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:93
verses.text: ) See what effrontery is shown by these, and what greatness of mind by the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:94
verses.text: "But Peter and John answered and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:95
verses.text: For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:96
verses.text: So when they had further threatened them, they let them go, finding nothing how they might punish them, because of the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:97
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:98
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:99
verses.text: ) The miracles shut their mouths: they would not so much as let them finish their speech, but cut them short in the middle, most insolently.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:100
verses.text: "For all men glorified God for that which was done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:101
verses.text: For the man was above forty years old, on whom this miracle of healing was showed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:102
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:103
verses.text: ) But let us look over what has been said from the beginning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:104
verses.text: "And as they spake unto the people, etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:105
verses.text: Being grieved that they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection of the dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:106
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:107
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:108
verses.text: ) So then at first they did all for the sake of man's opinion (or glory): but now another motive was added: that they should not be thought guilty of murder, as they said subsequently, "Do ye wish to bring this man's blood on us?" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:109
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:110
verses.text: ) O the folly! Persuaded that He was risen, and having received this proof of it, they expected that He Whom death could not hold, could be cast into the shade by their machinations! What can match the folly of this! Such is the nature of wickedness: it has no eyes for anything, but on all occasions it is thrown into perturbation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:111
verses.text: Finding themselves overborne, they felt like persons who have been outwitted: as is the case with people who have been forestalled and made a sport of in some matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:112
verses.text: And yet they everywhere affirmed that it was God that raised Him: but it was "in the Name of Jesus" that they spake; showing that Jesus was risen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:113
verses.text: "Through Jesus, the resurrection of the dead": for they themselves also held a resurrection: a cold and puerile doctrine, indeed, but still they held it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:114
verses.text: Why this alone, was it not sufficient to induce them to do nothing to them—I mean, that the disciples with such boldness bore themselves in the way they did? Say, wherefore, O Jew, dost thou disbelieve? Thou oughtest to have attended to the sign done, and to the words, not to the evil disposition of the many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:115
verses.text: "By their teaching the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:116
verses.text: For already they were in ill repute with them by reason of what they had done to Christ; so that they were rather increasing their own obloquy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:117
verses.text: "And they laid hands on them, and put them in hold until the morrow; for it was now eventide".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:118
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:119
verses.text: ) In the case of Christ, however, they did not so; but having taken Him at midnight, they immediately led him away, and made no delay, being exceedingly in fear of the multitude: whereas in the case of the Apostles here, they were bold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:120
verses.text: And they no more take them to Pilate, being ashamed and blushing at the thought of the former affair, lest they should also be taken to task for that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:121
verses.text: "And it came to pass on the morrow, that their rulers, and elders, and scribes were gathered together at Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:122
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:123
verses.text: ) Again in Jerusalem: and there it is that men's blood is poured out; no reverence for their city either; "And Annas, and Caiaphas," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:124
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:125
verses.text: ) "And Annas," it says, "and Caiaphas".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:126
verses.text: His maid-servant it was that questioned Peter, and he could not bear it: in his house it was that Peter denied, when Another was in bonds there: but now, when he has come into the midst of them all, see how he speaks! "By what name have ye done this?" Why dost thou not speak it, what it is, but keepest that out of sight? "By what name have ye done this?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:127
verses.text: ) And yet he affirmed, It was not we that did it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:128
verses.text: "Ye rulers of the people," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:129
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:130
verses.text: ) Observe his wisdom: he does not say outright, "In the Name of Jesus we did it," but how? "In His Name this man"—He does not say, "was made whole by us;" but—"doth stand here before you whole".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:131
verses.text: And again, "If we be examined concerning the good deed done to the impotent man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:132
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:133
verses.text: ) He hits them hard, that they are always making a crime of such acts, finding fault with works of beneficence done to men: and he reminds them of their former doings, that they run to do murder, and not only so, but make a crime of doing good deeds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:134
verses.text: Do you observe too (in point of rhetoric) with what dignity they express themselves? Even in the use of words they were becoming expert by practice, and henceforth they were not to be beaten down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:135
verses.text: "Be it known unto you all," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:136
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:137
verses.text: ) Whereby he shows them that they rather do, in spite of themselves, preach Christ; themselves extol the doctrine, by their examining and questioning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:138
verses.text: O exceeding boldness—"Whom ye crucified! Whom God raised up"—this is bolder still! Think not that we hide what there is to be ashamed of.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:139
verses.text: He says this all but tauntingly: and not merely says it, but dwells upon the matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:140
verses.text: "This," says he, "is the Stone which was set at naught by you builders;" and then he goes on to teach them, saying in addition, "Which is made the head of the corner" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:141
verses.text: ); that is to say, that the Stone is indeed approved! Great was the boldness they now had, in consequence of the miracle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:142
verses.text: And when there was need to teach, observe how they speak and allege many prophecies; but when the point was to use boldness of speech, then they only speak peremptorily.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:143
verses.text: Thus "Neither," says he, "is there any other name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:144
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:145
verses.text: ) It is manifest to all, he says, because not to us alone was that Name given; he cites even themselves as witnesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:146
verses.text: For, since they asked, "In what name did ye it?" "In Christ's," says he: "there is none other name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:147
verses.text: How is it that ye ask? On all hands this is palpable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:148
verses.text: "For there exists not another name under heaven, whereby we must be saved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:149
verses.text: This is the language of a soul which has renounced (κατεγνωκυίας) this present life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:150
verses.text: His exceeding out-spokenness proves here, that when he speaks in lowly terms of Christ, he does it not of fear, but of wise forbearance (συγκαταβαίνων): but now that it was the fitting time, he speaks not in lowly terms: by this very thing intending to strike dismay into them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:151
verses.text: Behold another miracle not less than the former.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:152
verses.text: "And beholding the boldness of Peter and John," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:153
verses.text: "And they took knowledge of them that they had been with Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:154
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:155
verses.text: ) Not without a meaning has the Evangelist set down this passage; but in saying, "they recognized them that they had been with Jesus," he means, in His Passion: for only these were with Him at that time, and then indeed they had seen them humble, dejected: and this it was that most surprised them: the greatness of the change.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:156
verses.text: For in fact Annas and Caiaphas with their company were there, and these then also had stood by Him, and their boldness now amazed them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:157
verses.text: "And beholding the boldness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:158
verses.text: For not only their words; their very bearing showed it; that they should stand there so intrepidly to be tried in a cause like this, and with uttermost peril impending over them! Not only by their words, but by their gesture also, and their look and voice, and, in short, by everything about them, they manifested the boldness with which they confronted the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:159
verses.text: From the things they uttered, they marvelled, perhaps: "that they were unlearned and common men:" for one may be unlearned, yet not a common or private man, and a common man, yet not unlearned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:160
verses.text: "Having perceived," it says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:161
verses.text: Whence? From what they said? Peter does not draw out long speeches, but then by his very manner and method (τἥς ἀπαγγελίας καὶ τἥς συνθήκης) he declares his confidence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:162
verses.text: "And they recognized them that they had been with Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:163
verses.text: Which circumstance made them believe that it was from Him they had learned these things, and that they did all in the character of His disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:164
verses.text: But not less than the voice of these, the miracle uttered a voice of its own: and that sign itself stopped their mouths.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:165
verses.text: "And beholding the man," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:166
verses.text: So that they would have been peremptory (ἐπέσκηψαν) with them, if the man had not been with them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:167
verses.text: "We cannot deny it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:168
verses.text: So that they would have denied it, if the thing had not been so: if the testimony had not been that of the people in general.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:169
verses.text: "But that it spread no further among the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:170
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:171
verses.text: ) And yet it was palpable to all men! But such is the nature of wickedness: everywhere it is shamed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:172
verses.text: "Let us straitly threaten them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:173
verses.text: What sayest thou? Threaten? And expect ye to stop the preaching? And yet all beginnings are hard and trying.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:174
verses.text: Ye slew the Master, and did not stop it: and now, if ye threaten, do ye expect to turn us back? The imprisonment did not prevail with us to speak submissively, and shall ye prevail? "And they called them, and commanded them," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:175
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:176
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:177
verses.text: ) It had been much better for them to let them go.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:178
verses.text: "And Peter and John answered and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:179
verses.text: When the terror was abated (for that command was tantamount to their being dismissed), then also the Apostles speak more mildly: so far were they from mere bravery: "Whether it be right," says he: and "We cannot but speak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:180
verses.text: Whether it be right in the sight of God to obey you rather than God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:181
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:182
verses.text: ) Here by "God" they mean Christ, for he it was that commanded them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:183
verses.text: And once more they confirm the fact of His Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:184
verses.text: "For we cannot but speak the things we have seen and heard:" so that we are witnesses who have a right to be believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:185
verses.text: "So when they had further threatened them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:186
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:187
verses.text: ) Again they threatened in vain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:188
verses.text: "They let them go, finding nothing how they might punish them, because of the people: for all men glorified God for that which was done".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:189
verses.text: So then the people glorified God, but these endeavored to destroy them: such fighters against God were they! Whereby they made them more conspicuous and illustrious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:190
verses.text: "For My strength," it is said, "is made perfect in weakness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:191
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:192
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:193
verses.text: )  Already these as martyrs have borne testimony: set in the battle against all, they said, "We cannot but speak the things we have seen and heard".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:194
verses.text: If the things we speak be false, reprehend them; if true, why hinderest thou? Such is philosophy! Those, in perplexity, these in gladness: those covered with exceeding shame, these doing all with boldness: those in fear, these in confidence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:195
verses.text: For who, I would ask, were the frightened? those who said, "That it spread no further among people," or these who said, "we cannot but speak the things we have seen and heard?" And these had a delight, a freedom of speech, a joy surpassing all; those a despondency, a shame, a fear; for they feared the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:196
verses.text: But these were not afraid of those; on the contrary, while these spake what they would, those did not what they would.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:197
verses.text: Which were in chains and dangers? was it not these last?  Let us then hold fast to virtue; let not these words end only in delight, and in a certain elevation of the spirits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:198
verses.text: This is not the theatre, for singers (κιθαρώδων), and tragedians, and musicians (κιθαριστὥν), where the fruit consists only in the enjoyment and where the enjoyment itself passes with the passing day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:199
verses.text: Nay, would that it were enjoyment alone, and not mischief also with the enjoyment! But so it is: each man carries home with him much of what he has witnessed there, sticking to him like the infection of a plague: and one indeed, of the younger sort, having culled such snatches of song here and there of those satanic plays, as he could fix in his memory, goes singing them about the house: while another, a senior, and forsooth too staid for such levity, does not this indeed, but what is there spoken, both the preachments and the very words, he remembers it all; and another again, some filthy and absurd ditty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:200
verses.text: From this place you depart, taking nothing with you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:201
verses.text: —We have laid down a law—nay, not we: God forbid! for it is said, "Call no man your master upon the earth" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:202
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:203
verses.text: ); Christ has laid down a law that none should swear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:204
verses.text: Now, say, what has been done with regard to this law? For I will not cease speaking of it; "lest," as the Apostle saith, "if I come again, I must not spare".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:205
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:206
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:207
verses.text: ) I ask then, have you laid the matter to heart? have you thought of it seriously? have you been in earnest about it, or must we again take up the same subject? Nay, rather, whether you have or not, we will resume it, that you may think seriously about it, or, if you have laid it to heart, may again do this the more surely, and exhort others also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:208
verses.text: With what then, I pray you, with what shall we begin? Shall it be with the Old Testament? For indeed this also is to our shame, that the precepts of the Law, which we ought to surpass, we do not even thus observe! For we ought not to be hearing such matters as these: these are precepts adapted to the poor Jewish level (τἥς ᾽Ιουδαἳκἥς εὐτελείας): we ought to be hearing those counsels of perfection; "Cast away thy property, stand courageously, and give up thy life in behalf of the Gospel, scorn all the goods of earth, have nothing in common with this present life; if any wrong thee, do him good; if any defraud thee, bless him; if any revile thee, show him honor; be above everything".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:209
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:210
verses.text: Ambros.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:211
verses.text: de Off.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:212
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:213
verses.text: ) These and such as these are what we ought to be hearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:214
verses.text: But here are we discoursing about swearing; and our case is just the same as if, when a person ought to be a philosopher, one should take him away from the great masters, and set him to spell syllables letter by letter! Just think now what a disgrace it would be for a man having a flowing beard, and with staff in hand, and cope on shoulders, to go to school with children, and be set the same tasks with them: would it not be above measure ridiculous? And yet the ridicule which belongs to us is even greater.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:215
verses.text: For not as the difference between philosophy and the spelling-lesson, so is that between the Jewish polity and ours: no indeed, but as the difference between angels and men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:216
verses.text: Say now, if one could fetch down an angel from heaven, and should bid him stand here and listen to our preaching, as one whose duty it is to conform himself thereto, would it not be shameful and preposterous? But if to be yet, like children, under teaching about these things be ridiculous; what must it be, not even to attend to these things: how great the condemnation, how great the shame! To be Christians still, and to have to learn that it is not right to swear! However, let us put up with that, lest we incur even worse ridicule.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:217
verses.text: Well, then, let us speak to you to-day from the Old Testament.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:218
verses.text: What does it tell us? "Accustom not thy mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:219
verses.text: And why? "For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a blue mark, so he that sweareth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:220
verses.text: (Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:221
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:222
verses.text: ) See the discernment of this wise man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:223
verses.text: He did not say, "Accustom not to swearing" thy mind, but "thy mouth"; because being altogether an affair of the mouth, thus it is easily remedied.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:224
verses.text: For at last it becomes a habit without intention; as for instance, there are many who entering the public baths, as soon as they have passed the threshold, cross (Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:225
verses.text: in  Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:226
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:227
verses.text: ) themselves (σφραγίζονται).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:228
verses.text: This the hand has got to do, without any one's bidding, by force of habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:229
verses.text: Again, at the lighting of a candle, often when the mind is intent on something else, the hand makes the sign.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:230
verses.text: In the same way also the mouth, without concurrence of the mind, articulates the word, from mere habit, and the whole affair is in the tongue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:231
verses.text: "Neither use thyself," he says, "to the naming of the Holy One.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:232
verses.text: For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a blue mark, so he that sweareth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:233
verses.text: He speaks not here of false oaths, but he cuts down all oaths, and to them also assigns their punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:234
verses.text: Why then, swearing is a sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:235
verses.text: For such in truth is the soul; full of all these ulcers, all these scars.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:236
verses.text: But you do not see them? Yes, this is the mischief of it; and yet you might see if you wished; for God has given you eyes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:237
verses.text: With eyes of this kind did the Prophet see, when he said, "My wounds stink, and are corrupt, because of my foolishness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:238
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:239
verses.text: xxxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:240
verses.text: ) We have despised God, we have hated that good Name, we have trodden Christ under foot, we have lost all reverence, none names the Name of God with honor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:241
verses.text: Yet if you love any one, even at his name you start to your feet; but God you thus continually invoke, and make nothing of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:242
verses.text: Call upon Him for the benefit of your enemy; call upon Him for the salvation of your own soul; then he will be present, then you will delight Him; whereas now you provoke Him to anger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:243
verses.text: Call upon Him as Stephen did; "Lord," he said, "lay not this sin to their charge".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:244
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:245
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:246
verses.text: ) Call upon Him as did the wife of Elkanah, with tears and sobs, and prayers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:247
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:248
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:249
verses.text: ) I prevent you not, rather I earnestly exhort you to it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:250
verses.text: Call upon him as Moses called upon Him, yea, cried, interceding for those who had driven him into banishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:251
verses.text: For you to make mention at random of any person of consideration, is taken as an insult: and do you bandy God about in your talk, in season, out of season? I do not want to hinder you from keeping God always in your mind: nay, this I even desire and pray for, only that you should do this, so as to honor Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:252
verses.text: Great good would this have done us, if we had called upon God only when we ought, and for what we ought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:253
verses.text: And why, I would ask, were such miracles wrought in the Apostles' times, and not in ours? And yet it is the same God, the same Name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:254
verses.text: But no, the case is not the same.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:255
verses.text: For then they called upon Him only for those objects which I have mentioned; whereas we call upon Him not for these, but quite other purposes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:256
verses.text: —If a man refuse to believe you, and that is why you swear, say to him, "Believe me:" however, if you will needs make oath, swear by yourself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:257
verses.text: I say this, not to set up a law against Christ's law; God forbid; for it is said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:258
verses.text: "Let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:259
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:260
verses.text: ): but by way of coming down to your present level, that I may more easily lead you to the practice of this commandment, and divert you from this tyrannical habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:261
verses.text: How many who have done well in other respects, have been undone by these practices! Shall I tell you why it was permitted the ancients to take oaths? (for to take false oaths, was not permitted to them either.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:262
