verses.text: ) Because they swore by idols.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:263
verses.text: But are you not ashamed to rest in laws, by which they in their infirmity were led on to something better? It is true, when I take a Gentile in hand, I do not immediately lay this injunction upon him, but in the first place I exhort him to know Christ; but if the believer, who has both learnt Him and heard Him, must needs crave the same forbearance with the Gentile, what is the use, what the gain (of his Christianity?)—But the habit is strong, and you cannot detach yourself from it? Well then, since the tyranny of habit is so great, transfer it into another channel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:264
verses.text: And how is this to be done? you will ask.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:265
verses.text: What I have said often, I say also now; let there be many monitors (λογισταὶ), let there be many examiners and censors (ἐξετασταὶ, δοκιμασταί).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:266
verses.text: Say, if you chance to put on your mantle inside out, you allow your servant to correct your mistake, and are ashamed to learn of him, although there is much to be ashamed of in this; and here when you are getting hurt to your soul, are you ashamed to be taught better by another? You suffer your menial to put your dress in order, and to fasten your shoes, and will you not endure him that would put your soul in order? Let even your menial, your child, your wife, your friend, your kinsman, your neighbor, be your teachers on this point.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:267
verses.text: For as when a wild beast is hunted down from all sides, it is impossible for it to escape; so he that has so many to watch him, so many to reprove him, who is liable to be struck at from all sides, cannot help being on his guard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:268
verses.text: The first day he will find it hard to put up with, and the second, and the third; but after that it will come easier, and, the fourth passed, there will not even be anything to do.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:269
verses.text: Make the experiment, if you doubt me; take it into consideration, I beseech you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:270
verses.text: It is not a trifling matter to be wrong in, nor yet to come right in; on both sides it is great for evil and for good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 33:271
verses.text: May the good be effected, through the grace and loving-mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, to Whom with the Father and the Holy Ghost be glory, power, and honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:1
verses.text: Homily XI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:2
verses.text: Acts IV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:3
verses.text: "And being let go, they went to their own company, and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said unto them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:4
verses.text: Not for their own glory did they tell the tale—how should such be their motive?—but what they displayed was the proofs therein exhibited of the grace of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:5
verses.text: All that their adversaries had said, this they told; their own part, it is likely, they omitted: this made the hearers all the more courageous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:6
verses.text: What then? These again flee to the true Succor, to the Alliance invincible, and again, "with one accord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:7
verses.text: And when they heard that," it is said, "with one accord they lifted up their voice to God, and said:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:8
verses.text: ) and with great earnestness, for it is no prayer made at random.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:9
verses.text: Observe with what exquisite propriety their prayers are framed: thus, when they besought to be shown who was meet for the Apostleship, they said, "Thou, Lord, which knowest the heart of all men, show:" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:10
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:11
verses.text: ) for it was a subject for Prescience there: but here, where the thing needed was that the mouths of their adversaries should be stopped, they speak of lordship; wherefore they begin thus: Lord, "(Δέσποτα) the God that madest heaven and earth, and the sea, and all that in them is: Who, by the Holy Ghost through the mouth of Thy servant, David our father, didst say, Why did the heathen rage, and the people imagine vain things? The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord, and against His Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:12
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:13
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:14
verses.text: ) It is to sue God, as one may say upon His own covenants, that they thus produce this prophecy: and at the same time to comfort themselves with the thought, that in vain are all the imaginations of their foes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:15
verses.text: This then is what they say: Bring those words into accomplishment, and show that they "imagine vain things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:16
verses.text: —For of a truth," they proceed, "there were gathered together in this city, against Thy holy Child Jesus, (Παἵδα) Whom Thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, together with the Gentiles and the people of Israel, for to do whatsoever Thy hand and Thy counsel determined before to be done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:17
verses.text: And now, Lord, behold their threatenings".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:20
verses.text: ) Observe their largeness of mind (φιλοσοφίαν).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:21
verses.text: These are not words of imprecation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:22
verses.text: In saying, "their threatenings, they do not mean this or that thing specifically threatened, but only in general, the fact of their threatening, perhaps, as being formidable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:23
verses.text: In fact, the writer is concise in his narrative.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:24
verses.text: And observe, they do not say, "Crush them, cast them down;" but what? "And grant unto Thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak Thy word".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:25
verses.text: Let us also learn thus to pray.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:26
verses.text: And yet how full of wrath one would be, when fallen among men intent upon killing him, and making threats to that effect? how full of animosity? But not so these saints.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:27
verses.text: "By stretching forth Thine hand to heal, and that signs and wonders may be done by the Name of Thy holy Child Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:29
verses.text: ) If in that Name the mighty deeds are wrought, great will be the boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:30
verses.text: "And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:32
verses.text: ) This was the proof that they were heard, and of His visitation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:33
verses.text: "And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:34
verses.text: What means, "They were filled?" It means, They were inflamed; and the Gift burned up within them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:35
verses.text: "And they spake the word of God with boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:36
verses.text: And the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:38
verses.text: ) Do you see that together with the grace of God they also contributed their part? For everywhere it ought to be well observed, that together with the grace of God they do their part likewise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:39
verses.text: Just as Peter said above, "Silver and gold have I none"; and again, that "they were all together".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:40
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:41
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:42
verses.text: ) But in this place, having mentioned that they were heard, the sacred writer proceeds to speak also of them, what virtue they showed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:43
verses.text: Moreover, he is just about to enter upon the narrative of Sapphira and Ananias, and with a view to show the detestable conduct of that pair, he first discourses of the noble behavior of the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:44
verses.text: Now say, did their love beget their poverty, or the poverty the love? In my opinion, the love begat the poverty, and then the poverty drew tight the cords of love.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:45
verses.text: For observe what he says: "They were all of one heart and of one soul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:46
verses.text: Behold, heart and soul are what make the "together".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:47
verses.text: "Neither said any of them that aught of the things which he possessed was his own; but they had all things common.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:48
verses.text: And with great power the Apostles rendered their testimony (ἀπεδίδουν) of the resurrection".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:49
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:50
verses.text: ) The phrase betokens them to be as persons put in trust with a deposit: he speaks of it as a debt or obligation: that is, their testimony they with boldness did render, or pay off, to all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:51
verses.text: "And great grace was upon them all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:52
verses.text: Neither was there any among them that lacked".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:54
verses.text: ) Their feeling was just as if they were under the paternal roof, all for awhile sharing alike.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:55
verses.text: It is not to be said, that though indeed they maintained the rest, yet they did it with the feeling that the means whereof they maintained them were still their own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:56
verses.text: No, the admirable circumstance is this, that they first alienated their property, and so maintained the rest, on purpose that the maintenance might not come as of their own private means, but as of the common property.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:57
verses.text: "For as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the price of the things that were sold, and laid them down at the Apostles' feet; and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:59
verses.text: ) A great mark of honor this, that "they laid them at the Apostles' feet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:60
verses.text: And Joses, who by the Apostles was surnamed Barnabas, ('which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:61
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:62
verses.text: ) I do not think that this is the same with the companion of Matthias; for that person was also called Justus and Barsabas, but this, Joses and "Barnabas" "son of consolation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:63
verses.text: I suppose he also received the name from his virtue, as being qualified and suited for this duty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:64
verses.text: "A Levite, and of the country of Cyprus by birth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:65
verses.text: Observe on all occasions how the writer indicates the breaking up of the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:66
verses.text: But how was he also a "Cyprian by birth?" Because they then even removed to other countries, and still were called Levites.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:67
verses.text: "Having land, sold it, and brought the price, and laid it at the Apostles' feet".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:68
verses.text: Let us now look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:69
verses.text: "And being let go, they went to their own company, and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said unto them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:70
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:71
verses.text: ) See the unostentatious conduct of the Apostles, and their largeness of mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:72
verses.text: They did not go about boasting, and say, "How we served (ἀπεχρησάμεθα) the priests!" nor were they ambitious of honor: but, we read, "they came unto their own company.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:73
verses.text: Observe how they do not cast themselves upon temptations, but when the temptations present themselves, with courage endure them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:74
verses.text: Had it been some other of the disciples, perhaps, emboldened by the countenance of the multitude, he might have insulted, might have vented ever so many harsh expressions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:75
verses.text: But not so these true philosophers; they do all with mildness and with gentleness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:76
verses.text: "And when they heard that, we read, with one accord they lifted up their voice to God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:77
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:78
verses.text: ) That shout proceeded from delight and great emotion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:79
verses.text: Such indeed are the prayers which do their work, prayers replete with true philosophy, prayers offered up for such objects, by such persons, on such occasions, in such a manner; whereas all others are abominable and profane.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:80
verses.text: "Lord, Thou the God that madest heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:81
verses.text: Observe how they say nothing idle, no old wives' talk and fables, but speak of His power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:82
verses.text: Just as Christ Himself said to the Jews, "If I by the Spirit of God do cast out devils:" behold the Father also speaks by the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:83
verses.text: For what saith it? "Lord, the God Who, by the Holy Ghost, through the mouth of our father Thy servant David didst say, Why did the nations rage?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:84
verses.text: ) Scripture is wont thus to speak of one as of many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:85
verses.text: "For of a truth, Lord, against Thy Holy Child Jesus, Whom Thou didst anoint, both Herod and Pontius Pilate," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:86
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:87
verses.text: ) Observe how, even in prayer, they circumstantially describe the Passion, and refer all to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:88
verses.text: —That is, Not they had power to do this: but Thou didst it all, Thou that didst permit, that dost call to account, and yet didst bring to accomplishment, Thou the All-skilful and Wise, that didst serve Thee of Thine enemies for Thine own pleasure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:89
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:90
verses.text: ) "For to do whatever Thy hand," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:91
verses.text: Here they discourse of His exceeding Skill and Wisdom and Power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:92
verses.text: So then, as enemies they came together, and with murderous purpose, and as opposing themselves, but they did what things Thou wouldest: "For to do," as it is said, "whatsoever Thy hand and Thy purpose determined before to be done".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:93
verses.text: What means, "Thy hand?" Here he seems to me to denote one and the same thing by power and purpose, meaning that for Thee it is enough but to will: for it is not by power that one determines.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:94
verses.text: "Whatsoever Thy hand," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:95
verses.text: i-e: Whatsoever Thou didst ordain: either this is the meaning, or, that by His hand He did effect.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:96
verses.text: "And now, Lord, regard their threatenings".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:97
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:98
verses.text: ) As at that time, it is said, they "imagined vain things," so "now," grant that their imaginations may be in vain: i-e: let not their threatenings come into accomplishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:99
verses.text: And this they said not because they would themselves deprecate any hardship, but for the preaching's sake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:100
verses.text: For they do not say, "and deliver us out of dangers;" but what? "And grant unto Thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak Thy word".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:101
verses.text: Thou Who didst bring to pass the former designs, bring these also to accomplishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:102
verses.text: Observe, how they affirm God to be the Author of their confidence; and how they ask all for God's sake, nothing for their own glory or ambition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:103
verses.text: They promise for their own part, that they will not be dismayed; but they pray that signs may be wrought "by stretching forth Thy hand to heal, and that signs and wonders may be done:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:104
verses.text: ) for without these, however great the zeal they showed, they would be striving to no purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:105
verses.text: God assented to their prayer, and manifested this, by shaking the place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:106
verses.text: For "when they had prayed," it is said, "the place was shaken".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:107
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:108
verses.text: ) And wherefore this was done, hear from the prophet, when he says, "He looketh on the earth, and maketh it to tremble.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:109
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:110
verses.text: civ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:111
verses.text: ) For by this He made it manifest that He is present to their prayers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:112
verses.text: And again, another prophet saith, "The earth was shaken, and did tremble at the presence of the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:113
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:114
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:115
verses.text: ; lxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:116
verses.text: ) And God did this, both to make it more awful, and to lead them on to a courageous trust.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:117
verses.text: "And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:118
verses.text: They gained increased boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:119
verses.text: As it was the beginning (of their work), and they had besought a sensible sign for their persuasion (πρὸς τὸ πεισθἥναι αὐτους)—but after this we nowhere find the like happening—therefore great was the encouragement they received.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:120
verses.text: In fact, they had no means of proving that He was risen, save by miraculous signs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:121
verses.text: So that it was not only their own assurance (ἀσφαλείαν) that they sought: but that they might not be put to shame, but that they might speak with boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:122
verses.text: "The place was shaken," and that made them all the more unshaken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:123
verses.text: For this is sometimes a token of wrath, sometimes of favor and providence, but on the present occasion, of wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:124
verses.text: For in those times it took place in an unusual manner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:125
verses.text: Thus, at the Crucifixion, the earth was shaken: and the Lord Himself says, "Then there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes in divers places".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:126
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:127
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:128
verses.text: ) But then the wrath of which it was a sign was against the adversaries: as for the disciples, it filled them with the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:129
verses.text: Observe, even the Apostles, after the prayer, are "filled with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:130
verses.text: "And the multitudes of them that believed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:131
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:132
verses.text: ) Great, you perceive, is the virtue of this thing, seeing their was need of this (grace) even in that Company.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:133
verses.text: For this is the foundation of all that is good, this of which he now for the second time makes mention, exhorting all men to the contempt of riches: "Neither said any of them that aught of the things he possessed was his own," "but they had all things common".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:134
verses.text: For that this was in consequence not merely of the miraculous signs, but of their own purpose, is manifest by the case of Sapphira and Ananias.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:135
verses.text: "And with great power gave the Apostles witness," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:136
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:137
verses.text: ) Not in word, but with power the Apostles exhibited their testimony of the Resurrection: just as Paul saith, "And my preaching was not with persuasive words of human wisdom, but with manifestation of the Spirit and of power".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:138
verses.text: And it is not merely, With power, but, "With great power".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:139
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:140
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:141
verses.text: ) "And great grace," it says, "was upon them all; for neither was there any among them that lacked".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:142
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:143
verses.text: ) This is why the grace (was upon them all,) for that "there was none that lacked:" that is, from the exceeding ardor of the givers, none was in want.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:144
verses.text: For they did not give in part, and in part reserve: nor yet in giving all, give it as their own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:145
verses.text: And they lived moreover in great abundance: they removed all inequality from among them, and made a goodly order.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:146
verses.text: "For as many as were possessors," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:147
verses.text: And with great respect they did this: for they did not presume to give into their hands, nor did they ostentatiously present, but brought to the Apostles' feet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:148
verses.text: To them they left it to be the dispensers, made them the owners, that thenceforth all should be defrayed as from common, not from private, property.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:149
verses.text: This was also a help to them against vain-glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:150
verses.text: If this were done now, we should live more pleasant lives, both rich and poor, nor would it be more pleasant to the poor than to the rich themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:151
verses.text: And if you please, let us now for awhile depict it in words, and derive at least this pleasure from it, since you have no mind for it in your actions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:152
verses.text: For at any rate this is evident, even from the facts which took place then, that by selling their possessions they did not come to be in need, but made them rich that were in need.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:153
verses.text: However, let us now depict this state of things in words, and let all sell their possessions, and bring them into the common stock—in words, I mean: let none be excited, rich or poor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:154
verses.text: How much gold think you would be collected? For my part, I conjecture—for of course it is not possible to speak exactly—that supposing all here, men and women, to empty out their whole property, lands, possessions, houses,—for I will not speak of slaves, since at that time there was no such thing, but doubtless such as were slaves they sat at liberty,—perhaps ten hundred thousand pounds weight of gold would be the amount collected: nay, twice or thrice as much.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:155
verses.text: For consider; at what number of "juga" (yokes) is our city rated? How many (of the population) shall we say are Christians? shall we say an hundred thousand, and the rest Greeks and Jews? Then what thousands (of pounds) of gold would be collected! And what is the number of poor? I do not think more than fifty thousand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:156
verses.text: Then to feed that number daily, what abundance there would be! And yet if the food were received in common, all taking their meals together, it would require no such great outlay after all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:157
verses.text: But, you will ask, what should we do after the money was spent? And do you think it ever could be spent? Would not the grace of God be ten thousand fold greater? Would not the grace of God be indeed richly poured out? Nay, should we not make it a heaven upon earth? If, where the numbers were three thousand and five thousand, the doing of this thing had such splendid success, and none of them complained of poverty, how much more glorious would this be in so vast a multitude? And even of those that are without, who would not contribute?—But, to show that it is the living separately that is expensive and causes poverty, let there be a house in which are ten children: and the wife and the man, let the one work at her wool, the other bring his earnings from his outdoor occupation: now tell me, in which way would these spend most? by taking their meals together and occupying one house, or by living separately? Of course, by living separately.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:158
verses.text: For if the ten children must live apart, they would need ten several rooms, ten tables, ten attendants, and the income otherwise in proportion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:159
verses.text: Is it not for this very reason, that where there is a great number of servants, they have all one table, that the expense may not be so great? For so it is, division always makes diminution, concord and agreement make increase.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:160
verses.text: The dwellers in the monasteries live just as the faithful did then: now did ever any of these die of hunger? was ever any of them not provided for with plenty of everything? Now, it seems, people are more afraid of this than of falling into a boundless and bottomless deep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:161
verses.text: But if we had made actual trial of this, then indeed we should boldly venture upon this plan (τοὕ πράγματος).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:162
verses.text: What grace too, think you, would there not be! For if at that time, when there was no believer but only the three thousand and the five thousand: when all, throughout the world, were enemies, when they could nowhere look for comfort, they yet boldly entered upon this plan with such success; how much more would this be the case now, when by the grace of God there are believers everywhere throughout the world? What Gentile would be left? For my part, I think there would not be one: we should so attract all, and draw them to us? But yet if we do but make fair progress, I trust in God that even this shall be realized.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:163
verses.text: Only do as I say, and let us successfully achieve things in their regular order; if God grant life, I trust that we shall soon bring you over to this way of life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:164
verses.text: In the first place, as regards that law about swearing: accomplish that; establish it firmly: and let him that has kept it make known him that has not, and call him to account withal and rebuke him sternly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:165
verses.text: For the (supra, Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:166
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:167
verses.text: ) appointed time (ἡ προθεσμία), is at hand and I am holding inquisition in the matter, and him that is found guilty I will banish and exclude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:168
verses.text: But God forbid that any such should be found among us; rather may it appear, that all have strictly kept this spiritual watchword.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:169
verses.text: And as in war it is by the watchword that friends and strangers are shown, so let it be now; for indeed now also we are engaged in a war; that we may know our brethren that are properly such.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:170
verses.text: For what a good thing it is that we should have this to be our cognizance both here and in a foreign land! What a weapon this, against the very head of the devil! A mouth that cannot swear will soon both engage God in prayers, and smite the devil a deadly blow.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:171
verses.text: A mouth that cannot swear will also be incapable of using insulting language.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:172
verses.text: Cast out this fire from your tongue, as you would from a house: this fire, drag it out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:173
verses.text: Give your tongue a little rest: make the sore less virulent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:174
verses.text: Yea, I beseech you, do this, that I may go on to set you another lesson: for as long as this is not rightly done, I dare not pass on to any other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:175
verses.text: Let this lesson be got perfectly, and you shall have a consciousness of the achievement, and then I will introduce you to other laws, or rather not I, but Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:176
verses.text: Implant in your soul this good thing, and by little and little ye shall be a paradise of God, far better than that paradise of old.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:177
verses.text: No serpent among you, no deadly tree, nor any such thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:178
verses.text: Fix this habit deep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:179
verses.text: If this be done, not ye only that are present shall be benefitted, but all that are in all the world; and not they alone, but those that are to succeed hereafter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:180
verses.text: For a good habit having once entered, and being kept by all, will be handed on to long ages, and no circumstances shall be able to erase it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:181
verses.text: If he that gathered sticks on the sabbath was stoned,—the man that is doing a far more heinous work than that gathering, the man that is amassing a load of sins, for such is the multitude of oaths, what shall he undergo? what shall he not have to endure? You will receive great assistance from God, if this be well achieved by you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:182
verses.text: If I were to say, Be not abusive, immediately you will plead to me your indignation; should I say, Be not envious, you will urge some other excuse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:183
verses.text: But in this case you have nothing of the kind to say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:184
verses.text: On which account I began with the easy precepts, which indeed is also the uniform practice in all arts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:185
verses.text: And thus one comes to the higher duties, by learning first those which are easier far.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:186
verses.text: How easy it is you will see, when by the grace of God having succeeded in this, you shall receive another precept.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:187
verses.text: Put it in my power to speak out boldly, in the presence both of Gentiles and of Jews, and, above all, of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:188
verses.text: Yea, I entreat you by the love, by the pangs wherewith I have travailed for your birth, "my little children".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:189
verses.text: I will not add what follows, "of whom I travail in birth again;" nor will I say, "until Christ be formed in you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:190
verses.text: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:191
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:192
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:193
verses.text: For I am persuaded, that Christ has been formed in you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:194
verses.text: Other language I will use towards you; "My brethren, dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and my crown".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:195
verses.text: (Phil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:196
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:197
verses.text: ) Believe me that I shall use no other language.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:198
verses.text: If at this moment there were placed upon my head ten thousand richly-jewelled royal crowns, they could not give me the joy which I feel at your growth in holiness; or rather, I do not think the monarch himself has such a joy, as that wherewith I joy over you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:199
verses.text: Let him have come home, victorious over all the nations at war with him, let him have won many other crowns besides the crown of his right; and receive other diadems as tokens of his victory: I do not think he would joy over his trophies, as I joy over your soul's progress.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:200
verses.text: For I exult, as if I had a thousand crowns on my head; and well may I rejoice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:201
verses.text: For if by the grace of God you achieve this good habit, you will have gained a thousand battles far more difficult than his; by wrestling and fighting with malicious demons, and fiendish spirits, with the tongue, not with sword, but by the will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:202
verses.text: For consider how much is gained, if so be that you do succeed! You have eradicated, first, a heinous habit; secondly, an evil conceit, the source of all evil, namely, the opinion that the thing is indifferent and can do no hurt; thirdly, wrath; fourthly, covetousness; for all these are the offspring of swearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:203
verses.text: Nay, hence you will acquire a sure footing in the way to all other virtues.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:204
verses.text: For as when children learn their letters, they learn not them alone, but by means of them are gradually taught to read; so shall it be with you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 34:205
verses.text: That evil conceit will no longer deceive you, you will not say, This is indifferent; you will no longer speak by mere habit, but will manfully stand against all, so that having perfected in all parts that virtue which is after God, you may reap eternal blessings, through the grace and loving-kindness of His Only-Begotten Son, to Whom with the Father and the Holy Ghost be glory, power and honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:1
verses.text: Homily XII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:2
verses.text: Acts IV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:3
verses.text: ,  And Joses, who by the Apostles was surnamed Barnabas (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation), a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus, having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the Apostles' feet".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:4
verses.text: The writer is now about to relate the affair of Ananias and Sapphira, and in order to show that the man's sin was of the worst description, he first mentions him who performed the virtuous deed; that, there being so great a multitude all doing the same, so great grace, so great miracles, he, taught by none of these, but blinded by covetousness, brought destruction upon his own head.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:5
verses.text: "Having land,—meaning that this was all he possessed,—sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the Apostles' feet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:6
verses.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, and kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the Apostles' feet".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:7
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:8
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:9
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:10
verses.text: ) The aggravating circumstance was, that the sin was concerted, and none other saw what was done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:11
verses.text: How came it into the mind of this hapless wretch to commit this crime? "But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:12
verses.text: ) Observe even in this, a great miracle performed, greater far than the former.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:13
verses.text: "Whiles it remained," says he, "was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:14
verses.text: ) That is, "Was there any obligation and force? do we constrain you against your will?" "Why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:15
verses.text: And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:16
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:17
verses.text: ) This miracle is greater than that of the lame man, in respect of the death inflicted, and the knowing what was in the thought of the heart, even what was done in secret.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:18
verses.text: "And great fear came on all them that heard these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:19
verses.text: And the young men arose, and wound him up, and carried him out, and buried him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:20
verses.text: And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:21
verses.text: And Peter answered unto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:23
verses.text: ) The woman he would fain save, for the man had been the author of the sin: therefore he gives her time to clear herself, and opportunity for repentance, saying, "Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:24
verses.text: Then Peter said unto her, How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Holy Ghost? Behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:25
verses.text: Then she fell down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost; and the young men came in, and found her dead, and, carrying her forth, buried her by her husband.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:26
verses.text: And great fear came upon all the Church, and upon as many as heard these things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:29
verses.text: )  After this fear had come upon them, he wrought more miracles; both Peter and the rest; "And by the hands of the Apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people; and they were all with one accord in Solomon's porch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:30
verses.text: And of the rest durst no man join himself to them," i-e: to the Apostles; "but the people magnified them," i-e: the Jewish people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:31
verses.text: If "no man durst join himself unto them," the Apostles, "there were," however, "the more added unto the Lord, believers, multitudes both of men and of women, insomuch that they brought out into the streets their impotent folk, and laid them upon couches and beds, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:32
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:34
verses.text: ) For Peter was the wonderful one, and he to whom they more gave heed both because of his public harangue, the first and the second and the third, and because of the miracle; for he it was that wrought the miracle, the first, the second, the third: for the present miracle was twofold: first, the convicting the thoughts of the heart, and next the inflicting of death at his word of command.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:35
verses.text: "That at the least the shadow of Peter passing by," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:36
verses.text: This had not occurred in the history of Christ; but see here what He had told them actually coming to pass, that "they which believe on Me, the works that I do shall they do also; and greater works than these shall they do".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:37
verses.text: (John xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:38
verses.text: ) "There came also a multitude out of the cities round about unto Jerusalem, bringing sick folks, and them that were vexed with unclean spirits; and they were healed every one".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:40
verses.text: )  And now I would have you observe the way in which their whole life is interwoven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:41
verses.text: First there was despondency on account of Christ taken from them, and then came joy because of the Spirit descending upon them; again, dejection because of the scoffers, and then joy in the result of their own apology.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:42
verses.text: And here again we find both dejection and gladness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:43
verses.text: In that they were become conspicuous, and that God made revelations to them, there was gladness: in that they had cut off some of their own company, there was sadness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:44
verses.text: Once more: again there is gladness upon their success, and again sadness by reason of the High Priest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:45
verses.text: And so it will be seen to be the case throughout.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:46
verses.text: And the same will be found to hold in the case of the ancient saints likewise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:47
verses.text: —But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:48
verses.text: "They sold them," it is written, "and brought the prices, and laid them down at the Apostles' feet".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:49
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:50
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:52
verses.text: ) See, my beloved brethren, how instead of leaving the Apostles to sell, they themselves sold, and presented the prices to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:53
verses.text: "But a certain man named Ananias," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:55
verses.text: ) This history touches Bishops too, and very forcibly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:56
verses.text: And the wife of Ananias was privy to the thing done: therefore he examines her.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:57
verses.text: But perhaps some one will say that he dealt very harshly with her.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:58
verses.text: What do you mean? What harshness? If for gathering sticks a man is to be stoned, much rather ought he for sacrilege; for this money was become sacred.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:59
verses.text: He that has chosen to sell his goods and distribute them, and then withdraws them, is guilty of sacrilege.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:60
verses.text: But if he is sacrilegious, who resumes from his own, much more he who takes from what is not his own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:61
verses.text: And do not think that because the consequence is not now the same, the crime will go unpunished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:62
verses.text: Do you see that this is the charge brought against Ananias, that having made the money sacred, he afterwards secreted it? Couldest thou not, said Peter, after selling thy land, use the proceeds as thine own? Wast thou forbidden? Wherefore after thou hadst promised it? See how at the very beginning, the devil made his attack; in the very midst of such signs and wonders, how this man was hardened! Something of the same kind had happened upon a time in the Old Testament.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:63
verses.text: The son of Charmi coveted the devoted thing: for observe there also what vengeance ensues upon the sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:64
verses.text: Sacrilege, beloved, is a most grievous crime, insulting, and full of contempt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:65
verses.text: We neither obliged thee to sell, the Apostle says, nor to give thy money when thou hadst sold; of thine own free choice thou didst it; why hast thou then stolen from the sacred treasury? "Why," he says, "hath Satan filled thine heart?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:66
verses.text: ) Well, if Satan did the thing, why is the man made guilty of it? For admitting the influence of the devil, and being filled with it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:67
verses.text: You will say, they ought to have corrected him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:68
verses.text: But he would not have received correction; for he that has seen such things as he had seen, and is none the better, would certainly be none the better for anything else that could be done; the matter was not one to be simply passed over: like a gangrene, it must be cut out, that it might not infect the rest of the body.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:69
verses.text: As it is, both the man himself is benefitted in regard that he is not left to advance further in wickedness, and the rest, in that they are made more earnest; otherwise the contrary would have ensued.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:70
verses.text: In the next place, Peter proves him guilty, and shows that the deed was not hidden from him, and then pronounces the sentence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:71
verses.text: But wherefore, upon what purpose hast thou done this? Didst thou wish to keep it? Thou oughtest to have kept it all along, and never to have professed to give it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:72
verses.text: The sacrilege, beloved, is a grievous one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:73
verses.text: For another, it may be, coveted what was not his own: but it was at thy discretion to keep what was thine own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:74
verses.text: Why then didst thou first make it sacred, and then take it? Out of excessive contempt hast thou done this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:75
verses.text: The deed does not admit of pardon, it is past pleading for.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:76
verses.text: —Therefore let it be no stumbling-block to any, if at present also there are sacrilegious persons.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:77
verses.text: If there were such persons then, much more now, when evils are many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:78
verses.text: But let us "rebuke them before all, that others also may fear".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:79
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:80
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:81
verses.text: ) Judas was sacrilegious, but it was no stumbling-block to the disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:82
verses.text: Do you see how many evils spring from love of money? "And great fear, it is said, came on all them that heard these things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:83
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:84
verses.text: ) That man was punished, and others profited thereby.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:85
verses.text: Not without cause.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:86
verses.text: And yet, signs had been wrought before: true, but there was not such a sense of fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:87
verses.text: So true is that saying, "The Lord is known by executing judgments".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:88
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:89
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:90
verses.text: ) The same thing had occurred in the case of the Ark: Uzzah was punished and fear came upon the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:91
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:92
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:93
verses.text: ) But in that instance the king through fear removed from him the Ark; but here the disciples became more earnestly heedful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:94
verses.text: "And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:95
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:96
verses.text: ) But observe how Peter, instead of sending for her, waited till she entered; and how none of the others durst carry out the intelligence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:97
verses.text: Such the teacher's awfulness, such the disciples' reverence, such the obedience! "An interval of three hours,"—and yet the woman did not hear of it, and none of those present reported it, although there was time enough for it to be noised abroad; but they were afraid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:98
verses.text: This circumstance the Evangelist relates with wonder even, when he says, "Not knowing what was done, came in".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:99
verses.text: "And Peter answered unto her," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:101
verses.text: ) And yet she might have perceived even from this that Peter knew the secret.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:102
verses.text: For why, having questioned none other, does he question you? Was it not clear that he asked because he knew? But so great was her hardness, it would not let her attempt to evade the guilt; and with great confidence she replied; for she thought she was speaking only to a man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:103
verses.text: The aggravation of the sin was, that they committed it as with one soul, just as upon a settled compact between them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:104
verses.text: "How is it that ye have agreed together," he said, "to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:105
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:106
verses.text: ) First he makes her learn the sin, and then shows that she will justly suffer the same punishment with her husband, since she has committed the same wickedness: "And they shall carry thee out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:107
verses.text: And she fell down straightway at his feet," for she was standing near him, "and yielded up the ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:108
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:109
verses.text: ) So entirely by their own act had they invited upon themselves the vengeance! Who after that would not be struck with awe? who would not fear the Apostle? who would not marvel? who not be afraid? "And they were with one accord, all of them in Solomon's porch," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:110
verses.text: ) no longer in a house, but having occupied the very Temple, they there passed their time! No longer they guarded themselves against touching the unclean; nay, without scruple they handled the dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:111
verses.text: And observe how, while to their own people they are severe, against the aliens they do not exercise their power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:112
verses.text: "But the people," he says, "magnified them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:113
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:114
verses.text: ) And as he had mentioned their being "in Solomon's porch," that you may not wonder how the multitude allowed this, he tells us that they did not dare even to approach them: for "no man," he says, "durst join himself unto them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:115
verses.text: "But believers were the more added unto the Lord, multitudes both of men and women: insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:116
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:117
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:118
verses.text: ) Great faith, surpassing what had been shown in the case of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:119
verses.text: How comes this? Because Christ declared: "And greater works than these shall he do, because I go unto My Father".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:120
verses.text: (John xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:121
verses.text: ) And these things the people do, while the Apostles remain there, and are not moving about from place to place: also from other places they were all bringing their sick on beds and couches: and from all quarters accrued to them fresh tribute of wonder; from them that believed, from them that were healed, from him that was punished; from their boldness of speech towards those (their adversaries), from the virtuous behavior of the believers: for certainly the effect produced was not owing to the miracles only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:122
verses.text: For though the Apostles themselves modestly ascribe it all to this cause, declaring that they did these things in the name of Christ, yet at the same time the life and noble conduct of the men helped to produce this effect.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:123
verses.text: "And believers were more added unto the Lord, multitudes both of men and women".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:124
verses.text: Observe, how he now no longer tells the number of them that believe; at such a rate was the faith making way even to an immense multitude, and so widely was the Resurrection proclaimed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:125
verses.text: So then "the people magnified them:" but they were now no longer lightly to be despised as once they were: for in a little moment, at a single turn of the scale, such have been the effects produced by the fisherman and by the publican! Earth was become a heaven, for manner of life, for boldness of speech, for wonders, for all besides; like Angels were they looked upon with wonder: all unconcerued for ridicule, for threats, for perils: compassionate were they, and beneficent; some of them they succoured with money, and some with words, and some with healing of their bodies and of their souls; no kind of healing (πἅν εἶδος ἰατρείας) but they accomplished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:126
verses.text: Peter all but pleads for himself, when at the point to inflict the punishment, and at the same time gives a lesson to the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:127
verses.text: For because the act would seem exceeding stern, therefore it is that he does so much in the case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:128
verses.text: In respect of the woman also the process of judgment was terrible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:129
verses.text: But see how many evils grow out of the sacrilege: covetousness, contempt of God, impiety; and upon these too he pleaded for himself before the assembly, in that he did not immediately proceed to punishment, but first exposed the sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:130
verses.text: None groaned, none lamented, all were terrified.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:131
verses.text: For as their faith increased, the signs also were multiplied, and great was the fear among their own company: for the things which are from without do not so militate (πολεμεἵ) against our peace, as do the acts of our own people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:132
verses.text: If we be firmly joined together, no warfare will be hard: but the mischief would be the being divided and broken up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:133
verses.text: Now they went about in the public place: with boldness they attacked even the market, and in the midst of enemies they prevailed, and that saying was fulfilled, "Be Thou Ruler in the midst among Thine enemies".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:134
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:135
verses.text: cx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:136
verses.text: ) This was a greater miracle, that they, arrested, cast into prison, should do such acts as these!  If those for lying suffered such things, what shall not the perjured suffer? Because she simply affirmed, "Yea, for so much," ye see what she suffered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:137
verses.text: Bethink you then; they that swear and forswear themselves, of what should they be worthy? It comes in opportunely to-day even from the Old Testament to show you the heinousness of perjury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:138
verses.text: "There was," it says, "a flying sickle, ten cubits in breadth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:139
verses.text: (Zech.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:140
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:141
verses.text: ) The "flying" betokens the swift advent of the vengeance which pursues oaths; that it is many cubits in length and breadth, signifies the force and magnitude of the woes; that it comes flying "from heaven," is to show that the vengeance comes from the judgment-seat on high: that it is in the form of a sickle," denotes the inevitableness of the doom: for just as the sickle, where it comes and has hooked the neck, is not drawn back with nothing but itself, but with the head reaped off, even so the vengeance which comes upon the swearers is severe, and will not desist until it have completed its work.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:142
verses.text: But if we swear and escape, let us not be confident; this is but to our woe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:143
verses.text: For what think ye? How many, since Ananias and Sapphira, have dared the same with them? How is it then, say you, that they have not met with the same fate? Not because it was allowed in them, but because they are reserved for a greater punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:144
verses.text: For those who often sin and are not punished, have greater reason to fear and dread than if they were punished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:145
verses.text: For the vengeance is increased for them by their present impunity and the long-suffering of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:146
verses.text: Then let us not look to this, that we are not punished; but let us consider whether we have not sinned: if sinning we are not punished, we have the more reason to tremble.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:147
verses.text: Say, if you have a slave, and you only threaten him, and do not beat him; when is he most in fear, when most inclined to run away? Is is not when you only threaten him? And hence we advise each other not to be continually using threats, thereby choosing rather to agitate the mind by the terror, and lacerating it worse than with blows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:148
verses.text: For in the one instance the punishment is momentary, but in the other it is perpetual.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:149
verses.text: If then no one feels the stroke of the sickle, do not look to this, but rather let each consider whether he commits such sins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:150
verses.text: Many like things are done now as were done before the Flood, yet no flood has been sent: because there is a hell threatened, and vengeance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:151
verses.text: Many sin as the people did in Sodom, yet no rain of fire has been poured down; because a river of fire is prepared.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:152
verses.text: Many go the lengths of Pharaoh; yet they have not fared like Pharaoh, they have not been drowned in a Red Sea: for the sea that awaits them, is the sea of the bottomless pit, where the punishment is not accompanied with insensibility, where there is no suffocation to end all, but in ever lengthened torture, in burning, in strangling, they are consumed there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:153
verses.text: Many have offended like the Israelites, but no serpents have devoured them: there awaits them the worm that never dieth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:154
verses.text: Many have been like Gehazi, yet they have not been struck with leprosy: for instead of leprosy, it remains for them to be cut asunder, and numbered among the hypocrites.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:155
verses.text: Many have both sworn and forsworn; but if they have indeed escaped, let us not be confident: the gnashing of teeth awaits them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:156
verses.text: Yea, here too they will suffer many grievous woes, though, it may be, not immediately, but after further transgressions, that the vengeance may be the greater; for even we often set out at first with small sins, and then through great offences lose all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:157
verses.text: Therefore when you see anything happening to you, call to mind that particular sin of yours.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:158
verses.text: The sons of Jacob are an example of this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:159
verses.text: Remember Joseph's brothers; they had sold their brother, they had even attempted to slay him; nay, they had slain him, as far as inclination went; they had deceived and grieved the old man; they suffered nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:160
verses.text: After many years they are brought into extreme peril, and now they are put in remembrance of this their sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:161
verses.text: Exceeding wisely is this circumstance brought in.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:162
verses.text: Hear what they say: "We are verily guilty concerning our brother".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:163
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:164
verses.text: xlii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:165
verses.text: ) In this manner then do thou also, when anything happens, say, We are verily guilty, because we have not obeyed Christ; because we have sworn; my much swearing, and my false swearing, has fallen upon my own head.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:166
verses.text: Confess thou; since they also confessed, and were saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:167
verses.text: For what though the punishment follow not immediately? Since Ahab also did not immediately after his sin in the matter of Naboth suffer that vengeance which he yet at last suffered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:168
verses.text: ( Kings xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:169
verses.text: ) And what is the reason of this? God sets thee a time, in which to wash thyself clean; but if thou persist, at last He will send down the vengeance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:170
verses.text: You have seen the fate of liars.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:171
verses.text: Consider what is the fate of false swearers, consider, and desist.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:172
verses.text: It is impossible a swearer should not forswear himself, whether he will or not; and no perjurer can be saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:173
verses.text: One false oath sufficeth to finish all, to draw down upon us the whole measure of vengeance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 35:174
verses.text: Let us then take heed to ourselves, that we may escape the punishment due to this offence, and be deemed worthy of the loving kindness of God, through the grace and mercies of His only-begotten Son, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost be glory, power, and honor, now and ever, and world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:1
verses.text: Homily XIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:2
verses.text: Acts V.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:3
verses.text: ,  "Then having risen up, the high-priest and they that were with him (which is the sect of the Sadducees) were filled with indignation, and laid their hands on the Apostles, and put them in the common prison".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:4
verses.text: "Having risen up," that is, being roused, being excited at the things taking place, the high-priest and they which were with him (which is the sect of the Sadducees) were filled with indignation, and laid their hands on the Apostles:" they now assault them more vigorously: "and put them in the common prison;" but did not forthwith bring them to trial, because they expected them again to be softened down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:5
verses.text: "But the Angel of the Lord opened the prison doors, and brought them forth, and said, Go, stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:6
verses.text: "And when they heard that, they entered into the temple early in the morning, and taught".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:7
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:8
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:9
verses.text: ) This was done both for the encouragement of the disciples, and for the benefit and instruction of the others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:10
verses.text: And observe how the proceeding in the present instance is just the same as in what Christ Himself did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:11
verses.text: Namely, in His miracles though He does not let men see them in the act of being wrought, He furnishes the means whereby they may be apprised of the things wrought: thus, in His Resurrection, He did not let them see how He rose: in the water made wine, the guests do not see it done, for they have been drinking much, and the discernment He leaves to others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:12
verses.text: Just so in the present case, they do not see them in the act of being brought forth, but the proofs from which they might gather what had been done, they do see.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:13
verses.text: And it was by night that the Angel put them forth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:14
verses.text: Why was this? Because in this way they were more believed than they would have been in the other: so, people would not even have had occasion to put the question: they would not in some other way have believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:15
verses.text: So it was in the old times, in the case of Nebuchadnezzar: he saw them praising God in the furnace, and then indeed he was put in amazement.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:16
verses.text: (Dan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:17
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:18
verses.text: ) Whereas then these priests ought as their first question to have asked, How came ye out? instead of this, as if nothing had happened, they ask, "Did we not straitly charge you not to speak?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:19
verses.text: ) And observe, by report of others they are apprised of all the circumstances: they see the prison remaining closed with safety, and the guards standing before the doors.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:20
verses.text: A twofold security this; as was the case at the sepulchre, where was both the seal, and the men to watch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:21
verses.text: See how they fought against God! Say, was this of man's doing, that happened to them? Who led them forth, when the doors were shut? How came they out, with the keepers standing before the door? Verily they must be mad or drunken to talk so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:22
