verses.text: Here are men, whom neither prison, nor bonds, nor closed doors, had been able to keep in; and yet they expect to overpower them: such is their childish folly! Their officers come and confess what has taken place, as if on purpose to debar them from all show of reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:23
verses.text: Do you mark how there is miracle upon miracle, differing in kind, some wrought by them, others on them, and these more illustrious than the others? "And when they heard that, they entered into the temple early in the morning, and taught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:24
verses.text: But the high-priest came, and they that were with him, and called the council together, and all the senate of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:25
verses.text: But when the officers came, and found them not in the prison, they returned, and told, saying, The prison truly found we shut with all safety, and the keepers standing without before the doors: but when we had opened, we found no man within.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:26
verses.text: Now when the high-priest and the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these things, they doubted of them whereunto this would grow".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:29
verses.text: ) It is well ordered that the information was not brought to them at once, but they are first utterly at a loss what to think, that when they have considered it well and seen that there is a Divine Power in the case, then they may learn the whole state of the case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:30
verses.text: "Then came one, and told them, saying, Behold, the men whom ye put in prison are standing in the temple, and teaching the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:31
verses.text: Then went the captain with the other officers, and brought them without violence: for they feared the multitude, lest they should have been stoned".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:32
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:34
verses.text: ) O the folly of the men! "They feared," saith he, "the multitude".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:35
verses.text: Why, how had the multitude helped the Apostles? When they ought to have feared that God Who was continually delivering them like winged creatures out of their power, instead of that, "they feared the multitude!" "And the high-priest," shameless, reckless, senseless, "asked them, saying, Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name? and, behold ye have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine and intend to bring this man's blood upon us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:38
verses.text: ) What then (say the Apostles)? Again with mildness they address them; and yet they might have said, "Who are ye, that ye countermand God?" But what do they say? Again in the way of exhortation and advice, and with much mildness, they make answer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:39
verses.text: "Then Peter and the other Apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:41
verses.text: ) High magnanimity! He shows them too that they are fighting against God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:42
verses.text: For, he says, Whom ye killed, Him hath God raised up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:43
verses.text: "The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, Whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:44
verses.text: Him hath God exalted with His right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:47
verses.text: ) And again they refer the whole to the Father, that He should not seem to be alien to the Father.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:48
verses.text: "And hath exalted," saith He, "with his right hand".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:49
verses.text: He affirms not merely the Resurrection, but the Exaltation also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:50
verses.text: "For to give repentance to Israel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:51
verses.text: Observe here as before the gain (to them): observe the perfection of doctrine conveyed in the form of apology.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:52
verses.text: "And we are witnesses of these things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:54
verses.text: ) Great boldness of speech! And the ground of their credibility: "And so is also the Holy Ghost, Whom God hath given to them that obey Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:55
verses.text: Do you observe that they allege not only the Spirit's testimony? And they said not, "Whom He hath given" to us, but, "to them that obey Him:" therein alike showing their own unassuming temper, and intimating the greatness of the gift, and showing the hearers that it was possible for them also to receive the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:56
verses.text: See, how these people were instructed both by deeds and by words, and yet they paid no heed, that their condemnation might be just.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:57
verses.text: For to this end did God suffer the Apostles to be brought to trial, that both their adversaries might be instructed, and all might learn, and that the Apostles might be invigorated to boldness of speech.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:58
verses.text: "And they hearing that, were cut to the heart".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:59
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:60
verses.text: ) The others (on a former occasion) "when they heard these things were pricked;" here they were cut (as with a saw) (διεπρίοντο) "and desired to slay them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:61
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:62
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:63
verses.text: )  But it is necessary now to look over again what we have read.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:64
verses.text: "But the angel of the Lord by night opened the prison doors, and brought them forth, and said, Go, stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:65
verses.text: Brought them forth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:66
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:67
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:68
verses.text: ) He did not bring them away to benefit themselves thereby, but, "Stand," he says, "and speak in the temple to the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:69
verses.text: But if the guards had put them out, as those thought, they would have fled, that is, supposing they had been induced to come out: and if those had put them forth, they would not have stood in the temple, but would have absconded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:70
verses.text: No one is so void of sense, as not at once to see this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:71
verses.text: "Did we not straitly charge you?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:72
verses.text: ) Well, if they undertook to obey you, ye do well to call them to account: but if even at the very time they told you they would not obey, what account have you to call them to, what defence is there for them to make? "And behold ye have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine, and intend to bring this man's blood upon us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:73
verses.text: Mark the inconsistency of the accusations, and the exceeding folly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:74
verses.text: They want to make it appear now, that the dispositions of the Jews are sanguinary, as if they were doing these things not for the truth's sake, but in the wish to be revenged.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:75
verses.text: And for this reason too the Apostles do not answer them with defiance (θρασέως): for they were teachers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:76
verses.text: And yet where is the man, who, with a whole city to back him, and endowed with so great grace, would not have spoken and uttered something big? But not so did these: for they were not angered; no, they pitied these men, and wept over them, and marked in what way they might free them from their error and wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:77
verses.text: And they no longer say to them, "Judge ye:" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:78
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:79
verses.text: ) but they simply affirm, saying, "Whom God raised up, Him do we preach: it is by the will of God that these things are done".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:80
verses.text: They said not, Did not we tell you even then, that "we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard?" (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:81
verses.text: ) for they are not contentious for glory; but they repeat again the same story,—the Cross, the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:82
verses.text: And they tell not, wherefore He was crucified—that it was for our sakes: but they hint at this indeed, but not openly as yet, wishing to terrify them awhile.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:83
verses.text: And yet what sort of rhetoric is here? None at all, but everywhere it is still the Passion, and the Resurrection and the Ascension, and the end wherefore: "The God of our fathers raised up Jesus," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:84
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:85
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:86
verses.text: ) And yet what improbable assertions are these! Very improbable, no doubt; but for all that, not rulers, not people, had a word to say against them: but those had their mouths stopped, and these received the teaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:87
verses.text: "And we," saith he, "are witnesses of these things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:88
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:89
verses.text: ) Of what things? Of His having promised forgiveness and repentance: for the Resurrection indeed was acknowledged, now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:90
verses.text: But that He giveth forgiveness, both we are witnesses, and "so is the Holy Ghost," Who would not have come down, unless sins had been first remitted: so that this is an indisputable proof.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:91
verses.text: "When they heard that, they were cut" (to the heart), "and took counsel to slay them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:92
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:93
verses.text: ) Hearest thou of the forgiveness of sins, O wretched man, and that God doth not demand punishment, and dost thou wish to slay them? What wickedness was this! And yet, either they ought to have convicted them of lying, or if they could not do that, to have believed: but if they did not choose to believe, yet they ought not to slay them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:94
verses.text: For what was there deserving of death? Such was their intoxication, they did not even see what had taken place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:95
verses.text: Observe, how everywhere the Apostles, when they have made mention of the crime, add the mention of forgiveness; showing, that while what had been done was worthy of death, that which was given was proffered to them as to benefactors! In what other way could any one have persuaded them?  "Then stood up the high-priest," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:96
verses.text: As men in high repute, these (the Apostles) were about to take their place near to the Prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:97
verses.text: The Sadducees were they that were most sore on the subject of the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:98
verses.text: But perchance some one will say: Why, what man, endowed with such gifts as the Apostles were, would not have been great? But consider, I pray you, how, before that they were endowed with the grace, "they were continuing steadfastly with one accord in prayer" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:99
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:100
verses.text: ), and depending on the aid from above.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:101
verses.text: And dost thou, my beloved, hope for the kingdom of heaven, yet endurest naught? And hast thou received the Spirit, yet sufferest not such things, nor encounterest perils? But they, before they had breathing-time from their former dangers, were again led into others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:102
verses.text: And even this too, that there is no arrogance, no conceit, how great a good it is! To converse with mildness, what a gain it is! For not all that they did was the immediate work of grace, but there are many marks of their own zeal as well.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:103
verses.text: That the gifts of grace shine forth in them, this was from their own diligence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:104
verses.text: See, for instance, from the very beginning, how careful Peter is; how sober and vigilant: how they that believed cast away their riches, had no private property, continued in prayer, showed that they were of one mind, passed their time in fastings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:105
verses.text: What grace, I ask (alone), did all this? Therefore it is that He brings the evidence home to them through their own officers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:106
verses.text: Just as in the case of Christ, it was their officers who said, "Never man spake as this Man speaketh".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:107
verses.text: (John vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:108
verses.text: ) These (proofs) are more apt to be believed than the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:109
verses.text: —Observe also the moderation shown by (the rulers) themselves, and how they give way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:110
verses.text: "The high-priest asked them, saying," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:111
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:112
verses.text: ): here he reasons with them, forsooth, in a moderate tone; for he was frightened: indeed to hinder was what he desired rather than to kill, since that he cannot do: and with the view to rouse them all, and show them the extreme danger they are in, "And intend," says he (to the Apostles), "to bring this man's blood upon us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:113
verses.text: Dost thou still take Him to be but man? He wants to make it appear that the injunction was necessary for their own safety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:114
verses.text: But mark what (Peter) says: "Him hath God exalted with His right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:116
verses.text: ) Here he forbears to mention the Gentiles, not to give them a handle against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:117
verses.text: "And they desired," it says, "to slay them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:118
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:119
verses.text: ) See again these in perplexity, these in pain: but those in quiet and cheerfulness and delight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:120
verses.text: It is not merely, They were grieved, but "They were cut" (to the heart).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:121
verses.text: Truly this makes good that proverb, "Evil do, evil fare:" as we may see in this case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:122
verses.text: Here were these men in bonds, set at the bar of judgment, and the men that sit in judgment upon them were in distress and helpless perplexity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:123
verses.text: For as he who strikes a blow upon the adamant, gets the shock of the blow himself, so it was with these men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:124
verses.text: But they saw that not only was their boldness of speech not stopped, but rather their preaching increased the more, and that they discoursed without a thought of fear, and afforded them no handles against them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:125
verses.text: Let us imitate these, my beloved: let us be undaunted in all our dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:126
verses.text: There is nothing dreadful to him that fears God; but all that is dreadful is for others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:127
verses.text: For when a man is delivered from his passions, and regards all present things as a shadow, say, from whom shall he suffer anything dreadful? whom shall he have to fear? whom shall he need plead to? Let us flee to this Rock which cannot be shaken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:128
verses.text: If any one were to build for us a city, and throw up a wall around it, and remove us to a land uninhabited, where there were none to disturb us, and there supply us with abundance of everything, and not suffer us to have aught to trouble us with anybody, he would not set us in such perfect safety, as Christ hath done now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:129
verses.text: Be it a city made of brass, if you will, surrounded on all sides with a wall, lofty and impregnable, let there be no enemy near it; let it have land plentiful and rich, let there be added abundance of other things, let the citizens too be mild and gentle, and no evil-doer there, neither robber, nor thief, no informer, no court of justice, but merely agreements (συναλλάλματα); and let us dwell in this city: not even thus would it be possible to live in security.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:130
verses.text: Wherefore? Because there could not but be differences with servants, with wives, with children, to be a groundwork of much discomfort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:131
verses.text: But here was nothing of the kind; for here was nothing at all to pain them or cause any discomfort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:132
verses.text: Nay, what is more wonderful to say, the very things which are thought to cause discomfort, became matter of all joy and gladness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:133
verses.text: For tell me, what was there for them to be annoyed at? what to take amiss? Shall we cite a particular case for comparison with them? Well, let there be one of consular dignity, let him be possessed of much wealth, let him dwell in the imperial city, let him have no troublesome business with anybody, but only live in delight, and have nothing else but this to do, seated at the very summit of wealth and honor and power: and let us set against him a Peter, in bonds if you will, in evils without number: and we shall find that he is the man that lives the most delightfully.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:134
verses.text: For when there is such excess of joy, as to be delighted when in bonds, think what must be the greatness of that joy! For like as those who are high in office, whatsoever evils may happen, are not sensible of them, but continue in enjoyment: so did these the more rejoice on account of these very evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:135
verses.text: For it is impossible, impossible in words to express how great pleasure falls to their lot, who suffer for Christ's sake: for they rejoice in their sufferings, rather than in their good things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:136
verses.text: Whoso loves Christ, knows what I say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:137
verses.text: —But what as regards safety? And who, I ask, if he were ever so rich, could have escaped so many perils, going about among so many different nations, for the sole purpose of bringing about a reformation in their manner of life? For it was just as if by royal mandate that they carried all before them, nay, far more easily, for never mandate could have been so effectual, as their words were.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:138
verses.text: For the royal edict compels by necessity, but these drew men willingly and spontaneously, yea, and with hearts above measure thankful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:139
verses.text: What royal edict, I ask, would ever have persuaded men to part with all their property and their lives; to despise home, country, kindred, yea, even self-preservation? Yet the voices of fishermen and tent-makers availed for this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:140
verses.text: So that they were both happy, and more powerful and strong than all others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:141
verses.text: "Yes," say you, "those of course were, for they wrought miracles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:142
verses.text: (supra, p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:143
verses.text: , note.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:144
verses.text: ) But I ask what miracles did those who believed work, the three thousand, and the five thousand; and yet these, we read, passed their time in gladness? And well they might: for that which is the groundwork of all discomforts, the possession of riches, was done away with.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:145
verses.text: For that, that, I say, was ever the cause both of wars and fighting, and grief, and discomfort, and all evils: the thing which makes life full of labor and troubles, it is that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:146
verses.text: And indeed it would be found that many more rich than poor have reason to be sad.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:147
verses.text: If any think this is not true, their notion is derived not from the nature of the things, but from their own fancy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:148
verses.text: And if the rich do enjoy some sort of pleasure, this is not to be wondered at: for even those who are covered all over with the itch, have a good deal of pleasure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:149
verses.text: For that the rich are for all the world like these, and their mind affected in the same sort, is plain from this circumstance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:150
verses.text: Their cares annoy them, and they choose to be engrossed with them for the sake of the momentary pleasure: while those who are free from these affections, are in health and without discomfort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:151
verses.text: Whether is more pleasant, I ask, whether of the two more safe? To have to take thought only for a single loaf of bread and suit of clothes, or for an immense family, both slaves and freemen, not having care about himself (only)? For as this man has his fears for himself, so have you for those who depend on your own person.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:152
verses.text: Why, I pray you, does poverty seem a thing to be shunned? Just in the same way as other good things are, in the judgment of many, things to be deprecated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:153
verses.text: "Yes," say you, "but it is not that those good things are subjects for deprecation, but that they are hard of attainment".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:154
verses.text: Well, so is poverty, not a thing to be deprecated, but hard of attainment: so that if one could bear it, there would be no reason to deprecate it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:155
verses.text: For how is it that the Apostles did not deprecate it? how is it that many even choose it, and so far from deprecating, even run to it? For that which is really a thing to be deprecated, cannot be an object of choice save to madmen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:156
verses.text: But if it be the men of philosophic and elevated minds that betake themselves to this, as to a safe and salubrious retreat, no wonder if to the rest it wears a different appearance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:157
verses.text: For, in truth, the rich man seems to me to be just like a city, unwalled, situated in a plain, inviting assailants from all sides: but poverty, a secure fortress, strong as brass can make it, and the way up to it difficult.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:158
verses.text: "And yet," say you, "the fact is just the reverse: for these are they, who are often dragged into courts of law, these are they who are overborne and ill-treated".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:159
verses.text: No: not the poor, as poor, but those who being poor want to be rich.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:160
verses.text: But I am not speaking of them, but of such as make it their study to live in poverty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:161
verses.text: For say, how comes it that nobody ever drags the brethren of the hills into courts of law? and yet if to be poor is to be a mark for oppression, those ought most of all to be dragged thither, since they are poorer than all others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:162
verses.text: How comes it that nobody drags the common mendicants into the law-courts? Because they are come to the extreme of poverty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:163
verses.text: How is it that none does violence to them, none lays vexatious informations against them? Because they abide in a stronghold too safe for that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:164
verses.text: How many think it a condition hard to struggle against, poverty, I mean, and begging! What then, I ask, is it a good thing to beg? "It is good, if there be comfort," say you; "if there be one to give: it is a life so free from trouble and reverses, as every one knows".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:165
verses.text: But I do not mean to commend this; God forbid! what I advise is the not aiming at riches.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:166
verses.text: For say, whom would you rather call blessed? those who find themselves at home with virtue, (ἐπιτηδείους πρὸς ἀρετήν) or those who stand aloof? Of course, those who are near.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:167
verses.text: Say then, which of the two is the man to learn anything that is profitable, and to shine in the true wisdom? the former, or the latter? The first, all must see.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:168
verses.text: If you doubt it, satisfy yourself in this way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:169
verses.text: Fetch hither from the market-place any of the poor wretches there; let him be a cripple, lame, maimed: and then produce some other person, comely of aspect, strong in body, full of life and vigor in every part, overflowing with riches: let him be of illustrious birth, and possessed of great power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:170
verses.text: Then let us bring both these into the school of philosophy: which of them, I ask, is more likely to receive the things taught? The first precept, at the outset, "Be lowly and moderate" (for this is Christ's command): which will be most able to fulfil it, this one or the other? "Blessed are they that mourn" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:171
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:172
verses.text: ): which will most receive this saying? "Blessed are the lowly:" which will most listen to this? "Blessed are the pure in heart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:173
verses.text: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:174
verses.text: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake" (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:175
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:176
verses.text: Which will with ease receive these sayings? And, if you will, let us apply to all of them these rules, and see how they will fit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:177
verses.text: Is not the one inflamed and swollen all over, while the other is ever lowly minded and subdued in his whole bearing? It is quite plain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:178
verses.text: Yes, and there is a saying to that effect among those that are without: "(I was) a slave, Epictetus by name, a cripple in body, for poverty a very Irus, and a friend of the Immortals".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:179
verses.text: For how, I would ask, can it be otherwise, but that the soul of the rich must teem with evils; folly, vainglory, numberless lusts, anger and passion, covetousness, iniquity, and what not? So that even for philosophy, the former is more congenially (ἐπιτηδεία) disposed than the latter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:180
verses.text: By all means seek to ascertain which is the more pleasant: for this I see is the point everywhere discussed, whether such an one has the more enjoyable way of life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:181
verses.text: And yet even as regards this, we need not be in doubt; for to be near to health, is also to have much enjoyment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:182
verses.text: But whether of the two, I would ask, is best disposed (ἐπιτήδειος) to the matter now in hand, that which we will needs carry into accomplishment—our law, I mean—the poor man or the rich? Whether of them will be apt to swear? The man who has children to be provoked with, the man who has his covenants with innumerable parties, or the man who is concerned to apply for just a loaf of bread or a garment? This man has not even need of oaths, should he wish, but always lives free from cares of business; nay, more, it is often seen that he who is disciplined to swear not at all, will also despise riches; and one shall see in his whole behavior his ways all branching off from this one good habit, and leading to meekness, to contempt of riches, to piety, to subduedness of soul, to compunction of heart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:183
verses.text: Then let us not be indolent, my beloved, but let us again show great earnestness: they who have succeeded, that they may keep the success achieved, that they be not easily caught by the receding wave, nor the refluent tide carry them back again they too who are yet behindhand, that they may be raised up again, and strive to make up that which is wanting.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:184
verses.text: And meanwhile let those who have succeeded, help those who have not been able to do the same: and by reaching out their hands, as they would to men struggling in the deep water, receive them into the haven of no-swearing (ἀνωμοσίας).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:185
verses.text: For it is indeed a haven of safety, to swear not at all: whatever storms burst upon us, to be in no danger of sinking there: be it anger, be it insult, be it passion, be it what it may, the soul is stayed securely; yea, though one have vented some chance word or other that ought not, and had been better not, to be spoken, yet he has laid himself under no necessity, no law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:186
verses.text: (Supra, Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:187
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:188
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:189
verses.text: ad.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:190
verses.text: Pop.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:191
verses.text: Ant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:192
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:193
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:194
verses.text: ) See what Herod did for his oath's sake: he cut off the head of the Fore-runner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:195
verses.text: "But because of his oaths," it says, "and because of them which sat at meat with him" (Mark vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:196
verses.text: ), he cut off the head of the Prophet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:197
verses.text: Think what the tribes had to suffer for their oath in the matter of the tribe of Benjamin (Judges xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:198
verses.text: –): what Saul had to suffer for his oath ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:199
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:200
verses.text: , etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:201
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:202
verses.text: For Saul indeed perjured himself, but Herod did what was even worse than perjury, he committed murder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:203
verses.text: Joshua again—you know how it fared with him, for his oath in the matter of the Gibeonites.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:204
verses.text: (Joshua, ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:205
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:206
verses.text: ) For it is indeed a snare of Satan, this swearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:207
verses.text: Let us burst the cords; let us bring ourselves into a condition in which it will be easy (not to swear); let us break loose from every entanglement, and from this snare of Satan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 36:208
verses.text: Let us fear the command of the Lord: let us settle ourselves in the best of habits: that, making progress, and having achieved this and the rest of the commandments, we may obtain those good things which are promised to them that love Him, through the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, power, and honor, now and ever, and world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:1
verses.text: Homily XIV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:2
verses.text: Acts V.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:3
verses.text: "Then stood there up one in the council, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people, and commanded the men to be put forth a little space".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:4
verses.text: This Gamaliel was Paul's teacher.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:5
verses.text: And one may well wonder, how, being so right-minded in his judgment, and withal learned in the law, he did not yet believe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:6
verses.text: But it cannot be that he should have continued in unbelief to the end.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:7
verses.text: Indeed it appears plainly from the words he here speaks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:8
verses.text: He "commanded," it says, "to put the men forth a little space and said unto them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:9
verses.text: Observe how judiciously he frames his speech, and how he immediately at the very outset puts them in fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:10
verses.text: And that he may not be suspected of taking their part, he addresses them as if he and they were of the same opinion, and does not use much vehemence, but as speaking to men intoxicated through passion, he thus expresses himself: "Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:12
verses.text: ) Do not, he would say, go to work rashly and in a hurry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:13
verses.text: "For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody: to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to naught".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:14
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:15
verses.text: ) By examples he teaches them prudence; and, by way of encouragement, mentions last the man who seduced the greatest number.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:16
verses.text: Now before he gives the examples, he says, "Take heed to yourselves;" but when he has cited them, then he declares his opinion, and says, "Refrain from these men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:17
verses.text: For, says he, "there rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:18
verses.text: And now I say unto you, Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this council or this work be of men, it will come to naught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:19
verses.text: But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:20
verses.text: (al.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:21
verses.text: it) (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:23
verses.text: ) Then what is there, he would say, to hinder you to be overthrown? For, says he (take heed), "lest haply ye be found even to fight against God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:24
verses.text: He would dissuade them both by the consideration that the thing is impossible, and because it is not for their good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:25
verses.text: And he does not say by whom these people were destroyed, but that there they "were scattered," and their confederacy fell away to nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:26
verses.text: For if, says he, it be of man, what needs any ado on your part? but if it be of God, for all your ado you will not be able to overcome it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:27
verses.text: The argument is unanswerable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:28
verses.text: "And they were persuaded by him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:30
verses.text: ) How were they persuaded? So as not to slay them, but merely to scourge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:31
verses.text: For, it says, "And when they had called the Apostles, and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:32
verses.text: See after what great works they are scourged! And again their teaching became more extended: for they taught at home and in the temple, "And they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:33
verses.text: And daily in the temple, and in every house, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:36
verses.text: ) And in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring of the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:37
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:38
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:39
verses.text: ) Not absolutely in those immediate days; for it is the custom of Scripture to speak of things next about to happen, as taking place in immediate succession.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:40
verses.text: But by "Hellenists" I suppose he means those who spoke Greek "against the Hebrews": for they did not use the Greek language.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:41
verses.text: Behold another trial! observe how from within and from without there are warrings, from the very first! "Then," it says, "the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them, and said, It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:42
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:43
verses.text: ) Well said: for the needful must give precedence to the more needful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:44
verses.text: But see, how straightway they both take thought for these (inferior matters), and yet do not neglect the preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:45
verses.text: "Because their widows were overlooked:" for those (the Hebrews) were treated as the persons of greater consequence (αἰδεσιμώτεροι).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:46
verses.text: "Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:47
verses.text: But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:48
verses.text: And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:49
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:50
verses.text: ) so were the others also full of faith; not to have the same things happening as in the case of Judas, as in the case of Ananias and Sapphira—"and Philip, and Prochoras, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch: whom they set before the Apostles: and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:51
verses.text: And the word of God increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:52
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:54
verses.text: )  But let us look over again what has been spoken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:55
verses.text: "Ye men of Israel take heed to yourselves".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:56
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:57
verses.text: ) See here, I pray you, how mildly Gamaliel reasons, and how he says but a few words to them, and does not recount ancient histories, although he might have done so, but more recent instances, which are most powerful to produce belief.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:58
verses.text: With this view he throws out a hint himself, saying, "For before these days" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:59
verses.text: ): meaning, not many days before.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:60
verses.text: Now had he at once said, "Let these men go," both himself would have fallen into suspicion, and his speech would not have been so effective: but after the examples, it acquired its own proper force.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:61
verses.text: And he mentions not one instance, but a second also: "for," saith the Scripture, "in the mouth of two witnesses" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:62
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:63
verses.text: ): and yet he had it in his power to mention even three.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:64
verses.text: "Refrain from these men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:65
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:66
verses.text: ) See how mild his manner is, and his speech not long, but concise, and his mention even of those (impostors) how free from passion: "And all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:67
verses.text: And for all this he does not blaspheme Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:68
verses.text: They heard him, all these unbelievers, heard him, these Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:69
verses.text: "For if this council or this work be of men, it will come to naught".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:70
verses.text: Well then, since it did not come to nought, it is not of men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:71
verses.text: "But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:72
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:73
verses.text: ) Once more he checks them by the impossibility and the inexpediency of the thing, saying, "Lest haply ye be found even to fight against God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:74
verses.text: And he does not say, If Christ be God; but the work (itself) declares (this).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:75
verses.text: He does not pronounce upon it, either that, it is "of men," or that it is "of God;" but he leaves the proof to the future.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:76
verses.text: "They were persuaded by him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:77
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:78
verses.text: ) Then why, it may be asked, do ye scourge them? Such was the incontrovertible justness of his speech, they could not look it in the face; nevertheless, they sated their own animosity; and again they expected to terrify them in this way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:79
verses.text: By the fact also of his saying these things not in the presence of the Apostles, he gained a hearing more than he would otherwise have done; and then the suavity of his discourse and the justness of what was said, helped to persuade them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:80
verses.text: In fact, this man all but preached the Gospel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:81
verses.text: "Ye were persuaded," one may say, "that ye had not strength to overthrow it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:82
verses.text: Wherefore did ye not believe?" Such is the witness borne even by enemies.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:83
verses.text: There it is four hundred, there, four thousand: and here the first movers were twelve.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:84
verses.text: Let not the number which added itself affright you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:85
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:86
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:87
verses.text: ; iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:88
verses.text: ) He might also have mentioned another instance, that of the Egyptian, but what he has spoken is fully sufficient.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:89
verses.text: And he closes his speech with an alarming topic: "Lest haply," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:90
verses.text: And he does not pronounce upon it, lest he should seem to be pleading their cause; but he reasons by way of syllogism from the issue of the matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:91
verses.text: And he does not venture to pronounce that it is not of men, nor yet that it is of God; for had he said that it was of God, they would have gainsaid him: but had he said that it was of men, they would again have taken prompt measures.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:92
verses.text: Therefore he bids them wait for the end, saying, "Refrain".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:93
verses.text: But they once more threaten knowing indeed that they avail nothing, but doing after their manner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:94
verses.text: Such is the nature of wickedness: it attempts even impossibilities.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:95
verses.text: —"And after this man rose up Judas," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:96
verses.text: These things Josephus relates in detail.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:97
verses.text: (Ant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:98
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:99
verses.text: ; ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:100
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:101
verses.text: ; xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:102
verses.text: B.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:103
verses.text: J.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:104
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:105
verses.text: ) But what a great thing it was that he ventured to affirm: that it was of God, when in the sequel it received its proof from the events! Great boldness of speech, great freedom from all respect of persons! And he does not say, "But if ye do not overthrow it, it is of God;" but, "If it be of God, it will not be overthrown".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:106
verses.text: "And to him they agreed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:107
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:108
verses.text: ) They reverenced the high character of the man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:109
verses.text: "And they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for the name of Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:110
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:111
verses.text: ) What miracles so wonderful as this? Nowhere is the like of this recorded of the old saints: for Jeremiah indeed was scourged for the word of God, and they threatened Elijah, and the rest: but in this case, even by this very thing, and not only by their miracles, these showed forth the power of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:112
verses.text: He does not say, that they were not pained, but that though pained they rejoiced.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:113
verses.text: How does this appear? From their boldness afterwards: they were so instant still, even after their beatings, in preaching the word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:114
verses.text: "But in the temple," it says, "and in every house, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:116
verses.text: ) "And in those days"—when these things were done, when there were scourgings, when there were threatenings, when the disciples were multiplying—also, it says, "there arose a murmuring".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:117
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:118
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:119
verses.text: ) And this comes of the multitude: for it is impossible to have strict order in a multitude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:120
verses.text: "There arose a murmuring," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:121
verses.text: to,—"And a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:122
verses.text: —There arose murmuring against the Hebrews"—for that description of people seemed to be more honorable—"because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:123
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:124
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:125
verses.text: ) So then there was a daily ministration for the widows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:126
verses.text: And observe how he calls it a "ministration" (διακονία), and not directly alms: extolling by this at once the doers, and those to whom it was done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:127
verses.text: "Were neglected".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:128
verses.text: This did not arise from malice, but perhaps from the carelessness of the multitude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:129
verses.text: And therefore he brought it forward openly, for this was no small evil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:130
verses.text: Observe, how even in the beginning the evils came not only from without, but also from within.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:131
verses.text: For you must not look to this only, that it was set to rights, but observe that it was a great evil that it existed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:132
verses.text: "Then the twelve," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:133
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:134
verses.text: ) Do you observe how outward concerns succeed to inward? They do not act at their own discretion, but plead for themselves to the congregation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:135
verses.text: So ought it to be done now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:136
verses.text: "It is not reason," says he, "that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:137
verses.text: First he puts to them the unreasonableness of the thing; that it is not possible for both things to be done with the same attention: just as when they were about to ordain Matthias, they first show the necessity of the thing, that one was deficient, and there must needs be twelve.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:138
verses.text: And so here they showed the necessity; and they did it not sooner, but waited till the murmuring arose; nor, on the other hand, did they suffer this to spread far.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:139
verses.text: And, lo! they leave the decision to them: those who pleased all, those who of all were honestly reputed, them they present: not now twelve, but "seven, full of the Spirit and of wisdom: well reported of" for their conversation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:140
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:141
verses.text: ) Now when Matthias was to be presented, it was said, "Therefore must one of these men which have companied with us all the time" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:142
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:143
verses.text: ): but not so here: for the case was not alike.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:144
verses.text: And they do not now put it to the lot; they might indeed themselves have made the election, as moved by the Spirit: but nevertheless, they desire the testimony of the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:145
verses.text: The fixing the number, and the ordaining them, and for this kind of business, rested with them: but the choice of the men they make over to the people, that they might not seem to act from favor: just as God also leaves it to Moses to choose as elders those whom he knew.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:146
verses.text: (Num.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:147
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:148
verses.text: ) "And of wisdom".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:149
verses.text: For indeed there needs much wisdom in such ministrations.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:150
verses.text: For think not, because he hath not the word committed unto him, that such an one has no need of wisdom: he does need it, and much too.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:151
verses.text: "But we," saith he, "will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:152
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:153
verses.text: ) Again they plead for themselves, beginning and ending with this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:154
verses.text: "Will give ourselves continually," he saith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:155
verses.text: For so it behooved, not just to do the mere acts, or in any chance way, but to be continually doing them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:156
verses.text: "And the saying," we are told, "pleased the whole multitude".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:157
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:158
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:159
verses.text: ) This too was worthy of their wisdom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:160
verses.text: All approved of what was said so sensible was it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:161
verses.text: "And they chose," it says (again it is the people (αὐτοί) that choose,) "Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch: whom they set before the Apostles: and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:162
verses.text: They separated them from the multitude, and it is the people (αὐτοί) that draw them, not the Apostles that lead them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:163
verses.text: Observe how he avoids all that is superfluous: he does not tell in what way it was done, but that they were ordained (ἐχειροτονήθησαν) with prayer: for this is the meaning of χειροτονία, (i-e: "putting forth the hand,") or ordination: the hand of the man is laid upon (the person,) but the whole work is of God, and it is His hand which toucheth the head of the one ordained, if he be duly ordained.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:164
verses.text: "And the word of God," it says, "increased: and the number of the disciples multiplied".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:165
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:166
verses.text: ) It is not for nothing that he says this: it shows how great is the virtue of alms and good order.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:167
verses.text: And as he is about in the sequel to enlarge (αὔξειν) upon the affair of Stephen, he puts first the causes which led to it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:168
verses.text: "And many," he says, "of the priests were obedient to the faith".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:169
verses.text: For since they perceived such to be the mind of their ruler and teacher, they put the matter to the test of facts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:170
verses.text: —It is also a subject for wonder, how it was that the multitude was not divided in its choice of the men, and how it was that the Apostles were not rejected by them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:171
verses.text: But what sort of rank these bore, and what sort of office they received, this is what we need to learn.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:172
verses.text: Was it that of Deacons? And yet this is not the case in the Churches.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:173
verses.text: But is it to the Presbyters that the management belongs? And yet at present there was no Bishop, but the Apostles only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:174
verses.text: Whence I think it clearly and manifestily follows, that neither Deacons nor Presbyters is their designation: but it was for this particular purpose that they were ordained.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:175
verses.text: And this business was not simply handed over to them without further ceremony, but the Apostles prayed over them, that power might be given to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:176
verses.text: But observe, I pray you, if there were need of seven men for this, great in proportion must have been the sums of money that flowed in, great in proportion also the number of widows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:177
verses.text: So then the prayers were not made in an off-hand way, but with much deliberate attention: and this office, as well as preaching, was thus brought to good effect; for what they did, they effected mostly by the means of these (their prayers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:178
verses.text: ) Thus they were enabled to give their attention to things spiritual; thus were these also free to undertake long journeys; thus were these put in trust with the word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:179
verses.text: But the writer does not say this, nor extol them, but that it was "not reason" that they should leave the work given to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:180
verses.text: Thus they had been taught by Moses's example not to undertake the management of everything by themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:181
verses.text: (Num.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:182
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:183
verses.text: ) "Only," it is said, "that we should remember the poor".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:184
verses.text: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:185
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:186
verses.text: ) And how did they bring these forward? They fasted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:187
verses.text: "Look you out seven men," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:188
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:189
verses.text: ) It is not simply, spiritual men, but, "full of the Spirit and of wisdom," for it needed very great superiority of mind (φιλοσοφίας) to bear the complainings of widows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:190
verses.text: For what profits it, that the dispenser of alms steal not, if nevertheless he waste all, or be harsh and easily provoked? "And they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:191
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:192
verses.text: ) And in this regard Philip also was admirable: for it is of him that the writer says: "And we entered into the house of Philip the Evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:193
verses.text: —(ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:194
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:195
verses.text: ) Dost thou mark how matters are ordered quite otherwise than after the matter of men? "And the number of disciples was multiplied in Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:196
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:197
verses.text: ) In Jerusalem the multitude increased.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:198
verses.text: Wonderful, where Christ was slain, there the preaching increased! And not only was it not the case that some were offended then in the manner of Ananias, but the awe became even greater: while these are scourged, those threatening, those tempting the Spirit, those murmuring.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:199
verses.text: But I would have thee remark under what circumstances the multitude increased: after these trials, then it was that the multitude increased, and not before.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:200
verses.text: Mark also how great the mercy of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:201
verses.text: Of those chief-priests, of the very men who had indignation and sore displeasure and so cried out and said, "He saved others, Himself He cannot save;" of these same, "Many," it says, "were obedient unto the faith".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:202
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:203
verses.text: xxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:204
verses.text: )  Him therefore let us also imitate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:205
verses.text: He received them, and did not cast them out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:206
verses.text: So let us requite those our enemies, who have wrought us even numberless ills.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:207
verses.text: Whatever good thing we may have, let us impart to them: let us not pass them by, in our acts of beneficence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:208
verses.text: For if we ought, by suffering ill, to sate their rage, much more, by doing them good: for this is a less thing than the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:209
verses.text: For it is not all alike, to do good to an enemy, and to be willing to suffer greater wrongs than he wishes (to inflict): from the one we shall come on to the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:210
verses.text: This is the dignity of Christ's disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:211
verses.text: Those crucified Him, when He had come for the very purpose of doing them good; His disciples they scourged; and after all this, He admits them to the same honor with His disciples, making them equally partakers of His gifts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:212
verses.text: I beseech you, let us be imitators of Christ: in this regard it is possible to imitate Him: this makes a man like unto God: this is more than human.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:213
verses.text: Let us hold fast to Mercy: she is the schoolmistress and teacher of that higher Wisdom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:214
verses.text: He that has learnt to show mercy to the distressed, will learn also not to resent injuries; he that has learnt this, will be able to do good even to his enemies.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:215
verses.text: Let us learn to feel for the ills our neighbors suffer, and we shall learn to endure the ills they inflict.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:216
verses.text: Let us ask the person himself who ill-treats us, whether he does not condemn himself? would he not be glad to show a nobler spirit (φιλοσοφεἵν)? must he not own that his behavior is nothing but passion, that it is little-minded, pitiful? would he not like to be of those who are wronged and are silent, and not of those who do wrong, and are beside themselves with passion? can he go away not admiring the patient sufferer? Do not imagine that this makes men despicable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:217
verses.text: Nothing makes men so despicable, as insolent and injurious behavior: nothing makes men so respectable, as endurance under insolence and injury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:218
verses.text: For the one is a ruffian, the other a philosopher; the one is less than man, the other is equal to angels.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:219
verses.text: For though he be inferior to the wrong-doer, yet, for all that, he has the power, if he had the mind, to be revenged.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:220
verses.text: And besides, the one is pitied by all, the other hated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:221
verses.text: What then? The former will be much the better of the two: for everybody will treat the one as a madman, the other as a man of sense.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:222
verses.text: He cannot speak of him in evil sort: yea, thou fearest, says one, lest perchance he be not such (as thou wouldest represent).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:223
verses.text: Best that thou speak not evil in thy thought even; next, that thou speak it not to another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:224
verses.text: Pray not then to God against this man: if thou hear him evil-spoken of, take his part: say, It was passion that spoke such words, not the man; say, It was anger, not my friend: his madness, not his heart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:225
verses.text: Thus let us account of each offence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:226
verses.text: Wait not for the fire to be kindled, but check it before it comes to that: do not exasperate the savage beast, rather do not suffer it to become exasperated: for thou wilt no longer be able to check it, if once the flame be kindled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:227
verses.text: For what has the man called thee? "Thou fool and simpleton".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:228
verses.text: And which then is liable to the name? the called, or the caller? For the one, be he ever so wise, gets the character of being a fool: but the other, even if he be a simpleton, gets credit for being wise, and of philosophic temper.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:229
verses.text: Say, which is the simpleton? he who alleges against another what is untrue, or he who even under such treatment is unmoved? For if it be the mark of true philosophy to be unmoved however moved; to fall into a passion when none moves to anger—what folly is it! I say not yet, how sore a manner of punishment is in store for those who utter such reproaches and revilings against their neighbor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:230
verses.text: But how? has he called thee "a low fellow and low-born, a sorry creature and of sorry extraction?" Again he has turned the taunt against himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:231
verses.text: For the other will appear worthy and respectable, but he a sorry creature indeed: for to cast up such things, that is to say, meanness of birth, as a disgrace, is little-minded indeed: while the other will be thought a great and admirable character, because he thinks nothing of such a taunt, and is no more affected by it than if he were told that he had about him any other ordinary and quite indifferent circumstance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 37:232
verses.text: But does he call thee "adulterer," and such like? At this thou mayest even laugh: for, when the conscience is not smitten, there can be no occasion for wrath.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:1
verses.text: For when one has considered what bad and disgraceful disclosures he makes, still for all that, there is no need to grieve.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:2
verses.text: He has but laid bare now, what everybody must be apprised of by and bye: meanwhile, as regards himself he has shown all men that he is not to be trusted, for that he knows not how to screen his neighbor's faults: he has disgraced himself more than he has the other; has stopped up against himself every harbor: has made terrible to himself the bar at which he must hereafter be tried.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:3
verses.text: For not the person (whose secrets are betrayed) will be the object of everybody's aversion, but he, who where he ought not to have raised the veil, has stripped off the clothes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:4
verses.text: But speak thou nothing of the secrets thou knowest: hold thou thy peace if thou wouldest bear off the good fame.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:5
verses.text: For not only wilt thou overthrow what has been spoken, and hide it: but thou wilt also bring about another capital result: thou wilt stop sentence being given against thyself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:6
verses.text: Does somebody speak evil of thee? Say thou: "Had he known all, he would not have spoken only thus much".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:7
verses.text: —So you admire what has been said, and are delighted with it? Aye, but you must follow it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:8
verses.text: For when we tell you all these maxims of the heathen moralists, it is not because Scripture does not contain hundreds of such sayings, but because these are of more force to put you to the blush.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:9
verses.text: As in fact Scripture itself is wont to use this appeal to our sense of shame; for, instance, when it says, "Do ye even as the heathen".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:10
