verses.text: (Jer.

verses.text: ) But not so we: on the contrary, this is what we most desire; to have all men know that they have not passed unpunished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:18
verses.text: How long shall we breathe of the earth?—One party cannot make a fight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:19
verses.text: Pluck the madmen from both sides, you will exasperate them the more: but pluck from right or from left, and you have quenched the passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:20
verses.text: The striker, if he has to do with one who will not put up with blows, is the more set on: but if with one who yields, he is the sooner unnerved, and his blow is spent upon himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:21
verses.text: For no practised pugilist so unnerves the strength of his antagonist, as does a man who being injuriously treated makes no return.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:22
verses.text: For the other only goes off ashamed, and condemned, first by his own conscience, and secondly by all the lookers on.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:23
verses.text: And there is a proverb too, which says, that "to honor another, is to honor one's self": therefore also to abuse another is to abuse one's self.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:24
verses.text: None, I repeat, will be able to harm us, unless we harm ourselves; nor will any make me poor, unless I make myself such.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:25
verses.text: For come, let us look at it in this way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:26
verses.text: Suppose that I have a beggarly soul, and let all lavish all their substance upon me, what of that? So long as the soul is not changed, it is all in vain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:27
verses.text: Suppose I have a noble soul, and let all men take from me my substance: what of that? So long as you do not make the soul beggarly, no harm is done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:28
verses.text: Suppose my life be impure, and let all men say just the contrary of me: what of that? For though they say it, yet they do not judge thus of me in their heart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:29
verses.text: Again, suppose my life be pure, and let all say of me just the reverse: and what of that? For in their own conscience they will condemn themselves: since they are not persuaded of what they say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:30
verses.text: Just as we ought not to admit the praise, so neither the criminations.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:31
verses.text: And why say I these things? None will ever be able to plot against us, nor lay us under any evil charge, if we choose (that they shall not).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:32
verses.text: For how now, I ask you? Let him drag me into a court of justice, let him lay vexatious informations, let him, if you will, have the very soul out of me: and what of that? for a little while, undeservedly to suffer these things, what does it signify? "Well, but this," say you, "is of itself an evil".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:33
verses.text: Well, but of itself this is a good, to suffer undeservedly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:34
verses.text: What? would you have the suffering to be deserved? Let me mention again a piece of philosophy, from one of the sages.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:35
verses.text: A certain person, says the story, had been put to death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:36
verses.text: And one of the sage's disciples said to him, "Woe is me, that he should have suffered unjustly!" The other turned upon him, "Why, how now?" said he, "would you have had him justly suffer?" (Socrates ap.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:42
verses.text: ) John also, was not he unjustly put to death? Which then do you rather pity: them that justly suffer death, or him? Do you not count them miserable, while him you even admire? Then what is a man injured, when from death itself he has got great gain, not merely no hurt? If indeed the man had been immortal, and this made him mortal, no doubt it would be a hurt: but if he be mortal, and in the course of nature must expect death a little later, and his enemy has but expedited his death, and glory with it, what is the harm? Let us but have our soul in good order, and there will be no harm from without.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:43
verses.text: But thou art not in a condition of glory? And what of that? That which is true of wealth, the same holds for glory: if I be magnanimous (μεγαλοπρεπής), I shall need none; if vainglorious, the more I get, the more I shall want.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:44
verses.text: In this way shall I most become illustrious, and obtain greater glory; namely, if I despise glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 39:45
verses.text: Knowing these things, let us be thankful to Him Who hath freely given us such a life, and let us ensue it unto His glory; for to Him belongs the glory, forever, Amen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:68

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:71

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:105
verses.text: , ) in such and such wise (τοιὣσδε).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:106
verses.text: But here, it seems to me, it says that he was also gracious to look at: "They saw his face as it had been the face of an angel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:107
verses.text: "Full of faith and of power": (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:108
verses.text: ) which is also the character given of Barnabas "he was a good man, full of faith and of the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:109
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:110
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:111
verses.text: ) Whence we learn that the sincere and innocent are, above all others, the men to be saved, and that these same are also more gracious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:112
verses.text: "Then they suborned men, which said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:113
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:114
verses.text: ) In the case of the Apostles they were annoyed that they preached the Resurrection, and that much people flowed unto them: but in this case, that they were getting their diseases healed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:115
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:116
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:117
verses.text: ) The things for which they ought to give thanks, they made matter of blame: O the madness! The men who overcame them by works, they expected to overcome by words! It is just what they did in the case of Christ, and always they forced them to words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:118
verses.text: For they were ashamed to seize them without more ado, having nothing to charge them with.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:119
verses.text: And observe, not the persons themselves who bring them to judgment bear witness against them; for they would have been refuted: but they simply hire others, that it may not seem to be an act of mere violence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:120
verses.text: It is all of a piece with their proceeding in the case of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:121
verses.text: And observe the power of the preaching, that, though they are not only scourged but stoned, it still prevails: not only, private individuals as they are, dragged to the bar, but assailed from all quarters: and, their enemies themselves being witnesses, not only were these worsted, but "they were not able" even "to resist" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:122
verses.text: ), though they were exceeding shameless: so mightily did it overthrow them, for all that they could do with their preposterous figments (as the saying that He had a devil—He that cast out devils!).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:123
verses.text: For the battle was not man's, but God's against men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:124
verses.text: And there were many combined together; not only they in Jerusalem, but others as well.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:125
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:126
verses.text: ) For "we have heard him," say they, "speaking blasphemous words against Moses and against God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:127
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:128
verses.text: ) O ye shameless ones! Ye work blasphemous deeds, and think nothing of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:129
verses.text: This is why Moses is added—because the things of God were no great concern to them: and it is ever and always Moses that they make mention of: "This Moses, which brought us out".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:130
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:131
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:132
verses.text: ) "And they stirred up the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:133
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:134
verses.text: ) Fickleness of the multitude! And yet how could a man who was a blasphemer have so succeeded? How could a blasphemer work such miracles among the people? But the undisciplined multitude made them strong who had the worst of it (in argument).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:135
verses.text: —This was what most annoyed them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:136
verses.text: "We have heard him," they say, "speaking blasphemous words against Moses and against God" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:137
verses.text: ): and again, "This man ceaseth not to speak blasphemous words against this holy place and the law," and with an addition, "the customs" "which Moses delivered to us" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:138
verses.text: ); Moses, not God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:139
verses.text: Upon the supposition of a design to overturn their manner of life (πολιτείας), they accused him of impiety also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:140
verses.text: But to show that it was not in the nature of such a man to speak such things, and harshly "Then all," it says, "which were in the council, looking steadfastly upon him, saw his face, as it had been the face of an angel" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:141
verses.text: ): so mild was he even in countenance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:142
verses.text: For, in cases where persons were not falsely accused, Scripture mentions nothing of this kind: but as in this case it was all false accusation, with reason does God rectify it by the very look of the man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:143
verses.text: For the Apostles indeed were not falsely accused, but were forbidden: but this man is falsely accused: and therefore before all else his countenance pleads for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:144
verses.text: This abashed even the priest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:145
verses.text: "And he said," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:146
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:147
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:148
verses.text: ) He shows here, that the promise was made before the Place, before Circumcision, before Sacrifice, before the Temple, and that it was not of their merit that these received either Circumcision or Law, but that the land was the reward of obedience alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:149
verses.text: Moreover, that neither on the giving of circumcision does the promise receive its fulfillment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:150
verses.text: Also, that these were figures, and (so was) both the leaving his country at God's command—not against the law (for home and country is where God shall lead): "Then came he out," it says, "of the land of the Chaldeans" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:151
verses.text: ):—and that if one look closely into the matter, the Jews are of Persian origin: and that, without miracles, one must do as God bids, whatever hardships be the consequence; since the Patriarch left both the grave of his father and all that he had, in obedience to God's command.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:152
verses.text: But if Abraham's father was not allowed to take part with him in the privilege of migrating to Palestine, because he was unworthy: much more shall the children (be excluded at last), for all that they may have gone a good distance on the way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:153
verses.text: "And He promised," it says, "to give it to him, and to his seed after him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:154
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:155
verses.text: ) Herein is shown the greatness both of God's goodness and of Abraham's faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:156
verses.text: For the expression, "when as yet he had no child," does show his obedience and faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:157
verses.text: "Promised to give it to him and to his seed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:158
verses.text: And yet the events showed the contrary: namely, after he came, he had not "so much as to set his foot on," had not a child; which very things were contrary to his faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:159
verses.text: These things having seen, let us likewise, whatever God shall promise, receive the same, however contrary may be the events.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:160
verses.text: And yet in our case, they are not contrary, but very suitable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:161
verses.text: For where the promises are, there, when the contraries turn out, they are really contrary; but in our case it is just the reverse: for He has told us that we should have tribulation here, but our rest there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:162
verses.text: Why do we confound the times? Why do we turn things upside down? Say, art thou afflicted, and livest in poverty, and in dejection? Be not troubled: for it were worth being troubled at, wert thou destined to be afflicted in that world: as for this present affliction, it is the cause of rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:163
verses.text: "This sickness," saith He, "is not unto death".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:164
verses.text: (John xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:165
verses.text: ) That affliction is punishment: this, schooling and correction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:166
verses.text: It is a contest, this life present: if so, to fight is our business now: it is war and battle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:167
verses.text: In war one does not seek to have rest, in war one does not seek to have dainty living, one is not anxious about riches, one's care is not about a wife then: one thing only he looks at, how he may overcome his foes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:168
verses.text: Be this our care likewise: if we overcome, and return with the victory, God will give us all things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:169
verses.text: Be this alone our study, how we may overcome the devil: though after all it is not our own study that does it, but God's grace does the whole business.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:170
verses.text: Be it our one study, how we may attract His grace, how we may draw to ourselves that assistance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:171
verses.text: "If God be for us, who can be against us?" (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:172
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:173
verses.text: ) Let us make one thing our study; that He be not our enemy, that He turn not away from us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:174
verses.text: Not the being afflicted is an evil; the evil is, to sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:175
verses.text: This is the sore affliction, however we may pass our days in luxury:—not to speak of the life to come, it is so even in this life present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:176
verses.text: Think how our conscience is stung with remorse, and whether this is not worse than any kind of torture! I should like to put the question searchingly to those who live in evil ways (ἐν κακοἵς), whether they never come to reflect upon their own sins, whether they do not tremble, and are in fear and anguish, whether they do not think those blessed who live in abstinence, them of the mountains, them of the strict rule? (τοὺς ἐν πολλῇ φιλοσοφί& ·.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:177
verses.text: ) Dost thou wish to find rest in the life to come? Suffer affliction in this life for Christ's sake: there is nothing equal to this rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:178
verses.text: The Apostles rejoiced when scourged.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:179
verses.text: Paul gives this exhortation, saying, "Rejoice in the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:180
verses.text: (Philip.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:181
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:182
verses.text: ) And how can there be rejoicing, where there are bonds, where there are tortures; where there are courts of justice? There, most of all, is rejoicing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:183
verses.text: But say, how can there be rejoicing, where these are not? For he who is conscious of no evil, will have a sort of exceeding delight, insomuch that in what degree you speak of tribulation, in the same you tell of his delight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:184
verses.text: The soldier who has received numberless wounds and is come home again, will he not return with exceeding delight, with his wounds as his title for speaking up boldly, and as evidence of his glory and renown? And thou, if thou be able to exclaim as Paul does, "I bear the marks of Jesus" (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:185
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:186
verses.text: ), wilt be able to become great and glorious and renowned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:187
verses.text: "But there is no persecution".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:188
verses.text: Make thy stand against glory: and should any one speak anything against thee, fear not to be evil-spoken of for Christ's sake: make thy stand against the tyranny of pride, against the fighting of anger, against the torment of concupiscence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:189
verses.text: These also are "marks," these also are torments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:190
verses.text: For, I ask, what is the worst in tortures? Is it not, that the soul is pained, and is on fire? For in the other case, the body too has its share: but in this, the whole belongs to the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:191
verses.text: On the soul alone comes all the smart, when one is angry, when one is envious, whatever else of this kind one does, or rather suffers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:192
verses.text: For, in fact, it is not action, but passion, not a doing, but a suffering—to be angered, to feel envy: therefore indeed they are called passions (or sufferings) (πάθη, perturbationes) of the soul, yea wounds, and bruises.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:193
verses.text: For it is indeed a suffering, and worse than suffering.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:194
verses.text: Bethink you, ye that are angry, that ye do such things in "passion," in a state of suffering.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:195
verses.text: Therefore he who is not angry suffers not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:196
verses.text: Do you mark that not he who is abused is the sufferer, but he that abuses, as I said above? For that he is a sufferer, is plain in the first place from the very fact, that such a thing is called by this name of passion: and it is also plain from the (effects on the) body: for these are the affections (πάθη) for "sufferings," as we call them engendered by anger, viz.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:197
verses.text: dimness of vision, insanity, and numberless others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:198
verses.text: "But he insulted my boy," say you; "but he called him clown".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:199
verses.text: Deem it not weakness thy not doing the same thing thyself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:200
verses.text: For, I ask you, was it well done? You will not say that: then leave that undone which being done were not well done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:201
verses.text: I know what passions are engendered in such cases.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:202
verses.text: "But," say you, "how if he despise me, how if he say it again?" Show him that he is in the wrong: rebuke him, entreat him: by meekness anger is put down: go and expostulate with him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:203
verses.text: For though in cases of wrong done to ourselves it is right not to do even this, yet it is quite necessary to do it in behalf of others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:204
verses.text: Do not look on it as an insult to yourself that your boy has been insulted: annoyed you may be for his sake, yet not as if you were insulted: for it does not follow because your boy has been ill-treated, that you are disgraced, but he is disgraced that did the ill.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:205
verses.text: Quench (thine anger) that sharp sword: let it lie in its scabbard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:206
verses.text: If we have it unsheathed, we shall be apt to use it even when the time is not proper, being drawn on by it: but if it be hidden, though a necessity should arise, yet, while we seek it in order to draw it, the anger will be quenched.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:207
verses.text: Christ would not have us be angry on his account: (hear what He saith to Peter: "Put up again thy sword into the sheath:") (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:208
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:209
verses.text: ) and art thou angry on account of a boy? Teach thy boy also to be philosophical: tell him thy own sufferings: imitate (herein) thy Teacher.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:210
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:211
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:212
verses.text: ) When they too (His disciples) were about to be treated with dishonor, He said not, "I will avenge you:" but, "to Me also," saith He, "they have done the same: bear it nobly, for ye are not better than I".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:213
verses.text: These words too do thou speak to thy son and thy boy: "Thou art not better than thy master".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:214
verses.text: But these words of philosophy are counted as the talk of a widow woman.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:215
verses.text: Alas! that it is not in the power of words to bring it home to people in the way that it is possible to be taught it by actual experience! And that you may learn this; stand between two combatants, take part with the wronged, not with the wrong-doers that you may learn whether you shall not see the victory on your side, whether you shall not get splendid crowns.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:216
verses.text: —See, how God is insulted, and how He answers; how gently, "Where," saith He, "is Abel thy brother?" and what saith the other: "Am I my brother's keeper?" (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:217
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:218
verses.text: ) What could be more contumacious than this? Would any one have heard it (patiently) even from a son? and if from a brother, would he not have thought such conduct an insult? What then? See how again God gently answers, "The voice of thy brother's blood," saith He "crieth unto Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:219
verses.text: "But God," it will be said, "is superior to wrath".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:220
verses.text: Yes, but for this reason the Son of God came down, that He might make thee a God as far as human power can go.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:221
verses.text: "But I cannot," says one, "seeing I am man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:222
verses.text: Well then, let us give you men for instances.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:223
verses.text: And do not suppose I speak of Paul or of Peter: no, but of some of inferior sort, yea, very much lower down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:224
verses.text: Eli's menial insulted Hannah, saying, "Put away thy wine from thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:225
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:226
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:227
verses.text: ) What could be more insulting than this? What then said she? "I am a woman of a hard lot".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:228
verses.text: Indeed, there is nothing equal to affliction: she is the mother of true philosophy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:229
verses.text: But this same woman, though she has her rival, insulted her not: but what does she? She takes refuge with God, and in her prayer does not even make mention of her, nor say, "Avenge me, for such an one reproaches me:" so magnanimous was that woman (let us men be ashamed):—and yet ye know, that there is nothing like jealousy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:230
verses.text: The publican, when insulted by the Pharisee, insulted not in return, though, had he wished it, he might have done so: but he bore it like a philosopher, saying, "Be merciful to me a sinner".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:231
verses.text: (Luke xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:232
verses.text: ) Mephibosheth, having been accused and calumniated by his servant, neither said, nor did, any evil to him, not even in the presence of the king himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:233
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:234
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:235
verses.text: ) Shall I tell you even of a harlot, what philosophic magnanimity she showed? Hear Christ saying, as she was wiping His feet with her hair, "The publicans and harlots go into the kingdom before you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:236
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:237
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:238
verses.text: ) Do you see her standing, and taking courage, and washing away her own sins? Observe, how she was not angry even with the Pharisee, when reproached by him: "for had He known," says he, "that this woman is a sinner, He would not have suffered her (Luke vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:239
verses.text: ): and how she said not to him, "What then? Say, art thou pure from sins?" but felt more, wept more, and let fall hotter tears.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:240
verses.text: But if women and publicans and harlots play the philosopher, and that before grace (i-e: of Baptism), what pardon can they deserve, who, after so great grace, fight, and worry, and kick one another, worse than beasts? Nothing is more base than passion, nothing more disgraceful, nothing more frightful, nothing more odious, nothing more hurtful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:241
verses.text: These things I say, not only in order that towards men we may be gentle, but also if a wife be a talker, that thou mayest bear it: let thy wife be to thee a school for training and exercise (παλαίστρα καὶ γυμνάσιον).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:242
verses.text: For how can it but be absurd, to submit to exercises which yield no profit, where we afflict the body, but not to practise exercises at home, which, even before the contest, present to us a crown? Does thy wife abuse thee? Do not thou become a woman: to be abusive is womanly: it is a disease of the soul, an inferiority.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:243
verses.text: Think not that it is unworthy of thee, when thy wife abuses thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:244
verses.text: Unworthy it is, when thou art abusive, but she bears patiently (φιλοσοφῇ): then dost thou act unseemly, then art thou disgraced: but if, having been abused, thou bear it, great is the proof of thy strength.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:245
verses.text: I do not say this, to induce wives to be abusive: God forbid: but only in case it should so happen at the instance of Satan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:246
verses.text: It is the part of men that are strong, to bear the weak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:247
verses.text: And if thy servant contradict thee, bear it philosophically: not what he deserves to have said to him, do thou say or do, but that which it behooves thee both to do and to say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:248
verses.text: Never insult a girl by uttering some foul word against her: never call thy servant, scoundrel (μιαρὸν): not he is disgraced, but thou.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:249
verses.text: It is not possible to be master of one's self, being in a passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:250
verses.text: Like a sea rolling mountains high, it is all hurly-burly: or even as a pure fountain, when mire is cast into it, becomes muddied, and all is in turmoil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:251
verses.text: You may beat him, you may rend his coat to rags, but it is you that sustain the greater damage: for to him the blow is on the body and the garment, but to you on the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:252
verses.text: It is your own soul that you have cut open; it is there that you have inflicted a wound: you have flung your own charioteer from his horses, you have got him dragging along the ground upon his back.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:253
verses.text: And it is all one, as if one driver being in a passion with another, should choose to be thus dragged along.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:254
verses.text: You may rebuke, you may chide, you may do whatever if be, only let it be without wrath and passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:255
verses.text: For if he who rebukes is physician to him who offends, how can he heal another, when he has first hurt himself, when he does not heal himself? Say, if a physician should go to heal another person, does he first wound his own hand, first blind his own eyes, and so set about healing that other? God forbid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:256
verses.text: So also, however thou rebuke, however thou chide, let thine eyes see clearly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:257
verses.text: Do not make thy mind muddy, else how shall the cure be wrought? It is not possible to be in the same tranquillity, being in a passion, and being free from passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:258
verses.text: Why dost thou first overturn thy master from his seat, and then discourse with him as he lies sprawling on the ground? Seest thou not the judges, how, when about to hold the assize, they seat themselves upon the bench, in their becoming attire? Thus do thou likewise dress thy soul with the judicial robe (which is gentleness).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:259
verses.text: "But he will not be afraid of me," say you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:260
verses.text: He will be the more afraid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 40:261
verses.text: In the other case, though you speak justly, your servant will impute it to passion: but if you do it with gentleness, he will condemn himself: and, what is of the first importance, God will accept thee, and thus thou wilt be able to attain unto the eternal blessings, through the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father together with the Holy Spirit be glory, dominion, and honor, now and ever, and world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:1
verses.text: Homily XVI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:2
verses.text: Acts VII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:3
verses.text: ,  "And God spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:4
verses.text: And the nation to whom they shall be in bondage will I judge, said God: and after that shall they come forth, and serve Me in this place".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:5
verses.text: See, what a number of years the Promise has been given, and the manner of the Promise, and nowhere sacrifice, nowhere circumcision! He here shows, how God Himself suffered them to be afflicted, not that He had anything to lay to their charge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:6
verses.text: "And they shall bring them into bondage," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:7
verses.text: But nevertheless, they did not these things with impunity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:8
verses.text: "And the nation to whom they shall be in bondage I will judge, said God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:9
verses.text: For, to show that they are not to go by this, in estimating who are pious (by reason of their saying, "He trusted in God, let Him deliver Him,") (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:10
verses.text: xxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:12
verses.text: —He, the Same that promised, He that gave the land, first permits the evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:13
verses.text: So also now, though He has promised a Kingdom, yet He suffers us to be exercised in temptations.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:14
verses.text: If here the freedom was not to be till after four hundred years, what wonder, with regard to the Kingdom? Yet he performed it, and lapse of time availed not to falsify His word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:15
verses.text: Moreover, it was no ordinary bondage they underwent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:16
verses.text: And the matter does not terminate solely in the punishment of those (their oppressors); but they themselves also, He saith, shall enjoy a mighty salvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:17
verses.text: Here he reminds them too of the benefit which they enjoyed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:18
verses.text: "And he gave him the covenant of circumcision: and so he begat Isaac".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:19
verses.text: Here he lets himself down to lower matters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:20
verses.text: "And circumcised him on the eighth day: and Isaac (begat) Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:23
verses.text: —Here he seems to hint now at the type.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:24
verses.text: "And the patriarchs moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:26
verses.text: ) Here again, the type of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:27
verses.text: Though they had no fault to find with him, and though he came on purpose to bring them their food, they thus ill-treated him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:28
verses.text: Still here again the promise, though it is a long while first, receives its fulfillment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:29
verses.text: "And God was with him"—this also is for them—"and delivered him out of all his afflictions".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:30
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:32
verses.text: He shows that unknowingly they helped to fulfil the prophecy, and that they were themselves the cause, and that the evils recoiled on their own selves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:33
verses.text: "And gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt, Gave him favor," in the eyes of a barbarian, to him, the slave, the captive: his brethren sold him, this (barbarian) honored him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:34
verses.text: "Now there came a dearth over all the land of Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction: and our fathers found no sustenance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:35
verses.text: But when Jacob heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:36
verses.text: And at the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:39
verses.text: They came down to buy, and had to depend upon him for everything.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:40
verses.text: What then did he? "He made himself known to his brethren:" not to this point only did he carry his friendliness; he also made them known to Pharaoh, and brought them down into the land.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:41
verses.text: "And Joseph's kindred was made known unto Pharaoh.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:42
verses.text: Then sent Joseph, and called his father Jacob to him, and all his kindred, threescore and fifteen souls.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:43
verses.text: So Jacob went down into Egypt, and died, he, and our fathers, and were carried over into Sychem, and laid in the sepulchre that Abraham bought for a sum of money of the sons of Emmor the father of Sychem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:44
verses.text: But when the time of the promise drew nigh, which God had sworn to Abraham the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, till another king arose, which knew not Joseph".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:47
verses.text: Then again, fresh disappointment (ἀνελπιστία): first, famine, but they came through that: secondly, the falling into the hands of their enemy: thirdly, the being destroyed by the king.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:48
verses.text: Then (to show) God's fulness of ways and means (εὐμήχανον), "In which time," it says, "Moses was born, and was exceeding fair".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:49
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:50
verses.text: ) If the former circumstance was wonderful, that Joseph was sold by his brethren, here again is another circumstance more wonderful still, that the king "nourished" the very person who was to overthrow his dominion, being himself the person that was to perish.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:51
verses.text: Do you observe all along a figurative enacting, so to say, of the resurrection of the dead? But it is not the same thing for God himself to do a thing, and for a thing to come to pass in connection with man's purpose (προαίρεσις).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:52
verses.text: For these things indeed were in connection with man's purpose but the Resurrection by itself, independently.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:53
verses.text: —"And he was mighty," it says, "in word and in deed" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:54
verses.text: ): he that was to have died.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:55
verses.text: Then again he shows how ungrateful they were to their benefactor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:56
verses.text: For, just as in the former instance, they were saved by the injured Joseph, so here again they were saved by another injured person, I mean, Moses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:57
verses.text: "And when he was full forty years old," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:58
verses.text: For what though they killed him not actually? In intention they did kill, as did the others in the former case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:59
verses.text: There, they sold out of their own into a strange land: here, they drive from one strange land into another strange land: in the former case, one in the act of bringing them food; in this, one in the act of giving them good counsel; one to whom, under God, the man was indebted for his life! Mark how it shows (the truth of) that saying of Gamaliel's, "If it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:60
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:61
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:62
verses.text: ) See the plotted-against eventually becoming the authors of salvation to those plotting against them: the people, plotting against itself, and itself plotted against by others; and for all this, saved! A famine, and it did not consume them: nor was this all: but they were saved by means of the very person, whom they had expected to be destroyed (by their means).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:63
verses.text: A royal edict, and it did not consume them: nay then most did their number increase, when he was dead "who knew" them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:64
verses.text: Their own Saviour they wished to kill, but for all that, they had not power to do it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:65
verses.text: Do you observe, that by the means whereby the devil tried to bring to naught the promise of God, by those very means it was advanced?  "And God spake on this wise," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:66
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:67
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:68
verses.text: ) This is suitable to be said here also: that God is rich in ways and means to bring us up from hence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:69
verses.text: For this above all showed the riches of God's resources, that in its very reverses (ἀποστροφῇ) the nation increased, while enslaved, while evil-entreated, and sought to be exterminated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:70
verses.text: And this is the greatness of the Promise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:71
verses.text: For had it increased in its own land, it had not been so wonderful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:72
verses.text: And besides, it was not for a short time, either, that they were in the strange land: but for four hundred years.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:73
verses.text: Hence we learn a (great lesson) of philosophic endurance (φιλοσοφίαν):—they did not treat them as masters use slaves, but as enemies and tyrants—and he foretold that they should be set in great liberty: for this is the meaning of that expression, "They shall serve (Me): and they shall come up hither again" (ἐνταὕθα ἐπανελεύσονται); and with impunity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:74
verses.text: —And observe, how, while he seems to concede something to circumcision, he in fact allows it nothing (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:75
verses.text: ); since the Promise was before it, and it followed after.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:76
verses.text: —"And the patriarchs," he says, "moved with envy".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:77
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:78
verses.text: ) Where it does no harm, he humors (χαρίζεται) them: for they prided themselves much on these also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:79
verses.text: —And he shows, that the saints were not exempt from tribulation, but that in their very tribulations they obtained help.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:80
verses.text: And that these persons did themselves help to bring about the results, who wished to cut short these same (afflictions): just as these made Joseph the more glorious: just as the king did Moses, by ordering the children to be killed: since had he not ordered, this would not have been: just as also that (Hebrew) drives Moses into exile, that there he may have the Vision, having become worthy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:81
verses.text: Thus also him who was sold for a slave, makes He to reign as king there, where he was thought to be a slave.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:82
verses.text: Thus also does Christ in His death give proof of His power: thus also does He there reign as king where they sold Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:83
verses.text: "And gave him favor and wisdom," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:84
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:85
verses.text: ) This was not only by way of honor, but that he should have confidence in his own power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:86
verses.text: "And he made him governor over Egypt and all his house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:87
verses.text: "Now there came a dearth," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:88
verses.text: On account of famine—such preparations is he making—"with threescore and fifteen souls," he says, "Jacob went down into Egypt, and died, he and our fathers, and were carried over into Sychem, and laid in the sepulchre that Abraham bought for a sum of money from the sons of Emmor the father of Sychem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:89
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:90
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:91
verses.text: It shows, that they were not masters even to the extent of a burying-place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:92
verses.text: "But when the time of the promise drew nigh, which God had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, till another king arose, which knew not Joseph" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:93
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:94
verses.text: Observe, that it is not during the four hundred years that He multiplies them, but (only) when the end was about to draw nigh.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:95
verses.text: And yet already four hundred years were passed, nay more, in Egypt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:96
verses.text: But this is the wonder of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:97
verses.text: "The same dealt subtly with our kindred, and evil-entreated our fathers, that they should cast out their young children, to the end they might not live".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:98
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:99
verses.text: ) "Dealt subtly:" he hints at their not liking to exterminate them openly: "that they should cast out their young children," it says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:100
verses.text: "In which time Moses was born and was exceeding fair".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:101
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:102
verses.text: ) This is the wonder, that he who is to be their champion, is born, neither after nor before, these things, but in the very midst of the storm (θυμῷ).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:103
verses.text: "And was nourished up in his father's house three months".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:104
verses.text: But when man's help was despaired of, and they cast him forth, then did God's benefit shine forth conspicuous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:105
verses.text: "And when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:106
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:107
verses.text: ) Not a word of Temple, not a word of Sacrifice, while all these Providences are taking place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:108
verses.text: And he was nourished in a barbarian house.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:109
verses.text: "And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:110
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:111
verses.text: ) "Was trained," both in discipline and in letters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:112
verses.text: "And when he was full forty years old".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:113
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:114
verses.text: ) Forty years he was there, and was not found out from his being circumcised.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:115
verses.text: Observe, how, being in safety, they overlook their own interests, both he and Joseph, in order that they may save others: "And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:116
verses.text: And seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him, and avenged him that was oppressed, and smote the Egyptian: for he supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:117
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:118
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:119
verses.text: )—See how up to this point he is not yet offensive to them; how they listened to him while he said all this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:120
verses.text: And "his face," we read, "was as the face of an angel" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:121
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:122
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:123
verses.text: —"For he supposed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:124
verses.text: And yet it was by deeds that his championship was shown; what intelligence was there need of here? but still for all this "they understood not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:125
verses.text: And the next day he showed himself unto them as they strove, and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, ye are brethren; why do ye wrong one to another?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:126
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:127
verses.text: ) Do you mark with what mildness he addresses them? He who had shown his wrath in the case of the other, shows his gentleness in his own case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:128
verses.text: "But he that did his neighbor wrong thrust him away, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? Wilt thou kill me, as thou didst the Egyptian yesterday?" Mark; the very words which they said to Christ: "Who made Thee ruler and judge over us?" So habitual a thing was it for Jews to wrong (their benefactors) when in the act of receiving benefits! And again, mark the atrocious baseness: (μιαρίαν al.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:129
verses.text: μοχθηρίαν, Sav.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:130
verses.text: marg.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:131
verses.text: ) "As thou didst the Egyptian yesterday! Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Midian, where he begat two sons".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:132
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:133
verses.text: ) But neither did flight extinguish the plan of Providence, as neither did death (i-e: the death of Christ).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:134
verses.text: "And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sinai an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:135
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:136
verses.text: ) Do you mark that it is not hindered by lapse of time? For when he was an exile, when a stranger, when he had now passed much time in a foreign land, so as to have two sons, when he no longer expected to return, then does the Angel appear to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:137
verses.text: The Son of God he calls an Angel, as also he calls Him man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:138
verses.text: (Appears) in the desert, not in a temple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:139
verses.text: See how many miracles are taking place, and no word of Temple, no word of Sacrifice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:140
verses.text: And here also not simply in the desert, but in the bush.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:141
verses.text: "When Moses saw it, he wondered at the sight: and as he drew near to behold it, the voice of the Lord came unto him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:142
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:143
verses.text: ) Lo! he was deemed worthy of the Voice also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:144
verses.text: "I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:145
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:146
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:147
verses.text: ) Lo! how He shows that He is none other than "the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob"—He, "the Angel of the Great Counsel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:148
verses.text: (Is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:149
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:150
verses.text: LXX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:151
verses.text: "Wonderful, Counsellor," E.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:152
verses.text: V.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:153
verses.text: ) Here he shows what great loving-kindness God herein exhibits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:154
verses.text: "Then Moses trembled, and durst not behold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:155
verses.text: Then said the Lord to him, Put off thy shoes from thy feet; for the place where thou standest is holy ground".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:156
verses.text: Not a word of Temple, and the place is holy through the appearance and operation of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:157
verses.text: Far more wonderful this than the place which is in the Holy of Holies: for there God is nowhere said to have appeared in this manner, nor Moses to have thus trembled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:158
verses.text: And then the greatness of His tender care.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:159
verses.text: "I have seen, I have seen the affliction of My people which is in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and am come down to deliver them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:160
verses.text: And now come, I will send thee into Egypt".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:161
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:162
verses.text: ) See, how he shows, that both by kindnesses, and by chastisements, and by miracles, God was drawing them to Him: but they were still the same.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:163
verses.text: That God is everywhere present, they learned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:164
verses.text: Hearing these things, let us in our afflictions flee to Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:165
verses.text: "And their groaning," saith He, "I have heard:" not simply, "because of their calamities".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:166
verses.text: But if any should ask, Why then did He suffer them to be evil entreated there? Why, in the first place, to every just man his sufferings are the causes of his rewards.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:167
verses.text: And in the next place, as to why He afflicted them: it was to show His power, that He can (do all), and not only so, but that He may also train them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:168
verses.text: Observe in fact; when they were in the desert, then they "waxed fat, they grew thick, they spread out in breadth, they kicked" (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:169
verses.text: xxxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:170
verses.text: ): and ever and always ease was an evil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:171
verses.text: Therefore also from the beginning He said to Adam: "In the sweat of thy face thou shall eat thy bread".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:172
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:173
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:174
verses.text: ) Also (it was) in order that having come out of much suffering into rest, they might give thanks to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:175
verses.text: For affliction is a great good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:176
verses.text: For hear the Prophet saying, "It is good for me, that Thou hast humbled me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:177
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:178
verses.text: cxix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:179
verses.text: ) But if to great and wonderful men affliction be a great (good), much more to us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:180
verses.text: And, if you will, let us examine into the nature of affliction as it is in itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:181
verses.text: Let there be some person rejoicing exceedingly, and gay, and giving a loose to jollity: what more unseemly, what more senseless than this? Let there be one sorrowing and dejected: what more truly philosophic than this? For, "It is better," we read, "to go into the house of mourning, than into the house of laughter".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:182
verses.text: (Eccles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:183
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:184
verses.text: ) But, likely enough, you do not like the saying, and want to evade it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:185
verses.text: Let us however see, what sort of man Adam was in Paradise, and what he was afterwards: what sort of man Cain was before, and what he was afterwards.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:186
verses.text: The soul does not stand fast in its proper place, but, like as by a running tide, (ῥεύματος, Edd.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:187
verses.text: πνεύματος, "wind") is raised and buoyed up by pleasure, having no steadfastness; facile in making professions, prompt at promising; the thoughts all in restless commotion: laughter ill-timed, causeless hilarity, idle clatter of unmeaning talk.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:188
verses.text: And why speak of others? Let us take in hand some one of the saints, and let us see what he was while in pleasure, what again, when in distress.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:189
verses.text: Shall we look at David himself? When he was in pleasure and rejoicing, from his many trophies, from his victory, from his crowns, from his luxurious living, from his confidence, see what sort of things he said and did: "But I said in my prosperity," says he, "I shall never be moved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:190
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:191
verses.text: xxx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:192
verses.text: ) But when he has come to be in affliction, hear what he says: "And if He say to me, I have no mind for thee; lo! here am I, let Him do that which is pleasing in His sight".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:193
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:194
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:195
verses.text: ) What can be more truly philosophic than these words? "Whatsoever may be pleasing to God," saith he, "so let it be".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:196
verses.text: And again he said to Saul: "If the Lord stirreth thee up against me, may thy sacrifice be acceptable".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:197
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:198
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:199
verses.text: ) And then too, being in affliction, he spared even his enemies: but afterwards, not friends even, nor those who had done him no injury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:200
verses.text: Again, Jacob when he was in affliction, said: "If the Lord will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:201
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:202
verses.text: xxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:203
verses.text: ) As also the son of Noah did nothing of the kind erewhile; but when he was no longer afraid for his safety, you hear how wanton he became.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:204
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:205
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:206
verses.text: ) Hezekiah too, when he was in affliction, see what things he did in order to his deliverance; he put on sackcloth, and such like; but when he was in pleasure, he fell through the haughtiness of his heart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:207
verses.text: ( Kings ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:208
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:209
verses.text: ) For, saith the Scripture, "When thou hast eaten, and drunk, and art filled, take heed to thyself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:210
verses.text: (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:211
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:212
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:213
verses.text: ) For perilous, as on a precipice's brink, is the post of affluence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:214
verses.text: "Take heed," saith he, "to thyself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:215
verses.text: When the Israelites were afflicted, they became all the more increased in number: but when He left them to themselves, then they all went to ruin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:216
verses.text: And why speak of examples from the ancients? In our own times, let us see, if you please, is it not the case, that when the most are in good case, they become puffed up, hostile to everybody, passionate, while the power is with them: but if it be taken away, they are gentle, lowly (and as) human beings, are brought to a consciousness of their own natural condition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:217
verses.text: Therefore the Scripture saith, "Pride hath holden them unto the end: their iniquity shall go forth as from fatness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:218
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:219
verses.text: lxxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:220
verses.text: LXX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:221
verses.text: )  Now these things I have spoken, that we should not make enjoyment every way our object.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:222
verses.text: How then does Paul say, "Rejoice alway?" He does not say simply, "Rejoice," but he adds, "in the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:223
verses.text: (Phil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:224
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:225
verses.text: ) This is the greatest joy, such as the Apostles rejoiced withal; the joy of which prisons, and scourges, and persecutions, and evil report, and all painful things, are the source, and the root, and the occasion; whence also it comes to a happy issue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:226
verses.text: But that of the world, on the contrary, begins with sweets and ends in bitters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:227
verses.text: Neither do I forbid to rejoice in the Lord, nay, I earnestly exhort to this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:228
verses.text: The Apostles were scourged, and they rejoiced: were bound, and they gave thanks: were stoned, and they preached.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:229
verses.text: This is the joy I also would have: from nothing bodily has it its origin, but from spiritual things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:230
verses.text: It is not possible for him who joys after the fashion of the world, to rejoice also after a godly sort: for every one who joys after the world's fashion, has his joy in riches, in luxury, in honor, in power, in arrogance: but he who rejoices after the mind of God, has his joy in dishonor for God's sake, in poverty, in want, in fasting, in humbleness of mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:231
verses.text: Seest thou, how opposite are the grounds (of joy)? To go without joy here, is to be without grief also: and to be without grief here, is to go without pleasure too.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:232
verses.text: And in truth these are the things which produce real joy, since the others have the name only of joy, but they altogether consist of pain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:233
verses.text: What misery the arrogant man endures! How is he cut short (διακόπτεται) in the midst of his arrogance, bespeaking for himself numberless insults, much hatred, great enmity, exceeding spite, and many an evil eye! Whether it be that he is insulted by greater men, he grieves: or that he cannot make his stand against everybody, he is mortified.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:234
verses.text: Whereas the humble man lives in much enjoyment: expecting honor from none, if he receive honor, he is pleased, but if not, he is not grieved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:235
verses.text: He takes it contentedly that he is honored; but above all, none dishonors him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:236
verses.text: Now not to seek honor, and yet to be honored—great must be the enjoyment of this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:237
verses.text: But in the other, it is just the reverse: he seeks honor, and is not honored.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:238
verses.text: And the pleasure that the honor gives is not the same to him who seeks it, as it is to him who seeks it not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:239
verses.text: The one, however much he receives, thinks he has received nothing: the other, though you give him ever so little, takes it as though he had received all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:240
verses.text: Then again, he who lives in affluence and luxury has numberless affairs of business, and let his revenues flow in to him ever so easily, and, as it were, from full fountains, yet he fears the evils arising from luxurious living, and the uncertainty of the future: but the other is always in a state of security and enjoyment, having accustomed himself to scantiness of diet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:241
verses.text: For he does not so bemoan himself at not partaking of a sumptuous board, as he luxuriates in not fearing the uncertainty of the future.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:242
verses.text: But the evils arising from luxurious living, how many and great they are, none can be ignorant: it is necessary, however, to mention them now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:243
verses.text: Twofold the war, in the body, and in the soul: twofold the storm: twofold the diseases; not only in this respect, but because they are both incurable, and bring with them great calamities.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:244
verses.text: Not so, frugality: but here is twofold health, twofold the benefits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:245
verses.text: "Sleep of health," we read, "is in moderate eating".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:246
verses.text: (Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:247
verses.text: xxxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:248
verses.text: ) For everywhere, that which keeps measure is pleasant, that which is beyond measure, ceases to please.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:249
verses.text: For say now: on a little spark put a great pile of fagots, and you will no longer see the fire shining, but much disagreeable smoke.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:250
verses.text: On a very strong and large man lay a burden which exceeds his strength, and you will see him with his burden lying prostrate on the ground.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:251
verses.text: Embark too large a freight in your vessel, and you have ensured a grievous shipwreck.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:252
verses.text: Just so it is here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:253
verses.text: For just as in overladen ships, great is the tumult of the sailors, the pilot, the man at the prow, and the passengers, while they cast into the sea the things above deck, and things below; so here too, with their vomitings upwards, and their purgings downwards, they mar their constitutions, and destroy themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:254
verses.text: And what is the most shameful of all, the mouth is made to do the office of the nether parts, and that becomes the more shameful member.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:255
verses.text: But if to the mouth the disgrace be such, think what must it be in the soul! For indeed there it is all mist, all storm, all darkness, great the uproar of the thoughts, at being so thronged and crushed, the soul itself crying out at the abuse done to it: all (the parts and faculties) complaining of one another, beseeching, entreating, that the filth may be discharged somewhere.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:256
verses.text: And after it is flung out, still the turmoil is not at an end; but then comes fever and diseases.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:257
verses.text: "And how comes it," say you, "that one may see these luxurious livers, in goodly plight, riding on horseback? What idle talk is this," say you, "to tell us of diseases? It is I that am diseased, I that am racked, I that am disgusting, while I have nothing to eat".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:258
verses.text: Ah me! for one may well lament at such words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:259
verses.text: But the sufferers with the gout, the men that are carried on litters, the men that are swathed with bandages, from what class of people, I ask you, shall we see these? And indeed, were it not that they would deem it an insult, and think my words opprobrious, I would before now have addressed them even by name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:260
