verses.text: "But there are some of them, who are in good health as well".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:261
verses.text: Because they give themselves not merely to luxurious living, but also to labors.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:262
verses.text: Else show me a man, who does nothing whatever but fatten himself, free from pain as he lies there, without an anxious thought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:263
verses.text: For though a host of physicians without number came together, they would not be able to rescue him from his diseases.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:264
verses.text: It is not in the nature of things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:265
verses.text: For I will hold you a medical discourse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:266
verses.text: Of the matters sent down into the belly, not all becomes nourishment; since even in the food itself, not all is nutritive, but part of it in the process of digestion passes into stool, part is turned into nourishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:267
verses.text: If then in the process of digestion the operation is perfect, this is the result, and each finds its proper place; the wholesome and useful part betakes itself to its appropriate place, while that which is superfluous and useless, withdraws itself, and passes off.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:268
verses.text: But if it be in too great quantity, then even the nutritive part of it becomes hurtful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:269
verses.text: And, to speak by way of example, in order that my meaning may be clearer to you: in wheat part is fine flour, part meal, part bran: now if the mill be able to grind (what is put in), it separates all these: but if you put in too much, all becomes mixed up together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:270
verses.text: Wine again, if it go through its proper process of formation, and under due influence of the seasons, then, whereas at first all is mixed together, anon part settles into lees, part rises into scum, part remains for enjoyment to those that use it, and this is the good part, and will not readily undergo any change.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:271
verses.text: But what they call "nourishment," is neither wine, nor lees, while all are mixed up together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:272
verses.text: —The same may be seen in the river, when its waters make a whirling flood.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:273
verses.text: As at such time we see the fishes floating at top, dead, their eyes first blinded by the muddy slime: so is it with us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:274
verses.text: For when gormandizing, like a flood of rain, has drenched the inward parts, it puts all in a whirl, and makes that the faculties (λογισμοὶ), healthy till then and living in a pure element, drift lifeless on the surface.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:275
verses.text: Since then by all these examples we have shown how great the mischief is, let us cease to count these men happy for that, for which we ought to think them wretched, and to bemoan ourselves for that, for which we ought to count ourselves happy, and let us welcome sufficiency with a contented mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:276
verses.text: Or do you not hear even what physicians tell you, that "want is the mother of health?" But what I say is, that want is mother, not of bodily health, but also of that of the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:277
verses.text: These things Paul also, that physician indeed, cries aloud; when he says, "Having food and raiment, let us therewith be content".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:278
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:279
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 41:280
verses.text: ) Let us therefore do as he bids us, that so, being in sound health, we may perform the work that we ought to do, in Christ Jesus our Lord, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:1
verses.text: Homily XVII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:2
verses.text: Acts VII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:3
verses.text: "This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? the same did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the Angel which appeared to him in the bush".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:4
verses.text: This is very suitable to the matter in hand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:5
verses.text: "This Moses," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:6
verses.text: "This," the man who had been in danger of losing his life; the man who had been set at naught by them; "this" the man whom they had declined: "this" same, God having raised up, sent unto them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:7
verses.text: "Whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler?" just as they themselves (the hearers) said, "We have no king, but Caesar".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:8
verses.text: (John xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:9
verses.text: ) He here shows also, that what was then done, was done by Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:10
verses.text: "The same did God send by the hand of the Angel," who said unto him, "I am the God of Abraham".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:11
verses.text: "This" same Moses, he says,—and observe how he points to his renown—"this" same Moses, he says, "brought them out, after that he had showed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red sea, and in the wilderness forty years.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:12
verses.text: This is that Moses, which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:13
verses.text: , ): set at naught like me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:14
verses.text: Him, likewise, Herod wished to kill, and in Egypt He found preservation just as it was with the former, even when He was a babe, He was aimed at for destruction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:15
verses.text: "This is he, that was in the Church in the wilderness with the Angel which spake to him in the mount Sina, and with our fathers: who received the lively oracles to give unto us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:16
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:17
verses.text: ) Again no mention of temple, none of sacrifice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:18
verses.text: "With the Angel," it says, "he received the lively oracles to give unto the fathers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:19
verses.text: It shows, that he not only wrought miracles, but also gave a law, as Christ did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:20
verses.text: Just as Christ first works miracles, and then legislates: so did Moses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:21
verses.text: But they did not hear him, keeping their disobedience, even after the miracles: "To whom," he says, "our fathers would not obey:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:22
verses.text: ) after the wonders done in those forty years.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:23
verses.text: And not only so, but just the contrary: "but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back again into Egypt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:24
verses.text: Saying unto Aaron, Make us gods to go before us; for as for this Moses, which brought us out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:25
verses.text: And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:26
verses.text: Then God turned, and gave them up to worship the host of heaven; as it is written in the book of the Prophets, O ye house of Israel, have ye offered to me slain beasts and sacrifices by the space of forty years in the wilderness? Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:29
verses.text: ) The expression, "gave them up," means, He suffered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:30
verses.text: "Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, as he had appointed, speaking unto Moses, that he should make it according to the fashion he had seen".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:32
verses.text: ) Even when there was a Tabernacle, yet there were no sacrifices.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:33
verses.text: "Did ye offer unto Me slain beasts and sacrifices?" (Amos v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:34
verses.text: ) There was "the tabernacle of witness," and yet it profited them nothing, but they were consumed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:35
verses.text: But neither before, nor afterwards, did the miracles profit them aught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:36
verses.text: "Which also, our fathers that came after brought in".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:37
verses.text: Seest thou, how the holy place is there wherever God may be? For to this end also he says, "in the wilderness," to compare place with place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:38
verses.text: Then the benefit (conferred upon them): And our fathers that came after brought it in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom God drave out before the face of our fathers, unto the days of David; who found favor before God, and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:41
verses.text: ) David "desired to find favor:" and he builded not, he, the wonderful, the great; but the castaway, Solomon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:42
verses.text: "But Solomon," it says, "built Him an house.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:43
verses.text: Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in (places) made with hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:44
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:46
verses.text: ) This was shown indeed already by what had been before said: but it is shown also by the voice of a prophet; "What house will ye build for Me? saith the Lord God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:47
verses.text: As saith the prophet, Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool: what house will ye build for me? saith the Lord: or what is the place of my rest? Hath not my hand made all these things?" (Is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:48
verses.text: lxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:49
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:50
verses.text: )  Marvel not, he says, if they on whom Christ confers His benefits refuse His kingdom, seeing in the case of Moses it was just the same.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:51
verses.text: (Recapitulation).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:52
verses.text: "He brought them out;" and rescued them not in a general way, but also while they were in the wilderness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:53
verses.text: "Wonders and signs," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:55
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:56
verses.text: ) Do you mark that they themselves (Stephen's hearers) are concerned in those old miracles also? "This is that Moses:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:57
verses.text: ) he, that conversed with God; he, that had been saved out of situations so strange and wonderful; he, that wrought so great works, and had so great power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:58
verses.text: "Which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:59
verses.text: He shows, that the prophecy must by all means be fulfilled, and that Moses is not opposed to Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:60
verses.text: "This is he that was in the Church in the wilderness, and, that said unto the children of Israel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:61
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:62
verses.text: ) Do you mark that thence comes the root, and that "salvation is from the Jews?" (John iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:63
verses.text: ) "With the Angel," it says, "which spake unto him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:64
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:65
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:66
verses.text: ) Lo, again he affirms that it was He (Christ) that gave the Law, seeing Moses was with "Him" in the Church in the wilderness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:67
verses.text: And here he puts them in mind of a great marvel, of the things done in the Mount: "Who received living oracles to give unto us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:68
verses.text: On all occasions Moses is wonderful, and (so) when need was to legislate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:69
verses.text: What means the expression, "Living oracles" (λόγια)? Those, whereof the end was shown by words (διὰ λόγων): in other words, he means the prophecies.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:70
verses.text: Then follows the charge, in the first instance, against the patriarchs after, the "signs and wonders," after the receiving of the "lively oracles: To whom," he says, "our fathers would not obey".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:71
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:72
verses.text: ) But concerning those, Ezekiel says that they are not "living;" as when he says, "And I gave you statutes that are not good".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:73
verses.text: (Ezek.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:74
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:75
verses.text: ) It is with reference to those that he says, "Living.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:76
verses.text: But thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back to Egypt"—the place where they groaned, where they cried, whence they called upon God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:77
verses.text: "And said unto Aaron, Make us gods which shall go before us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:78
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:79
verses.text: ) O the folly! "Make," say they; "that they may go before us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:80
verses.text: Whither? "Into Egypt".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:81
verses.text: See how hard they were to tear away from the customs of Egypt! What sayest thou? What, not wait for him that brought thee out, but flee the benefit, and deny the Benefactor? And mark how insulting they are: "For as for this Moses," they say:—"which brought us out of the land of Egypt" nowhere the name of God: instead of that, they ascribed all to Moses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:82
verses.text: Where they ought to give thanks (to God), they bring Moses forward: where it was, to do as the Law bade them, they no longer make account of Moses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:83
verses.text: "We know not what is become of him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:84
verses.text: And yet he told them that he was going up to receive the Law: and they had not patience to wait forty days.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:85
verses.text: "Make us gods"—they did not say, "a God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:86
verses.text: —And yet one may well wonder at this, that they do not even know.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:87
verses.text: —"And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifices unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:88
verses.text: ): for which they ought to have hid their faces.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:89
verses.text: What wonder that ye know not Christ, seeing ye knew not Moses, and God Who was manifested by such wonders? But they not only knew Him not: they also insulted in another way, by their idol making.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:90
verses.text: "Then God turned, and gave them up to worship the host of heaven" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:91
verses.text: ) Hence these same "customs" date their origin, hence the sacrifices: they were themselves the first that made sacrifices to their idols! For that is why it is marked, "They made a calf in Horeb, and offered sacrifices to the idol:" seeing that, before this the name of sacrifice is nowhere mentioned, but only lively ordinances, and "lively oracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:92
verses.text: And rejoiced"—that is the reason for the feasts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:93
verses.text: (Exod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:94
verses.text: xxxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:95
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:96
verses.text: ) "As it is written in the Book of the Prophets"—and observe, he does not cite the text without a purpose, but shows by it that there is no need of sacrifices; saying: "Did ye offer slain beasts and sacrifice to Me?"—He lays an emphasis on this word (to Me?).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:97
verses.text: "Ye cannot say that it was from sacrificing to Me, that ye proceeded to sacrifice to them:—"by the space of forty years:" and this too, "in the wilderness," where He had most signally shown Himself their Protector.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:98
verses.text: "Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan: images which ye made to worship them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:99
verses.text: The cause of sacrifices! "And I will carry you away beyond Babylon".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:101
verses.text: ) Even the captivity, an impeachment of their wickedness! "But a Tabernacle," say you, "there was (the Tabernacle) 'of Witness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:102
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:103
verses.text: ) (Yes,) this is why it was: that they should have God for Witness: this was all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:104
verses.text: "According to the fashion," it says, "that was shown thee on the mount:" so that on the mount was the Original.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:105
verses.text: And this Tabernacle, moreover, "in the wilderness," was carried about, and not locally fixed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:106
verses.text: And he calls it, "Tabernacle of witness:" i-e: (for witness) of the miracles, of the statutes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:107
verses.text: This is the reason why both it and those (the fathers) had no Temple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:108
verses.text: "As He had appointed, that spake unto Moses, that he should make it according to the fashion that he had seen".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:109
verses.text: Again, it was none other than He (Christ) that gave the fashion itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:110
verses.text: "Until the days of David" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:111
verses.text: ): and there was no temple! And yet the Gentiles also had been driven out: for that is why he mentions this: "Whom God drave out," he says, "before the face of our fathers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:112
verses.text: Whom He drave out," he says: and even then, no Temple! And so many wonders, and no mention of a Temple! So that, although first there is a Tabernacle, yet nowhere a Temple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:113
verses.text: "Until the days of David," he says: even David, and no Temple! "And he sought to find favor before God" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:114
verses.text: ): and built not:—so far was the Temple from being a great matter! "But Solomon built Him an house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:116
verses.text: ) They thought Solomon was great: but that he was not better than his father, nay not even equal to him, is manifest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:117
verses.text: "Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands; as saith the prophet, Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:118
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:119
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:120
verses.text: ) Nay, not even these are worthy of God, forasmuch as they are made, seeing they are creatures, the works of His hand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:121
verses.text: See how he leads them on by little and little (showing) that not even these are to be mentioned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:122
verses.text: And again the prophecy says openly, "What house will ye build Me?" etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:123
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:124
verses.text: )  What is the reason that at this point he speaks in the tone of invective (καταφορικὥς)? Great was his boldness of speech, when at the point to die: for in fact I think he knew that this was the case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:125
verses.text: "Ye stiffnecked," he says, "and uncircumcised in heart and ears".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:126
verses.text: This also is from the prophets: nothing is of himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:127
verses.text: "Ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:128
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:129
verses.text: ) When it was not His will that sacrifices should be, ye sacrifice: when it is His will, then again ye do not sacrifice: when He would not give you commandments, ye drew them to you: when ye got them, ye neglected them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:130
verses.text: Again, when the Temple stood, ye worshipped idols: when it is His will to be worshipped without a Temple, ye do the opposite.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:131
verses.text: Observe, he says not, "Ye resist God," but, "the Spirit:" so far was he from knowing any difference between Them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:132
verses.text: And, what is greater: "As your fathers did," he says, "so do ye".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:133
verses.text: Thus also did Christ (reproach them), forasmuch as they were always boasting much of their fathers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:134
verses.text: "Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which showed before of the coming of the Just One:" he still says, "the Just One," wishing to check them: "of Whom ye have been now the betrayers and murderers"—two charges he lays against them—"who have received the Law by the disposition of Angels, and have not kept it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:135
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:136
verses.text: ) How, "By the disposition of Angels?" Some say (The Law), disposed by Angels; or, put into his hand by the Angel Who appeared to him in the bush; for was He man? No wonder that He who wrought those works, should also have wrought these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:137
verses.text: "Ye slew them who preached of Him," much more Himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:138
verses.text: He shows them disobedient both to God, and to Angels, and the Prophets, and the Spirit, and to all: as also Scripture saith elsewhere: "Lord, they have slain Thy Prophets, and thrown down Thine altars".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:139
verses.text: ( Kings xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:140
verses.text: ) They, then, stand up for the Law, and say, "He blasphemeth against Moses:" he shows, therefore, that it is they who blaspheme, and that (their blasphemy is not only against Moses, but) against God; shows that "they" from the very beginning have been doing this: that "they" have themselves destroyed their "customs," that there is no need of these: that while accusing him, and saying that he opposed Moses, they themselves were opposing the Spirit: and not merely opposing, but with murder added to it: and that they had their enmity all along from the very beginning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:141
verses.text: Seest thou, that he shows them to be acting in opposition both to Moses and to all others, and not keeping the Law? And yet Moses had said, "A Prophet shall the Lord raise up unto you: and the rest also told of this (Christ) that He would come: and the prophet again said, "What house will ye build Me?" and again, "Did ye offer to Me slain beasts and sacrifices" those "forty years?" (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:142
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:143
verses.text: )  Such is the boldness of speech of a man bearing the Cross.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:144
verses.text: Let us then also imitate this: though it be not a time of war, yet it is always the time for boldness of speech.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:145
verses.text: For, "I spake," says one, "in Thy testimonies before kings, and was not ashamed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:146
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:147
verses.text: cxix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:148
verses.text: ) If we chance to be among heathens, let us thus stop their mouths.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:149
verses.text: without wrath, without harshness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:150
verses.text: (Comp.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:151
verses.text: Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:152
verses.text: in  Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:153
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:154
verses.text: §; xxxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:155
verses.text: §, ; Col.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:156
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:157
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:158
verses.text: ) For if we do it with wrath, it no longer seems to be the boldness (of one who is confident of his cause,) but passion: but if with gentleness, this is boldness indeed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:159
verses.text: For in one and the same thing success and failure cannot possibly go together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:160
verses.text: The boldness is a success: the anger is a failure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:161
verses.text: Therefore, if we are to have boldness, we must be clean from wrath that none may impute our words to that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:162
verses.text: No matter how just your words may be, when you speak with anger, you ruin all: no matter how boldly you speak, how fairly reprove, or what not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:163
verses.text: See this man, how free from passion as he discourses to them! For he did not abuse them: he did but remind them of the words of the Prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:164
verses.text: For, to show you that it was not anger, at the very moment he was suffering evil at their hands, he prayed, saying, "Lay not to their charge this sin".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:165
verses.text: So far was he from speaking these words in anger; no, he spake in grief and sorrow for their sakes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:166
verses.text: As indeed this is why it speaks of his appearance, that "they saw his face as it had been the face of an angel," on purpose that they might believe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:167
verses.text: Let us then be clean from wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:168
verses.text: The Holy Spirit dwelleth not where wrath is: cursed is the wrathful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:169
verses.text: It cannot be that aught wholesome should approach, where wrath goes forth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:170
verses.text: For as in a storm at sea, great is the tumult, loud the clamor, and then would be no time for lessons of wisdom (φιλοσοφεἵν): so neither in wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:171
verses.text: If the soul is to be in a condition either to say, or to be disciplined to, aught of philosophy, it must first be in the haven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:172
verses.text: Seest thou not how, when we wish to converse on matters of serious import, we look out for places free from noise, where all is stillness, all calm, that we may not be put out and discomposed? But if noise from without discomposes, much more disturbance from within.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:173
verses.text: Whether one pray, to no purpose does he pray "with wrath and disputings:" ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:174
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:175
verses.text: ) whether he speak, he will only make himself ridiculous: whether he hold his peace, so again it will be even then: whether he eat, he is hurt even then: whether he drink, or whether he drink not; whether he sit, or stand, or walk; whether he sleep: for even in their dreams such fancies haunt them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:176
verses.text: For what is there in such men that is not disagreeable? Eyes unsightly, mouth distorted, limbs agitated and swollen, tongue foul and sparing no man, mind distraught, gestures uncomely: much to disgust.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:177
verses.text: Mark the eyes of demoniacs, and those of drunkards and madmen; in what do they differ from each other? Is not the whole madness? For what though it be but for the moment? The madman too is possessed for the moment: but what is worse than this? And they are not ashamed at that excuse; "I knew not (saith one) what I said".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:178
verses.text: And how came it that thou didst not know this, thou the rational man, thou that hast the gift of reason, on purpose that thou mayest not act the part of the creatures without reason, just like a wild horse, hurried away by rage and passion? In truth, the very excuse is criminal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:179
verses.text: For thou oughtest to have known what thou saidst.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:180
verses.text: "It was the passion," say you, "that spoke the words, not I".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:181
verses.text: How should it be that? For passion has no power, except it get it from you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:182
verses.text: You might as well say, "It was my hand that inflicted the wounds, not I".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:183
verses.text: What occasion, think you, most needs wrath? would you not say, war and battle? But even then, if anything is done with wrath, the whole is spoiled and undone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:184
verses.text: For of all men, those who fight had best not be enraged: of all men, those had best not be enraged, who want to hurt (τοὺς ὑβρίζοντας).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:185
verses.text: And how is it possible to fight then? you will ask.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:186
verses.text: With reason, with self-command (ἐπιεικεί& ·): since fighting is, to stand in opposition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:187
verses.text: Seest thou not that even these (common) wars are regulated by definite law, and order, and times? For wrath is nothing but an irrational impulse: and an irrational creature cannot possibly perform aught rational.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:188
verses.text: For instance, the man here spoke such words, and did it without passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:189
verses.text: And Elias said," How long will ye halt on both your knees?" ( Kings xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:190
verses.text: ) and spake it not in passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:191
verses.text: And Phinees slew, and did it without passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:192
verses.text: For passion suffers not a man to see, but, just as in a night-battle, it leads him, with eyes blindfolded and ears stopped up, where it will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:193
verses.text: Then let us rid ourselves of this demon, at its first beginning let us quell it, let us put the sign of the Cross on our breast, as it were a curb.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:194
verses.text: Wrath is a shameless dog: but let it learn to hear the law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:195
verses.text: If there be in a sheep-fold a dog so savage as not to obey the command of the shepherd, nor to know his voice, all is lost and ruined.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:196
verses.text: He is kept along with the sheep: but if he makes a meal on the sheep, he is useless, and is put to death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:197
verses.text: If he has learnt to obey thee, feed thy dog: he is useful when it is against the wolves, against robbers, and against the captain of the robbers that he barks, not against the sheep, not against friends.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:198
verses.text: If he does not obey he ruins all: if he learns not to mind thee, he destroys all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:199
verses.text: The mildness in thee let not wrath consume, but let it guard it, and feed it up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:200
verses.text: And it will guard it, that it may feed in much security, if it destroy wicked and evil thoughts, if it chase away the devil from every side.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:201
verses.text: So is gentleness preserved, when evil works are nowhere admitted: so we become worthy of respect, when we learn not to be shameless.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:202
verses.text: For nothing renders a man so shameless, as an evil conscience.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:203
verses.text: Why are harlots without shame? Why are virgins shamefaced? Is it not from their sin that the former, from their chastity that the latter, are such? For nothing makes a person so shameless, as sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:204
verses.text: "And yet on the contrary," say you, "it puts to shame".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:205
verses.text: Yes; him who condemns himself: but him that is past blushing, it renders even more reckless: for desperation makes daring.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:206
verses.text: For "the wicked," saith the Scripture, "when he is come into the depths of evils, despiseth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:207
verses.text: (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:208
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:209
verses.text: ) But he that is shameless, will also be reckless, and he that is reckless, will be daring.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:210
verses.text: See in what way gentleness is destroyed, when evil thoughts gnaw at it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:211
verses.text: This is why there is such a dog, barking mightily: we have also sling and stone (ye know what I mean): we have also spear and enclosure and cattle-fold: let us guard our thoughts unhurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:212
verses.text: If the dog be gentle (σαίνῃ) with the sheep, but savage against those without, and keep vigilant watch, this is the excellence of a dog: and, be he ever so famished, not to devour the sheep; be he ever so full, not to spare the wolves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:213
verses.text: Such too is anger meant to be: however provoked, not to forsake gentleness; however at quiet, to be on the alert against evil thoughts: to acknowledge the friend, and not for any beating forsake him, and for all his caressing, to fly at the intruder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:214
verses.text: The devil uses caressing full oft: let the dog know at sight that he is an intruder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:215
verses.text: So also let us caress (σαίνωμεν) Virtue, though she put us to pain, and show our aversion to Vice, though she give us pleasure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:216
verses.text: Let us not be worse than the dogs, which, even when whipped and throttled, do not desert their master: but if the stranger also feed them, even so they do hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:217
verses.text: There are times when anger is useful; but this is when it barks against strangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:218
verses.text: What means it, "Whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause?" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:219
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:220
verses.text: ) It means, Stand not up in thine own quarrel, neither avenge thyself: if thou see another suffering deadly wrong, stretch out thy hand to help him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:221
verses.text: This is no longer passion, when thou art clear of all feeling for thyself alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:222
verses.text: David had gotten Saul into his power, and was not moved by passion, did not thrust the spear into him, the enemy he had in his power; but took his revenge upon the Devil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:223
verses.text: ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:224
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:225
verses.text: ) Moses, when he saw a stranger doing an injury, even slew him (Exod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:226
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:227
verses.text: ): but when one of his own people, he did not so: them that were brethren he would have reconciled; the others not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:228
verses.text: That "most meek" (Num.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:229
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:230
verses.text: ) Moses, as Scripture witnesseth of him, see how he was roused! But not so, we: on the contrary, where we ought to show meekness, no wild beast so fierce as we: but where we ought to be roused, none so dull and sluggish.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:231
verses.text: (Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:232
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:233
verses.text: de laud.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:234
verses.text: Pauli, ad fin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:235
verses.text: ) On no occasion do we use our faculties to the purpose they were meant for: and therefore it is that our life is spent to no purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:236
verses.text: For even in the case of implements; if one use them, one instead of other, all is spoilt: if one take his sword, and then, where he should use it and cut with it, uses only his hand, he does no good: again, where he should use his hand, by taking the sword in hand he spoils all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:237
verses.text: In like manner also the physician, if where he ought to cut, he cuts not, and where he ought not, he does cut, mars all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:238
verses.text: Wherefore, I beseech you, let us use the thing (τᾥ πράγματι) at its proper time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:239
verses.text: The proper time for anger is never, where we move in our own quarrel: but if it is our duty to correct others, then is the time to use it, that we may by force deliver others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:240
verses.text: (Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:241
verses.text: in Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:242
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:243
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 42:244
verses.text: ) So shall we both be like unto God, always keeping a spirit free from wrath, and shall attain unto the good things that are to come, through the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom, to the Father and the Holy Ghost together, be glory, dominion, and honor, now and evermore, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:1
verses.text: Homily XVIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:2
verses.text: Acts VII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:3
verses.text: "When they heard these things, they were cut to "the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:4
verses.text: {{small-caps|See, once more, the wrong-doers in trouble.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:5
verses.text: Just as the Jews are perplexed, saying, "What are we to do with these men?" so these also are "cut to the heart".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:6
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:7
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:8
verses.text: ) And yet it was he that had good right to be incensed, who, having done no wrong, was treated like a criminal, and was spitefully calumniated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:9
verses.text: But the calumniators had the worst of it in the end.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:10
verses.text: So true is that saying, which I am ever repeating, "Ill to do, is ill to fare".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:11
verses.text: And yet he (in his charges against them) resorted to no calumny, but proved (what he said).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:12
verses.text: So sure are we, when we are shamefully borne down in a matter wherein we have a clear conscience, to be none the worse for it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:13
verses.text: —"If they desired," say you, "to kill him, how was it that they did not take occasion, out of what he said, that they might kill him?" They would fain have a fair-seeming plea to put upon their outrage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:14
verses.text: "Well then, was not the insulting them a fair plea?" It was not his doing, if they were insulted: it was the Prophet's accusation of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:15
verses.text: And besides, they did not wish it to look as if they killed him because of what he had said against them—just as they acted in the case of Christ; no, but for impiety: now this word of his was the expression of piety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:16
verses.text: Wherefore, as they attempted, besides killing him, to hurt his reputation also, "they were cut to the heart".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:17
verses.text: For they were afraid lest he should on the contrary become an object of even greater reverence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:18
verses.text: Therefore, just what they did in Christ's case, the same they do here also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:19
verses.text: For as He said, "Ye shall see the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of God" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:20
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:21
verses.text: ), and they, calling it blasphemy, "ran upon Him;" just so was it here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:22
verses.text: There, they "rent their garments;" here, they "stopped their ears.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:23
verses.text: But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up steadfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing on the right hand of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:24
verses.text: Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, and cast him out of the city, and stoned him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:27
verses.text: ) And yet, if he lied, they ought to have thought him beside himself, and to have let him go.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:28
verses.text: —But he wished to bring them over, "and said, Behold," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:29
verses.text: , for, since he had spoken of Christ's death, and had said nothing of His resurrection, he would fain add this doctrine also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:30
verses.text: "Standing at the right hand of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:31
verses.text: And in this manner He appeared to him: that, were it but so, the Jews might receive Him: for since the (idea of His) sitting (at the right hand of God) was offensive to them, for the present he brings forward only what relates to His Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:32
verses.text: This is the reason also why his face was glorified.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:33
verses.text: For God, being merciful, desired to make their machinations the means of recalling them unto Himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:34
verses.text: And see, how many signs are wrought! "And cast him out of the city, and stoned him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:35
verses.text: Here again, "without the city," and even in death, Confession and Preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:36
verses.text: (Heb.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:37
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:38
verses.text: ) "And the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man's feet, whose name was Saul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:39
verses.text: And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:41
verses.text: ) This is meant to show them that he is not perishing, and to teach them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:42
verses.text: "And he knelt down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:43
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:44
verses.text: ) To clear himself, and show that neither were his former words prompted by passion, he says, "Lord" "lay not this sin to their charge": wishing also even in this way to win them over.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:45
verses.text: For to show that he forgave their wrath and rage in murdering him, and that his own soul was free from all passion, was the way to make his saying to be favorably received.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:46
verses.text: "And Saul was consenting unto his death".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:47
verses.text: Hereupon arises a persecution, and it becomes a great one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:48
verses.text: "And at that time there was a great persecution against the Church which was at Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:49
verses.text: And they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the Apostles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:50
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:51
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:52
verses.text: ) Mark how once more God permits temptations to arise; mark, and well observe, how the events are ordered by Divine Providence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:53
verses.text: They were admired because of the signs: being scourged, they were none the worse for it: (some) were ordained in the matter of the widows: the word increased: once more, God permits a great hindrance to arise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:54
verses.text: And a persecution of no ordinary kind "and they were all scattered," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:55
verses.text: ; for they feared their enemies, now become more daring: and at the same time it is shown that they were but men, these that were afraid, that fled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:56
verses.text: For, that thou mayest not say after these things that by grace alone they effected (what they did), they were also persecuted, and themselves became more timorous, while their adversaries were more daring.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:57
verses.text: "And were all scattered abroad," it says, "except the Apostles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:58
verses.text: But this was divinely ordered, so that they should no longer all sit there in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:59
verses.text: "And devout men," it says, "carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:60
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:61
verses.text: ) If they were "devout," why did they "make great lamentation over him?" They were not yet perfect.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:62
verses.text: The man was gracious and amiable: this also shows that they were men—not their fear alone, but their grief and lamentation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:63
verses.text: Who would not have wept to see that mild, that lamb-like person stoned, and lying dead? Fit eulogy to be spoken over his grave has the Evangelist recorded, in this one speech, "Lay not this sin to their charge".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:64
verses.text: —"And made," he says, "great lamentation over him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:65
verses.text: —But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:66
verses.text: He mentions the cause of his (angelic) appearance (Recapitulation, vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:67
verses.text: ; viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:68
verses.text: ); "But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up steadfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:69
verses.text: And when he said, "I see the heavens opened, they stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:70
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:71
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:72
verses.text: ) And yet in what respect are these things deserving of accusation? "Upon him," the man who has wrought such miracles, the man who has prevailed over all in speech, the man who can hold such discourse! As if they had got the very thing they wanted, they straightway give full scope to their rage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:73
verses.text: "And the witnesses," he says, "laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man, whose name was Saul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:74
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:75
verses.text: ) Observe how particularly he relates what concerns Paul, to show thee that the Power which wrought in him was of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:76
verses.text: But after all these things, not only did he not believe, but also aimed at Him with a thousand hands: for this is why it says, "And Saul was consenting unto his death".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:77
verses.text: —And this blessed man does not simply pray, but does it with earnestness: "having kneeled down".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:78
verses.text: Mark his divine death! So long only the Lord permitted the soul to remain in him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:79
verses.text: "And having said this, he fell asleep".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:80
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:81
verses.text: )—"And they were all scattered abroad throughout the region of Judea and Samaria.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:82
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:83
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:84
verses.text: ) And now without scruple they had intercourse with Samaria, whereas it had been said to them, "Go not into the way of the Gentiles" "and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:85
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:86
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:87
verses.text: ) "Except the Apostles," it says: they, in this way also, wishing to win the Jews,—but not to leave the city,—and to be the means of inspiring others with boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:88
verses.text: "As for Saul, he made havoc of the Church, entering into every house, and haling men and women committed them to prison".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:89
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:90
verses.text: ) Great was his frenzy: that he was alone, that he even entered into houses: for indeed he was ready to give his life for the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:91
verses.text: "Haling," it says, "men and women:" mark both the confidence, and the violence, and the frenzy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:92
verses.text: All that fell into his hands, he put to all manner of ill-treatment: for in consequence of the recent murder, he was become more daring.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:93
verses.text: "Therefore they that were scattered abroad went everywhere preaching the word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:94
verses.text: Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and preached Christ unto them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:95
verses.text: And the people with one accord gave heed unto those things which Philip spake, hearing and seeing the miracles which he did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:96
verses.text: For unclean spirits, crying with loud voice, came out of many that were possessed with them: and many taken with palsies, and that were lame, were healed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:97
verses.text: And there was great joy in that city.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:98
verses.text: But there was a certain man, called Simon, which before time in the same city used sorcery, and bewitched the people of Samaria".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:99
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:101
verses.text: ) Observe another trial, this affair of Simon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:102
verses.text: "Giving out," it says, "that he was himself some great one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:103
verses.text: To whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:104
verses.text: And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:105
verses.text: But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of God, and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:106
verses.text: Then Simon himself believed also: and when he was baptized, he continued with Philip, and wondered, beholding the miracles and signs which were done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:107
verses.text: Now when the Apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John: who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:108
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:109
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:110
verses.text: ) And (yet) great signs had been done: how then had they not received the Spirit? They had received the Spirit, namely, of remission of sins: but the Spirit of miracles they had not received.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:111
verses.text: "For as yet He was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:112
verses.text: Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:113
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:114
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:115
verses.text: ) For, to show that this was the case, and that it was the Spirit of miracles they had not received, observe how, having seen the result, Simon came and asked for this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:116
verses.text: "And when Simon saw that through laying on of the Apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:117
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:118
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:119
verses.text: )  "The persecution," say you, "gained strength".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:120
verses.text: True, but at that very time to men possessed before (by a hostile power) it brought deliverance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:121
verses.text: For it planted the miracles like a stronghold, in the heart of the enemy's country.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:122
verses.text: —Not even the death of Stephen quenched their rage, nay, increased it rather: it scattered wide the teachers, so that the greater became the discipleship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:123
verses.text: —"And there was joy".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:124
verses.text: And yet there had been "great lamentation:" true; but mark again the good—"Of a long time" was the malady, but this man brought them deliverance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:125
verses.text: —And how came he to baptize Simon also? Just as Christ chose Judas.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:126
verses.text: —And "beholding the signs" which he did, forasmuch as the others did not receive the (power of working) signs, he durst not ask for it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:127
verses.text: —How was it then that they did not strike him dead, as they did Ananias and Sapphira? Because even in the old times, he that gathered sticks (on the sabbath-day) was put to death as a warning to others (Num.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:128
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:129
verses.text: ) and in no other instance did any suffer the same fate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:130
verses.text: So too on the present occasion, "Peter said to him, Thy money perish, because thou hast imagined that the gift of God is to be purchased with money".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:131
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:132
verses.text: ) Why had not these received the Holy Ghost, when baptized? Either because Philip kept this honor for the Apostles; or, because he had not this gift (to impart); or, he was one of the Seven: which is rather to be said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:133
verses.text: Whence, I take it, this Philip was one of the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:134
verses.text: But observe; those went not forth: it was Providentially ordered that these should go forth and those be lacking, because of the Holy Ghost: for they had received power to work miracles, but not also to impart the Spirit to others: this was the prerogative of the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:135
verses.text: And observe (how they sent) the chief ones: not any others, but Peter and John.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:136
verses.text: "And when Simon," it says, "saw that through laying on of the Apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:137
verses.text: He would not have said, "And having seen," unless there had been some sensible manifestation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:138
verses.text: "Then laid they their hands on them," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:139
verses.text: Just as Paul also did, when they spake with tongues.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:140
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:141
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:142
verses.text: ) Observe the execrable conduct of Simon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:143
verses.text: "He offered money," with what object? And yet he did not see Peter doing this for money.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:144
verses.text: And it was not of ignorance that he acted thus; it was because he would tempt them, because he wished to get matter of accusation against them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:145
verses.text: And therefore also Peter says, "Thou hast no part nor lot in this matter, for thine heart is not right before God "because thou hast thought," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:146
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:147
verses.text: ) Once more he brings to light what was in the thoughts, because Simon thought to escape detection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:148
verses.text: "Repent therefore of this thy wickedness and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:149
verses.text: For I perceive the bond of inquity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:150
verses.text: Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:151
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:152
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:153
verses.text: ) Even this he did only formally, as words of course, when he ought to have wept and mourned as a penitent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:154
verses.text: "If perchance it may be forgiven thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:155
verses.text: Not as though it would not have been pardoned, had he wept, but this is the manner of the Prophet also, to denounce absolutely, (ἀπαγορεύειν) and not to say, "Howbeit, if thou do this, thy sin shall be forgiven," but that in any wise the punishment shall take effect.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:156
verses.text: (a) "Therefore they that were scattered abroad, went everywhere, preaching the word".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:157
verses.text: But I would have thee admire how even in a season of calamity they neglected not the preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:158
verses.text: "Hearing and seeing the miracles which he did".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:159
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:160
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:161
verses.text: ) Just as in the case of Moses by contrast (with the magicians) the miracles were evident miracles, so here also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:162
verses.text: There was magic, and so these signs were manifest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:163
verses.text: (b) "For unclean spirits came out of many that were possessed with them" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:164
verses.text: ); for this was a manifest miracle:—not as the magicians did: for the other (Simon), it is likely, bound (men with spells);—"and many," it says, "that were palsied and lame were healed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:165
verses.text: There was no deceit here: for it needed but that they should walk and work.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:166
verses.text: "And to him they all gave heed, saying, This (man) is the Power of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:167
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:168
verses.text: ) And that was fulfilled which was spoken by Christ, "There shall come false Christs and false Prophets in My name".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:169
verses.text: —(Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:170
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:171
verses.text: ) "And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:172
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:173
verses.text: ) (a) And yet there ought to have been not one demoniac there, seeing that of a long time he had been bewitching them with sorceries: but if there were many demoniacs, many palsied, these pretences were not truth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:174
verses.text: But Philip here by his word also won them over, discoursing concerning the kingdom of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:175
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:176
verses.text: ) "And Simon," it says, "being baptized, continued with Philip (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:177
verses.text: ): not for faith's sake, but in order that he might become such (as he).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:178
verses.text: (b) But why did they not correct him instantly? They were content with his condemning himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:179
verses.text: For this too belonged to their work of teaching (τἥς διδασκαλίας).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:180
verses.text: But when he had not power to resist, he plays the hypocrite, just as did the magicians, who said, "This is the finger of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:181
verses.text: And indeed that he might not be driven away again, therefore he "continued with Philip," and did not part from him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:182
verses.text: "And when the Apostles which were at Jerusalem," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:183
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:184
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:185
verses.text: ) See how many things are brought about by God's Providence through the death of Stephen! (a) "But they," it says, "having come down, prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost: for as yet He was fallen upon none of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:186
verses.text: Then laid they their hands upon them, and they received the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:187
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:188
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:189
verses.text: ) Seest thou that it was not to be done in any ordinary manner, but it needed great power to give the Holy Ghost? For it is not all one, to obtain remission of sins, and to receive such a power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:190
verses.text: (b) By degrees it is, that those receive the gift.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:191
verses.text: It was a twofold sign: both the giving to those, and the not giving to this man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:192
verses.text: Whereas then this man ought, on the contrary, to have asked to receive the Holy Ghost, he, because he cared not for this, asks power to give It to others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:193
verses.text: And yet those received not this power to give: but this man wished to be more illustrious than Philip, he being among the disciples! (a) "He offered them money".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:194
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:195
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:196
verses.text: ) What? had he seen the others doing this? had he seen Philip? Did he imagine they did not know with what mind he came to them? (b) "Thy money with thee to perdition" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:197
verses.text: ): since thou hast not used it as it ought to be used.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:198
verses.text: These are not words of imprecation, but of chastisement.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:199
verses.text: "To thee," he says, be it (to thee): being such.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:200
verses.text: As if one should say, Let it perish along with thy purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:201
verses.text: Hast thou so mean conceptions of the gift of God, that thou hast imagined it to be altogether a thing of man? It is not this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:202
verses.text: (a) Wherefore also Peter well calls the affair a gift: "Thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:203
verses.text: Dost thou observe how on all occasions they are clean from money? "For thine heart is not right in the sight of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:204
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:205
verses.text: ) Dost thou see how he does all of malice? To be simple, however, was the thing needed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:206
verses.text: (b) For had it been done with simplicity, he would have even welcomed his willing mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:207
verses.text: Seest thou that to have mean conceptions of great things is to sin doubly? Accordingly, two things he bids him: "Repent and pray, if haply the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:208
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:209
verses.text: ) Seest thou it was a wicked thought he had entertained? Therefore he says, "If haply it may be forgiven thee:" because he knew him to be incorrigible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:210
verses.text: (a) "For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:211
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:212
verses.text: ) Words of exceeding wrath!
