But otherwise he did not punish him: that faith may not thereafter be of compulsion; that the matter may not seem to be carried ruthlessly; that he may introduce the subject of repentance: or also, because it suffices for correction to have convicted him, to have told him what was in his heart, to have brought him to confess himself overcome (ὅτι ἐ& ·λω).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:213
verses.text: For that he says, "Pray ye for me," is a confession that he has done wrong.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:214
verses.text: Observe him, what a miscreant he is; when he was convicted, then he believed: when again he was convicted, then he became humble.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:215
verses.text: "Seeing his miracles," "he was amazed," and came over.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 43:216
verses.text: He thought to be able to escape detection: he thought the thing was an art: but when he had not power to defeat (ἑλεἵν) the Apostles,.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:1
verses.text: (b) Again, he fears the multitude, and is afraid to deny it; and yet he might have said, "I did not know: I did it in simplicity: but he was struck with dismay first by the former circumstance, that he was overcome (ὅτι ἐ& ·λω), by the miracles and secondly by this, that his thoughts are made manifest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:2
verses.text: Therefore he now takes himself a long wayoff, to Rome, thinking the Apostle would not soon come there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:3
verses.text: "And they, when they had testified, and preached the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:4
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:5
verses.text: ) "Testified," probably because of him (Simon), that they may not be deceived; that thenceforth they may be safe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:6
verses.text: "Having preached," it says, "the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:7
verses.text: Why do they go thither again where was the tyranny of the bad, where were those most bent upon killing them? Just as generals do in wars, they occupy that part of the scene of war which is most distressed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:8
verses.text: "And preached the Gospel in many villages of the Samaritans".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:9
verses.text: Observe them again, how they do not (προηγουμένως) of set purpose come to Samaria, but driven by stress of persecution, just as it was in the case of Christ; and how when the Apostles go thither, it is to men now believers, no longer Samaritans.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:10
verses.text: "But when the Apostles," it says, "which were at Jerusalem heard this, they sent unto them Peter and John.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:11
verses.text: Sent" them, again, to rid them of magic.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:12
verses.text: And besides, (the Lord) had given them a pattern at the time when the Samaritans believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:13
verses.text: "And in many villages," it says, "of the Samaritans, they preached the Gospel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:14
verses.text: (John iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:15
verses.text: ) Observe how actively employed even their journeys were, how they do nothing without a purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:16
verses.text: Such travels should we also make.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:17
verses.text: And why do I speak of travels? Many possess villages and lands, and give themselves no concern, nor make any account of this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:18
verses.text: That baths may be provided, their revenues increased, courts and buildings erected, for this they take plenty of pains: but for the husbandry of souls, not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:19
verses.text: When you see thorns—answer me—you cut them up, you burn, you utterly destroy them, to rid your land of the hurt thence arising.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:20
verses.text: And seest thou the laborers themselves overrun with thorns, and dost not cut them up, and art thou not afraid of the Owner Who shall call thee to account? For ought not each individual believer to build a Church, to get a Teacher, to cooperate (συναί· ρεσθαι) (with him), to make this above all his object, that all may be Christians? Say, how is it likely thy laborer should be a Christian, when he sees thee so regardless of his salvation? Thou canst not work miracles, and so convert (πεῖσαι) him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:21
verses.text: By the means which are in thy power, convert him; by kindness, by good offices, by gentleness, by courting (κολακεί& ·) him, by all other means.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:22
verses.text: Market-places, indeed, and baths, the most do provide; but no Churches: nay, sooner everything than this! Wherefore I beseech and implore, as a favor I entreat, yea as a law I lay it down, that there be no estate to be seen destitute of a Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:23
verses.text: Tell not me, There is one hard by; there is one in the neighboring properties; the expense is great, the income not great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:24
verses.text: If thou have anything to expend upon the poor, expend it there: better there than here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:25
verses.text: Maintain a Teacher, maintain a Deacon, and a sacerdotal body complete.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:26
verses.text: As by a bride, whether a wife whom thou takest, or a daughter whom thou givest in marriage, so act by the Church: give her a dowry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:27
verses.text: So shall thy estate be filled with blessing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:28
verses.text: For what shall not be there of all that is good? Is it a small thing, tell me, that thy wine-press should be blessed; a small thing, tell me, that of thy fruits God is the first to taste, and that the first fruits are there (with Him)? And then even for the peace of the laboring people this is profitable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:29
verses.text: Then as one whom they must respect, there will be the presbyter among them and this will contribute to the security of the estate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:30
verses.text: There will be constant prayers there through thee (infra, note , p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:31
verses.text: ) hymns and Communions through thee; the Oblation on each Lord's Day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:32
verses.text: For only consider what a praise it will be, that, whereas others have built splendid tombs, to have it said hereafter: "Such a one built this," thou hast reared Churches! Bethink thee that even until the coming of Christ thou shalt have thy reward, who hast reared up the altars of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:33
verses.text: Suppose an Emperor had ordered thee to build an house that he might lodge there, wouldest thou not have done everything to please him? And here now it is palace of Christ, the Church, the Church which thou buildest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:34
verses.text: Look not at the cost, but calculate the profit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:35
verses.text: Thy people yonder cultivate thy field: cultivate thou their souls: they bring to thee thy fruits, raise thou them to heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:36
verses.text: He that makes the beginning is the cause of all the rest: and thou wilt be the cause that the people are brought under Christian teaching (κατηχουμένων) both there, and in the neighboring estates.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:37
verses.text: Your baths do but make the peasants less hardy, your taverns give them a taste for luxury, and yet you provide these for credit's sake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:38
verses.text: Your markets and fairs, (πανηγύρεις) on the other hand, promote covetousness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:39
verses.text: But think now what a thing it would be to see a presbyter, the moving picture of Abraham, gray-headed, girded up, digging and working with his own hands? What more pleasant than such a field! Their virtue thrives.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:40
verses.text: No intemperance there, nay, it is driven away: no drunkenness and wantonness, nay, it is cast out: no vanity, nay, it is extinguished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:41
verses.text: All benevolent tempers shine out the brighter through the simplicity of manners.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:42
verses.text: How pleasant to go forth and enter into the House of God, and to know that one built it himself: to fling himself on his back in his litter, and after the bodily benefit of his pleasant airing, be present both at the evening and the morning hymns, have the priest as a guest at his table, in associating with him enjoy his benediction, see others also coming thither! This is a wall for his field, this its security.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:43
verses.text: This is the field of which it is said, "The smell of a full field which the Lord hath blessed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:44
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:45
verses.text: xxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:46
verses.text: ) If, even without this, the country is pleasant, because it is so quiet, so free from distraction of business, what will it not be when this is added to it? The country with a Church is like the Paradise of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:47
verses.text: No clamor there, no turmoil, no enemies at variance, no heresies: there you shall see all friends, holding the same doctrines in common.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:48
verses.text: The very quiet shall lead thee to higher views, and receiving thee thus prepared by philosophy, the presbyter shall give thee an excellent cure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:49
verses.text: For here, whatever we may speak, the noise of the market drives it all out: but there, what thou shalt hear, thou wilt keep fixed in thy mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:50
verses.text: Thou wilt be quite another man in the country through him: and moreover to the people there he will be director, he will watch over them both by his presence and by his influence in forming their manners.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:51
verses.text: And what, I ask, would be the cost? Make for a beginning a small house (ἐν τάξει ναοὕ) to serve as temple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:52
verses.text: Thy successor will build a porch, his successor will make other additions, and the whole shall be put to thy account.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:53
verses.text: Thou givest little, and receivest the reward for the whole.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:54
verses.text: At any rate, make a beginning: lay a foundation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:55
verses.text: Exhort one another, vie one with another in this matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:56
verses.text: But now, where there is straw and grain and such like to be stored, you make no difficulty of building: but for a place where the fruits of souls may be gathered in, we bestow not a thought; and the people are forced to go miles and miles, and to make long journeys, that they may get to Church! Think, how good it is, when with all quietness the priest presents himself in the Church, that he may draw near unto God, and say prayers for the village, day by day, and for its owner! Say, is it a small matter, that even in the Holy Oblations evermore thy name is included in the prayers, and that for the village day by day prayers are made unto God?—How greatly this profits thee for all else! It chances that certain (great) persons dwell in the neighborhood, and have overseers: now to thee, being poor, one of them will not deign even to pay a visit: but the presbyter, it is likely, he will invite, and make him sit at his table.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:57
verses.text: How much good results from this! The village will in the first place be free from all evil suspicion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:58
verses.text: None will charge it with murder, with theft: none will suspect anything of the kind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:59
verses.text: —They have also another comfort, if sickness befall, if death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:60
verses.text: —Then again the friendships formed there by people as they go side by side (to and from the Church) are not struck up at random and promiscuously: and the meetings there are far more pleasant than those which take place in marts and fairs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:61
verses.text: The people themselves also will be more respectable, because of their presbyter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:62
verses.text: How is it you hear that Jerusalem was had in honor in the old times above all other cities? Why was this? Because of the then prevailing religion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:63
verses.text: Therefore it is that where God is honored, there is nothing evil: as, on the contrary, where He is not honored, there is nothing good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:64
verses.text: It will be great security both with God and with men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:65
verses.text: Only, I beseech you, that ye be not remiss: only may you put your hand to this work.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:66
verses.text: For if he who brings out "the precious from the vile," shall be "as the mouth of God" (Jer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:67
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:68
verses.text: ); he who benefits and recovers so many souls, both that now are and that shall be even until the coming of Christ, what favor shall not that person reap from God! Raise thou a garrison against the devil: for that is what the Church is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:69
verses.text: Thence as from headquarters let the hands go forth to work: first let the people hold them up for prayers, and then go their way to work.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:70
verses.text: So shall there be vigor of body; so shall the tillage be abundant; so shall all evil be kept aloof.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:71
verses.text: It is not possible to represent in words the pleasure thence arising, until it be realized.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:72
verses.text: Look not to this, that it brings in no revenue: if thou do it at all in this spirit, then do it not at all; if thou account not the revenue thou gettest thence greater than from the whole estate beside; if thou be not thus affected, then let it alone; if thou do not account this work to stand thee more in stead than any work beside.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:73
verses.text: What can be greater than this revenue, the gathering in of souls into the threshing-floor which is in heaven! Alas, that ye know not how much it is, to gain souls! Hear what Christ says to Peter, "Feed My sheep".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:74
verses.text: (John xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:75
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:76
verses.text: ) If, seeing the emperor's sheep, or herd of horses, by reason of having no fold or stable, exposed to depredation, thou wert to take them in hand, and build a fold or stables, or also provide a shepherd or herdsman to take charge of them, what would not the emperor do for thee in return? Now, thou gatherest the flock of Christ, and puttest a shepherd over them, and thinkest thou it is no great gain thou art earning? But, if for offending even one, a man shall incur so great a punishment, how can he that saves so many, ever be punished? What sin will he have thenceforth? for, though he have it, does not this blot it out? From the punishment threatened to him that offends, learn the reward of him that saves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:77
verses.text: Were not the salvation of even one soul a matter of great importance, to offend would not move God to so great anger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:78
verses.text: Knowing these things, let us apply ourselves forthwith to this spiritual work.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:79
verses.text: And let each invite me, and we will together help to the best of our ability.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:80
verses.text: If there be three joint-owners, let them do it by each bearing his part: if but one, he will induce the others also that are near.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 46:81
verses.text: Only be earnest to effect this, I beseech you, that in every way being well-pleasing unto God, we may attain unto the eternal blessings, by the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, dominion, and honor, now and ever world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:1
verses.text: Homily XIX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:2
verses.text: Acts VIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:3
verses.text: ,  "And the Angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, arise and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:4
verses.text: And he arose and went".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:5
verses.text: It seems to me, this (Philip) was one of the seven; for from Jerusalem he would not have gone southwards, but to the north; but from Samaria it was "towards the south.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:6
verses.text: The same is desert:" so that there is no fear of an attack from the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:7
verses.text: And he did not ask, Wherefore? but "arose and went.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:8
verses.text: And, behold," it says, "a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:9
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:10
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:11
verses.text: ) High encomiums for the man, that he, residing in Ethiopia and beset with so much business, and when there was no festival going on, and living in that superstitious city, came "to Jerusalem for to worship".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:12
verses.text: Great also is his studiousness, that even "sitting in his chariot he read.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:13
verses.text: And," it says, "the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:14
verses.text: And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him reading the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:16
verses.text: ) Observe again his piety; that though he did not understand, he read, and then after reading, examines.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:17
verses.text: "And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:18
verses.text: The place of the Scripture which he read was this, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened He not His mouth: in His humiliation His judgment was taken away: and who shall declare His generation? for His life is taken from the earth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:19
verses.text: And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man? Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same Scripture, and preached unto him Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:20
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:22
verses.text: ) Observe how it is Providentially ordered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:23
verses.text: First he reads and does not understand; then he reads the very text in which was the Passion and the Resurrection and the Gift.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:24
verses.text: "And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:25
verses.text: ) Mark the eager desire, mark the exact knowledge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:26
verses.text: "And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:27
verses.text: And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:30
verses.text: ) But why did the Spirit of the Lord bear him away? (Hereby) the occurrence was shown to be more wonderful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:31
verses.text: Even then, the eunuch did not know him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:32
verses.text: Consequently this was done, that Philip might afterwards be a subject of wonder to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:33
verses.text: "For," it says, "he went on his way rejoicing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:34
verses.text: But Philip was found at Azotus: and passing through he preached in all the cities, till he came to Caesarea".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:36
verses.text: ) This (Philip, therefore) was one of the seven; for there in fact he is afterwards found at Caesarea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:37
verses.text: It was well and expedient therefore that the Spirit caught Philip away; else the eunuch would have desired to go with him, and Philip would have grieved him by declining to comply with his request, the time being not yet come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:38
verses.text: (a) But at the same time here was an encouraging assurance for them that they shall also prevail over the heathen: for indeed the high character (τὸ ἀξιόπιστον) of the (first) believers was enough to move them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:39
verses.text: If however the eunuch had stayed there, what fault could have been found? But he knew him not: for this is why it says, "he went on his way rejoicing:" so that had he known him, he would not have been (so) delighted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:40
verses.text: "And the Angel of the Lord," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:41
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:42
verses.text: ) (b) See Angels assisting the preaching, and not themselves preaching, but calling these (to the work).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:43
verses.text: But the wonderful nature of the occurrence is shown also by this: that what of old was rare, and hardly done, here takes place with ease, and see with what frequency! (c) "An eunuch," it says, "a man of great authority, under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:44
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:45
verses.text: ) For there women bore rule of old, and this was the law among them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:46
verses.text: Philip did not yet know for whose sake he had come into the desert: (d) but what was there to hinder his learning all (these particulars) accurately, while in the chariot? "Was reading the prophet Esaias".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:48
verses.text: ) For the road was desert, and there was no display in the matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:49
verses.text: Observe also at what time: in the most violent heat (of the day).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:50
verses.text: (e) "And the Spirit said unto him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:52
verses.text: ) Not now the Angel but the Spirit urges him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:53
verses.text: Why is this? "Then," the vision took place, in grosser form, through the Angel, for this is for them that are more of the body, but the Spirit is for the more spiritual.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:54
verses.text: And how did He speak to him? Of course, suggested it to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:55
verses.text: Why does not the Angel appear to the other, and bring him to Philip? Because it is likely he would not have been persuaded, but rather terrified.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:56
verses.text: Observe the wisdom of Philip: he did not accuse him, not say, "I know these things exactly:" did not pay court to him, and say, "Blessed art thou that readest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:57
verses.text: But mark his speech, how far it is from harshness alike and from adulation; the speech rather of a kind and friendly man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:58
verses.text: "Understandest thou what thou readest?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:59
verses.text: ) For it was needful that he should himself ask, himself have a longing desire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:60
verses.text: He plainly intimates, that he knows that the other knew nothing: and says, "Understandest thou what thou readest?" at the same time he shows him that great was the treasure that lay therein.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:61
verses.text: It tells well also, that the eunuch looked not to the outward appearance (σχἥμα) (of the man), said not, "Who art thou?" did not chide, not give himself airs, not say that he did know.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:62
verses.text: On the contrary, he confesses his ignorance: wherefore also he learns.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:63
verses.text: He shows his hurt to the physician: sees at a glance, that he both knows the matter, and is willing to teach.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:64
verses.text: Look how free he is from haughtiness; the outward appearance announced nothing splendid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:65
verses.text: So desirous was he of learning, and gave heed to his words; and that saying, "He that seeketh, findeth," (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:66
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:67
verses.text: ) was fulfilled in him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:68
verses.text: "And," it says, "he besought Philip, that he would come up and sit with him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:69
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:70
verses.text: ) Do you mark the eagerness, the longing desire? But should any say he ought to have waited for Philip (to speak), (the answer is), he does not know what is the matter: he could not in the least tell what the other was going to say to him, but supposed merely that he was about to receive some (lesson of) prophecy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:71
verses.text: And moreover, this was more respectful, that he did not draw him into his chariot, but besought him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:72
verses.text: "And Philip," we have read, "ran to him, and heard him reading;" even the fact of his running, showed that he wished to say (something).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:73
verses.text: "And the place," it says, "of the Scripture which he read was this: As a sheep He was led to the slaughter".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:74
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:75
verses.text: ) And this circumstance, also, is a token of his elevated mind, (φιλοσοφίας) that he had in hand this prophet, who is more sublime than all others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:76
verses.text: Philip does not relate matters to him just as it might happen, but quietly: nay, does not say anything until he is questioned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:77
verses.text: Both in the former instance he prayed him, and so he does now, saying, "I pray thee of whom speaketh the prophet this?" That he should at all know either that the Prophets speak in different ways about different persons, or that they speak of themselves in another person—the question betokens a very thoughtful mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:78
verses.text: Let us be put to shame, both poor and rich, by this eunuch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:79
verses.text: Then, it says, "they came to a certain water, and he said, Lo, here is water".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:80
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:81
verses.text: ) Again, of his own accord he requests, saying, "What doth hinder me to be baptized?" And see again his modesty: he does not say, Baptize me, neither does he hold his peace; but he utters somewhat midway betwixt strong desire and reverent fear, saying, "What doth hinder me?" Do you observe that he has the doctrines (of faith) perfect? For indeed the Prophet had the whole, Incarnation, Passion, Resurrection, Ascension, Judgment to come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:82
verses.text: And if he shows exceeding earnestness of desire, do not marvel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:83
verses.text: Be ashamed, all ye as many as are unbaptized.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:84
verses.text: "And," it says, "he commanded the chariot to stand still".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:85
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:86
verses.text: ) He spoke, and gave the order at the same moment, before hearing (Philip's answer).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:87
verses.text: "And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip;" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:88
verses.text: ) in order that the occurrence might be shown to be of God; that he might not consider it to be merely man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:89
verses.text: "And he went," it says, "on his way rejoicing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:90
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:91
verses.text: , note.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:92
verses.text: ) This hints, that he would have been grieved had he known: for the greatness of his joy, having had the Spirit also vouchsafed to him, he did not even see things present—"But Philip was found at Azotus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:93
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:94
verses.text: ) Great was the gain to Philip also:—that which he heard concerning the Prophets, concerning Habakkuk, concerning Ezekiel, and the rest, he saw done in his own person.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:95
verses.text: (Bel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:96
verses.text: & Dr.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:97
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:98
verses.text: ; Ez.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:99
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:100
verses.text: ) Thence it appears that he went a long distance, seeing he "was found at Azotus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:101
verses.text: (The Spirit) set him there, where he was thenceforth to preach: "And passing through, he preached in all the cities, until he came to Caesarea".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:102
verses.text: "And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest, and desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:103
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:104
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:105
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:106
verses.text: ) He fitly mentions Paul's zeal, and shows that in the very midst of his zeal he is drawn.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:107
verses.text: "Yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter," and not yet sated with the murder of Stephen, he was not yet glutted with the persecution of the Church, and the dispersion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:108
verses.text: Lo, this was fulfilled which was spoken by Christ, that "they which kill you shall think they offer worship to God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:109
verses.text: (John xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:110
verses.text: ) He then in this wise did it, not as the Jews: God forbid! For that he did it through zeal, is manifest from his going abroad even to strange cities: whereas they would not have cared even for those in Jerusalem; they were for one thing only, to enjoy honor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:111
verses.text: But why went he to Damascus? It was a great city, a royal city: he was afraid lest that should be preoccupied.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:112
verses.text: And observe his strong desire and ardor (and), how strictly according to the Law he went to work: he goes not to the governor, but "to the priest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:113
verses.text: That if he found any of this way:" for so the believers were called, probably because of their taking the direct way that leads to heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:114
verses.text: And why did he not receive authority to have them punished there, but brings them to Jerusalem! He did these things here with more authority.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:115
verses.text: And mark on what a peril he casts himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:116
verses.text: He was not afraid lest he should take any harm, but (yet) he took others also with him, "that if," it says, "he found any of this way, whether they were men or women"—Oh, the ruthlessness!—"he might bring them bound".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:117
verses.text: By this journey of his, he wished to show them all (how he would act): so far were they from being earnest in this matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:118
verses.text: Observe him also casting (people) into prison before this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:119
verses.text: The others therefore did not prevail: but this man did prevail, by reason of his ardent mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:120
verses.text: "And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven: and he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:121
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:122
verses.text: ) Why not in Jerusalem? why not in Damascus? That there might be no opening for different persons to relate the occurrence in different ways, but that he alone should be the authentic narrator (ἀξιόπιστος), he that went for this purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:123
verses.text: In fact, he says this both in his oration on the stairs, and when pleading before Agrippa.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:124
verses.text: "Fell to the earth": (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:125
verses.text: xxii, : xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:126
verses.text: ) for excess of light is wont to shock, because the eyes have their measure: it is said also that excess of sound makes people deaf and stunned (as in a fit) (ἀποπλἥγας).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:127
verses.text: But him it only blinded, and extinguished his passion by fear, so that he should hear what was spoken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:128
verses.text: "Saul, Saul," saith He, "why persecutest thou me?" And He tells him nothing: does not say, Believe, nor anything whatever of the kind: but expostulates with him, all but saying, What wrong, great or small, hast thou suffered from Me, that thou doest these things? "And he said, Who art Thou Lord?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:129
verses.text: ) thus in the first place confessing himself His servant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:130
verses.text: "And the Lord said, I am Jesus, whom thou persecutest:" think not thy warring is with men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:131
verses.text: And they which were with him heard the voice of Paul, but saw no person to whom he answered—for (the Lord) suffered them to be hearers of what was less important.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:132
verses.text: Had they heard the other Voice, they would not have believed; but perceiving Paul answering (some person), they marvelled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:133
verses.text: "But arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:134
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:135
verses.text: ) Observe, how He does not immediately add all, but first softens his mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:136
verses.text: In the same way He called the disciples also a second time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:137
verses.text: "It shall be told thee," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:138
verses.text: : He gives him good hopes, and (intimates) that he shall recover his sight also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:139
verses.text: "And the men which journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:140
verses.text: And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:141
verses.text: , ):—the spoils of the devil (τὰ σκεύη αὐτοὕ), "his goods" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:142
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:143
verses.text: ), as from some city, yea, some metropolis which has been taken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:144
verses.text: And the wonder of it is, the enemies and foes themselves brought him in, in the sight of all! "And for three days he neither did eat nor drink, being blinded".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:145
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:146
verses.text: ) What could equal this? To compensate the discouragement in the matter of Stephen, here is encouragement, in the bringing in of Paul: though that sadness had its consolation in the fact of Stephen's making such an end, yet it also received this further consolation: moreover, the bringing in of the villages of the Samaritans afforded very great comfort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:147
verses.text: —But why did this take place not at the very first, but after these things? That it might be shown that Christ was indeed risen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:148
verses.text: This furious assailant of Christ, the man who would not believe in His death and resurrection, the persecutor of His disciples, how should this man have become a believer, had not the power of His resurrection been great indeed? Be it so, that the other Apostles favored (His pretensions): what say you to this man? Why then not immediately after His resurrection? That his hostility might be more clearly shown as open war.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:149
verses.text: The man who is so frantic as even to shed blood and cast men into prisons, all at once believes! It was not enough that he had never been in Christ's company: the believers must be warred upon by him with vehement hostility: he left to none the possibility of going beyond him in fury: none of them all could be so violent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:150
verses.text: But when he was blinded, then he saw the proofs of His sovereignty and loving kindness: then he answers, "Lord, what wilt Thou have me to do?" that none may say that he played the hypocrite, he that was even eager for blood, and went to the priests, and flung himself upon such dangers, in persecuting and bringing to punishment even them that were in foreign parts—under these circumstances he now acknowledges His sovereignty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:151
verses.text: And why was he shone upon by that light not within the city, but before it? The many would not have believed, since even there (at Jerusalem when the people heard the voice which came from above, they said that "it thundered" (John xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:152
verses.text: , supra, note , p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:153
verses.text: ); but this man was authority enough in reporting what was his own affair.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:154
verses.text: And bound he was brought in, though not with bonds upon him: and they drew him, who had expected to draw the others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:155
verses.text: "And he eat not, neither drank:" he condemned himself for the past, he confessed, prayed, besought God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:156
verses.text: But should any say, This was the effect of compulsion: (we answer) The same thing happened to Elymas: then how came it that he was not changed? (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:157
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:158
verses.text: de Laud.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:159
verses.text: Pauli Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:160
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:161
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:162
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:163
verses.text: p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:164
verses.text: ) What (evidence) could be more compulsory than the earthquake at the Resurrection, the report of the soldiers, the other miracles, the seeing Himself risen? But these things do not compel (belief) they are calculated to teach (it) (οὐκ ἀναγκαστικὰ ἀλλὰ διδακτικά).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:165
verses.text: Why did not the Jews believe when they were told of these things? That he spoke truth was manifest: for he would not have been changed, had this not happened; so that all were bound to believe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:166
verses.text: He was not inferior to them that preached the Resurrection, and was more credible, by being all at once converted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:167
verses.text: He had no intercourse with any of the believers; it was at Damascus that he was converted, or rather before he came to Damascus that this happened to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:168
verses.text: I ask the Jew: Say, by what was Paul converted? He saw so many signs, and was not converted: his teacher (Gamaliel, supra, p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:169
verses.text: , note ) was converted, and he remained unconverted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:170
verses.text: Who convinced him—and not only convinced, but all at once inspired him with such ardent zeal? Wherefore was it, that he wished even to go into hell itself for Christ's sake? The truth of the facts is manifest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:171
verses.text: But, as I said, for the present let us take shame to ourselves (when we think of) the eunuch, both in his baptism and his reading.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:172
verses.text: Do ye mark how he was in a station of great authority, how he was in possession of wealth, and even on his journey allowed himself no rest? What must he have been at home, in his leisure hours, this man who rested not even on his travels? What must he have been at night? Ye that are in stations of dignity, hear: imitate his freedom from pride, (de Lazaro, Conc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:173
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:174
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:175
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:176
verses.text: p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:177
verses.text: c) his piety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:178
verses.text: Though about to return home, he did not say to himself: "I am going back to my country, there let me receive baptism;" those cold words which most men use! No need had he of signs, no need of miracles: from the Prophet merely, he believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:179
verses.text: (b) But why is it (so ordered) that he sees (Philip) not before he goes to Jerusalem, but after he has been there? It was not meet that he should see the Apostles under persecution.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:180
verses.text: Because he was yet weak, the Prophet was not easy; (but yet the Prophet) catechized him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:181
verses.text: For even now, if any of you would apply himself to the study of the Prophets, he would need no miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:182
verses.text: And, if you please, let us take in hand the prophecy itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:183
verses.text: "He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened He not His mouth: in His humiliation His judgment was taken away: and who shall declare His generation? for His life is taken from the earth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:184
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:185
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:186
verses.text: ) It is likely he had heard that He was crucified, and now he learns, that "His life is taken away from the earth," and the rest that "He did no sin, nor deceit in His mouth:" that He prevailed to save others also: and who He is, Whose generation is unutterable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:187
verses.text: It is likely he had seen the riven rocks there (on the spot), and (had heard) how the veil was rent, and how there was darkness, and so forth: and all these things Philip mentioned, merely taking his text from the Prophet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:188
verses.text: It is a great thing, this reading of the Scriptures! That was fulfilled which was spoken by Moses, "Sitting, lying down, rising up, and walking, remember the Lord thy God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:189
verses.text: (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:190
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:191
verses.text: ) For the roads, especially when they are lonely, give us opportunity for reflection, there being none to disturb us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:192
verses.text: Both this man is on the road and Paul on the road: howbeit the latter no man draws, but Christ alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:193
verses.text: This was too great a work for the Apostles: and, greater still, in that, the Apostles being at Jerusalem, and no person of authority at Damascus, he nevertheless returned thence converted: yet those at Damascus knew that he did not come from Jerusalem converted, for he brought letters, that he might put the believers in bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:194
verses.text: Like a consummate Physician, when the fever was at its height, Christ brought help to him: for it was needful that he should be quelled in the midst of his frenzy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:195
verses.text: For then most of all would he be brought down, and condemn himself as one guilty of dreadful audacity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:196
verses.text: (a) For these things Paul deplores himself, saying, "Howbeit for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first Jesus Christ might show all His long suffering".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:197
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:198
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:199
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:200
verses.text: ) Verily one has reason to admire this eunuch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:201
verses.text: He did not see Christ, he saw no miracle: he beheld Jerusalem standing yet entire (συνεστὥτα): he believed Philip.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:202
verses.text: How came he to behave thus? His soul was earnest (μεμεριμνημένη).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:203
verses.text: Yet the thief (on the cross) had seen miracles: the wise men had seen a star; but this man, nothing of the kind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:204
verses.text: So great a thing is the careful reading of the Scriptures! What of Paul then! did he not study the law? But he, it seems to me, was specially reserved, for the purpose which I have already mentioned by anticipation, because Christ would fain draw to Himself the Jews by inducements from every quarter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:205
verses.text: For had they been in their right mind, nothing was so likely to do them good as this; for this, more than miracles and all else, was calculated to attract them: as, on the other hand, nothing is so apt to prove a stumbling block to men of duller minds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:206
verses.text: See then how, after the Apostle, we have God also doing miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:207
verses.text: They accused the Apostles after these miracles of theirs; they cast them into prison: see thereupon God doing the miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:208
verses.text: For instance, the bringing them out of prison, was His miracle: the bringing Philip, His miracle: the bringing Paul over, was His.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:209
verses.text: —Observe in what way Paul is honored, in what way the eunuch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:210
verses.text: There, Christ appears, probably because of his hardness, and because Ananias would not (else) have been persuaded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:211
verses.text: Conversant with these wonders, let us show ourselves worthy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:212
verses.text: But many in these times, even when they come to church, do not know what is read; whereas the eunuch, even in public (ἐπ᾽ ἀγορἅς) and riding in his chariot, applied himself to the reading of the Scriptures.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:213
verses.text: Not so you: none takes the Bible in hand: nay, everything rather than the Bible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:214
verses.text: Say, what are the Scriptures for? For as much as in you lies, it is all undone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:215
verses.text: What is the Church for? Tie up the Bibles: perhaps the judgment would not be such, not such the punishment: if one were to bury them in dung, that he might not hear them, he would not so insult them as you do now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:216
verses.text: For say, what is the insult there? That the man has buried them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:217
verses.text: And what here? That we do not hear them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:218
verses.text: Say, when is a person most insulted—when he is silent, and one makes no answer, or, when he does speak (and is unheeded)? So that the insult is greater in the present case, when He does speak and thou wilt not hear: greater the contempt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:219
verses.text: "Speak not to us" (Is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:220
verses.text: xxx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:221
verses.text: ), we read, they said of old to the Prophets: but ye do worse, saying, Speak: we will not do.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:222
verses.text: For there they turned them away that they should not even speak, as feeling that from the voice itself they got some sort of awe and obligation; whereas you, in the excess of your contempt, do not even this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:223
verses.text: Believe me, if you stopped our mouths by putting your hands over them, the insult would not be so great as it is now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:224
verses.text: For say, whether shows greater contempt, he that hears, even when hindering by this action, or, he that will not even hear? Say—if we shall look at it as a case of an insult offered—suppose one person to check the party insulting him, and to stop his mouth, as being hurt by the insults, and another person to show no concern, but pretend not even to hear them: whether will show most contempt? Would you not say the latter? For the former shows that he feels himself hit: the latter all but stops the mouth of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:225
verses.text: Did ye shudder at what was said? Why, the mouth by which God speaks, is the mouth of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:226
verses.text: Just as our mouth is the mouth of our soul, though the soul has no mouth, so the mouth of the Prophets is the mouth of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:227
verses.text: Hear, and shudder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:228
verses.text: There, common (to the whole congregation) stands the deacon crying aloud, and saying, "Let us attend to the reading".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:229
verses.text: It is the common voice of the whole Church, the voice which he utters, and yet none does attend.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:230
verses.text: After him begins the Reader, "The Prophecy of Esaias," and still none attends, although Prophecy has nothing of man in it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:231
verses.text: Then after this, he says, "Thus saith the Lord," and still none attends.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:232
verses.text: Then after this punishments and vengeances, and still even then none attends.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:233
verses.text: But what is the common excuse? "It is always the same things over again".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:234
verses.text: This it is most of all, that ruins you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:235
verses.text: Suppose you knew the things, even so you certainly ought not to turn away: since in the theatres also, is it not always the same things acted over again, and still you take no disgust? How dare you talk about "the same things," you who know not so much as the names of the Prophets? Are you not ashamed to say, that this is why you do not listen, because it is "the same things over again," while you do not know the names of those who are read, and this, though always hearing the same things? You have yourself confessed that the same things are said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:236
verses.text: Were I to say this as a reason for finding fault with you, you would need to have recourse to quite a different excuse, instead of this which is the very thing you find fault with.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:237
verses.text: —Do not you exhort your son? Now if he should say, "Always the same things!" would not you count it an insult? It would be time enough to talk of "the same things," when we both knew the things, and exhibited them in our practice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:238
verses.text: Or rather, even then, the reading of them would not be superfluous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:239
verses.text: What equal to Timothy? tell me that: and yet to him says Paul, "Give attention to reading, to exhortation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:240
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:241
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:242
verses.text: ) For it is not possible, I say not possible, ever to exhaust the mind of the Scriptures.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:243
verses.text: It is a well which has no bottom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:244
verses.text: "I said," saith the Preacher, "I am become wise: and then it departed from me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:245
verses.text: —(Eccles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:246
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:247
verses.text: ) Shall I show you that the things are not "the same?" How many persons, do you suppose, have spoken upon the Gospels? And yet all have spoken in a way which was new and fresh.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:248
verses.text: For the more one dwells on them, the more insight does he get, the more does he behold the pure light.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:249
verses.text: Look, what a number of things I am going to speak of:—say, what is narrative? what is prophecy? what is parable? what is type? what is allegory? what is symbol? what are Gospels? Answer me only to this one point, which is plain: why are they called Gospels, "good tidings?" And yet ye have often heard that good news ought to have nothing sad in it: yet this "good news" has abundance of sadness in it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:250
verses.text: "Their fire," it saith, "shall never be quenched: their worm shall not die:" (Mark ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:251
verses.text: ) "Shall appoint his portion," it saith, "with the hypocrites," with them that are "cut asunder: then shall He say, I know you not: Depart from Me, ye that work iniquity".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:252
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:253
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:254
verses.text: ; vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:255
verses.text: ) Surely, we do not deceive ourselves, when we imagine that we tell you in your own mother-tongue (῾Ελληνιστί) these good tidings? You look downcast; you are stunned; you are struck all of a heap, unable to hold up your heads.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:256
verses.text: "Good news" should have nothing in it of a duty to be done, but rather should counsel what is good: whereas these "Gospels" have endless duties to be done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:257
verses.text: And again, to mention other things, as for instance, Except a man hate father and mother, he is not worthy of Me" (Luke xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:258
verses.text: ): and "I am not come to bring peace upon earth, but a sword" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:259
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:260
verses.text: ; Luke xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:261
verses.text: ): and "In the world ye shall have tribulation—(John xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:262
verses.text: ) excellent good tidings these, are they not! For good news is such as this—"You shall have this and that good thing:" as in common life men say one to another, "What shall I have for my good news? Your father is coming, or, your mother:" he does not say, "You must do this or that".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:263
verses.text: —Again, tell me, how do the Gospels differ from the Prophets? Why are not the Prophecies also called Gospels, good tidings? For they tell the same things: for instance, "The lame shall leap as an hart".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:264
verses.text: (Is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:265
verses.text: xxxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:266
verses.text: ) "The Lord shall give the word to them that preach the Gospel" (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:267
verses.text: lxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:268
verses.text: ): and, "A new heaven and a new earth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:269
verses.text: (Is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:270
verses.text: lxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:271
verses.text: ) Why are not those also called Gospels? But if, while you do not so much as know what "Gospels" mean, you so despise the reading of the Scriptures, what shall I say to you?—Let me speak of something else.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:272
verses.text: Why four Gospels? why not, ten? why not twenty? If "many have taken in hand to set forth a narrative" (Luke i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:273
verses.text: ), why not one person? Why they that were disciples (i-e: Apostles)? why they that were not disciples? But why any Scriptures at all? And yet, on the contrary, the Old Testament says, "I will give you a New Testament".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:274
verses.text: (Jer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:275
verses.text: xxxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:276
verses.text: ) Where are they that say, "Always the same things?" If ye knew these, that, though a man should live thousands of years, they are not "the same things," ye would not say this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:277
verses.text: Believe me, I will not tell you the answers to any of these questions; not in private, not in public: only, if any find them out, I will nod assent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:278
verses.text: For this is the way we have made you good-for-nothing, by always telling you the things ready to your hands, and not refusing when we ought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:279
verses.text: Look, you have questions enough: consider them, tell me the reasons.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:280
verses.text: Why Gospels? Why not Prophecies? Why duties, to be done, in the Gospels? If one is at a loss, let another seek the answer, and contribute each to the others from what he has: but now we will hold our peace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:281
verses.text: For if what has been spoken has done you no good, much less would it, should we add more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:282
verses.text: We only pour water into a vessel full of holes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:283
verses.text: And the punishment too is all the greater for you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:284
verses.text: Therefore, we will hold our peace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:285
verses.text: Which that we may not have to do, it rests with yourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 47:286
verses.text: For if we shall see your diligence, perhaps we will again speak, that both ye may be more approved, and we may rejoice over you, in all things giving glory to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ: to Him be glory and dominion now and ever, and world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:1
verses.text: Homily XX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:2
verses.text: Acts IX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:3
verses.text: ,  "And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:4
verses.text: And he said, Behold, I am here, Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:5
verses.text: And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth, and hath seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in, and putting his hand on him, that he might receive his sight".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:6
verses.text: What may be the reason that He neither drew any one of high authority and importance, nor caused such to be forthcoming for the purpose of instructing Paul? It was, because it was not meet that he should be induced by men, but only by Christ Himself: as in fact this man taught him nothing, but merely baptized him; for, as soon as baptized (φωτισθείς), he was to draw upon himself the grace of the Spirit, by his zeal and exceeding earnestness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:7
verses.text: And that Ananias was no very distinguished person, is plain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:8
verses.text: For, "the Lord," it says, "spake unto him in a vision, and Ananias answered and said, Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to Thy saints at Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:9
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:10
verses.text: ) For if he spoke in objection to Him, much more would he have done so, had He sent an Angel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:11
verses.text: And this is why, in the former instance, neither is Philip told what the matter is; but he sees the Angel, and then the Spirit bids him go near to the chariot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:12
verses.text: But observe here how the Lord relieves him of his fear: "He is blind," saith He, "and prayeth, and art thou afraid?" In the same way Moses also is afraid: so that the words betokened that he was afraid, and shrunk from the task, not that he did not believe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:13
verses.text: He said," have heard from many concerning this man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:14
verses.text: What sayest thou? God speaketh, and thou hesitatest? They did not yet well know the power of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:15
verses.text: "And here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on Thy name".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:16
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:17
verses.text: ) How was that known? It is likely that they, being in fear, made minute enquiries.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:18
verses.text: He does not say this, as thinking that Christ does not know the fact, but, "such being the case, how," says he, "can these things be?" As in fact those (in the Gospel) say, "Who can be saved?"—(Mark x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:19
verses.text: ) This is done, in order that Paul may believe him that shall come to him: "he hath seen in a vision:" it hath showed him beforehand: "he prayeth," saith (the Lord): fear not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:20
verses.text: And observe, He speaks not to him of the success achieved: teaching us not to speak of our achievements.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:21
verses.text: And, though He saw him afraid, for all this He said it not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:22
verses.text: "Thou shalt not be disbelieved:" "he hath seen," saith He, "in a vision a man (named) Ananias:" for this is why it was "in a vision," namely, because he was blind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:23
verses.text: And not even the exceeding wonderfulness of the thing took possession of the disciple's mind, so greatly was he afraid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:24
verses.text: But observe: Paul being blind, in this way He restored to sight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:25
verses.text: "But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto Me, to bear My name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: for I will show him how great things he must suffer for My name's sake".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:28
verses.text: ) "Not only," saith He, "shall he be a believer, but even a teacher, and great boldness shall he show: 'before Gentiles and kings'—such shall be the spread of the doctrine!—that just as He astonished (him) by the former, so He may (startle him even more) by the latter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:29
verses.text: "And Ananias went, and entered into the house, and laid his hands upon him, and said, Brother Saul"—he straightway addresses him as a friend by that name—"Jesus, Who appeared unto thee in the way in which thou camest"—and yet Christ had not told him this, but he learnt it from the Spirit—"hath sent me unto thee, that thou mayest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:30
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:31
verses.text: ) As he said this, he laid his hands upon him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:32
verses.text: "And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:34
verses.text: ) Some say this was a sign of his blindness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:35
verses.text: Why did he not blind his eyes (entirely)? This was more wonderful, that, with his eyes open, he did not see: (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:36
verses.text: ) which was just his case in respect of the Law, until the Name of Jesus was put on him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:37
verses.text: "And he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:38
verses.text: And having taken food, he recovered strength".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:40
verses.text: ) He was faint, therefore, both from his journey and from his fear; both from hunger, and from dejection of mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:41
verses.text: Wishing therefore to deepen his dejection, He made the man blind until the coming of Ananias: and, that he might not imagine the blindness to be (only) fancy, this is the reason of the scales.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:42
verses.text: He needed no other teaching: that which had befallen was made teaching (to him).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:43
verses.text: "And he was with the disciples which were at Damascus certain days.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:44
verses.text: And straightway in the synagogues he preached Jesus, that He is the Son of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:46
verses.text: ) See, straightway he was a teacher in the synagogues.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:47
verses.text: He was not ashamed of the change, was not afraid while the very things in which he was glorious afore-time, the same he destroyed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:48
verses.text: Even from his first appearance on the stage here was a man, death-dealing, ready for deeds of blood: seest thou what a manifest sign (was here)? And with this very thing, he put all in fear: for, said they, Hither also is he come for this very thing.
