verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:49
verses.text: "But all that heard him were amazed, and said: Is not this he that destroyed them which called on this name in Jerusalem, and came hither for that intent, that he might bring them bound unto the chief priests? But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews which dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:50
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:52
verses.text: ) As one learned in the Law, he stopped their mouths, and suffered them not to speak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:53
verses.text: They thought they were rid of disputation in such matters, in getting rid of Stephen, and they found another, more vehement than Stephen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:54
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:55
verses.text: ) But let us look at what relates to Ananias.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:56
verses.text: The Lord said not to him, Converse with him, and catechize him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:57
verses.text: For if, when He said, "He prayeth, and hath seen a man laying his hands upon him," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:59
verses.text: ) He did not persuade him, much less had He said this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:60
verses.text: So that he shall not disbelieve thee, "he hath seen in a vision".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:61
verses.text: Observe how in the former instance neither is Philip told all immediately.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:62
verses.text: Fear not, He saith: "for this man is a chosen vessel for Me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:63
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:64
verses.text: ) He more than sufficiently released him of his fear, if the case be so that this man shall be so zealous in our cause, as even to suffer many things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:65
verses.text: And justly he is called "a vessel" (or, instrument)—for reason shows that evil is not a physical quality: "a vessel of election" (or, chosen instrument), He saith; for we choose that which is approved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:66
verses.text: And let not any imagine, that (Ananias) speaks in unbelief of what was told him, as imagining that Christ was deceived: far from it! but affrighted and trembling, he did not even attend to what was said, at hearing the name of Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:67
verses.text: Moreover, the Lord does not tell that He has blinded him: at the mention of his name fear had prepossessed his soul: "see," he says, "to whom Thou art betraying me: 'and hither for this very purpose is he come, to bind all that call upon Thy Name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:68
verses.text: ' I fear, lest he take me to Jerusalem: why dost Thou cast me into the mouth of the lion?" He is terrified, even while he speaks these words; that from every quarter we may learn the energetic character (ἀρετήν) of the man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:69
verses.text: For that these things should be spoken by Jews, were nothing wonderful: but that these (the believers) are so terrified, it is a most mighty proof of the power of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:70
verses.text: Both the fear is shown, and the obedience greater after the fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:71
verses.text: For there was indeed need of strength.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:72
verses.text: Since He says, "a vessel of election," that thou mayest not imagine that God is to do all, He adds, "to bear My Name before Gentiles and kings, and the children of Israel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:73
verses.text: Ananias has heard what he most desired—that against the Jews also he will take his stand: this above all gave him courage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:74
verses.text: "For I," saith He, "will show him how great things he must suffer for My Name's sake".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:75
verses.text: At the same time also this is said by way of putting Ananias to the blush: If he, that was so frantic, shall suffer all things, and thou not willing even to baptize him! "It is well," saith he: "let him continue blind" (this is why he says these words): "he is blind: why dost Thou at all bid me open his eyes, that he may bind (men) again?" Fear not the future: for that opening of his eyes he will use not against you, but for you (with reference to that saying, "That he may receive his sight" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:76
verses.text: ), these words are spoken): for not only will he do you no harm, but he "will suffer many things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:77
verses.text: And what is wonderful indeed is, that he shall first know "how great things he shall suffer," and then shall take the field against the perils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:78
verses.text: —"Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus"—he saith not, "Who made thee blind," but, "Who appeared with thee in the way, hath sent me unto thee that thou mayest receive thy sight" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:79
verses.text: ): observe this man also, how he utters nothing boastful, but just as Peter said in the case of the lame man, "Why look ye on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made him to walk," (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:80
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:81
verses.text: ) so here also he saith, "Jesus, Who appeared unto thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:82
verses.text: (b) Or, (he saith it) that the other may believe: and he saith not, He that was crucified, the Son of God, He that doeth wonders: but what? "He that appeared unto thee:" (speaking) from what the other knew: as Christ also added no more, neither said, I am Jesus, the Crucified, the Risen: but what? "Whom thou persecutest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:83
verses.text: Ananias said not, "The persecuted," that he may not seem as it were to rave over him (ἐπενθουσί& ·ν), to deride him, "Who appeared unto thee in the way:" and yet He did not (visibly) appear, but was seen by the things done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:84
verses.text: And immediately he added, wishing to draw a veil over the accusation: "That thou mayest receive thy sight".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:85
verses.text: I came not to reprove the past, but to bestow the gift: "that thou mayest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:86
verses.text: (a) With hands laid on, he spake these words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:87
verses.text: "And immediately there fell from his eyes," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:88
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:89
verses.text: ): a double blindness is removed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:90
verses.text: —And why saith it, "Having taken food, he was strengthened?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:91
verses.text: ) Because they that are in such case become relaxed: he had no heart to partake of food before, until he obtained the mighty gifts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:92
verses.text: (c) It seems to me, that both Paul and Cornelius, at the very instant when the words were spoken, received the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:93
verses.text: And yet (in this case) the giver was no great one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:94
verses.text: So true is it, that there was naught of man's in the things done, nor aught was done by man, but God was present, the Doer of these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:95
verses.text: And at the same time (the Lord) both teaches him to think modestly of himself, in that He does not bring him to the Apostles who were so admired, and shows that there is nothing of man here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:96
verses.text: He was not filled, however, with the Spirit which works signs: that in this way also his faith might be shown; for he wrought no miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:97
verses.text: "And straightway," it says, "in the synagogues he preached Jesus"—(v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:98
verses.text: ) not that He is risen—not this: no, nor that He liveth: but what? immediately he strictly expounded the doctrine—"that this is the Son of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:99
verses.text: And all that heard him were amazed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:101
verses.text: ) They were reduced to utter incredulity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:102
verses.text: And yet they ought not to have wondered only, but to worship and reverence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:103
verses.text: "Is not this he," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:104
verses.text: He had not merely been a persecutor, but "destroyed them which called on this Name"—they did not say, "on Jesus;" for hatred, they could not bear even to hear His name—and what is more marvellous still, "and came hither for this purpose," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:105
verses.text: "We cannot say, that he associated with the Apostles before".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:106
verses.text: See by how many (witnesses) he is confessed to have been of the number of the enemies! But Paul not only was not confounded by these things, nor hid his face for shame, but "increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:107
verses.text: ), i-e: put them to silence, left them nothing to say for themselves, "proving, that this is very Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:108
verses.text: "Teaching," it says: for this man was a teacher.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:109
verses.text: "And after that many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:110
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:111
verses.text: ) The Jews again resort to that valid argument (ἰσχυρὸν συλλογισμόν) of theirs, not now seeking false-accusers and false-witnesses; they cannot wait for these now: but what do they? They set about it by themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:112
verses.text: For as they see the affair on the increase, they do not even use the form of a trial.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:113
verses.text: "But their laying await was known of Saul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:114
verses.text: And they watched the gates day and night to kill him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:116
verses.text: ) For this was more intolerable to them than the miracles which had taken place—than the five thousand, the three thousand, than everything, in short.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:117
verses.text: And observe him, how he is delivered, not by (miraculous) grace, but by man's wisdom—not as the apostles were—(ἐκεἴνοι, ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:118
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:119
verses.text: ) that thou mayest learn the energetic (ἀρετὴν) character of the man, how he shines even without miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:120
verses.text: "Then the disciples took him by night," that the affair might not be suspected, "and let him down by the wall in a basket".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:121
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:122
verses.text: ) What then? having escaped such a danger, does he flee? By no means, but goes where he kindled them to greater rage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:123
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:124
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:125
verses.text: ) "And straightway in the synagogues he preached Jesus"—for he was accurate in the faith—"that this is the Son of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:126
verses.text: But all that heard him were amazed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:127
verses.text: , for indeed it was incredible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:128
verses.text: "But Saul increased," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:129
verses.text: Therefore "after many days" this happens: viz.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:130
verses.text: the Jews "took counsel to kill him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:131
verses.text: And their laying await was known of Saul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:132
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:133
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:134
verses.text: ) What does this mean? It is likely that for awhile he did not choose to depart thence, though many, perhaps, besought him; but when he learnt it, then he permitted his disciples: for he had disciples immediately.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:135
verses.text: "Then the disciples," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:136
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:137
verses.text: ) Of this occurrence he says: "The ethnarch of Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desiring to apprehend me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:138
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:139
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:140
verses.text: ) But observe the Writer here, that he does not tell the story ambitiously, and so as to show what an important person Paul was, saying, "For they stirred up the king," and so forth: but only, "Then the disciples took him by night, and let him down by the wall—in a basket:" for they sent him out alone, and none with him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:141
verses.text: And it was well they did this: the consequence being, that he showed himself to the Apostles in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:142
verses.text: Now they sent him out, as bound to provide for his safety by flight: but he did just the contrary—he leaped into the midst of those who were mad against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:143
verses.text: This it is to be on fire, this to be fervent indeed! From that day forth he knew all the commands which the Apostles had heard: "Except a man take up his cross, and follow Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:144
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:145
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:146
verses.text: ) The very fact that he had been slower to come than the rest made him more zealous: for "to whom much is forgiven" (Luke vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 48:147
verses.text: ) the same will love more, so that the later he came, the more he loved:.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:1
verses.text: and having done ten thousand wrongs, he thought he could never do enough to cast the former deeds into the shade.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:2
verses.text: "Proving" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:3
verses.text: ), it says: i-e: with mildness teaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:4
verses.text: And observe, they did not say to him, Thou art he that destroyed: why art thou changed? for they were ashamed: but they said it to themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:5
verses.text: For he would have said to them, This very thing ought to teach you, as in fact he does thus plead in his speech before Agrippa.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:6
verses.text: Let us imitate this, man: let us bear our souls in our hands ready to confront all dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:7
verses.text: —(That he fled from Damascus) this was no cowardice: he preserved himself for the preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:8
verses.text: Had he been a coward, he would not have gone to Jerusalem, would not immediately have commenced teaching: he would have abated somewhat of his vehemence: for he had been taught by the fate of Stephen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:9
verses.text: He was no coward, but he was also prudent (οἰκονομικός) (in husbanding himself).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:10
verses.text: Wherefore he thought it no great thing to die for the Gospel's sake, unless he should do this to great advantage: willing not even to see Christ, Whom most of all he longed to see, while the work of his stewardship among men was not yet complete.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:11
verses.text: (Phil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:12
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:13
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:14
verses.text: Such ought to be the soul of a Christian.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:15
verses.text: From his first appearance from the very outset, the character of Paul declared itself: nay even before this, even in the things which he did "not according to knowledge" (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:16
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:17
verses.text: ), it was not by man's reasoning that he was moved to act as he did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:18
verses.text: For if, so long afterwards, he was content not to depart, much more at the beginning of his trading voyage, when he had but just left the harbor! Many things Christ leaves to be done by (ordinary) human wisdom, that we may learn that (his disciples) were men, that it was not all everywhere to be done by grace: for otherwise they would have been mere motionless logs: but in many things they managed matters themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:19
verses.text: —This is not less than martyrdom,—to shrink from no suffering for the sake of the salvation of the many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:20
verses.text: Nothing so delights God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:21
verses.text: Again will I repeat what I have often said: and I repeat it, because I do exceedingly desire it: as Christ also did the same, when discoursing concerning forgiveness: "When ye pray, forgive if ye have aught against any man:" (Mark xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:22
verses.text: ) and again to Peter He said, "I say not unto thee, Forgive until seven times, but until seventy-times seven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:23
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:24
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:25
verses.text: ) And Himself in fact forgives the transgressions against Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:26
verses.text: So do we also, because we know that this is the very goal of Christianity, continually discourse thereof.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:27
verses.text: Nothing is more frigid than a Christian, who cares not for the salvation of others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:28
verses.text: Thou canst not here plead poverty: for she that cast down the two mites, shall be thine accuser.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:29
verses.text: (Luke xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:30
verses.text: ) And Peter said, "Silver and gold have I none".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:31
verses.text: (Acts iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:32
verses.text: ) And Paul was so poor, that he was often hungered, and wanted necessary food.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:33
verses.text: Thou canst not plead lowness of birth: for they too were ignoble men, and of ignoble parents.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:34
verses.text: Thou canst not allege want of education: for they too were "unlearned men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:35
verses.text: (Acts iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:36
verses.text: ) Even if thou be a slave therefore and a runaway slave, thou canst perform thy part: for such was Onesimus: yet see to what Paul calls him, and to how great honor he advances him: "that he may communicate with me," he says, "in my bonds".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:37
verses.text: (Philem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:38
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:39
verses.text: ) Thou canst not plead infirmity: for such was Timothy, having often infirmities; for, says the apostle, "Use a little wine for thy stomach's sake, and thine often infirmities".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:40
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:41
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:42
verses.text: ) Every one can profit his neighbor, if he will fulfil his part.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:43
verses.text: See ye not the unfruitful trees, how strong they are, how fair, how large also, and smooth, and of great height? But if we had a garden; we should much rather have pomegranates, or fruitful olive trees: for the others are for delight to the eye, not for profit, which in them is but small.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:44
verses.text: Such are those men who only consider their own interest: nay, not such even since these persons are fit only for burning: whereas those trees are useful both for building and for the safety of those within.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:45
verses.text: Such too were those Virgins, chaste indeed, and decent, and modest, but profitable to none (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:46
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:47
verses.text: ) wherefore they are burned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:48
verses.text: Such are they who have not nourished Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:49
verses.text: For observe that none of those are charged with particular sins of their own, with fornication, for instance, or with perjury; in short, with no sin but the having been of no use to another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:50
verses.text: Such was he who buried his talent, showing indeed a blameless life, but not being useful to another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:51
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:52
verses.text: ) How can such an one be a Christian? Say, if the leaven being mixed up with the flour did not change the whole into its own nature, would such a thing be leaven? Again, if a perfume shed no sweet odor on those who approach it, could we call it a perfume? Say not, "It is impossible for me to induce others (to become Christians)"—for if thou art a Christian, it is impossible but that it should be so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:53
verses.text: For as the natural properties of things cannot be gainsaid, so it is here: the thing is part of the very nature of the Christian.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:54
verses.text: Do not insult God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:55
verses.text: To say, that the sun cannot shine, would be to insult Him: to say that a Christian cannot do good, is to insult God, and call Him a liar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:56
verses.text: For it is easier for the sun not to give heat, nor to shine, than for the Christian not to send forth light: it is easier for the light to be darkness, than for this to be so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:57
verses.text: Tell me not that it is impossible: the contrary is the impossible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:58
verses.text: Do not insult God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:59
verses.text: If we once get our own affairs in a right state, the other will certainly follow as a natural and necessary consequence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:60
verses.text: It is not possible for the light of a Christian to be hid; not possible for a lamp so conspicuous as that to be concealed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:61
verses.text: Let us not be careless.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:62
verses.text: For, as the profit from virtue reaches both to ourselves, and to those who are benefited by it: so from vice there is a two-fold loss, reaching both to ourselves, and to those who are injured by it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 51:63
verses.text: Let there be (if you will) some private man, who has suffered numberless ills from some one, and let no one take his part, yet let that man still return good offices; what teaching so mighty as this? What words, or what exhortations could equal it? What wrath were it not enough to extinguish and soften? Knowing therefore these things, let us hold fast to virtue, as knowing that it is not possible to be saved otherwise, than by passing through this present life in doing these good works, that we may also obtain the good things which are to come, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father together with the Holy Spirit be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:1
verses.text: Homily XXI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:2
verses.text: Acts IX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:3
verses.text: ,  "And when Saul was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: but they were all afraid of him, and believed not that he was a disciple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:4
verses.text: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the Apostles, and declared unto them how he had seen the Lord in the way".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:5
verses.text: One may well be much at a loss here to understand how it is that, whereas in the Epistle to the Galatians Paul says, "I went not to Jerusalem," but "into Arabia" and "to Damascus," and, "After three years I went up to Jerusalem," and "to see Peter" (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:6
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:7
verses.text: ), (ἱστορἥσαι Cat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:8
verses.text: ) here the writer says the contrary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:9
verses.text: (There, Paul says,) "And none of the Apostles saw I; but here, it is said (Barnabas), brought him to the Apostles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:10
verses.text: —Well, then, either (Paul) means, "I went not up with intent to refer or attach myself to them (ἀναθέσθαι)—for what saith he? "I referred not myself, neither went I to Jerusalem to those who were Apostles before me:" or else, that the laying await for him in Damascus was after his return from Arabia; or else, again, that the visit to Jerusalem was after he came from Arabia.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:11
verses.text: Certainly of his own accord he went not to the Apostles, but "assayed to join himself unto the disciples"—as being a teacher, not a disciple—"I went not," he says, "for this purpose, that I should go to those who were Apostles before me: certainly, I learnt nothing from them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:12
verses.text: Or, he does not speak of this visit, but passes it by, so that the order is, "I went into Arabia, then I came to Damascus, then to Jerusalem, then to Syria:" or else, again, that he went up to Jerusalem, then was sent to Damascus, then to Arabia, then again to Damascus, then to Caesarea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:13
verses.text: Also, the visit "after fourteen years," probably, was when he brought up the alms to the brethren together with Barnabas: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:14
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:15
verses.text: ) or else he means a different occasion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:16
verses.text: (Acts xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:17
verses.text: ) For the Historian for conciseness, often omits incidents, and condenses the times.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:18
verses.text: Observe how unambitious the writer is, and how he does not even relate (related in ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:19
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:20
verses.text: –) that vision, but passes it by.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:21
verses.text: "He assayed," it says, "to join himself to the disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:22
verses.text: And they were afraid of him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:23
verses.text: By this again is shown the ardor of Paul's character: not (only) from the mouth of Ananias, and of those who wondered at him there, but also of those in Jerusalem: "they believed not that he was a disciple:" for truly that was beyond all human expectation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:24
verses.text: He was no longer a wild beast, but a man mild and gentle! And observe how he does not go to the Apostles, such is his forbearance, but to the disciples, as being a disciple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:25
verses.text: He was not thought worthy of credit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:26
verses.text: "But Barnabas"—"Son of Consolation" is his appellation, whence also he makes himself easy of access to the man: for "he was a kind man" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:27
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:28
verses.text: ), exceedingly, and this is proved both by the present instance, and in the affair of John (Mark)—"having taken him, brought him to the Apostles, and related to them how he had seen the Lord in the way".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:29
verses.text: (xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:30
verses.text: ) It is likely that at Damascus also he had heard all about him: whence he was not afraid but the others were, for he was a man whose glance inspired fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:31
verses.text: "How," it says, "he had seen the Lord in the way, and that He had spoken unto him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of the Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:32
verses.text: And he was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem, and speaking boldly in the name of Jesus" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:33
verses.text: ): these things were demonstrative of the former, and by his acts he made good what was spoken of him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:34
verses.text: "And he spake, and disputed with the Hellenists".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:36
verses.text: ) So then the disciples were afraid of him, and the Apostles did not trust him; by this therefore he relieves them of their fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:37
verses.text: "With the Hellenists:" he means those who used the Greek tongue: and this he did, very wisely; for those others, those profound Hebrews had no mind even to see him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:38
verses.text: "But they," it says, "went about to slay him:" a token, this, of his energy, and triumphant victory, and of their exceeding annoyance at what had happened.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:39
verses.text: Thereupon, fearing lest the issue should be the same as in the case of Stephen, they sent him to Caesarea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:40
verses.text: For it says, "When the brethren were aware of this, they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:41
verses.text: ), at the same time to preach, and likely to be more in safety, as being in his own country.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:42
verses.text: But observe, I pray you, how far it is from being the case that everything is done by (miraculous) grace; how, on the contrary, God does in many things leave them to manage for themselves by their own wisdom and in a human way; so to cut off the excuse of idle people: for if it was so in the case of Paul, much more in theirs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:43
verses.text: "Then, it says, "the Church throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace (they), being edified, and walking in the fear of the Lord, and abounded in the comfort of the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:44
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:45
verses.text: ) He is about to relate that Peter goes down (from Jerusalem), therefore that you may not impute this to fear, he first says this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:46
verses.text: For while there was persecution, he was in Jerusalem, but when the affairs of the Church are everywhere in security, then it is that he leaves Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:47
verses.text: See how fervent and energetic he is! For he did not think, because there was peace, therefore there was no need of his presence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:48
verses.text: Paul departed, and there was peace: there is no war nor disturbance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:49
verses.text: Them, they respected most, as having often stood by them, and as being held in admiration by the multitude: but him, they despised, and were more savage against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:50
verses.text: See, how great a war, and immediately, peace! See what that war effected.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:51
verses.text: It dispersed the peace-makers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:52
verses.text: In Samaria, Simon was put to shame: in Judea, the affair of Sapphira took place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:53
verses.text: Not that, because there was peace, therefore matters became relaxed, but such was the peace as also to need exhortation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:54
verses.text: "And it came to pass, as Peter passed throughout all quarters, he came down also to the saints which dwelt at Lydda".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:55
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:56
verses.text: ) Like the commander of an army, he went about, inspecting the ranks, what part was compact, what in good order, what needed his presence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:57
verses.text: See how on all occasions he goes about, foremost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:58
verses.text: When an Apostle was to be chosen, he was the foremost: when the Jews were to be told, that these were "not drunken," when the lame man was to be healed, when harangues to be made, he is before the rest: when the rulers were to be spoken to, he was the man; when Ananias, he (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:59
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:60
verses.text: ; ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:61
verses.text: ; iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:62
verses.text: –; iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:63
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:64
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:65
verses.text: ): when healings were wrought by the shadow, still it was he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:66
verses.text: And look: where there was danger, he was the man, and where good management (was needed); but where all is calm, there they act all in common, and he demands no greater honor (than the others).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:67
verses.text: When need was to work miracles, he starts forward, and here again he is the man to labor and toil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:68
verses.text: "And there he found a certain man named aeneas, which had kept his bed eight years, and was sick of the palsy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:69
verses.text: And Peter said unto him, aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:70
verses.text: And he arose immediately".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:71
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:72
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:73
verses.text: ) And why did he not wait for the man's faith, and ask if he wished to be healed? In the first place, the miracle served for exhortation to many: hear then how great the gain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:74
verses.text: "And all that dwelt at Lydda and Saron saw him, and turned to the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:75
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:76
verses.text: ) For the man was notable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:77
verses.text: "Arise, and make thy bed:" he does well to give a proof of the miracle: for they not only released men of their diseases, but in giving the health they gave the strength also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:78
verses.text: Moreover, at that time they had given no proofs of their power, so that the man could not reasonably have been required to show his faith, as neither in the case of the lame man did they demand it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:79
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:80
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:81
verses.text: ) As therefore Christ in the beginning of His miracles did not demand faith, so neither did these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:82
verses.text: For in Jerusalem indeed, as was but reasonable, the faith of the parties was first shown; "they brought out their sick into the streets, but as Peter passed by, his shadow at least might fall upon some of them" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:83
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:84
verses.text: ); for many miracles had been wrought there; but here this is the first that occurs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:85
verses.text: For of the miracles, some were wrought for the purpose of drawing others (to faith); some for the comfort of them that believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:86
verses.text: "Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and alms-deeds which she did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:87
verses.text: And it came to pass in those days, that she was sick, and died: whom when they had washed, they laid her in an upper chamber.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:88
verses.text: And forasmuch as Lydda was nigh to Joppa, and the disciples had heard that Peter was there, they sent unto him two men, desiring him that he would not delay to come to them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:89
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:90
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:91
verses.text: Why did they wait till she was dead? Why was not Peter solicited (ἐσκύλη) before this? So right-minded (φιλοσοφοὕντες) were they, they did not think it proper to trouble (σκύλλειν) the Disciples about such matters, and to take them away from the preaching: as indeed this is why it mentions that the place was near, seeing they asked this as a thing beside his mark, and not now in the regular course.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:92
verses.text: "Not to delay to come unto them:" for she was a disciple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:93
verses.text: And Peter arose, and went with them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:94
verses.text: And when he was come, they led him into the upper chamber".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:95
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:96
verses.text: ) They do not beseech, but leave it to him to give her life (σωτηρίαν.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:97
verses.text: ) See what a cheering inducement to alms is here! "And all the widows," it says, "stood round him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:98
verses.text: Peter went into the apartment, as one who took it calmly, but see what an accession came of it! It is not without a meaning that the Writer has informed us of the woman's name, but to show that the name she bore (φερώνυμος ἦν) matched her character; as active and wakeful was she as an antelope.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:99
verses.text: For in many instances there is a Providence in the giving of names, as we have often told you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:100
verses.text: "She was full," it says, "of good works:" not only of alms, but "of good works," first, and then of this good work in particular.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:101
verses.text: "Which," it says, "Dorcas made while she was with them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:102
verses.text: Great humility! Not as we do; but they were all together in common, and in company with them she made these things and worked.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:103
verses.text: "But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning him to the body said, Tabitha, arise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:104
verses.text: And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:105
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:106
verses.text: ) Why does he put them all out? That he may not be confused nor disturbed by their weeping.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:107
verses.text: "And having knelt down, he prayed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:108
verses.text: Observe the intentness of his prayer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:109
verses.text: "And he gave her his hand".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:110
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:111
verses.text: ) So did Christ to the daughter of Jairus: "And (says the Evangelist) having taken her by the hand".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:112
verses.text: Mark severally, first the life, then the strength brought into her, the one by the word, the other by his hand—"And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up, and when he had called the saints and widows, presented her alive:" to some for comfort, because they received back their sister, and because they saw the miracle, and for kindly support (προστασίαν) to others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:113
verses.text: "And it was known throughout all Joppa; and many believed in the Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:114
verses.text: And it came to pass, that he tarried many days in Joppa with one Simon a tanner".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:116
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:117
verses.text: ) Mark the unassuming conduct, mark the moderation of Peter, how he does not make his abode with this lady, or some other person of distinction, but with a tanner: by all his acts leading men to humility, neither suffering the mean to be ashamed, nor the great to be elated! "Many days;" for they needed his instruction, who had believed through the miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:118
verses.text: —Let us look then again at what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:119
verses.text: "Assayed," it says, "to join himself to the disciples".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:120
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:121
verses.text: ) He did not come up to them unabashed, but with a subdued manner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:122
verses.text: "Disciples" they were all called at that time by reason of their great virtue, for there was the likeness of the disciples plainly to be seen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:123
verses.text: "But they were all afraid of him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:124
verses.text: See how they feared the dangers, how the alarm was yet at its height in them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:125
verses.text: "But Barnabas," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:126
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:127
verses.text: )—it seems to me that Barnabas was of old a friend of his—"and related," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:128
verses.text: : observe how Paul says nothing of all this himself: nor would he have brought it forward to the others, had he not been compelled to do so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:129
verses.text: "And he was with them, coming in and going out at Jerusalem, and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:130
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:131
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:132
verses.text: ) This gave them all confidence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:133
verses.text: "But they went about to slay him: which when the brethren knew" etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:134
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:135
verses.text: ) Do you observe how both there (at Damascus), and here, the rest take care for him, and provide for him the means of departure, and that we nowhere find him thus far receiving (direct supernatural) aid from God? So the energy of his character is betokened.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:136
verses.text: "To Caesarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus:" so that, I suppose, he did not continue his journey by land, but sailed the rest of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:137
verses.text: And this (departure) is Providentially ordered, that he might preach there also: and so likewise were the plots against him ordered by God's Providence, and his coming to Jerusalem, that the story about him might no longer be disbelieved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:138
verses.text: For there he was "speaking boldly," it says, "in the name of the Lord Jesus; and he spake and disputed against the Hellenists;" and again, "he was with them coming in and going out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:139
verses.text: —So the Church throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace"—i-e: it increased: and peace with itself, that peace which is peace indeed: for the war from without would have done them no harm —"they being edified, and walking in the fear of the Lord, and abounded in the consolation of the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:140
verses.text: And the spirit consoled them both by the miracles and by the works, and independently of these in the person of each individual.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:141
verses.text: "And it came to pass, etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:142
verses.text: And Peter said unto him, Eneas," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:143
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:144
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:145
verses.text: ) But before discourse, before exhortations, he says to the lame man himself, "Jesus Christ maketh thee whole".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:146
verses.text: This word he believed in any wise, and was made whole.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:147
verses.text: Observe how unassuming he is: for he said not, "In the Name," but rather as a sign he narrates the miracle itself, and speaks as its Evangelist.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:148
verses.text: "And having seen him," it says, "all that dwelt in Lydda, and Saron, turned unto the Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:149
verses.text: —Now there was at Joppa," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:150
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:151
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:152
verses.text: ) Observe everywhere the signs taking place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:153
verses.text: But let us so believe them, as if we were now beholding them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:154
verses.text: It is not simply said, that Tabitha died, but that she died, having been in a state of weakness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:155
verses.text: And (yet) they did not call Peter until she died; then "they sent and told him not to delay to come unto them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:156
verses.text: Observe, they send and call him by others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:157
verses.text: And he comes: he did not think it a piece of disrespect, to be summoned by two men: for, it says, "they sent two men unto him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:158
verses.text: —Affliction, my beloved, is a great thing, and rivets our souls together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:159
verses.text: Not a word of wailing there, nor of mourning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:160
verses.text: See how thoroughly matters are cleansed! "Having washed her," it says, "they laid her in an upper chamber:" that is, they did all (that was right) for the dead body.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:161
verses.text: Then Peter having come, "knelt down, and prayed; and turning him to the body, said, Tabitha, arise".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:162
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:163
verses.text: ) They did not perform all their miracles with the same ease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:164
verses.text: But this was profitable for them: for truly God took thought not only for the salvation of others, but for their own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:165
verses.text: He that healed so many by his very shadow, how is it that he now has to do so much first? There are cases also in which the faith of the applicants coöperated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:166
verses.text: This is the first dead person that he raises.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:167
verses.text: Observe how he, as it were, awakes her out of sleep: first she opened her eyes: then upon seeing (Peter) she sat up: then from his hand she received strength.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:168
verses.text: "And it was known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:169
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:170
verses.text: ) Mark the gain, mark the fruit, that it was not for display.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:171
verses.text: Indeed, this is why he puts them all out, imitating his Master in this also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:172
verses.text: For where tears are—or rather, where miracles are, there tears ought not to be; not where such a mystery is celebrating.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:173
verses.text: Hear, I beseech you: although somewhat of the like kind does not take place now, yet in the case of our dead likewise, a great mystery is celebrating.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:174
verses.text: Say, if as we sit together, the Emperor were to send and invite some one of us to the palace, would it be right, I ask, to weep and mourn? Angels are present, commissioned from heaven and come from thence, sent from the King Himself to call their fellow servant, and say, dost thou weep? Knowest thou not what a mystery it is that is taking place, how awful, how dread, and worthy indeed of hymns and lauds? Wouldest thou learn, that thou mayest know, that this is no time for tears? For it is a very great mystery of the Wisdom of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:175
verses.text: As if leaving her dwelling, the soul goes forth, speeding on her way to her own Lord, and dost thou mourn? Why then, thou shouldst do this on the birth of a child: for this in fact is also a birth, and a better than that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:176
verses.text: For here she goes forth to a very different light, is loosed as from a prison-house, comes off as from a contest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:177
verses.text: "Yes," say you, "it is all very well to say this, in the case of those of whose salvation we are assured".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:178
verses.text: Then, what ails thee, O man, that even in the case of such, thou dost not take it in this way? Say, what canst thou have to condemn in the little child? Why dost thou mourn for it? What in the newly baptized? for he too is brought into the same condition: why dost thou mourn for him? For as the sun arises clear and bright, so the soul, leaving the body with a pure conscience, shines joyously.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:179
verses.text: Not such the spectacle of Emperor as he comes in state to take possession of the city (ἐπιβαίνοντα πόλεως), not such the hush of awe, as when the soul having quitted the body is departing in company with Angels.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:180
verses.text: Think what the soul must then be! in what amazement, what wonder, what delight! Why mournest thou? Answer me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:181
verses.text: —But it is only in the case of sinners thou doest this? Would that it were so, and I would not forbid your mournings, would that this were the object! This lamentation were Apostolic, this were after the pattern of the Lord; for even Jesus wept over Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:182
verses.text: I would that your mournings were discriminated by this rule.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:183
verses.text: But when thou speakest the words of one that would call back (the dead), and speakest of thy long intimacy and his beneficence, it is but for this thou mournest (not because he was a sinner), thou dost but pretend to say it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:184
verses.text: Mourn, bewail the sinner, and I too will give a loose to tears; I, more than thou, the greater the punishment to which he is liable as such: I too will lament, with such an object.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:185
verses.text: But not thou alone must lament him that is such; the whole city must do the same, and all that meet you on the way, as men bewail them that are led to be put to death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:186
verses.text: For this is a death indeed, an evil death, the death of sinners.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:187
verses.text: But (with you) all is clean reversed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:188
verses.text: Such lamentation marks a lofty mind, and conveys much instruction; the other marks a littleness of soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:189
verses.text: If we all lamented with this sort of lamentation, we should amend the persons themselves while yet living.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:190
verses.text: For as, if it rested with thee to apply medicines which would prevent that bodily death, thou wouldest use them, just so now, if this death were the death thou lamentest, thou wouldest prevent its taking place, both in thyself and in him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:191
verses.text: Whereas now our behavior is a perfect riddle; that having it in our power to hinder its coming, we let it take place, and mourn over it when it has come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:192
verses.text: Worthy indeed of lamentations are they (when we consider), what time as they shall stand before the judgment seat of Christ, what words they shall then hear, what they shall suffer! To no purpose have these men lived: nay, not to no purpose, but to evil purpose! Of them too it may be fitly said, "It were good for them had they never been born".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:193
verses.text: (Mark xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:194
verses.text: ) For what profit is it, I ask, to have spent so much time to the hurt of his own person? Had it been spent only to no purpose, were not that, I ask you, punishment enough! If one who has been an hired servant twenty years were to find that he has had all his labor in vain, would he not weep and lament, and think himself the most miserable of men? Why, here is a man who has lost all the labor of a whole life: not one day has he lived for himself, but to luxury, to debauchery, to covetousness, to sin, to the devil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:195
verses.text: Then, say, shall we not bewail this man? shall we not try to snatch him from his perils? For it is, yes, it is possible, if we will, to mitigate his punishment, if we make continual prayers for him, if for him we give alms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:196
verses.text: However unworthy he may be, God will yield to our importunity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:197
verses.text: For if Paul showed mercy on one (who had no claims on his mercy), and for the sake of others spared one (whom he would not have spared), much more is it right for us to do this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:198
verses.text: By means of his substance, by means of thine own, by what means thou wilt, aid him: pour in oil, nay rather, water.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:199
verses.text: Has he no alms-deeds of his own to exhibit? Let him have at least those of his kindred.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:200
verses.text: Has he none done by himself? At least let him have those which are done for him, that his wife may with confidence beg him off in that day, having paid down the ransom for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:201
verses.text: The more sins he has to answer for, the greater need has he of alms, not only for this reason, but because the alms has not the same virtue now, but far less: for it is not all one to have done it himself, and to have another do it for him; therefore, the virtue being less, let us by quantity make it the greatest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:202
verses.text: Let us not busy ourselves about monuments, not about memorials.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:203
verses.text: This is the greatest memorial: set widows to stand around him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:204
verses.text: Tell them his name: bid them all make for him their prayers, their supplications: this will overcome God: though it have not been done by the man himself, yet because of him another is the author of the almsgiving.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:205
verses.text: Even this pertains to the mercy of God: "widows standing around and weeping" know how to rescue, not indeed from the present death, but from that which is to come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:206
verses.text: Many have profited even by the alms done by others on their behalf: for even if they have not got perfect (deliverance), at least they have found some comfort thence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:207
verses.text: If it be not so, how are children saved? And yet there, the children themselves contribute nothing, but their parents do all: and often have women had their children given them, though the children themselves contributed nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:208
verses.text: Many are the ways God gives us to be saved, only let us not be negligent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:209
verses.text: How then if one be poor? say you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:210
verses.text: Again I say, the greatness of the alms is not estimated by the quantity given, but by the purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:211
verses.text: Only give not less than thine ability, and thou hast paid all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:212
verses.text: How then, say you, if he be desolate and a stranger, and have none to care for him? And why is it that he has none, I ask you? In this very thing thou sufferest thy desert, that thou hast none to be thus thy friend, thus virtuous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:213
verses.text: This is so ordered on purpose that, though we be not ourselves virtuous, we may study to have virtuous companions and friends—both wife, and son, and friend—as reaping some good even through them, a slight gain indeed, but yet a gain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:214
verses.text: If thou make it thy chief object not to marry a rich wife, but to have a devout wife, and a religious daughter, thou shalt gain this consolation; if thou study to have thy son not rich but devout, thou shalt also gain this consolation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:215
verses.text: If thou make these thine objects then wilt thyself be such as they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:216
verses.text: This also is part of virtue, to choose such friends, and such a wife and children.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:217
verses.text: Not in vain are the oblations made for the departed, not in vain the prayers, not in vain the almsdeeds: all those things hath the Spirit ordered, wishing us to be benefited one by the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:218
verses.text: See: he is benefited, thou art benefited: because of him, thou hast despised wealth, being set on to do some generous act: both thou art the means of salvation to him, and he to thee the occasion of thine almsgiving.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:219
verses.text: Doubt not that he shall get some good thereby.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:220
verses.text: It is not for nothing that the Deacon cries, "For them that are fallen asleep in Christ, and for them that make the memorials for them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:221
verses.text: It is not the Deacon that utters this voice, but the Holy Ghost: I speak of the Gift.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:222
verses.text: What sayest thou? There is the Sacrifice in hand, and all things laid out duly ordered: Angels are there present, Archangels, the Son of God is there: all stand with such awe, and in the general silence those stand by, crying aloud: and thinkest thou that what is done, is done in vain? Then is not the rest also all in vain, both the oblations made for the Church, and those for the priests, and for the whole body? God forbid! but all is done with faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:223
verses.text: What thinkest thou of the oblation made for the martyrs, of the calling made in that hour, martyrs though they be, yet even "for martyrs?" It is a great honor to be named in the presence of the Lord, when that memorial is celebrating, the dread Sacrifice, the unutterable mysteries.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:224
verses.text: For just as, so long as the Emperor is seated, is the time for the petitioner to effect what he wishes to effect, but when he is risen, say what he will, it is all in vain, so at that time, while the celebration of the mysteries is going on, it is for all men the greatest honor to be held worthy of mention.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:225
verses.text: For look: then is declared the dread mystery, that God gave Himself for the world: along with that mystery he seasonably puts Him in mind of them that have sinned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:226
verses.text: For as when the celebration of Emperors' victories is in progress, then, as many as had their part in the victory receive their meed of praise, while at the same time as many as are in bonds are set at liberty in honor of the occasion; but when the occasion is past, he that did not obtain this favor then, no longer gets any: so is it here likewise: this is the time of celebration of a victory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:227
verses.text: For, saith it, "so often as ye eat this bread, ye do show forth the Lord's death".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:228
verses.text: Then let us not approach indifferently, nor imagine that these things are done in any ordinary sort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:229
verses.text: But it is in another sense that we make mention of martyrs, and this, for assurance that the Lord is not dead: and this, for a sign that death has received its death's blow, that death itself is dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 52:230
verses.text: Knowing these things, let us devise what consolations we can for the departed, instead of tears, instead of laments, instead of tombs, our alms, our prayers, our oblations, that both they and we may attain unto the promised blessings, by the grace and loving-kindness of His only-begotten Son our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:1
verses.text: Homily XXII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:2
verses.text: Acts X.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:3
verses.text: –  "There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band, a devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:4
verses.text: He saw in a vision evidently about the ninth hour of the day an angel of God coming in to him, and saying unto him, Cornelius.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:5
verses.text: And when he looked on him, he was afraid, and said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:6
verses.text: This man is not a Jew, nor of those under the Law, but he had already forestalled our manner of life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:7
verses.text: Observe, thus far, two persons, both of high rank, receiving the faith, the eunuch at Gaza and this man; and the pains taken on behalf of these men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:8
verses.text: But do not imagine that this was because of their high rank: God forbid! it was because of their piety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:9
verses.text: For that the Scripture mentions their dignified stations, is to show the greatness of their piety; since it is more wonderful when a person being in a position of wealth and power is such as these were.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:10
verses.text: What makes the praise of the former is, his undertaking so long a journey, and this when there was no (festival) season to require it, and his reading on his road, and while riding in his chariot, and his beseeching Philip, and numberless other points: and the great praise of the latter is, that he makes alms and prayers, and is a just man, holding such a command.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:11
verses.text: The reason why the writer describes the man so fully, is, that none may say that the Scripture history relates falsehoods: "Cornelius," he says, "a centurion of the band called the Italian band".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:12
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:13
verses.text: ) A "band," σπεἵρα, is what we now call a "numerous".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:14
verses.text: "A devout man," he says, "and one that feared God with all his house" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:15
verses.text: ): that you may not imagine that it is because of his high station that these things are done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:16
verses.text: —When Paul was to be brought over, there is no angel, but the Lord Himself: and He does not send him to some great one, but to a very ordinary person: but here, on the contrary, He brings the chief Apostle (to these Gentiles), not sends them to him: herein condescending to their weakness, and knowing how such persons need to be treated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:17
verses.text: As indeed on many occasions we find Christ Himself hasting (to such), as being more infirm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:18
verses.text: Or (it may be) because (Cornelius) was not able himself to leave his home.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:19
verses.text: But here again is a high commendation of alms, just as was there given by means of Tabitha.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:20
verses.text: "A devout man," it says, "and one that feared God with all his house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:21
verses.text: Let us hear this, whoever of us neglect them of our own house, whereas this man was careful of his soldiers also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:22
verses.text: "And that gave alms," it says, "to all the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:23
verses.text: Both his doctrines and his life were right.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:24
verses.text: "He saw in a vision evidently, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in to him, and saying unto him, Cornelius".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:26
verses.text: ) Why does he see the angel? This also was in order to the full assurance of Peter, or rather, not of him, but of the others, the weaker ones.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:27
verses.text: "At the ninth hour," when he was released from his cares and was at quiet, when he was engaged in prayers and compunction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:28
verses.text: "And when he looked on him, he was afraid".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:30
verses.text: ) Observe how what the angel speaks he does not speak immediately, but first rouses and elevates his mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:31
verses.text: At the sight, there was fear, but a fear in moderation, just so far as served to fix his attention.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:32
verses.text: Then also the words relieved him of his fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:33
verses.text: The fear roused him: the praise mitigated what was unpleasant in the fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:34
verses.text: "Thy prayers," saith he, "and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:35
verses.text: And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:37
verses.text: ) Lest they should come to a different person, he designates the man not only by his surname, but by the place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:38
verses.text: "And the same," saith he, "is lodging with one Simon a tanner, who hath his house by the seaside".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:40
verses.text: ) Do you mark how the Apostles, for love of solitude and quiet, affected the retired quarters of the cities? "With one Simon a tanner:" how then if it chanced that there was another? Behold, there is another token, his dwelling by the seaside.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:41
verses.text: All three tokens could not possibly coincide (elsewhere).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:42
