verses.text: He does not tell him for what purpose, that he may not take off the intense desire, but he leaves him to an eager and longing expectation of what he shall hear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:43
verses.text: "And when the Angel which spake unto Cornelius was departed, he called two of his household servants, and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually; and when he had declared all these things unto them, he sent them to Joppa".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:44
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:46
verses.text: ) Do you see, that it is not without purpose that the writer says this? (it shows) that those also "who waited on him continually" were such as he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:47
verses.text: "And when he had declared the whole matter unto them:" observe the unassuming character of the man: for he does not say, Call Peter to me: but, in order also to induce him to come, he declared the whole matter:—this was so ordered by Providence;—for he did not choose to use the authority of his rank to fetch Peter to him; therefore "he declared the matter;" such was the moderation of the man: and yet no great notion was to be formed of one lodging with a tanner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:48
verses.text: "And on the morrow, as they journeyed, and drew nigh to the city" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:49
verses.text: )—observe how the Spirit connects the times: no sooner than this, and no later, He Causes this to take place—"Peter about the sixth hour went up upon the housetop to pray:" that is, privately and quietly, as in an upper chamber.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:50
verses.text: "And he became very hungry, and would have eaten; but while they made ready, there fell upon him a trance".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:52
verses.text: ) What means this expression, ἔκστασις, "trance?" Rather, there was presented to him a kind of spiritual view (θεωρία): the soul, so to say, was caused to be out of the body (ἐξέστη).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:53
verses.text: "And saw heaven opened, and, knit at the four corners, a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet, and let down to the earth: wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:54
verses.text: And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:55
verses.text: But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:56
verses.text: And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:57
verses.text: This was done thrice: and the vessel was received up again into heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:59
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:60
verses.text: ) What is this? It is a symbol of the whole world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:61
verses.text: The man was uncircumcised: and —for he had nothing in common with the Jews—they would all accuse him as a transgressor: "thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:62
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:63
verses.text: )" this was a thing altogether offensive to them: observe then what is providentially managed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:64
verses.text: He himself also says, "I have never eaten:" not being himself afraid—far be the thought from us—but it is so contrived by the Spirit, in order that he may have it to say in answer to those accusing him, that he did object: for it was altogether necessary for them to observe the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:65
verses.text: He was in the act of being sent to the Gentiles: therefore that these also may not accuse him, see how many things are contrived (by the Providence of God).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:66
verses.text: For, that it may not seem to be a mere fancy, "this was done thrice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:67
verses.text: I said," saith he, "Not so, Lord, for I have never eaten aught common or unclean.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:68
verses.text: —And the voice came unto him, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:69
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:70
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:71
verses.text: , with x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:72
verses.text: ) It seems indeed to be spoken to him, but the whole is meant for the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:73
verses.text: For if the teacher is rebuked, much more these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:74
verses.text: The earth then, this is what the linen sheet denotes, and the wild beasts in it, are they of the Gentiles, and the command, "Kill and eat," denotes that he must go to them also; and that this thing is thrice done, denotes baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:75
verses.text: "What God hath cleansed," saith it, "call not thou common".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:76
verses.text: Great daring! Wherefore did he object? That none may say that God was proving him, as in the case of Abraham, this is why he says, "Not so, Lord," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:77
verses.text: not gainsaying—just as to Philip also He said, "How many loaves have ye?" Not to learn, but tempting, or "proving him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:78
verses.text: And yet it was the same (Lord) that had discoursed above (in the Law) concerning things clean and unclean.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:79
verses.text: But in that sheet were also "all the four-footed beasts of the earth:" the clean with the unclean.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:80
verses.text: And for all this, he knew not what it meant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:81
verses.text: "Now while Peter doubted in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean, behold, the men which were sent from Cornelius had made enquiry for Simon's house, and stood before the gate, and called, and asked whether Simon, which was surnamed Peter, were lodged there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:82
verses.text: But while Peter," it says, "doubted in himself" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:83
verses.text: , ), the men come at the right moment to solve his doubt: just as (the Lord) suffered Joseph first to be perturbed in mind, and then sends the Angel: for the soul with ease accepts the solution, when it has first been in perplexity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:84
verses.text: His perplexity neither lasts long (when it did occur), nor (did it occur) before this, but just at the moment when they "asked whether he were lodging there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:85
verses.text: While Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit said unto him, Behold, three men seek thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:86
verses.text: Arise therefore, and get thee down, and go with them, doubting nothing: for I have sent them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:87
verses.text: (supra, p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:88
verses.text: , and , note ; v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:89
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:90
verses.text: ) And this again is a plea for Peter in answer to the disciples, that he did doubt, and was instructed to doubt nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:91
verses.text: "For I," saith He, "have sent them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:92
verses.text: Great is the authority of the Spirit! What God doth, this the Spirit is said to do.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:93
verses.text: Not so the Angel, but having first said, "Thy prayers and thine alms have ascended, for a memorial before God," to show that he is sent from thence, then he adds, "And now send men," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:94
verses.text: : the Spirit not so, but, "For I have sent them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:95
verses.text: Then Peter went down to the men which were sent unto him from Cornelius; and said, Behold, I am he whom ye seek: what is the cause wherefore ye are come? And they said, Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God and of good report among all the nation of the Jews, was warned from God by an holy angel to send for thee into his house, and to hear words of thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:96
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:97
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:98
verses.text: ) They speak his praises, so as to persuade him that an Angel has in fact appeared unto him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:99
verses.text: "Then called he them in," (b) that they may suffer no harm, "and lodged them:" thenceforth he without scruple takes his meals with them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:100
verses.text: "And on the morrow Peter went away with them, and certain brethren from Caesarea accompanied him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:101
verses.text: And the morrow after, they entered into Caesarea".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:102
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:103
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:104
verses.text: ) The man was a person of note, and it was in a city of note that he then was.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:105
verses.text: (a) But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:106
verses.text: "There was a certain man in Caesarea," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:107
verses.text: (Recapitulation, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:108
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:109
verses.text: ) Observe with whom the beginning of the Gentiles is made—with "a devout man," and one proved to be worthy by his works.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:110
verses.text: For if, though the case be so, they are still offended, if this had not been the case, what would not have been the consequence! But mark the greatness of the assurance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:111
verses.text: (c) To this end all is done (in the way it is done), and the affair takes its beginning from Judea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:112
verses.text: (d) "He saw in a vision, evidently," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:113
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:114
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:115
verses.text: It was not in his sleep that the Angel appeared to him, but while he was awake, in the daytime, "about the ninth hour.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:116
verses.text: He saw an Angel of God coming in unto him, and saying unto him, Cornelius.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:117
verses.text: And when he looked on him, he was afraid".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:118
verses.text: So occupied was he with himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:119
verses.text: Implying, that it was in consequence of the Angel's calling him by a voice that he saw him; as, had he not called him, he would not have seen him: so taken up was he with the act in which he was engaged.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:120
verses.text: But the Angel says to him, "Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God, and now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, who is called Peter".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:121
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:122
verses.text: ) So far, he signified that the sending for him would be for good consequences, but in what way good, he did not intimate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:123
verses.text: So, neither does Peter relate the whole matter, but everywhere, the narratives are in part only, for the purpose of making the hearers apply their minds to what is said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:124
verses.text: "Send and call for Simon:" in like manner the Angel only calls Philip.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:125
verses.text: "And as they went on their journey, and drew nigh to the city" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:126
verses.text: ): in order that Peter should not be in perplexity too long.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:127
verses.text: "Peter went up upon the housetop," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:128
verses.text: Observe, that not even his hunger forced him to have recourse to the sheet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:129
verses.text: "Rise, Peter," saith the Voice, "kill and eat".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:130
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:131
verses.text: ) Probably he was on his knees when he saw the vision.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:132
verses.text: —To me it seems that this also denotes the Gospel (or, "the Preaching").

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:133
verses.text: That the thing taking place was of God (the circumstances made evident, namely), both that he sees it (descending) from above, and that he is in a trance; and, that the voice comes from thence, and the thrice confessing that the creatures there were unclean, and its coming from thence, and being drawn back thither (all this), is a mighty token of the cleanness (imparted to them).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:134
verses.text: —But why is this done? For the sake of those thereafter, to whom he is about to relate it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:135
verses.text: For to himself it had been said, "Go not into the way of the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 53:136

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:1
verses.text: For if Paul needed both (to give) circumcision, and (to offer) sacrifice, much more (was some assurance needed) then, in the beginning of the Preaching, while they were as yet weaker.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:2
verses.text: (Acts xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:3
verses.text: ; xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:4
verses.text: )—Observe too how he did not at once receive them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:5
verses.text: For, it says, they "called, and asked, whether Simon, which was surnamed Peter, were lodging there".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:6
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:7
verses.text: ) As it was a mean looking house, they asked below, they inquired of the neighbors.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:8
verses.text: "And while Peter thought, the Spirit said unto him, Arise, get thee down, and go, nothing doubting, for I have sent them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:9
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:10
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:11
verses.text: ) And he does not say, For to this end did the vision appear unto thee; but, "I have sent them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:12
verses.text: Then Peter went down" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:13
verses.text: )—this is the way the Spirit must be obeyed, without demanding reasons.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:14
verses.text: For it is sufficient for all assurance to be told by Him, This do, this believe: nothing more (is needed)—"Then Peter went down, and said, Behold, I am he whom ye seek: what is the cause wherefore ye are come?" He saw a soldier, saw a man: it was not that he was afraid, on the contrary, having first confessed that he was the person whom they sought, then he asks for the cause (of their coming); that it may not be supposed that the reason of his asking the cause, was, that he wished to hide himself: (he asks it) in order, that if it be immediately urgent, he may also go forth with them, but if not, may receive them as guests.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:15
verses.text: "And they said, etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:16
verses.text: into his house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:17
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:18
verses.text: ) This he had ordered them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:19
verses.text: Do not think he has done this out of contempt: not as of contempt has he sent, but so he was ordered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:20
verses.text: "And Cornelius was waiting for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:22
verses.text: ) It was right that his kinsmen and friends should be gathered to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:23
verses.text: But being there present, they would have heard from him (what had happened).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:24
verses.text: See how great the virtue of alms, both in the former discourse, and here! There, it delivered from death temporal; here, from death eternal; and opened the gates of heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:25
verses.text: Such are the pains taken for the bringing of Cornelius to the faith, that both an angel is sent, and the Spirit works, and the chief of the Apostles is fetched to him, and such a vision is shown, and, in short, nothing is left undone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:26
verses.text: How many centurions were there not besides, and tribunes, and kings, and none of them obtained what this man did! Hear, all ye that are in military commands, all ye that stand beside kings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:27
verses.text: "A just man," it says, "fearing God; devout" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:28
verses.text: , and ); and what is more than all, with all his house.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:29
verses.text: Not as we (who): that our servants may be afraid of us, do everything.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:30
verses.text: but not that they may be devout.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 55:31
verses.text: And over the domestics too, so.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 57

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 57:1
verses.text: Not so this man; but he was "one that feared God with all his house" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 57:2
verses.text: ), for he was as the common father of those with him, and of all the others (under his command.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 57:3
verses.text: ) But observe what (the soldier) says himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 57:4
verses.text: For, fearing.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:1
verses.text: , he adds this also: "well reported of by all the nation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:2
verses.text: For what if he was uncircumcised? Nay, but those give him a good report.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:3
verses.text: Nothing like alms: great is the virtue of this practice, when the alms is poured forth from pure stores; for it is like a fountain discharging mud, when it issues from unjust stores, but when from just gains, it is as a limpid and pure stream in a paradise, sweet to the sight, sweet to the touch, both light and cool, when given in the noon-day heat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:4
verses.text: Such is alms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:5
verses.text: Beside this fountain, not poplars and pines, nor cypresses, but other plants than these, and far better, of goodly stature: friendship with God, praise with men, glory to Godward, good-will from all; blotting out of sins, great boldness, contempt of wealth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:6
verses.text: This is the fountain by which the plant of love is nourished: for nothing is so wont to nourish love, as the being merciful: it makes its branches to lift themselves on high.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:7
verses.text: This fountain is better than that in Paradise (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:8
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:9
verses.text: ); a fountain, not dividing into four heads, but reaching unto Heaven itself: this gives birth to that river "which springeth up into eternal life" (John iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:10
verses.text: ): on this let Death light, and like a spark it is extinguished by the fountain: such, wherever it drops, are the mighty blessings it causes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:11
verses.text: This quenches, even as a spark, the river of fire: this so strangles that worm, as naught else can do.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:12
verses.text: (Mark ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:13
verses.text: ) He that has this, shall not gnash his teeth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:14
verses.text: Of the water of this, let there be dropped upon the chains, and it dissolves them: let it but touch the firebrands, it quenches all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:15
verses.text: —A fountain does not give out streams for a while and anon run dry,—else must it be no more a fountain,—but ever gushes: so let our fountain give out more copiously of the streams of mercy (in alms).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:16
verses.text: This cheers him that receives: this is alms, to give out not only a copious, but a perennial, stream.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:17
verses.text: If thou wouldest that God rain down His mercy upon thee as from fountains, have thou also a fountain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:18
verses.text: And yet there is no comparison (between God's fountain and thine): for if thou open the mouths of this fountain, such are the mouths of God's Fountain as to surpass every abyss.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:19
verses.text: God does but seek to get an opportunity on our part, and pours forth from His storehouses His blessings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:20
verses.text: When He expends, when He lavishes, then is He rich, then is He affluent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:21
verses.text: Large is the mouth of that fountain: pure and limpid its water.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:22
verses.text: If thou stop not up the fountain here, neither wilt thou stop up that fountain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:23
verses.text: —Let no unfruitful tree stand beside it, that it may not waste its spray.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:24
verses.text: Hast thou wealth? Plant not poplars there: for such is luxury: it consumes much, and shows nothing for it in itself, but spoils the fruit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:25
verses.text: Plant not a pine-tree—such is wantonness in apparel, beautiful only to the sight, and useful for nothing—nor yet a fir-tree, nor any other of such trees as consume indeed, but are in no sort useful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:26
verses.text: Set it thick with young shoots: plant all that is fruitful, in the hands of the poor, all that thou wilt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:27
verses.text: Nothing richer than this ground.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:28
verses.text: Though small the reach of the hand, yet the tree it plants starts up to heaven and stands firm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:29
verses.text: This it is to plant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:30
verses.text: For that which is planted on the earth will perish, though not now, at any rate a hundred years hence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:31
verses.text: Thou plantest many trees, of which thou shalt not enjoy the fruit, but ere thou canst enjoy it, death comes upon thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:32
verses.text: This tree will give thee its fruit then, when thou art dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:33
verses.text: —If thou plant, plant not in the maw of gluttony, that the fruit end not in the draught-house: but plant thou in the pinched belly, that the fruit may start up to heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:34
verses.text: Refresh the straightened soul of the poor, lest thou pinch thine own roomy soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:35
verses.text: —See you not, that the plants which are over-much watered at the root decay, but grow when watered in moderation? Thus also drench not thou thine own belly, that the root of the tree decay not: water that which is thirsty, that it may bear fruit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:36
verses.text: If thou water in moderation, the sun will not wither them, but if in excess, then it withers them: such is the nature of the sun.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:37
verses.text: In all things, excess is bad; wherefore let us cut it off, that we also may obtain the things we ask for.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:38
verses.text: —Fountains, it is said, rise on the most elevated spots.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:39
verses.text: Let us be elevated in soul, and our alms will flow with a rapid stream: the elevated soul cannot but be merciful, and the merciful cannot but be elevated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:40
verses.text: For he that despises wealth, is higher than the root of evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:41
verses.text: —Fountains are oftenest found in solitary places: let us withdraw our soul from the crowd, and alms will gush out with us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:42
verses.text: Fountains, the more they are cleaned, the more copiously they flow: so with us, the more we spend, the more all good grows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:43
verses.text: —He that has a fountain, has nothing to fear: then neither let us be afraid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:44
verses.text: For indeed this fountain is serviceable to us for drink, for irrigation, for building, for everything.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:45
verses.text: Nothing better than this draught: it is not possible for this to inebriate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:46
verses.text: Better to possess such a fountain, than to have fountains running with gold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:47
verses.text: Better than all gold-bearing soil is the soul which bears this gold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:48
verses.text: For it advances us, not into these earthly palaces, but into those above.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:49
verses.text: The gold becomes an ornament to the Church of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:50
verses.text: Of this gold is wrought "the sword of the Spirit" (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:51
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:52
verses.text: ), the sword by which the dragon is beheaded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:53
verses.text: From this fountain come the precious stones which are on the King's head.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 59:54
verses.text: Then let us not neglect so great wealth, but contribute our alms with largeness, that we may be found worthy of the mercy of God, by the grace and tender compassion of His only begotten Son, with Whom to the Father and Holy Ghost together be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:1
verses.text: Homily XXIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:2
verses.text: Acts X.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:3
verses.text: ,  "Then called he them in, and lodged them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:4
verses.text: And on the morrow Peter went away with them, and certain brethren from Joppa accompanied him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:5
verses.text: And the morrow after they entered into Caesarea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:6
verses.text: And Cornelius waited for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:7
verses.text: "He" called them in, and lodged them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:8
verses.text: Good, that first he gives the men friendly treatment, after the fatigue of their journey, and makes them at home with him; "and on the morrow," sets out with them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:9
verses.text: And certain accompany him: this too as Providence ordered it, that they should be witnesses afterwards when Peter would need to justify himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:10
verses.text: "And Cornelius was waiting for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:11
verses.text: This is the part of a friend, this the part of a devout man, that where such blessings are concerned, he takes care that his near friends shall be made partakers of all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:12
verses.text: Of course (his "near" friends), those in whom he had ever full confidence; fearing, with such an interest at stake, to entrust the matter to others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:13
verses.text: In my opinion, it was by Cornelius himself that both friends and kinsmen had been brought to a better mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:14
verses.text: "And as Peter was coming in, Cornelius met him, and fell down at his feet, and worshipped him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:16
verses.text: ) This, both to teach the others, and by way of giving thanks to God, and showing his own humility: thereby making it plain, that though he had been commanded, yet in himself he had great piety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:17
verses.text: What then did Peter? "But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:19
verses.text: ) Do you mark how, before all else (the Apostles) teach them this lesson, not to think great things of them? "And as he talked with him, he went in, and found many that were come together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:20
verses.text: And he said unto them, Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath showed me that I should not call any man common or unclean".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:23
verses.text: ) Observe, he straightway speaks of the mercy of God, and points out to them that it is a great grace that God has shown them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:24
verses.text: Observe also how while he utters great things, at the same time he speaks modestly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:25
verses.text: For he does not say, We, being men who do not deign to keep company with any (such), have come to you: but what says he? "Ye know"—God commanded this—"that it is against law to keep company with, or come unto, one of another nation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:26
verses.text: Then he goes on to say, "And to me God has shown"—this he says, that none may account the thanks due to him—"that I should call no man"—that it may not look like obsequiousness to him, "no human being," says he—"common or unclean".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:28
verses.text: ) "Wherefore also"—that they may not think the affair a breach of the law on his part, nor (Cornelius) suppose that because he was in a station of command therfore he had complied, but that they may ascribe all to God,—"wherefore also I came without gainsaying as soon as I was sent for:" (though) not only to keep company, but even to come unto (him) was not permitted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:29
verses.text: "I ask therefore, for what intent ye have sent for me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:30
verses.text: Already Peter had heard the whole matter from the soldiers also, but he wishes them first to confess, and to make them amenable to the Faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:31
verses.text: What then does Cornelius? He does not say, Why, did not the soldiers tell thee? but observe again, how humbly he speaks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:32
verses.text: For he says, "From the fourth day I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and, behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing, and said, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:33
verses.text: And at the ninth hour," he says, "I was praying".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:36
verses.text: ) It seems to me, that this man had also fixed for himself set times of a life under stricter rule, and on certain days.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:37
verses.text: For this is why he he says, "From the fourth day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:38
verses.text: See how great a thing prayer is! When he advanced in piety, then the Angel appears to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:39
verses.text: "From the fourth day:" i-e: of the week; not "four days ago".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:40
verses.text: For, "on the morrow Peter went away with them, and on the morrow after they entered into Caesarea:" this is one day: and the day on which the persons sent came (to Joppa) one day: and on the third (the Angel) appeared: so that there are two days after that on which (Cornelius) had been praying.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:41
verses.text: "And, behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing:" he does not say, an Angel, so unassuming is he: "and said, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:42
verses.text: Send therefore to Joppa, and call hither Simon, whose surname is Peter: he is lodged in the house of one Simon a tanner by the seaside: who, when he cometh, shall speak unto thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:43
verses.text: Immediately therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou art come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:44
verses.text: Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:47
verses.text: ) (b) See what faith, what piety! He knew that it was no word of man that Peter spake, when he said, "God hath shown me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:48
verses.text: Then says the man, "We are present to hear all things that are commanded thee of the Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:49
verses.text: (a) Therefore it was that Peter asked, "For what intent have ye sent for me?" on purpose that he might so speak these very words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:50
verses.text: (d) "Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respector of persons: but in every nation he that feareth Him, and worketh righteousness, is acceptable to him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:52
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:53
verses.text: ) That is, be he uncircumcised or circumcised.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:54
verses.text: (c) This also Paul declaring, saith, "For there is no respect of persons with God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:55
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:56
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:57
verses.text: ) (e) What then? (it may be asked) is the man yonder in Persia acceptable to Him? If he be worthy, in this regard he is acceptable, that it should be granted him to be brought unto faith (τᾥ καταξιωθἥναι τῆς πίστεως).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:58
verses.text: The Eunuch from Ethiopia He overlooked not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:59
verses.text: "What shall one say then of the religious men who have been overlooked?" It is not the case, that any (such) ever was overlooked.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:60
verses.text: But what he says is to this effect, that God rejects no man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:61
verses.text: "In every nation, he that feareth God and worketh righteousness:" (by righteousness) he means, all virtue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:62
verses.text: Mark, how he subdues all elation of mind in him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:63
verses.text: That (the Jews) may not seem to be in the condition of persons cast off (he adds), "The word which He sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: He is Lord of all (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:64
verses.text: ): this he says also for the sake of those present (of the Jews), that He may persuade them also: this is why he forces Cornelius to speak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:65
verses.text: "He," saith he, "is Lord of all".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:66
verses.text: But observe at the very outset, "The word," says he, "which He sent unto the children of Israel;" he gives them the preëminence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:67
verses.text: Then he adduces (these Gentiles) themselves as witnesses: "ye know," says he, "the matter which came to pass throughout all Judea, beginning at Galilee"—then he confirms it from this also—"after the baptism which John preached" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:68
verses.text: )—"even Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed Him with the Holy Ghost and with power".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:69
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:70
verses.text: ) He does not mean, Ye know Jesus, for they did not know Him, but he speaks of the things done by Him: "Who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil: by this he shows that many cases of lost senses or paralyzed limbs are the devil's work, and a wrench given to the body by him: as also Christ said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:71
verses.text: "For God was with Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:72
verses.text: Again, lowly terms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:73
verses.text: "And we are witnesses of all things which He did, both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:74
verses.text: ): both "we," saith he, and ye.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:75
verses.text: Then the Passion, and the reason why they do not believe: "Whom also they slew, and hanged on a tree.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:76
verses.text: Him God raised up the third day, and showed Him openly; not to all the people, but unto witnesses chosen before of God, even to us, who did eat and drink with Him after He rose from the dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:77
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:78
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:79
verses.text: ) This is a proof of the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:80
verses.text: "And he commanded us to preach unto the people, and to testify that it is He which was ordained of God to be the Judge of quick and dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:81
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:82
verses.text: ) This is great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:83
verses.text: Then he adduces the testimony from the Prophets: "To Him give all the prophets witness, that through His name, whosoever believeth in Him shall receive remission of sins".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:84
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:85
verses.text: ) This is a proof of that which was about to be: this is the reason why he here cites the Prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:86
verses.text: But let us look over again what relates to Cornelius.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:87
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:88
verses.text: ) He sent, it says, to Joppa to fetch Peter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:89
verses.text: "He was waiting for him," etc; see how fully he believed that Peter would certainly come: (b) "and fell down at his feet, and worshipped him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:90
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:91
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:92
verses.text: ) (a) Mark how on every side it is shown how worthy he is! (So) the Eunuch there desired Philip to come up and sit in the chariot (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:93
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:94
verses.text: ), although not knowing who he was, upon no other introduction (ἐπαγγελίας) than that given by the Prophet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:95
verses.text: But here Cornelius fell at his feet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:96
verses.text: (c) "Stand up, I myself also am a man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:97
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:98
verses.text: ) Observe how free from adulation his speech is on all occasions, and how full of humility.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:99
verses.text: "And conversing with him, he came in".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:101
verses.text: ) Conversing about what? I suppose saying these words: "I myself also am a man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:102
verses.text: (e) Do you mark (Peter's) unassuming temper? He himself also shows that his coming is God's doing: "Ye know that it is unlawful for a man that is a Jew," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:103
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:104
verses.text: ) And why did he not speak of the linen sheet? Observe Peter's freedom from all vainglory: but, that he is sent of God, this indeed he mentions; of the manner in which he was sent, he speaks not at present; when the need has arisen, seeing he had said, "Ye know that it is unlawful for a man that is a Jew to keep company with, or to come unto, one of another nation," he simply adds, "but to me God hath shown," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:105
verses.text: There is nothing of vainglory here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:106
verses.text: "All ye," he says, "know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:107
verses.text: He makes their knowledge stand surety for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:108
verses.text: But Cornelius says, "We are present before God to hear all things that are commanded thee of the Lord" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:109
verses.text: ): not, Before man, but, "Before God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:110
verses.text: This is the way one ought to attend to God's servants.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:111
verses.text: Do you see his awakened mind? do you see how worthy he was of all these things? "And Peter," it says, "opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:112
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:113
verses.text: ) This he said also by way of justifying himself with the Jews then present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:114
verses.text: For, being at the point to commit the Word to these (Gentiles), he first puts this by way of apology.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:115
verses.text: What then? Was He "a respecter of persons" beforetime? God forbid! For beforetime likewise it was just the same: "Every one," as he saith, "that feareth Him, and worketh righteousness, would be acceptable to Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:116
verses.text: As when Paul saith, "For when the Gentiles which have not the Law, do by nature the things of the Law".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:117
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:118
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:119
verses.text: ) "That feareth God and worketh righteousness:" he assumes both doctrine and manner of life: is "accepted with Him;" for, if He did not overlook the Magi, nor the Ethiopian, nor the thief, nor the harlot, much more them that work righteousness, and are willing, shall He in anywise not overlook.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:120
verses.text: "What say you then to this, that there are likely persons (ἐπιεικεἵς), men of mild disposition, and yet they will not believe?" (Above, p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:121
verses.text: , note.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:122
verses.text: ) Lo, you have yourself named the cause: they will not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:123
verses.text: But besides the likely person he here speaks of is not this sort of man, but the man "that worketh righteousness:" that is, the man who in all points is virtuous and irreproachable, when he has the fear of God as he ought to have it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:124
verses.text: But whether a person be such, God only knows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:125
verses.text: See how this man was acceptable: see how, as soon as he heard, he was persuaded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:126
verses.text: "Yes, and now too," say you, "every one would be persuaded, be who he may".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:127
verses.text: But the signs that are now, are much greater than those, and more wonderful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:128
verses.text: —Then Peter commences his teaching, and reserves for the Jews the privilege of their birth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:129
verses.text: "The word," he says, "which He sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:130
verses.text: ), not bringing judgment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:131
verses.text: He is sent to the Jews also: yet for all this He did not spare them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:132
verses.text: "Preaching peace through Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:133
verses.text: He is Lord of all".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:134
verses.text: First he discourses of His being Lord and in exceeding elevated terms, seeing he had to deal with a soul more than commonly elevated, and that took all in with ardor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:135
verses.text: Then he proves how He was Lord of all, from the things which He achieved "throughout all Judea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:136
verses.text: For ye know," saith he, "the matter which came to pass throughout all Judea:" and, what is the wonderful part of it, "beginning at Galilee: after the baptism which John preached".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:137
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:138
verses.text: ) First he speaks of His success, and then again he says concerning Him, "Jesus of Nazareth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:139
verses.text: Why, what a stumbling-block, this birthplace! "How God anointed Him with the Holy Ghost and with power".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:140
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:141
verses.text: ) Then again the proof—how does that appear?—from the good that He did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:142
verses.text: "Who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil:" and the greatness of the power shown when He overcomes the devil; and the cause, "Because God was with Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:143
verses.text: Therefore also the Jews spake thus: "We know that Thou art a teacher come from God: for none can do these miracles except God be with him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:144
verses.text: (John iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:145
verses.text: ) Then, when he has shown that He was sent from God, he next speaks of this, that He was slain: that thou mayest not imagine aught absurd.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:146
verses.text: Seest thou how far they are from hiding the Cross out of view, nay, that together with the other circumstances they put also the manner? "Whom also," it says, "they slew by hanging on a tree.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:147
verses.text: And gave Him," it is added, "to be made manifest not to all the people, but to witnesses before ordained of God, even unto us:" and yet it was (Christ) Himself that elected them; but this also he refers to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:148
verses.text: "To the before-ordained," he says, "even to us, who did eat and drink with Him after that He was risen from the dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:149
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:150
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:151
verses.text: ) See whence he fetches his assurance of the resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:152
verses.text: What is the reason that being risen he did no sign, but only ate and drank? Because the Resurrection itself was a great sign, and of this nothing was so much a sign as the eating and drinking.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:153
verses.text: "To testify," saith he—in a manner calculated to alarm—that they may not have it in their power to fall back upon the excuse of ignorance: and he does not say, "that He is the Son of God," but, what would most alarm them, "that it is He which is ordained of God, to be the Judge of quick and dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:154
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:155
verses.text: ) "To him give all the Prophets witness," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:156
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:157
verses.text: ) When by the terror he has agitated them, then he brings in the pardon, not spoken from himself but from the Prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:158
verses.text: And what is terrifying is from him, what is mild from the Prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:159
verses.text: All ye that have received this forgiveness, all ye to whom it has been vouchsafed to attain unto faith, learn, I beseech you, the greatness of the Gift, and study not to be insolent to your Benefactor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:160
verses.text: For we obtained forgiveness, not that we should become worse, but to make us far better and more excellent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:161
verses.text: Let none say that God is the cause of our evil doings, in that He did not punish, nor take vengeance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:162
verses.text: If (as it is said) a ruler having taken a murderer, lets him go, say, is he (not) judged to be the cause of the murders afterwards committed? See then, how we expose God to the tongues of the wicked.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:163
verses.text: For what do they not say, what leave unuttered? "(God) Himself," say they, "allowed them; for he ought to have punished them as they deserved, not to honor them, nor crown them, nor admit them to the foremost privileges, but to punish and take vengeance upon them: but he that, instead of this, honors them, has made them to be such as they are".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:164
verses.text: Do not, I beseech and implore you, do not let any man utter such speech as far as we are concerned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:165
verses.text: Better to be buried ten thousand times over, than that God through us should be so spoken of! The Jews, we read, said to (Christ) Himself, "Thou that destroyest the Temple, and in three days buildest it up, come down from the Cross" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:166
verses.text: xxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:167
verses.text: ): and again, "If Thou be the Son of God:" but the reproaches here are more grievous than those, that through us He should be called a teacher of wickedness! Let us cause the very opposite to be said, by having our conversation worthy of Him that calleth us, and (worthily) approaching to the baptism of adoption.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:168
verses.text: For great indeed is the might of baptism (φωτίσματου): it makes them quite other men than they were, that partake of the gift; it does not let the men be men (and nothing more).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:169
verses.text: Make thou the Gentile (τὸν ῞Ελληνα), to believe that great is the might of the Spirit, that it has new-moulded, that it has fashioned thee anew.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:170
verses.text: Why waitest thou for the last gasp, like a runaway slave, like a malefactor, as though it were not thy duty to live unto God? Why dost thou stand affected to Him, as if thou hadst in Him a ruthless, cruel Master? What can be more heartless (ψυχρότερον), what more miserable, than those who make that the time to receive baptism? God made thee a friend, and vouchsafed thee all His good things, that thou mayest act the part of a friend.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:171
verses.text: Suppose you had done some man the greatest of wrongs, had insulted him, and brought upon him disgraces without end, suppose you had fallen into the hands of the person wronged, and he, in return for all this, had honored you, made you partaker of all that he had, and in the assembly of his friends, of those in whose presence he was insulted, had crowned you, and declared that he would hold you as his own begotten son, and then straightway had died: say, would you not have bewailed him? would you not have deemed his death a calamity? would you not have said, Would that he were alive, that I might have it in my power to make the fit return, that I might requite him, that I might show myself not base to my benefactor? So then, where it is but man, this is how you would act; and where it is God, are you eager to be gone, that you may not requite your benefactor for so great gifts? Nay rather, choose the time for coming to Him so that you shall have it in your power to requite Him like for like.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:172
verses.text: True, say you, but I cannot keep (the gift).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:173
verses.text: Has God commanded impossibilities? Hence it is that all is clean reversed, hence that, all the world over, every thing is marred—because nobody makes it his mark to live after God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:174
verses.text: Thus those who are yet Catechumens, because they make this their object, (how they may defer baptism to the last,) give themselves no concern about leading an upright life: and those who have been baptized (φωτισθεντες), whether it be because they received it as children, or whether it be that having received it in sickness, and afterwards recovered (ἀνενεγκόντες), they had no hearty desire to live on (to the glory of God), so it is, that neither do these make an earnest business of it: nay, even such as received it in health, have little enough to show of any good impression, and warmly affected for the time, these also presently let the fire go out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:175
verses.text: Why do you flee? why do you tremble? what is it you are afraid of? You do not mean to say that you are not permitted to follow your business? I do not part you from your wife! No, it is from fornication that I bar you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:176
verses.text: I do not debar you from the enjoyment of your wealth? No, but from covetousness and rapacity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:177
verses.text: I do not oblige you to empty out all your coffers? No, but to give some small matter according to your means to them that lack, your superfluities to their need, and not even this unrewarded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:178
verses.text: We do not urge you to fast? We do but forbid you to besot yourselves with drunkenness and gormandizing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:179
verses.text: The things we would retrench are but the very things which bring you disgrace; things which even here, on this side of hell-fire, you yourselves confess to be things to be shunned and hated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:180
verses.text: We do not forbid you to be glad and to rejoice? Nay, only rejoice not with a disgraceful and unbecoming merriment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:181
verses.text: What is it you dread, why are you afraid, why do you tremble? Where marriage is, where enjoyment of wealth, where food in moderation, what matter of sin is there in these things? And yet, they that are without enjoin the opposites to these, and are obeyed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:182
verses.text: For they demand not according to thy means, but they say, Thou must give thus much: and if thou allege poverty, they will make no account of that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:183
verses.text: Not so Christ: Give, saith He, of what thou hast, and I inscribe thee in the first rank.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:184
verses.text: Again those say, If thou wilt distinguish thyself, forsake father, mother, kindred, friends, and keep close attendance on the Palace, laboring, toiling, slaving, distracted, suffering miseries without number.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:185
verses.text: Not so Christ; but keep thou, saith He, at home with thy wife, with thy children, and as for thy daily occupations reform and regulate them on the plan of leading a peaceable life, free from cares and from perils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:186
verses.text: True, say you, but the other promises wealth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:187
verses.text: Aye, but Christ a kingdom, and more, He promises wealth also with it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:188
verses.text: For, "Seek ye," saith He, "the kingdom of Heaven, and all these things shall be added unto you" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:189
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:190
verses.text: ): throwing in, by way of additional boon, what the other holds out as the main thing: and the Psalmist says, he has "never seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging their bread".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:191
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:192
verses.text: xxxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:193
verses.text: ) Let us set about practising virtue, let us make a beginning; let us only lay hold on it, and you shall see what the good will be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:194
verses.text: For surely in these (worldly) objects you do not succeed so without labor, that you should be so faint-hearted for these (higher) objects—that you should say, Those are to be had without labor, these only with toil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:195
verses.text: Nay,—what need to tell you what is the true state of the case?—those are had only with greater labor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:196
verses.text: Let us not recoil from the Divine Mysteries, I beseech you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:197
verses.text: Look not at this, that one who was baptized before thee, has turned out ill, and has fallen from his hope: since among soldiers also we see some not doing their duty by the service, while we see others distinguishing themselves, and we do not look only at the idle ones, but we emulate these, the men who are successful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:198
verses.text: But besides, consider how many, after their baptism, have of men become angels!  Fear the uncertainty of the future.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:199
verses.text: "As a thief in the night," so death comes: and not merely as a thief, but while we sleep it sets upon us, and carries us off while we are idling.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:200
verses.text: To this end has God made the future uncertain, that we may spend our time in the practice of virtue, because of the uncertainty of expectation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:201
verses.text: But He is merciful, say you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:202
verses.text: How long shall we hear this senseless, ridiculous talk? I affirm not only that God is merciful, but that nothing can be more merciful than He, and that He orders all things concerning us for our good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:203
verses.text: How many all their life do you see afflicted with the worst form of leprosy! (ἐν ἐλέφαντι διάγοντας, "Elephantiasis,") how many blind from their earliest youth even to old age! others who have lost their eyesight, others in poverty, others in bonds, others again in the mines, others entombed (καταχωσθέντας) together, others (slaughtered) in wars! These things say you, do not look like mercy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:204
verses.text: Say, could He not have prevented these things had He wished, yet He permits them? True, say you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:205
verses.text: Say, those who are blind from their infancy, why are they so? I will not tell you, until you promise me to receive baptism, and, being baptized, to live aright.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:206
verses.text: It is not right to give you the solution of these questions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:207
verses.text: The preaching is not meant just for amusement.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:208
verses.text: For even if I solve this, on the back of this follows another question: of such questions there is a bottomless deep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:209
verses.text: Therefore do not get into a habit of looking to have them solved for you: else we shall never stop questioning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:210
verses.text: For look, if I solve this, I do but lead the way to question upon question, numberless as the snowflakes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:211
verses.text: So that this is what we learn, rather to raise questions, not to solve the questions that are raised.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:212
verses.text: For even if we do solve them, we have not solved them altogether, but (only) as far as man's reasoning goes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:213
verses.text: The proper solution of such questions is faith: the knowing that God does all things justly and mercifully and for the best: that to comprehend the reason of them is impossible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:214
verses.text: This is the one solution, and another better than this exists not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:215
verses.text: For say, what is the use of having a question solved? This, that one needs no longer to make a question of the thing which is solved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:216
verses.text: And if thou get thyself to believe this, that all things are ordered by the Providence of God, Who, for reasons known to Himself, permits some things and actively works others, thou art rid of the need of questioning, and hast gotten the gain of the solution.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:217
verses.text: But let us come back to our subject.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:218
verses.text: Do you not see such numbers of men suffering chastisements? God (say you) permits these things to be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:219
verses.text: Make the right use of the health of the body, in order to the health of the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:220
verses.text: But you will say, What is the use to me of labors and toil, when it is in my power to get quit of all (my sins) without labor? In the first place, this is not certain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:221
verses.text: It may happen, that a person not only does not get quit of his sins without labor, but that he departs hence with all his sins upon him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:222
verses.text: However, even if this were certain, still your argument is not to be tolerated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:223
verses.text: He has drawn thee to the contests: the golden arms lie there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:224
verses.text: When you ought to take them, and to handle them, you wish to be ingloriously saved, and to do no good work! Say, if war broke out, and the Emperor were here, and you saw some charging into the midst of the phalanxes of the enemy, hewing them down, dealing wounds by thousands, others thrusting (with the sword's point), others bounding (now here, now there), others dashing on horseback, and these praised by the Emperor, admired, applauded, crowned: others on the contrary thinking themselves well off if they take no harm, and keeping in the hindmost ranks, and sitting idly there; then after the close of the war, the former sort summoned, honored with the greatest gifts, their names proclaimed by the heralds: while of the latter, not even the name becomes known, and their reward of the good obtained is only that they are safe: which sort would you wish to belong to? Why, if you were made of stone, if you were more stupid even than senseless and lifeless things, would you not ten thousand times rather belong to the former? Yea, I beseech and implore you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:225
verses.text: For if need were to fall fighting, ought you not eagerly to choose this? See you not how it is with them that have fallen in the wars, how illustrious they are, how glorious? And yet they die a death, after which there is no getting honor from the emperor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:226
verses.text: But in that other war, there is nothing of the kind, but thou shalt in any wise be presented with thy scars.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 60:227
verses.text: Which scars, even without persecutions, may it be granted all us to have to exhibit, through Jesus Christ our Lord, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, and world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:1
verses.text: Homily XXIV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:2
verses.text: Acts X.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:3
verses.text: ,  "While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:4
verses.text: And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:5
verses.text: For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:6
verses.text: Observe God's providential management.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:7
verses.text: He does not suffer the speech to be finished, nor the baptism to take place upon a command of Peter, but, when He has made it evident how admirable their state of mind is, and a beginning is made of the work of teaching, and they have believed that assuredly baptism is the remission of sins, then forthwith comes the Spirit upon them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:8
verses.text: Now this is done by God's so disposing it as to provide for Peter a mighty ground of justification.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:9
verses.text: And it is not simply that the Spirit came upon them, but, "they spake with tongues:" which was the thing that astonished those who had come together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:10
verses.text: They altogether disliked the matter, wherefore it is that the whole is of God; and as for Peter, it may almost be said, that he is present only to be taught (with them) the lesson, that they must take the Gentiles in hand, and that they themselves are the persons by whom this must be done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:11
verses.text: For whereas after all these great events, still both in Caesarea and in Jerusalem a questioning is made about it, how would it have been if these (tokens) had not gone step by step with the progress of the affair? Therefore it is that this is carried to a sort of excess.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:12
verses.text: Peter seizes his advantage, and see the plea he makes of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:13
verses.text: "Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:14
verses.text: ) Mark the issue to which he brings it; how he has been travailing to bring this forth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:15
verses.text: So (entirely) was he of this mind! "Can any one, he asks, "forbid water?" It is the language, we may almost say, of one triumphantly pressing his advantage (ἐπεμβαίνοντος) against such as would forbid, such as should say that this ought not to be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:16
verses.text: The whole thing, he says, is complete, the most essential part of the business, the baptism with which we were baptized.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:17
verses.text: "And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:19
verses.text: ) After he has cleared himself, then, and not before, he commands them to be baptized: teaching them by the facts themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:20
verses.text: Such was the dislike the Jews had to it! Therefore it is that he first clears himself, although the very facts cry aloud, and then gives the command.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:21
verses.text: "Then prayed they him"—well might they do so—"to tarry certain days:" and with a good courage thenceforth he does tarry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:22
verses.text: "And the Apostles and brethren that were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:23
