verses.text: And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him, saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:24
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:25
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:27
verses.text: ) After such great things, "they of the circumcision contended:" not the Apostles; God forbid! It means, they took no small offence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:28
verses.text: And see what they allege.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:29
verses.text: They do not say, Why didst thou preach? but, Why didst thou eat with them? But Peter, not stopping to notice this frigid objection—for frigid indeed it is—takes his stand (ἵσταται) on that great argument, If they had the Spirit Itself given them, how could one refuse to give them the baptism? But how came it that in the case of the Samaritans this did not happen, but, on the contrary, neither before their baptism nor after it was there any controversy, and there they did not take it amiss, nay, as soon as they heard of it, sent the Apostles for this very purpose? (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:30
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:31
verses.text: ) True, but neither in the present case is this the thing they complain of; for they knew that it was of Divine Grace: what they say is, Why didst thou eat with them? Besides, the difference is not so great for Samaritans as it is for Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:32
verses.text: Moreover, it is so managed (as part of the Divine plan) that he is accused in this way: on purpose that they may learn: for Peter, without some cause given, would not have related the vision.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:33
verses.text: But observe his freedom from all elation and vainglory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:34
verses.text: For it says, "But Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning, and expounded it by order unto them, saying, I was in the city of Joppa, praying:" he does not say why, nor on what occasion: "and in a trance I saw a vision, a certain vessel descend, as it had been a great sheet, let down from heaven by four corners; and it came even to me (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:35
verses.text: , ): upon the which when I had fastened mine eyes, I considered, and saw fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:36
verses.text: And I heard a voice saying unto me, Arise, Peter; slay and eat".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:39
verses.text: ) As much as to say, This of itself was enough to have persuaded me—my having seen the linen sheet: but moreover a Voice was added.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:40
verses.text: "But I said, Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath at any time entered into my mouth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:42
verses.text: ) Do you mark? "I did my part," says he: "I said, that I have never eaten aught common or unclean:" with reference to this that they said, "Thou wentest in, and didst eat with them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:43
verses.text: But this he does not say to Cornelius: for there was no need to mention it to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:44
verses.text: "But the voice answered me again from heaven, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:45
verses.text: And this was done three times: and all were drawn up again into heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:48
verses.text: ) The essential points were those (that ensued at Caesarea); but by these he prepares the way for them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:49
verses.text: Observe how he justifies himself (by reasons), and forbears to use his authority as teacher.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:50
verses.text: For the more mildly he expresses himself, the more tractable he makes them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:51
verses.text: "At no time," says he, "has aught common or unclean entered into my mouth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:52
verses.text: —And, behold—this too was part of his defence—three men stood at the house in which I was, sent to me from Caesarea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:53
verses.text: And the Spirit bade me go with them, nothing doubting".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:55
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:56
verses.text: ) Do you mark that it is to the Spirit the enacting of laws belongs! "And these also accompanied me"—nothing can be more lowly, when he alleges the brethren for witnesses!—"these six men, and we entered into the man's house: and he showed us how he had seen an angel in his house, which stood and said unto him, Send men to Joppa, and call for Simon, whose surname is Peter; who shall tell thee words, whereby thou and all thy house shall be saved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:57
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:59
verses.text: ) And he does not mention the words spoken by the Angel to Cornelius, "Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God, that he may not disgust them; but what says he? "He shall tell thee words, whereby thou and all thy house shall be saved:" with good reason this is added.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:60
verses.text: Also he says nothing of the man's fitness (ἐπιεικές).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:61
verses.text: "The Spirit," he might say, "having sent (me), God having commanded, on the one part having summoned (me) through the Angel, on the other urging (me) on, and solving my doubt about the things, what was I to do?" He says none of these things, however: but makes his strong point of what happened last, which even in itself was an incontrovertible argument.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:62
verses.text: "And as I began to speak," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:63
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:64
verses.text: ) Then why did not this happen alone? Of superabundance (ἐκ περιουσίας) this is wrought by God, that it might be shown that the beginning too was not from the Apostle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 61:65
verses.text: But had he set out of his own motion, without any of these things having taken place, they would have been very much hurt: so that from the beginning he disposes their minds in his favor.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:1
verses.text: : saying to them, "Who have received the Holy Ghost even as we".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:2
verses.text: And not content with this, he reminds them also of the words of the Lord: "Then remembered I the word of the Lord, how that he said, John indeed baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:3
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:4
verses.text: ) He means, that no new thing has happened, but just what the Lord foretold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:5
verses.text: "But there was no need to baptize?" (Comp.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:6
verses.text: p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:7
verses.text: ) But the baptism was completed already.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:8
verses.text: And he does not say, I ordered them to be baptized: but what says he? "Forasmuch then as God gave them the like gift as He did unto us, who believed on the Lord Jesus Christ; what was I, that I could withstand God?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:9
verses.text: ) He shows that he had himself done nothing: for the very thing which we have obtained, he says, that same did those men receive.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:10
verses.text: That he may more effectually stop their mouths, therefore he says, "The like gift".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:11
verses.text: Do you perceive how he does not allow them to have less: when they believed, says he, the same gift did God give unto them, as He did to us who believed on the Lord, and Himself cleanses them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:12
verses.text: And he does not say, To you, but to us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:13
verses.text: Why do you feel aggrieved, when we call them partakers (with us?) "When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:14
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:15
verses.text: ) Do you mark that it all came of Peter's discourse, by his admirably skilful way of relating the facts? They glorified God that He had given repentance to themselves (καὶ αὐτοῖς) also: they were humbled by these words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:16
verses.text: Hence was the door of faith opened thenceforth to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:17
verses.text: But, if you please, let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:18
verses.text: "While Peter yet spake," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:19
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:20
verses.text: ) He does not say that Peter was astonished, but, "They of the circumcision:" since he knew what was in preparation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:21
verses.text: And yet they ought to have marvelled at this, how they themselves had believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:22
verses.text: When they heard that they had believed, they were not astonished, but when God gave them the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:23
verses.text: Then "answered Peter and said," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:24
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:25
verses.text: ) And therefore it is that he says, "God hath shown that I should not call common or unclean any human being".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:27
verses.text: ) He knew this from the first, and plans his discourse beforehand (with a view to it).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:28
verses.text: Gentiles? What Gentiles henceforth? They were no longer Gentiles, the Truth being come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:29
verses.text: It is nothing wonderful, he says, if before the act of baptism they received the Spirit: in our own case this same happened.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:30
verses.text: Peter shows that not as the rest either were they baptized, but in a much better way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:31
verses.text: This is the reason why the thing takes place in this manner, that they may have nothing to say, but even in this way may account them equal with themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:32
verses.text: "And they besought him," it says, "to tarry certain days".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:34
verses.text: ) "And the Apostles and brethren, etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:35
verses.text: And they of the circumcision contended with him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:36
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:37
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:39
verses.text: ) Do you remark how they were not kindly disposed towards him? Saying "Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:41
verses.text: ) Do you note what zeal they had for the Law? Not Peter's authority abashed them, not the signs which had taken place, not the success achieved, what a thing it was, the Gentiles having "received the word:" but they contended about those petty things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:42
verses.text: For if none of those (signs) had taken place, was not the success (itself) enough? But not so does Peter frame his defence: for he was wise, or rather it was not his wisdom, but the Spirit that spake the words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:43
verses.text: And by the matter of his defence, he shows that in no one point was he the author, but in every point God, and upon Him he casts the whole.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:44
verses.text: "The trance," he says—"it was He that caused me to fall into it, for "I was in Joppa," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:45
verses.text: : the vessel—it was He that showed it; I objected: again, He spake, and even then I did not hear: the Spirit commanded me to go, and even then though I went, I did not run: I told that God had sent me, and after these things, even then I did not baptize, but again God did the whole.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:46
verses.text: God baptized them, not I".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:47
verses.text: And he does not say, Was it not right then to add the water? but, implying that nothing was lacking, "What was I, that I should withstand God?" What a defence is here! For he does not say, Then knowing these things, hold your peace; but what? He stands their attack, and to their impeachment he pleads—"What was I, to be able to hinder God?" It was not possible for me to hinder—a forcible plea indeed, and such as might well put them to shame.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:48
verses.text: Whence being at last afraid, "they held their peace and glorified God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:49
verses.text: In like manner ought we also to glorify God for the good things which befall our neighbors, only not in the way that the rest of the newly-baptized are insulted, when they see others receiving baptism, and immediately departing this life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:50
verses.text: It, is right to glorify God, even though all be saved: and as for thee, if thou be willing, thou hast received a greater gift (than they): I do not mean in respect of the baptism, for the gift there is the same for him as for thee, but in regard that thou hast received a set time for winning distinction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:51
verses.text: The other put on the robe, and was not suffered to exhibit himself therewith in the procession, whereas to thee, God hath given full opportunity to use thine arms for the right purpose, thereby to make proof of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:52
verses.text: The other goes his way, having only the reward of his faith: thou standest in the course, both able to obtain an abundant recompense for thy works, and to show thyself as much more glorious than he, as the sun is than the smallest star, as the general, nay rather as the Emperor himself, than the lowest soldier.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:53
verses.text: Then blame thyself, or rather not blame, but correct: for it is not enough to blame thyself; it is in thy power to contend afresh.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:54
verses.text: Hast thou been thrown? hast thou taken grievous hurt? Stand up, recover thyself: thou art still in the course, the meeting (θέατρον) is not yet broken up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:55
verses.text: Do you not see how many that have been thrown in the wrestling have afterwards resumed the combat? Only do not willingly come by thy fall.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:56
verses.text: Dost thou count him a happy man for departing this life? Much rather count thyself happy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:57
verses.text: Was he released of his sins? But thou, if thou wilt, shalt not only wash away thy sins, but shalt also have achievements (of good works), which in his case is not possible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:58
verses.text: It is in our power to recover ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:59
verses.text: Great are the medicinal virtues (φάρμακα) of repentance: let none despair of himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:60
verses.text: That man truly deserves to be despaired of, who despairs of himself; that man has no more salvation, nor any hopes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:61
verses.text: It is not the having fallen into a depth of evils, it is the lying there when fallen, that is dreadful, it is not the having come into such a condition, it is the making light of it that is impious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:62
verses.text: The very thing that ought to make thee earnest, say, is it this that makes thee reckless? Having received so many wounds, hast thou fallen back? Of the soul, there can be no incurable wound; for the body, there are many such, but none for the soul: and yet for those we cease not in our endeavors to cure them, while for these we are supine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:63
verses.text: Seest thou not the thief (on the cross), in how short a time he achieved (his salvation)? Seest thou not the Martyrs, in how short a time they accomplished the whole work? "But martyrdom is not to be had nowadays".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:64
verses.text: True, but there are contests to be had, as I have often told you, if we had the mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:65
verses.text: "For they that wish," says the Apostle, "to live godly in Christ Jesus, shall suffer persecution".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:66
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:67
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:68
verses.text: ) They that live godly are always undergoing persecution, if not from men, at any rate from evil spirits, which is a more grievous persecution.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:69
verses.text: Yes, and it is in consequence, first and foremost, of ease and comfort, that those who are not vigilant undergo this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:70
verses.text: Or thinkest thou it is a trifling persecution to be living at ease? This is more grievous than all, this is worse than persecution.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:71
verses.text: For, like a running flux, ease makes the soul languid (χαυνοἵ): and as summer and winter, so persecution and ease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:72
verses.text: But to show you that this is the worse persecution, listen: it induces sleep in the soul, an excessive yawning and drowsiness, it stirs up the passions on every side, it arms pride, it arms pleasure, it arms anger, envy, vainglory, jealousy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:73
verses.text: But in time of persecution none of these is able to make a disturbance; but fear, entering in, and plying the lash vigorously, as one does to a barking dog, will not let any of these passions so much as attempt to give tongue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:74
verses.text: Who shall be able in time of persecution to indulge in vainglory? Who to live in pleasure? Not one: but there is much trembling and fear, making a great calm, composing the harbor into stillness, filling the soul with awe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:75
verses.text: I have heard from our fathers (for in our own time God grant it may not happen, since we are bidden not to ask for temptation), that in the persecution of old time one might see men that were indeed Christian.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:76
verses.text: None of them cared for money, none for wife, none for children, nor home, nor country: the one great concern with all was to save their lives (or, souls).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:77
verses.text: There were they hiding, some in tombs and sepulchres, some in deserts: yes tender and dainty women too, fighting all the while with constant hunger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:78
verses.text: Then think whether any longing for sumptuous and dainty living at all came into the mind of a woman, while in hiding beside a coffin (παρὰ λάρνακι), and waiting for her maid-servant to bring her meal, and trembling lest she should be taken, and lying in her terror as in a furnace: was she even aware that there ever was such a thing as dainty living, that such things as dress and ornaments exist at all (ὅτι κόσμος ὅλως ἐστίν)? Seest thou that now is the persecution, with our passions, like wild beasts, setting upon us on every side? Now is the trying persecution, both in this regard, and especially if it is not even thought to be persecution at all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:79
verses.text: For this (persecution) has also this evil in it, that being war, it is thought to be peace, so that we do not even arm ourselves against it, so that we do not even rise: no one fears, no one trembles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:80
verses.text: But if ye do not believe me, ask the heathen, the persecutors, at what time was the conduct of the Christians more strict, at what time were they all more proved? Few indeed had they then become in number, but rich in virtue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:81
verses.text: For say, what profit is it, that there should be hay in plenty, when there might be precious stones? The amount consists not in the sum of numbers, but in the proved worth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:82
verses.text: Elias was one: yet the whole world was not worth so much as he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:83
verses.text: And yet the world consists of myriads: but they are no myriads, when they do not even come up to that one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:84
verses.text: "Better is one that doeth the will of God, than ten thousand who are transgressors:" for the ten thousands have not yet reached to the one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:85
verses.text: "Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:86
verses.text: (Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:87
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:88
verses.text: ) Such bring more blasphemy against God, than if they were not Christians.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:89
verses.text: What need have I of a multitude? It is (only) more food for the fire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:90
verses.text: This one might see even in the body, that better is moderate food with health, than a (fatted) calf with damage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:91
verses.text: This is more food than the other: this is food, but that is disease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:92
verses.text: This too one may see in war: that better are ten expert and brave men, than ten thousand of no experience.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:93
verses.text: These latter, besides that they do no work, hinder also those that do work.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:94
verses.text: The same too one may see to be the case in a ship, viz.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:95
verses.text: that better are two experienced mariners, than ever so great a number of unskilful ones: for these will sink the ship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:96
verses.text: These things I say, not as looking with an evil eye upon your numbers, but wishing that all of you should be approved men, and not trust in your numbers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:97
verses.text: Many more in number are they who go down into hell: but greater than it is the Kingdom, however few it contain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:98
verses.text: As the sand of the sea was the multitude of the people (Israel) yet one man saved them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:99
verses.text: Moses was but one, and yet he availed more than they all: Joshua was one and he was enabled to do more than the six hundred thousand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:100
verses.text: Let us not make this our study merely, that (the people) may be many, but rather, that they may be excellent; when this shall have been effected, then will that other follow also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:101
verses.text: No one wishes at the outset to make a spacious house, but he first makes it strong and sure, then spacious: no one lays the foundations so that he may be laughed at.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:102
verses.text: Let us first aim at this, and then at the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:103
verses.text: Where this is, that also will be easy: but where this is not, the other, though it be, is to no profit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:104
verses.text: For if there be those who are able to shine in the Church, there will soon be also numbers: but where these are not, the numbers will never be good for anything.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:105
verses.text: How many, suppose you, may there be in our city who are likely to be saved (τοὺς σωζομένους)? It is disagreeable, what I am going to say, but I will say it nevertheless.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:106
verses.text: Among all these myriads, there are not to be found one hundred likely to be saved: nay, even as to these, I question it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:107
verses.text: For think, what wickedness there is in the young, what supineness in the aged! None makes it his duty to look after his own boy, none is moved by anything to be seen in his elder, to be emulous of imitating such an one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:108
verses.text: The patterns are defaced, and therefore it is that neither do the young become admirable in conduct.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:109
verses.text: Tell not me, "We are a goodly multitude:" this is the speech of men who talk without thought or feeling (ψυχρὥν.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:110
verses.text: ) In the concerns of men indeed, this might be said with some show of reason: but where God is concerned, (to say this with regard to Him) as having need of us, can never be allowed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:111
verses.text: Nay, let me tell you, even in the former case, this is a senseless speech (ψυχρόν).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:112
verses.text: Listen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:113
verses.text: A person that has a great number of domestics, if they be a corrupt set what a wretched time will he have of it! For him who has none, the hardship, it seems, amounts to this, that he is not waited on: but where a person has bad servants, the evil is, that he is ruining himself withal, and the damage is greater (the more there are of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:114
verses.text: ) For it is far worse than having to be one's own servant, to have to fight with others, and take up a (continual) warfare.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:115
verses.text: These things I say, that none may admire the Church because of its numbers, but that we may study to make the multitude proof-worthy; that each may be earnest for his own share of the duty—not for his friends only, nor his kindred as I am always saying, nor for his neighbors, but that he may attract the strangers also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:116
verses.text: For example, Prayer is going on; there they lie (on bended knees), all the young, stupidly unconcerned (ψυχροὶ), (yes,) and old too: filthy nuisances rather than young men; giggling, laughing outright, talking—for I have heard even this going on—and jeering one another as they lie along on their knees: and there stand you, young man or elder: rebuke them, if you see them (behaving thus): if any will not refrain, chide him more severely: call the deacon, threaten, do what is in your power to do: and if he dare do anything to you, assuredly you shall have all to help you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:117
verses.text: For who is so irrational, as, when he sees you chiding for such conduct, and them chidden not to take your part? Depart, having received your reward from the Prayer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:118
verses.text: —In a master's house, we count those his best-disposed servants, who cannot bear to see any part of his furniture in disorder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:119
verses.text: Answer me; if at home you should see the silver plate lie tossed out of doors, though it is not your business, you will pick it up and bring it into the house: if you see a garment flung out of its place, though you have not the care of it, though you be at enmity with him whose business it is, yet, out of good-will to the master, will you not put it right? So in the present case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:120
verses.text: These are part of the furniture: if you see them lying about in disorder, put them to rights: apply to me, I do not refuse the trouble: inform me, make the offender known to me: it is not possible for me to see all: excuse me (in this).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:121
verses.text: See, what wickedness overspreads the whole world! Said I without reason that we are (no better than) so much hay (disorderly as) a troubled sea? I am not talking of those (young people), that they behave thus; (what I complain of, is) that such a sleepy indifference possesses those who come in here, that they do not even correct this misbehavior.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:122
verses.text: Again I see others stand talking while Prayer is going on; while the more consistent of them (do this) not only during the Prayer, but even when the Priest is giving the Benediction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:123
verses.text: O, horror! When shall there be salvation? when shall it be possible for us to propitiate God?—Soldiers go to their diversion, and you shall see them, all keeping time in the dance, and nothing done negligently, but, just as in embroidery and painting, from the well-ordered arrangement in each individual part of the composition, there results at once an exceeding harmony and good keeping, so it is here: we have one shield, one head, all of us (in common): and if but some casual point be deranged by negligence, the whole is deranged and is spoilt, and the good order of the many is defeated by the disorder of the one part.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:124
verses.text: And, fearful indeed to think of, here you come, not to a diversion, not to act in a dance, and yet you stand disorderly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:125
verses.text: Know you not that you are standing in company with angels? with them you chant, with them sing hymns, and do you stand laughing? Is it not wonderful that a thunderbolt is not launched not only at those (who behave thus), but at us? For such behavior might well be visited with the thunderbolt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:126
verses.text: The Emperor is present, is reviewing the army: and do you, even with His eyes upon you, stand laughing, and endure to see another laughing? How long are we to go on chiding, how long complaining? Ought not such to be treated as very pests and nuisances; as abandoned, worthless reprobates, fraught with innumerable mischiefs, to be driven away from the Church? When will these forebear laughing, who laugh in the hour of the dread Mystery (ἑν ὣρᾳ φρίκης)? when refrain from their trifling, who talk at the instant of the Benediction? Have they no sense of shame before those who are present? have they no fear of God? Are our own idle thoughts not enough for us, is it not enough that in our prayers we rove hither and thither, but laughter also must needs intrude, and bursts of merriment? Is it a theatrical amusement, what is done here? Aye, but, methinks, it is the theatres that do this: to the theatres we owe it that the most of you so refuse to be curbed by us, and to be reformed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:127
verses.text: What we build up here, is thrown down there: and not only so, but the hearers themselves cannot help being filled with other filthinesses besides: so that the case is just the same as if one should want to clean out a place with a fountain above it discharging mire; for however much you may clean out, more runs in.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:128
verses.text: So it is here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:129
verses.text: For when we clean people out, as they come here from the theatres with their filthiness, thither they go again, and take in a larger stock of filthiness, as if they lived for the purpose of only giving us trouble, and then come back to us, laden with ordure, in their manners, in their movements, in their words, in their laughter, in their idleness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:130
verses.text: Then once more we begin shovelling it out afresh, as if we had to do this only on purpose that, having sent them away clean, we may again see them clogging themselves with filth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:131
verses.text: Therefore I solemnly protest to you, the sound members, that this will be to you judgment and condemnation, and I give you over to God from this time forth, if any having seen a person behaving disorderly, if any having seen any person talking, especially in that part (of the Service), shall not inform against him, not bring him round (to a better behavior).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:132
verses.text: To do this is better than prayer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 63:133
verses.text: Leave thy prayer and rebuke him, that thou mayst both do him good, and thyself get profit, and so we may be enabled all to be saved and to attain unto the Kingdom of Heaven, through the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, and world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:1
verses.text: Homily XXV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:2
verses.text: Acts XI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:3
verses.text: "Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that rose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:4
verses.text: The persecution turned out to be no slight benefit as "to them that love God all things work together for good".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:5
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:6
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:7
verses.text: ) If they had made it their express study how best to establish the Church, they would have done no other thing than this—they dispersed the teachers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:8
verses.text: Mark in what quarters the preaching was extended.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:9
verses.text: "They travelled," it says, "as far as Phenice and Cyprus and Antioch; to none however did they preach the word but to Jews only".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:10
verses.text: Dost thou mark with what wise purposes of Providence so much was done in the case of Cornelius? This serves both to justify Christ, and to impeach the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:11
verses.text: When Stephen was slain, when Paul was twice in danger, when the Apostles were scourged, then the Gentiles received the word, then the Samaritans.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:12
verses.text: Which Paul also declares: "To you it was necessary that the Word of God should first be spoken; but since ye thrust it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy, lo, we turn unto the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:13
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:14
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:15
verses.text: ) Accordingly they went about, preaching to Gentiles also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:16
verses.text: "But some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they were come to Antioch, spake unto the Greeks, preaching the Lord Jesus:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:17
verses.text: ) for it is likely both that they could now speak Greek, and that there were such men in Antioch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:18
verses.text: "And the hand of the Lord," it says, "was with them," that is, they wrought miracles; "and a great number believed, and turned unto the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:20
verses.text: ) Do you mark why now also there was heed of miracles (namely) that they might believe? "Then tidings of these things came unto the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:22
verses.text: ) What may be the reason that, when such a city received the word, they did not come themselves? Because of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:23
verses.text: But they send Barnabas.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:24
verses.text: However, it is no small part of the providential management even so that Paul comes to be there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:25
verses.text: It is both natural, and it is wisely ordered, that they are averse to him, and (so) that Voice of the Gospel, that Trumpet of heaven, is not shut up in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:26
verses.text: Do you mark how on all occasions, Christ turns their ill dispositions to needful account and for the benefit of the Church? Of their hatred to the man, He availed Himself for the building up of the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:27
verses.text: But observe this holy man—Barnabas, I mean—how he looked not to his own interests, but hasted to Tarsus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:28
verses.text: "Who, when he came, and had seen the grace of God, was glad, and exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart, they would cleave unto the Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:29
verses.text: For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost, and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:30
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:32
verses.text: ) He was a very kind man, and single-hearted, and considerate (συγγνωμονικός).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:33
verses.text: "Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus, for to seek Saul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:35
verses.text: ) He came to the athletic wrestler, the general (fit to lead armies), the champion of single combat, the lion—I am at a loss for words, say what I will—the hunting-dog, killer of lions, bull of strength, lamp of brightness, mouth sufficing for a world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:36
verses.text: "And when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:38
verses.text: ) Verily this is the reason why it was there they were appointed to be called Christians, because Paul there spent so long time! "And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the Church, and taught much people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:39
verses.text: And the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:40
verses.text: No small matter of praise to that city! This is enough to make it a match for all, that for so long a time it had the benefit of that mouth, it first, and before all others: wherefore also it was there in the first place that men were accounted worthy of that name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:41
verses.text: Do you observe the benefit resulting (to that city) from Paul, to what a height that name, like a standard (σημεἵον), exalted it? Where three thousand, where five thousand, believed, where so great a multitude, nothing of the sort took place, but they were called "they of the way:" here they were called Christians.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:42
verses.text: "And in these days came prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:43
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:44
verses.text: ) It was need that the fruit of alms should also be planted there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:45
verses.text: And see how of necessity (ἀναγκαίως) (it comes about that) none of the men of note becomes their teacher.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:46
verses.text: They got for their teachers, men of Cyprus, and Cyrene, and Paul—though he indeed surpassed (the Apostles) themselves—since Paul also had for teachers Ananias and Barnabas.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:47
verses.text: But here of necessity (this was the case).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:48
verses.text: "And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the spirit that there would be great dearth throughout the world, which also came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:49
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:50
verses.text: ) "By the Spirit," it says: for, that they may not imagine that this was the reason why the famine came, (namely) because Christianity was come in, because the demons were departed, the Holy Ghost foretells it: this, however, was nothing wonderful, for in fact Christ predicted it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:51
verses.text: Not this was the reason, else this must have been the case from the beginning: but it was because of the evils done to the Apostles—and God had borne long with them; but, when they pressed upon them, a great famine ensues, betokening to the Jews the coming woes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:52
verses.text: "If it was because of them, in any wise it ought to have stopped (there), when it did exist.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:53
verses.text: What harm had the Gentiles done, that they should have their share in the evils? They ought rather to have been marked as approved (εὐδοκιμἥσαι), because they were doing their part, were slaying, punishing, taking vengeance, persecuting on every side.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:54
verses.text: And mark also at what time the famine comes: precisely when the Gentiles were thenceforth added to the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:55
verses.text: But if, as you say, it was because of the evils (done by the Jews), these ought to have been exempted".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:56
verses.text: How so? Christ, forestalling this objection, said, "Ye shall have tribulation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:57
verses.text: (John xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:58
verses.text: ) (It is) just as if you should say, They ought not to have been scourged either.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:59
verses.text: "Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judea".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:60
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:61
verses.text: ) Mark how the famine becomes to them the means of salvation, an occasion of alms-giving, a harbinger of many blessing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:62
verses.text: And (so it might have been) to you, one may say, if you were so minded, but ye would not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:63
verses.text: But it is predicted, that they might be prepared beforehand for almsgiving.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:64
verses.text: "Unto the brethren which dwelt in Judaea;" for they were enduring great hardships, but before this, they were not suffering from famine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:65
verses.text: "Which also they did, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:66
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:67
verses.text: ) Do you mark them, that no sooner do they believe than they bring forth fruit, not only for their own but for those afar off? And Barnabas is sent and Saul, to minister (the same.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:68
verses.text: ) Of this occasion (᾽Ενταὕθα) he says (to the Galatians), "And James, Cephas, and John gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, only" (they would) "that we should remember the poor".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:69
verses.text: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:70
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:71
verses.text: ) James was yet living.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:72
verses.text: "Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:73
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:74
verses.text: ) Do you mark how even in the tribulation instead of falling to lamentations and tears, as we do, they give themselves up to a great and good work? "Travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch," and there with more security preached the word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:75
verses.text: "And some of them, which were men of Cyprus and Cyrene," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:76
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:77
verses.text: ) And they did not say, "(What), we, Cyrenians and Cyprians, to attack this splendid and great city!" but trusting in the grace of God, they applied themselves to the work of teaching, nor did these (Gentiles) themselves think scorn to learn anything of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:78
verses.text: Mark how by small means all is brought about: mark the preaching how it spreads: mark those in Jerusalem, having like care for all, holding the whole world as one house.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:79
verses.text: "They heard that Samaria had received the word, and" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:80
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:81
verses.text: ) to Samaria they send the Apostles: they heard what had befallen at Antioch, and to Antioch they send Barnabas: they also send again, and (these) prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:82
verses.text: For the distance was great, and it was not meet the Apostles at present should separate from thence, that they might not be thought to be fugitives, and to have fled from their own people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:83
verses.text: But then, almost precisely, is the time of their parting from Jerusalem, when the state (of the Jews) was shown to be past remedy, when the war was close at hand, and they must needs perish: when the sentence was made absolute.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:84
verses.text: For, until Paul went to Rome, the Apostles were there (at Jerusalem).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:85
verses.text: But they depart, not because afraid of the war—how should it be so?—seeing those they went to, were those that should bring the war: and moreover the war breaks out only after the Apostles were dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:86
verses.text: For of them (the Apostles) says, "The wrath is come upon them unto the end".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:87
verses.text: ( Thess.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:88
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:89
verses.text: ) The more insignificant the persons, the more illustrious the grace, working great results by small means.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:90
verses.text: —"And he exhorted them to cleave unto the Lord, for he was a good man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:91
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:92
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:93
verses.text: ) By "good man," I take it, he means one that is kind, (χρηστὸν) sincere, exceedingly desirous of the salvation of his neighbors—"for he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:94
verses.text: To cleave unto the Lord with purpose of heart" (this is said): with encomium and praise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:95
verses.text: "And much people was added unto the Lord:" for like rich land this city received the word, and brought forth much fruit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:96
verses.text: "Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:97
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:98
verses.text: ) But why did he take him off from Tarsus and bring him here? Not without good reason; for here were both good hopes, and a greater city, and a great body of people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:99
verses.text: See how grace works all, not Paul: by small means the affair was taking its commencement.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:100
verses.text: When it is become difficult the Apostles take it up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:101
verses.text: Why did they not before this seen Barnabas? Because they had enough to do (ἠσχόληντο) with Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:102
verses.text: Again they justified themselves to the Jews, that the Gentiles were receiving (προσελάμβανε) the word, even without enjoying so great attention.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:103
verses.text: There is about to be a questioning: therefore the affair of Cornelius forestalled it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:104
verses.text: Then indeed they say, "That we to the Gentiles, and they to the Circumcision".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:105
verses.text: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:106
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:107
verses.text: ) Observe, henceforth the very stress of the famine introduces the fellowship on the part of the Gentiles, namely, from the alms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:108
verses.text: For they receive the offerings sent from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:109
verses.text: "Now they which were scattered abroad," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:110
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:111
verses.text: ) and not as we who pass our time in lamentations and tears, in our calamities; but with more fearlessness they passed their time, as having got to a distance from those hindering them, and as being among men not afraid of the Jews: which also helped.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:112
verses.text: And they came to Cyprus, where they had the sea between them, and greater freedom from anxiety: so they made no account of the fear of men, but (still) they gave the precedence to the regard of the Law: "they spake to Jews only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:113
verses.text: But there were in Antioch certain men of Cyprus and Cyrene:" these, of all others, least cared for the Jews: "who spake unto the Greeks, preaching the Lord Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:114
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:115
verses.text: ) Probably it was because of their not knowing Hebrew, that they called them Greeks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:116
verses.text: And "when" Barnabas, it says, "came and had seen the grace of God,"—not the diligence of men—"he exhorted them to cleave unto the Lord" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:117
verses.text: ): and by this he converted more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:118
verses.text: "And much people was added unto the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:119
verses.text: Why do they not write to Paul, but send Barnabas? They did not yet know the virtue of the man: but it is providentially ordered that Barnabas should come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:120
verses.text: As there was a multitude, and none to hinder, well might the faith grow, and above all because they had no trials to undergo.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:121
verses.text: Paul also preaches, and is no longer compelled to flee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:122
verses.text: And it is well ordered, that not they speak of the famine, but the prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:123
verses.text: The men of Antioch also did not take it amiss that they sent not the Apostles, but were content with their teachers: so fervent were they all for the word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:124
verses.text: They did not wait for the famine to come, but before this they sent: "according as each had the ability".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:125
verses.text: And observe, among the Apostles, others are put in charge with this trust, but here Paul and Barnabas.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:126
verses.text: For this was no small order (οἰκονομία) of Providence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:127
verses.text: Besides, it was the beginning, and it was not fit they should be offended.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:128
verses.text: "As each had the ability, they sent".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:129
verses.text: But now, none does this, although there is a famine more grievous than that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:130
verses.text: For the cases are not alike, for (all) to bear the calamity in common, and, while all (the rest) abound, for the poorer to be famishing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:131
verses.text: And the expression shows that the givers also were poor, for, it says, "as each of them had the means".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:132
verses.text: A twofold famine, even as the abundance is twofold: a severe famine, a famine not of hearing the word of the Lord, but of being nourished by alms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:133
verses.text: Then, both the poor in Judea enjoyed the benefit, and so did those in Antioch who gave their money; yea, these more than those: but now, both we and the poor are famishing: they being in lack of necessary sustenance, and we in luxurious living, lacking the mercy of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:134
verses.text: But this is a food, than which nothing can be more necessary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:135
verses.text: This is not a food, from which one has to undergo the evils of repletion: not a food, of which the most part ends in the draught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:136
verses.text: (ἀφεδρὥνα.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:137
verses.text: ) Nothing more beauteous, nothing more healthful, than a soul nurtured by this food: it is set high above all disease, all pestilence, all indigestion and distemper: none shall be able to overcome it, (ἑλεἵν) but just as, if one's body were made of adamant, no iron, nor anything else, would have power to hurt it, even so when the soul is firmly compact by almsgiving, nothing at all shall be able to overcome it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:138
verses.text: For say, what shall spoil this? Shall poverty? It cannot be, for it is laid up in the royal treasuries.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:139
verses.text: But shall robber and housebreaker? Nay, those are walls which none shall be able to break through.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:140
verses.text: But shall the worm? Nay, this treasure is set far above the reach of this mischief also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:141
verses.text: But shall envy and the evil eye? Nay, neither by these can it be overcome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:142
verses.text: But shall false accusations and plottings of evil? No, neither shall this be, for safe as in an asylum is this treasure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:143
verses.text: But it were a shame should I make it appear as if the advantages which belong to almsgiving were only these (the absence of these evils), and not (the presence of) their opposites.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:144
verses.text: For in truth it is not merely that it is secure from ill-will; it also gets abundant blessing from those whom it benefits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:145
verses.text: For as the cruel and unmerciful not only have for enemies those whom they have injured, but those also who are not themselves hurt, partake the grief and join in the accusation: so those that have done great good have not only those who are benefited, but those also who are not themselves affected, to speak their praises.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:146
verses.text: Again (that), it is secure from the attacks of the evil-disposed, and robbers, and housebreakers—what, is this all the good, or is it this—that besides the not suffering diminution, it grows also and increases into multitude? What more shameful than Nebuchadnezzar, what more foul, what more iniquitous? The man was impious; after tokens and signs without number he refused to come to his senses (ανενεγκεἵν), but cast the servants of God into a furnace: and (yet) after these doings, he worshipped.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:147
verses.text: What then said the Prophet? "Wherefore," saith he, "O king let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, ransom (λύτρωσαι) thy sins by alms, and thine iniquities by mercies to the poor: peradventure there shall be pardon for thy transgressions".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:148
verses.text: (Dan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:149
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:150
verses.text: ) In so speaking, he said it not doubting, nay, with entire confidence, but wishing to put him in greater fear, and to make a stronger necessity of doing these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:151
verses.text: For if he had spoken it as a thing unquestionable, the king would have been more supine: just as it is with us, we then most urge some person (whom we wish to persuade), when they say to us, "Exhort such an one," and do not add, "he will be sure to hear," but only, "peradventure he will hear:" for by leaving it doubtful, the fear is made greater, and urges him the more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:152
verses.text: This is the reason why the Prophet did not make the thing certain to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:153
verses.text: What sayest thou? For so great impieties shall there be pardon? Yes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:154
verses.text: There is no sin, which alms cannot cleanse, none, which alms cannot quench: all sin is beneath this: it is a medicine adapted for every wound.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:155
verses.text: What worse than a publican? The very matter (ὑπόθεσις) (of his occupation) is altogether one of injustice: and yet Zaccheus washed away all these (sins).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:156
verses.text: Mark how even Christ shows this, by the care taken to have a purse, and to bear the contributions put into it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:157
verses.text: And Paul also says, "Only that we remember the poor" (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:158
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:159
verses.text: ): and everywhere the Scripture has much discourse concerning this matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:160
verses.text: "The ransom," it saith, "of a man's soul is his own wealth" (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:161
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:162
verses.text: ): and with reason: for, saith (Christ), "if thou wouldest be perfect, sell what thou hast, and give to the poor, and come, follow Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:163
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:164
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:165
verses.text: ) This may well be part of perfection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:166
verses.text: But alms may be done not only by money, but by acts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:167
verses.text: For example: one may kindly stand (προστἥναι) by a person (to succor and defend him), one may reach to him a helping hand: the service rendered (προστασία) by acts has often done more good even than money.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:168
verses.text: Let us set to work all the different kinds of almsgiving.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:169
verses.text: Can you do alms by money? Be not slack.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:170
verses.text: Can you by good offices? Say not, Because I have no money, this is nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:171
verses.text: This is a very great point: look upon it as if you had given gold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:172
verses.text: Can you do it by kind attentions (θεραπείας)? Do this also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:173
verses.text: For instance, if you be a physician, (give) your skill: for this also is a great matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:174
verses.text: Can you by counsel? This (service) is much greater than all: this (alms) is better than all, or it is also more, by how much the gain it has is greater.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:175
verses.text: For in so doing you put away not starvation, but a grievous death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:176
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:177
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:178
verses.text: ; vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:179
verses.text: ) With such alms the Apostles above measure abounded: therefore it was that the distribution of money they put into the hands of those after them, themselves exhibiting the (mercy) shown by words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:180
verses.text: Or is it, think you, a small alms, to a lost, castaway soul, a soul in uttermost jeopardy, possessed by a burning fever (πυρώσεως), to be able to rid it of its disease? For example, do you see one possessed by love of money? Pity the man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:181
verses.text: Is he in danger of suffocation? Quench his fire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:182
verses.text: "What if he will not be persuaded?" Do your part, and be not remiss.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:183
verses.text: Have you seen him in bonds?—for wealth is indeed bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:184
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:185
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:186
verses.text: ff.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:187
verses.text: ) Go to him, visit him, console him, try to release him of his bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:188
verses.text: If he refuse, he shall bear the blame himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:189
verses.text: Have you seen him naked, and a stranger?—for he is indeed naked, and a stranger to heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:190
verses.text: Bring him to your own inn, clothe him with the garment of virtue, give him the city which is in heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:191
verses.text: "What if I myself be naked?" say you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:192
verses.text: Clothe also yourself first: if you know that you are naked, assuredly you know that you need to be clothed; if you know what sort of nakedness this is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:193
verses.text: What numbers of women now wear silken apparel but are indeed naked of the garments of virtue! Let their husbands clothe these women.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:194
verses.text: "But they will not admit those garments; they choose to have these".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:195
verses.text: Then do this also first: induce them to have a longing for those garments: show them that they are naked: speak to them of judgment to come: answer me, what is the clothing we shall need there? But if ye will bear with me, I also will show you this nakedness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:196
verses.text: He that is naked, when it is cold, shrinks and shudders, and stands there cowering, and with his arms folded: but in summer heat, not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:197
verses.text: If then I shall prove to you that your rich men, and rich women, the more they put on, the more naked they are, do not take it amiss.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:198
verses.text: How then, I ask you, when we raise the subject of hell-fire, and of the torments there? Do not these shrink and shudder more than those naked ones? Do they not bitterly groan and condemn themselves? What? when they come to this or that man, and say to him, Pray for me, do they not speak the same words as those (naked wretches)?  Now indeed, after all that we can say, the nakedness is not yet apparent: but it will be plain enough there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:199
verses.text: How, and in what way? When these silken garments and precious stones shall have perished, and it shall be only by the garments of virtue and of vice that all men are shown, when the poor shall be clad with exceeding glory, but the rich, naked and in disgraceful sort, shall be haled away to their punishments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:200
verses.text: What more naked (Edd.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:201
verses.text: "more dainty") than that rich man who arrayed himself in purple? What poorer than Lazarus? Then which of them uttered the words of beggars? which of them was in abundance? Say, if one should deck his house with abundance of tapestry hangings, and himself sit naked within, what were the benefit? So it is in the case of these women.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:202
verses.text: Truly, the house of the soul, the body I mean, they hang round with plenty of garments: but the mistress of the house sits naked within.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:203
verses.text: Lend me the eyes of the soul, and I will show you the soul's nakedness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:204
verses.text: For what is the garment of the soul? Virtue, of course.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:205
verses.text: And what its nakedness? Vice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:206
verses.text: For just as, if one were to strip any decent person, that person would be ashamed, and would shrink and cower out of sight; just so the soul, if we wish to see it, the soul which has not these garments, blushes for shame.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:207
verses.text: How many women, think you, at this moment feel ashamed, and would fain sink to the very depth, as if seeking some sort of curtain, or screen, that they may not hear these words? But those who have no evil conscience, are exhilarated, rejoice, find delight, and gayly deck themselves (ἐγκαλλωπίζονται) with the things said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:208
verses.text: Hear concerning that blessed Thekla, how, that she might see Paul, she gave even her gold: and thou wilt not give even a farthing that thou mayest see Christ: thou admirest what she did, but dost not emulate her.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:209
verses.text: Hearest thou not that "Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy?" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:210
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 64:211
verses.text: ) What is the gain of your costly garments? how long shall we continue agape for this attire? Let us put on the glory of Christ: let us array ourselves with that beauty, that both here we may be praised, and there attain unto the eternal good things, by the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom, to the Father and the Holy Ghost together, be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:1
verses.text: Homily XXVI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:2
verses.text: Acts XII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:3
verses.text: ,  "Now at that time Herod the King stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:4
verses.text: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:5
verses.text: And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:6
verses.text: Then were the days of unleavened bread".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:7
verses.text: "At that time," of course meaning the time immediately following: for this is the custom of Scripture.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:8
verses.text: And he well says that Herod "the king" (did this): this was not he of Christ's time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:9
verses.text: Lo, a different sort of trial—and mark what I said in the beginning, how things are blended, how rest and trouble alternate in the whole texture of the history—not now the Jews, nor the Sanhedrim, but the king.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:10
verses.text: Greater the power, the warfare more severe, the more it was done to obtain favor with the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:11
verses.text: "And," it says, "he slew James the brother of John with the sword:" (taking him) at random and without selection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:12
verses.text: But, should any raise a question, why God permitted this, we shall say, that it was for the sake of these (Jews) themselves: thereby, first, convincing them, that even when slain (the Apostles) prevail, just as it was in the case of Stephen: secondly, giving them opportunity, after satiating their rage, to recover from their madness; thirdly, showing them that it was by His permission this was done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:13
verses.text: "And when he saw," it says, "that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to seize Peter also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:14
verses.text: O excessive wickedness! On whose behalf was it, that he gratified them by doing murders thus without plan or reason? "And it was the day of unleavened bread".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:15
verses.text: Again, the idle preciseness of the Jews: to kill indeed they forbade not, but at such a time they did such things! "Whom having arrested, he put in ward, having delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:16
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:17
verses.text: ) This was done both of rage, and of fear.
