verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:18
verses.text: "He slew," it says, "James the brother of John with the sword".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:19
verses.text: Do you mark their courage? For, that none may say that without danger or fear of danger they brave death, as being sure of God's delivering them, therefore he permits some to be put to death, and chief men too, Stephen and James, thereby convincing their slayers themselves, that not even these things make them fall away, and hinder them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:20
verses.text: "Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the Church unto God for him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:22
verses.text: ) For the contest was now for life and death: both the slaying of the one made them fearful, and the casting of the other into prison.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:23
verses.text: "And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains; and the keepers before the door kept the prison.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:24
verses.text: And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:25
verses.text: And his chains fell off from his hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:28
verses.text: ) In that night He delivered him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:29
verses.text: "And a light shined in the prison," that he might not deem it fancy: and none saw the light, but he only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:30
verses.text: For if, notwithstanding this was done, he thought it a fancy, because of its unexpectedness; if this had not been, much more would he have thought this: so prepared was he for death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:31
verses.text: For his having waited there many days and not being saved caused this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:32
verses.text: Why then, say you, did He not suffer him to fall into the hands of Herod, and then deliver him? Because that would have brought people into astonishment, whereas this was credible: and they would not even have been thought human beings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:33
verses.text: But in the case of Stephen, what did He not do? Did He not show them his face as it had been the face of an angel? But what in short did He leave undone here also? "And the angel said to him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:35
verses.text: ) Here again it shows, that it was not done of craft: for one that is in haste and wishes to break out (of prison), is not so particular as to take his sandals, and gird himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:36
verses.text: "And he did so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:37
verses.text: And he said unto him, Put on thy cloak, and follow me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:38
verses.text: And he went out, and followed him; and wist not that it was true which was done by the Angel; but thought he saw a vision.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:39
verses.text: When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of its own accord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:42
verses.text: ) Behold, a second miracle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:43
verses.text: "And they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:44
verses.text: And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the Lord hath sent His Angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:47
verses.text: ) When the angel departed, then Peter understood: "Now I perceive," says he, not then.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:48
verses.text: But why is this so, and why is Peter not sensible of the things taking place, although he had already experienced a like deliverance when all were released? (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:49
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:50
verses.text: ) (The Lord) would have the pleasure come to him all at once, and that he should first be at liberty, and then be sensible of what had happened.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:51
verses.text: The circumstance also of the chains having fallen off from his hands, is a strong argument of his not having fled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:52
verses.text: "And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:54
verses.text: ) Observe how Peter does not immediately withdraw, but first brings the good tidings to his friends.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:55
verses.text: "And as Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:56
verses.text: And when she knew Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for gladness,"—Mark even the servant-girls, how full of piety they are,—"but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:57
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:59
verses.text: ) But they, though it was so, shook their heads (incredulously): "And they said unto her, Thou art mad.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:60
verses.text: But she constantly affirmed that it was even so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:61
verses.text: And they said, It is his angel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:62
verses.text: "But Peter continued knocking: and when they had opened the door, and saw him, they were astonished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:63
verses.text: But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:64
verses.text: And he said, Go show these things unto James, and to the brethren.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:65
verses.text: And he departed, and went into another place".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:66
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:67
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:68
verses.text: ) But let us review the order of the narrative.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:69
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:70
verses.text: ) "At that time," it says, "Herod the king stretched forth his hands to afflict certain of the Church".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:71
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:72
verses.text: ) Like a wild beast, he attacked all indiscriminately and without consideration.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:73
verses.text: This is what Christ said: "My cup indeed ye shall drink, and with the baptism wherewith I am baptized, shall ye be baptized".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:74
verses.text: (Mark x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:75
verses.text: ) (b) "And he killed James the brother of John".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:76
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:77
verses.text: ) For there was also another James, the brother of the Lord: therefore to distinguish him, he says, "The brother of John".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:78
verses.text: Do you mark that the sum of affairs rested in these three, especially Peter and James? (a) And how was it he did not kill Peter immediately? It mentions the reason: "it was the day of unleavened bread:" and he wished rather to make a display (ἐκπομπεὕσαι) with the killing of him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:79
verses.text: "And when he saw it pleased the Jews".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:80
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:81
verses.text: ) For their own part, they now in consequence of Gamaliel's advice, abstained from bloodshedding: and besides, did not even invent accusations; but by means of others they compassed the same results.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:82
verses.text: (c) This (counsel of Gamaliel's) above all was their condemnation: for the preaching was shown to be no longer a thing of men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:83
verses.text: "He proceeded further to kill Peter also".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:84
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:85
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:86
verses.text: ) In very deed was that fulfilled, "We are accounted as sheep for the slaughter".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:87
verses.text: (Psa.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:88
verses.text: xliv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:89
verses.text: ) "Seeing," it says, "it was a pleasing thing to the Jews".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:90
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:91
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:92
verses.text: ) A pleasing thing, bloodshed, and unrighteous bloodshed, wickedness, impiety! He ministered to their senseless (ἀτόποις) lusts: for, whereas he ought to have done the contrary, to check their rage, he made them more eager, as if he were an executioner, and not a physician to their diseased minds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:93
verses.text: (And this) though he had numberless warnings in the case of both his grandfather and his father Herod, how the former in consequence of his putting the children to death suffered the greatest calamities, and the latter by slaying John raised up against himself a grievous war.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 65:94
verses.text: But as they thought.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:1
verses.text: He feared lest Peter, in consequence of the slaying of James, should withdraw; and wishing to have him in safe keeping, he put him in prison: "and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:2
verses.text: ): the stricter the custody, the more wondrous the display.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:3
verses.text: "Peter therefore was kept in prison".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:4
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:5
verses.text: ) But this was all the better for Peter, who was thereby made more approved, and evinced his own manly courage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:6
verses.text: And it says, "there was earnest prayer making".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:7
verses.text: It was the prayer of (filial) affection: it was for a father they asked, a father mild.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:8
verses.text: "There was," it says, "earnest prayer".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:9
verses.text: Hear how they were affected to their teachers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:10
verses.text: No factions, no perturbation: but they betook them to prayer, to that alliance which is indeed invincible, to this they betook them for refuge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:11
verses.text: They did not say, "What? I, poor insignificant creature that I am, to pray for him!" for, as they acted of love, they did not give these things a thought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:12
verses.text: And observe, it was during the feast, that (their enemies) brought these trials upon them, that their worth might be the more approved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:13
verses.text: "And when Herod," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:14
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:15
verses.text: ) See Peter sleeping, and not in distress or fear! That same night, after which he was to be brought forth, he slept, having cast all upon God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:16
verses.text: "Between two soldiers, bound with two chains".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:17
verses.text: (comp.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:18
verses.text: Pet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:19
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:20
verses.text: ) Mark, how strict the ward! "And says, Arise".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:22
verses.text: ) The guards were asleep with him, and therefore perceived nothing of what was happening.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:23
verses.text: "And a light shined".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:24
verses.text: What was the light for? In order that Peter might see as well as hear, and not imagine it to be all fancy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:25
verses.text: And the command, "Arise quickly," that he may not be remiss.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:26
verses.text: He also smote him; so deeply did he sleep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:27
verses.text: (a) "Rise," says he, "quickly:" this is not to hurry him (θορυβοὕντος) but to persuade him not to delay.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:28
verses.text: (c) "And" immediately "his chains fell off from his hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:29
verses.text: (b) How? answer me: where are the heretics?—let them answer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:30
verses.text: "And the Angel said unto him," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:32
verses.text: ) by this also convincing him that it is no fancy: to this end he bids him gird himself and put on his shoes, that he may shake off his sleep, and know that it is real.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:33
verses.text: (a) (e) "And he wist not that it was true that was done by the Angel, but thought he saw a vision" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:34
verses.text: ): (e) well he might, by reason of the excessive greatness (ὑπερβολὴν) of the things taking place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:35
verses.text: Do you mark what a thing it is for a miracle to be excessive (ὑπερβολὴ σημείου)? how it amazes (ἐκπλήττει) the beholder? how it will not let the thing be believed? For if Peter "thought he saw a vision," though he had girded himself and put on his shoes, what would have been the case with another? "And," it says, "when they had passed the first and the second ward, they came to the iron gate, which opened unto them of its own accord" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:36
verses.text: ): and yet the things that had happened within (the prison) were more marvellous: but this was now more after the manner of man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:37
verses.text: "And having gone out, they went along one street and immediately (all 'until') the Angel departed from him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:39
verses.text: ) When there was no hindrance, then the Angel departed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:40
verses.text: For Peter would not have gone along (προἥλθεν), there being so many hindrances.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:41
verses.text: "And when he came to himself:" for in very truth, it was indeed an amazement (ἔκπληξις).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:42
verses.text: "Now," saith he, "I know"—now, not then, when I was in the prison,—"that the Lord hath sent His Angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:43
verses.text: And when he had considered" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:44
verses.text: ), it says: viz.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:45
verses.text: where he was, or, that he must not without more ado depart but requite his Benefactor: "he came to the house of Mary the mother of John".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:46
verses.text: Who is this John? Probably he that was always with them: for this is why he adds his distinctive name (τὸ παράσημον), "whose surname was Mark".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:47
verses.text: But observe, "praying" in the night, how much they got by it: what a good thing affliction is; how wakeful it made them! Do you see how great the gain resulting from the death of Stephen? do you see how great the benefit accruing from this imprisonment? For it is not by taking vengeance upon those who wronged them that God shows the greatness of the Gospel: but in the wrong-doers themselves, without any harm happening to those, he shows what a mighty thing the afflictions in themselves are, that we may not seek in any wise deliverance from them, nor the avenging of our wrongs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:48
verses.text: And mark how the very servant-girls were henceforth upon an equality with them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:49
verses.text: "For joy," it says, "she opened not".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:50
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:52
verses.text: ) This too is well done, that they likewise may not be amazed by seeing him at once, and that they may be incredulous, and their minds may be exercised.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:53
verses.text: "But ran in," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:54
verses.text: just as we are wont to do, she was eager to be herself the bringer of the good tidings, for good news it was indeed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:55
verses.text: "And they said unto her, Thou art mad: but she constantly affirmed that it was even so: then said they, It is his Angel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:56
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:57
verses.text: ) This is a truth, that each man has an Angel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:58
verses.text: And what would the Angel? It was from the time (of night) that they surmised this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:59
verses.text: But when he "continued knocking, and when they had opened, and saw him, they were astonished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:60
verses.text: But he beckoning to them with his hand" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:61
verses.text: , ), made them keep quiet, to hear all that had happened to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:62
verses.text: He was now an object of more affectionate desire to the disciples, not only in consequence of his being saved, but by his sudden coming in upon them and straightway departing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:63
verses.text: Now, both his friends learn all clearly; and the aliens also learn, if they had a mind, but they had not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:64
verses.text: The same thing happened in the case of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:65
verses.text: "Tell these things," he says, "to James, and to the brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:66
verses.text: How free from all vainglory! Nor did he say, Make known these things to people everywhere, but, "to the brethren.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:67
verses.text: And he withdrew to another place:" for he did not tempt God, nor fling himself into temptation: since, when they were commanded to do this, then they did it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:68
verses.text: "Go," it was said, "speak in the temple to the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:69
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:70
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:71
verses.text: ) But this the Angel said not (here); on the contrary, by silently removing him and bringing him out by night, he gave him free permission to withdraw—and this too is done, that we may learn that many things are providentially brought about after the manner of men—so that he should not again fall into peril.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:72
verses.text: —For that they may not say, "It was his Angel," after he was gone, they say this first, and then they see himself overthrowing their notion of the matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:73
verses.text: Had it been the Angel, he would have knocked at the door, would not have retired to another place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:74
verses.text: And what followed in the day, make them sure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:75
verses.text: "So Peter was kept in the prison," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:76
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:77
verses.text: ) They, being at large, were at prayer: he, bound, was in sleep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:78
verses.text: "And he wist not that it was true".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:79
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:80
verses.text: ) If he thought it was true that was happening, he would have been astonished, he would not have remembered (all the circumstances): but now, seeming to be in a dream, he was free from perturbation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:81
verses.text: "When," it says, "they were past the first and the second ward"—see also how strong the guard was—"they came unto the iron gate".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:82
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:83
verses.text: ) "Now know I that the Lord hath sent His Angel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:84
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:85
verses.text: ) Why is not this effected by themselves? (I answer,) By this also the Lord honors them, that by the ministry of His Angels he rescues them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:86
verses.text: Then why was it not so in the case of Paul? There with good reason, because the jailer was to be converted, whereas here, it was only that the Apostle should be released.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:87
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:88
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:89
verses.text: ) And God disposes all things in divers ways.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:90
verses.text: And there too, it is beautiful, that Paul sings hymns, while here Peter was asleep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:91
verses.text: "And when he had considered, he came to the house of Mary," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:92
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:93
verses.text: ) Then let us not hide God's marvels, but for our own good let us study to display these abroad for the edifying of the others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:94
verses.text: For as he deserves to be admired for choosing to be put into bonds, so is he worthy of more admiration, that he withdrew not until he had reported all to his friends.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:95
verses.text: "And he said, Tell James and the brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:96
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:97
verses.text: ) That they may rejoice: that they may not be anxious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:98
verses.text: Through these those learn, not those through him: such thought had he for the humbler part!—  Truly, nothing better than affliction not above measure (συμμέτρου).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:99
verses.text: What think you must have been their state of mind—how full of delight! Where now are those women, who sleep the whole night through? Where are those men, who do not even turn themselves in their bed? Seest thou the watchful soul? With women, and children, and maid-servants, they sang hymns to God, made purer than the sky by affliction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:100
verses.text: But now, if we see a little danger, we fall back.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:101
verses.text: Nothing ever was more splendid than that Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:102
verses.text: Let us imitate these, let us emulate them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:103
verses.text: Not for this was the night made, that we should sleep all through it and be idle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:104
verses.text: To this bear witness the artisans, the carriers, and the merchants (to this), the Church of God rising up in the midst of the night.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:105
verses.text: Rise thou up also, and behold the quire of the stars, the deep silence, the profound repose: contemplate with awe the order (οἰκονομίαν) of thy Master's household.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:106
verses.text: Then is thy soul purer: it is lighter, and subtler, and soaring disengaged: the darkness itself, the profound silence, are sufficient to lead thee to compunction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:107
verses.text: And if also thou look to the heavens studded with its stars, as with ten thousand eyes, if thou bethink thee that all those multitudes who in the daytime are shouting, laughing, frisking, leaping, wronging, grasping, threatening, inflicting wrongs without number, lie all one as dead, thou wilt condemn all the self-willedness of man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:108
verses.text: Sleep hath invaded and defeated (ἡλεγξεν) nature: it is the image of death, the image of the end of all things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:109
verses.text: If thou (look out of window and) lean over into the street, thou wilt not hear even a sound: if thou look into the house, thou wilt see all lying as it were in a tomb.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:110
verses.text: All this is enough to arouse the soul, and lead it to reflect on the end of all things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:111
verses.text: Here indeed my discourse is for both men and women.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:112
verses.text: Bend thy knees, send forth groans, beseech thy Master to be merciful: He is more moved by prayers in the night, when thou makest the time for rest a time for mourning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:113
verses.text: Remember what words that king uttered: "I have been weary with my groaning: every night will I wash my bed, I will water my couch with my tears".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:114
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:115
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:116
verses.text: ) However delicate a liver thou mayest be, thou art not more delicate than he: however rich thou mayest be, thou art not richer than David.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:117
verses.text: And again the same Psalmist saith, "At midnight I rose to give thanks unto Thee for the judgments of Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:118
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:119
verses.text: cxix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:120
verses.text: ) No vainglory then intrudes upon thee: how can it, when all are sleeping, and not looking at thee? Then neither sloth nor drowsiness invades thee: how can they, when thy soul is aroused by such great things? After such vigils come sweet slumbers and wondrous revelations.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:121
verses.text: Do this, thou also the man, not the woman only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:122
verses.text: Let the house be a Church, consisting of men and women.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:123
verses.text: For think not because thou art the only man, or because she is the only woman there, that this is any hindrance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:124
verses.text: "For where two," He saith, "are gathered together in My Name, there am I in the midst of them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:125
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:126
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:127
verses.text: ) Where Christ is in the midst, there is a great multitude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:128
verses.text: Where Christ is, there needs must Angels be, needs must Archangels also and the other Powers be there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:129
verses.text: Then ye are not alone, seeing ye have Him Who is Lord of all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:130
verses.text: Hear again the prophet also saying, "Better is one that doeth the will of the Lord, than ten thousand transgressors".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:131
verses.text: (comp.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:132
verses.text: Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:133
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:134
verses.text: ) Nothing more weak than a multitude of unrighteous men, nothing more strong than one man who lives according to the law of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:135
verses.text: If thou hast children wake up them also, and let thy house altogether become a Church through the night: but if they be tender, and cannot endure the watching, let them stay for the first or second prayer, and then send them to rest: only stir up thyself, establish thyself in the habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:136
verses.text: Nothing is better than that storehouse which receives such prayers as these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:137
verses.text: Hear the Prophet speaking: "If I remembered Thee upon my bed, I thought upon Thee in the dawn of the morning".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:138
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:139
verses.text: lxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:140
verses.text: ) But you will say: I have labored much during the day, and I cannot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:141
verses.text: Mere pretext this and subterfuge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:142
verses.text: For however much thou hast labored, thou wilt not toil like the smith, who lets fall such a heavy hammer from a great height upon the (metal flying off in) sparks, and takes in the smoke with his whole body: and yet at this work he spends the greater part of the night.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:143
verses.text: Ye know also how the women, if there is need for us to go into the country, or to go forth unto a vigil, watch through the whole night.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:144
verses.text: Then have thou also a spiritual forge, to fashion there not pots or cauldrons, but thine own soul, which is far better than either coppersmith or goldsmith can fashion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:145
verses.text: Thy soul, waxen old in sins, cast thou into the smelting-furnace of confession: let fall the hammer from on high: that is, the condemnation of thy words (τὥν ῥημάτων τὴν κατάγνωσιν): light up the fire of the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:146
verses.text: Thou hast a far mightier craft (than theirs).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:147
verses.text: Thou art beating into shape not vessels of gold, but the soul, which is more precious than all gold, even as the smith hammers out his vessel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:148
verses.text: For it is no material vessel that thou art working at, but thou art freeing thy soul from all imaginations belonging to this life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:149
verses.text: Let a lamp be by thy side, not that one which we burn, but that which the prophet had, when he said, "Thy law is a lamp unto my feet".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:150
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:151
verses.text: cxix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:152
verses.text: ) Bring thy soul to a red heat, by prayer: when thou seest it hot enough, draw it out, and mould it into what shape thou wilt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:153
verses.text: Believe me, not fire so effectual to burn off rust, as night prayer to remove the rust of our sins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:154
verses.text: Let the night-watchers, if no one else, shame us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:155
verses.text: They, by man's law, go their rounds in the cold, shouting loudly, and walking through lanes (στενωπὥν) and alleys, oftentimes drenched with rain and (all) congealed with cold, for thee and for thy safety, and the protection of thy property.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:156
verses.text: There is he taking such care for thy property, while thou takest none even for thy soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:157
verses.text: And yet I do not make thee go thy rounds in the open air like him, nor shout loudly and rend thy sides: but in thy closet itself, or in thy bedchamber, bend thy knees, and entreat thy Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:158
verses.text: Why did Christ Himself pass a whole night on the mountain? Was it not, that He might be an ensample to us? Then is it that the plants respire, in the night, I mean: and then also does the soul take in the dew even more than they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:159
verses.text: What the sun has parched by day becomes cool again at night.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:160
verses.text: More refreshing than all dew, the tears of the night descend upon our lusts and upon all heat and fever of the soul, and do not let it be affected in any such way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:161
verses.text: But if it do not enjoy the benefit of that dew, it will be burnt up in the daytime.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 67:162
verses.text: But God forbid (it should be so)! Rather, may we all, being refreshed, and enjoying the mercy of God, be freed from the burden of our sins, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father together with the Holy Spirit be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:1
verses.text: Homily XXVII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:2
verses.text: Acts XII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:3
verses.text: ,  "Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:4
verses.text: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the keepers, and commanded that they should be put to death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:5
verses.text: And he went down from Judea to Caesarea, and there abode".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:6
verses.text: Some persons, it is likely, are at a loss how to explain it, that God should quietly look on while (His) champions are put to death, and now again the soldiers on account of Peter: and yet it was possible for Him after (delivering) Peter to rescue them also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:7
verses.text: But it was not yet the time of judgment, so as to render to each according to his deserts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:8
verses.text: And besides, it was not Peter that put them into his hands.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:9
verses.text: For the thing that most annoyed him was the being mocked; just as in the case of his grandfather when he was deceived by the wise men, that was what made him (feel) cut to the heart—the being (eluded and) made ridiculous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:10
verses.text: "And having put them to the question," it says, "he ordered them to be led away to execution".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:11
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:12
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:13
verses.text: ) And yet he had heard from them—for he had put them to the question—both that the chains had been left, and that he had taken his sandals, and that until that night he was with them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:14
verses.text: "Having put them to the question:" but what did they conceal? Why then did they not themselves also flee? "He ordered them to be led away to execution:" and yet he ought to have marvelled, ought to have been astonished at this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:15
verses.text: The consequence is, by the death of these men (the thing), is made manifest to all: both his wickedness is exposed to view, and (it is made clear that) the wonder (is) of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:16
verses.text: "And he went down from Judea to Caesarea, and there abode: and Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon: but they came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus the king's chamberlain their friend, desired peace; because their country was nourished by the king's country.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:17
verses.text: And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:18
verses.text: And the people gave a shout, saying, 'It is the voice of a god, and not of a man,' And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:20
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 68:21

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:1
verses.text: But see how (the writer) here does not hide these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:2
verses.text: Why does he mention this history? Say, what has it to do with the Gospel, that Herod is incensed with the Tyrians and Sidonians? It is not a small matter, even this, how immediately justice seized him; although not because of Peter, but because of his arrogant speaking.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:3
verses.text: And yet, it may be said, if those shouted, what is that to him? Because he accepted the acclamation, because he accounted himself to be worthy of the adoration.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:4
verses.text: Through him those most receive a lesson, who so thoughtlessly flattered him (al.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:5
verses.text: οἱ κολακεύοντες).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:6
verses.text: Observe again, while both parties deserve punishment, this man is punished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:7
verses.text: For this is not the time of judgment, but He punishes him that had most to answer for, leaving the others to profit by this man's fate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:8
verses.text: "And the word of God," it says, "grew," i-e: in consequence of this, "and multiplied".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:9
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:10
verses.text: ) Do you mark God's providential management? "But Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their ministry, and took with them John, whose surname was Mark".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:12
verses.text: ) "Now there were in the Church that was at Antioch, certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaën, which had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:13
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:14
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:15
verses.text: ) He still mentions Barnabas first: for Paul was not yet famous, he had not yet wrought any sign.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:16
verses.text: "As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate Me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:17
verses.text: And when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:20
verses.text: ) What means, "Ministering?" Preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:21
verses.text: "Separate for Me," it says, "Barnabas and Saul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:22
verses.text: What means, "Separate for Me?" For the work, for the Apostleship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:23
verses.text: See again by what persons he is ordained (γυμνοτέρα.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:24
verses.text: Cat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:25
verses.text: σεμνοτέρα, "more awful".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:26
verses.text: ) By Lucius the Cyrenean and Manaën, or rather, by the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:27
verses.text: The less the persons, the more palpable the grace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:28
verses.text: He is ordained henceforth to Apostleship, so as to preach with authority.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:29
verses.text: How then does he himself say, "Not from men, nor by man?" (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:30
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:31
verses.text: ) Because it was not man that called or brought him over: this is why he says, "Not from men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:32
verses.text: Neither by man," that is, that he was not sent by this (man), but by the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:33
verses.text: Wherefore also (the writer) thus proceeds: "So they, being sent forth by the Holy Ghost, departed unto Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:35
verses.text: ) But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:36
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:37
verses.text: ) "And when it was day," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:39
verses.text: ) For if the Angel had brought out the soldiers also, along with Peter, it would have been thought a case of flight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:40
verses.text: Then why, you may ask, was it not otherwise managed? Why, where is the harm? Now, if we see that they who have suffered unjustly, take no harm, we shall not raise these questions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:41
verses.text: For why do you not say the same of James? Why did not (God) rescue him? "There was no small stir among the soldiers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:42
verses.text: So (clearly) had they perceived nothing (of what had happened).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:43
verses.text: Lo, I take up the plea in their defence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:44
verses.text: The chains were there, and the keepers within, and the prison shut, nowhere a wall broken through, all told the same tale: the man had been carried off: why dost thou condemn them? Had they wished to let him off, they would have done it before, or would have gone out with him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:45
verses.text: "But he gave them money?" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:46
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:47
verses.text: ) And how should he, who had not to give even to a poor man, have the means to give to these? And then neither had the chains been broken, nor were they loosed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:48
verses.text: He ought to have seen, that the thing was of God, and no work of man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:49
verses.text: "And he went down from Judea to Caesarea, and there abode.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:50
verses.text: And Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:52
verses.text: ) He is now going to mention (a matter of) history: this is the reason why he adds the names, that it may be shown how he keeps to the truth in all things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:53
verses.text: "And," it says, "having made Blastus the king's chamberlain their friend, they desired peace; because their country was nourished by the king's country".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:55
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:56
verses.text: ) For probably there was a famine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:57
verses.text: "And on a set day," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:58
verses.text: (Joseph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:59
verses.text: Ant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:60
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:61
verses.text: ) Josephus also says this, that he fell into a lingering disease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:62
verses.text: Now the generality were not aware of this, but the Apostle sets it down: yet at the same time their ignorance was an advantage, in regard that they imputed what befell (Agrippa) to his putting James and the soldiers to death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:63
verses.text: Observe, when he slew the Apostle, he did nothing of this sort but when (he slew) these; in fact he knew not what to say about it: as being at a loss, then, and feeling ashamed, "he went down from Judea to Caesarea".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:64
verses.text: I suppose it was also to bring those (men of Tyre and Sidon) to apologize, that he withdrew (from Jerusalem): for with those he was incensed, while paying such court to these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:65
verses.text: See how vainglorious the man is: meaning to confer the boon upon them, he makes an harangue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:66
verses.text: But Josephus says, that he was also arrayed in a splendid robe made of silver.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:67
verses.text: Observe both what flatterers those were, and what a high spirit was shown by the Apostles: the man whom the whole nation so courted, the same they held in contempt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:68
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:69
verses.text: ) But observe again a great refreshing granted to them, and the numberless benefits accruing from the vengeance inflicted upon him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:70
verses.text: But if this man, because it was said to him, "It is the voice of God and not of a man (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:71
verses.text: ) although he said nothing himself, suffered such things: much more should Christ, had He not Himself been God (have suffered) for saying always as He did, "These words of mine are not Mine" (John xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:72
verses.text: ; xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:73
verses.text: ) and, "Angels minister to Me," and such like.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:74
verses.text: But that man ended His life by a shameful and miserable death, and thenceforth no more is seen of him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:75
verses.text: And observe him also, easily talked over even by Blastus, like a poor creature, soon incensed and again pacified, and on all occasions a slave of the populace, with nothing free and independent about him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:76
verses.text: But mark also the authority of the Holy Ghost: "As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate Me Barnabas and Saul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:77
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:78
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:79
verses.text: ) What being would have dared, if not of the same authority, to say this? "Separate," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:80
verses.text: But this is done, that they may not keep together among themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:81
verses.text: The Spirit saw that they had greater power, and were able to be sufficient for many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:82
verses.text: And how did He speak to them? Probably by prophets: therefore the writer premises, that there were prophets also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:83
verses.text: And they were fasting and ministering: that thou mayest learn that there was need of great sobriety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:84
verses.text: In Antioch he is ordained, where he preaches.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:85
verses.text: Why did He not say, Separate for the Lord, but, "For me?" It shows that He is of one authority and power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:86
verses.text: "And when they had fasted," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:87
verses.text: Seest thou what a great thing fasting is? "So they being sent forth by the Holy Ghost:" it shows that the Spirit did all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:88
verses.text: A great, yes a great good is fasting: it is circumscribed by no limits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:89
verses.text: When need was to ordain, then they fast: and to them while fasting, the Spirit spake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:90
verses.text: Thus much only do I enjoin: (I say) not fast, but abstain from luxury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:91
verses.text: Let us seek meats to nourish, not things to ruin us; seek meats for food, not occasions of diseases, of diseases both of soul and body: seek food which hath comfort, not luxury which is full of discomfort: the one is luxury, the other mischief; the one is pleasure, the other pain; the one is agreeable to nature, the other contrary to nature.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:92
verses.text: For say, if one should give thee hemlock juice to drink, would it not be against nature? if one should give thee logs and stones, wouldest thou not reject them? Of course, for they are against nature.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:93
verses.text: Well, and so is luxury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:94
verses.text: For just as in a city, under an invasion of enemies when there has been siege and tumult, great is the uproar, so is it in the soul, under invasion of wine and luxury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:95
verses.text: "Who hath woe? who hath tumults? who hath discomforts and babblings? Are they not they that tarry long at the wine? Whose are bloodshot eyes?" (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:96
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:97
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:98
verses.text: ) But yet, say what we will, we shall not bring off those who give themselves up to luxury, unless we bring into conflict therewith a different affection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:99
verses.text: And first, let us address ourselves to the women.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:100
verses.text: Nothing uglier than a woman given to luxury, nothing uglier than a woman given to drink.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:101
verses.text: The bloom of her complexion is faded: the calm and mild expression of the eyes is rendered turbid, as when a cloud intercepts the rays of the sunshine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:102
verses.text: It is a vulgar, (ἀνελεύθερον) slave-like, thoroughly low-lived habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:103
verses.text: How disgusting is a woman when from her breath you catch sour whiffs of fetid wine: a woman belching, giving out a fume (χυμὸν) of decomposing meats; herself weighed down, unable to keep upright; her face flushed with an unnatural red; yawning incessantly, and everything swimming in a mist before her eyes! But not such, she that abstains from luxurious living: no (this abstinence makes her look) a more beautiful, well-bred (σωφρονεστέρα) woman.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:104
verses.text: For even to the body, the composure of the soul imparts a beauty of its own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:105
verses.text: Do not imagine that the impression of beauty results only from the bodily features.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:106
verses.text: Give me a handsome girl, but turbulent (τεταραγμένην), loquacious, railing, given to drink, extravagant, (and tell me) if she is not worse-looking than any ugly woman? But if she were bashful, if she would hold her peace, if she learnt to blush, if to speak modestly (συμμέτρως), if to find time for fastings; her beauty would be twice as great, her freshness would be heightened, her look more engaging, fraught with modesty and good breeding (σωφροσύνης καὶ κοσμιότητος).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:107
verses.text: Now then, shall we speak of men? What can be uglier than a man in drink? He is an object of ridicule to his servants, of ridicule to his enemies, of pity to his friends; deserving condemnation without end: a wild beast rather than a human being; for to devour much food is proper to panther, and lion, and bear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:108
verses.text: No wonder (that they do so), for those creatures have not a reasonable soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:109
verses.text: And yet even they, if they be gorged with food more than they need, and beyond the measure appointed them by nature, get their whole body ruined by it: how much more we? Therefore hath God contracted our stomach into a small compass; therefore hath He marked out a small measure of sustenance, that He may instruct us to attend to the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:110
verses.text: Let us consider our very make, and we shall see there is in us but one little part that has this operation—for our mouth and tongue are meant for singing hymns, our throat for voice—therefore the very necessity of nature has tied us down, that we may not, even involuntarily, get into much trouble (πραγματείαν) (in this way).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:111
verses.text: Since, if indeed luxurious living had not its pains, nor sickness and infirmities, it might be tolerated: but as the case is, He hath stinted thee by restrictions of nature, that even if thou wish to exceed, thou mayest not be able to do so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:112
verses.text: Is not pleasure thine object, beloved? This thou shalt find from moderation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:113
verses.text: Is not health? This too thou shalt so gain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:114
verses.text: Is not easiness of mind? This too.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:115
verses.text: Is not freedom? is not vigor and good habit of body, is not sobriety and alertness of mind? (All these thou shalt find); so entirely are all good things there, while in the other are the contraries to these, discomfort, distemper, disease, embarrassment—waste of substance (ἀνελευθερία).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:116
verses.text: Then how comes it, you will ask, that we all run eagerly after this? It comes of disease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:117
verses.text: For say, what is it that makes the sick man hanker after the thing that does him harm? Is not this very hankering a part of his disease? Why is it that the lame man does not walk upright? This very thing, does it come of his being lazy, and not choosing to go to the physician? For there are some things, in which the pleasure they bring with them is temporary, but lasting the punishment: others just the contrary, in which the endurance is for a time, the pleasure perpetual.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:118
verses.text: He, therefore, that has so little solidity and strength of purpose as not to slight present sweets for future, is soon overcome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:119
verses.text: Say, how came Esau to be overcome? how came he to prefer the present pleasure to the future honor? Through want of solidity and firmness of character.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:120
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:121
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:122
verses.text: ) And this fault itself, say you, whence comes it? Of our ownselves: and it is plain from this consideration.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:123
verses.text: When we have the mind, we do rouse ourselves, and become capable of endurance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:124
verses.text: Certain it is, if at any time necessity comes upon us, nay, often only from a spirit of emulation, we get to see clearly what is useful for us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:125
verses.text: When therefore thou art about to indulge in luxury, consider how brief the pleasure, consider the loss—for loss it is indeed to spend so much money to one's own hurt—the diseases, the infirmities: and despise luxury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:126
verses.text: How many shall I enumerate who have suffered evils from indulgence? Noah was drunken, and was exposed in his nakedness, and see what evils came of this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:127
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:128
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:129
verses.text: ) Esau through greediness abandoned his birthright, and was set upon fratricide.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:130
verses.text: The people of Israel "sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:131
verses.text: (Ex.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:132
verses.text: xxxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:133
verses.text: ) Therefore saith the Scripture, "When thou hast eaten and drunken, remember the Lord thy God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:134
verses.text: (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:135
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:136
verses.text: ) For they fell over a precipice, in failing into luxury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:137
verses.text: "The widow," he saith, "that liveth in pleasure, is dead while she liveth" ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:138
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:139
verses.text: ): and again, "The beloved waxed sleek, grew thick, and kicked" (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:140
verses.text: xxxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:141
verses.text: ): and again the Apostle, "Make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:142
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:143
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:144
verses.text: ) I am not enacting as a law that there shall be fasting, for indeed there is no one who would listen; but I am doing away with daintiness, I am cutting off luxury for the sake of your own profit: for like a winter torrent, luxury overthrows all: there is nothing to stop its course: it casts out from a kingdom: what is the gain of it (τί τὸ πλέον)? Would you enjoy a (real) luxury? Give to the poor; invite Christ, so that even after the table is removed, you may still have this luxury to enjoy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:145
verses.text: For now, indeed, you have it not, and no wonder: but then you will have it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:146
verses.text: Would you taste a (real) luxury? Nourish your soul, give to her of that food to which she is used: do not kill her by starvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:147
verses.text: —It is the time for war, the time for contest: and do you sit enjoying yourself? Do you not see even those who wield sceptres, how they live frugally while abroad on their campaigns? "We wrestle not against flesh and blood" (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:148
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:149
verses.text: ); and are you fattening yourself when about to wrestle? The adversary stands grinding his teeth, and are you giving a loose to jollity, and devoting yourself to the table? I know that I speak these things in vain, yet not (in vain) for all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:150
verses.text: "He that hath ears to hear, let him hear".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:151
verses.text: (Luke viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:152
verses.text: ) Christ is pining through hunger, and are you frittering yourself away (διασπᾅς) with gluttony? Two inconsistencies (Δύο ἀμετρίαι).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:153
verses.text: For what evil does not luxury cause? It is contrary to itself: so that I know not how it gets its name: but just as that is called glory, which is (really) infamy, and that riches, which in truth is poverty, so the name of luxury is given to that which in reality is nauseousness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:154
verses.text: Do we intend ourselves for the shambles, that we so fatten ourselves? Why cater for the worm that it may have a sumptuous larder? Why make more of their humors (ἰχὥρας)? Why store up in yourself sources of sweat and rank smelling? Why make yourself useless for everything? Do you wish your eye to be strong? Get your body well strung? For in musical strings, that which is coarse and not refined, is not fit to produce musical tones, but that which has been well scraped, stretches well, and vibrates with full harmony.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:155
verses.text: Why do you bury the soul alive? why make the wall about it thicker? Why increase the reek and the cloud, with fumes like a mist steaming up from all sides? If none other, let the wrestlers teach you, that the more spare the body, the stronger it is: and (then) also the soul is more vigorous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:156
verses.text: In fact, it is like charioteer and horse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:157
verses.text: But there you see, just as in the case of men giving themselves to luxury, and making themselves plump, so the plump horses are unwieldy, and give the driver much ado.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:158
verses.text: One may think one's self (ἀγαπητὸν) well off, even with a horse obedient to the rein and well-limbed, to be able to carry off the prize: but when the driver is forced to drag the horse along, and when the horse falls, though he goad him ever so much, he cannot make him get up, be he ever so skilful himself, he will be deprived of the victory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 70:159
verses.text: Then let us not endure to see our soul wronged because of the body, but let us make the soul herself more clear-sighted, let us make her wing light, her bonds looser: let us feed her with discourse, with frugality, (feeding) the body only so much that it may be healthy, that it may be vigorous, that it may rejoice and not be in pain: that having in this sort well ordered our concerns, we may be enabled to lay hold upon the highest virtue, and to attain unto the eternal good things by the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom, to the Father and Holy Ghost together, be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:1
verses.text: Homily XXVIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:2
verses.text: Acts XIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:3
verses.text: ,  "So they, being sent forth by the Holy Ghost, departed unto Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:4
verses.text: And when they were at Salamis, they preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews: and they had also John to their minister".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:5
verses.text: As soon as they were ordained they went forth, and hasted to Cyprus, that being a place where was no ill-design hatching against them, and where moreover the Word had been sown already.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:6
verses.text: In Antioch there were (teachers) enough, and Phoenice too was near to Palestine; but Cyprus not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:7
verses.text: However, you are not to make a question of the why and wherefore, when it is the Spirit that directs their movements: for they were not only ordained by the Spirit, but sent forth by Him likewise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:8
verses.text: "And when they were come to Salamis, they preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:9
verses.text: Do you mark how they make a point of preaching the word to them first, not to make them more contentious? The persons mentioned before "spake to none but to Jews only" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:10
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:11
verses.text: ), and so here they betook them to the synagogues.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:12
verses.text: "And when they had gone through the isle unto Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesus: which was with the deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:13
verses.text: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:14
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:16
verses.text: ) Again a Jew sorcerer, as was Simon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:17
verses.text: And observe this man, how, while they preached to the others, he did not take it much amiss, but only when they approached the proconsul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:18
verses.text: And then in respect of the proconsul the wonder is, that although prepossessed by the man's sorcery, he was nevertheless willing to hear the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:19
verses.text: So it was with the Samaritans: and from the competition (συγκρίσεως) the victory appears, the sorcery being worsted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:20
verses.text: Everywhere, vainglory and love of power are a (fruitful) source of evils! "But Saul, who is also Paul,"—(v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:21
verses.text: ) here his name is changed at the same time that he is ordained, as it was in Peter's case,—"filled with the Holy Ghost, looked upon him, and said, O full of all guile and all villany, thou child of the devil:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:22
verses.text: ) and observe, this is not abuse, but accusation: for so ought forward, impudent people to be rebuked "thou enemy of all righteousness;" here he lays bare what was in the thoughts of the man, while under pretext of saving he was ruining the proconsul: "wilt thou not cease," he says, "to pervert the ways of the Lord?" (He says it) both confidently (αξιοπίστως), It is not with us thou art warring, nor art thou fighting (with us), but "the ways of the Lord" thou art perverting, and with praise (of these, he adds) "the right" ways.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:23
verses.text: "And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:24
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:25
verses.text: ) It was the sign by which he was himself converted, and by this he would fain convert this man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:26
verses.text: As also that expression, "for a season," puts it not as an act of punishing, but as meant for his conversion: had it been for punishment, he would have made him lastingly blind, but now it is not so, but "for a season" (and this), that he may gain the proconsul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:27
verses.text: For, as he was prepossessed by the sorcery, it was well to teach him a lesson by this infliction (and the sorcerer also), in the same way as the magicians (in Egypt) were taught by the boils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:28
verses.text: (Ex.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:29
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:30
verses.text: ) "And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness: and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:31
verses.text: Then the deputy, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the doctrine of the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:32
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:33
verses.text: ) But observe, how they do not linger there, as (they might have been tempted to do) now that the proconsul was a believer, nor are enervated by being courted and honored, but immediately keep on with their work, and set out for the country on the opposite coast.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:34
verses.text: "Now when Paul and his company loosed from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia; and John departing from them returned to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:35
verses.text: But when they departed from Perga, they came to Antioch in Pisidia, and went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and sat down".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:38
verses.text: ) And here again they entered the synagogues, in the character of Jews, that they might not be treated as enemies, and be driven away: and in this way they carried the whole matter successfully.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:39
