verses.text: "And after the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent unto them, saying, Ye men and brethren, if ye have any word of exhortation for the people, say on".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:41
verses.text: ) From this point, we learn the history of Paul's doings, as in what was said above we have learned not a little about Peter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:42
verses.text: But let us review what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:43
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:44
verses.text: ) "And when they were come to Salamis," the metropolis of Cyprus, "they preached the word of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:46
verses.text: ) They had spent a year in Antioch: it behooved that they should go hither also (to Cyprus) and not sit permanently where they were (the converts in Cyprus): needed greater teachers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:47
verses.text: See too how they remain no time in Seleucia, knowing that (the people there) might have reaped much benefit from the neighboring city (of Antioch): but they hasten on to the more pressing duties.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:48
verses.text: When they came to the metropolis of the island, they were earnest to disabuse (διορθωσαι) the proconsul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:49
verses.text: But that it is no flattery that (the writer) says, "he was with the proconsul, a prudent man" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:50
verses.text: ), you may learn from the facts; for he needed not many discourses, and himself wished to hear them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 71:51
verses.text: And he mentions also the names.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:1
verses.text: Observe, how he said nothing to the sorcerer, until he gave him an occasion: but they only "preached the word of the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:2
verses.text: Since (though Elymas) saw the rest attending to them, he looked only to this one object, that the proconsul might not be won over.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:3
verses.text: Why did not (Paul) perform some other miracle? Because there was none equal to this, the taking the enemy captive.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:4
verses.text: And observe, he first impeaches, and then punishes, him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:5
verses.text: He shows how justly the man deserved to suffer, by his saying, "O full of all deceit" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:6
verses.text: ): ("full of all,") he says: nothing wanting to the full measure: and he well says, of all "deceit," for the man was playing the part of a hypocrite.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:7
verses.text: —"Child of the devil," because he was doing his work: "enemy of all righteousness," since this (which they preached) was the whole of righteousness (though at the same time): I suppose in these words he reproves his manner of life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:8
verses.text: His words were not prompted by anger, and to show this, the writer premises, "filled with the Holy Ghost," that is, with His operation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:9
verses.text: "And now behold the hand of the Lord is upon thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:10
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:11
verses.text: ) It was not vengeance then, but healing: for it is as though he said: "It is not I that do it, but the hand of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:12
verses.text: Mark how unassuming! No "light," as in the case of Paul, "shone round about him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:13
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:14
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:15
verses.text: ) "Thou shalt be blind," he says, "not seeing the sun for a season," that he may give him opportunity for repentance: for we nowhere find them wishing to be made conspicuous by the more stern (exercise of their authority), even though it was against enemies that this was put forth: in respect of those of their own body (they used severity), and with good reason, but in dealing with those without, not so; that (the obedience of faith) might not seem to be matter of compulsion and fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:16
verses.text: It is a proof of his blindness, his "seeking some to lead him by the hand".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:17
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:18
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:19
verses.text: ff.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:20
verses.text: ) And the proconsul sees the blindness inflicted, "and when he saw what was done, he believed:" and both alone believed not merely this, but, "being astonished at the doctrine of the Lord" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:21
verses.text: ): he saw that these things were not mere words, nor trickery.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:22
verses.text: Mark how he loved to receive instruction from his teachers, though he was in a station of so high authority.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:23
verses.text: And (Paul) said not to the sorcerer, "Wilt thou not cease to pervert" the proconsul? What may be the reason of John's going back from them? For "John," it says, "departing from them returned to Jerusalem" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:24
verses.text: ): (he does it) because they are undertaking a still longer journey: and yet he was their attendant, and as for the danger, they incurred it (not he).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:25
verses.text: —Again, when they were come to Perga, they hastily passed by the other cities, for they were in haste to the metropolis, Antioch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:26
verses.text: And observe how concise the historian is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:27
verses.text: "They sat down in the synagogue," he says, and, "on the sabbath day" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:28
verses.text: , ): that they might prepare the way beforehand for the Word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:29
verses.text: And they do not speak first, but when invited: since as strangers, they called upon them to do so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:30
verses.text: Had they not waited, there would have been no discourse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:31
verses.text: Here for the first time we have Paul preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:32
verses.text: And observe his prudence: where the word was already sown, he passes on: but where there was none (to preach), he makes a stay: as he himself writes: "Yea, so have I strived to preach the Gospel, not where Christ was named".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:33
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:34
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:35
verses.text: ) Great courage this also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:36
verses.text: Truly, from the very outset, a wonderful man! crucified, ready for all encounters (παρατεταγμένος), he knew how great grace he had obtained, and he brought to it zeal equivalent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:37
verses.text: He was not angry with John: for this was not for him: but he kept to the work, he quailed not, he was unappalled, when shut up in the midst of a host.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:38
verses.text: Observe how wisely it is ordered that Paul should not preach at Jerusalem: the very hearing that he is become a believer, this of itself is enough for them; for him to preach, they never would have endured, such was their hatred of him: so he departs far away, where he was not known.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:39
verses.text: But it is well done, that "they entered the synagogue on the sabbath day" when all were collected together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:40
verses.text: "And after the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent unto them, saying, Ye men and brethren, if ye have any word or exhortation for the people, say on".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:42
verses.text: ) Behold how they do this without grudging, but no longer after this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:43
verses.text: If ye did wish this (really), there was more need to exhort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:44
verses.text: He first convicted the sorcerer (and showed), what he was; and that he was such, the sign showed: "thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun" this was a sign of the blindness of his soul: "for a season" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:45
verses.text: ): he says, to bring him to repentance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:46
verses.text: But, oh that love of rule! oh, that lust of vainglory! how it does overturn and ruin everything; makes people stand up against their own, against each other's salvation; renders them blind indeed, and dark, insomuch that they have even to seek for some to lead them by the hand! Oh that they did even this, oh that they did seek were it but some to lead them by the hand! But no, they no longer endure this, they take the whole matter into their own hands.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:47
verses.text: (This vice) will let no man see: like a mist and thick darkness it spreads itself over them, not letting any see through it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:48
verses.text: What pleas shall we have to offer, we who for one evil affection, overcome another evil affection (supra p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:49
verses.text: ), but not for the fear of God! For example, many who are both lewd and covetous, have for their niggardliness put a bridle upon their lust, while other such, on the contrary, have for pleasure's sake, despised riches.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:50
verses.text: Again, those who are both the one and the other, have by the lust of vainglory overcome both, lavishing their money unsparingly, and practising temperance to no (good) purpose; others again, who are exceedingly vainglorious, have despised that evil affection, submitting to many vile disgraces for the sake of their amours, or for the sake of their money: others again, that they may satiate their anger, have chosen to suffer losses without end, and care for none of them, provided only they may work their own will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:51
verses.text: And yet, what passion can do with us, the fear of God is impotent to effect! Why speak I of passion? What shame before men can do with us, the fear of God has not the strength to effect! Many are the things we do right and wrong, from a feeling of shame before men; but God we fear not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:52
verses.text: How many have been shamed by regard to the opinions of men into flinging away money! How many have mistakenly made it a point of honor to give themselves up to the service of their friends (only), to their hurt! How many from respect for their friendships have been shamed into numberless wrong acts! Since then both passion and regard for the opinion of men are able to put us upon doing wrong things and right, it is idle to say, "we cannot:" we can, if we have the mind: and we ought to have the mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:53
verses.text: Why canst not thou overcome the love of glory, when others do overcome it, having the same soul as thou, and the same body; bearing the same form, and living the same life? Think of God, think of the glory that is from above: weigh against that the things present, and thou wilt quickly recoil from this worldly glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:54
verses.text: If at all events thou covet glory, covet that which is glory, indeed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:55
verses.text: What kind of glory is it, when it begets infamy? What kind of glory, when it compels one to desire the honor of those who are inferior, and stands in need of that? Real honor is the gaining the esteem of those who are greater than one's self.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:56
verses.text: If at all events thou art enamoured of glory, be thou rather enamoured of that which comes from God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:57
verses.text: If enamoured of that glory thou despisest this world's glory, thou shalt see how ignoble this is: but so long as thou seest not that glory, neither wilt thou be able to see this, how foul it is, how ridiculous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:58
verses.text: For as those who are under the spell of some wicked, hideously ugly woman, so long as they are in love with her, cannot see her ill-favoredness, because their passion spreads a darkness over their judgment: so is it here also: so long as we are possessed with the passion, we cannot perceive what a thing it is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:59
verses.text: How then might we be rid of it? Think of those who (for the sake of glory) have spent countless sums, and now are none the better for it: think of the dead, what glory they got, and (now) this glory is nowhere abiding, but all perished and come to naught: bethink thee how it is only a name, and has nothing real in it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:60
verses.text: For say, what is glory? give me some definition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:61
verses.text: "The being admired by all," you will say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:62
verses.text: With justice, or also not with justice? For if it be not with justice, this is not admiration, but crimination (κατηγορία), and flattery, and misrepresentation (διαβολή).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:63
verses.text: But if you say, With justice, why that is impossible: for in the populace there are no right judgments; those that minister to their lusts, those are the persons they admire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:64
verses.text: And if you would (see the proof of this), mark those who give away their substance to the harlots, to the charioteers, to the dancers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:65
verses.text: But you will say, we do not mean these, but those who are just and upright, and able to do great and noble good acts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:66
verses.text: Would that they wished it, and they soon would do good: but as things are, they do nothing of the kind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:67
verses.text: Who, I ask you, now praises the just and upright man? Nay, it is just the contrary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:68
verses.text: Could anything be more preposterous than for a just man, when doing any such good act, to seek glory of the many—as if an artist of consummate skill, employed upon an Emperor's portrait, should wish to have the praises of the ignorant! Moreover, a man who looks for honor from men, will soon enough desist from the acts which virtue enjoins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:69
verses.text: If he will needs be gaping for their praises, he will do just what they wish, not what himself wishes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:70
verses.text: What then would I advise you? You must look only to God, to the praise that is from Him, perform all things which are pleasing to Him, and go after the good things (that are with Him), not be gaping for anything that is of man: for this mars both fasting and prayer and alms-giving, and makes all our good deeds void.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:71
verses.text: Which that it be not our case, let us flee this passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 74:72
verses.text: To one thing alone let us look, to the praise which is from God, to the being accepted of Him, to the commendation from our common Master; that, having passed through our present life virtuously, we may obtain the promised blessings together with them that love Him, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom to the Father, together with the Holy Ghost, be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:1
verses.text: Homily XXIX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:2
verses.text: Acts XIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:3
verses.text: ,  "Then Paul stood up, and beckoning with his hand said, Men of Israel, and ye that fear God, give audience.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:4
verses.text: The God of this people of Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt, and with an high arm brought He them out of it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:5
verses.text: Behold Barnabas giving place to Paul—how should it be otherwise?—to him whom he brought from Tarsus; just as we find John on all occasions giving way to Peter: and yet Barnabas was more looked up to than Paul: true, but they had an eye only to the common advantage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:6
verses.text: "Then Paul stood up," it says;—this was a custom of the Jews—"and beckoned with his hand".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:7
verses.text: And see how he prepares the way beforehand for his discourse: having first praised them, and showed his great regard for them in the words, "ye that fear God," he so begins his discourse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:8
verses.text: And he says not, Ye proselytes, since it was a term of disadvantage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:9
verses.text: "The God of this people chose our fathers: and the people"—See, he calls God Himself their God peculiarly, Who is the common God of men; and shows how great from the first were His benefits, just as Stephen does.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:10
verses.text: This they do to teach them, that now also God has acted after the same custom, in sending His own Son; (Luke xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:11
verses.text: ): as (Christ) Himself (does) in the parable of the vineyard—"And the people," he says, "He exalted when it sojourned in the land of Egypt"—and yet the contrary was the case: true, but they increased in numbers; moreover, the miracles were wrought on their account: "and with an high arm brought He them out of it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:12
verses.text: Of these things (the wonders) which were done in Egypt, the prophets are continually making mention.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:13
verses.text: And observe, how he passes over the times of their calamities, and nowhere brings forward their faults, but only God's kindness, leaving those for themselves to think over.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:14
verses.text: "And about the time of forty years suffered He their manners in the wilderness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:16
verses.text: ) Then the settlement.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:17
verses.text: "And when he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, He divided their land to them by lot".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:19
verses.text: ) And the time was long; four hundred and fifty years.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:20
verses.text: "And after that He gave unto them judges about the space of four hundred and fifty years, until Samuel the prophet".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:22
verses.text: ) Here he shows that God varied His dispensations towards them (at divers times).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:23
verses.text: "And afterward they desired a king:" and (still) not a word of their ingratitude, but throughout he speaks of the kindness of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:24
verses.text: "And God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, by the space of forty years".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:26
verses.text: ) "And when he had removed him, He raised up unto them David to be their king: to whom also He gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after Mine own heart, which shall fulfil all My will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:27
verses.text: Of this man's seed hath God according to His promise raised unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:30
verses.text: ) This was no small thing that Christ should be from David.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:31
verses.text: Then John bears witness to this: "When John had first preached before His coming the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:32
verses.text: And as John fulfilled his course, he said, Whom think ye that I am? I am not He.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:33
verses.text: But, behold, there cometh one after me, whose shoes of His feet I am not worthy to loose".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:36
verses.text: ) And John too not merely bears witness (to the fact), but (does it in such sort that) when men were bringing the glory to him, he declines it: for it is one thing (not to affect) an honor which nobody thinks of offering; and another, to reject it when all men are ready to give it, and not only to reject it, but to do so with such humility.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:37
verses.text: "Men and brethren, children of the stock of Abraham, and whosoever among you feareth God, to you is the word of this salvation sent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:38
verses.text: For they that dwell at Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they knew Him not, nor yet the voices of the prophets which are read every sabbath day, they have fulfilled them in condemning Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:39
verses.text: And though they found no cause of death in Him, yet desired they Pilate that He should be slain".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:42
verses.text: ) On all occasions we find them making a great point of showing this, that the blessing is peculiarly theirs, that they may not flee (from Christ), as thinking they had nothing to do with Him, because they had crucified Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:43
verses.text: "Because they knew Him not," he says: so that the sin was one of ignorance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:44
verses.text: See how he gently makes an apology even on behalf of those (crucifiers).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:45
verses.text: And not only this: but he adds also, that thus it must needs be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:46
verses.text: And how so? "By condemning Him, they fulfilled the voices of the prophets".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:47
verses.text: Then again from the Scriptures.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:48
verses.text: "And when they had fulfilled all that was written of Him, they took Him down from the tree, and laid Him in a sepulchre.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:49
verses.text: But God raised Him from the dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:50
verses.text: And He was seen many days of them which came up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are His witnesses unto the people—"(v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:51
verses.text: –) that He rose again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:52
verses.text: "And we declare unto you glad tidings, how that the promise which was made unto the fathers, God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that He hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second Psalm, Thou art My Son, this day have I begotten Thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:53
verses.text: And as concerning that He raised Him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, He said on this wise, I will give you the sure mercies of David.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:54
verses.text: Wherefore he saith also in another Psalm, Thou shalt not suffer Thine Holy One to see corruption.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:55
verses.text: For David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep, and was laid unto his fathers, and saw corruption: but He, Whom God raised again, saw no corruption.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:56
verses.text: Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this Man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: and by Him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:57
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:59
verses.text: ) Observe how Paul here is more vehement in his discourse: we nowhere find Peter saying this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:60
verses.text: Then too he adds the terrifying words: "Beware therefore, lest that come upon you, which is spoken of in the prophets; Behold, ye despisers, and wonder, and perish: for I work a work in your days, a work which ye shall in no wise believe, though a man declare it unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:61
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:62
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:63
verses.text: )  (a) Observe how he twines (the thread of) his discourse (alternately) from things present, from the prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:64
verses.text: Thus, "from (this man's) seed according to the promise"—(v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:65
verses.text: ): (c) the name of David was dear to them; well then, is it not (a thing to be desired) that a son of his, he says, should be their king?—(b) then he adduces John: then again the prophets, where he says, "By condemning they fulfilled," and again, "All that was written:" then the Apostles as witnesses of the Resurrection: then David bearing witness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:66
verses.text: For neither the Old Testament proofs seemed so cogent when taken by themselves as they are in this way, nor yet the latter testimonies apart from the former: wherefore he makes them mutually confirm each other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:67
verses.text: "Men and brethren," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:68
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:69
verses.text: ) For since they were possessed by fear, as having slain Him, and conscience made them aliens (the Apostles), discourse not with them as unto Christicides, neither as putting into their hands a good which was not theirs, but one peculiarly their own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:70
verses.text: (d) "For they that dwell at Jerusalem, and their rulers:" as much as to say, not ye, but they: and again, apologizing even for those, "Because they knew Him not, and the voices of the Prophets which are read every sabbath day, in condemning Him, they fulfilled them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:71
verses.text: A great charge it is against them that they continually hearing heeded not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:72
verses.text: But no marvel: for what was said above concerning Egypt and the wilderness, was enough to show their ingratitude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:73
verses.text: And observe how this Apostle also, as one moved by the Spirit Himself, continually preaches the Passion, the Burial.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:74
verses.text: (g) "Having taken Him down from the tree".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:75
verses.text: Observe, what a great point they make of this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:76
verses.text: He speaks of the manner of His death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:77
verses.text: Moreover they bring Pilate (conspicuously) forward, that (the fact of) the Passion may be proved by the mention of the tribunal (by which he was condemned), but at the same time, for the greater impeachment of those (His crucifiers), seeing they delivered Him up to an alien.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:78
verses.text: And he does not say, They made a complaint (against Him), (ἐνέτυχον, al.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:79
verses.text: ἐντυγχάνει) but, "They desired, though having found no cause of death" (in Him), "that He should be slain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:80
verses.text: (e) Who appeared," he says, "for many days to them that came up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:81
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:82
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 75:83
verses.text: ) Instead of.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:1
verses.text: he says, "Who are His witnesses unto the people," to wit, "The men which came up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:2
verses.text: Then he produces David and Esaias bearing witness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:3
verses.text: "The faithful (mercies)," the abiding (mercies), those which never perish.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:4
verses.text: (h) Paul loved them exceedingly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:5
verses.text: And observe, he does not enlarge on the ingratitude of the fathers, but puts before them what they must fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:6
verses.text: For Stephen indeed with good reason does this, seeing he was about to be put to death, not teaching them; and showing them, that the Law is even now on the point of being abolished: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:7
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:8
verses.text: ) but not so Paul; he does but threaten and put them in fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:9
verses.text: (f) And he does not dwell long on these, as taking it for granted that the word is of course believed; nor enlarge upon the greatness of their punishment, and assail that which they affectionately love, by showing the Law about to be cast out: but dwells upon that which is for their good (telling them), that great shall be the blessings for them being obedient, and great the evils being disobedient.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:10
verses.text: But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:11
verses.text: "Ye men of Israel," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:12
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:13
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:14
verses.text: ) The Promise then, he says, the fathers received; ye, the reality.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:15
verses.text: (j) And observe, he nowhere mentions right deeds of theirs, but (only) benefits on God's part: "He chose: Exalted: Suffered their manners:" these are no matters of praise to them: "They asked, He gave".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:16
verses.text: But David he does praise (and him) only, because from him the Christ was to come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:17
verses.text: "I have found David, the son of Jesse, a man after Mine own heart, which shall fulfil all My will".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:19
verses.text: ) (i) Observe also; it is with praise (that he says of him), "David after that he had served the will of God:" just as Peter—seeing it was then the beginning of the Gospel—making mention of him, said, "Let it be permitted me to speak freely of the patriarch David".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:20
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:21
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:22
verses.text: ) Also, he does not say, Died, but, "was added to his fathers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:23
verses.text: (k) Of this man's seed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:24
verses.text: "When John," he says, "had first preached before His entry"—by entry he means the Incarnation—"the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:27
verses.text: ) Thus also John, writing his Gospel, continually has recourse to him: for his name was much thought of in all parts of the world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:28
verses.text: And observe, he does not say it "Of this man's seed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:29
verses.text: from himself, but brings John's testimony.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:30
verses.text: "Men and brethren, children of the stock of Abraham"—he also calls them after their father—"unto you was the word of this salvation sent".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:32
verses.text: ) Here the expression, "Unto you," does not mean, Unto (you) Jews, but it gives them a right to sever themselves from those who dared that murder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:33
verses.text: And what he adds, shows this plainly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:34
verses.text: "For," he says, "they that dwell at Jerusalem, because they know Him not".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:36
verses.text: ) And how, you will say, could they be ignorant, with John to tell them? What marvel, seeing they were so, with the prophets continually crying aloud to them? Then follows another charge: "And having found no cause of death in Him:" in which ignorance had nothing to do.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:37
verses.text: For let us put the case, that they did not hold Him to be the Christ: why did they also kill Him? And "they desired of Pilate, he says, that He should be slain".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:39
verses.text: ) "And when they had fulfilled all that was written of Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:41
verses.text: ) Observe what a point he makes of showing that the (whole) thing was a (Divine) Dispensation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:42
verses.text: See, by saying what did they persuade men? (By telling them) that He was crucified? Why, what could be less persuasive than this? That He was buried—by them to whom it was promised that He should be salvation? that He who was buried forgives sins, yea, more than the Law (has power to do)? And (observe), he does not say, From which ye would not but, "from which ye could not be justified by the Law of Moses".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:43
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:44
verses.text: ) "Every one," he says: be who he may.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:45
verses.text: For those (ordinances) are of no use, unless there be some benefit (accruing therefrom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:46
verses.text: ) This is why he brings in forgiveness later: and shows it to be greater, when, the thing being (otherwise) impossible, yet this is effected.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:47
verses.text: "Who are His witnesses," he says, "unto the people"—the people that slew Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:48
verses.text: Who would never have been so, were they not strengthened by a Divine Power: for they would never have borne such witness to blood-thirsty men, to the very persons that killed Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:49
verses.text: But, "He hath raised up Jesus again: This day," he says, "I have begotten thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:50
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:51
verses.text: ) Aye, upon this the rest follows of course.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:52
verses.text: Why did he not allege some text by which they would be persuaded that forgiveness of sins is by Him? Because the great point with them was to show, in the first place, that He was risen: this being acknowledged, the other was unquestionable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:53
verses.text: "Through this man," nay more, by Him, "is remission of sins".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:55
verses.text: ) And besides, he wished to bring them to a longing desire of this great thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:56
verses.text: Well then, His death was not dereliction, but fulfilling of Prophecy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:57
verses.text: —For the rest, he puts them in mind of historical facts, wherein they through ignorance suffered evils without number.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:58
verses.text: And this he hints in the conclusion, saying, "Look, ye despisers, and behold".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:59
verses.text: And observe how, this being harsh, he cuts it short.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:60
verses.text: Let not that, he says, come upon you, which was spoken for the others, that "I work a work which ye shall in no wise believe, though one declare it unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:61
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:62
verses.text: ) Marvel not that it seems incredible: this very thing was foretold from the first—(that it would not be believed).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:63
verses.text: "Behold, ye despisers," as regards those who disbelieve in the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:64
verses.text: This too might with reason be said to us: "Behold ye despisers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:65
verses.text: For the Church indeed is in very evil case, although ye think her affairs to be in peace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:66
verses.text: For the mischief of it is, that while we labor under so many evils, we do not even know that we have any.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:67
verses.text: "What sayest thou? We are in possession of our Churches, our Church property, and all the rest, the services are held, the congregation comes to Church every day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:68
verses.text: True, but one is not to judge of the state of a Church from these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:69
verses.text: From what then? Whether there be piety, whether we return home with profit each day, whether reaping some fruit, be it much or little, whether we do it not merely of routine and for the formal acquittance of a duty (ἀφοσιούμενοι).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:70
verses.text: Who has become a better man by attending (daily) service for a whole month? That is the point: otherwise the very thing which seems to bespeak a flourishing condition (of the Church,) does in fact bespeak an ill condition, when all this is done, and nothing comes of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:71
verses.text: Would to God (that were all), that nothing comes of it: but indeed, as things are, it turns out even for the worse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:72
verses.text: What fruit do ye get from your services? Surely if you were getting any profit by them, ye ought to have been long leading the life of true wisdom (τἥς φιλοσοφίας), with so many Prophets twice in every week discoursing to you, so many Apostles, and Evangelists, all setting forth the doctrines of salvation, and placing before you with much exactness that which can form the character aright.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:73
verses.text: The soldier by going to his drill, becomes more perfect in his tactics: the wrestler by frequenting the gymnastic ground becomes more skilful in wrestling: the physician by attending on his teacher becomes more accurate, and knows more, and learns more: and thou—what hast thou gained? I speak not to those who have been members of the Church only a year, but to those who from their earliest age have been attending the services.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:74
verses.text: Think you that to be religious is to be constant in Church-going (παραβάλλειν τᾕ συνάξει)? This is nothing, unless we reap some fruit for ourselves: if (from the gathering together in Church) we do not gather (συνάγωμεν) something for ourselves, it were better to remain at home.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:75
verses.text: For our forefathers built the Churches for us, not just to bring us together from our private houses and show us one to another: since this could have been done also in a market-place, and in baths, and in a public procession:—but to bring together learners and teachers, and make the one better by means of the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:76
verses.text: With us it has all become mere customary routine, and formal discharge of a duty: a thing we are used to; that is all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:77
verses.text: Easter comes, and then great the stir, great the hubbub, and crowding of—I had rather not call them human beings, for their behavior is not commonly human.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:78
verses.text: Easter goes, the tumult abates, but then the quiet which succeeds is again fruitless of good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:79
verses.text: "Vigils, and holy hymn-singing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:80
verses.text: —And what is got by these? Nay, it is all the worse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:81
verses.text: Many do so merely out of vanity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:82
verses.text: Think how sick at heart it must make me, to see it all like (so much water) poured into a cask with holes in it! But ye will assuredly say to me, We know the Scriptures.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:83
verses.text: And what of that? If ye exemplify the Scriptures by your works, that is the gain, that the profit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:84
verses.text: The Church is a dyer's vat: if time after time perpetually ye go hence without receiving any dye, what is the use of coming here continually? Why, the mischief is all the greater.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:85
verses.text: Who (of you) has added ought to the customary practices he received from his fathers? For example: such an one has a custom of observing the memorial of his mother, or his wife, or his child: this he does whether he be told or whether he be not told by us, drawn to it by force of habit and conscience.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:86
verses.text: Does this displease thee, you ask? God forbid: on the contrary, I am glad of it with all my heart: only, I would wish that he had gained some fruit also from our discoursing, and that the effect which habit has, were also the effect as regards us (your teachers)—the superinducing of another habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:87
verses.text: Else why do I weary myself in vain, and talk uselessly, if ye are to remain in the same state, if the Church services work no good in you? Nay, you will say, we pray.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:88
verses.text: And what of that? "Not every one that saith unto Me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the Kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of My Father which is in heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:89
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:90
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:91
verses.text: ) Many a time have I determined to hold my peace, seeing no benefit accruing to you from my words; or perhaps there does accrue some, but I, through insatiableness and strong desire, am affected in the same way as those that are mad after riches.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:92
verses.text: For just as they, however much they may get, think they have nothing; so I, because I ardently desire your salvation, until I see you to have made good progress, think nothing done, because of my exceeding eager desire that you should arrive at the very summit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:93
verses.text: I would that this were the case, and that my eagerness were in fault, not your sloth: but I fear I conjecture but too rightly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:94
verses.text: For ye must needs be persuaded, that if any benefit had arisen in all this length of time, we ought ere now to have done speaking.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:95
verses.text: In such case, there were no need to you of words, since both in those already spoken there had been enough said for you, and you would be yourselves able to correct others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:96
verses.text: But the fact, that there is still a necessity of our discoursing to you, only shows, that matters with you are not in a state of high perfection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:97
verses.text: Then what would we have to be brought about? for one must not merely find fault.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:98
verses.text: I beseech and entreat you not to think it enough to have invaded the Church, but that ye also withdraw hence, having taken somewhat, some medicine, for the curing of your own maladies: and, if not from us, at any rate from the Scriptures, ye have the remedies suitable for each.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:99
verses.text: For instance, is any passionate? Let him attend to the Scripture-readings, and he will of a surety find such either in history or exhortation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:100
verses.text: In exhortation, when it is said, "The sway of his fury is his destruction" (Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:101
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:102
verses.text: ); and, "A passionate man is not seemly" (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:103
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:104
verses.text: ); and such like: and again, "A man full of words shall not prosper" (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:105
verses.text: cxl.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:106
verses.text: ); and Christ again, "He that is angry with his brother without a cause" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:107
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:108
verses.text: ); and again the Prophet, "Be ye angry, and sin not" (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:109
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:110
verses.text: ); and, "Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:111
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:112
verses.text: xlix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:113
verses.text: ) And in histories, as when thou hearest of Pharaoh filled with much wrath, and the Assyrian.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:114
verses.text: Again, is any one taken captive by love of money? let him hear, that "There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for this man setteth even his own soul for sale" (Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:115
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:116
verses.text: ); and how Christ saith, "Ye cannot serve God and mammon" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:117
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:118
verses.text: ); and the Apostle, that "the love of money is a root of all evils" ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:119
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:120
verses.text: ); and the Prophet, "If riches flow in, set not your heart upon them" (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:121
verses.text: lxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:122
verses.text: ); and many other like sayings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:123
verses.text: And from the histories thou hearest of Gehazi, Judas, the chief scribes, and that "gifts blind the eyes of the wise".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:124
verses.text: (Exod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:125
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:126
verses.text: and Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:127
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:128
verses.text: ) Is another proud? Let him hear that "God resisteth the proud" (James iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:129
verses.text: ); and, "Pride is the beginning of sin" (Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:130
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:131
verses.text: ) and, "Every one that hath a high heart, is impure before the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:132
verses.text: (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:133
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:134
verses.text: ) And in the histories, the devil, and all the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:135
verses.text: In a word, since it is impossible to recount all, let each choose out from the Divine Scriptures the remedies for his own hurts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:136
verses.text: So wash out, if not the whole at once, a part at any rate, part today, and part tomorrow, and then the whole.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:137
verses.text: And with regard to repentance too, and confession, and almsgiving, and justice also, and temperance, and all other things, thou wilt find many examples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:138
verses.text: "For all these things," says the Apostle, "were written for our admonition".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:139
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:140
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:141
verses.text: ) If then Scripture in all its discoursing is for our admonition, let us attend to it as we ought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:142
verses.text: Why do we deceive ourselves in vain? I fear it may be said of us also, that "our days have fallen short in vanity, and our years with haste".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:143
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:144
verses.text: lxxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:145
verses.text: ) Who from hearing us has given up the theatres? Who has given up his covetousness? Who has become more ready for almsgiving? I would wish to know this, not for the sake of vainglory, but that I may be inspirited to more zeal, seeing the fruit of my labors to be clearly evident.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:146
verses.text: But as things now are, how shall I put my hand to the work, when I see that for all the rain of doctrine pouring down upon you shower after shower, still our crops remain at the same measure, and the plants have waxed none the higher? Anon the time of threshing is at hand (and) He with the fan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:147
verses.text: I fear me, lest it be all stubble: I fear, lest we be all cast into the furnace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:148
verses.text: The summer is past, the winter is come: we sit, both young and old, taken captive by our own evil passions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:149
verses.text: Tell not me, I do not commit fornication: for what art thou the better, if though thou be no fornicator thou art covetous? It matters not to the sparrow caught in the snare that he is not held tight in every part, but only by the foot: he is a lost bird for all that; in the snare he is, and it profits him not that he has his wings free, so long as his foot is held tight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:150
verses.text: Just so, thou art caught, not by fornication, but by love of money: but caught thou art nevertheless; and the point is, not how thou art caught, but that thou art caught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:151
verses.text: Let not the young man say, I am no money-lover: well, but perchance thou art a fornicator: and then again what art thou the better? For the fact is, it is not possible for all the passions to set upon us at one and the same time of life: they are divided and marked off, and that, through the mercy of God, that they may not by assailing us all at once become insuperable, and so our wrestling with them be made more difficult.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:152
verses.text: What wretched inertness it shows, not to be able to conquer our passions even when taken one by one, but to be defeated at each several period of our life, and to take credit to ourselves for those which (let us alone) not in consequence of our own hearty endeavors, but merely because, by reason of the time of life, they are dormant? Look at the chariot-drivers, do you not see how exceedingly careful and strict they are with themselves in their training-practice, their labors, their diet, and all the rest, that they may not be thrown down from their chariots, and dragged along (by the reins)?—See what a thing art is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:153
verses.text: Often even a strong man cannot master a single horse: but a mere boy who has learnt the art shall often take the pair in hand, and with ease lead them and drive them where he will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:154
verses.text: Nay, in India it is said that a huge monster of an elephant shall yield to a stripling of fifteen, who manages him with the utmost ease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:155
verses.text: To what purpose have I said all this? To show that, if by dint of study and practice we can throttle into submission (ἄγχομεν) even elephants and wild horses, much more the passions within us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:156
verses.text: Whence is it that throughout life we continually fail (in every encounter)? We have never practised this art: never in a time of leisure when there is no contest, talked over with ourselves what shall be useful for us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:157
verses.text: We are never to be seen in our place on the chariot, until the time for the contest is actually come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:158
verses.text: Hence the ridiculous figure we make there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:159
verses.text: Have I not often said, Let us practise ourselves upon those of our own family before the time of trial? With our servants (παἵδας) at home we are often exasperated, let us there quell our anger, that in our intercourse with our friends we may come to have it easily under control.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:160
verses.text: And so, in the case of all the other passions, if we practised ourselves beforehand, we should not make a ridiculous figure in the contests themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:161
verses.text: But now we have our implements and our exercises and our trainings for other things, for arts and feats of the palaestra, but for virtue nothing of the sort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:162
verses.text: The husbandman would not venture to meddle with a vine, unless he had first been practised in the culture of it: nor the pilot to sit by the helm, unless he had first practised himself well at it: but we, in all respects unpractised, wish for the first prizes! It were good to be silent, good to have no communication with any man in act or word, until we were able to charm (κατεπᾴδειν) the wild beast that is within us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:163
verses.text: The wild beast, I say: for indeed is it not worse than the attack of any wild beast, when wrath and lust make war upon us? Beware of invading the market-place (Μὴ ἐμβάλῃς εἰς ἀγοράν) with these beasts, until thou have got the muzzle well upon their mouths, until thou have tamed and made them tractable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:164
verses.text: Those who lead about their tame lions in the market-place, do you not see what a gain they make of it, what admiration they get, because in the irrational beast they have succeeded in producing such tameness—but, should the lion suddenly take a savage fit, how he scares all the people out of the market-place, and then both the man that leads him about is himself in danger, and if there be loss of life to others, it is his doing? Well then do thou also first tame thy lion, and so lead him about, not for the purpose of receiving money, but that thou mayest acquire a gain, to which there is none equal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:165
verses.text: For there is nothing equal to gentleness, which both to those that possess it, and to those who are its objects, is exceeding useful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 77:166
verses.text: This then let us follow after, that having kept in the way of virtue, and with all diligence finished our course therein, we may be enabled to attain unto the good things eternal, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:1
verses.text: Homily XXX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:2
verses.text: Acts XIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:3
verses.text: "And as they were going out (text rec.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:4
verses.text: 'from the syn.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:5
verses.text: of the Jews,') they besought (the Gentiles) that these words might be spoken unto them on the following sabbath".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:6
verses.text: Do you mark Paul's wisdom? He not only gained admiration at the time, but put into them a longing desire for a second hearing, while in what he said he dropped some seeds (εἰπών τινα σπέρματα) as it were, and forbore to solve (the questions raised), or to follow out the subject to its conclusion, his plan being to interest them and engage their good-will to himself, and not make (people) listless and indifferent by casting all at once into the minds of those (who first heard him).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:7
verses.text: He told them the fact, that "through this Man is remission of sins announced unto you," but the how, he did not declare.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:8
verses.text: "And when the congregation was broken up, many of the Jews and worshipping proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas"—after this point he puts Paul first—"who, speaking unto them, persuaded them to continue in the grace of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:9
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:10
verses.text: ) Do you observe the eagerness, how great it is? They "followed" them, it says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:11
verses.text: Why did they not baptize them immediately? It was not the proper time: there was need to persuade them in order to their steadfast abiding therein.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:12
verses.text: "And the next sabbath day came almost the whole city together to hear the word of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:13
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:14
verses.text: ) "But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and contradicted the things spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:16
verses.text: ) See malice wounded in wounding others: this made the Apostles more conspicuous—the contradiction which those offered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:17
verses.text: In the first instance then they of their own accord besought them to speak (and now they opposed them): "contradicting," it says, "and blaspheming".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:18
verses.text: O recklessness! "Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:20
verses.text: ) Do you mark how by their contentious behavior they the more extended the preaching, and (how the Apostles here) gave themselves the more to the Gentiles, having (by this very thing) pleaded their justification, and made themselves clear of all blame with their own people (at Jerusalem)? (c) See how by their "envy" they bring about great things, other (than they looked for): they brought it about that the Apostles spake out boldly, and came to the Gentiles! For this is why he says, "And speaking out boldly, Paul and Barnabas said".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:21
verses.text: They were to go out to the Gentiles: but observe the boldness coming with measure: for if Peter pleaded in his justification, much more these needed a plea, none having called them there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:22
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:23
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:24
verses.text: ) But by saying "To you first," he showed that to those also it was their duty (to preach), and in saying "Necessary," he showed that it was necessary to be preached to them also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:25
verses.text: "But since ye turn away from it"—he does not say, "Woe unto you," and "Ye are punished," but "We turn unto the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:26
verses.text: With great gentleness is the boldness fraught! (a) Also he does not say, "Ye are unworthy," but "Have judged yourselves unworthy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:27
verses.text: Lo, we turn unto the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:28
verses.text: For so hath the Lord commanded us, saying, I have sent thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:30
verses.text: ) For that the Gentiles might not be hurt at hearing this, as if the case were so that, had the Jews been in earnest, they themselves would not have obtained the blessings, therefore he brings in the prophecy, saying, "A light of the Gentiles," and, "for salvation unto the ends of the earth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:31
verses.text: And hearing" (this) "the Gentiles" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:32
verses.text: )—this, while it was more cheering to them, seeing the case was this, that whereas those were of right to hear first, they themselves enjoy the blessing, was at the same time more stinging to those—"and the Gentiles," it says, "hearing" (this) "were glad, and glorified the word of the Lord: and believed, as many as were ordained unto eternal life": i-e:, set apart for God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:33
verses.text: Observe how he shows the speediness of the benefit: "And the word of the Lord was borne through all the region," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:34
verses.text: ) διεφέρετο, instead of διεκομίζετο, "was carried or conveyed through (it)".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:35
verses.text: (d) "But the Jews stirred up the devout and honorable women, and the chief men of the city, and raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled them out of their coasts".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:37
verses.text: ) "The devout women," (b) instead of the proselyte-women.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:38
verses.text: They did not stop at "envy," but added deeds also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:39
verses.text: (e) Do you see what they effected by their opposing the preaching? to what dishonor they brought these ("honorable women")? "But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:41
verses.text: ) Here now they used that terrible sign which Christ enjoined, "If any receive you not, shake off the dust from your feet" (Matt.

verses.text: ; Mark vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:44
verses.text: ); but these did it upon no light ground, but because they were driven away by them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:45
verses.text: This was no hurt to the disciples; on the contrary, they the more continued in the word: "And the disciples were filled with joy, and with the Holy Ghost" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:46
verses.text: ) for the suffering of the teacher does not check his boldness, but makes the disciple more courageous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:47
verses.text: "And it came to pass in Iconium, that they went both together into the synagogue of the Jews".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:48
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:49
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:50
verses.text: ) Again they entered into the synagogues.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:51
verses.text: See how far they were from becoming more timid! Having said, "We turn unto the Gentiles," nevertheless (by going into the synagogues) they superabundantly fortify their own justification (with their Jewish brethren).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:52
verses.text: "So that," it says, "a great multitude both of Jews and Greeks believed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:53
verses.text: For it is likely they discoursed as to Greeks also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:54
verses.text: "But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles, and made their minds evil affected against the brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:55
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:56
verses.text: ) Together (with themselves) now they took to stirring up the Gentiles too, as not being themselves sufficient.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:57
verses.text: Then why did the Apostles not go forth thence? Why, they were not driven away, only attacked.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:58
verses.text: "Long time therefore abode they speaking boldly in the Lord, which gave testimony unto the word of His grace, and granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:59
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:60
verses.text: ) This caused their boldness; or rather, of their boldness indeed their own hearty good-will was the cause—therefore it is that for a long while they work no signs—while the conversion of the hearers was (the effect) of the signs, though their boldness also contributed somewhat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:61
verses.text: "But the multitude of the city was divided: and part held with the Jews, and part with the Apostles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:62
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:63
verses.text: ) No small matter this dividing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:64
verses.text: And this was what the Lord said, "I am not come to bring peace, but a sword".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:65
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:66
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:67
verses.text: ) "And when there was an assault made both of the Gentiles, and also of the Jews with their rulers, to use them despitefully, and to stone them, they were ware of it, and fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and unto the region that lieth round about: and there they preached the Gospel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:68
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:69
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:70
verses.text: ) Again, as if they purposely wished to extend the preaching after it was increased, they once more sent them out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:71
verses.text: See on all occasions the persecutions working great good, and defeating the persecutors, and making the persecuted illustrious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:72
verses.text: For having come to Lystra, he works a great miracle, by raising the lame man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:73
verses.text: "And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother's womb, who never had walked: the same heard Paul speak: who steadfastly beholding him, and perceiving that he had faith to be healed, said with a loud voice"—why with a loud voice? that the multitude should believe—"Stand upright on thy feet".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:74
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:75
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:76
verses.text: ) But observe, he gave heed, it says, to the things spoken by Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:77
verses.text: Do you mark the elevation of the man's mind (φιλοσοφίαν)? He was nothing defeated (παρεβλάβη) by his lameness for earnestness of hearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:78
verses.text: "Who fixing his eyes upon him, and perceiving," it says, "that he had faith to be made whole".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:79
verses.text: He was already predisposed in purpose of mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:80
verses.text: And yet in the case of the others, it was the reverse: for first receiving healing in their bodies, they were then taken in hand for cure of their souls, but this man not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:81
verses.text: It seems to me, that Paul saw into his soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:82
verses.text: "And he leaped," it says, "and walked".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:83
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:84
verses.text: ) It was a proof of his perfect cure, the leaping.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:85
verses.text: "And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:86
verses.text: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:87
verses.text: Then the priest of Jupiter, which was before their city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:88
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:89
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:90
