verses.text: ) But this purpose was not yet manifest, for they spake in their own tongue, saying, "The gods in the likeness of men are come down to us:" therefore the Apostle said nothing to them as yet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:91
verses.text: But when they saw the garlands, then they went out, and rent their garments, "Which when the Apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of, they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out, and saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:92
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:93
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:94
verses.text: ) See how on all occasions they are clean from the lust of glory, not only not coveting, but even repudiating it when offered: just as Peter also said, "Why gaze ye on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made him to walk" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:95
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:96
verses.text: )? so these also say the same.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:97
verses.text: And Joseph also said of the dreams, "Is not their interpretation of God?" (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:98
verses.text: lx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:99
verses.text: ) And Daniel in like manner, "And to me also, not through the wisdom that is in me was it revealed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:100
verses.text: (Dan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:101
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:102
verses.text: ) And Paul everywhere says this, as when he says, "And for these things who is sufficient? Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think (aught) as of ourselves, but our sufficiency is of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:103
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:104
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:105
verses.text: ; iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:106
verses.text: ) But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:107
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:108
verses.text: ) "And when they were gone out," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:109
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:110
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:111
verses.text: Not merely were the multitudes drawn to them, but how? they besought to have the same words spoken to them again, and by their actions they showed their earnestness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:112
verses.text: "Now when the congregation," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:113
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:114
verses.text: ) See the Apostles on all occasions exhorting, not merely accepting men, nor courting them, but, "speaking unto them," it says, "they persuaded them to continue in the grace of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:115
verses.text: But when the Jews," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:116
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:117
verses.text: ) Why did they not contradict before this? Do you observe who on all occasions they were moved by passion? And they not only contradicted, but blasphemed also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:118
verses.text: For indeed malice stops at nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:119
verses.text: But see what boldness of speech! "It was necessary," he says, "that the word should have been spoken first to you, but since ye put it from you,"—(v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:120
verses.text: ) it is not put as affronting (though) it is in fact what they did in the case of the prophets: "Talk not to us," said they, "with talk"—(Is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:121
verses.text: xxx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:122
verses.text: ): "but since ye put it from you"—it, he saith, not us: for the affront on your part is not to us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:123
verses.text: For that none may take it as an expression of their piety (that he says,) "Ye judge not yourselves worthy," therefore he first says, "Ye put it from you," and then, "We turn unto the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:124
verses.text: The expression is full of gentleness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:125
verses.text: He does not say, We abandon you, but so that it is possible—he would say—that we may also turn hither again: and this too is not the consequence of the affront from you, "for so hath (the Lord) commanded us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:126
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:127
verses.text: ) "Then why have ye not done this?" It was indeed needful that the Gentiles should hear, and this not before you: it is your own doing, the "before you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:128
verses.text: "For so hath the Lord commanded us: I have set thee for a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation," i-e: for knowledge which is unto salvation, and not merely of the Gentiles, but of all men, "unto the ends of the earth—As many as were ordained unto eternal life" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:129
verses.text: ): this is also a proof, that their having received these Gentiles was agreeable with the mind of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:130
verses.text: But "ordained," not in regard of necessity: "whom He foreknew," saith the Apostle, "He did predestinate".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:131
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:132
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:133
verses.text: ) "And the word of the Lord," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:134
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:135
verses.text: ) No longer in the city (only) were (their doctrines) disseminated, but also in the (whole) region.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:136
verses.text: For when they of the Gentiles had heard it, they also after a little while came over.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:137
verses.text: "But the Jews stirred up the devout women, and raised persecution"—observe even of what is done by the women, they are the authors—"and cast them," it says, "out of their coasts" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:138
verses.text: ), not from the city merely.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:139
verses.text: Then, what is more terrible, "they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:140
verses.text: But the disciples, it says, were filled with joy, and with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:141
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:142
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:143
verses.text: ) The teachers were suffering persecution, and the disciples rejoiced.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:144
verses.text: "And so spake, that a great multitude," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:145
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:146
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:147
verses.text: ) Do you mark the nature of the Gospel, the great virtue it has? "Made their minds evil-affected," it says, "against the brethren:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:148
verses.text: ) i-e: slandered the Apostles, raised numberless accusations against them: (these people, being simple, they "made evil-affected," disposed them to act a malignant part.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:149
verses.text: And see how on all occasions he refers all to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:150
verses.text: "Long time," he says, "abode they speaking boldly in the Lord, which gave testimony unto the word of His grace".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:151
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:152
verses.text: ) Think not this (expression, "Gave testimony,") hath aught derogatory (to the Lord's Divine Majesty): "Who witnessed," it is said, "before Pontius Pilate".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:153
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:154
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:155
verses.text: ) Then the boldness—"and granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:156
verses.text: Here he speaks it as concerning their own nation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:157
verses.text: "And the multitude of the city," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:158
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:159
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:160
verses.text: ) Accordingly they did not wait for it, but saw the intention of attacking them, and fled, on no occasion kindling their wrath, "to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, and Derbe, and the adjacent region".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:161
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:162
verses.text: ) They went away into the country, not into the cities only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:163
verses.text: —Observe both the simplicity of the Gentiles, and the malignity of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:164
verses.text: By their actions they showed that they were worthy to hear: they so honored them from the miracles only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:165
verses.text: The one sort honored them as gods, the other persecuted them as pestilent fellows: and (those) not only did not take offence at the preaching, but what say they? "The gods, in the likeness of men, are come down to us;" but the Jews were offended.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:166
verses.text: "And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:167
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:168
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:169
verses.text: ) I suppose Barnabas was a man of dignified appearance also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:170
verses.text: Here was a new sort of trial, from immoderate zeal, and no small one: but hence also is shown the virtue of the Apostles, (and) how on all occasions they ascribe all to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:171
verses.text: Let us imitate them: let us think nothing our own, seeing even faith itself is not our own, but more God's (than ours).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:172
verses.text: "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and this," saith he, "not of ourselves; it is the gift of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:173
verses.text: (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:174
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:175
verses.text: ) Then let us not think great things of ourselves, nor be puffed up, being as we are, men, dust and ashes, smoke and shadow.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:176
verses.text: For say, Why dost thou think great things of thyself? Hast thou given alms, and lavished thy substance? And what of that? Think, what if God had chosen not to make thee rich? think of them that are impoverished, or rather, think how many have given (not their substance only, but) their bodies moreover, and after their numberless sacrifices, have felt still that they were miserable creatures! Thou gavest for thyself, Christ (not for Himself, but) for thee: thou didst but pay a debt, Christ owed thee not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:177
verses.text: —See the uncertainty of the future, and "be not high-minded, but fear" (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:178
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:179
verses.text: ); do not lessen thy virtue by boastfulness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:180
verses.text: Wouldest thou do something truly great? Never let a surmise of thy attainments as great enter thy mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:181
verses.text: But thou art a virgin? So were those in (the Gospel) virgins, but they got no benefit from their virginity, because of their cruelty and inhumanity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:182
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:183
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:184
verses.text: ) Nothing like humility: this is mother, and root, and nurse,and foundation, and bond of all good things: without this we are abominable, and execrable, and polluted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:185
verses.text: For say—let there be some man raising the dead, and healing the lame, and cleansing the lepers, but with proud self-complacency: than this there can be nothing more execrable, nothing more impious, nothing more detestable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:186
verses.text: Account nothing to be of thyself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:187
verses.text: Hast thou utterance and grace of teaching? Do not for this account thyself to have aught more than other men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:188
verses.text: For this cause especially thou oughtest to be humbled, because thou hast been vouchsafed more abundant gifts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:189
verses.text: For he to whom more was forgiven, will love more (Luke vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:190
verses.text: ): if so, then oughtest thou to be humbled also, for that God having passed by others, took notice of thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:191
verses.text: Fear thou because of this: for often this is a cause of destruction to thee, if thou be not watchful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:192
verses.text: Why thinkest thou great things of thyself? Because thou teachest by words? But this is easy, to philosophize in words: teach me by thy life: that is the best teaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:193
verses.text: Sayest thou that it is right to be moderate, and dost thou make a long speech about this thing, and play the orator, pouring forth thy eloquence without a check? But "better than thou is he" shall one say to thee, "who teaches me this by his deeds"—for not so much are those lessons wont to be fixed in the mind which consist in words, as those which teach by things: since if thou hast not the deed, thou not only hast not profited him by thy words, but hast even hurt him the more—"better thou wert silent".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:194
verses.text: Wherefore? "Because the thing thou proposest to me is impossible: for I consider, that if thou who hast so much to say about it, succeedest not in this, much more am I excusable".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:195
verses.text: For this cause the Prophet says, "But unto the sinner said God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:196
verses.text: Why declarest thou My statutes?" (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:197
verses.text: lx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:198
verses.text: ) For this is a worse mischief, when one who teaches well in words, impugns the teaching by his deeds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:199
verses.text: This has been the cause of many evils in the Churches.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:200
verses.text: Wherefore pardon me, I beseech you, that my discourse dwells long on this evil affection (πάθει).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:201
verses.text: Many take a deal of pains to be able to stand up in public, and make a long speech: and if they get applause from the multitude, it is to them as if they gained the very kingdom (of heaven): but if silence follows the close of their speech, it is worse than hell itself, the dejection that falls upon their spirits from the silence! This has turned the Churches upside down, because both you desire not to hear a discourse calculated to lead you to compunction, but one that may delight you from the sound and composition of the words, as though you were listening to singers and minstrels (κιθαρῳδὥν καὶ κιθαριστὣν, supra p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:202
verses.text: ): and we too act a preposterous and pitiable part in being led by your lusts, when we ought to root them out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:203
verses.text: And so it is just as if the father of a poor cold-blooded child (already, more delicate than it ought to be), should, although it is so feeble, give it cake and cold (drink) and whatever only pleases the child, and take no account of what might do it good; and then, being reproved by the physicians, should excuse himself by saying, "What can I do? I cannot bear to see the child crying".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:204
verses.text: Thou poor, wretched creature, thou betrayer! for I cannot call such a one a father: how much better were it for thee, by paining him for a short time, to restore him to health forever, than to make this short-lived pleasure the foundation of a lasting sorrow? Just such is our case, when we idly busy ourselves about beautiful expressions, and the composition and harmony of our sentences, in order that we may please, not profit: (when) we make it our aim to be admired, not to instruct; to delight, not prick to the heart; to be applauded and depart with praise, not to correct men's manners! Believe me, I speak not other than I feel—when as I discourse I hear myself applauded, at the moment indeed I feel it as a man (for why should I not own the truth?): I am delighted, and give way to the pleasurable feeling: but when I get home, and bethink me that those who applauded received no benefit from my discourse, but that whatever benefit they ought to have got, they lost it while applauding and praising, I am in pain, and groan, and weep, and feel as if I had spoken all in vain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:205
verses.text: I say to myself: "What profit comes to me from my labors, while the hearers do not choose to benefit by what they hear from us?" Nay, often have I thought to make a rule which should prevent all applauding, and persuade you to listen with silence and becoming orderliness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:206
verses.text: But bear with me, I beseech you, and be persuaded by me, and, if it seem good to you, let us even now establish this rule, that no hearer be permitted to applaud in the midst of any person's discourse, but if he will needs admire, let him admire in silence: there is none to prevent him: and let all his study and eager desire be set upon the receiving the things spoken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:207
verses.text: —What means that noise again? I am laying down a rule against this very thing, and you have not the forbearance even to hear me!—Many will be the good effects of this regulation: it will be a discipline of philosophy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:208
verses.text: Even the heathen philosophers—we hear of their discoursing, and nowhere do we find that noisy applause accompanied their words: we hear of the Apostles, making public speeches, and yet nowhere do the accounts add, that in the midst of their speeches the hearers interrupted the speakers with loud expressions of approbation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:209
verses.text: A great gain will this be to us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:210
verses.text: But let us establish this rule: in quiet let us all hear, and speak the whole (of what we have to say).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:211
verses.text: For if indeed it were the case that we departed retaining what we had heard, what I insist upon is, that even so the praise is not beneficial—but not to go too much into particulars (on this point); let none tax me with rudeness —but since nothing is gained by it, nay, it is even mischievous, let us loose the hindrance, let us put a stop to the boundings, let us retrench the gambollings of the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:212
verses.text: Christ spoke publicly on the Mount: yet no one said aught, until He had finished His discourse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:213
verses.text: I do not rob those who wish to be applauded: on the contrary, I make them to be more admired.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:214
verses.text: It is far better that one's hearer, having listened in silence, should by his memory throughout all time applaud, both at home and abroad, than that having lost all he should return home empty, not possessed of that which was the subject of his applauses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:215
verses.text: For how shall the hearer be otherwise than ridiculous? Nay, he will be deemed a flatterer, and his praises no better than irony, when he declares that the teacher spoke beautifully, but what he said, this he cannot tell.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:216
verses.text: This has all the appearance of adulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:217
verses.text: For when indeed one has been hearing minstrels and players, it is no wonder if such be the case with him, seeing he knows not how to utter the strain in the same manner: but where the matter is not an exhibition of song or of voice, but the drift and purport of thoughts and wise reflection (φιλοσοφίας), and it is easy for every one to tell and report what was said, how can he but deserve the accusation, who cannot tell what the matter was for which he praised the speaker? Nothing so becomes a Church as silence and good order.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:218
verses.text: Noise belongs to theatres, and baths, and public processions, and market-places: but where doctrines, and such doctrines, are the subject of teaching, there should be stillness, and quiet, and calm reflection, and a haven of much repose (φιλοσοφία καὶ πολὺς ὁ λιμήν).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:219
verses.text: These things I beseech and entreat: for I go about in quest of ways by which I shall be enabled to profit your souls.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:220
verses.text: And no small way I take this to be: it will profit not you only, but us also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:221
verses.text: So shall we not be carried away with pride (ἐκτραχηλίζεσθαί), not be tempted to love praises and honor, not be led to speak those things which delight, but those which profit: so shall we lay the whole stress of our time and diligence not upon arts of composition and beauties of expression, but upon the matter and meaning of the thoughts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:222
verses.text: Go into a painter's study, and you will observe how silent all is there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:223
verses.text: Then so ought it to be here: for here too we are employed in painting portraits, royal portraits (every one of them), none of any private man, by means of the colors of virtue—How now? Applauding again? This is a reform not easy, but (only) by reason of long habit, to be effected.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:224
verses.text: —The pencil moreover is the tongue, and the Artist the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:225
verses.text: Say, during the celebration of the Mysteries, is there any noise? any disturbance? when we are baptizing (βαπτιζώμεθα), when we are doing all the other acts? Is not all Nature decked (as it were) with stillness and silence? Over all the face of heaven is scattered this charm (of repose).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:226
verses.text: —On this account are we evil spoken of even among the Gentiles, as though we did all for display and ostentation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:227
verses.text: But if this be prevented, the love of the chief seats also will be extinguished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:228
verses.text: It is sufficient, if any one be enamoured of praise, that he should obtain it after having been heard, when all is gathered in.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 78:229
verses.text: Yea, I beseech you, let us establish this rule, that doing all things according to God's will, we may be found worthy of the mercy which is from Him, through the grace and compassion of His only begotten Son our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father together with the Holy Spirit be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:1
verses.text: Homily XXXI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:2
verses.text: Acts XIV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:3
verses.text: ,  "Which when the Apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of, they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out and saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and preach unto you that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God, which made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all things that are therein".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:4
verses.text: Mark the vehemence with which all this is done by the Apostles: "rent their clothes, ran in, cried out," all from strong affection of the soul, revolted by the things that were done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:5
verses.text: For it was a grief, indeed a grief inconsolable, that they should needs be thought gods, and introduce idolatry, the very thing which they came to destroy! This also was a contrivance of the devil—but he did not prevail.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:6
verses.text: But what say they? "We also are men of like passions with you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:7
verses.text: At the very outset they overthrew the evil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:8
verses.text: They said not simply, "Men," but "As ye".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:9
verses.text: Then, that they may not seem to honor the gods, hear what they add: "Preaching unto you, that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God, Who made heaven, the sea, and all things that are therein".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:10
verses.text: Observe how they nowhere mention things invisible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:11
verses.text: (b) For they had learnt that one should study not so much to say somewhat worthy of God, as to say what is profitable for the hearers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:12
verses.text: (a) What then? if He be Maker of all things, why does He not also attend to these things by His Providence?—"Who in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:13
verses.text: )—but wherefore He suffered them, this he does not say, for at present he keeps to the matter of immediate importance, nowhere bringing in the name of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:14
verses.text: Observe, he does not wish to swell the accusation against them, but rather that they themselves should refer all to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:15
verses.text: "Nevertheless, He left not Himself without witness, in that He did good, giving you rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:16
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:17
verses.text: ) (c) See how covertly he puts the accusation "in that He did good," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:18
verses.text: And yet if God did this, He could not have "let them alone;" on the contrary, they ought to be punished, for that, enjoying so great benefits, they had not acknowledged Him, not even as their feeder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:19
verses.text: "From heaven," he says, "giving you rain".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:20
verses.text: Thus also David said, "From the fruit of their corn and wine and oil were they made to abound" (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:21
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:22
verses.text: ), and in many places speaking of Creation, he brings forward these benefits: and Jeremiah mentions first Creation, then Providence (shown) by the rains, so that the Apostle here discourses as taught from those Scriptures.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:23
verses.text: "Filling," he says, "with food and gladness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:24
verses.text: (Jer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:25
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:26
verses.text: ) With large liberality (φιλοτιμίας) the food is given, not merely for a frugal sufficiency, nor stinted by the need.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:27
verses.text: "And saying these things, they scarcely stopped the multitudes" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:28
verses.text: )—indeed by this very thing they gained most admiration—"from sacrificing to them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:29
verses.text: Do you observe that this was the point with them to put an end to that madness? "But there came," it says, "certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:30
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:31
verses.text: —Indeed children of the devil, that not in their own cities only, but also beyond them, they did these things, and as much made it their study to make an end of the preaching, as the Apostles were in earnest to establish it!—"and having persuaded the multitude and stoned Paul, they dragged him out of the city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:32
verses.text: (e) So then, the Gentiles regarded them as gods, but these "dragged" him, "out of the city, supposing he had been dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:33
verses.text: Having persuaded the multitude"—for it is not likely that all thus reverenced them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:34
verses.text: In the very city in which they received this reverence, in the same were they thus terribly ill treated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:35
verses.text: And this also profited the beholders.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:36
verses.text: "Lest any man," he says, "should think of me above that which he seeth me to be, or that he heareth aught from me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:38
verses.text: )—"Howbeit as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up and came into the city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:39
verses.text: (d) Here is fulfilled that saying, "My grace is sufficient for thee, for My strength is made perfect in weakness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:40
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:41
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:42
verses.text: ) Greater this than the raising of the lame man! (f) "Came into the city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:43
verses.text: Do you mark the zeal, do you mark how fervent he is, how set on fire! He came into the city itself again: for proof that if on any occasion he did retire, it was because he had sown the word, and because it was not right to inflame their wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:44
verses.text: (h) Then they went over all the cities in which they had been in danger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:45
verses.text: "And on the morrow," it says, "he went forth with Barnabas to Derbe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:46
verses.text: And when they had preached the Gospel to that city, and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch, confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:48
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:49
verses.text: ) This they said, this they showed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:50
verses.text: But it is purposely so done, not only by the Apostles, but by the disciples also, that they may learn from the very outset both the might of the preaching, and that they must themselves also suffer such things, that they may stand nobly, not idly gaping for the miracles, but much more (ready) for the trials.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:51
verses.text: Therefore also the Apostle himself said, "Having the same conflict which ye saw in me and heard".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:52
verses.text: (Phil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:53
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:54
verses.text: ) Persecutions succeeded to persecutions: wars, fightings, stonings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:55
verses.text: (g) These things, not less than the miracles, both made them more illustrious, and prepared for them a greater rejoicing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:56
verses.text: The Scripture nowhere says that they returned rejoicing because they had done miracles, but (it does say that they rejoiced), that "they were counted worthy for that Name to suffer shame".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:57
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:58
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:59
verses.text: ) And this they were taught of Christ, saying, "Rejoice not that the devils obey you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:60
verses.text: (Luke x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:61
verses.text: ) For the joy indeed and without alloy is this, to suffer aught for Christ's sake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:62
verses.text: (i) "And that through much tribulation:" what sort of cheering (προτροπή) is this? how did they persuade them, by telling them at the outset of tribulations? Then also another consolation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:63
verses.text: "And when they had appointed for them elders in every Church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they believed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:64
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:65
verses.text: ) Do you mark Paul's ardor?—Then other consolation: "Commended them," it says, "to the Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:66
verses.text: And after they had passed throughout Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:67
verses.text: And when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down into Attalia (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:68
verses.text: , ): (l) and thence sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been recommended to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:69
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:70
verses.text: ) Why do they come back to Antioch? To report what had taken place yonder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:71
verses.text: And besides, there is a great purpose of Providence concerned: for it was needful that they should thenceforth preach with boldness to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:72
verses.text: They come therefore, reporting these things, that they may be able to know them: and it is providentially ordered, that just then came those who forbade to keep company with the Gentiles in order that from Jerusalem they might obtain great encouragement, and so go their ways with boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:73
verses.text: And besides, it shows that in their temper there was nothing of self-will: for they come, at the same time showing their boldness, in that without the authority of those (at Jerusalem) they had preached to the Gentiles, and their obedience, in that they refer the matter to them: for they were not made arrogant, as (ἀπενοήθησαν) having achieved so great successes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:74
verses.text: "Whence," it says, "they had been recommended to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:75
verses.text: And yet moreover the Spirit had said, "Separate Me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:76
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:77
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:78
verses.text: ) "And when they were come, and had gathered the Church together, they rehearsed all that God had done with them, and how He had opened the door of faith unto the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:79
verses.text: And there they abode long time with the disciples".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:80
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:81
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:82
verses.text: ) For the city being great had need of teachers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:83
verses.text: —But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:84
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:85
verses.text: ) "Which when the Apostles," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:86
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:87
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:88
verses.text: First by the sight they checked them, by rending their garments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:89
verses.text: This did Joshua the son of Nun upon the occasion of the defeat of the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:90
verses.text: Then think not that this action was unworthy of them: for such was the eagerness, they would not otherwise have restrained it would not otherwise have quenched the conflagration (πύραν).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:91
verses.text: Therefore when need is to do something that is fit to be done, let us not decline it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:92
verses.text: For if even after all this they hardly persuaded them, if they had not acted thus, what might have been the consequence? For if they had not done thus, they would have been thought to make a show of humility (ταπεινοθρονεἵν), and to be all the more desirous of the honor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:93
verses.text: And observe their language, how in rebuking it is moderated, alike full of wonder and of rebuke.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:94
verses.text: This above all it was that hindered them, the saying, "Preaching unto you to turn from these vanities unto God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:95
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:96
verses.text: ) We are men indeed, they say, but greater than these: for these are dead things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:97
verses.text: Mark how they not only subvert (the false), but teach (the true), saying nothing about things invisible—"Who made," say they, "heaven and earth, and the sea, and all things that are therein.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:98
verses.text: Who in times past," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:99
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:101
verses.text: ) He names as witnesses even the years (in their courses).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:102
verses.text: "And there came thither certain Jews," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:103
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:104
verses.text: ) O that Jewish madness! Among a people that had so honored the Apostles, they had the hardihood to come, and to stone Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:105
verses.text: "And they dragged him out of the city," being afraid of those (others),—"Supposing he had been dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:106
verses.text: (k) "Howbeit," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:107
verses.text: "and came into the city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:108
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:109
verses.text: ) For that the spirits of the disciples might not be downcast because they who were accounted gods suffered such treatment, they came in unto them and discoursed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:110
verses.text: "Then on the morrow," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:111
verses.text: And observe, first he goes forth to Derbe, and then comes back to Lystra and Iconium and Antioch, (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:112
verses.text: ) giving way to them while their passions are roused, but when they have ceased, then attacking them again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:113
verses.text: Do you mark, that it was not by (supernatural) grace that they managed all that they did, but by their own diligence? "Confirming," it says "the souls of the disciples:" ἐπιστηρίζοντες, "further establishing;" so that they were established, but they added more thereto.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:114
verses.text: "And that we must," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:116
verses.text: ): they foretold (this), that they might not be offended.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:117
verses.text: "And when they had appointed for them," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:118
verses.text: Again the ordinations accompanied with fastings: and again fasting, that purifying of our souls.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:119
verses.text: (m) "And having prayed," it says, "with fastings, they commended them unto the Lord" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:120
verses.text: ): they taught them to fast also in their trials.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:121
verses.text: (o) Why did they not make elders in Cyprus nor in Samaria? Because the latter was near to Jerusalem, the former to Antioch, and the word was strong there; whereas in those parts they needed much consolation, especially they of the Gentiles, who behooved to have much instruction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:122
verses.text: "And when they were come," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:123
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:124
verses.text: ) They came, teaching them that with good reason had they been ordained by the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:125
verses.text: (n) They said not what they themselves, but "what God had done with them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:126
verses.text: It seems to me, that they mean their trials.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:127
verses.text: It was not for nothing that they come here, nor to rest, but providentially guided by the Spirit, to the end that the preaching to the Gentiles might be firmly established.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:128
verses.text: (p) And mark Paul's ardor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:129
verses.text: He does not ask whether it be right to speak to Gentiles, but he straightway speaks: therefore it is that he says, "I did not refer myself to flesh and blood".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:130
verses.text: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:131
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:132
verses.text: )  For it is indeed a great thing, a great, a generous soul (like this)! How many have since believed, and none of them all has shone like him! What we want is earnestness, exceeding ardor, a soul ready to encounter death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:133
verses.text: Else is it not possible to attain unto the Kingdom, not being crucified.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:134
verses.text: Let us not deceive ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:135
verses.text: For if in war it is impossible to come off safe while living daintily, and trafficking, and huckstering and idling, much more in this war.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:136
verses.text: Or think ye not that it is a war worse than all others? (Infra, p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:137
verses.text: , note.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:138
verses.text: ) "For we wrestle not," he says, "against flesh and blood".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:139
verses.text: (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:140
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:141
verses.text: ) Since even while taking our meals and walking, and bathing, the enemy is present with us, and knows no time of truce, except that of sleep only: nay, often even then he carries on the war, injecting into us unclean thoughts, and making us lewd by means of dreams.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:142
verses.text: We watch not, we do not rouse ourselves up, do not look to the multitude of the forces opposed to us, do not reflect, that this very thing constitutes the greatest misfortune—that though surrounded by so great wars, we live daintily as in time of peace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:143
verses.text: Believe me, worse than Paul suffered may have to be suffered now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:144
verses.text: Those enemies wounded him with stones: there is a wounding with words, even worse than stones.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:145
verses.text: What then must we do? The same that he did: he did not hate those who cast stones at him, but after they had dragged him out, he entered again into their city, to be a benefactor to those who had done him such wrongs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:146
verses.text: If thou also endurest him who harshly insults thee, and has done thee wrongs, then hast thou too been stoned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:147
verses.text: Say not, "I have done him no injury".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:148
verses.text: For what injury had Paul done, that he should be stoned? He was announcing a Kingdom, he was bringing men away from error, and bringing them to God: benefits these, worthy of crowns, worthy of proclamation by voice of herald, worthy of a thousand good things—not of stones.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:149
verses.text: And yet (far from resenting) he did just the contrary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:150
verses.text: For this is the splendid victory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:151
verses.text: "And they dragged him," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:152
verses.text: ) it says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:153
verses.text: These too they often drag: but be not thou angry; on the contrary, preach thou the word with gentleness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:154
verses.text: Hath one insulted thee? Hold thy peace, and bless if thou canst, and thou also hast preached the word, hast given a lesson of gentleness, a lesson of meekness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:155
verses.text: I know that many do not so smart under wounds, as they do under the blow which is inflicted by words: as indeed the one wound the body receives the other the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:156
verses.text: But let us not smart, or rather feeling the smart let us endure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:157
verses.text: Do you not see the pugilists, how, with their heads sorely battered, they bite their teeth into their lips, and so bear their smarts kindly? No need to grind the teeth, no need to bite (the lips).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:158
verses.text: Remember thy Master, and by the remembrance thou hast at once applied the remedy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:159
verses.text: Remember Paul: reflect that thou, the beaten hast conquered, and he the beater, is defeated; and by this hast thou cured the whole.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:160
verses.text: It is the turning of the scale a moment and thou hast achieved the whole: be not hurried away, do not even move, thou hast extinguished the whole (fire).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:161
verses.text: Great eloquence of persuasion there is in suffering aught for Christ: thou preachest not the word of faith, but thou preachest the word of patience (φιλοσοφίας).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:162
verses.text: But, you will say, the more he sees my gentleness, the more he sets upon me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:163
verses.text: Is it for this then that thou art pained, that he increases thy rewards the more? "But this is the way," you say, "to make him unbearable".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:164
verses.text: This is mere pretext of thine own littleness of mind: on the contrary, the other is the way to make him unbearable, namely, that thou avenge thyself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:165
verses.text: If God had known, that through forbearance of revenge, the unjust became unbearable, He would not have done this Himself: on the contrary, He would have said, Avenge thyself: but He knew, that other than this is the more likely way to do good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:166
verses.text: Make not thou a law contrary to God: do as He bids thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:167
verses.text: Thou art not kinder than He that made us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:168
verses.text: He hath said, "Bear to be wronged:" thou sayest, "I requite wrong for wrong, that he may not become unbearable".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:169
verses.text: Hast thou then more care for him than God has? Such talk is mere passion and ill temper, arrogance and setting up laws against God's laws.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:170
verses.text: For even if the man were hurt (by our forbearance), would it not be our duty to obey? When God orders anything, let us not make a contrary law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:171
verses.text: "A submissive answer," we read, turneth away wrath" (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:172
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:173
verses.text: ): not an answer of opposition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:174
verses.text: If it profits thee, it profits him also: but if it hurts thee who art to set him right, how much more will it hurt him? "Physician, heal thyself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:175
verses.text: Hath one spoken ill of thee? Commend him thou.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:176
verses.text: Hath he reviled thee? Praise him thou.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:177
verses.text: Hath he plotted against thee? Do him a kindness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:178
verses.text: Requite him with the contrary things, if at least thou at all carest for his salvation and wish not thou to revenge thine own suffering.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:179
verses.text: And yet, you will say, though he has often met with long-suffering from me he has become worse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:180
verses.text: This is not thine affair, but his.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:181
verses.text: Wilt thou learn what wrongs God suffered? They threw down His altars, and slew His prophets ( Kings xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:182
verses.text: ), yet He endured it all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:183
verses.text: Could He not have launched a thunderbolt from above? Nay, when He had sent His prophets, and they killed them, then He sent His Son (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:184
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:185
verses.text: ), when they wrought greater impieties, then He sent them greater benefits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:186
verses.text: And thou too, if thou seest one exasperated, then yield the more: since this madness has greater need of soothing (παραμθίας).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:187
verses.text: The more grievous his abuse of thee, the more meekness does he need from thee: and even as a gale when it blows strong, then it requires yielding to, so also he who is in a passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:188
verses.text: When the wild beast is most savage, then we all flee: so also should we flee from him that is angry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:189
verses.text: Think not that this is an honor to him: for is it an honor we show to the wild beast, and to madmen, when we turn aside out of their way? By no means it is a dishonor and a scorn: or rather not dishonor and scorn, but compassion and humanity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:190
verses.text: Seest thou not how the sailors, when the wind blows violently, take down their sails, that the vessel may not sink? how, when the horses have run away with the driver, he only leads them into the (open) plain, and does not pull against them that he may not voluntarily exhaust his strength? This do thou also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:191
verses.text: Wrath is afire, it is a quick flame needing fuel: do not supply food to the fire, and thou hast soon extinguished the evil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:192
verses.text: Anger has no power of itself; there must be another to feed it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:193
verses.text: For thee there is no excuse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:194
verses.text: He is possessed with madness, and knows not what he does; but when thou, seeing what he is, fallest into the same evils, and art not brought to thy right senses by the sight, what excuse can there be for thee? If coming to a feast thou see at the very outset of the feast some one drunken and acting unseemly, would not he, who after seeing him makes himself drunk, be much more inexcusable? Just so it is here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:195
verses.text: Do we think it any excuse to say, I was not the first to begin? This is against us, that even the sight of the other in that condition did not bring us to our right senses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:196
verses.text: It is just as if one should say, "I did not murder him first".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:197
verses.text: For this very thing makes thee deserving of punishment, that even upon the warning of such a spectacle thou didst not restrain thyself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:198
verses.text: If thou shouldest see the drunken man in the act of vomiting, retching, bursting, his eyes strained, filling the table with his filthiness, everybody hurrying out of his way, and then shouldest fall into the same state thyself, wouldest thou not be more hateful? Like him is he that is in a passion: more than he who vomits, he has his veins distended, his eyes inflamed, his bowels racked; he vomits forth words far more filthy than that food; all crude what he utters, nothing duly digested, for his passion will not let it be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:199
verses.text: But as in that case excess of fumes (χυμων), making an uproar in the stomach, often rejects all its contents; so here, excess of heat, making a tumult in the soul suffers him not to conceal what it were right to leave unsaid, but things fit and unfit to be spoken, he says all alike, not putting the hearers but himself to shame.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:200
verses.text: As then we get out of the way of those that vomit, so let us from those who are angry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:201
verses.text: Let us cast dust upon their vomit: By doing what? By holding our peace: let us call the dogs to eat up the vomit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:202
verses.text: I know that ye are disgusted at hearing this: but I wish you to feel this same disgust when ye see these things take place, and not to be pleased at the thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:203
verses.text: The abusive man is filthier than the dog that returneth to its own vomit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:204
verses.text: For if indeed having vomited once he were done with it, he would not be like that dog: but if he vomits the same things again, it is plain that he does so from having eaten the same again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:205
verses.text: What then is more abominable than such an one? What filthier than that mouth which chews such food? And yet this is a work of nature, but the other not or rather both the one and the other are contrary to nature.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:206
verses.text: How? Since it is not according to nature to be causelessly abusive, but against nature: he speaks nothing then like a man, but part as beast, part as madman.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:207
verses.text: As then the disease of the body is contrary to nature, so also is this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:208
verses.text: And to show that it is contrary to nature, if he shall continue in it, he will perish by little and little: but if he continue in that which is natural, he will not perish.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:209
verses.text: I had rather sit at table with a man who eats dirt, than with one who speaks such words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:210
verses.text: See ye not the swine devouring dung? So also do these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:211
verses.text: For what is more stinking than the words which abusive men utter? It is their study to speak nothing wholesome, nothing pure, but whatever is base, whatever is unseemly, that they study both to do and say: and what is worse, they think to disgrace others, while they in fact are disgracing themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:212
verses.text: For that it is themselves they disgrace is plain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:213
verses.text: For, leaving out of the question those who speak lies (in their railings), say it be some notorious harlot, or even from the stage some other (abandoned creature), and let that person be having a fight with some other person: then let the latter cast this up to the former (what she or he is), and the former retort upon the latter the same reproach: which of them is most damaged by the words? For the former is but called what in fact he or she is, which is not the case with the other: so that the first gets nothing more in the way of shame (than there was before), while to the other there accrues a great accession of disgrace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:214
verses.text: But again, let there be some hidden actions (mod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:215
verses.text: text εἰργασμένα "which have been done"), and let only the person abusing know of them: then, holding his peace until now, let him openly parade (ἐκπομπευέτω) the reproach: even so, he himself is more disgraced than the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:216
verses.text: How? by making himself the herald of the wickedness, so getting for himself either the imputation of not being privy to any such thing, or the character of one not fit to be trusted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:217
verses.text: And you shall see all men forthwith accuse him: "If indeed he had been privy to a murder being done, he ought to have revealed it all:" and so they regard him with aversion as not human even, they hate him, they say he is a wild beast, fierce and cruel: while the other they pardon much rather than him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:218
verses.text: For we do not so much hate those that have wounds, as those that compel one to uncover and show them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:219
verses.text: Thus that man has not only disgraced the other, but himself as well and his hearers, and the common nature of men: he has wounded the hearer, done no good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:220
verses.text: For this reason Paul says: "If there be any word that is good for edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:221
verses.text: (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:222
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:223
verses.text: ) Let us get a tongue speaking only good things, that we may be lovely and amiable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:224
verses.text: But indeed, everything is come to that pitch of wickedness, that many boast of the very things, for which they should hide their faces.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:225
verses.text: For the threats of the many are of this kind: "thou canst not bear my tongue," say they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:226
verses.text: Words, these, worthy only of a woman, of an abandoned drunken old hag, one of those that are dragged (to punishment) in the forum, a procuress.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:227
verses.text: Nothing more shameful than these words, nothing more unmanly, more womanlike, than to have your strength in the tongue, and to think great things of yourself because you can rail, just like the fellows in processions, like the buffoons, parasites, and flatterers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:228
verses.text: Swine they are rather than men, who pride themselves upon this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:229
verses.text: Whereas you should (sooner) have buried yourself, and if another gave you this character, should recoil from the charge as odious and unmanly, instead of that you have made yourself the herald of (your own) disgrace (ὓβρεων).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:230
verses.text: But you will not be able to hurt him you speak ill of.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 79:231
verses.text: Wherefore I beseech you, considering how the wickedness is come to such a height, that many boast of it, let us return to our senses, let us recover those who are thus mad, let us take away these councils out of the city, let us make our tongue gracious, let us rid it of all evil speaking, that being clean from sins, we may be able to draw down upon us the good-will from above, and to have mercy vouchsafed unto us from God, through the grace and compassion of His only-begotten Son, with Whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:1
verses.text: Homily XXXII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:2
verses.text: Acts XV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:3
verses.text: "And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:4
verses.text: {{small-caps|Mark how at every step of the right progress in respect of the Gentiles, the beginning is brought in as matter of necessity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:5
verses.text: Before this (Peter) being found fault with, justified himself, and said all that he said in the tone of apology, which was what made his words acceptable: then, the Jews having turned away, upon this (Paul) came to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:6
verses.text: Here again, seeing another extravagance coming in, upon this (the apostle) enacts the law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:7
verses.text: For as it is likely that they, as being taught of God, discoursed to all indifferently, this moved to jealousy them of the Jews (who had believed).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:8
verses.text: And they did not merely speak of circumcision, but they said, Ye cannot even be saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:9
verses.text: Whereas the very opposite to this was the case, that receiving circumcision they could not be saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:10
verses.text: Do you mark how closely the trials succeed each other, from within, from without? It is well ordered too, that this happens when Paul is present, that he may answer them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:11
verses.text: "When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:12
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:13
verses.text: ) And Paul does not say, What? Have I not a right to be believed after so many signs? but he complied for their sakes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:14
verses.text: "And being brought on their way by the Church, they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:16
verses.text: ) And observe, the consequence is that all the Samaritans also, learn what has come to the Gentiles: and they rejoiced.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:17
verses.text: "And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the Church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:19
verses.text: ) See what a providence is here! "But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:20
verses.text: And the apostles and elders came together to consider of this matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:21
verses.text: And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that of old days God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the Gospel, and believe".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:23
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:24
verses.text: ) Observe Peter from the first standing aloof (κεχωρισμένον) from the affair, and even to this time judaizing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:25
verses.text: And yet (says he) "ye know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:26
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:27
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:28
verses.text: ; xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:29
verses.text: ) Perhaps those were present who of old found fault with him in the matter of Cornelius, and went in with him (on that occasion): for this reason he brings them forward as witnesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:30
verses.text: "From old days," he says, "did choose among you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:31
verses.text: What means, "Among you?" Either, in Palestine, or, you being present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:32
verses.text: "By my mouth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:33
verses.text: Observe how he shows that it was God speaking by him, and no human utterance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:34
verses.text: "And God, that knoweth the hearts, gave testimony unto them:" he refers them to the spiritual testimony: "by giving them the Holy Ghost even as unto us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:36
verses.text: ) Everywhere he puts the Gentiles upon a thorough equality.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:37
verses.text: "And put no difference between us and them, having purified their hearts by faith".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:39
verses.text: ) From faith alone, he says, they obtained the same gifts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:40
verses.text: This is also meant as a lesson to those (objectors); this is able to teach even them that faith only is needed, not works nor circumcision.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:41
verses.text: For indeed they do not say all this only by way of apology for the Gentiles, but to teach (the Jewish believers) also to abandon the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:42
verses.text: However, at present this is not said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:43
verses.text: "Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:44
verses.text: ) What means, "Tempt ye God?" As if He had not power to save by faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:45
verses.text: Consequently, it proceeds from a want of faith, this bringing in the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:46
verses.text: Then he shows that they themselves were nothing benefited by it, and he turns the whole (stress of his speech) against the Law, not against them, and (so) cuts short the accusation of them: "which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:47
verses.text: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus we shall be saved, even as they".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:48
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:49
verses.text: ) How full of power these words! The same that Paul says at large in the Epistle to the Romans, the same says Peter here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:50
verses.text: "For if Abraham," says (Paul), "was justified by works, he hath whereof to glory, but not before God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:51
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:52
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:53
verses.text: ) Do you perceive that all this is more a lesson for them than apology for the Gentiles? However, if he had spoken this without a plea for speaking, he would have been suspected: an occasion having offered, he lays hold of it, and speaks out fearlessly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:54
verses.text: See on all occasions how the designs of their foes are made to work with them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:55
verses.text: If those had not stirred the question, these things would not have been spoken, nor what follows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:56
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:57
verses.text: ) (b) But let us look more closely at what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:58
verses.text: "And certain men," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:59
verses.text: In Jerusalem, then, there were not any believers from among the Gentiles: but in Antioch of course there were.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:60
verses.text: Therefore there came down certain yet laboring under this disease of the love of rule, and wishing to have those of the Gentiles attached to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:61
verses.text: And yet Paul, though he too was learned in the Law, was not thus affected.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:62
verses.text: "When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small disputation with them," etc.
