verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:63
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:64
verses.text: ) But when he returned from thence, the doctrine also became more exact.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:65
verses.text: For if they at Jerusalem enjoin no such thing, much more these (have no right to do so).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:66
verses.text: "And being brought on their way," etc, "they caused no small joy to the brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:67
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:68
verses.text: ) Do you mark, as many as are not enamoured of rule, rejoiced in their believing? It was no ambitious feeling that prompted their recitals, neither was it for display, but in justification of the preaching to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:69
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:70
verses.text: ) Thus they say nothing of what had happened in the matter of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:71
verses.text: "But there arose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:72
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:73
verses.text: ) (a) But even if they would needs bring over the Gentiles to their side, they learn that neither must the Apostles overlook it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:74
verses.text: "And the Apostles and elders," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:75
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:76
verses.text: ) "Among us," he says, "God chose:" and "from old days:" long ago, he says, not now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:77
verses.text: And this too is no small point—at a time when Jews believed, not turned away (from the Gospel).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:78
verses.text: "Among us;" an argument from the place: "of old days," from the time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:79
verses.text: And that expression, "Chose:" just as in their own case he says not, (so) willed it, but, "Chose that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the Gospel and believe".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:80
verses.text: Whence is this proved? From the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:81
verses.text: Then he shows that the testimony given them is not of grace merely, but of their virtue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:82
verses.text: "And God which knoweth the hearts bare them witness" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:83
verses.text: ); having afforded to them nothing less (than to us), for, he says, "Put no difference between us and them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:84
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:85
verses.text: ) Why then, hearts are what one must everywhere look to.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:86
verses.text: And it is very appositely said, "God that knoweth the hearts bare them witness:" as in the former instance, "Thou, Lord, that knowest the hearts of all men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:87
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:88
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:89
verses.text: ) For to show that this is the meaning, observe what he adds, "Put no difference between us and them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:90
verses.text: When he has mentioned the testimony borne to them, then he utters that great word, the same which Paul speaks, "Neither circumcision availeth anything, nor uncircumcision".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:91
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:92
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:93
verses.text: ) "That he may make the twain one in Himself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:94
verses.text: (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:95
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:96
verses.text: ) Of all these the seeds lie in Peter's discourse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:97
verses.text: And he does not say (between) them of the circumcision, but "Between us," that is the Apostles, "and them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:98
verses.text: Then, that the expression, "no difference" may not seem an outrage, After faith, he says—"Having purified their hearts by faith" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:99
verses.text: )—He thoroughly cleansed them first.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:100
verses.text: Then he shows, not that the Law was evil, but themselves weak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:101
verses.text: —"But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus we shall be saved even as they".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:102
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:103
verses.text: ) Mark how he ends with a fearful consideration.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:104
verses.text: He does not discourse to them from the Prophets, but from things present, of which themselves were witnesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:105
verses.text: Of course (the Prophets) also themselves anon add their testimony (infra v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:106
verses.text: ), and make the reason stronger by what has now come to pass.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:107
verses.text: And observe, he first permits the question to be moved in the Church, and then speaks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:108
verses.text: "And put no difference between"—he said not, them of the circumcision, but "us and them," i-e: the Gentiles: for this (gradual advance) little by little is stronger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 80:109
verses.text: "Why therefore tempt ye God?" who is become (the) God of the Gentiles: for this was tempting:.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:1
verses.text: whether He is able to save even after the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:2
verses.text: See what he does.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:3
verses.text: He shows that they are in danger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:4
verses.text: For if, what the Law could not do, faith had power to do, "we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus we shall be saved even as they" (comp.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:5
verses.text: Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:6
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:7
verses.text: ): but faith falling off, behold, themselves (are) in destruction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:8
verses.text: And he did not say, Why do ye disbelieve? which was more harsh, but, "Tempt God," and that when the fact is demonstrated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:9
verses.text: (c) Great effrontery this, of the Pharisees, that even after faith they set up the Law, and will not obey the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:10
verses.text: But see these, how mildly they speak, and not in the tone of authority: such words are amiable, and more apt to fix themselves in the mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:11
verses.text: Observe, it is nowhere a display of words, but demonstration by facts, by the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:12
verses.text: And yet, though they have such proofs, they still speak gently.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:13
verses.text: And observe they do not come accusing those at Antioch, but "declaring all things that God had done with them:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:14
verses.text: ) but thence again these men lay hold upon the occasion (to compass their own objects), "but there rose up," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:16
verses.text: ) Such were the pains they took in their love of power: and it was not with the knowledge of the Apostles that they Paul and Barnabas were blamed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:17
verses.text: But still they brought forward none of these charges: but when they have proved the matter, then (the Apostles) write in stronger terms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:18
verses.text: For gentleness is everywhere a great good: gentleness, I say, not stupid indifference; gentleness, not adulation: for between these there is a vast difference.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:19
verses.text: Nothing ruffled Paul, nothing discomposed Peter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:20
verses.text: When thou hast convincing proofs, why lose thy temper, to render these of none effect? It is impossible for one who is out of temper ever to persuade.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:21
verses.text: Yesterday also we discoursed about anger; but there is no reason why we should not to-day also; perchance a second exhortation coming directly after the first will effect somewhat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:22
verses.text: For indeed a medicine though of virtue to heal a wound, unless it be constantly renewed, mars all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:23
verses.text: And think not that our continual discoursing about the same things is a condemning of you: for if we condemned you, we should not discourse; but now, hoping that you will gain much, we speak these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:24
verses.text: Would indeed that we did speak constantly of the same things: would that there were no other subject of our discourses, than how we might overcome our passions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:25
verses.text: For is it not contrary to all reason, that while emperors, living in luxury and so great honor, have no subject of discourse either while sitting at table, or at any other time, save only how to overcome their enemies—and therefore it is that they hold their assemblies each day, and appoint generals and soldiers, and demand taxes and tributes; and that of all state affairs, the moving causes are these two, the overcoming of those who make war upon them, and the establishing of their subjects in peace—we have no mind for such themes as this, nor ever even dream of conversing upon them: but how we may buy land, or purchase slaves, and make our property greater, these are subjects we can talk about every day, and never be tired of them: while concerning things in ourselves and really our own, we neither wish to speak ourselves, nor so much as dream of tolerating advice, nor of enduring to hear others speaking about them? But answer me, what do you talk about? About dinner? Why that is a subject for cooks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:26
verses.text: Of money? Nay, that is a theme for hucksters and merchants.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:27
verses.text: Of buildings? That belongs to carpenters and builders.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:28
verses.text: Of land? That talk is for husbandmen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:29
verses.text: But for us, there is no other proper business, save this, how we may make wealth for the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:30
verses.text: Then let not the discourse be wearisome to you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:31
verses.text: Why is it that none finds fault with the physician for always discoursing of the healing art, nor with people of other crafts for talking about their peculiar arts? If indeed the mastery over our passions were really achieved, so that there were no need of putting us in mind, we might reasonably be taxed with ambition and display: or rather, not then either.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:32
verses.text: For even if it were gained, for all that, there would be need of discoursing, that one might not relapse and remain uncorrected: as in fact physicians discourse not only to the sick, but also to the whole, and they have books on this subject, on the one part how to free from disease, on the other how to preserve health.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:33
verses.text: So that even if we are well, still we must not give over, but must do all in order to the preserving of our health.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:34
verses.text: And when we are sick there is a twofold necessity for advice: first, that we may be freed from the disease; secondly, that having been freed, we may not fall into it again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:35
verses.text: Well then, we are discoursing now by the method of treating the sick, not by the rules for the treatment of the healthy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:36
verses.text: How then may one root out this evil passion? how subdue (ὑποσκελίσειε) this violent fever? Let us see whence it had its birth, and let us remove the cause.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:37
verses.text: Whence is it wont to arise? From arrogance and much haughtiness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:38
verses.text: This cause then let us remove, and the disease is removed together with it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:39
verses.text: But what is arrogance? whence does it arise? for perhaps we are likely to have to go back to a still higher origin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:40
verses.text: But whatever course the reason of the thing may point out, that let us take, that we may go to the bottom of the mischief, and pluck it up by the roots.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:41
verses.text: Whence then comes arrogance? From our not looking into our own concerns, but instead of that, busying ourselves about the nature of land, though we are not husbandmen, and the nature of gold, though we are not merchants, and concerning clothing, and everything else: while to ourselves and our own nature we never look at all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:42
verses.text: And who, you will say, is ignorant of his own nature? Many: perhaps all, save a few: and if ye will, I will show the proof of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:43
verses.text: For, tell me, what is man? If one were asked, will he be able to answer outright to the questions, In what he differs from the brutes, in what he is akin to the heavenly inhabitants, what can be made of man? For as in the case of any other material, so also in this case: man is the subject-matter, but of this can be made either an angel or a beast.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:44
verses.text: Does not this seem a strange saying? And yet ye have often heard it in the Scriptures.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:45
verses.text: For of certain human beings it was said, "he is the angel of the Lord" (Mal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:46
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:47
verses.text: ): and "from his lips," saith it, "they shall seek judgment" (Mal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:48
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:49
verses.text: ): and again, "I send My angel before Thy face:" but of some, "Serpents, generation of vipers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:50
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:51
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:52
verses.text: ) So then, it all depends upon the use.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:53
verses.text: Why do I say, an angel? the man can become God, and a child of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:54
verses.text: For we read, "I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:55
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:56
verses.text: lxxxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:57
verses.text: ) And what is greater, the power to become both God and angel and child of God is put into his own hands.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:58
verses.text: Yea, so it is, man can be the maker of an angel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:59
verses.text: Perchance this saying has startled you? Hear however Christ saying: "In the Resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like unto the angels".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:60
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:61
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:62
verses.text: ) And again, "He that is able to receive it, let him receive it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:63
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:64
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:65
verses.text: ) In a word, it is virtue which makes angels: but this is in our power: therefore we are able to make angels, though not in nature, certainly in will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:66
verses.text: For indeed if virtue be absent, it is no advantage to be an angel by nature; and the Devil is a proof of this, who was an angel once: but if virtue be present, it is no loss to be a man by nature; and John is a proof of this, who was a man, and Elias who went up into heaven, and all those who are about to depart thither.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:67
verses.text: For these indeed, though with bodies, were not prevented from dwelling in heaven: while those others, though without bodies, could not remain in heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:68
verses.text: Let no one then grieve or be vexed with his nature as if it were a hindrance to him, but with his will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:69
verses.text: He (the Devil) from being incorporeal became a lion: for lo! it saith, "Our adversary, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour" ( Pet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:70
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:71
verses.text: ): we from being corporeal, become angels.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:72
verses.text: For just as if a person, having found some precious material, should despise it, as not being an artificer, it will be a great loss to him, whether it be pearls, or a pearl shell, or any other such thing that he has seen; so we likewise, if we are ignorant of our own nature, shall despise it much: but if we know what it is, we shall exhibit much zeal, and reap the greatest profits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:73
verses.text: For from this nature is wrought a king's robe, from this a king's house, from this nature are fashioned a king's members: all are kingly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:74
verses.text: Let us not then misuse our own nature to our hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:75
verses.text: He has made us "a little lower than the angels," (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:76
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:77
verses.text: ), I mean, by reason of death: but even that little we have now recovered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:78
verses.text: There is nothing therefore to hinder us from becoming nigh to the angels, if we will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 83:79
verses.text: Let us then will it, let us will it, and having exercised ourselves thoroughly, let us return honor to the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:1
verses.text: Homily XXXIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:2
verses.text: Acts XV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:3
verses.text: ,  "And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying, Men and brethren, hearken unto me: Symeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:4
verses.text: And to this agree the words of the prophets".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:5
verses.text: This (James) was bishop, as they say, and therefore he speaks last, and herein is fulfilled that saying, "In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:6
verses.text: (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:7
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:8
verses.text: ; Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:9
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:10
verses.text: ) But observe the discretion shown by him also, in making his argument good from the prophets, both new and old.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:11
verses.text: For he had no acts of his own to declare, as Peter had and Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:12
verses.text: And indeed it is wisely ordered that this (the active) part is assigned to those, as not intended to be locally fixed in Jerusalem, whereas (James) here, who performs the part of teacher, is no way responsible for what has been done, while however he is not divided from them in opinion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:13
verses.text: (b) "Men and brethren," he says, "hearken unto me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:14
verses.text: Great is the moderation of the man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:15
verses.text: His also is a more complete oration, as indeed it puts the completion to the matter under discussion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:16
verses.text: (a) "Symeon," he says, "declared:" (namely,) in Luke, in that he prophesied, "Which Thou hast prepared before the face of all nations, a light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of Thy people Israel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:17
verses.text: (c) "How God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for His Name".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:18
verses.text: (Luke ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:19
verses.text: ) Then, since that (witness), though from the time indeed he was manifest, yet had not authority by reason of his not being ancient, therefore he produces ancient prophecy also, saying, "And to this agree the words of the Prophets, as it is written: After this I wilt return, and will build again the tabernacle of David which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:20
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:21
verses.text: ) What? was Jerusalem raised up? Was it not rather thrown down? What sort of raising up does he call that which took place after the return from Babylon? "That the residue of men," he says, "may seek the Lord, even all the Gentiles upon whom My Name is called".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:23
verses.text: ) Then, what makes his word authoritative—"Saith the Lord, which doeth all these things:" and, for that this is no new thing, but all was planned from the beginning, "Known unto God are all His works from everlasting".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:24
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:25
verses.text: ) And then again his authority (καὶ τὸ ἀξίωμα πάλιν) (as Bishop): "Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God: but that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollution of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:26
verses.text: For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:29
verses.text: ) Since then they had heard of the Law, with good reason he enjoins these things from the Law, that he may not seem to make it of no authority.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:30
verses.text: And (yet) observe how he does not let them be told these things from the Law, but from himself, saying, It is not that I heard these things from the Law, but how? "We have judged".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:31
verses.text: Then the decree is made in common.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:32
verses.text: "Then pleased it the Apostles and elders, together with the whole Church, to choose men of their own company"—do you observe they do not merely enact these matters, and nothing more?—"and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren: and they wrote letters by them after this manner".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:34
verses.text: ) And observe, the more to authenticate the decree, they send men of their own, that there may be no room for regarding Paul and his company with suspicion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:35
verses.text: "The Apostles and elders and brethren send greeting unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:37
verses.text: ) And mark with what forbearance of all harsh vituperation of those (brethren) they indite their epistle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:38
verses.text: "Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the Law: to whom we gave no such commandment".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:40
verses.text: ) Sufficient was this charge against the temerity of those men, and worthy of the Apostles' moderation, that they said nothing beyond this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:41
verses.text: Then to show that they do not act despotically, that all are agreed in this, that with deliberation they write this—"It seemed good to us, being assembled with one accord, to send men of ours whom we have chosen" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:42
verses.text: )—then, that it may not look like disparagement of Paul and Barnabas, that those men are sent, observe the encomium passed upon them—"together with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:43
verses.text: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas; who shall also tell you the same things by mouth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:44
verses.text: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us"—it is not man's doing, it says—"to lay upon you no greater burden"—again it calls the Law a burden: then apologizing even for these injunctions—"save these necessary things" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:45
verses.text: –): "That ye abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication from which if ye keep yourselves, ye shall do well.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:47
verses.text: ) For these things the New Testament did not enjoin: we nowhere find that Christ discoursed about these matters; but these things they take from the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:48
verses.text: "From things strangled," it says, "and from blood".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:49
verses.text: Here it prohibits murder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:50
verses.text: (Comp.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:51
verses.text: Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:52
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:53
verses.text: ) "So when they were dismissed, they came to Antioch: and when they had gathered the multitude together, they delivered the epistle: which when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:55
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:56
verses.text: ) Then those (brethren) also exhorted them: and having established them, for towards Paul they were contentiously disposed, so departed from them in peace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:57
verses.text: "And Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:58
verses.text: And after they had tarried there a space, they were let go in peace from the brethren unto the Apostles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:59
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:60
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:61
verses.text: ) No more factions and fightings, but thenceforth Paul taught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:62
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:63
verses.text: ) "Then all the multitude kept silence," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:64
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:65
verses.text: ) There was no arrogance in the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:66
verses.text: After Peter Paul speaks, and none silences him: James waits patiently, not starts up (for the next word).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:67
verses.text: Great the orderliness (of the proceedings).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:68
verses.text: No word speaks John here, no word the other Apostles, but held their peace, for James was invested with the chief rule, and think it no hardship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:69
verses.text: So clean was their soul from love of glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:70
verses.text: "And after that they had held their peace, James answered," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:71
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:72
verses.text: ) (b) Peter indeed spoke more strongly, but James here more mildly: for thus it behooves one in high authority, to leave what is unpleasant for others to say, while he himself appears in the milder part.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:73
verses.text: (a) But what means it, "How God first (πρὥτον) did visit?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:74
verses.text: ) (It means) from the beginning (ἐξ ἀρχἥς).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:75
verses.text: (c) Moreover he well says, "Symeon expounded" (ἐξηγήσατο) (or, interpreted), implying that he too spake the mind of others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:76
verses.text: "And to this agree," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:77
verses.text: Observe how he shows that this is a doctrine of old time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:78
verses.text: "To take out of the Gentiles," he says, "a people for His Name".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:79
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:80
verses.text: ) Not simply, Chose, but, "for His Name," that is for His glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:81
verses.text: His Name is not shamed by the taking (προλήψει) the Gentiles first, but it is even a greater glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:82
verses.text: —Here some even great thing is hinted at: that these are chosen before all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:83
verses.text: "After this I will return, and rebuild the tabernacle of David which is fallen down".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:84
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:85
verses.text: ) But if one would look into the matter closely, the kingdom of David does in fact now stand, his Offspring reigning everywhere.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:86
verses.text: For what is the good of the buildings and the city, with none obeying there? And what is the harm arising from the destruction of the city, when all are willing to give their very souls? There is that come which is more illustrious than David: in all parts of the world is he now sung.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:87
verses.text: This has come to pass: if so, then must this also come to pass, "And I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up:" to what end? "that the residue of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom My Name is called".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:88
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:89
verses.text: ) If then it was to this end that the city rose again (namely) because of Him (that was to come) of them, it shows that of the building of the city the cause is, the calling of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:90
verses.text: Who are "the residue?" those who are then left.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:91
verses.text: "And all the Gentiles, upon whom My Name is called:" but observe, how he keeps the due order, and brings them in second.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:92
verses.text: "Saith the Lord, which doeth these things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:93
verses.text: Not "saith" (only), but "doeth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:94
verses.text: Why then, it was God's work.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:95
verses.text: —"But the question is other than this (namely), what Peter spoke more plainly, whether they must be circumcised.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:96
verses.text: Then why dost thou harangue about these matters?" For what the objectors asserted, was not that they must not be received upon believing, but that it must be with the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:97
verses.text: And upon this Peter well pleaded: but then, as this very thing above all others troubled the hearers, therefore he sets this to rights again (θεραπεύει).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:98
verses.text: And observe, that which was needful to be enacted as a rule, that it is not necessary to keep the Law, this Peter introduced: but the milder part, the truth which was received of old, this James saith, and dwells upon that concerning which nothing is written, in order that having soothed their minds by that which is acknowledged, he may opportunely introduce this likewise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:99
verses.text: "Wherefore," saith he, "my sentence is, not to trouble them which from among the Gentiles do turn unto God" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:100
verses.text: ), that is, not to subvert: for, if God called them, and these observances subvert, we fight against God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:101
verses.text: And again, "them which from the Gentiles," he saith, "do turn".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:102
verses.text: And he says well, with authority, the "my sentence is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:103
verses.text: But that we write unto them that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication"—(b) and yet they often insisted upon these points in discoursing to them—but, that he may seem also to honor the Law (he mentions), these also, speaking (however) not as from Moses but from the Apostles, and to make the commandments many, he has divided the one into two (saying), "and from things strangled, and from blood".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:104
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:105
verses.text: ) For these, although relating to the body, were necessary to be observed, because (these things) caused great evils, "For Moses hath of old times in every city," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:106
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:107
verses.text: ) This above all quieted them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:108
verses.text: (ἀνέπαυσεν) (a) For this cause I affirm that it is good (so "to write to them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:109
verses.text: ) Then why do we not write the same injunctions to Jews also? Moses discourses unto them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:110
verses.text: See what condescension (to their weakness)! Where it did no harm, he set him up as teacher, and indulged them with a gratification which hindered nothing, by permitting Jews to hear him in regard of these matters, even while leading away from him them of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:111
verses.text: See what wisdom! He seems to honor him, and to set him up as the authority for his own people, and by this very thing he leads away the Gentiles from him! "Being read in the synagogues every sabbath day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 84:112
verses.text: Then why do they not learn (what is to be learnt) out of him, for instance.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:1
verses.text: ? Through the perversity of these men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:2
verses.text: He shows that even these (the Jews) need observe no more (than these necessary things).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:3
verses.text: And if we do not write to them, it is not that they are bound to observe anything more, but only that they have one to tell them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:4
verses.text: And he does not say, Not to offend, nor to turn them back, which is what Paul said to the Galatians, but, "not to trouble them:" he shows that the point (κατόρθωμα) if carried is nothing but a mere troubling.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:5
verses.text: Thus he made an end of the whole matter; and while he seems to preserve the Law by adopting these rules from it, he unbinds it by taking only these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:6
verses.text: (c) There was a design of Providence in the disputation also, that after the disputation the doctrine might be more firm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:7
verses.text: "Then pleased it the Apostles to send chosen men of their own company," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:8
verses.text: , no ordinary persons, but the "leading men; having written" (letters) "by them after this manner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:9
verses.text: To those in Antioch," it says, "and Syria and Cilicia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:10
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:11
verses.text: , ) where the disease had its birth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:12
verses.text: Observe how they say nothing harsher (φορτικώτερον) against those men, but look to one thing only, namely, to undo (the mischief) which has been done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:13
verses.text: For this would make even the movers of the faction there to confess (that they were wrong).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:14
verses.text: They do not say, The seducers, the pestilent fellows, or suchlike: though where need is, Paul does this, as when he says, "O full of all guile" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:15
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:16
verses.text: ): but here, the point being carried, there was no need.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:17
verses.text: And observe, they do not put it, That certain from us ordered you to keep the Law, but, "Troubled you with words, subverting your souls,"—nothing could be more proper (κυριώτερον) than that word: none (of the other speakers) has so spoken of the things done by those men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:18
verses.text: "The souls," he says, already strongly established, these persons are ἀνασχευάζοντες as in speaking of a building, "taking them down again:" displacing them (μετατιθέντες) from the foundation).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:19
verses.text: "To whom," he says, "we gave no such commandment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:20
verses.text: It seemed good therefore to us being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you together with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, men that have hazarded their lives for the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:23
verses.text: ) If "beloved," they will not despise them, if they "have hazarded their lives," they have themselves a right to be believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:24
verses.text: "We have sent," it saith, "Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same things by word of mouth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:26
verses.text: ) For it was necessary that there should be not merely the Epistle there by itself, lest they should say that Paul and Barnabas had suppressed (the real purport), that they said one thing instead of another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:27
verses.text: The encomium passed upon Paul stopped their mouths.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:28
verses.text: For this is the reason why neither Paul comes alone nor Barnabas (with him), but others also from the Church; that he may not be suspected, seeing it was he that advocated that doctrine: nor yet those from Jerusalem alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:29
verses.text: It shows that they have a right to be believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:30
verses.text: "For it seemed good," say they, "to the Holy Ghost and to us" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:31
verses.text: ): not making themselves equal (to Him)—they are not so mad.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:32
verses.text: But why does it put this (so)? Why did they add, "And to us," and yet it had sufficed to say, "To the Holy Ghost?" The one, "To the Holy Ghost," that they may not deem it to be of man; the other, "To us," that they may be taught that they also themselves admit (the Gentiles), although themselves being in circumcision.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:33
verses.text: They have to speak to men who are still weak and afraid of them: this is the reason why this also is added.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:34
verses.text: And it shows that it is not by way of condescension that they speak, neither because they spared them, nor as considering them weak, but the contrary; for great was the reverence of the teachers also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:35
verses.text: "To lay upon you no greater burden"—they are ever calling it a burden—and again, "save these necessary things:" for that was a superfluous burden.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:36
verses.text: See here a brief Epistle, with nothing more in it (than was needed), neither arts of persuasion (κατασκευὰς) nor reasonings, but simply a command: for it was the Spirit's legislating.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:37
verses.text: "So when they were dismissed they came to Antioch, and having gathered the multitude together, they delivered to them the epistle".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:39
verses.text: ) After the epistle, then (Judas and Silas) also themselves exhort them by word (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:40
verses.text: ): for this also was needful, that (Paul and Barnabas) might be quit of all suspicion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:41
verses.text: "Being prophets also themselves," it says, exhorted the brethren "with many words".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:42
verses.text: It shows here the right that Paul and Barnabas have to be believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:43
verses.text: For Paul also might have done this, but it behooved to be done by these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:44
verses.text: "And after they had tarried there a space, they were let go in peace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:46
verses.text: )  No more faction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:47
verses.text: On this occasion, I suppose, it was that they received the right hand, as he says himself, "They gave to me and Barnabas right hands of fellowship".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:48
verses.text: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:49
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:50
verses.text: ) There he says, "They added nothing to me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:51
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:52
verses.text: ) For they confirmed his view: they praised and admired it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:53
verses.text: —It shows that even from human reasonings it is possible to see this, not to say from the Holy Ghost only, that they sinned a sin not easy to be corrected.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:54
verses.text: For such things need not the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:55
verses.text: —It shows that the rest are not necessary, but superfluous, seeing these things are necessary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:56
verses.text: "From which if ye keep yourselves," it saith, "ye shall do well".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:57
verses.text: It shows that nothing is lacking to them, but this is sufficient.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:58
verses.text: For it might have been done also without letters, but that there may be a law in writing (they send this Epistle): again, that they may obey the law (the Apostles), also told those men (the same things), and they did this, "and confirmed them, and having tarried a space were let go in peace".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:59
verses.text: Let us not then be offended on account of the heretics.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:60
verses.text: For look, here at the very outset of the preaching, how many offences there were: I speak not of those which arose from them that were without; for these were nothing: but of the offences which were within.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:61
verses.text: For instance, first Ananias, then the "murmuring," then Simon the sorcerer; afterwards they that accused Peter on account of Cornelius, next the famine, lastly this very thing, the chief of the evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:62
verses.text: For indeed it is impossible when any good thing has taken place, that some evil should not also subsist along with it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:63
verses.text: Let us not then be disturbed, if certain are offended, but let us thank God even for this, because it makes us more approved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:64
verses.text: For not tribulations only, but even temptations also render us more illustrious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:65
verses.text: A man is no such great lover of the truth, only for holding to it when there is none to lead him astray from it: to hold fast to the truth when many are drawing him away, this makes the proved man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:66
verses.text: What then? Is this why offences come? I am not speaking as if God were the author of them: God forbid! but I mean, that even out of their wickedness He works good to us: it was never His wish that they should arise: "Grant to them," He saith, "that they may be one" (John xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:67
verses.text: ): but since offences do come, they are no hurt, to these, but even a benefit: just as the persecutors unwillingly benefit the Martyrs by dragging them to martyrdom, and yet they are not driven to this by God; just so is it here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:68
verses.text: Let us not look (only at this), that men are offended: this very thing is itself a proof of the excellence of the doctrine—that many stimulate and counterfeit it: for it would not be so, if it were not good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:69
verses.text: And this I will now show, and make on all hands plain to you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:70
verses.text: Of perfumes, the fragrant spices are they which people adulterate and counterfeit; as, for instance, the amomum leaf.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:71
verses.text: For because these are rare and of necessary use, therefore there come to be spurious imitations likewise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:72
verses.text: Nobody would care to counterfeit any common article.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:73
verses.text: The pure life gets many a false pretender to it: no man would care to counterfeit the man of vicious life; no, but the man of monastic life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:74
verses.text: —What then shall we say to the heathen? There comes a heathen and says, "I wish to become a Christian, but I know not whom to join: there is much fighting and faction among you, much confusion: which doctrine am I to choose?" How shall we answer him? "Each of you" (says he) "asserts, 'I speak the truth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:75
verses.text: '" (b) No doubt: this is in our favor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:76
verses.text: For if we told you to be persuaded by arguments, you might well be perplexed: but if we bid you believe the Scriptures, and these are simple and true, the decision is easy for you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:77
verses.text: If any agree with the Scriptures, he is the Christian; if any fight against them, he is far from this rule.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:78
verses.text: (a) "But which am I to believe, knowing as I do nothing at all of the Scriptures? The others also allege the same thing for themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:79
verses.text: What then (c)if the other come, and say that the Scripture has this, and you that it has something different, and ye interpret the Scriptures diversely, dragging their sense (each his own way)?" And you then, I ask, have you no understanding, no judgment? "And how should I be able (to decide)," says he, "I who do not even know how to judge of your doctrines? I wish to become a learner, and you are making me forthwith a teacher".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:80
verses.text: If he say this, what, say you, are we to answer him? How shall we persuade him? Let us ask whether all this be not mere pretence and subterfuge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:81
verses.text: Let us ask whether he has decided (κατέγνωκε) against the heathen (that they are wrong).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:82
verses.text: The fact he will assuredly affirm, for of course, if he had not so decided, he would not have come to (enquire about) our matters: let us ask the grounds on which he has decided, for to be sure he has not settled the matter out of hand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:83
verses.text: Clearly he will say, "Because (their gods) are creatures, and are not the uncreated God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:84
verses.text: Good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:85
verses.text: If then he find this in the other parties (αἰρέσεις), but among us the contrary, what argument need we? We all confess that Christ is God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:86
verses.text: But let us see who fight (against this truth), and who not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:87
verses.text: Now we, affirming Him to be God speak of Him things worthy of God, that He hath power, that He is not a slave, that He is free, that He doeth of Himself: whereas the other says the reverse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 86:88
verses.text: Again I ask: if you would learn (to be) a physician,.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:1
verses.text: ? And yet among them are many (different) doctrines.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:2
verses.text: For if you accept without more ado just what you are told, this is not acting like a man: but if you have judgment and sense, you shall assuredly know what is good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:3
verses.text: We affirm the Son to be God, we verify (ἐπαληθεύομεν) what we affirm: but they affirm indeed, but (in fact) confess not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:4
verses.text: —But to mention (something) even plainer: those have certain persons from whom they are called, openly showing the name of the heresiarch himself, and each heresy in like manner: with us, no man has given us a name, but the faith itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:5
verses.text: However, this (talk of yours) is mere pretence and subterfuge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:6
verses.text: For answer me: how is it that if you would buy a cloak, though ignorant of the art of weaving, you do not speak such words as these—"I do not know how to buy; they cheat me"—but do all you can to learn, and so whatever else it be that you would buy: but here you speak these words? For at this rate, you will accept nothing at all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:7
verses.text: For let there be one that has no (religious) doctrine whatever: if he should say what you say about the Christians—"There is such a multitude of men, and they have different doctrines; this a heathen, that a Jew, the other a Christian: no need to accept any doctrine whatever, for they are at variance one with another; but I am a learner, and do not wish to be a judge"—but if you have yielded (so far as) to pronounce against (καταγινώσκειν) one doctrine, this pretext no longer has place for you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:8
verses.text: For just as you were able to reject the spurious, so here also, having come, you shall be able to prove what is profitable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:9
verses.text: For he that has not pronounced against any doctrine at all, may easily say this: but he that has pronounced against any, though he have chosen none, by going on in the same way, will be able to see what he ought to do.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:10
verses.text: Then let us not make pretexts and excuses, and all will be easy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:11
verses.text: For, to show you that all this is mere excuse, answer me this: Do you know what you ought to do, and what to leave undone? Then why do you not what you ought? Do that, and by right reason seek of God, and He will assuredly reveal it to thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:12
verses.text: "God," it saith, "is no respecter of persons, but in every nation he that feareth Him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:13
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:14
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:16
verses.text: ) It cannot be that he who hears without prejudice should not be persuaded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:17
verses.text: For just as, if there were a rule, by which everything behooved to be put straight, it would not need much consideration, but it would be easy to detect the person who measures falsely (τὸν παραμετροὕντα λαβἕιν), so is it here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:18
verses.text: "Then how is it they do not see it at a glance?" Many things are the cause of this: both preconceived opinion, and human causes (αἰτίαι).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:19
verses.text: The others, say you, say the same thing about us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:20
verses.text: How? For are we separated from the Church? have we our heresiarchs? Are we called after men—as one of them has Marcion, another Manichaeus, a third Arius, for the author and leader (of his sect)? Whereas if we likewise do receive an appellation from any man, we do not take them that have been the authors of some heresy, but men that presided over us, and governed the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:21
verses.text: We have no "masters upon the earth"—God forbid—we have "One Master that is in heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:22
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:23
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:24
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:25
verses.text: ) "And those also," says he, "say the same".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:26
verses.text: But there stands the name set over them, accusing them, and stopping their mouths.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:27
verses.text: —How is it, there have been many heathen, and none of them asked these questions: and among the philosophers there were these (differences), and yet none of those holding the right party (αἵρεσιν) was hindered (thereby)?—Why did not (those believers) say, when (the others) raised these questions, "Both these and those are Jews: which must we believe?" But they believed as they ought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 89:28
verses.text: Then let us also obey the laws of God, and do all things according to His good pleasure, that having virtuously passed this life present, we may be enabled to attain unto the good things promised to them that love Him, by the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together, be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:1
verses.text: Homily XXXIV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:2
verses.text: Acts XV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:3
verses.text: "Paul also and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:4
verses.text: Observe again their humility, how they let others also take part in the preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:5
verses.text: "And some days after Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:6
verses.text: And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:7
verses.text: But Paul thought not good (ἡξίου see note , p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:8
verses.text: ) to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:9
verses.text: And the contention (or exasperation) was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:10
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:12
verses.text: ) And already indeed Luke has described to us the character of the Apostles, that the one was more tender and indulgent, but this one more strict and austere.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:13
verses.text: For the gifts are diverse—(the gifts, I say), for that this is a gift is manifest—but the one befitting one, the other another set of characters, and if they change places, harm results instead of good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:14
verses.text: (b) In the Prophets too we find this: diverse minds, diverse characters: for instance, Elias austere, Moses meek.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:15
verses.text: So here Paul is more vehement.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:16
verses.text: And observe for all this, how gentle he is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:17
verses.text: "Thought not good," it says, "to take him with them that had departed from them from Pamphylia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:18
verses.text: (a) And there seems indeed to be exasperation (παροξυσμός), but in fact the whole matter is a plan of the Divine Providence, that each should receive his proper place: and it behooved that they should not be upon a par, but the one should lead, and the other be led.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:19
verses.text: "And so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus; and Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:20
verses.text: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the Churches".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:23
verses.text: ) And this also is a work of Providence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:24
verses.text: For the Cyprians had exhibited nothing of the like sort as they at Antioch and the rest: and those needed the softer character, but these needed such a character as Paul's.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 90:25
verses.text: "Which then," say you, "did well? he that took, or he that left?".

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:1
verses.text: (c) For just as a general would not choose to have a low person always to his baggage-bearer, so neither did the Apostle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:2
verses.text: This corrected the other's, and instructed (Mark) himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:3
verses.text: "Then did Barnabas ill?" say you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:4
verses.text: "And how is it not amiss (ἄτοπον), that upon so small a matter there should arise so great an evil?" In the first place then, no evil did come of it, if, sufficing each for whole nations, they were divided the one from the other, but a great good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:5
verses.text: And besides, they would not readily have chosen to leave each other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:6
verses.text: But admire, I pray you, the writer, how he does not conceal this either.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:7
verses.text: "But at any rate," say you, "if they must needs part, let it be without exasperation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:8
verses.text: Nay, but if nothing more, observe this, that in this too is shown what was of man (in the preaching of the Gospel).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:9
verses.text: For if the like behooved to be shown (even) in what Christ did, much more here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:10
verses.text: And besides, the contention cannot be said to be evil, when each disputes for such objects (as here) and with just reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:11
verses.text: I grant you, if the exasperation were in seeking his own, and contending for his own honor, this might well be (reproved): but if wishing, both the one and the other, to instruct and teach, the one took this way and the other that, what is there to find fault with? For in many things they acted upon their human judgment; for they were not stocks or stones.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:12
verses.text: And observe how Paul impeaches (Mark), and gives the reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:13
verses.text: For of his exceeding humility he reverenced Barnabas, as having been partner with him in so great works, and being with him: but still he did not so reverence him, as to overlook (what was necessary).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:14
verses.text: Now which of them advised best, it is not for us to pronounce: but thus far (we may affirm), that it was a great arrangement of Providence, if these were to be vouchsafed a second visitation, but those were not to be visited even once.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:15
verses.text: (a) "Teaching and preaching the word of the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:16
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:17
verses.text: ) They did not simply tarry in Antioch, but taught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:18
verses.text: What did they "teach," and what "preach" (evangelize)? They both (taught) those that were already believers, and (evangelized) those that were not yet such.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:19
verses.text: "And some days after," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:20
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:21
verses.text: ) For because there were offences without number, their presence was needed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:22
verses.text: (d) "How they do," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:23
verses.text: And this he did not know: naturally.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:24
verses.text: See him ever alert, solicitous, not bearing to sit idle, though he underwent dangers without end.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:25
verses.text: Do you mark, it was not of cowardice that he came to Antioch? He acts just as a physician does in the case of the sick.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:26
verses.text: And the need of visiting them he showed by saying, "In which we preached the word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:27
verses.text: And Barnabas determined," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:30
verses.text: ) (So) Barnabas "departed, and went not with (him)".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:31
verses.text: (b) The point to be considered, is not that they differed in their opinions, but that they accommodated themselves the one to the other (seeing), that thus it was a greater good their being parted: and the matter took a pretext from this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:32
verses.text: What then? did they withdraw in enmity? God forbid! In fact you see after this Barnabas receiving many encomiums from Paul in the Epistles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:33
verses.text: There was "sharp contention," it says, not enmity nor quarrelling.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:34
verses.text: The contention availed so far as to part them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:35
verses.text: "And Barnabas took Mark," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:36
verses.text: And with reason: for what each supposed to be profitable, he did not forego thereafter, because of the fellowship with the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:37
verses.text: Nay, it seems to me that the parting took place advisedly (κατὰ σύνεσιν), and that they said one to another, "As I wish not, and thou wishest, therefore that we may not fight, let us distribute the places".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:38
verses.text: So that in fact they did this, altogether yielding each to the other: for Barnabas wished Paul's plan to stand, therefore withdrew; on the other hand, Paul wished the other's plan to stand, therefore he withdrew.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:39
verses.text: Would to God we too made such separations, as to go forth for preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:40
verses.text: A wonderful man this is; and exceedingly great! To Mark this contest was exceedingly beneficial.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:41
verses.text: For the awe inspired by Paul converted him, while the kindness of Barnabas caused that he was not left behind: so that they contend indeed, but the gain comes to one and the same end.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:42
verses.text: For indeed, seeing Paul choosing to leave him, he would be exceedingly awed, and would condemn himself, and seeing Barnabas so taking his part, he would love him exceedingly: and so the disciple was corrected by the contention of the teachers: so far was he from being offended thereby.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 93:43
verses.text: For if indeed they did this with a view to their own honor, he might well be offended: but if for his salvation, and they contend for one and the same object, to show that he who honored him.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:1
verses.text: had well determined, what is there amiss (ἄτοπον) in it?  (e) "But Paul," it says, "departed, having chosen Silas, and being commended to the grace of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:2
verses.text: What is this? They prayed it says: they besought God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:3
verses.text: See on all occasions how the prayer of the brethren can do great things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:4
verses.text: And now he journeyed by land, wishing even by his journeying to benefit those who saw (τοὺς ὁρὥντας) him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:5
verses.text: For when indeed they were in haste they sailed, but now not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:6
verses.text: (c) "And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the Churches.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:7
verses.text: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:8
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:9
verses.text: ) Mark the wisdom of Paul: he does not go to other cities before he has visited them which had received the Word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:10
verses.text: For it is folly to run at random.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:11
verses.text: This let us also do: let us teach the first in the first place, that these may not become an hindrance to them that are to come after.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:12
verses.text: "And, behold a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek: which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:13
verses.text: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters; for they knew all that his father was a Greek".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:14
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:15
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:16
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:17
verses.text: ) It is indeed amazing, the wisdom of Paul! He that has had so many battles about circumcision, he that moved all things to this end, and did not give over until he had carried his point, now that the decree is made sure, circumcises the disciple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:18
verses.text: He not only does not forbid others, but himself does this thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:19
verses.text: (b) "Him," it says, "he would have to go forth with him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:20
verses.text: And the wonder is this, that he even took him unto him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:21
verses.text: "Because of the Jews," it says, "which were in those parts:" for they would not endure to hear the word from one uncircumcised.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:22
verses.text: (a) Nothing could be wiser.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:23
