verses.text: So that in all things he looked to what was profitable: he did nothing upon his own preference (προλήψει).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:24
verses.text: (c) And what (then)? Mark the success: he circumcised, that he might take away circumcision: for he preached the decrees of the Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:25
verses.text: "And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep, that were ordained of the Apostles and elders which were at Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:26
verses.text: And so were the Churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:29
verses.text: ) Dost thou mark fighting, and by fighting, edification? Not warred upon by others, but themselves doing contrary things, so they edified the Church! They introduced a decree not to circumcise, and he circumcises! "And so were the Churches," it says, "established in the faith," and in multitude: "increased," it says, "in number daily".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:30
verses.text: Then he does not continue to tarry with these, as having come to visit them: but how? he goes further.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:31
verses.text: "Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:32
verses.text: ) having left Phrygia and Galatia, they hastened into the interior.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:33
verses.text: For, it says, "After they were come to Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:35
verses.text: ) Wherefore they were forbidden, he does not say, but that they were "forbidden," he does say, teaching us to obey and not ask questions, and showing that they did many things as men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:36
verses.text: "And the Spirit," it says, "suffered them not: but having passed by Mysia they came down to Troas".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:38
verses.text: ) "And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:40
verses.text: ) Why a vision, and not the Holy Ghost? because He forbade the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:41
verses.text: He would even in this way draw them over: since to the saints also He appeared in a dream, and in the beginning (Paul) himself saw a vision, "a man coming in and laying his hands upon him".

verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:43

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:44
verses.text: ) In this manner also Christ appears to him, saying, "Thou must stand before Caesar".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:45
verses.text: Then for this reason also He draws him thither, that the preaching may be extended.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:46
verses.text: This is why he was forbidden to tarry long in the other cities, Christ urging him on.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:47
verses.text: For these were to enjoy the benefit of John for a long time, and perhaps did not extremely need him (Paul), but thither he behooved to go.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:48
verses.text: And now he crosses over and goes forth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:49
verses.text: "And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavored to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the Gospel unto them".

Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:51
verses.text: ) Then the writer mentions also the places, as relating a history, and showing where he made a stay (namely), in the greater cities, but passed by the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:52
verses.text: "Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis; and from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony".

Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:55

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:76
verses.text: Thus also here: the one is wroth, the other not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:77
verses.text: The same happens also in matters where we are concerned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:78
verses.text: And the sharp contention with good reason, that Mark may receive a lesson, and the affair may not seem mere stage-playing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:79
verses.text: For it is not to be thought that he who bids, "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath," (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:80
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:81
verses.text: ) would have been wroth because of such a matter as this: nor that he who on all occasions gave way would not have given way here, he who so greatly loved Paul that before this he sought him in Tarsus, and brought him to the Apostles, and undertook the alms in common with him, and in common the business relating to the decree.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:82
verses.text: But they take themselves so as to instruct and make perfect by their separation them that need the teaching which was to come from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:83
verses.text: And he rebukes others indeed, but bids do good to all men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:84
verses.text: As in fact he does elsewhere, saying, "But ye, be not weary in well-doing".

verses.text: ( Thess.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:86
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:87
verses.text: ) This we also do in our common practice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:88
verses.text: Here it seems to me that others also were alike displeased with Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:89
verses.text: And thereupon taking them also apart, he does all, and exhorts and admonishes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:90
verses.text: Much can concord do, much can charity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:91
verses.text: Though it be for a great matter thou askest; though thou be unworthy, thou shalt be heard for thy purpose of heart: fear not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:92
verses.text: "He went," it says, "through" the cities "And, behold, there was a disciple, by name Timothy, who had a good report of the brethren which were in Lystra and Iconium".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:93
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:94
verses.text: ; xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:95
verses.text: ) Great was the grace of Timothy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:96
verses.text: When Barnabas departed (ἀπέστη), he finds another, equivalent to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:97
verses.text: Of him he saith, "Remembering thy tears and thy unfeigned faith, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and in thy mother Eunice".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:98
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:99
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:100
verses.text: ) His father continued to be a Gentile, and therefore it was that (Timothy) was not circumcised.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:101
verses.text: (a) Observe the Law already broken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:102
verses.text: Or if not so, I suppose he was born after the preaching of the Gospel but this is perhaps not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:103
verses.text: (c) He was about to make him a bishop, and it was not meet that he should be uncircumcised.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:104
verses.text: (e) And this was not a small matter, seeing it offended after so long a time: (b) "for from a child," he says, "thou hast known the Holy Scriptures".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:105
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:106
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:107
verses.text: ) (d) "And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:108
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:109
verses.text: ) For until then, there was no need for the Gentiles to keep any such.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:110
verses.text: The beginning of the abrogation was the Gentiles' not keeping these things, and being none the worse for it: nor having any inferiority in respect of faith: anon, of their own will they abandoned the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:111
verses.text: (f) Since therefore he was about to preach, that he might not smite the Jews a double blow, he circumcised Timothy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:112
verses.text: And yet he was but half (a Jew by birth), his father being a Greek: but yet, because that was a great point carried in the cause of the Gentiles, he did not care for this: for the Word must needs be disseminated: therefore also he with his own hands circumcised him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:113
verses.text: "And so were the churches established in the faith".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:114
verses.text: Do you mark here also how from going counter (to his own object) a great good results? "And increased in number daily".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:116
verses.text: ) Do you observe, that the circumcising not only did no harm, but was even of the greatest service? "And a vision appeared unto Paul in the night".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:117
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:118
verses.text: ) Not now by Angels, as to Philip, as to Cornellius, but how? By a vision it is now shown to him: in more human sort, not now as before (i-e:, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:119
verses.text: , ) in more divine manner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:120
verses.text: For where the compliance is more easy, it is done in more human sort; but where great force was needed, there in more divine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:121
verses.text: For since he was but urged to preach, to this end it is shown him in a dream: but to forbear preaching, he could not readily endure: to this end the Holy Ghost reveals it to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:122
verses.text: Thus also it was then with Peter, "Arise, go down".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:123
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:124
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:125
verses.text: ) For of course the Holy Spirit did not work what was otherwise easy: but (here) even a dream sufficed him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:126
verses.text: And to Joseph also, as being readily moved to compliance, the appearance is in a dream, but to the rest in waking vision.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:127
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:128
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:129
verses.text: ; ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:130
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:131
verses.text: ) Thus to Cornelius, and to Paul himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:132
verses.text: "And lo, a man of Macedonia," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:133
verses.text: and not simply enjoining, but "beseeching," and from the very persons in need of (spiritual) cure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:134
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:135
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:136
verses.text: ; ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:137
verses.text: ) "Assuredly gathering," it says, "that the Lord had called us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:138
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:139
verses.text: ), that is, inferring, both from the circumstance that Paul saw it and none other, and from the having been "forbidden by the Spirit," and from their being on the borders; from all these they gathered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:140
verses.text: "Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:141
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:142
verses.text: ) That is, even the voyage made this manifest: for there was no tardiness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:143
verses.text: It became the very root of Macedonia.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:144
verses.text: It was not always in the way of "sharp contention" that the Holy Spirit wrought: but this so rapid progress (of the Word) was a token that the thing was more than human.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:145
verses.text: And yet it is not said that Barnabas was exasperated, but, "Between them there arose a sharp contention".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:146
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:147
verses.text: ) If the one was not exasperated neither was the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:148
verses.text: Knowing this, let us not merely pick out (ἐκλέγωμεν) these things, but let us learn and be taught by them: for they were not written without a purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:149
verses.text: It is a great evil to be ignorant of the Scriptures: from the things we ought to get good from, we get evil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:150
verses.text: Thus also medicines of healing virtue, often, from the ignorance of those who use them, ruin and destroy: and arms which are meant to protect, are themselves the cause of death unless one know how to put them on.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:151
verses.text: But the reason is, that we seek everything rather than what is good for ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:152
verses.text: And in the case of a house, we seek what is good for it, and we would not endure to see it decaying with age, or tottering, or hurt by storms: but for our soul we make no account: nay, even should we see its foundations rotting, or the fabric and the roof, we make no account of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:153
verses.text: Again, if we possess brute creatures, we seek what is good for them: we call in both horse-feeders and horse-doctors, and all besides: we attend to their housing, and charge those who are entrusted with them, that they may not drive them at random or carelessly, nor take them out by night at unseasonable hours nor sell away their provender; and there are many laws laid down by us for the good of the brute creatures: but for that of our soul there is no account taken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:154
verses.text: But why speak I of brute creatures which are useful to us? There are many who keep small birds (or "sparrows") which are useful for nothing except that they simply amuse, and there are many laws even about them, and nothing is neglected or without order, and we take care for everything rather than for our own selves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:155
verses.text: Thus we make our selves more worthless than all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:156
verses.text: And if indeed a person abusively call us "dog," we are annoyed: but while we are opprobrious to ourselves, not in word, but in deed, and do not even bestow as much care on our soul as on dogs, we think it no great harm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:157
verses.text: Do you see how all is full of darkness? How many are careful about their dogs, that they may not be filled with more than the proper food, that so they may be keen and fit for hunting, being set on by famine and hunger: but for themselves they have no care to avoid luxury: and the brute creatures indeed they teach to exercise philosophy, while they let themselves sink down into the savageness of the brutes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:158
verses.text: The thing is a riddle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:159
verses.text: "And where are your philosophic brutes?" There are such; or, say, do you not take it to be philosophy, when a dog gnawed with hunger, after having hunted and caught his prey, abstains from the food; and though he sees his meal ready before him, and with hunger urging him on, yet waits for his master? Be ashamed of yourselves: teach your bellies to be as philosophic.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:160
verses.text: You have no excuse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:161
verses.text: When you have been able to implant such philosophic self-command in an irrational nature, which neither speaks nor hears reason, shall you not much more be able to implant it in yourself? For that it is the effect of man's care, not of nature is plain: since otherwise all dogs ought to have this habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:162
verses.text: Do you then become as dogs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:163
verses.text: For it is you that compel me to fetch my examples thence: for indeed they should be drawn from heavenly things; but since if I speak of those, you say, "Those are (too) great," therefore I speak nothing of heavenly things: again, if I speak of Paul, you say, "He was an Apostle:" therefore neither do I mention Paul: if again I speak of a man, you say, "That person could do it:" therefore I do not mention a man even, but a brute creature; a creature too, that has not this habit by nature, lest you should say that it effected this by nature, and not (which is the fact) from choice: and what is wonderful, choice not self-acquired, but (the result of) your care.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:164
verses.text: The creature does not give a thought to the fatigue, the wear and tear it has undergone in running down the prey, not a thought to this, that by its own proper toil it has made the capture: but casting away all these regards, it observes the command of its master, and shows itself superior to the cravings of appetite.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:165
verses.text: "True; because it looks to be praised, it looks to get a greater meal".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:166
verses.text: Say then to yourself, that the dog through hope of future pleasure, despises that which is present: while you do not choose for hope of future good things to despise those which are present; but he indeed knows, that, if he tastes of that food at the wrong time and against his master's will, he will both be deprived of that, and not get even that which was apportioned to him, but receive blows instead of food: whereas you cannot even perceive this, and that which he has learnt by dint of custom, you do not succeed in acquiring even from reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:167
verses.text: Let us imitate the dogs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:168
verses.text: The same thing hawks also and eagles are said to do: what the dogs do with regard to hares and deer, the same do those with regard to birds; and these too act from a philosophy learnt from men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:169
verses.text: These facts are enough to condemn us, these enough to convict us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:170
verses.text: To mention another thing:—they that are skilled in breaking horses, shall take them, wild, fierce, kicking, biting, and in a short time so discipline them, that though the teacher be not there, it is a luxury to ride them, their paces are so thoroughly well-ordered: but the paces of the soul may be all disordered, and none cares for it: it bounds, and kicks, and its rider is dragged along the ground like a child, and makes a most disgraceful figure, and yet no one puts curbs on her, and leg-ties, and bits, nor mounts upon her the skilful rider—Christ, I mean.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:171
verses.text: And therefore it is that all is turned upside down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:172
verses.text: For when you both teach dogs to master the craving of the belly, and tame the fury in a lion, and the unruliness of horses, and teach the birds to speak plainly, how inconsistent must it not be—to implant achievements of reason in natures that are without reason, and to import the passions of creatures without reason into natures endowed with reason? There is no excuse for us, none.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:173
verses.text: All who have succeeded (in mastering their passions) will accuse us, both believers and unbelievers: for even unbelievers have so succeeded; yea, and wild beasts, and dogs, not men only: and we shall accuse our own selves, since we succeed, when we will, but when we are slothful, we are dragged away.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:174
verses.text: For indeed many even of those who live a very wicked life, have oftentimes changed themselves when they wished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:175
verses.text: But the cause is, as I said, that we go about seeking for what is good for other things, not what is good for ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:176
verses.text: If you build a splendid house, you know what is good for the house, not what is good for yourself: if you take a beautiful garment, you know what is good for the body, not for yourself: and if you get a good horse, it is so likewise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:177
verses.text: None makes it his mark how his soul shall be beautiful; and yet, when that is beautiful, there is no need of any of those things: as, if that be not beautiful, there is no good of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:178
verses.text: For like as in the case of a bride, though there be chambers hung with tapestry wrought with gold, though there be choirs of the fairest and most beautiful women, though there be roses and garlands, though there be a comely bridegroom, and the maidservants and female friends, and everybody about them be handsome, yet, if the bride herself be full of deformity, there is no good of all those; as on the other hand if she were beautiful, neither would there be any loss arising from (the want of) those, nay just the contrary; for in the case of an ugly bride, those would make her look all the uglier, while in the other case, the beautiful would look all the more beautiful: just so, the soul, when she is beautiful, not only needs none of those adjuncts, but they even cast a shade over her beauty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:179
verses.text: For we shall see the philosopher shine, not so much when in wealth, as in poverty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:180
verses.text: For in the former case many will impute it to his riches, that he is not superior to riches: but when he lives with poverty for his mate, and shines through all, and will not let himself be compelled to do anything base, then none claims shares with him in the crown of philosophy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:181
verses.text: Let us then make our soul beauteous, if at least we would fain be rich.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:182
verses.text: What profit is it, when your mules indeed are white and plump and in good condition, but you who are drawn by them are lean and scurvy and ill-favored? What is the gain, when your carpets indeed are soft and beautiful, full of rich embroidery and art, and your soul goes clad in rags, or even naked and foul? What the gain, when the horse indeed has his paces beautifully ordered, more like dancing than stepping, while the rider, together with his choral train and adorned with more than bridal ornaments, is more crooked than the lame, and has no more command over hands and feet than drunkards and madmen? Tell me now, if some one were to give you a beautiful horse, and to distort your body, what would be the profit? Now you have your soul distorted, and care you not for it? Let us at length, I beseech you, have a care for our own selves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:183
verses.text: Do not let us make our own selves more worthless than all beside.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:184
verses.text: If anyone insult us with words, we are annoyed and vexed: but insulting ourselves as we do by our deeds, we do not give a thought to it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 96:185
verses.text: Let us, though late, come at last to our senses, that we may be enabled by having much care for our soul, and laying hold upon virtue, to obtain eternal good things, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, might, honor, now and evermore, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:1
verses.text: Homily XXXV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:2
verses.text: Acts XVI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:3
verses.text: ,  "And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont (Chrys.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:4
verses.text: "was thought likely") to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted thither.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:5
verses.text: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:6
verses.text: See again Paul judaizing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:7
verses.text: "Where it was thought," it says, both from the time and from the place, "that prayer would be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:8
verses.text: —Out of the city, by a river side:" for it is not to be supposed that they prayed only where there was a synagogue; they also prayed out of synagogue, but then for this purpose they set apart, as it were, a certain place, because as Jews they were more corporeal—and, "on the sabbath-day," when it was likely that a multitude would come together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:9
verses.text: "And we sat down, and spake to the women which resorted thither".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:10
verses.text: Mark again the freedom from all pride.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:11
verses.text: "And a certain woman:" a woman and she of low condition, from her trade too: but mark (in her) a woman of elevated mind (φιλόσοφον).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:12
verses.text: In the first place, the fact of God's calling her bears testimony to her: "And when she was baptized," it says, "she and her household"—mark how he persuaded all of them—"she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:13
verses.text: And she constrained us" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:14
verses.text: ): then look at her wisdom, how she importunes (δυσωπεἵ), the Apostles how full of humility her words are, how full of wisdom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:15
verses.text: "If ye have judged me faithful," she says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:16
verses.text: Nothing could be more persuasive.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:17
verses.text: Who would not have been softened by these words? She did not request (or, "claim") did not entreat simply: but she left them to decide, and (yet) exceedingly forced them: "And she constrained us," it says, by those words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:18
verses.text: And again in a different way: for see how she straightway bears fruit, and accounts it a great gain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:19
verses.text: "If ye have judged me," that is, That ye did judge me is manifest, by your delivering to me such (holy) mysteries (i-e: sacraments, see p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:20
verses.text: , note ): and she did not dare to invite them before this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:21
verses.text: But why was there any unwillingness on the part of Paul and those with them, that they should need to be constrained? It was either by way of calling her to greater earnestness of desire, or because Christ had said, "Enquire who is worthy, and there abide".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:22
verses.text: (Luke x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:23
verses.text: ) (It was not that they were unwilling), but they did it for a purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:24
verses.text: —"And it came to pass," it says, "as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying: the same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which show unto us the way of salvation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:27
verses.text: ) What may be the reason that both the demon spoke these words, and Paul forbade him? Both the one acted maliciously, and the other wisely: the demon wished in fact to make himself credible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:28
verses.text: For if Paul had admitted his testimony, he would have deceived many of the believers, as being received by him: therefore he endures to speak what made against himself, that he may establish what made for himself: and so the demon himself uses accommodation (συγκαταβάσει) in order to destruction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:29
verses.text: At first then, Paul would not admit it, but scorned it, not wishing to cast himself all at once upon miracles; but when it continued to do this, and pointed to their work (καὶ τὸ ἔργον ἐδείκνυ) "who preach unto us the way of salvation," then he commanded it to come out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:30
verses.text: For it says, "Paul being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:31
verses.text: And he came out the same hour.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:32
verses.text: (a) And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:35
verses.text: ) (d) So then Paul did all, both miracles and teaching, but of the dangers Silas also is partaker.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:36
verses.text: And why says it, "But Paul being grieved?" It means, he saw through the malice of the demon, as he saith, "For we are not ignorant of his devices".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:37
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:38
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:39
verses.text: ) (b) "And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:40
verses.text: Everywhere money the cause of evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:41
verses.text: O that heathen cruelty! they wished the girl to be still a demoniac, that they might make money by her.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:42
verses.text: "They caught Paul and Silas," it says, "and dragged them into the marketplace unto the rulers, and brought them unto the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city!" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:43
verses.text: ): by doing what? Then why did you not drag them (hither) before this? "Being Jews:" the name was in bad odor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:44
verses.text: "And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:46
verses.text: ) They made a charge of treason of it (εἰς καθοσίωσιν ἤγαγον).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:47
verses.text: (e) Why did they not say, Because they cast out the demon, they were guilty of impiety against God? For this was a defeat to them: but instead of that, they have recourse to a charge of treason (ἐπὶ καθοσίωσιν): like the Jews when they said, "We have no king but Caesar: whoso maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:48
verses.text: (John xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:49
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:50
verses.text: ) (c) "And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:52
verses.text: ) O the irrational conduct! They did not examine, did not allow them to speak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:53
verses.text: And yet, such a miracle having taken place, ye ought to have worshipped them, ought to have held them as saviors and benefactors.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:54
verses.text: For if money was what ye wished, why, having found so great wealth, did ye not run to it? This makes you more famous, the having power to cast out demons than the obeying them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:55
verses.text: Lo, even miracles, and yet love of money was mightier.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:56
verses.text: (f) "And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:57
verses.text: —great was their wrath—"charging the jailer to keep them safely" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:58
verses.text: ): "who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:59
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:60
verses.text: ) Observe, he also again thrust them into the "inner" prison: and this too was done providentially, because there was to be a great miracle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:61
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:62
verses.text: ) "Out of the city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:63
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:64
verses.text: ) The place was convenient for hearing the word, aloof from troubles and dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:65
verses.text: (b) "On the sabbath".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:66
verses.text: As there was no work going on, they were more attentive to what was spoken.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:67
verses.text: (a) "And a certain woman, named Lydia, a seller of purple" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:68
verses.text: ): observe how the writer of the history is not ashamed of the occupations (of the converts): (c) moreover neither was this city of the Philippians a great one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:69
verses.text: Having learnt these things, let us also be ashamed of no man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:70
verses.text: Peter abides with a tanner (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:71
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:72
verses.text: ): (Paul) with a woman who was a seller of purple, and a foreigner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:73
verses.text: Where is pride? "Whose heart the Lord opened".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:74
verses.text: Therefore we need God, to open the heart: but God opens the hearts that are willing: for there are hardened hearts to be seen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:75
verses.text: "So that she attended to the things which were spoken of Paul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:76
verses.text: The opening, then, was God's work, the attending was hers: so that it was both God's doing and man's.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:77
verses.text: And she was baptized (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:78
verses.text: ), and receives the Apostles with such earnestness of entreaty; with more than that used by Abraham.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:79
verses.text: And she speaks of no other token than that whereby she was saved (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:80
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:81
verses.text: ): she says not, "If ye have judged me" a great, a devout woman; but what? "faithful to the Lord:" if to the Lord, much more to you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:82
verses.text: "If ye have judged me:" if ye do not doubt it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:83
verses.text: And she says not, Abide with me, but, "Come into my house and abide:" with great earnestness (she says it).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:84
verses.text: Indeed a faithful woman!—"A certain damsel possessed with a spirit of Python".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:85
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:86
verses.text: ) Say, what is this demon? The god, as they call him, Python: from the place he is so called.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:87
verses.text: Do you mark that Apollo also is a demon? And (the demon) wished to bring them into temptation: (therefore) to provoke them, "the same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which show unto us the way of salvation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:88
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:89
verses.text: ) O thou accursed, thou execrable one! if then thou knowest that it is "His way of salvation" that "they show," why dost thou not come out freely? But just what Simon wished, when he said, "Give me, that on whomsoever I lay my hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:90
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:91
verses.text: ), the same did this demon: since he saw them becoming famous, here also he plays the hypocrite: by this means he thought to be allowed to remain in the body, if he should preach the same things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:92
verses.text: But if Christ "receive not testimony from man," (John v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:93
verses.text: ), meaning John, much less from a demon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:94
verses.text: "Praise is not comely in the mouth of a sinner" (Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:95
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:96
verses.text: ), much less from a demon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:97
verses.text: For that they preach is not of men, but of the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:98
verses.text: Because they did not act in a spirit of boasting.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:99
verses.text: "And Paul being grieved," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:100
verses.text: By their clamor and shouting they thought to alarm them (the magistrates): saying, "These men do exceedingly trouble our city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:101
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:102
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:103
verses.text: ) What sayest thou? Dost thou believe the demon? Why not here also? He saith, They are "servants of the most high God;" thou sayest, "They exceedingly trouble our city:" he saith, "They show us the way of salvation;" thou sayest, "They teach customs which are not lawful for us to receive".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:104
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:105
verses.text: ) Observe, how they do not attend even to the demon, but look only to one thing, their covetousness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:106
verses.text: But observe them (Paul and Silas), how they do not answer, nor plead for themselves; (b) "For when," saith he, "I am weak, then am I strong.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:107
verses.text: My grace is sufficient for thee, for My strength is made perfect in weakness" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:108
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:109
verses.text: ): so that by reason of their gentleness also they should be admired.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:110
verses.text: (a) "And the magistrates," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:111
verses.text: , "charging the jailer to keep them safely" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:112
verses.text: ): that they may be the means of a greater miracle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:113
verses.text: (c) The stricter the custody, the greater the miracle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:114
verses.text: It was probably from the wish to cut short the disturbance, that the magistrates did these things; because they saw the crowd urgent, and wished to stay their passion at the instant, therefore they inflicted the stripes: at the same time it was their wish to hear the matter, and that was why they cast them into prison and gave charge "to keep them safely".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:115
verses.text: And, it says, "he made them fast in the stocks" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:116
verses.text: ), (το ξύλον) as we should say, the nervum (νέρβον).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:117
verses.text: What tears do not these things call for! (Think) what they suffer, while we (live) in luxury, we in theatres, we perishing and drowning (in dissolute living), seeking always idle amusement, not enduring to suffer pain for Christ, not even as far as words, not even as far as talk.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:118
verses.text: These things I beseech you let us ever call to mind, what things they suffered, what things they endured, how undismayed they were, how unoffended.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:119
verses.text: They were doing God's work, and suffered these things! They did not say, Why do we preach this, and God does not take our part? But even this was a benefit to them, even apart from the truth, in the thing itself; it made them more vigorous, stronger, intrepid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:120
verses.text: "Tribulation worketh endurance".
