verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:123
verses.text: ) Then let us not seek loose and dissolute living.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:124
verses.text: For as in the one case the good is twofold, that the sufferers are made strong, and that the rewards are great; so in the other the evil is twofold, that such are rendered more enervated, and that it is to no good, but only evil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:125
verses.text: For nothing can be more worthless than a man who passes all his time in idleness and luxury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:126
verses.text: For the man untried, as the saying is, is also unapproved; unapproved not only in the contests, but also in everything else.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:127
verses.text: Idleness is a useless thing, and in luxury itself nothing is so unsuited to the end proposed as the leading a luxurious life: for it palls with satiety, so that neither the enjoyment of the viands is so great, nor the enjoyment of relaxation, but all becomes vapid, and runs to waste.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:128
verses.text: Then let us not seek after this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:129
verses.text: For if we will consider which has the pleasanter life, he that is toiled and hardworked, or he that lives in luxury, we shall find it to be the former.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:130
verses.text: For in the first place, the bodily senses are neither clear nor sound, but dull (χαὕναι) and languid; and when those are not right, even of health there is plainly no enjoyment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:131
verses.text: Which is the useful horse, the pampered or the exercised? which the serviceable ship, that which sails, or that which lies idle? which the best water, the running or the stagnant? which the best iron, that which is much used, or that which does no work? does not the one shine bright as silver, while the other becomes all over rusty, useless, and even losing some of its own substance? The like happens also to the soul as the consequence of idleness: a kind of rust spreads over it, and corrodes both its brightness and everything else.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:132
verses.text: How then shall one rub off this rust? With the whetstone of tribulations: so shall one make the soul useful and fit for all things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:133
verses.text: Else, how, I ask, will she be able to cut off the passions, with her edge turned (ἀνακλώσης) and bending like lead? How shall she wound the devil?—And then to whom can such an one be other than a disgusting spectacle—a man cultivating obesity, dragging himself along like a seal? I speak not this of those who are naturally of this habit, but of those who by luxurious living have brought their bodies into such a condition, of those who are naturally of a spare habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:134
verses.text: The sun has risen, has shot forth his bright beams on all sides, and roused up each person to his work: the husbandman goes forth with his spade, the smith with his hammer, and each artisan with his several instruments, and you will find each handling his proper tools; the woman also takes either her distaff or her webs: while he, like the swine, immediately at the first dawn goes forth to feed his belly, seeking how he may provide sumptuous fare.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:135
verses.text: And yet it is only for brute beasts to be feeding from morning to night; and for them, because their only use is to be slaughtered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:136
verses.text: Nay, even of the beasts, those which carry burdens and admit of being worked, go forth to their work while it is yet night.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:137
verses.text: But this man, rising from his bed, when the (noon-tide) sun has filled the market-place, and people are tired of their several works, then this man gets up, stretching himself out just as if he were indeed a hog in fattening, having wasted the fairest part of the day in darkness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 97:138
verses.text: Then he sits there for a long time on his bed, often unable even to lift himself up from the last evening's debauch, and having wasted (still) more time in this (listlessness), proceeds to adorn himself, and issues forth, a spectacle of unseemliness, with nothing human about him, but with all the appearance of a beast with a human shape: his eyes rheumy from the effect of wine,.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:1
verses.text: while the miserable soul, just like the lame, is unable to rise, bearing about its bulk of flesh, like an elephant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:2
verses.text: Then he comes and sits in (various) places, and says and does such things, that it were better for him to be still sleeping than to be awake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:3
verses.text: If it chance that evil tidings be announced, he shows himself weaker than any girl; if good, more silly than any child; on his face there is a perpetual yawn.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:4
verses.text: He is a mark for all that would do harm, if not for all men, at least for all evil passions; and wrath easily excites such a man, and lust, and envy, and all other passions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:5
verses.text: All flatter him, all pay court to him, rendering his soul weaker than it is already: and each day he goes on and on, adding to his disease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:6
verses.text: If he chance to fall into any difficulty of business, he becomes dust and ashes, and his silken garments are of no help to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:7
verses.text: We have not said all this without a purpose, but to teach you, that none of you should live idly and at random.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:8
verses.text: For idleness and luxury are not conducive to work, to good reputation, to enjoyment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:9
verses.text: For who will not condemn such a man? Family, friends, kinsfolk (will say), He is indeed a very encumbrance of the ground.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:10
verses.text: Such a man as this has come into the world to no purpose: or rather, not to no purpose, but to ill purpose against his own person, to his own ruin, and to the hurt of others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:11
verses.text: But that this is more pleasant—let us look to this; for this is the question.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:12
verses.text: Well then, what can be less pleasant than (the condition of) a man who has nothing to do; what more wretched and miserable? Is it not worse than all the fetters in the world, to be always gaping and yawning, as one sits in the market-place, looking at the passers by? For the soul, as its nature is to be always on the move, cannot endure to be at rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:13
verses.text: God has made it a creature of action: to work is of its very nature; to be idle is against its nature.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:14
verses.text: For let us not judge of these things from those who are diseased, but let us put the thing itself to the proof of fact.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:15
verses.text: Nothing is more hurtful than leisure, and having nothing to do: indeed therefore hath God laid on us a necessity of working: for idleness hurts everything.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:16
verses.text: Even to the members of the body, inaction is a mischief.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:17
verses.text: Both eye, if it perform not its work, and mouth, and belly, and every member that one could mention, falls into the worst state of disease: but none so much as the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:18
verses.text: But as inaction is an evil, so is activity in things that ought to be let alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:19
verses.text: For just as it is with the teeth, if one eats not, one receives hurt to them, and if one eats things unfitting, it jars them, and sets them on edge: so it is here; both if the soul be inactive, and if inactive in wrong things, it loses its proper force.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:20
verses.text: Then let us eschew both alike; both inaction, and the activity which is worse than inaction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:21
verses.text: And what may that be? Covetousness, anger, envyings, and the other passions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 100:22
verses.text: As regards these, let us make it our object to be inactive, in order that we may obtain the good things promised to us, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:1
verses.text: Homily XXXVI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:2
verses.text: Acts XVI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:3
verses.text: ,  "And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:4
verses.text: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:5
verses.text: What could equal these souls? These men had been scourged, had received many stripes, they had been misused, were in peril of their lives, were thrust into the inner prison, and set fast in the stocks: and for all this they did not suffer themselves to sleep, but kept vigil all the night.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:6
verses.text: Do you mark what a blessing tribulation is? But we, in our soft beds, with none to be afraid of, pass the whole night in sleep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:7
verses.text: But belike this is why they kept vigil, because they were in this condition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:8
verses.text: Not the tyranny of sleep could overpower them, not the smart of pain could bow them, not the fear of evil east them into helpless dejection: no, these were the very things that made them wakeful: and they were even filled with exceeding delight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:9
verses.text: "At midnight," it says, "and the prisoners listened to them:" it was so strange and surprising! "And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and immediately, all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:10
verses.text: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:12
verses.text: ) There was an earthquake, that the keeper should be roused from sleep, and the doors flew open, that he should wonder at what had happened: but these things the prisoners saw not: otherwise they would all have fled: but the keeper of the prison was about to slay himself, thinking the prisoners were escaped.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:13
verses.text: "But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:14
verses.text: ) (b) "Then he called for lights, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas; and brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:16
verses.text: ) Do you mark how the wonder overpowered him? (a) He wondered more at Paul's kindness; he was amazed at his manly boldness, that he had not escaped when he had it in his power, that he hindered him from killing himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:17
verses.text: (c) "And they said, believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:18
verses.text: And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:20
verses.text: , ) and (so) immediately gave proof of their kindness towards him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:21
verses.text: "And he took them the same hour of the night and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:23
verses.text: ) He washed them, and was himself baptized, he and his house.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:24
verses.text: "And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:25
verses.text: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, Let those men go".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:28
verses.text: ) It is likely the magistrates had learnt what had happened, and did not dare of themselves to dismiss them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:29
verses.text: "And the keeper of the prison told these words to Paul, saying, the magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:30
verses.text: But Paul said unto them, they have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust as out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:31
verses.text: And the sergeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:32
verses.text: And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:33
verses.text: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:36
verses.text: ) Even upon the declaration of the magistrates Paul does not go out, but for the sake both of Lydia and the rest he puts them in fear: that they may not be supposed to have come out upon their own request, that they may set the rest in a posture of boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:37
verses.text: The impeachment was twofold: that "being Romans," and "uncondemned," they had openly cast them into prison.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:38
verses.text: You see that in many things they took their measures as men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:39
verses.text: (Recapitulation) "And at midnight," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:41
verses.text: ) Let us compare, beloved, with that night these nights of ours, with their revellings, their drunkenness, and wanton excesses, with their sleep which might as well be death, their watchings which are worse than sleep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:42
verses.text: For while some sleep without sense or feeling, others lie awake to pitiable and wretched purpose, plotting deceits, anxiously thinking about money, studying how they may be revenged upon those who do them wrong, meditating enmity, reckoning up the abusive words spoken during the day: thus do they rake up the smouldering embers of wrath, doing things intolerable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:43
verses.text: Mark how Peter slept.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:44
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:45
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:46
verses.text: ) Both there, it was wisely ordered (that he should be asleep); for the Angel came to him, and it behooved that none should see what happened; and on the other hand it was well ordered here (that Paul should be awake), in order that the keeper of the prison might be prevented from killing himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:47
verses.text: "And suddenly there was a great earthquake".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:48
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:49
verses.text: ) And why did no other miracle take place? Because this was, of all others, the thing sufficient for his conversion, seeing he was personally in danger: for it is not so much miracles that overpower us, as the things which issue in our own deliverance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:50
verses.text: That the earthquake should not seem to have come of itself, there was this concurrent circumstance, bearing witness to it: "the doors were opened, and all their bonds were loosed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:51
verses.text: And it appears in the night-time; for the Apostles did not work for display, but for men's salvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:52
verses.text: "And the keeper of the prison," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:54
verses.text: ) The keeper was not an evil-disposed man that he "thrust them into the inner prison," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:55
verses.text: ) was because of his "having received such a command," not of himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:56
verses.text: The man was all in a tumult of perturbation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:57
verses.text: "What shall I do to be saved?" he asks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:58
verses.text: Why not before this? Paul shouted, until he saw, and is beforehand with him saying, "We are all here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:59
verses.text: And having called for lights," it says, "he sprang in, and fell down at the feet" of the prisoner; he, the prison keeper, saying, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:60
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:61
verses.text: ) Why, what had they said? Observe, he does not, on finding himself safe, think all is well; he is overcome with awe at the miraculous power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:62
verses.text: Do you mark what happened in the former case, and what here? There a girl was released from a spirit, and they cast them into prison, because they had liberated her from the spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:63
verses.text: Here, they did but show the doors standing open, and it opened the doors of his heart, it loosed two sorts of chains; that (prisoner) kindled the (true) light; for the light in his heart was shining.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:64
verses.text: "And he sprang in, and fell before them;" and he does not ask, How is this? What is this? but straightway he says, "What must I do to be saved?" What then answers Paul? "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, thou and thine house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:65
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:66
verses.text: ) For this above all, wins men: that one's house also should be saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:67
verses.text: "And they spake the word to him, and to all that were in his house.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:68
verses.text: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:69
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:70
verses.text: , ), washed them and was washed: those he washed from their stripes, himself was washed from his sins: he fed and was fed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:71
verses.text: "And rejoiced," it says: although there was nothing but words only and good hopes: "having believed in God with all his house (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:72
verses.text: ): this was the token of his having believed—that he was released of all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:73
verses.text: What worse than a jailer, what more ruthless, more savage? He entertained them with great honor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:74
verses.text: Not, because he was safe, he made merry, but, having believed God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:75
verses.text: (a) "Believe on the Lord," said the Apostle: therefore it is that the writer here says, "Having believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:76
verses.text: —(d) Now therefore," it says, "depart, and go in peace" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:77
verses.text: ): that is, in safety, fearing no man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:78
verses.text: (b) "But Paul said unto them" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:79
verses.text: ): that he may not seem to be receiving his liberty as one condemned, and as one that has done wrong: therefore it is that he says, "Having openly beaten us uncondemned," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:80
verses.text: —that it may not be matter of grace on their part.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:81
verses.text: (e) And besides, they wish the jailer himself to be out of danger, that he may not be called to account for this afterwards.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:82
verses.text: And they do not say, "Having beaten us," who have wrought miracles: for they (the magistrates) did not even heed these: but, that which was most effectual to shake their minds, "uncondemned, and being Romans".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:83
verses.text: (c) Observe how diversely grace manages things: how Peter went out, how Paul, though both were Apostles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:84
verses.text: "They feared," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:85
verses.text: ) it says: because the men were Romans, not because they had unjustly cast them into prison, "And besought them to depart out of the city" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:86
verses.text: ): begged them as a favor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:87
verses.text: And they went to the house of Lydia, and having confirmed her, so departed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:88
verses.text: For it was not right to leave their hostess in distress and anxiety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:89
verses.text: But they went out, not in compliance with the request of those rulers, but hasting to the preaching: the city having been sufficiently benefited by the miracle: for it was fit they should not be there any longer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:90
verses.text: For in the absence of them that wrought it, the miracle appeared greater, itself crying out more loudly: the faith of the jailer was a voice in itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:91
verses.text: What equal to this? He is put in bonds, and looses, being bound: looses a twofold bond: him that bound him, he looses by being bound.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:92
verses.text: These are indeed works of (supernatural) grace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:93
verses.text: (f) Let us constantly bear in mind this jailer, not the miracle: how, prisoner as he was (the Apostle), persuaded his jailer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:94
verses.text: What say the heathen? "And of what things," say they, "was such a man as this to be persuaded—a vile, wretched creature, of no understanding, full of all that is bad and nothing else, and easily brought over to anything? For these, say they, are the things, a tanner, a purple-seller, an eunuch, slaves, and women believed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:95
verses.text: This is what they say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:96
verses.text: What then will they be able to say, when we produce the men of rank and station, the centurion, the proconsul, those from that time to the present, the rulers themselves, the emperors? But for my part, I speak of something else, greater than this: let us look to these very persons of no consideration.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:97
verses.text: "And where is the wonder?" say you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:98
verses.text: Why, this, I say, is a wonder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:99
verses.text: For, if a person be persuaded about any common things, it is no wonder: but if resurrection, a kingdom of heaven, a life of philosophic self-command, be the subjects, and, discoursing of these to persons of mean consideration, one persuades them, it will be more wonderful than if one persuaded wise men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:100
verses.text: For when there is no danger attending the things of which one persuades people, then (the objector) might with some plausibility allege want of sense on their part: but when (the preacher) says—to the slave, as you will have it—"If thou be persuaded by me, it is at thy peril, thou wilt have all men for thine enemies, thou must die, thou must suffer evils without number," and yet for all this, convinces that man's soul, there can be no more talk here of want of sense.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:101
verses.text: Since, if indeed the doctrines contained what was pleasant, one might fairly enough say this: but if, what the philosohers would never have chosen to learn, this the slave does learn, then is the wonder greater.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:102
verses.text: And, if you will, let us bring before us the tanner himself, and see what were the subjects on which Peter conversed with him: or if you will, this same jailer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:103
verses.text: What then said Paul to him? "That Christ rose again," say you; "that there is a resurrection of the dead, and a kingdom: and he had no difficulty in persuading him, a man easily led to anything".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:104
verses.text: How? Said he nothing about the mode of life; that he must be temperate, that he must be superior to money, that he must not be unmerciful, that he must impart of his good things to others? For it cannot be said, that the being persuaded to these things also was from the want of power of mind; no, to be brought to all this required a great soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:105
verses.text: For be it so, that as far as the doctrines went, they were rendered more apt to receive these by their want of intelligence: but to accept such a virtuous, self-denying rule of life, how could that be owing to any defect of understanding? So that the less understanding the person may have, if nevertheless he is persuaded to things, to which even philosophers were unable to persuade their fellow-philosophers, the greater the wonder—when women and slaves are persuaded of these truths, and prove it by their actions, of which same truths the Platos and all the rest of them were never able to persuade any man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:106
verses.text: And why say I, "any man?" Say rather, not themselves even: on the contrary, that money is not to be despised, Plato persuaded (his disciples) by getting, as he did, such an abundance of property, and golden rings, and goblets; and that the honor to be had from the many is not to be despised, this Socrates himself shows, for all that he may philosophize without end on this point: for in everything he did, he had an eye to fame.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:107
verses.text: And if you were conversant with his discourses, I might go at great length into this subject, and show what a deal of insincerity (εἰρωνείαν) there was in them,—if at least we may believe what his disciple says of him,—and how that all his writings have their ground-work in vainglory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:108
verses.text: But, leaving them, let us direct the discourse to our own selves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:109
verses.text: For besides the things that have been said, there is this also to be added, that men were persuaded of these things to their own peril.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:110
verses.text: Be not thou therefore shameless, but let us think over that night, the stocks, and the hymns of praise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:111
verses.text: This let us also do, and we shall open for ourselves—not a prison, but—heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:112
verses.text: If we pray, we shall be able even to open heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:113
verses.text: Elias both shut and opened heaven by prayer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:114
verses.text: (James v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:115
verses.text: ) There is a prison in heaven also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:116
verses.text: "Whatsoever," He saith, "ye shall bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:117
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:118
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:119
verses.text: ) Let us pray by night, and we shall loose these bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:120
verses.text: For that prayers loose sins, let that widow convince us, let that friend convince us, who at that untimely hour of the night persists and knocks (Luke xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:121
verses.text: ): let Cornelius convince us, for, "thy prayers," it says, "and thine alms are come up before God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:122
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:123
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:124
verses.text: ) Let Paul convince us, who says, "Now she that is a widow indeed and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications night and day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:125
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:126
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:127
verses.text: ) If he speaks thus of a widow, a weak woman, much more would he of men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:128
verses.text: I have both before discoursed to you on this, and now repeat it: let us arouse ourselves during the night: though thou make not many prayers, make one with watchfulness, and it is enough, I ask no more: and if not at midnight, at any rate at the first dawn.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:129
verses.text: Show that the night is not only for the body, but also for the soul: do not suffer it to pass idly, but make this return to thy Master: nay rather (the benefit) itself returns to thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:130
verses.text: Say, if we fall into any difficult strait, to whom do we not make request? and if we soon obtain our request, we breathe freely again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:131
verses.text: What a boon were it for thee, to have a friend to go to with thy request, who shall be ready to take it as a kindness, and to be obliged to thee for thy asking? What a boon, not to have to go about and seek one to ask of, but to find one ready? to have no need of others through whom thou mayest solicit? What could be greater than this? Since here is One who then does most, when we make not our requests of others than Himself: just as a sincere friend then most complains of us for not trusting in his friendship, when we ask of others to make request to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:132
verses.text: Thus also let us act.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:133
verses.text: "But what," you will ask, "if I should have offended Him?" Cease to give offence, and weep, and so draw near to Him, and thou wilt quickly render Him propitious as to thy former sins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:134
verses.text: Say only, I have offended: say it from thy soul and with a sincere mind, and all things are remitted to thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:135
verses.text: Thou dost not so much desire thy sins to be forgiven, as He desires to forgive thee thy sins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:136
verses.text: In proof that thou dost not so desire it, consider that thou hast no mind either to practice vigils, or to give thy money freely: but He, that He might forgive our sins, spared not His Only-begotten and True Son, the partner of His throne.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:137
verses.text: Seest thou how He more desires to forgive thee thy sins (than thou to be forgiven )? Then let us not be slothful, nor put off this any longer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:138
verses.text: He is merciful and good: only let us give Him an opportunity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:139
verses.text: And (even) this (He seeks), only that we may not become unprofitable, since even without this He could have freed us from them: but like as we (with the same view) devise and arrange many things for our servants to do, so does He in the matter of our salvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:140
verses.text: "Let us anticipate His face with thanksgiving".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:141
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:142
verses.text: xcv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:143
verses.text: "Let us come before His presence".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:144
verses.text: E.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:145
verses.text: V.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:146
verses.text: ), since He is good and kind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:147
verses.text: But if thou call not upon Him, what will He do? Thou dost not choose to say, Forgive; thou wilt not say it from thy heart, but with thy mouth only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:148
verses.text: What is it, to call in truth? (To call) with purpose of heart, with earnestness, with a sincere mind; just as men say of perfumes, "This is genuine, and has nothing spurious," so here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:149
verses.text: He who truly calls on Him, he who truly prays to Him, continually attends to it, and desists not, until he obtain (his request): but he who does it in a merely formal manner (ἀφοσιούμενος), and even this only by way of fulfilling a law, does not call in truth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:150
verses.text: Whosoever thou art, say not only, "I am a sinner," but be earnest also to rid thyself of this character; say not this only, but also grieve.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:151
verses.text: If thou grievest, thou art in earnest: if thou art not in earnest, thou grievest not: if thou grievest not, thou triflest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:152
verses.text: What sort of man is he who shall say, "I am sick," and not to do all to be freed from his sickness? A mighty weapon is Prayer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:153
verses.text: "If ye," saith the Lord, "know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more your Father?" (Luke xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:154
verses.text: ) Then wherefore art thou unwilling to approach Him? He loves thee, He is of more power than all besides.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:155
verses.text: Both willing is He and able, what is there to hinder? Nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:156
verses.text: But then, on our part, let us draw near with faith, draw near, offering the gifts that He desires, forgetfulness of wrongs, kindness, meekness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:157
verses.text: Though thou be a sinner, with boldness shalt thou ask of Him forgiveness of thy sins, if thou canst show that this has been done by thyself: but though thou be righteous, and possess not this virtue of forgetfulness of injuries, thou art none the better for it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:158
verses.text: It cannot be that a man who has forgiven his neighbor should not obtain perfect forgiveness: for God is beyond comparison more merciful than we.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:159
verses.text: What sayest thou? If thou sayest, "I have been wronged, I have subdued my anger, I have endured the onset of wrath because of Thy command, and dost Thou not forgive?" Full surely He will forgive: and this is plain to all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:160
verses.text: Therefore let us purge our soul from all resentment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 101:161
verses.text: This is sufficient for us, in order that we may be heard; and let us pray with watching and much perseverance, that having enjoyed His bountiful mercy, we may be found worthy of the good things promised, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:15
verses.text: "Opening," it says, "from the Scriptures, he reasoned with them for three sabbaths, putting before them that the Christ must suffer".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:16
verses.text: Do thou mark how before all other things he preaches the Passion: so little were they ashamed of it, knowing it to be the cause of salvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:17
verses.text: "And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:20
verses.text: "But the Jews which believed not (the best texts omit "which believed not"), moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:21
verses.text: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also; whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:23
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:24

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:25

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:26
verses.text: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go".

Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:29
verses.text: ) A man worthy to be admired, that he put himself into danger, and sent them away from it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:31

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:32
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:34
verses.text: ) "Therefore many of them believed; also of honorable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:35

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:36

Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:39

Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:42

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:44
verses.text: ) "Three sabbath-days," it says, being the time when they had leisure from work, "he reasoned with them, opening out of the Scriptures" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:45
verses.text: ): for so used Christ also to do: as on many occasions we find Him reasoning from the Scriptures, and not on all occasions (urging men) by miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:46
verses.text: Because to this indeed they stood in a posture of hostility, calling them deceivers and jugglers; but he that persuades men by reasons from the Scriptures, is not liable to this imputation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:47
verses.text: And on many occasions we find (Paul) to have convinced men simply by force of teaching: and in Antioch "the whole city was gathered together" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:49
verses.text: ): so great a thing is this also, for indeed this itself is no small miracle, nay, it is even a very great one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:50
verses.text: And that they might not think that they did it all by their own strength, but rather that God permitted it, two things resulted, namely, "Some of them were persuaded," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:51

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:54
verses.text: But how comes it that he said, "That we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision" (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:66
verses.text: )? In the same way as those Apostles also had intercourse with the Gentiles, though they had been set apart for the circumcision, so likewise did our Apostle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:67
verses.text: The more part of his work indeed was with the Gentiles: still he did not neglect the Jews either, that they might not seem to be severed from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:68
verses.text: And how was it, you will ask, that he entered in the first place into the synagogues, as if this were his leading object? True; but he persuaded the Gentiles through the Jews, and from the things which he discoursed of to the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:69
verses.text: And he knew, that this was most suitable for the Gentiles, and most conducive to belief.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:70
verses.text: Therefore he says: "Inasmuch as I am the "Apostle of the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:77

verses.text: "These all," say they, "do contrary to the decrees of Caesar" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:85
verses.text: ): for since they spoke nothing contrary to what had been decreed, nor made any commotion in the city, they bring them under a different charge: "saying that there is another king, one Jesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:86
verses.text: And they troubled the people," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:87
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:88
verses.text: ) And what are ye afraid of, seeing He is dead? (β) "And when they had taken security," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:89
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:90
verses.text: ) See how by giving security Jason sent Paul away: so that he gave his life (to the hazard) for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:91
verses.text: (α) "And brethren," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:92
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:93
verses.text: ) See how the persecutions in every case extend the preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:94
verses.text: "Now these," it says, "were more noble than those in Thessalonica" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:95
verses.text: ): i-e: they were not (men) practising base things, but some were convinced, and the others (who were not), did nothing (of that sort).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:96
verses.text: (β) "Daily," it says, "searching the Scriptures whether these things were so:" not merely upon a sudden impetus or (burst of) zeal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:97
verses.text: "More noble," it says: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:98
verses.text: e.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:99
verses.text: in point of virtue(α)"Therefore many of them," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:101
verses.text: ) And here again are Greeks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:102
verses.text: (β) "But when the Jews of Thessalonica," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:103
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:104
verses.text: ), because there were lewd persons there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:105
verses.text: And yet that city was greater.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:106
verses.text: But it is no wonder in the greater city the people were worse: nay, of course to the greater city there go the worse men, where the occasions of disturbances are many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:107
verses.text: And as in the body, where the disease is more violent for having more matter and fuel, just so is it here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:108
verses.text: (α) But look, I beg you, how their fleeing was providentially ordered, not from cowardice: otherwise they would have ceased to preach, and would not have exasperated them still more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:109
verses.text: But from this (flight) two things resulted: both the rage of those (Jews) was quenched, and the preaching spread.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:110
verses.text: But in terms befitting their disorderly conduct, he says, "Agitating the multitude".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:111
verses.text: (β) Just what was done at Iconium—that they may have the additional condemnation of destroying others besides themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:112
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:113
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:114
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:115
verses.text: ) This is what Paul says of them: "Forbidding to preach to the Gentiles, to fill up their sins alway, for the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:116
verses.text: ( Thess.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:117
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:118
verses.text: ) Why did he not stay? for if (at Lystra, ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:119
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:120
verses.text: , ) there, where he was stoned, he nevertheless stayed a long time, much more here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:121
verses.text: Why? (The Lord) did not wish them to be always doing signs; for this is itself a sign, not less than the working of signs—that being persecuted, they overcame without signs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:122
verses.text: So that just as now He prevails without signs, so was it on many occasions His will to prevail then.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:123
verses.text: Consequently neither did the Apostles run after signs: as in fact he says himself, "We preach Christ crucified" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:124
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:125
verses.text: )—to them that crave signs, to them that crave wisdom, we give that which cannot even after signs persuade, and yet we do persuade! So that this was a mighty sign.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:126
verses.text: See then, how when the preaching is extended, they are not in a hurry to run after signs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:127
verses.text: For it was right that thenceforth the believers should be mighty signs to the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:128
verses.text: Howbeit, by retreating and advancing they did these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:129
verses.text: (α) "And immediately," it says, "the brethren sent away Paul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:130
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:131
verses.text: ) Here now they send Paul alone: for it was for him they feared, lest he should suffer some harm, the head and front of all being in fact none other than he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:132
verses.text: (β) "They sent him away," it says, "as it were to the sea:" that it might not be easy for them to seize him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:133
verses.text: For at present they could not have done much by themselves; and with him they accomplished and achieved many things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:134
verses.text: For the present, it says, they wished to rescue him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:135
verses.text: (α) So far is it from being the case, that (supernatural) Grace worked all alike on all occasions: on the contrary, it left them to take their measures upon human judgment, (only) stirring them up and rousing them out of sleep, and making them to take pains.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:136
verses.text: Thus, observe, it brought them safe only as far as Philippi, but no more after that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:137
verses.text: "And receiving," it says, "a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:138
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:139
verses.text: ) For though he was a Paul, nevertheless he needed them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:140
verses.text: And with good reason are they urged by God to go into Macedonia, for there lay Greece moreover bright (before them).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:141
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:142
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:143
verses.text: )  See what zeal the rest of the disciples showed with respect to their leaders: not as it is now with us, who are separated and divided into great and small: some of us exalted, while others are envious: for this is the reason why those are envious, because we are puffed up, because we will not endure to be put upon a par with them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:144
verses.text: The reason why there is harmony in the body, is because there is no puffing up: and there is no puffing up, because the members are of necessity made to stand in need of each other, and the head has need of the feet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:145
verses.text: And God has made this to be the case with us, and, for all that, we will not endure it: although even without this, there ought to be love among us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:146
verses.text: Hear ye not how they that are without accuse us when they say, "Needs make friendships?" The laity have need of us; and we again exist for them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:147
verses.text: Since teacher or ruler would not exist, if there were not persons to be taught, nor would he perform his part, for it would not be possible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:148
verses.text: As the land has need of the husbandman, and the husbandman of the land, so is it here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:149
verses.text: What reward is there for the teacher to receive, when he has none to produce that he has taught? and what for the taught, who have not had the benefit of the best teaching? So that we need each other alike in turn, both the governed, them that govern, and leaders, them that obey: for rulers are for the sake of many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:150
verses.text: Since no one is sufficient to do anything by himself alone, whether need be to ordain (χειροτονἥσαι), or to examine men's counsels and opinions, but they become more honorable by assembly and numbers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:151
verses.text: For instance, the poor need givers, the givers again need receivers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:152
verses.text: "Considering one another" he says, "to provoke unto love and to good works".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:153
verses.text: (Heb.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:154
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:155
verses.text: ) On this account the assembly of the whole Church has more power: and what each cannot do by himself singly, he is able to do when joined with the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:156
verses.text: Therefore most necessary are the prayers offered up, here, for the world, for the Church, from the one end of the earth to the other, for peace, for those who are in adversities.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:157
verses.text: And Paul shows this when he says, "That for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:158
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:159
verses.text: ); that is, that He might confer the favor on many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:160
verses.text: And often he asks for their prayers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:161
verses.text: See also what God says with regard to the Ninevites: "And shall not I spare that city, wherein dwell more than six score thousand persons?" (Jonah iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:162
verses.text: ) For if, "where two or three," He says, "are gathered together in My Name" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:163
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:164
verses.text: ), they prevail much, how much more, being many? And yet thou mayest prevail, though thou be but one; yet not equally so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:165
verses.text: For why art thou but one? Why dost thou not make many? Why dost thou not become the maker of love? Why dost thou not create (κατασκευάζεις) friendship? Thou lackest the chief excellence of virtue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:166
verses.text: For as men's being bad by agreement together more provokes God; so for men to be good by unanimity delights Him more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:167
verses.text: "Thou shalt not follow a multitude," He says, "to do evil".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:168
verses.text: (Ex.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:169
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:170
verses.text: ) "They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable" (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:171
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:172
verses.text: ), and have become as it were men singing in concert in their wickedness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:173
verses.text: Make for thyself friends in preference to domestics, and all besides.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:174
verses.text: If the peacemaker is a son of God, how much more he who makes friends also? (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:175
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:176
verses.text: ) If he who reconciles only is called a son of God, of what shall not he be worthy, who makes friends of those who are reconciled? Let us engage ourselves in this trade, let us make those who are enemies to each other friends, and those who are not indeed enemies, but are not friends, them let us bring together, and before all, our own selves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:177
verses.text: For as he who is at enmity in his house, and has differences with his wife, carries no authority when reconciling others, but will be told, "Physician, heal thyself" (Luke iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:178
verses.text: ), so will a man be told in this case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:179
verses.text: What then is the enmity that is in us? That of the soul against the body, that of vice against virtue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:180
verses.text: This enmity let us put an end to, this war let us take away, and then being in peace we shall also address others with much boldness of speech, our conscience not accusing us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:181
verses.text: Anger fights against gentleness, love of money against contempt of it, envy against goodness of heart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:182
verses.text: Let us make an end of this war, let us overthrow these enemies, let us set up these trophies, let us establish peace in our own city.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:183
verses.text: We have within us a city and a civil polity, and citizens and aliens many: but let us banish the aliens, that our own people may not be ruined.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:184
verses.text: Let no foreign nor spurious doctrine enter in, no carnal desire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:185
verses.text: See we not that, if any enemy has been caught in a city, he is judged as a spy? Then let us not only banish aliens, but let us drive out enemies also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:186
verses.text: If we see one, let us deliver up to the ruler, (that is), to conscience (τᾥ νᾥ), that imagination which is indeed an alien, a barbarian, albeit tricked out with the garb of a citizen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:187
verses.text: For there are within us many imaginations of this kind, which are by nature indeed enemies, but are clad in sheep's skins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:188
verses.text: Just as the Persians, when they have put off the tiara, and the drawers, and the barbarian shoes, and put on the other dress which is usual with us, and have shorn themselves close, and converse in our own tongue, conceal war under their outward garb: but once apply the tortures (βασάνους or "tests"), and thou bringest to light what is hidden: so here, examine (or "put to the test,") by torture again and again such an imagination as this, and thou wilt quickly see that its spirit is that of a stranger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:189
verses.text: But to show you also by way of example the sort of spies which the devil sends into us to spy out what is in us, come let us strip one of them, and examine it strictly at the tribunal: and if you please, let us bring forward some of those which were detected by Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:190
verses.text: "Which things," he says, "have indeed a show of wisdom in will-worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body: not in any honor to the satisfying of the flesh".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:191
verses.text: (Col.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:192
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:193
verses.text: ) The devil wished to bring in Judaism: now if he had introduced it in its own form, he would not have carried his point.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:194
verses.text: Accordingly, mark how he brought it about.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:195
verses.text: "You must neglect the body," he says: "this is (the true) philosophy, not to admit of meats, but to guard against them: this is humility".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:196
verses.text: And now again in our own times, in the case of the heretics, he wished to bring us down to the creature.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:197
verses.text: See then how he dressed up his deceit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:198
verses.text: Had he said, "Worship a creature," he would have been detected: but what says he? "God" (viz.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:199
verses.text: the Son and the Holy Ghost), he says, "is a created being".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:200
verses.text: But let us lay bare for the decision of the judges the meaning of the Apostolic writings: there let us bring him: themselves will acknowledge both the preaching and the language.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:201
verses.text: Many make gains "that they may have wherewith to give to the poor," unjust gains: this too is a wicked imagination.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 102:202
verses.text: But let us undress it, let us convict it, that we may not be taken by it, but that having escaped all the devices of the devil, and holding to the sound doctrines with strictness, we may be able both to pass in safety through this life present, and to obtain the good things promised, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father, together with the Holy Ghost, be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:1
verses.text: Homily XXXVIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:2
verses.text: Acts XVII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:3
verses.text: ,  "Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:4
verses.text: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:5
verses.text: Observe how he meets with greater trials among the Jews than among the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:6
verses.text: Thus in Athens he undergoes nothing of this kind; the thing goes as far as ridicule, and there an end: and yet he did make some converts: whereas among the Jews he underwent many perils; so much greater was their hostility against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:7
verses.text: —"His spirit," it says, "was roused within him when he saw the city all full of idols".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:8
verses.text: Nowhere else were so many objects of worship to be seen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:9
verses.text: But again "he disputed with the Jews in the synagogue, and in the market daily with them that met with him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:10
verses.text: Then certain of the philosophers of the Stoics and Epicureans encountered him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:12
verses.text: ) It is a wonder the philosophers did not laugh him to scorn, speaking in the way he did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:13
verses.text: "And some said, What does this babbler mean to say?" insolently, on the instant:—this is far from philosophy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:14
verses.text: "Other some said, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods," from the preaching, because he had no arrogance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:15
verses.text: They did not understand, nor comprehend the subjects he was speaking of—how should they? affirming as they did, some of them, that God is a body; others, that pleasure is the (true) happiness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:16
verses.text: "Of strange gods, because he preached unto them Jesus and the Resurrection:" for in fact they supposed "Anastasis" (the Resurrection) to be some deity, being accustomed to worship female divinities also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:17
verses.text: "And having taken him, they brought him to the Areopagus" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:18
verses.text: )—not to punish, but in order to learn—"to the Areopagus" where the trials for murder were held.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:19
verses.text: Thus observe, in hope of learning (they ask him), saying, "May we know what is this new doctrine spoken of by thee? For thou bringest certain strange matters to our ears" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:20
verses.text: ): everywhere novelty is the charge: "we would fain know therefore, what these things may mean".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:21
verses.text: It was a city of talkers, that city of theirs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:22
verses.text: "For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:23
verses.text: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I look upon you as being in all things" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:24
verses.text: , )—he puts it by way of encomium: (the word) does not seem to mean anything offensive—δεισιδαιμονεστέρους, that is, εὐλαβεστέρους, "more religiously disposed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:25
verses.text: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with his inscription, To an Unknown God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:26
verses.text: What therefore ye ignorantly worship, this declare I unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:28
verses.text: )—"On which was inscribed, To an Unknown God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:29
verses.text: The Athenians, namely, as on many occasions they had received gods from foreign parts also—for instance, the temple of Minerva, Pan, and others from different countries—being afraid that there might be some other god not yet known to them, but worshipped elsewhere, for more assurance, forsooth, erected an altar to that god also: and as the god was not known, it was inscribed, "To an Unknown God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:30
verses.text: This God then, he tells them, is Christ; or rather, the God of all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:31
verses.text: "Him declare I unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:32
verses.text: Observe how he shows that they had already received Him, and "it is nothing strange," says he, "nothing new that I introduce to you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:33
verses.text: All along, this was what they had been saying: "What is this new doctrine spoken of by thee? For thou bringest certain strange matters to our ears".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:34
verses.text: Immediately therefore he removes this surmise of theirs: and then says, "God that made the world and all things therein, He being Lord of heaven and earth"—for, that they may not imagine Him to be one of many, he presently sets them right on this point; adding, "dwelleth not in temples made with hands" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:35
verses.text: ), "neither is worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed anything"—do you observe how, little by little, he brings in the philosophy? how he ridicules the heathen error? "seeing it is He that giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; and hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:36
verses.text: This is peculiar to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:37
verses.text: Look, then, whether these things may not be predicated of the Son also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:38
verses.text: "Being Lord," he saith, "of heaven and earth"—which they accounted to be God's.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:39
verses.text: Both the creation he declares to be His work, and mankind also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:40
verses.text: "Having determined," he says, "the times assigned to them, and the bounds of their habitation," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:41
verses.text: , ), "that they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after Him, and find Him, though He be not far from every one of us: for in Him we live, and move, and have our being: as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also His offspring".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:42
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:43
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:44
verses.text: ) This is said by Aratus the poet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:45
verses.text: Observe how he draws his arguments from things done by themselves, and from sayings of their own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:46
verses.text: "Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:48
verses.text: ) And yet for this reason we ought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:49
verses.text: By no means: for surely we are not like (to such), nor are these souls of ours.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:50
verses.text: "And imagination of man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 103:51
verses.text: How so?.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:1
verses.text: But some person might say, "We do not think this".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:2
verses.text: But it was to the many that he was addressing himself, not now to Philosophy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:3
verses.text: How then did they think so unworthily of Him? Again, putting it upon their ignorance, he says, "Now the times of ignorance God overlooked".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:4
verses.text: Having agitated their minds by the fear, he then adds this: and yet he says, "but now he commandeth all men everywhere to repent".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:5
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:6
verses.text: ) "Because He hath appointed a day, in the which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained; whereof He hath given assurance unto all men, in that He hath raised Him from the dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:7
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:8
verses.text: ) But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:9
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:10
verses.text: ) (b) "And while Paul waited," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:12
verses.text: ) It is providentially ordered that against his will he stays there, while waiting for those others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:13
verses.text: (a) "His spirit," it says, "within him" παρωξύνετο.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:14
verses.text: It does not mean there anger or exasperation: just as elsewhere it says, "There was παροξυσμὸς between them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:15
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:16
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:17
verses.text: ) (c) Then what is παρωξύνετο? Was roused: for the gift is far removed from anger and exasperation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:18
verses.text: He could not bear it, but pined away.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:19
verses.text: "He reasoned therefore in the synagogue," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:20
