Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:21
verses.text: ) Observe him again reasoning with Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:22
verses.text: By "devout persons" he means the proselytes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:23
verses.text: For the Jews were dispersed everywhere before (mod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:24
verses.text: text "since") Christ's coming, the Law indeed being henceforth, so to say, in process of dissolution, but at the same time (the dispersed Jews) teaching men religion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:25
verses.text: But those prevailed nothing, save only that they got witnesses of their own calamities.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:26
verses.text: (e) "And certain philosophers," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:28
verses.text: ) How came they to be willing to confer with him? (They did it) when they saw others reasoning, and the man having repute (in the encounter).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:29
verses.text: And observe straightway with overbearing insolence, "some said, What would this babbler say? For the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:30
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:31
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:32
verses.text: ) Other some, He seemeth to be a setter-forth of strange deities: δαιμονίων, for so they called their gods.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:33
verses.text: "And having taken him, they brought him," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:35
verses.text: ) (a) The Athenians no longer enjoyed their own laws, but were become subject to the Romans.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:36
verses.text: (g) (Then) why did they hale him to the Areopagus? Meaning to overawe him—(the place) where they held the trials for bloodshed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:37
verses.text: "May we know, what is this new doctrine spoken of by thee? For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears; we would fain know therefore what these things mean.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:38
verses.text: For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:41
verses.text: ) Here the thing noted is, that though ever occupied only in this telling and hearing, yet they thought those things strange—things which they had never heard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:42
verses.text: "Then Paul standing in the midst of the Areopagus said, Ye men of Athens, I look upon you as being in all things more religiously disposed" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:43
verses.text: ): (f) for the cities were full of gods (δαιμόνων, al.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:44
verses.text: εἰδώλων): (h) this is why he says δεισιδαιμονεστέρους.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:45
verses.text: For as I passed by and viewed the objects of your worship —he does not say simply τοὺς δαίμονας (the demons, or deities), but paves the way for his discourse: "I beheld an altar," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:47
verses.text: ) This is why he says, "I look upon you as being more religiously disposed," viz.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:48
verses.text: because of the altar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:49
verses.text: "God," he says, "that made the world".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:50
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:51
verses.text: ) He uttered one word, by which he has subverted all the (doctrines) of the philosophers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:52
verses.text: For the Epicureans affirm all to be fortuitously formed and (by concourse) of atoms, the Stoics held it to be body and fire (ἐκπύρωσιν).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:53
verses.text: "The world and all that is therein".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:54
verses.text: Do you mark the conciseness, and in conciseness, clearness? Mark what were the things that were strange to them: that God made the world! Things which now any of the most ordinary persons know, these the Athenians and the wise men of the Athenians knew not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:55
verses.text: "Seeing He is Lord of heaven and earth:" for if He made them, it is clear that He is Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:56
verses.text: Observe what he affirms to be the note of Deity—creation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:57
verses.text: Which attribute the Son also hath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:58
verses.text: For the Prophets everywhere affirm this, that to create is God's prerogative.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:59
verses.text: Not as those affirm that another is Maker but not Lord, assuming that matter is uncreated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:60
verses.text: Here now he covertly affirms and establishes his own, while he overthrows their doctrine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:61
verses.text: "Dwelleth not in temples made with hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:62
verses.text: For He does indeed dwell in temples, yet not in such, but in man's soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:63
verses.text: He overthrows the corporeal worship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:64
verses.text: What then? Did He not dwell in the temple at Jerusalem? No indeed: but He wrought therein.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:65
verses.text: "Neither is worshipped by men's hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:66
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:67
verses.text: ) How then was He worshipped by men's hands among the Jews? Not by hands, but by the understanding.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:68
verses.text: "As though He needed anything:" since even those (acts of worship) He did not in this sort seek, "as having need.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:69
verses.text: Shall I eat," saith He, "the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?" (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:70
verses.text: l.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:71
verses.text: ) Neither is this enough—the having need of naught—which he has affirmed: for though this is Divine, yet a further attribute must be added.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:72
verses.text: "Seeing it is He that giveth unto all, life and breath and all things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:73
verses.text: Two proofs of Godhead: Himself to have need of naught, and to supply all things to all men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:74
verses.text: Produce here Plato (and) all that he has philosophized about God, all that Epicurus has: and all is but trifling to this! "Giveth," he says, "life and breath".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:75
verses.text: Lo, he makes Him the Creator of the soul also, not its begetter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:76
verses.text: See again how he overthrows the doctrine about matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:77
verses.text: "And made," he says, "of one blood every nation of men to dwell upon all the face of the earth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:78
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:79
verses.text: ) These things are better than the former: and what an impeachment both of the atoms and of matter, that (creation) is not partial (work), nor the soul of man either.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:80
verses.text: But this, which those say, is not to be Creator.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:81
verses.text: —But by the mind and understanding He is worshipped.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:82
verses.text: —"It is He that giveth," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:83
verses.text: He not the partial (μερικοὶ δαίμονες) deities.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:84
verses.text: "And all things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:85
verses.text: It is "He," he saith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:86
verses.text: —How man also came into being.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:87
verses.text: —First he showed that "He dwelleth not," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:88
verses.text: , and then declared that He "is not worshipped as though He had need of aught".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:89
verses.text: If God, He made all: but if He made not, He is not God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:90
verses.text: Gods that made not heaven and earth, let them perish.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:91
verses.text: He introduces much greater doctrines, though as yet he does not mention the great doctrines; but he discoursed to them as unto children.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:92
verses.text: And these were much greater than those.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:93
verses.text: Creation, Lordship, the having need of naught, authorship of all good—these he has declared.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:94
verses.text: But how is He worshipped? say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:95
verses.text: It is not yet the proper time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:96
verses.text: What equal to this sublimity? Marvellous is this also—of one, to have made so many: but also, having made, Himself sustains them (συγκρατεἵ) in being, "giving life and breath and all things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:97
verses.text: (b) And hath determined the times appointed, and the bounds of their habitation, that they should seek God, if haply they might feel after Him and find Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:98
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:99
verses.text: ) (a) It means either this, that He did not compel them to go about and seek God, but according to the bounds of their habitation: (c) or this, that He determined their seeking God, yet not determined this (to be done) continually, but (determined) certain appointed times (when they should do so): showing now, that not having sought they had found: for since, having sought, they had not found, he shows that God was now as manifest as though He were in the midst of them palpably (ψηλαφώμενος).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:100
verses.text: (e) "Though He be not far," he saith, "from every one of us," but is near to all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:101
verses.text: See again the power (or, "what it is to be God,") of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:102
verses.text: What saith he? Not only He gave "life and breath and all things," but, as the sum and substance of all, He brought us to the knowledge of Himself, by giving us these things by which we are able to find and to apprehend Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:103
verses.text: But we did not wish to find Him, albeit close at hand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:104
verses.text: "Though He be not far from every one of us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:105
verses.text: Why look now, He is near to all, to every one all the world over! What can be greater than this? See how he makes clear riddance of the parcel deities (τοὺς μερικούς)! What say I, "afar off?" He is so near, that without Him we live not: "for in Him we live and move and have our being".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:106
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:107
verses.text: ) "In him;" to put it by way of corporeal similitude, even as it is impossible to be ignorant of the air which is diffused on every side around us, and is "not far from every one of us," nay rather, which is in us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:108
verses.text: (d) For it was not so that there was a heaven in one place, in another none, nor yet (a heaven) at one time, at another none.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:109
verses.text: So that both at every "time" and at every "bound" it was possible to find Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:110
verses.text: He so ordered things, that neither by place nor by time were men hindered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:111
verses.text: For of course even this, if nothing else, of itself was a help to them—that the heaven is in every place, that it stands in all time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:112
verses.text: (f) See how (he declares) His Providence, and His upholding power (συγκράτησιν); the existence of all things from Him, (from Him) their working (τὸ ἐνεργεἵν), (from Him their preservation) that they perish not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:113
verses.text: And he does not say, "Through Him," but, what was nearer than this, "In him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:114
verses.text: —That poet said nothing equal to this, "For we are His offspring".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:115
verses.text: He, however, spake it of Jupiter, but Paul takes it of the Creator, not meaning the same being as he, God forbid! but meaning what is properly predicated of God: just as he spoke of the altar with reference to Him, not to the being whom they worshipped.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:116
verses.text: As much as to say, "For certain things are said and done with reference to this (true God), but ye know not that they are with reference to Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:117
verses.text: For say, of whom would it be properly said, "To an Unknown God?" Of the Creator, or of the demon? Manifestly of the Creator: because Him they knew not, but the other they knew.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:118
verses.text: Again, that all things are filled (with the presence)—of God? or of Jupiter—a wretch of a man, a detestable impostor! But Paul said it not in the same sense as he, God forbid! but with quite a different meaning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:119
verses.text: For he says we are God's offspring, i-e: God's own, His nearest neighbors as it were.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:120
verses.text: For lest, when he says, "Being the offspring of God" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:121
verses.text: ), they should again say, Thou bringest certain strange things to our ears, he produces the poet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:122
verses.text: He does not say, "Ye ought not to think the Godhead like to gold or silver," ye accursed and execrable: but in more lowly sort he says, "We ought not".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:123
verses.text: For what (says he)? God is above this? No, he does not say this either: but for the present this—"We ought not to think the Godhead like unto such," for nothing is so opposite to men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:124
verses.text: "But we do not affirm the Godhead to be like unto this, for who would say that?" Mark how he has introduced the incorporeal (nature of God) when he said, "In Him," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:125
verses.text: , for the mind, when it surmises body, at the same time implies the notion of distance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:126
verses.text: (Speaking) to the many he says, "We ought not to think the Godhead like unto gold, or silver, or stone, the shaping of art," for if we are not like to those as regards the soul, much more God (is not like to such).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:127
verses.text: So far, he withdraws them from the notion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:128
verses.text: But neither is the Godhead, he would say, subjected to any other human conception.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:129
verses.text: For if that which art or thought has found—this is why he says it thus, "of art or imagination of man"—if that, then, which human art or thought has found, is God, then even in the stone (is) God's essence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:130
verses.text: —How comes it then, if "in Him we live," that we do not find Him? The charge is twofold, both that they did not find Him, and that they found such as these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:131
verses.text: The (human) understanding in itself is not at all to be relied upon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:132
verses.text: —But when he has agitated their soul by showing them to be without excuse, see what he says: "The times of ignorance God overlooked, but now commands all men everywhere to repent".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:133
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:134
verses.text: ) What then? Are none of these men to be punished? None of them that are willing to repent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:135
verses.text: He says it of these men, not of the departed, but of them whom He commands to repent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:136
verses.text: He does not call you to account, he would say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:137
verses.text: He does not say, Took no notice (παρεἵδεν); does not say, Permitted: but, Ye were ignorant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:138
verses.text: "Overlooked," i-e: does not demand punishment as of men that deserve punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:139
verses.text: Ye were ignorant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:140
verses.text: And he does not say, Ye wilfully did evil; but this he showed by what he said above.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:141
verses.text: —"All men everywhere to repent:" again he hints at the whole world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:142
verses.text: Observe how he takes them off from the parcel deities! "Because He has appointed a day, in the which He will judge the world in righteousness by that Man whom He hath ordained, whereof He hath given assurance to all men, in that He raised Him from the dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:143
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:144
verses.text: ) Observe how he again declares the Passion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:145
verses.text: Observe the terror again: for, that the judgment is true, is clear from the raising Him up: for it is alleged in proof of that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:146
verses.text: That all he has been saying is true, is clear from the fact that He rose again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:147
verses.text: For He did give this "assurance to all men," His rising from the dead: this (i-e: judgment), also is henceforth certain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:148
verses.text: These words were spoken indeed to the Athenians: but it were seasonable that one should say to us also, "that all men everywhere must repent, because he hath appointed a day, in the which He will judge the world".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:149
verses.text: See how he brings Him in as Judge also: Him, both provident for the world, and merciful and forgiving and powerful and wise, and, in a word possessing all the attributes of a Creator.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:150
verses.text: "Having given assurance to all men," i-e: He has given proof in the rising (of Jesus) from the dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:151
verses.text: Let us repent then: for we must assuredly be judged.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:152
verses.text: If Christ rose not, we shall not be judged: but if he rose, we shall without doubt be judged.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:153
verses.text: "For to this end," it is said, "did He also die, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:154
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:155
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:156
verses.text: ) "For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ, that every one may receive according to that he hath done".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:157
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:158
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:159
verses.text: , and  Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:160
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:161
verses.text: ) Do not imagine that these are but words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:162
verses.text: Lo! he introduced also the subject of the resurrection of all men; for in no other way can the world be judged.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:163
verses.text: And that, "In that He hath raised Him from the dead," relates to the body: for that was dead, that had fallen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:164
verses.text: Among the Greeks, as their notions of Creation, so likewise of the Judgment, are children's fancies, ravings of drunken men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:165
verses.text: But let us, who know these things accurately, do something that is to the purpose: let us be made friends unto God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:166
verses.text: How long shall we be at enmity with Him? How long shall we entertain dislike towards Him? "God forbid!" you will say: "Why do you say such things?" I would wish not to say the things I say, if ye did not do the things ye do: but as things are, what is the use now in keeping silence from words, when the plain evidence of deeds so cries aloud? How then, how shall we love Him? I have told you thousands of ways, thousands of times: but I will speak it also now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:167
verses.text: One way I seem to myself to have discovered, a very great and admirable way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:168
verses.text: Namely, after acknowledging to Him our general obligations,—what none shall be able to express (I mean), what has been done for each of us in his own person, of these also let us bethink ourselves, because these are of great force: let each one of us reckon them up with himself, and make diligent search, and as it were in a book let him have the benefits of God written down; for instance, if at any time having fallen into dangers he has escaped the hands of his enemies; if ever having gone out on a journey at an untimely hour, he has escaped danger; if ever, having had an encounter with wicked men, he has got the better of them; or if ever, having fallen into sickness, he has recovered when all had given him over: for this avails much for attaching us to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:169
verses.text: For if that Mordecai, when the services done by him were brought to the king's remembrance, found them to be so available, that he in return rose to that height of splendor (Esther vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:170
verses.text: –): much more we, if we call to mind, and make diligent enquiry of these two points, what sins we have committed against God, and what good He has done to us, shall thus both be thankful, and give Him freely all that is ours.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:171
verses.text: But no one gives a thought to any of these things: but just as regarding our sins we say that we are sinners, while we do not enquire into them specifically, so with regard to God's benefits (we say), that God has done us good, and do not specifically enquire, where, and in how great number and at what time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:172
verses.text: But from this time forth let us be very exact in our reckoning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:173
verses.text: For if any one can recall even those things which happened long ago, let him reckon up all accurately, as one who will find a great treasure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:174
verses.text: This is also profitable to us in keeping us from despair.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:175
verses.text: For when we see that he has often protected us, we shall not despair, nor suppose that we are cast off: but we shall take it as a strong pledge of His care for us, when we bethink us how, though we have sinned, we are not punished, but even enjoy protection from Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:176
verses.text: Let me now tell you a case, which I heard from a certain person, in which was a child, and it happened on a time that he was in the country with his mother, being not yet fifteen years old.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:177
verses.text: Just then there came a bad air, in consequence of which a fever attacked them both, for in fact it was the autumn season.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:178
verses.text: It happened that the mother succeeded in getting into the town before (they could stop her); but the boy, when the physicians on the spot ordered him, with the fever burning within him, to gargle his throat, resisted, having forsooth his own wise view of the matter, and thinking he should be better able to quench the fire, if he took nothing whatever, therefore, in his unseasonable spirit of opposition, boy-like, he would take nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:179
verses.text: But when he came into the town, his tongue was paralyzed, and he was for a long time speechless, so that he could pronounce nothing articulately; however, he could read indeed, and attended masters for a long time, but that was all, and there was nothing to mark his progress.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:180
verses.text: So all his hopes (in life) were cut off, and his mother was full of grief: and though the physicians suggested many plans, and many others did so too, yet nobody was able to do him any good, until the merciful God loosed the string of his tongue (cf.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:181
verses.text: Mark vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:182
verses.text: ), and then he recovered, and was restored to his former readiness and distinctness of speech.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:183
verses.text: His mother also related, that when a very little child, he had an affection in the nose, which they call a polypus: and then too the physicians had given him over and his father cursed him (for the father was then living), and (even) his mother prayed for him to die; and all was full of distress.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:184
verses.text: But he on a sudden having coughed, owing to the collection of mucus, by the force of the breath expelled the creature (τὸ θηρίον) from his nostrils, and all the danger was removed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:185
verses.text: But this evil having been extinguished, an acrid and viscid running from the eyes formed such a thick gathering of the humors (τὰς λήμας), that it was like a skin drawn over the pupil, and what was worse, it threatened blindness, and everybody said this would be the issue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:186
verses.text: But from this disease also was he quickly freed by the grace of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:187
verses.text: So far what I have heard from others: now I will tell you what I myself know.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:188
verses.text: Once on a time a suspicion of tyrants was raised in our city—at that time I was but a youth—and all the soldiers being set to watch without the city as it chanced, they were making strict inquisition after books of sorcery and magic.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:189
verses.text: And the person who had written the book, had flung it unbound (ἀκατασκέυαστον) into the river, and was taken, and when asked for it, was not able to give it up, but was carried all around the city in bonds: when, however, the evidence being brought home to him, he had suffered punishment, just then it chanced that I, wishing to go to the Martyrs' Church, was returning through the gardens by the riverside in company with another person.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:190
verses.text: He, seeing the book floating on the water at first thought it was a linen cloth, but when he got near, perceived it was a book, so he went down, and took it up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:191
verses.text: I however called shares in the booty, and laughed about it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:192
verses.text: But let us see, says he, what in the world it is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:193
verses.text: So he turns back a part of the page, and finds the contents to be magic.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 105:194
verses.text: At that very moment it chanced that a soldier came by:.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:1
verses.text: then having taken from within, he went off.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:2
verses.text: There were we congealed with fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:3
verses.text: For who would have believed our story that we had picked it up from the river, when all were at that time, even the unsuspected, under strict watch? And we did not dare to cast it away, lest we should be seen, and there was a like danger to us in tearing it to pieces.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:4
verses.text: God gave us means, and we cast it away, and at last we were free for that time from the extreme peril.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:5
verses.text: And I might mention numberless cases, if I had a mind to recount all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:6
verses.text: And even these I have mentioned for your sakes, so that, if any have other cases, although not such as these, let him bear them in mind constantly: for example, if at any time a stone having been hurled, and being about to strike thee, has not struck thee, do thou bear this ever in thy mind: these things produce in us great affection towards God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:7
verses.text: For if on remembering any men who have been the means of saving us, we are much mortified if we be not able to requite them, much more (should we feel thus) with regard to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:8
verses.text: This too is useful in other respects.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:9
verses.text: When we wish not to be overmuch grieved, let us say: "If we have received good things at the hand of the Lord, shall not we endure evil things?" (Job ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:10
verses.text: ) And when Paul told them from whence he had been delivered, ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:11
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:12
verses.text: ) the reason was that he might put them also in mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:13
verses.text: See too how Jacob kept all these things in his mind: wherefore also he said: "The Angel which redeemed me from my youth up" (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:14
verses.text: xlviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:15
verses.text: ); and not only that he redeemed him, but how and for what purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:16
verses.text: See accordingly how he also calls to mind the benefits he had received in particular.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:17
verses.text: "With my staff," he says, "I passed over Jordan".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:18
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:19
verses.text: xxxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:20
verses.text: ) The Jews also always remembered the things which happened to their forefathers, turning over in their minds the things done in Egypt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 108:21
verses.text: Then much more let us, bearing in mind the special mercies which have happened to us also, how often we have fallen into dangers and calamities, and unless God had held his hand over us, should long ago have perished: I say, let us all, considering these things and recounting them day by day, return our united thanks all of us to God, and never cease to glorify Him, that so we may receive a large recompense for our thankfulness of heart, through the grace and compassion of His only begotten Son, with Whom to the Father, together with the Holy Ghost, be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:1
verses.text: Homily XXXIX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:2
verses.text: Acts XVII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:3
verses.text: –, XVIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:4
verses.text: "And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:5
verses.text: So Paul departed from among them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:6
verses.text: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:7
verses.text: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:8
verses.text: What can be the reason that, having persuaded (some so far as to say) that they would hear him again, and there being no dangers, Paul is so in haste to leave Athens? Probably he knew that he should do them no great good; moreover he was led by the Spirit to Corinth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:9
verses.text: (b) For the Athenians, although fond of hearing strange things, nevertheless did not attend (to him); for this was not their study, but only to be always having something to say; which was the cause that made them hold off from him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:10
verses.text: But if this was their custom, how is it that they accuse him, "he seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods?" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:11
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:12
verses.text: ) Yes, but these were matters they did not at all know what to make of.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:13
verses.text: Howbeit, he did convert both Dionysius the Areopagite, and some others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:14
verses.text: For those who were careful of (right) living, quickly received the word; but the others not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:15
verses.text: It seemed to Paul sufficient to have cast the seeds of the doctrines.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:16
verses.text: (a) To Corinth then, as I said, he was led by the Spirit, in which city he was to abide.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:17
verses.text: (c) "And having found a certain Jew named Aquila, of Pontus by birth, lately come from Italy"—for the greater part of his life had been passed there—"and Priscilla his wife, because that Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:19
verses.text: ) For though it was in the reign of Nero that the war against the Jews was consummated, yet from the time of Claudius and thenceforward it was fanning up, at a distance indeed, so that, were it but so, they might come to their senses, and from Rome they were now driven as common pests.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:20
verses.text: This is why it is so ordered by Providence that Paul was led thither as a prisoner, that he might not as a Jew be driven away, but as acting under military custody might even be guarded there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:21
verses.text: (Having found these,) "he came to them, and because he was of the same craft, he abode with them and wrought: for by occupation they were tent-makers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:23
verses.text: ) Lo, what a justification he found for dwelling in the same house with them! For because here, of all places, it was necessary that he should not receive, as he himself says, "That wherein they glory, they may be found, even as we" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:24
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:25
verses.text: ), it is providentially ordered that he there abides.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:26
verses.text: "And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:27
verses.text: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was straitened in the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:28
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:30
verses.text: ) "And when the Jews opposed and blasphemed," i-e: they tried to bear him down (ἐπηρέαζον), they set upon him—What then does Paul? He separates from them, and in a very awful manner: and though he does not now say, "It was need that the word should be spoken unto you," yet he darkly intimates it to them:—"and when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:32
verses.text: ) "And he departed thence, and entered into a certain man's house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:33
verses.text: See how having again said, "Henceforth—" for all that, he does not neglect them; so that it was to rouse them that he said this, and thereupon came to Justus, whose house was contiguous to the synagogue, so that even from this they might have jealousy, from the very proximity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:34
verses.text: "And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:35
verses.text: This also was, of all things, enough to bring them over.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:36
verses.text: "And many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:37
verses.text: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace: for I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:40
verses.text: ) See by how many reasons He persuades him, and how He puts last the reason which of all others most prevailed with him, "I have much people in this city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:41
verses.text: Then how was it, you may ask, that they set upon him? And yet, the writer tells us, they prevailed nothing, but brought him to the proconsul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:42
verses.text: "And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:43
verses.text: And when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment-seat".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:44
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:45
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:46
verses.text: ) Do you mark why those men were ever contriving to give a public turn to the misdemeanors (they accused them of)? Thus see here: (b) "Saying, This fellow seduceth men contrary to the law to worship God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:47
verses.text: And when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said: If indeed it were any wrong-doing or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:48
verses.text: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it; for I will be no judge of such matters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:49
verses.text: And he drave them from the judgment-seat".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:50
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:52
verses.text: ) This Gallio seems to me to have been a sensible man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:53
verses.text: (a) Thus observe, when these had said, "Against the law he seduceth men to worship God," he "cared for none of these things:" and observe how he answers them: "If indeed it were" any matter affecting the city, "any wrong-doing or wicked lewdness," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:54
verses.text: (c) "Then all the Jews took Sosthenes the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment-seat: and Gallio cared for none of these things" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:55
verses.text: ): but their beating him he did not take as an insult to himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:56
verses.text: So petulant were the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:57
verses.text: But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:58
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:59
verses.text: ) "And when they heard," (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:60
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:61
verses.text: ) what great and lofty doctrines, they did not even attend, but jeered at the Resurrection! "For the natural man," it saith, "receiveth not the things of the Spirit".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:62
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:63
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:64
verses.text: ) "And so," it says, "Paul went forth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:65
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:66
verses.text: ) How? Having persuaded some; derided by others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:67
verses.text: "But certain men," it says, "clave unto him, and believed, among whom was also Dionysius the Areopagite and some others".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:68
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:69
verses.text: ) "And after these things," etc.

verses.text: (ch.

verses.text: xviii.

Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 109:74

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:1
verses.text: Observe how, not in Jerusalem, nor near it (the crisis), was hasting to come, but at a greater distance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:2
verses.text: And with him he abides, and is not ashamed to abide, nay, for this very reason he does abide, as having a suitable lodging-place, for to him it was much more suitable than any king's palace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:3
verses.text: And smile not thou, beloved, to hear (of his occupation).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:4
verses.text: For (it was good for him) even as to the athlete the palaestra is more useful than delicate carpets; so to the warrior the iron sword (is useful), not that of gold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:5
verses.text: "And wrought," though he preached.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:6
verses.text: Let us be ashamed, who though we have no preaching to occupy us, live in idleness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:7
verses.text: "And he disputed in the synagogue every sabbath day, and persuaded both Jews and Greeks" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:8
verses.text: ): but "when they opposed and blasphemed" he withdrew, by this expecting to draw them more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:9
verses.text: For wherefore having left that house did he come to live hard by the synagogue? was it not for this? For it was not that he saw any danger here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:10
verses.text: But therefore it is that Paul having testified to them—not teaches now, but testifies—"having shaken his garments," to terrify them not by word only but by action, "said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:11
verses.text: ): he speaks the more vehemently as having already persuaded many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:12
verses.text: "I," says he, "am clean".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:13
verses.text: Then we also are accountable for the blood of those entrusted to us, if we neglect them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:14
verses.text: "From this time forth I will go to the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:15
verses.text: So that also when he says, "Henceforth let no man trouble me" (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:16
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:17
verses.text: ), he says it to terrify.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:18
verses.text: For not so much did the punishment terrify, as this stung them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:19
verses.text: "And having removed thence he came into the house of one named Justus, that worshipped God, whose house was contiguous to the synagogue" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:20
verses.text: ), and there abode, by this wishing to persuade them that he was in earnest (πρὸς τὰ ἐθνη ἠπείγετο) to go to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:21
verses.text: Accordingly, mark immediately the ruler of the synagogue converted, and many others, when he had done this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:22
verses.text: "Crispus the ruler of the synagogue believed in the Lord, with his whole house: and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:23
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:24
verses.text: ) "With his whole house:" observe the converts in those times doing this with their entire household.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:25
verses.text: This Crispus he means where he writes, "I baptized none save Crispus and Gaius".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:26
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:27
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:28
verses.text: ) This (same) I take to be called Sosthenes—(evidently) a believer, insomuch that he is beaten, and is always present with Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:29
verses.text: "And the Lord said in the night," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:30
verses.text: Now even the number (of the "much people") persuaded him, but Christ's claiming them for His own (moved him) more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:31
verses.text: Yet He says also, "Fear not:" for the danger was become greater now, both because more believed, and also the ruler of the synagogue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:32
verses.text: This was enough to rouse him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:33
verses.text: Not that he was reproved as fearing; but that he should not suffer aught; "I am with thee, and none shall set upon thee to hurt thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:36
verses.text: ) For He did not always permit them to suffer evil, that they might not become too weak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:37
verses.text: For nothing so grieved Paul, as men's unbelief and setting themselves (against the Truth): this was worse than the dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:38
verses.text: Therefore it is that (Christ) appears to him now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:39
verses.text: "And he continued a year and six months," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:41
verses.text: ) After the year and six months, they set upon him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:42
verses.text: "And when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:43
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:44
verses.text: , ), because they had no longer the use of their own laws.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:45
verses.text: (c) And observe how prudent he is: for he does not say straightway, I care not, but, "If," says he, "it were a matter of wrong-doing or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you; but if it be a question of doctrine and words and of your law, see ye to it, for I do not choose to be a judge of such matters".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:48
verses.text: ) (g) He taught them that not such are the matters which crave a judicial sentence, but they do all things out of order.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:49
verses.text: And he does not say, It is not my duty, but, "I do not choose," that they may not trouble him again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:50
verses.text: Thus Pilate said in the case of Christ, "Take ye Him, and judge him according to your law".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:51
verses.text: (John xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:52
verses.text: ) But they were just like men drunken and mad.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:53
verses.text: (d) "And he drave them from the judgment-seat" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:54
verses.text: )—he effectually closed the tribunal against them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:55
verses.text: "Then all" (the Jews) "having seized Sosthenes the ruler of the synagogue, beat him before the judgment-seat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:56
verses.text: And Gallio cared for none of these things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:57
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:59
verses.text: (a) This thing, of all others, set them on (to this violence)—their persuasion that the governor would not even let himself down (to notice it).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:60
verses.text: (e) It was a splendid victory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:61
verses.text: O the shame they were put to! (b) For it is one thing to have come off victorious from a controversy, and another for those to learn that he cared nothing for the affair.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:62
verses.text: (f) "And Gallio cared for none of these things:" and yet the whole was meant as an insult to him! But, forsooth, as if they had received authority (they did this).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:63
verses.text: Why did he (Sosthenes), though he also had authority, not beat (them)? But they were (otherwise) trained: so that the judge should learn which party was more reasonable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:64
verses.text: This was no small benefit to those present—both the reasonableness of these, and the audacity of those.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:65
verses.text: (h) He was beaten, and said nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:66
verses.text: This man let us also imitate: to them that beat us, let us return blow for blow, by meekness, by silence, by long-suffering.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:67
verses.text: More grievous these wounds, greater this blow, and more heavy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:68
verses.text: For to show that it is not the receiving a blow in the body that is grievous, but the receiving it in the mind, we often smite people, but since it is in the way of friendship, they are even pleased: but if you smite any indifferent person in an insolent manner, you have pained him exceedingly, because you have touched his heart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:69
verses.text: So let us smite their heart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:70
verses.text: But that meekness inflicts a greater blow than fierceness, come, let us prove, so far as that is possible, by words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:71
verses.text: For the sure proof indeed is by acts and by experience: but if you will, let us also make the enquiry by word, though indeed we have often made it already.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:72
verses.text: Now in insults, nothing pains us so much, as the opinion passed by the spectators; for it is not the same thing to be insulted in public and in private, but those same insults we endure even with ease, when we suffer them in a solitary place, and with none by to witness them, or know of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:73
verses.text: So true is it that it is not the insult, as it is in itself, that mortifies us, but the having to suffer it in the sight of all men: since if one should do us honor in the sight of all men, and insult us in private, we shall notwithstanding even feel obliged to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:74
verses.text: The pain then is not in the nature of the insult, but in the opinion of the beholders; that one may not seem to be contemptible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:75
verses.text: What then, if this opinion should be in our favor? Is not the man attempting to disgrace us himself more disgraced, when men give their opinion in our favor? Say, whom do the bystanders despise? Him who insults, or him who being insulted keeps silence? Passion indeed suggests, that they despise him who is insulted: but let us look into it now while we are free from that excitement, in order that we may not be carried away when the time comes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:76
verses.text: Say, whom do we all condemn? Plainly the man who insults: and if he be an inferior, we shall say that he is even mad; if an equal, that he is foolish; if a superior, still we shall not approve of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:77
verses.text: For which man, I ask, is worthy of approval, the man who is excited, who is tossed with a tempest of passion, who is infuriated like a wild beast, who demeans himself in this sort against our common nature, or he who lives in a state of calm, in a haven of repose, and in virtuous equanimity? Is not the one like an angel, the other not even like a man? For the one cannot even bear his own evils, while the other bears even those of others also: here, the man cannot even endure himself; there, he endures another too: the one is in danger of shipwreck, the other sails in safety, his ship wafted along the favoring gales: for he has not suffered the squall of passion to catch his sails and overturn the bark of his understanding: but the breath of a soft and sweet air fanning upon it, the breath of forbearance, wafts it with much tranquillity into the haven of wise equanimity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:78
verses.text: And like as when a ship is in danger of foundèring, the sailors know not what they cast away, whether what they lay hands upon be their own or other men's property, but they throw overboard all the contents without discrimination, alike the precious and what is not such: but when the storm has ceased, then reckoning up all that they have thrown out, they shed tears, and are not sensible of the calm for the loss of what they have thrown overboard: so here, when passion blows hard, and the storm is raised, people in flinging out their words know not how to use order or fitness; but when the passion has ceased, then recalling to mind what kind of words they have given utterance to, they consider the loss and feel not the quiet, when they remember the words by which they have disgraced themselves, and sustained most grievous loss, not as to money, but as to character for moderation and gentleness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:79
verses.text: Anger is a darkness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:80
verses.text: "The fool," saith Scripture, "hath said in his heart, There is no God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:81
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:82
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:83
verses.text: ) Perhaps also of the angry man it is suitable to say the same, that the angry man hath said, There is no God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:84
verses.text: For, saith Scripture, "Through the multitude of his anger he will not seek" (after God).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:85
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:86
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:87
verses.text: ) For let what pious thought will enter in, (passion) thrusts and drives all out, flings all athwart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:88
verses.text: (b) When you are told, that he whom you abused uttered not one bitter word, do you not for this feel more pain than you have inflicted? (a) If you in your own mind do not feel more pain than he whom you have abused, abuse still; (but) though there be none to call you to account, the judgment of your conscience, having taken you privately, shall give you a thousand lashes, (when you think) how you poured out a flood of railings on one so meek, and humble, and forbearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:89
verses.text: We are forever saying these things, but we do not see them exhibited in works.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:90
verses.text: You, a human being, insult your fellow-man? You, a servant, your fellow-servant? But why do I wonder at this, when many even insult God? Let this be a consolation to you when suffering insult.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:91
verses.text: Are you insulted? God also is insulted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:92
verses.text: Are you reviled? God also was reviled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:93
verses.text: Are you treated with scorn? Why, so was our Master also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:94
verses.text: In these things He shares with us, but not so in the contrary things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:95
verses.text: For He never insulted another unjustly: God forbid! He never reviled, never did a wrong.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:96
verses.text: So that we are those who share with Him, not ye.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:97
verses.text: For to endure when insulted is God's part: to be merely abusive, is the part of the devil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:98
verses.text: See the two sides.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:99
verses.text: "Thou hast a devil" (John vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:100
verses.text: ; ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:101
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:102
verses.text: ), Christ was told: He received a blow on the face from the servant of the high-priest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:103
verses.text: They who wrongfully insult, are in the same class with these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:104
verses.text: For if Peter was even called "Satan" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:105
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:106
verses.text: ) for one word; much more shall these men, when they do the works of the Jews, be called, as those were called, "children of the devil" (John viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:107
verses.text: ), because they wrought the works of the devil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:108
verses.text: You insult; who are you, I ask (that you do so)? Nay, rather the reason why you insult, is this, that you are nothing: no one that is human insults.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:109
verses.text: So that what is said in quarrels, "Who are you?" ought to be put in the contrary way: "Insult: for you are nothing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:110
verses.text: Instead of that the phrase is, "Who are you, that you insult?" "A better man than you," is the answer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:111
verses.text: And yet it is just the contrary: but because we put the question amiss, therefore they answer amiss: so that the fault is ours.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:112
verses.text: For as if we thought it was for great men to insult, therefore we ask, "Who are you, that you insult?" And therefore they make this answer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:113
verses.text: But, on the contrary, we ought to say: "Do you insult? insult still: for you are nobody:" whereas to those who do not insult this should be said: "Who are you that you insult not?—you have surpassed human nature".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:114
verses.text: This is nobility, this is generosity, to speak nothing ungenerous, though a man may deserve to have it spoken to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:115
verses.text: Tell me now, how many are there who are not worthy to be put to death? Nevertheless, the judge does not this in his own person, but interrogates them; and not this either, in his own person.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:116
verses.text: But if it is not to be suffered, that the judge, sitting in judgment, should (in his own person) speak with a criminal, but he does all by the intervention of a third person, much more is it our duty not to insult our equals in rank; for all the advantage we shall get of them will be, not so much to have disgraced them, as to be made to learn that we have disgraced ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:117
verses.text: Well then, in the case of the wicked, this is why we must not insult (even them); in the case of the good there is another reason also because they do not deserve it: and for a third, because it is not right to be abusive.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:118
verses.text: But as things are, see what comes of it; the person abused is a man, and the person abusing is a man, and the spectators men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:119
verses.text: What then? must the beasts come between them and settle matters? for only this is left.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:120
verses.text: For when both the wrong-doers and those who delight in the wrong-doing are men, the part of reconciler is left for the beasts: for just as when the masters quarrel in a house, there is nothing left but for the servants to reconcile them,—even if this be not the result, for the nature of the thing demands this,—just so is it here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:121
verses.text: —Are you abusive? Well may you be so, for you are not even human.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:122
verses.text: Insolence seemed to be a high-born thing; it seemed to belong to the great; whereas it belongs rather to slaves; but to give good words belongs to free men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:123
verses.text: For as to do ill is the part of those, so to suffer ill is the part of these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:124
verses.text: —Just as if some slave should steal the master's property, some old hag,—such a thing as that is the abusive man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:125
verses.text: And like as some detestable thief and runaway, with studied purpose stealing in, looks all around him, wishing to filch something: so does this man, even as he, look narrowly at all on every side, studying how to throw out some (reproach).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:126
verses.text: Or perhaps we may set him forth by a different sort of example.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:127
verses.text: Just as if one should steal filthy vessels out of a house, and bring them out in the presence of all men, the things purloined do not so disgrace the persons robbed, as they disgrace the thief himself: just so this man, by bringing out his words in the presence of all men, casts disgrace not on others but on himself by the words, in giving vent to this language, and be-fouling both his tongue and his mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:128
verses.text: For it is all one, when we quarrel with bad men, as if one for the sake of striking a man who is immersed in putrefying filth should defile himself by plunging his hands into the nastiness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 112:129
verses.text: Therefore, reflecting on these things, let us flee the mischief thence accruing, and keep a clean tongue, that being clear from all abusiveness, we may be enabled with strictness to pass through the life present, and to attain unto the good things promised to those that love Him, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113

verses.text: Homily XL.
