verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:3
verses.text: "And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:4
verses.text: See how the Law was breaking up; see how they were bound by conscience.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:5
verses.text: This, namely, was a Jewish custom, to shear their heads agreeably with a vow.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:6
verses.text: But then there ought to be also a sacrifice (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:7
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:8
verses.text: ), which was not the case here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:9
verses.text: —"Having yet tarried:" after the beating of Sosthenes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:10
verses.text: For it was necessary that he should yet tarry, and comfort them concerning these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:11
verses.text: "He sailed for Syria".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:12
verses.text: Why does he desire again to come to Syria? It was there that "the disciples were ordered to be called Christians" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:13
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:14
verses.text: ): there, that he had been "commended to the grace of God" (xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:15
verses.text: ): there, that he had effected such things concerning the doctrine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:16
verses.text: "And with him Priscilla"—lo, a woman also—"and Aquila".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:17
verses.text: But these he left at Ephesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:18
verses.text: With good reason, namely, that they should teach.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:19
verses.text: For having been with him so long time, they were learning many things: and yet he did not at present withdraw them from their custom as Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:20
verses.text: "And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:21
verses.text: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not; but bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:22
verses.text: Therefore it was that he was hindered from coming into Asia, being impelled to what was of pressing moment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:23
verses.text: Thus observe him here, entreated (by them) to stay, but because he could not comply, being in haste to depart, "he bade them farewell".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:24
verses.text: However, he did not leave them without more ado, but with promise (to return): "But I will return again unto you, if God will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:25
verses.text: And he sailed from Ephesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:28
verses.text: ) "And when he had landed at Caesarea, and gone up, and saluted the Church, he went down to Antioch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:29
verses.text: And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:30
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:32
verses.text: ) He came again to those places which he had previously visited.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:33
verses.text: "And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the Scriptures, came to Ephesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:35
verses.text: ) Lo, even learned men are now urgent, and the disciples henceforth go abroad.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:36
verses.text: Do you mark the spread of the preaching? "This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the Spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:37
verses.text: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:40
verses.text: ) If this man knew only the baptism of John, how is it that he was "fervent in the Spirit," for the Spirit was not given in that way? And if those after him needed the baptism of Christ, much more would he need it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:41
verses.text: Then what is to be said? For it is not without a meaning that the writer has strung the two incidents together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:42
verses.text: It seems to me that this was one of the hundred and twenty who were baptized with the Apostles: or, if not so, then the same that took place in the case of Cornelius, took place also in the case of this man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:43
verses.text: But neither does he receive baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:44
verses.text: That expression, then, "they expounded more perfectly," seems to me to be this, that he behooved also to be baptized.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:45
verses.text: Because the other twelve knew nothing accurate, not even what related to Jesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:46
verses.text: And it is likely that he did in fact receive baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:47
verses.text: But if these (disciples) of John, after that baptism again received baptism, was this needful for the disciples also? And wherefore the need of water? These are very different from him, men who did not even know whether there were a Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:48
verses.text: "He was fervent," then, "in the Spirit, knowing only the baptism of John:" but these "expounded to him more perfectly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:49
verses.text: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him; who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:50
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:51
verses.text: ) He wished then also to depart into Achaia, and these also encouraged (him to do so), having also given him letters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:52
verses.text: "Who when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace: for he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publicly, showing by the Scriptures that Jesus was Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:54
verses.text: ) "And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper coasts"—meaning what we have read as to Caesarea and the other places—"came to Ephesus, and having found certain disciples (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:55
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:56
verses.text: ), "he said to them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:57
verses.text: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:58
verses.text: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on Him who should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:59
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:60
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:61
verses.text: ) For that they did not even believe in Christ is plain from his saying, "that they should believe on Him that was to come after him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:62
verses.text: And he did not say, The baptism of John is nothing, but, It is incomplete.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:63
verses.text: Nor does he add this (in so many words), but he taught them, and many received the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:64
verses.text: "When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:65
verses.text: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:66
verses.text: And all the men were about twelve" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:67
verses.text: –): so that it was likely they had the Spirit, but it did not appear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:68
verses.text: "And all the men were about twelve".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:69
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:70
verses.text: ) "And they came to Ephesus, and there he left them" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:71
verses.text: ): for he did not wish to take them about with him, but left them at Ephesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:72
verses.text: But they subsequently dwelt at Corinth, and he bears high testimony to them, and writing to the Romans, salutes them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:73
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:74
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:75
verses.text: ) Whence it seems to me that they afterwards went back to Rome, in the time of Nero, as having an attachment for those parts whence they had been expelled in the time of Claudius.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:76
verses.text: "But he himself went into the synagogue".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:77
verses.text: It seems to me that the faithful still assembled there, for they did not immediately withdraw them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:78
verses.text: "And when they besought him to stay, he consented not" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:79
verses.text: , ), for he was hastening to Caesarea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:80
verses.text: "And having arrived at Caesarea," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:81
verses.text: , "passing through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, confirming all the disciples".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:82
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:83
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:84
verses.text: ) Through these regions also he merely passes again, just enough to establish them by his presence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:85
verses.text: "And a certain Jew, Apollos by name," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:86
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:87
verses.text: ) For he was an awakened man, travelling in foreign parts for this very purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:88
verses.text: Writing of him the Apostle said, "Now concerning Apollos our brother".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:89
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:90
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:91
verses.text: ) (β) "Whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:92
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:93
verses.text: ) It was not for nothing that he left them at Ephesus, but for Apollos' sake, the Spirit so ordered it, that he might come with greater force to the attack (ἑπιβἥναι) upon Corinth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:94
verses.text: What may be the reason that to him they did nothing, but Paul they assault? They knew that he was the leader, and great was the name of the man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:95
verses.text: "And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:96
verses.text: ) i-e: in faith, he did all by faith; "the brethren wrote," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:97
verses.text: nowhere envy, nowhere an evil eye.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:98
verses.text: Aquila teaches, or rather this man lets himself be taught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:99
verses.text: He was minded to depart, and they send letters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:100
verses.text: (a) "For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publicly," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:101
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:102
verses.text: ) Now by this, that he "publicly" convinced them, his boldness was shown: by the clearness of his arguing, his power was declared: by his convicting them out of the Scriptures, his skill (of learning).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:103
verses.text: For neither boldness by itself contributes aught, where there is not power, nor power where there is not boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:104
verses.text: "He mightily convinced," it says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:105
verses.text: (β) "And it came to pass," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:106
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:107
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:108
verses.text: ) But whence had those, being in Ephesus, the baptism of John? Probably they had been on a visit at Jerusalem at the time (of John's preaching), and did not even know Jesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:109
verses.text: And he does not say to them, Do ye believe in Jesus? but what? "Have ye received the Holy Ghost?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:110
verses.text: ) He knew that they had not, but wishes themselves to say it, that having learnt what they lack, they may ask.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:111
verses.text: "John verily baptized," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:112
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:113
verses.text: ) From the baptism itself he (John) prophesies: and he leads them (to see) that this is the meaning of John's baptism.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:114
verses.text: (a) "That they should believe on Him that was to come:" on what kind (of Person)? "I indeed baptize you with water, but He that cometh after me, shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:115
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:116
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:117
verses.text: ) "And when Paul," it says, "had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:118
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:119
verses.text: ) (β) The gift is twofold: tongues and prophesyings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:120
verses.text: Hence is shown an important doctrine, that the baptism of John is incomplete.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:121
verses.text: And he does not say, "Baptism" of forgiveness, but, "of repentance".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:122
verses.text: What (is it) then? These had not the Spirit: they were not so fervent, not even instructed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:123
verses.text: And why did (Apollos) not receive baptism? (The case) seems to me to be this: Great was the boldness of the man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:124
verses.text: "He taught diligently the things concerning Jesus," but he needed more diligent teaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:125
verses.text: Thus, though not knowing all, by his zeal he attracted the Holy Ghost, in the same manner as Cornelius and his company.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:126
verses.text: Perhaps it is the wish of many, Oh that we had the baptism of John now! But (if we had), many would still be careless of a life of virtue, and it might be thought that each for this, and not for the kingdom of heaven's sake, aimed at virtue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:127
verses.text: There would be many false prophets: for then "they which are approved" would not be very "manifest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:128
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:129
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:130
verses.text: ) As, "blessed are they that have not seen and yet have believed" (John xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:131
verses.text: ), so they that (believe) without signs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:132
verses.text: "Except," saith (Christ), "ye see signs, ye will not believe".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:133
verses.text: (Ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:134
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:135
verses.text: ) For we lose nothing (by lack of miracles), if we will but take heed to ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:136
verses.text: We have the sum and substance of the good things: through baptism we received remission of sins, sanctification, participation of the Spirit, adoption, eternal life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:137
verses.text: What would ye more? Signs? But they come to an end (ἀλλὰ καταργεἵται).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:138
verses.text: Thou hast "faith, hope, charity," the abiding things: these seek thou, these are greater than signs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:139
verses.text: Nothing is equal to charity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:140
verses.text: For "greater than all," saith he, "is charity".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:141
verses.text: (cf.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:142
verses.text: Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:143
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:144
verses.text: ) But now, love is in jeopardy, for only its name is left behind, while the reality is nowhere (seen), but we are divided each from the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:145
verses.text: What then shall one do to reunite (ourselves)? For to find fault is easy, but how may one make friendship, this is the point to be studied; how we may bring together the scattered members.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:146
verses.text: For be it so, that we have one Church, or one doctrine—yet this is not the (main) consideration: no, the evil is, that in these we have not fellowship—"living peaceably," as the Apostle says, "with all men" (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:147
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:148
verses.text: ), on the contrary, we are at variance one with another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:149
verses.text: For be it that we are not having fights every day, yet look not thou to this, but (to this), that neither have we charity, genuine and unswerving.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:150
verses.text: There is need of bandages and oil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:151
verses.text: Let us bear it in mind, that charity is the cognizance of the disciples of Christ: that without this, all else avails nothing: that it is an easy task if we will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:152
verses.text: Yes, say you, we know all this, but how (to go to work) that it may be achieved? What (to do), that it may be effected? in what way, that we may love one another? First, let us put away the things which are subversive of charity, and then we shall establish this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:153
verses.text: Let none be resentful, none be envious, none rejoicing in (others') misfortunes: these are the things that hinder love; well then, the things that make it are of the other sort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:154
verses.text: For it is not enough to put away the things that hinder; the things that establish must also be forthcoming.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:155
verses.text: Now Sirach tells us the things that are subversive (of friendship), and does not go on to speak of the things which make union.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:156
verses.text: "Reproaching," he says, "and revealing of a secret, and a treacherous wound".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:157
verses.text: (cf.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:158
verses.text: Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:159
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:160
verses.text: ) But in speaking of the men of those times, these things might well be named, seeing they were carnal: but in our case, God forbid they should be (even) named.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:161
verses.text: Not from these things do we bring our inducements for you, but from the others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:162
verses.text: For us, there is nothing good without friendship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:163
verses.text: Let there be good things without number, but what is the benefit—be it wealth, be it luxury—without friendship? No possession equal to this, even in matters of this life, just as there is nothing worse than men hating (us).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:164
verses.text: "Charity hides a multitude of sins" ( Pet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:165
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:166
verses.text: ): but enmity, even where sins are not, suspects them to be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:167
verses.text: It is not enough not to be an enemy; no, one must also love.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:168
verses.text: Bethink thee, that Christ has bidden, and this is enough.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:169
verses.text: Even affliction makes friendships, and draws (men) together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:170
verses.text: "What then," say you, "now, when there is no affliction? say, how (are we to act) to become friends?" Have ye not other friends, I ask? In what way are ye their friends, how do ye continue such? For a beginning, let none have any enemy: this (in itself) is not a small matter: let none envy; it is not possible to accuse the man who envies not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:171
verses.text: (b) How then shall we be warmly affected? What makes love of persons? Beauty of person.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:172
verses.text: Then let us also make our souls beautiful, and we shall be amiable one to another: for it is necessary, of course, not only to love, but also to be loved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:173
verses.text: Let us first achieve this point, that we may be loved, and the other will be easy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:174
verses.text: How to act that we may be loved? Let us become beautiful, and let us do this, that we may always have lovers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:175
verses.text: Let none make it his study to get money, to get slaves, to get houses, (so much) as to be loved, as to have a good name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:176
verses.text: Better is a name than much wealth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:177
verses.text: For the one remains, the other perishes: and the one it is possible to acquire, the other impossible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:178
verses.text: For he that has got an evil character, will with difficulty lay it aside: but by means of his (good) name the poor man may quickly be rich.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:179
verses.text: Let there be a man having ten thousand talents, and another a hundred friends; the latter is more rich in resources than the former.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:180
verses.text: Then let us not merely do this, but let us work it as a kind of trade.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:181
verses.text: "And how can we?" say you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:182
verses.text: "A sweet mouth multiplieth its friends, and a gracious tongue".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:183
verses.text: Let us get a well-spoken mouth, and pure manners.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:184
verses.text: It is not possible for a man to be such, and not to be known.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:185
verses.text: (a) We have one world that we all inhabit, with the same fruits we all are fed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:186
verses.text: But these are small matters: by the same Sacraments we partake of the same spiritual food.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:187
verses.text: These surely are justifications of loving! (c) Mark how many (inducements and pleas) for friendship they that are without have excogitated; community of art or trade, neighborhood, relationships: but mightier than all these are the impulses and ties which are among us: this Table is calculated more (than all else) to shame us into friendliness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:188
verses.text: But many of us who come thereto do not even know one another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:189
verses.text: The reason, it may be said, is that there are so many of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:190
verses.text: By no means; it is only our own sluggish indifference.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:191
verses.text: (Once) there were three thousand (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:192
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:193
verses.text: )—there were five thousand (iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:194
verses.text: )—and yet they had all one soul: but now each knows not his brother, and is not ashamed to lay the blame on the number, because it is so great! Yet he that has many friends is invincible against all men: stronger he than any tyrant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:195
verses.text: Not such the safety the tyrant has with his body-guards, as this man has with his friends.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:196
verses.text: Moreover, this man is more glorious than he: for the tyrant is guarded by his own slaves, but this man by his peers: the tyrant, by men unwilling and afraid of him; this man by willing men and without fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:197
verses.text: And here too is a wonderful thing to be seen—many in one, and one in many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:198
verses.text: (a) Just as in an harp, the sounds are diverse, not the harmony, and they all together give out one harmony and symphony, (c) I could wish to bring you into such a city, were it possible, wherein (all) should be one soul: then shouldest thou see surpassing all harmony of harp and flute, the more harmonious symphony.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:199
verses.text: (b) But the musician is the Might of Love: it is this that strikes out the sweet melody, (d) singing, (withal) a strain in which no note is out of tune.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:200
verses.text: This strain rejoices both Angels, and God the Lord of Angels; this strain rouses (to hear it) the whole audience that is in heaven; this even lulls (evil) passions—it does not even suffer them to be raised, but deep is the stillness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:201
verses.text: For as in a theatre, when the band of musicians plays, all listen with a hush, and there is no noise there; so among friends, while Love strikes the chords, all the passions are still and laid to sleep, like wild beasts charmed and unnerved: just as, where hate is, there is all the contrary to this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:202
verses.text: But let us say nothing just now about enmity; let us speak of friendship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:203
verses.text: Though thou let fall some casual hasty word, there is none to catch thee up, but all forgive thee; though thou do (some hasty thing), none puts upon it the worse construction, but all allowance is made: every one prompt to stretch out the hand to him that is falling, every one wishing him to stand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:204
verses.text: A wall it is indeed impregnable, this friendship; a wall, which not the devil himself, much less men, can overpower.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:205
verses.text: It is not possible for that man to fall into danger who has gotten many friends.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:206
verses.text: (Where love is) no room is there to get matter of anger, but only for pleasantness of feeling: no room is there to get matter of envying; none, to get occasion of resentment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:207
verses.text: Mark him, how in all things both spiritual and temporal, he accomplishes all with ease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:208
verses.text: What then, I pray you, can be equal to this man? Like a city walled on every side is this man, the other as a city unwalled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:209
verses.text: —Great wisdom, to be able to be a creator of friendship! Take away friendship, and thou hast taken away all, thou hast confounded all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:210
verses.text: But if the likeness of friendship have so great power, what must the reality itself be? Then let us, I beseech you, make to ourselves friends, and let each make this his art.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:211
verses.text: But, lo! you will say, I do study this, but the other does not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:212
verses.text: All the greater the reward to thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:213
verses.text: True, say you, but the matter is more difficult.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:214
verses.text: How, I ask? Lo! I testify and declare to you, that if but ten of you would knit yourselves together, and make this your work, as the Apostles made the preaching theirs, and the Prophets theirs the teaching, so we the making of friends, great would be the reward.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:215
verses.text: Let us make for ourselves royal portraits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:216
verses.text: For if this be the common badge of disciples, we do a greater work than if we should put ourselves into the power to raise the dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:217
verses.text: The diadem and the purple mark the Emperor, and where these are not, though his apparel be all gold, the Emperor is not yet manifest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:218
verses.text: So now thou art making known thy lineage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:219
verses.text: Make men friends to thyself, and (friends) to others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:220
verses.text: There is none who being loved will wish to hate thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:221
verses.text: Let us learn the colors, with what ingredients they are mixed, with what (tints) this portrait is composed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:222
verses.text: Let us be affable: let us not wait for our neighbors to move.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:223
verses.text: Say not, if I see any person hanging back (for me to make the first advances), I become worse than he: but rather when thou seest this, forestall him, and extinguish his bad feeling.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:224
verses.text: Seest thou one diseased, and addest to his malady? This, most of all, let us make sure of—"in honor to prefer one another, to account others better than one's self" (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:225
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:226
verses.text: ), deem not this to be a lessening of thyself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:227
verses.text: If thou prefer (another) in honor, thou hast honored thyself more, attracting to thyself a still higher extinction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:228
verses.text: On all occasions let us yield the precedence to others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:229
verses.text: Let us bear nothing in mind of the evil done to us, but if any good has been done (let us remember only that).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:230
verses.text: Nothing so makes a man a friend, as a gracious tongue, a mouth speaking good things, a soul free from self-elation, a contempt of vain-glory, a despising of honor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 113:231
verses.text: If we secure these things, we shall be able to become invincible to the snares of the Devil, and having with strictness accomplished the pursuit of virtue, to attain unto the good things promised to them that love Him, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

verses.text: Homily XLI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:3
verses.text: ,  "And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:4
verses.text: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:5
verses.text: (a) See him in every place forcing his way into the synagogue, and in this manner departing thence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:6
verses.text: For in every place, he wished to have the occasion given him by them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:7
verses.text: (c) He wished to separate the disciples thence, and to have the beginning for ceasing to assemble with them, given by (the Jews) themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:8
verses.text: And it was not for nothing that he did this (b) which I have said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:9
verses.text: He was henceforth "provoking them to jealousy".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:10
verses.text: For both the Gentiles readily received him, and the Jews, upon the Gentiles receiving him, repented.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:11
verses.text: (a) This is why he continually made a stir among them, "for three months arguing and persuading concerning the kingdom of God:" for you must not suppose because you hear of his "speaking boldly," that there was any harshness: it was of good things that he discoursed, of a kingdom: who would not have heard him? "But when divers were hardened, speaking evil of the way".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:12
verses.text: They might well call it "the way;" this was indeed the way, that led into the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:13
verses.text: "He departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:14
verses.text: And this was done for the space of two years, so that all that were in Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:15
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:16

verses.text: (g) "He that believeth on Me," saith Christ, "doeth greater works than those which I do".

verses.text: (John xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:28
verses.text: ) This, and the miracle of the shadows is what He meant (in those words).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:29
verses.text: (d) "Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:30
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:31
verses.text: ) So entirely did they do all by way of trade! Observe: vagabond, or, itinerant, Jewish exorcists.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:32
verses.text: And to believe indeed, they had no mind; but by that Name they wished to cast out the demons.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:33
verses.text: "By Jesus, whom Paul preacheth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:34
verses.text: Only see what a name Paul had got! "And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:35
verses.text: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye? And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:38
verses.text: ) They did it in secret: then their impotence is publicly exposed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:39
verses.text: (f) Then not the Name does anything, unless it be spoken with faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:40
verses.text: (h) See how they used their weapons against themselves! (j) So far were they from thinking Jesus to be anything great: no, they must needs add Paul, as thinking him to be something great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:41
verses.text: Here one may marvel how it was that the demon did not cooperate with the imposture of the exorcists, but on the contrary exposed them, and laid open their stage-play.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:42
verses.text: He seems to me (to have done this) in exceeding wrath: just as it might be, if a person being in uttermost peril, should be exposed by some pitiful creature, and wish to vent all his rage upon him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:43
verses.text: "Jesus I know, and Paul I know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:44
verses.text: For, that there may not seem to be any slight put upon the Name of Jesus, (the demon) first confesses (Him), and then has permission given him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:45
verses.text: For, to show that it was not any weakness of the Name, but all owing to the imposture of those men, why did not the same take place in the case of Paul? "They fled out of that house naked and wounded:" he sorely battered their heads, perhaps rent their garments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:46
verses.text: (e) "And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, that dwelt at Ephesus, and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:47
verses.text: And many of them that had believed came confessing and making known their practices".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:48
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:49
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:50
verses.text: ) For since they had got to possess such power as, by means of the demons, to do such things, well might this be the consequence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:51
verses.text: "And many of them that practised curious arts, brought their books together, and burnt them in the presence of all men;"—having seen that there was no more use of them now that the demons themselves do these things—"and reckoned up the price of them, and found the amount fifty thousand pieces of silver.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:52
verses.text: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:55
verses.text: ) (i) "And" (so) "he disputed," in the school of one Tyrannus for two years:" where were believers, and believers exceedingly (advanced in the faith).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:56
verses.text: Moreover (Paul) writes (to them) as to great men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:57
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:58
verses.text: ) (b) "And having entered in to the synagogue," etc.

Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:60
verses.text: ) But why ἐπαρρησιάζετο? It means, he was ready to confront dangers, and disputed more openly, not veiling the doctrines.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:61
verses.text: (a) "But when some were hardened, and spake evil of the way, having departed from them, he separated the disciples".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:62
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:63
verses.text: ) He put a stop, it means, to their evil-speaking: he did not wish to kindle their envy, nor to bring them into more contention.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:64
verses.text: (c) Hence let us also learn not to put ourselves in the way of evil-speaking men, but to depart from them: he did not speak evil, when himself evil spoken of.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:65
verses.text: "He disputed daily," and by this gained the many, that, being evil intreated and (evil) spoken of, he did not (utterly) break away from them, and keep aloof.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:66
verses.text: (e) The evil-speakers are defeated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 114:67
verses.text: They calumniated the doctrine itself; (therefore) so as neither to rouse the disciples to wrath, nor.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:1
verses.text: them, he withdrew, showing that everywhere alike they repel salvation from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:2
verses.text: Here now he does not even apologize, seeing that the Gentiles everywhere have believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:3
verses.text: "In the school of one Tyrannus:" it was not that he sought the place, but without more ado where there was a school (there he discoursed).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:4
verses.text: (d) And look, no sooner is the trial from those without over, than this from the demons begins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:5
verses.text: Mark the infatuated Jewish hardness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:6
verses.text: Having seen his garments working miracles, they paid no heed to it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:7
verses.text: What could be greater than this? But, on the contrary, it resulted in just the opposite effect.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:8
verses.text: If any of the heathens believe not, having seen the (very) dust working these effects, let him believe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:9
verses.text: (f) Wonderful, how great the power of them that have believed! Both Simon for the sake of merchandise sought the grace of the Spirit, and these for this object did this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:10
verses.text: What hardness (of heart)! Why does not Paul rebuke them? It would have looked like envy, therefore it is so ordered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:11
verses.text: This same took place in the case of Christ (Mark ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:12
verses.text: ): but then the person is not hindered, for it was the beginning of the new state of things: since Judas also is not hindered, whereas Ananias and Sapphira were struck dead: and many Jews even for opposing (Christ) suffered nothing, while Elymas was blinded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:13
verses.text: "For I am not come," saith Christ, "to judge the world, but that the world might be saved".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:14
verses.text: (John iii.

Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:17
verses.text: ) See the villany of the men! They still continued to be Jews, while wishing to make a gain of that Name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:18
verses.text: All that they did was for glory and profit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:19
verses.text: (g) Look, in every case, how men are converted not so much in consequence of good things as of things fearful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:20
verses.text: In the case of Sapphira, fear fell upon the Church, and men dared not join themselves to them: here they received handkerchiefs and aprons, and were healed: and after this, then they came confessing their sins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:21
verses.text: (Hereby) the power of the demons is shown to be a great one, when it is against unbelievers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:22
verses.text: For why did he not say, "Who is Jesus?" He was afraid, lest he also should suffer punishment; but, that it might be permitted him to take revenge upon those who mocked him, he did this; "Jesus," says he, "I know," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:23
verses.text: He was in dread of Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:24
verses.text: For why did not those wretched men say to him, We believe? How much more splendid an appearance they would have made had they said this, that is, if they had claimed Him as their Master? But instead of that, they spoke even those senseless words, "By Jesus, whom Paul preacheth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:25
verses.text: Do you mark the forbearance (of the writer), how he writes history and does not call names? This makes the Apostles admirable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:26
verses.text: "And the evil spirit," etc.

verses.text: ) had given a lesson to these also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:31
verses.text: He mentions the name, and the number, thereby giving to the persons then living a credible proof of what he wrote.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:32
verses.text: And why were they itinerant? For the sake of merchandise: not assuredly to bear tidings of the word; how should that be their object? And how ran they anon, preaching by the things they suffered? "Insomuch," it says, "that all that dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:33
verses.text: Ought not this to have converted all? And marvel not, for nothing convinces malice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:34
verses.text: But come now, let us look at the affair of the exorcists, with what an evil disposition (they acted).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:35
verses.text: Why the same was not done in the case of Christ, is an inquiry for another time, and not for the present, save that this also was well and usefully ordered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:36
verses.text: It seems to me that they did this also in mockery, and that in consequence of this (punishment), none dared even at random to name that Name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:37
verses.text: Why did this put them upon confession? Because this was a most mighty argument of God's omniscience (therefore), before they should be exposed by the demons, they accused themselves, fearing lest they should suffer the same things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:38
verses.text: For when the demons their helpers are their accusers, what hope is there thenceforth, save the confession by deeds?  But see, I pray you, after such signs had been wrought, what evils within a short space ensue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:39
verses.text: Such is human nature: it soon forgets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:40
verses.text: Or, do ye not remember what has been the case among ourselves? Did not God last year shake our whole city? Did not all run to baptism? Did not whoremongers and effeminate and corrupt persons leave their dwellings, and the places where they spent their time, and change and become religious? But three days passed, and they returned again to their own proper wickedness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:41
verses.text: And whence is this? From the excessive laziness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:42
verses.text: And what marvel if, when the things have passed away (this be the case), seeing that, the images lasting perpetually, the result is such? The fate of Sodom—say, does it not still last (in its effects)? Well, did the dwellers beside it become any the better? And what say you to the son of Noah? Was he not such (as he is represented), did he not see with his eyes so vast a desolation, and yet was wicked? Then let us not marvel how, when such things had been done, these Jews (at Ephesus) believe not, when we see that belief itself often comes round for them into its opposite, into malignity; as, for instance, when they say that He hath a devil, He, the Son of God! Do you not see these things even now, and how men are many of them like serpents, both faithless and thankless, men who, viper-like, when they have enjoyed benefits and have been warmed by some, then they sting their benefactors? This we have said, lest any should marvel, how, such signs having been wrought, they were not all converted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:43
verses.text: For behold, in our own times happened those (miracles) relating to the martyr Babylas, those relating to Jerusalem, those relating to the destruction of the temples, and not all were converted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:44
verses.text: Why need I speak of ancient things? I have told you what happened last year; and none gave heed to it, but again little by little they fell off and sunk back.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:45
verses.text: The heaven stands perpetually crying aloud that it has a Master, and that it is the work of an Artificer, all this that we see—I mean the world—and yet some say that it is not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:46
verses.text: What happened to that Theodorus last year—whom did it not startle? And yet nothing came of it, but having for a season become religious, they returned to the point from which they had started in their attempt to be religious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:47
verses.text: So it was with the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:48
verses.text: This is what the Prophet said of them: "When He slew them, then they sought Him, and turned early unto God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:49
verses.text: (Ps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:50
verses.text: lxxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:51
verses.text: ) And what need to speak of those things that are common to all? How many have fallen into diseases, how many have promised, if raised up, to work so great a change, and yet they have again become the same as ever! This, if nothing else, shows that we have natural free-will—our changing all at once.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:52
verses.text: Were evil natural, this would not be: things that are natural and necessary, we cannot change from.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:53
verses.text: "And yet," you will say, "we do change from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 116:54
verses.text: For do we not see some, who have the natural faculty to see, but are blinded by fear?" (True—) because this also is natural:.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:1
verses.text: if a different (necessity of) nature come not also into operation: (thus) it is natural to us, that being terrified we do not see; it is natural to us that when a greater fear supervenes, the other gives way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:2
verses.text: "What then," you will say, "if right-mindedness be indeed according to nature, but fear having overpowered it cast it out?" What then if I shall show that some even then are not brought to a right mind, but even in these fears are reckless? Is this natural? Shall I speak of ancient things? Well then, of recent? How many in the midst of those fears continued laughing, mocking, and experienced nothing of the sort? Did not Pharaoh change immediately, and (as quickly) run back to his former wickedness? But here, as if (the demons) knew Him not, they (the exorcists) added, "Whom Paul preacheth," whereas they ought to have said, "the Saviour of the world".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:3
verses.text: "Him that rose again".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:4
verses.text: By this they show that they do know, but they did not choose to confess His glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:5
verses.text: Wherefore the demon exposes them, leaping upon them, and saying, "Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are ye?" So that not ye are believers, but ye abuse that Name when ye say this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:6
verses.text: Therefore the Temple is desolate, the implement easy to be overcome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:7
verses.text: So that ye are not preachers; mine, says he, ye are.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:8
verses.text: Great was the wrath of the demon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:9
verses.text: The Apostles had power to do this to them, but they did it not as yet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:10
verses.text: For they that had power over the demons that did these things to them, much more had power over the men themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:11
verses.text: Mark how their forbearance is shown, in that they whom they repulsed do these things, while the demons whom they courted do the contrary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:12
verses.text: "Jesus," says he, "I know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:13
verses.text: Be ashamed, ye that are ignorant (of Him).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:14
verses.text: "And Paul I know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:15
verses.text: Well said, "Think not that it is because I despise them, that I do these things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:16
verses.text: Great was the fear of the demon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:17
verses.text: And why without these words did he not rend their garments? For so he would both have sated his wrath, and established the delusion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:18
verses.text: He feared as I said, the unapproachable force, and would not have had such power had he not said this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:19
verses.text: But observe how we find the demons everywhere more right minded (than the Jews), not daring to contradict nor accuse the Apostles, or Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:20
verses.text: There they say, "We know Thee who Thou art" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:21
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:22
verses.text: ); and, "Why art Thou come hither before the time to torment us" (Mark i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:23
verses.text: ): and again, "I know Thee who Thou art, the Son of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:24
verses.text: And here, "These men are servants of the most high God" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:25
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:26
verses.text: ): and again, "Jesus I know, and Paul I know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:27
verses.text: For they exceedingly feared and trembled before those holy persons.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:28
verses.text: Perhaps some one of you, hearing of these things, wishes he were possessed of this power, so that the demons should not be able to look him in the face, and accounts those saints happy for this, that they had such power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:29
verses.text: But let him hear Christ saying, "Rejoice not because the demons are subject unto you" (Luke x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:30
verses.text: ), because He knew that all men rejoice most in this, through vainglory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:31
verses.text: For if thou seekest that which pleaseth God, and that which is for the common good, there is another, a greater way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:32
verses.text: It is not so great to free from a demon as it is to rescue from sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:33
verses.text: A demon hinders not to attain unto the kingdom of Heaven, nay, even cooperates, unwillingly indeed, but nevertheless cooperates by making him that has the demon more sober-minded; but sin casts a man out.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:34
verses.text: But it is likely some man will say, "God forbid it should ever befall me to be sobered in this way!" Nor do I wish it for you, but a very different way, that you should do all from love of Christ: if however, which God forbid, it should so befall you, then even on this behalf I would comfort you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:35
verses.text: If then the demon does not cast out (from the kingdom of heaven), but sin does cast out, to free a man from sin is greater beneficence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:36
verses.text: From this let us study to free our neighbors, and before our neighbors, our own selves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:37
verses.text: Let us see to it, lest we have a demon: let us examine ourselves strictly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:38
verses.text: More grievous than a demon is sin, for the demon makes men humble.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:39
verses.text: See ye not those possessed with a demon, when they have recovered from the attack, how downcast they are, of how sad a countenance, how fraught with shame their faces are, how they have not even courage to look one in the face? See the strange inconsistency! While those are ashamed on account of the things they suffer, we are not ashamed on account of the things we do; while they are abashed being wronged, we are not abashed when doing wrong: and yet their condition is not a subject for shame, but for pity and tenderness and indulgence: nay, great is the admiration it calls for, and many the praises, when struggling against such a spirit, they bear all thankfully: whereas our condition in very deed is a subject for ridicule, for shame, for accusation, for correction, for punishment, for the worst of evils, for hell-fire; calling for no compassion whatever.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:40
verses.text: Seest thou, that worse than a demon is sin? And those indeed, from the ills they suffer, reap a double profit: first, their being sobered and brought to more self-control; then, that having suffered here the chastisement of their own sins, they depart hence to their Master, purified.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:41
verses.text: For indeed upon this we have often discoursed to you, that those who are punished here, if they bear it thankfully, may naturally be supposed to put away thereby many of their sins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:42
verses.text: Whereas from sins the mischief resulting is twofold; first, that we offend; secondly, that we become worse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:43
verses.text: Attend to what I say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:44
verses.text: Not this is the only injury we get from sin, that we commit a sin: but another and a worse is this, that our soul receives a habit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:45
verses.text: Just as it is in the case of the body—for it will be more plain when put in the form of an example—as he who has taken a fever has got harm not only in this respect, that he is sick, but also that after the sickness he is become weaker, even though he may return to health after a long disease: just so in the case of sin, though we may regain health, yet we are far from having the strength we need.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:46
verses.text: For take the case of one who has been insolently abusive: does he not suffer his deserts for his abusive conduct? Aye, but there is another and a worse thing to rue (which is), that his soul is become more insensible to shame.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:47
verses.text: For from each several sin that is committed, even after the sin has been done and has ceased, there remains a kind of venom instilled into our souls.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:48
verses.text: Do you not hear people saying, when they are recovered from sickness, "I dare not drink water now?" And yet the man has regained his health: aye, but the disease has done him this harm also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:49
verses.text: And whereas those (possessed) persons, albeit suffering ill, are thankful, we, when faring well, blaspheme God, and think ourselves very ill used: for you will find more persons behaving thus in health and wealth than in poverty and sickness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:50
verses.text: For there stands the demon over (the possessed), like a very hangman, fierce, uttering many (menaces), even as a schoolmaster brandishing the lash, and not suffering them to give way to any laxity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:51
verses.text: And suppose that some are not at all brought to a sober mind, neither are these liable to punishment; no small thing this: even as fools, even as madmen and children, are not called to account, so neither are these: since for things that are done in a state of unconsciousness, none can be so merciless as to call the doers to account.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:52
verses.text: Why then, in a far worse condition than those who are possessed of evil sprits are we that sin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:53
verses.text: We do not, indeed, foam at the mouth, nor distort our eyes, or throw about our hands convulsively; but as for this, would that we did it in our body and not in our soul! Will you that I show you a soul, foaming, filthy, and a distortion of the mind's eyes? Think of those who are in a passion and drunken with rage; can any form be filthier than the words they discharge? In very deed it is like a sputtering of noisome slaver.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:54
verses.text: And just as the possessed know none of those who are present, so neither do these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:55
verses.text: Their understanding darkened, their eyes distorted, they see not who is friend, who foe, who worthy of respect, who contemptible, but they see all alike without a difference.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:56
verses.text: And then, do you not see them, how they tremble, just like those others? But they do not fall to the ground, say you? True, but their soul lies on the ground and falls there in convulsions: since had it stood upright, it would not have come into the condition it is in.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:57
verses.text: Or think you not that it betokens a soul abjectly sprawling and lost to all self-possession, the things men can do and say when drunken with rage? There is also another form of madness worse than this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:58
verses.text: What may this be? When men cannot so much as suffer themselves to vent their anger, but instead of that nourish within their own bosoms, to their own proper hurt, as it were a very hangman with his lash, the rancorous remembrance of wrongs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:59
verses.text: For it is a bane to themselves first, the malice that they bear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:60
verses.text: To say nothing of the things to come, what torture, think you, must that man undergo in the scourging of his soul, as day by day he looks how he may avenge himself on his enemy? He chastises himself first, and suffers punishment, swelling (with suppressed passion), fighting against himself, setting himself on fire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:61
verses.text: For needs must the fire be always burning within thee: while raising the fever to such a height, and not suffering it to wane, thou thinkest thou art inflicting some evil on the other, whereas thou art wasting thyself, ever bearing about with thee a flame which is always at its height, and not letting thy soul have rest, but evermore being in a state of fury, and having thy thoughts in a turmoil and tempest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:62
verses.text: What is more grievous than this madness, to be always smarting with pain, and ever swelling and inflamed? For such are the souls of the resentful: when they see him on whom they wish to be revenged, straightway it is as if a blow were struck them: if they hear his voice, they cower and tremble: if they be on their bed, they picture to themselves numberless revenges, hanging, torturing that enemy of theirs: and if, beside all this, they see him also to be in renown, O! the misery they suffer! Forgive him the offence, and free thyself from the torment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:63
verses.text: Why continue always in a state of punishment, that thou mayest once punish him, and take thy revenge? Why establish for thyself a hectic disease? Why, when thy wrath would fain depart from thee, dost thou keep it back? Let it not remain until the evening, says Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:64
verses.text: (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:65
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:66
verses.text: ) For like some eating rot or moth, even so does it gnaw through the very root of our understanding.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:67
verses.text: Why shut up a beast within thy bowels? Better a serpent or an adder to lie within thy heart, than anger and resentment: for those indeed would soon have done with us, but this remains forever fixing in us its fangs, instilling its poison, letting loose upon us an invading host of bitter thoughts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:68
verses.text: "That he should laugh me to scorn," say you, "that he should despise me!" O wretched, miserable man, wouldest thou not be ridiculed by thy fellow-servant, and wouldest thou be hated by thy Master? Wouldest thou not be despised by thy fellow-servant, and despisest thou thy Master?  To be despised by him, is it more than thou canst bear, but thinkest thou not that God is indignant, because thou ridiculest Him, because thou despisest Him, when thou wilt not do as He bids thee? But that thine enemy will not even ridicule thee, is manifest from hence (that), whereas if thou follow up the revenge, great is the ridicule, great the contempt, for this is a mark of a little mind; on the contrary, if thou forgive him, great is the admiration, for this is a mark of greatness of soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:69
verses.text: But you will say, he knows not this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:70
verses.text: Let God know it, that thou mayest have the greater reward.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:71
verses.text: For He says, "Lend to those of whom ye hope not to receive".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:72
verses.text: (Luke vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:73
verses.text: ) So let us also do good to those who do not even perceive that one is doing them good, that they may not, by returning to us praise or any other thing, lessen our reward.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:74
verses.text: For when we receive nothing from men, then we shall receive greater things from God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:75
verses.text: But what is more worthy of ridicule, what more paltry, than a soul which is always in anger, and wishing to take revenge? It is womanly, this disposition, it is babyish.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:76
verses.text: For as the babes are angry even with lifeless things, and unless the mother beats the ground, they will not let go their anger: so do these persons wish to revenge themselves on those who have aggrieved them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:77
verses.text: Why then, it is they who are worthy of ridicule: for to be overcome by passion, is the mark of a childish understanding, but to overcome it, is a sign of manliness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:78
verses.text: Why then, not we are the objects of ridicule, when we keep our temper, but they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:79
verses.text: It is not this that makes men contemptible—not to be conquered by passion: what makes them contemptible is this—to be so afraid of ridicule from without, as on this account to choose to subject one's self to one's besetting passion, and to offend God, and take revenge upon one's self.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:80
verses.text: These things are indeed worthy of ridicule.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:81
verses.text: Let us flee them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:82
verses.text: Let a man say, that having done us numberless ills, he has suffered nothing in return: let him say that he might again frantically assault us, and have nothing to fear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:83
verses.text: Why, in no other (better) way could he have proclaimed our virtue; no other words would he have sought, if he had wished to praise us, than those which he seems to say in abuse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:84
verses.text: Would that all men said these things of me: "he is a poor tame creature; all men heap insults on him, but he bears it: all men trample upon him, but he does not avenge himself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:85
verses.text: Would that they added, "neither, if he should wish to do so, can he:" that so I might have praise from God, and not from men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:86
verses.text: Let him say, that it is for want of spirit that we do not avenge ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:87
verses.text: This does us no hurt, when God knows (all): it does but cause our treasure to be in greater safety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:88
verses.text: If we are to have regard to them, we shall fall away from everything.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:89
verses.text: Let us not look to what they say, but to what becomes us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:90
verses.text: But, says he, "Let no man ridicule me," and some make a boast of this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:91
verses.text: O! what folly! "No man," says he, "having injured me, has ridiculed me:" that is, "I had my revenge".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:92
