verses.text: And yet for this thou deservest to be ridiculed, that thou didst take revenge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:93
verses.text: Whence came these words among us—being, as they are, a disgrace to us and a pest, an overthrow of our own proper life and of our discipline? It is in downright opposition to God that thou (so) speakest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:94
verses.text: The very thing which makes thee equal to God—the not avenging thyself—this thou thinkest a subject for ridicule! Are not we for these things worthy to be laughed at, both by ourselves, and by the heathen, when we thus speak against God? I wish to tell you a story of a thing that happened in the old times (which they tell) not on the subject of anger, but of money.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:95
verses.text: A man had an estate in which there was a hidden treasure, unknown to the owner: this piece of ground he sold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:96
verses.text: The buyer, when digging it for the purpose of planting and cultivation, found the treasure therein deposited, and came and wanted to oblige the seller to receive the treasure, urging that he had bought a piece of ground, not a treasure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:97
verses.text: The seller on his part repudiated the gift, saying, "The piece of ground (is not mine), I have sold it, and I have no concern whatever with this (treasure)".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:98
verses.text: So they fell to altercation about it, the one wishing to give it, the other standing out against receiving it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:99
verses.text: So chancing upon some third person, they argued the matter before him, and said to him, "To whom ought the treasure to be assigned?" The man could not settle that question; he said, however, that he would put an end to their dispute—he would (if they pleased) be master of it himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:100
verses.text: So he received the treasure, which they willingly gave up to him; and in the sequel got into troubles without end, and learnt by actual experience that they had done well to have nothing to do with it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:101
verses.text: So ought it be done likewise with regard to anger; both ourselves ought to be emulous not to take revenge, and those who have aggrieved us, emulous to give satisfaction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:102
verses.text: But perhaps these things also seem to be matter of ridicule: for when that madness is widely prevalent among men, those who keep their temper are laughed at, and among many madmen he who is not a madman seems to be mad.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 118:103
verses.text: Wherefore I beseech you that we may recover (from this malady), and come to our senses, that becoming pure from this pernicious passion, we may be enabled to attain unto the kingdom of heaven, through the grace and mercy of His only-begotten Son, with Whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:1
verses.text: Homily XLII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:2
verses.text: Acts XIX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:3
verses.text: ,  "After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the Spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:4
verses.text: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:5
verses.text: And the same time there arose no small stir about the Way".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:6
verses.text: He sends Timothy and Erastus into Macedonia, but himself remains at Ephesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:7
verses.text: Having made a long enough stay in that city, he wishes to remove elsewhere again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:8
verses.text: But how is it, that having from the first chosen to depart into Syria, he turns back to Macedonia? "He purposed," it says, "in the Spirit," showing that all (that he did) was done not of his own power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:9
verses.text: Now he prophesies, saying, "I must also see Rome:" perhaps to comfort them with the consideration of his not remaining at a distance, but coming nearer to them again, and to arouse the minds of the disciples by the prophecy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:10
verses.text: At this point, I suppose, it was that he wrote his Epistle to the Corinthians from Ephesus, saying, "I would not have you ignorant of the trouble which came to us in Asia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:11
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:12
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:13
verses.text: ) For since he had promised to go to Corinth, he excuses himself on the score of having loitered, and mentions the trial relating the affair of Demetrius.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:14
verses.text: "There arose no small stir about the Way".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:15
verses.text: Do you see the renown (acquired)? They contradicted, it says: (then) came miracles, twofold: (then) again, danger: such is the way the threads alternate throughout the whole texture (of the history).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:16
verses.text: "For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver temples of Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:17
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:19
verses.text: "Which made," it says, "silver temples of Diana".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:20
verses.text: And how is it possible that temples could be made of silver? Perhaps as small boxes (κιβώρια.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:21
verses.text: ) Great was the honor paid to this (Diana) in Ephesus; since, when (Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:22
verses.text: in Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:23
verses.text: Prol.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:24
verses.text: ) their temple was burnt it so grieved them, that they forbade even the name of the incendiary ever to be mentioned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:25
verses.text: See how, wherever there is idolatry, in every case we find money at the bottom of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:26
verses.text: Both in the former instance it was for money, and in the case of this man, for money.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:27
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:28
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:29
verses.text: ) It was not for their religion, because they thought that in danger; no, it was for their lucrative craft, that it would have nothing to work upon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:30
verses.text: Observe the maliciousness of the man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:31
verses.text: He was wealthy himself, and to him indeed it was no such great loss; but to them the loss was great, since they were poor, and subsisted on their daily earnings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:32
verses.text: Nevertheless, these men say nothing, but only he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:33
verses.text: And observe: "Whom having collected, and the workmen of like occupation," having themselves common cause with him, "he said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:34
verses.text: ); then he brought the danger home to them, that we are in danger of falling from this our craft into starvation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:35
verses.text: "Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands: so that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at naught; but also, that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:36
verses.text: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:39
verses.text: ) And yet the very things he spoke were enough to bring them to true religion: but being poor senseless creatures, this is the part they act.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:40
verses.text: For if this (Paul being) man is strong enough to turn away all, and the worship of the gods is in jeopardy, one ought to reflect, how great must this man's God be, and that he will much more give you those things, for which ye are afraid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:41
verses.text: Already (at the outset) he has secured a hold upon their minds by saying, "This Paul hath turned away much people, saying, that they be no gods, which are made with men's hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:42
verses.text: See what it is that the heathen are so indignant at; because he said that "they which be made of men are no gods".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:43
verses.text: Throughout, he drives his speech at their craft.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:44
verses.text: Then that which most grieved them he brings in afterwards.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:45
verses.text: But, with the other gods, he would say, we have no concern, but that "the temple also of the great goddess Diana is in danger to be destroyed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:46
verses.text: Then, lest he should seem to say this for the sake of lucre, see what he adds: "Whom the whole world worshippeth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:47
verses.text: Observe how he showed Paul's power to be the greater, proving all (their gods) to be wretched and miserable creatures, since a mere man, who was driven about, a mere tentmaker, had so much power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:48
verses.text: Observe the testimonies borne to the Apostles by their enemies, that they overthrew their worship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:49
verses.text: There (at Lystra) they brought "garlands and oxen".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:50
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:51
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:52
verses.text: ) Here he says, "This our craft is in danger to be set at naught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:53
verses.text: —Ye have filled (all) everywhere with your doctrine".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:54
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:55
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:56
verses.text: ) So said the Jews also with regard to Christ: "Ye see how the world is going after Him" (John xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:57
verses.text: ); and, "The Romans shall come and take away our city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:58
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:59
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:60
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:61
verses.text: And again on another occasion, "These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:62
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:63
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:64
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:65
verses.text: —"And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:66
verses.text: Upon what was that wrath called forth? On hearing about Diana, and about their source of gain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:67
verses.text: "And cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:68
verses.text: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and rushed with one accord into the theatre".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:69
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:70
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:71
verses.text: Such is the way with vulgar minds, any trivial occasion shall hurry them away and inflame their passions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:72
verses.text: Therefore it behooves to do (things) with (strict) examination.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:73
verses.text: But see how contemptible they were, to be so exposed to all (excitements)! "Having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel, they dragged them:" (here) again recklessly, just as did the Jews in the case of Jason; and everywhere they set upon them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:74
verses.text: "And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:75
verses.text: ) so far were they from all display and love of glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:76
verses.text: "And certain of the Asiarchs, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:77
verses.text: ) to a disorderly populace and tumult.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:78
verses.text: And Paul complies, for he was not vainglorious, nor ambitious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:79
verses.text: "Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:80
verses.text: Such is the nature of the multitude: it recklessly follows, like fire when it has fallen upon fuel; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:81
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:82
verses.text: ) "And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:83
verses.text: It was the Jews that thrust him forward; but as providence ordered it, this man did not speak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:84
verses.text: "And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:85
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:86
verses.text: ) "But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:87
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:88
verses.text: ) A childish understanding indeed! as if they were afraid, lest their worship should be extinguished, they shouted without intermission.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:89
verses.text: For two years had Paul abode there, and see how many heathen there were still! "And when the town clerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:90
verses.text: ) As if the thing were not palpable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:91
verses.text: With this saying first he extinguished their wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:92
verses.text: "And of the Diopetes".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:93
verses.text: There was another sacred object (ἱερὸν) that was so called.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:94
verses.text: Either he means the piece of burnt earth or her image.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:95
verses.text: This (is) a lie.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:96
verses.text: "Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:97
verses.text: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:98
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:99
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:100
verses.text: ) All this however he says to the people; but in order that those (workmen) also might become more reasonable, he says: "Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsman which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:101
verses.text: But if ye enquire anything concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:102
verses.text: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar, there being no cause, for which (matter) we shall not be able to give an account for this concourse".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:103
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:104
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:105
verses.text: ) "A lawful assembly," he says, for there were three assemblies according to law in each month; but this one was contrary to law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:106
verses.text: Then he terrified them also by saying, "We are in danger to be called to account" for sedition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:107
verses.text: But let us look again at the things said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:108
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:109
verses.text: ) "After these things were ended," it says, "Paul purposed in the Spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem," saying, "After I have been there, I must also see Rome".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:110
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:111
verses.text: ) He no longer speaks here after the manner of a man, or, He purposed to pass through those regions, without tarrying longer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:112
verses.text: Wherefore does he send away Timothy and Erastus? Of this I suppose he says, "Wherefore when we could no longer forbear, we thought it good to be left at Athens alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:113
verses.text: He sent away," it says, "two of those who ministered to him" ( Thess.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:114
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:115
verses.text: ), both to announce his coming, and to make them more eager.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:116
verses.text: "But he himself tarried awhile in Asia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:117
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:118
verses.text: ) Most of all does he pass his time in Asia; and with reason: there, namely, was the tyranny, of the philosophers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:119
verses.text: (Afterwards) also he came and discoursed to them again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:120
verses.text: "And the same time" etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:121
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:122
verses.text: ), for indeed the superstition was excessive.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:123
verses.text: (a) "Ye both see and hear," so palpable was the result that was taking place—"that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul by persuading hath turned away," not by violence: this is the way to persuade a city.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:124
verses.text: Then, what touched them closely, "that they be no gods which are made with hands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:125
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:126
verses.text: ) He overturns, says he, our craft: (e) "From this work we have our wealth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:127
verses.text: Hath persuaded".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:128
verses.text: How did he persuade—he, a man of mean consideration? How prevail over so great a force of habit? by doing what—by saying what? It is not for a Paul (to effect this), it is not for a man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:129
verses.text: Even this is enough, that he said, "They are no gods".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:130
verses.text: Now if the impiety (of the heathen religions) was so easy to detect, it ought to have been condemned long ago: if it was strong, it ought not to have been overthrown so quickly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:131
verses.text: (b) For, lest they should consider within themselves (how strange), that a human being should have such power as this, and if a human being has power to effect such things, why then one ought to be persuaded by that man, he adds: (f) "not only is this our craft in danger to be set at naught, but also," as if forsooth alleging a greater consideration, "the temple of the great goddess Diana," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:132
verses.text: (c) "whom all Asia and the world worshippeth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:133
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:134
verses.text: ) (g) "And when they heard, they were filled with wrath, and shouted, Great is Diana of the Ephesians!" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:135
verses.text: ) For each city had its proper gods.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:136
verses.text: (d) They thought to make their voice a barrier against the Divine Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:137
verses.text: Children indeed, these Greeks! (h) And their feeling was as if by their voice they could reinstate the worship of her, and undo what had taken place! "And the whole city," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:138
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:139
verses.text: ) See a disorderly multitude! "And when Paul," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:140
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:141
verses.text: ) Paul then wished to enter in that he might harangue them: for he took his persecutions as occasions for teaching: "but the disciples suffered him not".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:142
verses.text: Mark, how great forethought we always find them taking for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:143
verses.text: At the very first they brought him out that they might not (in his person) receive a mortal blow; and yet they had heard him say, "I must also see Rome".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:144
verses.text: But it was providential that he so predicts beforehand, that they might not be confounded at the event.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:145
verses.text: But they would not that he should even suffer any evil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:146
verses.text: "And certain of the Asiarchs besought him that he would not enter into the theatre".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:147
verses.text: Knowing his eagerness, they "besought him:" so much did all the believers love him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:148
verses.text: —"And they drew Alexander," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:149
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:150
verses.text: ) This Alexander, why did he wish to plead? Was he accused? No, but it was to find an opportunity, and overturn the whole matter, and inflame the anger of the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:151
verses.text: "But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:152
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:153
verses.text: ) Do you mark the inordinate rage? Well, and with rebuke does the town clerk say, "What man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians—" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:154
verses.text: ) (coming to the point) which they were frightened about.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:155
verses.text: Is it this, says he, that ye do not worship her? And he does not say, "That knoweth not" Diana, but, "our city," that it always worshipped her.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:156
verses.text: "Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:157
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:158
verses.text: ) Why then do ye make a question about them, as if these things were not plain? (b) Then he quietly chides them, showing that they had come together without reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:159
verses.text: "And to do nothing rashly," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:160
verses.text: Showing that they had acted rashly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:161
verses.text: (a) "For ye have brought hither," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:162
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:163
verses.text: ) They wanted to make religion the pretext for what concerned their own money-making: (c) and it was not right on account of private charges to hold a public assembly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:164
verses.text: For he put them to a nonplus, and left them not a word to say for themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:165
verses.text: "There being no cause," he says, "for this concourse, for which" (matter) "we shall not be able to give the account".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:166
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:167
verses.text: ) See how prudently, how cleverly, the unbelievers (act).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:168
verses.text: Thus he extinguished their wrath.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:169
verses.text: For as it is easily kindled, so also is it easily extinguished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:170
verses.text: "And when he had thus spoken," it says, "he dismissed the assembly".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:171
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:172
verses.text: )  Seest thou how God permits trials, and by them stirs up and awakens the disciples, and makes them more energetic? Then let us not sink down under trials: for He Himself will "also make the way of escape, that we may be able to bear them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:173
verses.text: ( Cor x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:174
verses.text: ) Nothing so makes friends, and rivets them so firmly, as affliction: nothing so fastens and compacts the souls of believers: nothing is so seasonable for us teachers in order that the things said by us may be heard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:175
verses.text: For the hearer when he is in ease is listless and indolent, and seems to suffer annoyance from the speaker: but when he is in affliction and distress, he falls into a great longing for the hearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:176
verses.text: For when distressed in his soul, he seeks on all sides to find comfort for his affliction: and the preaching brings no small comfort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:177
verses.text: "What then," you will say, "of the Jews? How was it that in consequence of their weakheartedness, they did not hear?" Why, they were Jews, those ever weak and miserable creatures: and besides, the affliction in their case was great, but we speak of affliction in moderation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:178
verses.text: For observe: they expected to be freed from the evils that encompassed them, and they fell into numberless greater evils: now this is no common distress to the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:179
verses.text: Afflictions cut us off from the sympathy we have for the present world, as appears in this, that we wish for death immediately, and cease to be loving of the body: which very thing is the greatest part of wisdom, to have no hankering, no ties to the present life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:180
verses.text: The soul which is afflicted does not wish to be concerned about many things: repose and stillness are all it desired, content for its part to have done with the things present, even though there be nothing else to follow.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:181
verses.text: As the body when wearied and distressed does not wish to indulge in amours, or gormandizing, but only to repose and lie down in quiet; so the soul, harassed by numberless evils, is urgent to be at rest and quiet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:182
verses.text: The soul which is at ease is (apt to be) fluttered, alarmed, unsettled: whereas in this there is no vacuity, no running to waste: and the one is more manly, the other more childish; the one has more gravity, in the other more levity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:183
verses.text: And as some light substance, when it falls upon deep water, is tossed to and fro, just so is the soul when it falls into great rejoicing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:184
verses.text: Moreover, that our greatest faults arise out of overmuch pleasure, any one may see.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:185
verses.text: Come, if you will, let us represent to ourselves two houses, the one where people are marrying, the other where they are mourning: let us enter in imagination into each: let us see which is better than the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:186
verses.text: Why, that of the mourner will be found full of seriousness (φιλοσοφίας); that of the marrying person, full of indecency.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:187
verses.text: For look, (here are) shameful words, unrestrained laughter, more unrestrained motions, both dress and gait full of indecency, words fraught with mere nonsense and foolery: in short, all is ridicule there, all ridiculous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:188
verses.text: I do not say the marriage is this; God forbid; but the accompaniments of the marriage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:189
verses.text: Then nature is beside itself in excess of riot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:190
verses.text: Instead of human beings, those present become brute creatures, some neighing like horses, others kicking like asses: such utter license, such dissolute unrestraint: nothing serious, nothing noble: (it is) the devil's pomp, cymbals, and pipes, and songs teeming with fornication and adultery.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:191
verses.text: But not so in that house where there is mourning; all is well-ordered there: such silence, such repose, such composure; nothing disorderly, nothing extravagant: and if any one does speak, every word he utters is fraught with true philosophy: and then the wonderful circumstance is, that at such times not men only, but even servants and women speak like philosophers—for such is the nature of sorrow—and while they seem to be consoling the mourner, they in fact utter numberless truths full of sound philosophy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:192
verses.text: Prayers are there to begin with, that the affliction may stop there, and go no further: many a one comforting the sufferer, and recitals without number of the many who have the like cause for mourning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:193
verses.text: "For what is man?" (they ask) (and thereupon) a serious examination of our nature—"aye, then, what is man!" (and upon this) an impeachment of the life (present) and its worthlessness, a reminding (one another) of things to come, of the Judgment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:194
verses.text: (So from both these scenes) each returns home: from the wedding, grieved, because he himself is not in the enjoyment of the like good fortune; from the mourning, light-hearted, because he has not himself undergone the like affliction, and having all his inward fever quenched.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:195
verses.text: But what will you? Shall we take for another contrast the prisons and the theatres? For the one is a place of suffering, the other of pleasure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:196
verses.text: Let us again examine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:197
verses.text: In the former there is seriousness of mind; for where there is sadness, there must needs be seriousness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:198
verses.text: He who aforetime was rich, and inflated with his own importance, now will even suffer any common person to converse with him, fear and sorrow, like some mightier fire, having fallen on his soul, and softening down his harshness: then he becomes humble, then of a sad countenance, then he feels the changes of life, then he bears up manfully against everything.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:199
verses.text: But in a theatre all is the reverse of this—laughter, ribaldry, devil's pomp, dissoluteness, waste of time, useless spending of days, planning for extravagant lust, adultery made a study of, practical training to fornication, schooling in intemperance, encouragement to filthiness, matter for laughter, patterns for the practice of indecency.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:200
verses.text: Not so the prison: there you will find humbleness of mind, exhoration, incentive to seriousness, contempt of worldly things; (these) are all trodden under foot and spurned and, fear stands over (the man there), as a schoolmaster over a child, controlling him to all his duties.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:201
verses.text: But if you will, let us examine in a different way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:202
verses.text: I should like you to meet a man on his return from a theatre, and another coming out of prison; and while you would see the soul of the one fluttered, perturbed, actually tied and bound, that of the other you would see enlarged, set free, buoyant as on wings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:203
verses.text: For the one returns from the theatre, enfettered by the sight of the women there, bearing about chains harder than any iron, the scenes, the words, the gestures, that he saw there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:204
verses.text: But the other on his return from the prison, released from all (bounds), will no longer think that he suffers any evil as comparing his own case with that of (those) others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:205
verses.text: (To think) that he is not in bonds will make him thankful ever after; he will despise human affairs, as seeing so many rich men there in calamity, men (once) having power to do many and great things, and now lying bound there: and if he should suffer anything unjustly, he will bear up against this also; for of this too there were many examples there: he will be led to reflect upon the Judgment to come and will shudder, seeing here (in the earthly prison) how it will be there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:206
verses.text: For as it is with one here shut up in prison, so in that world also before the Judgment, before the Day that is to come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:207
verses.text: Towards wife, children, and servants, he will be more gentle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:208
verses.text: Not so he that comes from the theatre: he will look upon his wife with more dislike, he will be peevish with his servants, bitter towards his children, and savage towards all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:209
verses.text: Great are the evils theatres cause to cities, great indeed, and we do not even know that they are great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:210
verses.text: Shall we examine other scenes of laughter also, I mean the feasts, with their parasites, their flatterers, and abundance of luxury, and (compare with them) places where are the halt and blind? As before, in the former is drunkenness, luxury, and dissoluteness, in the latter the reverse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:211
verses.text: —See also with regard to the body, when it is hot-blooded, when it is in good case, it undergoes the quickest change to sickness: not so, when it has been kept low.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:212
verses.text: Then let me make my meaning clearer to you:—let there be a body having plenty of blood, plenty of flesh, plump with good living: this body will be apt even from any chance food to engender a fever, if it be simply idle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:213
verses.text: But let there be another, struggling rather with hunger and hardship: this is not easily overcome, not easily wrestled down by disease.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:214
verses.text: Blood, though it may be healthy in us, does often by its very quantity engender disease: but if it be small in quantity, even though it be not healthy, it can be easily worked off.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:215
verses.text: So too in the case of the soul, that which leads an easy, luxurious life, has its impulses quickly swayed to sin: for such a soul is next neighbor to folly, to pleasure, to vainglory also, and envy, and plottings, and slanderings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:216
verses.text: Behold this great city of ours, what a size it is! Whence arise the evils? is it not from those who are rich? is it not from those who are in enjoyment? Who are they that "drag" men "before the tribunals?" Who, that dissipate properties? Those who are wretched and outcasts, or those who are inflated with consequence, and in enjoyment? It is not possible that any evil can happen from a soul that is afflicted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:217
verses.text: (James ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:218
verses.text: ) Paul knew the gain of this: therefore he says, "Tribulation worketh patience, and patience experience, and experience hope, and hope maketh not ashamed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:219
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:220
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:221
verses.text: ) Then let us not sink in our afflictions, but in all things give thanks, that so we may get great gain, that we may be well-pleasing to God, who permits afflictions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:222
verses.text: A great good is affliction: and we learn this from our own children: for without affliction (a boy) would learn nothing useful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:223
verses.text: But we, more than they, need affliction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:224
verses.text: For if there, when the passions (as yet) are quiet, (chastisement) benefits them, how much more us, especially possessed as we are by so many! Nay, we behoove rather to have schoolmasters than they: since the faults of children cannot be great, but ours are exceeding great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:225
verses.text: Our schoolmaster is affliction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 119:226
verses.text: Let us then not draw it down willingly upon ourselves, but when it is come let us bear it bravely, being, as it is, always the cause of numberless good things; that so we may both obtain grace from God, and the good things which are laid up for them that love Him, in Christ Jesus our Lord, with Whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, might, honor, now and evermore, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:1
verses.text: Homily XLIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:2
verses.text: Acts XX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:3
verses.text: "And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:4
verses.text: There was need of much comforting after that uproar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:5
verses.text: Accordingly, having done this, he goes into Macedonia, and then into Greece.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:6
verses.text: For, it says, "when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece, and there abode three months.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:7
verses.text: And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:8
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:9
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:10
verses.text: ) Again he is persecuted by the Jews, and goes into Macedonia.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:11
verses.text: "And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:12
verses.text: These going before tarried for us at Troas".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:13
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:14
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:15
verses.text: ) But how does he call Timothy a man "of Thessalonica?" This is not his meaning, but, "Of Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus and Gaius: of Derbe, Timothy," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:16
verses.text: , these, he says, went before him to Troas, preparing the way for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:17
verses.text: "And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:19
verses.text: ) For it seems to me that he made a point of keeping the feasts in the large cities.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:20
verses.text: "From Philippi," where the affair of the prison had taken place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:21
verses.text: This was his third coming into Macedonia, and it is a high testimony that he bears to the Philippians, which is the reason why he makes some stay there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:22
verses.text: "And upon the day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:23
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:24
verses.text: ) It was then the (season between Easter and) Pentecost.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:25
verses.text: See how everything was subordinate to the preaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:26
verses.text: It was also, it says, the Lord's day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:27
verses.text: Not even during night-time was he silent, nay he discoursed the rather then, because of stillness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:28
verses.text: Mark how he both made a long discourse, and beyond the time of supper itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:29
verses.text: But the Devil disturbed the feast—not that he prevailed, however—by plunging the hearer in sleep, and causing him to fall down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:30
verses.text: "And," it says, "there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:31
verses.text: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:32
verses.text: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him, said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:33
verses.text: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:34
verses.text: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:37
verses.text: ) But observe, I pray you, the theatre, how crowded it was: and the miracle, what it was.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:38
verses.text: "He was sitting in a window," at dead of night.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:39
verses.text: Such was their eagerness to hear him! Let us take shame to ourselves! "Aye, but a Paul" say you, "was discoursing then".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:40
verses.text: Yes, and Paul discourses now, or rather not Paul, either then or now, but Christ, and yet none cares to hear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:41
verses.text: No window in the case now, no importunity of hunger, or sleep, and yet we do not care to hear: no crowding in a narrow space here, nor any other such comfort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:42
verses.text: And the wonderful circumstance is, that though he was a youth, he was not listless and indifferent; and though (he felt himself) weighed down by sleep, he did not go away, nor yet fear the danger of falling down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:43
verses.text: It was not from listlessness that he slumbered, but from necessity of nature.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:44
verses.text: But observe, I beseech you, so fervent was their zeal, that they even assembled in a third loft: for they had not a Church yet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:45
verses.text: "Trouble not yourselves," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:46
verses.text: He said not, "He shall come to life again, for I will raise him up:" but mark the unassuming way in which he comforts them: "for his life," says he, "is in him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:47
verses.text: When he was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:48
verses.text: This thing cut short the discourse; it did no harm, however.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:49
verses.text: "When he had eaten," it says, "and discoursed a long while, even till break of day, so he departed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:50
verses.text: Do you mark the frugality of the supper? Do you observe how they passed the whole night? Such were their meals, that the hearers came away sober, and fit for hearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:51
verses.text: But we, in what do we differ from dogs? Do you mark what a difference (between us and those men)? "And they brought the young man alive, and," it says, "were not a little comforted," both because they received him back alive, and because a miracle had been wrought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:52
verses.text: "And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Thasos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:54
verses.text: ) We often find Paul parting from the disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:55
verses.text: For behold again, he himself goes afoot: giving them the easier way, and himself choosing the more painful.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:56
verses.text: He went afoot, both that he might arrange many matters, and by way of training them to bear a parting from him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:57
verses.text: "And when he had joined us at Thasos, having taken him on board, we came to Mytilene; and having sailed thence on the morrow, we come over against Chios"—then they pass the island—"and on the next day we touched at Samos, and having stopped at Trogylium, on the following day we came to Miletus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:58
verses.text: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem the day of Pentecost".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:59
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:60
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:61
verses.text: ) Why this haste? Not for the sake of the feast, but of the multitude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:62
verses.text: At the same time, by this he conciliated the Jews, as being one that did honor the feasts, wishing to gain even his adversaries: at the same time also he delivers the word.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:63
verses.text: Accordingly, see what great gain accrued, from all being present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:64
verses.text: But that the interests of the people of Ephesus might not be neglected on that account, he managed for this in a different way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:65
verses.text: But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:66
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:67
verses.text: ) "And having embraced them," it says, "he departed for to go into Macedonia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:68
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:69
verses.text: ) By this again he refreshed them (ἀνεκτήσατο), giving them much consolation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:70
verses.text: "And having exhorted" the Macedonians, "with much discourse, he came into Greece".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:71
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:72
verses.text: ) Observe how we everywhere find him accomplishing all by means of preaching, not by miracles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:73
verses.text: "And we, sailed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:74
verses.text: The writer constantly shows him to us as hasting to get to Syria; and the reason of it was the Church, and Jerusalem, but still he restrained his desire, so as to set all right in those parts also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:75
verses.text: And yet Troas is not a large place: why then do they pass seven days in it? Perhaps it was large as regarded the number of believers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:76
verses.text: And after he had passed seven days there, on the following day he spent the night in teaching: so hard did he find it to tear himself away from them, and they from him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:77
verses.text: "And when we came together" it says, "to break bread".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:78
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:79
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 120:80
verses.text: ) At the very time (of breaking bread) the discourse having taken its commencement,.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:1
verses.text: extended: as representing that they were hungry, and it was not unseasonable: for the principal object (which brought them together) was not teaching, but they came together "to break bread;" discourse however having come up, he prolonged the teaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:2
verses.text: See how all partook also at Paul's table.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:3
verses.text: It seems to me, that he discoursed while even sitting at table, teaching us to consider all other things as subordinate to this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:4
verses.text: Picture to yourselves, I beseech you, that house with its lights, with its crowd, with Paul in the midst, discoursing, with even the windows occupied by many: what a thing it was to see, and to hear that trumpet, and behold that gracious countenance! But why did he discourse during night time? Since "he was about to depart," it says, and was to see them no more: though this indeed he does not tell them, they being too weak (to bear it), but he did tell it to the others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:5
verses.text: At the same time too the miracle which took place would make them evermore to remember that evening; so that the fall turned out to the advantage of the teacher.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:6
verses.text: Great was the delight of the hearers, and even when interrupted it was the more increased.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:7
verses.text: That (young man) was to rebuke all that are careless (of the word), he whose death was caused by nothing else than this, that he wished to hear Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:8
verses.text: "And we went before to ship," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:9
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:10
verses.text: ) Wherefore does the writer say where they came, and where they went to? To show in the first place that he was making the voyage more leisurely—and this upon human grounds—and sailing past (some): also (for the same reason he tells) where he made a stay, and what parts he sailed past; (namely,) "that he might not have to spend the time in Asia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:12
verses.text: ) Since had he come there, he could not have sailed by; he did not like to pain those who would have begged him to remain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:13
verses.text: "For he hasted," it says, "if it were possible for him to keep the day of Pentecost in Jerusalem:" and (this) was not possible (if he stayed).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:14
verses.text: Observe, how he is also moved like other men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:15
verses.text: For therefore it is that all this is done, that we may not fancy that he was above human nature: (therefore) you see him desiring (something), and hasting, and in many instances not obtaining (his object): for those great and holy men were partakers of the same nature with us; it was in the will and purpose that they differed, and so it was that also they attracted upon themselves the great grace they did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:16
verses.text: See, for instance, how many things they order by an economy of their own.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:17
verses.text: "That we give not offence" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:18
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:19
verses.text: ) to those who wish (to take offence), and, "That our ministry be not blamed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:20
verses.text: Behold, both an irreproachable life and on the other hand condescension.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:21
verses.text: This is (indeed to be) called economy, to the (very) summit and height (of it).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:22
verses.text: For he that went beyond the commandments of Christ, was on the other hand more humble than all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:23
verses.text: "I am made all things to all men," he says, "that I might gain all".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:24
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:25
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:26
verses.text: ) He cast himself also upon dangers, as he says in another place; "In much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses, in stripes, in imprisonments".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:27
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:28
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:30
verses.text: ) And great was his love for Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:31
verses.text: For if there be not this, all else is superfluous, both the economy (of condescending accommodation), and the irreproachable life, and the exposing himself to dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:32
verses.text: "Who is weak," he says, "and I am not weak? Who is offended, and I burn not?" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:33
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:34
verses.text: ) These words let us imitate, and let us cast ourselves upon dangers for our brethren's sake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:35
verses.text: Whether it be fire, or the sword, cast thyself on it, beloved, that thou mayest rescue (him that is) thy member: cast thyself, be not afraid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:36
verses.text: Thou art a disciple of Christ, Who laid down His life for His brethren: a fellow-disciple with Paul, who chose to suffer numberless ills for his enemies, for men that were warring against him; be thou filled with zeal, imitate Moses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:37
verses.text: He saw one suffering wrong, and avenged him; he despised royal luxury, and for the sake of those who were afflicted he became a fugitive, a wanderer, lonely and deserted; he passed his days in a foreign land; and yet he blamed not himself, nor said, "What is this? I despised royalty, with all that honor and glory: I chose to avenge those who were wronged, and God hath overlooked me: and not only hath He not brought me back to my former honor, but even forty years am I passing in a foreign land.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:38
verses.text: Truly, handsomely have I received my wages, have I not!" But nothing of the kind did he say or think.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:39
verses.text: So also do thou: be it that thou suffer any evil for doing good, be it that (thou have to wait) a long time, be not thou offended, be not discomposed: God will of a surety give thee thy reward.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:40
verses.text: The more the recompense is delayed, the more is the interest of it increased.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:41
verses.text: Let us have a soul apt to sympathize, let us have a heart that knows how to feel with others in their sorrows: no unmerciful temper (ὠμόν), no inhumanity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:42
verses.text: Though thou be able to confer no relief, yet weep thou, groan, grieve over what has happened: even this is not to no purpose.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:43
verses.text: If it behooves us to feel for those who are justly punished by God, much more for those who suffer unjustly at the hands of men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:44
verses.text: (They of) "aenan," it saith, "came not forth to mourn for the house which was near her" (Micah i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:45
verses.text: ): they shall receive pain, "in return for that they built for derision".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:46
verses.text: And again, Ezekiel makes this an accusation against them, that they did not grieve for (the afflicted).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:47
verses.text: (Ezek.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:48
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:49
verses.text: ) What sayest thou, O Prophet? God punisheth, and shall I grieve for those that He is punishing? Yea verily: for God Himself that punisheth wisheth this: since neither does He Himself wish to punish, nay, even Himself grieves when punishing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:50
verses.text: Then be not thou glad at it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:51
verses.text: You will say, "If they are justly punished, we ought not to grieve".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:52
verses.text: Why, the thing we ought to grieve for is this—that they were found worthy of punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:53
verses.text: Say, when thou seest thy son undergoing cautery or the knife, dost thou not grieve? and sayest thou not to thyself, "What is this? It is for health this cutting, to quicken his recovery; it is for his deliverance, this burning?" but for all that, when thou hearest him crying out, and not able to bear the pain, thou grievest, and the hope of health being restored is not enough to carry off the shock to nature.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:54
verses.text: So also in the case of these, though it be in order to their health that they are punished, nevertheless let us show a brotherly feeling, a fatherly disposition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:55
verses.text: They are cuttings and cauteries, the punishments sent by God: but it is for this we ought to weep, that they were sick, that they needed such a mode of cure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:56
verses.text: If it be for crowns that any suffer these things, then grieve not; for instance, as Paul, as Peter suffered: but when it is for punishment that one suffers justice, then weep, then groan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:57
verses.text: Such was the part the prophets acted; thus one of them said, "Ah! Lord, dost thou destroy the residue of Israel?" (Ezek.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:58
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:59
verses.text: ) We see men-slayers, wicked men, suffering punishment, and we are distressed, and grieve for them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:60
verses.text: Let us not be philosophical beyond measure: let us show ourselves pitiful, that we may be pitied; there is nothing equal to this beautiful trait: nothing so marks to us the stamp of human nature as the showing pity, as the being kind to our fellow-men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:61
verses.text: In fact, therefore do the laws consign to public executioners the whole business of punishment: having compelled the judge to punish so far as to pronounce the sentence, thereafter they call forth those to perform the act itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:62
verses.text: So true is it, that though it be justly done, it is not the part of a generous (φιλοσόφου) soul to inflict punishment, but it requires another sort of person for this: since even God punishes not by His own hand, but by means of the angels.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:63
verses.text: Are they then executioners, the angels? God forbid: I say not this, but they are avenging powers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:64
verses.text: When Sodom was destroyed, the whole was done by them as the instruments: when the judgments in Egypt were inflicted, it was through them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:65
verses.text: For, "He sent," it says, "evil angels among them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:66
verses.text: (Psalm lxxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:67
verses.text: ) But when there is need of saying, God does this by Himself: thus, He sent the Son:—(b) but, "He that receiveth you, receiveth Me, and he that receiveth Me, receiveth Him that sent Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:68
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:69
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:70
verses.text: ) (a) And again He saith, "Then will I say unto the angels, Gather together them that do iniquity, and cast them into the furnace".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:71
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:72
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:73
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:74
verses.text: ) But concerning the just, not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:75
verses.text: (c) And again, "Bind him hand and foot, and cast him into outer darkness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:76
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:77
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:78
verses.text: ) Observe how in that case His servants minister: but when the point is to do good, see Himself doing the good, Himself calling: "Come, ye blessed of My Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:79
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:80
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:81
verses.text: ) When the matter is, to converse with Abraham, then Himself comes to him: when it is, to depart to Sodom, He sends His servants, like a judge raising up those who are to punish.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:82
verses.text: "Thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:83
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:84
verses.text: ); I (will make thee): but that other, not Himself, but His servants bind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:85
verses.text: Knowing these things, let us not rejoice over those who are suffering punishment, but even grieve: for these let us mourn, for these let us weep, that for this also we may receive a reward.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:86
verses.text: But now, many rejoice even over those who suffer evil unjustly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 121:87
verses.text: But not so, we: let us show all sympathy: that we also may have God vouchsafed us, through the grace and mercy of His only-begotten Son, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:1
verses.text: Homily XLIV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:2
verses.text: Acts XX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:3
verses.text: –  "And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:4
verses.text: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons, serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews: and how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have showed you, and have taught you publicly, and from house to house, testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:5
verses.text: See him, hasting to sail by, and yet not overlooking them, but taking order for all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:6
verses.text: Having sent for the rulers, through those he discourses to them (the Ephesians): but it is worthy of admiration, how finding himself under a necessity of saying certain great things about himself, he tries to make the least he can of it (πειρἅτα μετριάζειν).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:7
verses.text: "Ye know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:8
verses.text: For just as Samuel, when about to deliver up the government to Saul says in their presence, "Have I taken aught of your hands? Ye are witnesses, and God also" ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:9
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:10
verses.text: , ); (so Paul here).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:11
verses.text: David also, when disbelieved, says, "I was with the flock keeping my father's sheep: and when the bear came, I scared her away with my hands" ( Sam.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:12
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:13
verses.text: , ): and Paul himself too says to the Corinthians, "I am become a fool; ye have compelled me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:14
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:15
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:16
verses.text: ) Nay, God Himself also does the same, not speaking of himself upon any and every occasion, but only when He is disbelieved, then He brings up His benefits.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:17
verses.text: Accordingly, see what Paul does here: first he adduces their own testimony: that you may not imagine his words to be mere boasting, he calls the hearers themselves as witnesses of the things he says, since he was not likely to speak lies in their presence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:18
verses.text: This is the excellence of a teacher, to have for witnesses of his merits those who are his disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:19
verses.text: And what is wonderful, Not for one day nor for two, says he, have I continued doing this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:20
verses.text: He wishes to cheer them for the future, that they may bravely bear all things, both the parting from him, and the trials about to take place—just as it was in the case of Moses and Joshua.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:21
verses.text: And see how he begins: "How I have been with you the whole time, serving the Lord with all humility of mind".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:22
verses.text: Observe, what most becomes rulers: "hating pride" (Exod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:23
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:24
verses.text: , LXX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:25
verses.text: ), says (Moses): which (qualification) is especially in point for rulers, because to them there is (almost) a necessity of becoming arrogant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:26
verses.text: This (humility) is the groundwork of all that is good, as in fact Christ saith, "Blessed are the poor in spirit".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:27
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:28
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:29
verses.text: ) And (here) not simply, "with humility of mind," but, "with all humility".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:30
verses.text: For there are many kinds of humility, in word and in action, towards rulers, and toward the ruled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:31
verses.text: Will you that I mention to you some kinds of humility? There are some who are lowly towards those who are lowly, and high towards the high: this is not the character of humility.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:32
verses.text: Some then are such.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:33
