verses.text: Then, that he may not seem to be arrogant, he lays a foundation beforehand, removing that suspicion: For, "if, says he, I have acted 'with all humility of mind,' it is not from arrogance that I say the things I say".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:34
verses.text: Then for his gentleness, ever with much condescension making them his fellows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:35
verses.text: "With you," he says, "have I been, serving the Lord;" he makes the good works common to them with himself: none of it his own peculiar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:36
verses.text: "What?" (you will say) "why, against God could he possibly bear himself arrogantly?" And yet there are many who do bear themselves arrogantly against God: but this man not even against his own disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:37
verses.text: This is the merit of a teacher, by his own achievements of virtue to form the character of his disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:38
verses.text: Then for his fortitude, upon which also he is very concise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:39
verses.text: "With many tears," he says, "and temptations which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:40
verses.text: Do you see that he grieves at their doings? But here too he seems to show how sympathizing he was: for he suffered for those who were going to perdition, for the doers themselves: what was done to himself, he even rejoiced at it; for he belonged to that band which "rejoiced that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for that Name" (Acts v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:41
verses.text: ): and again he says, "Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you" (Col.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:42
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:43
verses.text: ): and again, "For our light affliction, which is but for the moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:44
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:45
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:47
verses.text: These things, however, he says, by way of making the least of his merits (μετριάζων).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:48
verses.text: But there he show his fortitude, not so much of daring, as of enduring: "I," says he, "have been evil entreated, but it was with you: and what is indeed the grievous part of the business, at the hands of Jews".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:49
verses.text: Observe, he puts here both love and fortitude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:50
verses.text: Mark, here, I pray you, a character of teaching: "I kept back nothing," he says, ungrudging fulness, unshrinking promptness—"of what was profitable unto you:" because there were things which they did not need to learn.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:51
verses.text: For as the hiding some things would have been like grudging, so the saying all things would be folly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:52
verses.text: This is why he adds, "that was profitable unto you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:53
verses.text: But have showed you, and have taught you:" have not only said, but also taught: not doing this either as a mere matter of form.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:54
verses.text: For that this is what he means, observe what he says: "publicly, and from house to house:" thereby representing the exceeding toil, the great earnestness and endurance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:55
verses.text: "Both Jews, and Greeks".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:56
verses.text: Not (addressing myself) to you alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:57
verses.text: "Testifying:" here, the boldness of speech: and that, even though we do no good, yet we must speak: for this is the meaning of "testifying," when we speak to those who do not pay attention: and so the word διαμαρτύρασθαι is for the most part used.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:58
verses.text: "I call heaven and earth to witness" (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:59
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:60
verses.text: ), διαμαρτύρομαι, Moses says: and now Paul himself, Διαμαρτυρόμενος "both to Jews and Greeks repentance toward God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:61
verses.text: What testifiest thou? That they should be careful about their manner of life: that they should repent, and draw near to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:62
verses.text: "Both to Jews and Greeks"—for neither did the Jews know Him—both by reason of their works, he says, "repentance towards God," and, by reason that they knew not the Son, he adds, "and faith in the Lord Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:63
verses.text: To what end, then, sayest thou these things? to what end dost thou put them in mind of them? What has come of it? hast thou anything to lay to their charge? Having first alarmed their feeling, then he adds, "And now, behold, I go bound in the Spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there: save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:64
verses.text: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the Gospel of the grace of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:65
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:66
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:67
verses.text: Wherefore says he this? By way of preparing them to be always ready to meet dangers, whether seen or unseen, and in all things to obey the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:68
verses.text: He shows that it is for great objects that he is led away from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:69
verses.text: "Save that the Holy Ghost," he says, "in every city witnesseth to me saying"—to show that he departs willingly; that (see Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:70
verses.text: xlv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:71
verses.text: p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:72
verses.text: ) you may not imagine it any bond or necessity, when he says, "bound in the Spirit—that in every city bonds and afflictions await me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:73
verses.text: Then also he adds this, "I count not my life dear, until I shall have fulfilled my course and the ministry, which I received of the Lord Jesus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:74
verses.text: Until I shall have finished my course, says he, with joy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:75
verses.text: Do you mark how (clearly) these were the words not of one lamenting, but of one who forbore to make the most (of his troubles) (μετριάζοντος), of one who would instruct those (whom he addressed), and sympathize with them in the things which were befalling He says not, "I grieve indeed, but one must needs bear it:" "but," says he, "of none of those things do I make account, neither do I have," i-e: account "my life dear to me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:76
verses.text: Why this again? not to extol himself, but to teach them, as by the former words, humility, so by these, fortitude and boldness: "I have it not precious," i-e: "I love it not before this: I account it more precious to finish my course, to testify".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:77
verses.text: And he says not, "to preach," "to teach"—but what says he? "to testify (διαμαρτύρασθαι)—the Gospel of the grace of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:78
verses.text: He is about to say something more uncomfortable (φορτικώτερον), namely, "I am pure from the blood of all men (because on my part) there is nothing lacking:" he is about to lay upon them the whole weight and burden: so he first mollifies their feelings by saying, "And now behold I know that ye shall see my face no more".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:79
verses.text: The consolation is twofold: both that "my face ye shall see no more," for in heart I am with you: and that it was not they alone (who should see him no more): for, "ye shall see my face no more, ye all, among whom I have gone about preaching the Kingdom".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:80
verses.text: So that he may well (say), "Wherefore I take you to record (read διὸ μαρτ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:81
verses.text: for διαμαρτ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:82
verses.text: ),—seeing I shall be with you no more—"that I am pure from the blood of all men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:83
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:84
verses.text: ) Do you mark how he terrifies them, and troubled and afflicted as their souls are, how hard he rubs them (ἐπιτρίβει)? But it was necessary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:85
verses.text: "For I have not shunned," he says, "to declare unto you all the counsel of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:86
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:87
verses.text: ) Why then, he who does not speak, has blood to answer for: that is, murder! Nothing could be more terrifying than this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:88
verses.text: He shows that they also, if they do it not, have blood to answer for.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:89
verses.text: So, whereas he seems to be justifying himself, in fact he is terrifying them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:90
verses.text: "Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers (or, bishops) to feed the Church of God (see note ), which He hath purchased with His own blood".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:91
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:92
verses.text: ) Do you mark? he enjoins them two things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:93
verses.text: Neither success in bringing others right of itself is any gain—for, I fear, he says, "lest by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a cast-away" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:94
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:95
verses.text: ); nor the being diligent for one's self alone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:96
verses.text: For such an one is selfish, and seeks his own good only, and is like to him who buried his talent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:97
verses.text: "Take heed to yourselves:" this he says, not because our own salvation is more precious than that of the flock, but because, when we take heed to ourselves, then the flock also is a gainer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:98
verses.text: "In which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the Church of God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:99
verses.text: See, it is from the Spirit ye have your ordination.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:100
verses.text: This is one constraint: then he says, "To feed the Church of the Lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:101
verses.text: Lo! another obligation: the Church is the Lord's.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:102
verses.text: And a third: "which He hath purchased with His own blood".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:103
verses.text: It shows how precious the concern is; that the peril is about no small matters, seeing that even His own blood He spared not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:104
verses.text: He indeed, that he might reconcile those who were enemies, poured out even His blood: but thou, even when they are become thy friends, art not able to retain them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:105
verses.text: "For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:106
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:107
verses.text: ) Again he engages (ἐπιστρέφει) them from another quarter, from the things which should come after: as when he says, "We wrestle not against flesh and blood.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:108
verses.text: After my departing," he says, "grievous wolves shall enter in among you" (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:109
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:110
verses.text: ); twofold the evil, both that he himself would not be present, and that others would assail them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:111
verses.text: "Then why depart, if thou knowest this beforehand?" The Spirit draws me, he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:112
verses.text: Both "wolves," and "grievous, not sparing the flock;" and what is worse, even "from among your own selves:" the grievous thing (this), when the war is moreover an intestine war.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:113
verses.text: The matter is exceeding serious, for it is "the Church of the Lord:" great the peril for with blood He redeemed it: mighty the war, and twofold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:114
verses.text: "Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:116
verses.text: ) "How then? what comfort shall there be?" "Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:117
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:118
verses.text: ) See how many strong expressions are here: "with tears," and "night and day," and "every one".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:119
verses.text: For it was not that if he saw many, then he came in (to the work), but even were it for a single soul, he was capable of doing everything (for that one soul).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:120
verses.text: So it was, in fact, that he compacted them together (συνεκρότησεν) (so firmly as he did).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:121
verses.text: "Enough done on my part: three years have I remained:" they had establishing enough, he says; enough of roofing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:122
verses.text: "With tears," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:123
verses.text: Seest thou that the tears were on this account? The bad man grieves not: grieve thou: perhaps he will grieve also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:124
verses.text: As, when the sick man sees his physician partaking of food, he also is incited to do the same: so likewise here, when he sees thee weeping, he is softened: he will be a good and great man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:125
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:126
verses.text: ) "Not knowing," he says, "the things that shall befall me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:127
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:128
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:129
verses.text: ) Then is this why thou departest? By no means; on the contrary (I know that), "bonds and afflictions await me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:130
verses.text: That (there are) trials, I know, but of what kind I know not: which was more grievous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:131
verses.text: "But none of these things move me" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:132
verses.text: ): for do not suppose that I say these things as lamenting them: for "I hold not my own life dear".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:133
verses.text: It is to raise up their minds that he says all this, and to persuade them not only not to flee, but also to bear nobly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:134
verses.text: Therefore it is that he calls it a "course" and a "ministry," on the one hand, showing it to be glorious from its being a race, on the other, showing what was due from it, as being a ministry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:135
verses.text: I am a minister: nothing more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:136
verses.text: Having comforted them, that they might not grieve that he was so evil entreated, and having told them that he endured those things "with joy," and having shown the fruits of them, then (and not before) he brings in that which would give them pain, that he may not overwhelm their minds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:137
verses.text: "And now behold," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:138
verses.text: "Wherefore I take you to record, that I am pure from the blood of all men, because I have not shrunk from declaring unto you the whole counsel of God" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 122:139

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:1
verses.text: that (counsel) which concerns the present matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:2
verses.text: "For I know this," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:3
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:4
verses.text: ) "What then," someone might say, "thinkest thou thyself so great? if thou shouldest depart, are we to die?" I say not this, he replies, that my absence causeth this: but what? That there should rise up against you certain of another sort: he says not, "because of my departing," but "after my departing:" that is, after his going on his journey.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:5
verses.text: —And yet this thing has happened already: much more (then will it happen) hereafter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:6
verses.text: Then we have the cause, "to draw away disciples after them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:7
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:8
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:9
verses.text: That there are heresies, this is the cause, and no other than this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:10
verses.text: Then comes also consolation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:11
verses.text: But if He "purchased" it "with His own blood," He will assuredly stand forward in its defence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:12
verses.text: "Night and day," he says, "I cease not to warn with tears".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:13
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:14
verses.text: ) This might well be said in our case also: and though the speech seems to refer peculiarly to the teachers, it is common also to the disciples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:15
verses.text: For what, though I speak and exhort and weep night and day, while the disciple obeys not? Therefore it is that he says, "I take you to record:" since also himself says, "I am pure from the blood of all men: for I have not shunned to declare unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:16
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:17
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:18
verses.text: ) Why then, this only is to be a teacher, to declare, to preach, to instruct, shrink from nothing, to exhort night and day: but if, while one is doing all this, nothing comes of it, ye know what remains.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:19
verses.text: Then ye have another justification: "I am pure from the blood of all men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:20
verses.text: Think not that these words are spoken to us only: for indeed this speech is addressed to you also, that ye should attend to the things spoken, that ye should not start away from the hearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:21
verses.text: What can I do? Lo! each day I rend myself with crying out, "Depart from the theatres:" and many laugh at us: "Desist from swearing, from covetousness:" numberless are our exhortations, and there is none to hear us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:22
verses.text: But I do not discourse during night? Fain would I do this also in the night time, and at your tables, if it were possible that one could be divided into ten thousand pieces, so as to be present with you and discourse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:23
verses.text: But if once in the week we call to you, and ye shrink back, and some of you do not even come here, and you that do come, depart having received no profit,—what shall we do? Many I know even sneer at us, that we are forever discoursing about the same things: so wearisome are we become to you by very satiety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:24
verses.text: But for this not we are to blame, but the hearers may thank themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:25
verses.text: For he indeed who is making good progress, rejoices to hear the same things always; it seems to be his praises that he hears spoken: but he who does not wish to get on, seems even to be annoyed, and though he hear the same thing but twice, it seems to him that he is hearing it often.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:26
verses.text: "I am pure," he says, "from the blood of all men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:28
verses.text: ) This was fit and proper for Paul to say, but we dare not say it, conscious as we are of numberless faults.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:29
verses.text: Wherefore for him the ever vigilant, ever at hand, the man enduring all things for the sake of the salvation of his disciples, it was fit and proper to say this: but we must say that of Moses, "The Lord was wroth with me for your sakes" (Deut.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:30
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:31
verses.text: ), because ye lead us also into many sins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:32
verses.text: For when we are dispirited at seeing you make no progress, is not the greater part of our strength struck down? For what, I ask you has been done? Lo! by the grace of God we also have now passed the space of three years, not indeed night and day exhorting you, but doing this, often every third day, or every seventh.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:33
verses.text: What more has come of it? We accuse, we rebuke, we weep, we are in anguish, although not openly, yet in heart.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:34
verses.text: But those (inward) tears are far more bitter than these (outward ones): for these indeed bring a kind of relief to the feelings of the sorrowful, whereas those aggravate it, and bind it fast.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:35
verses.text: Since when there is any cause of grief, and one cannot give vent to the sorrow, lest he should seem to be vainglorious, think what he suffers! Were it not that people would tax me with excessive love of display, you would see me each day shedding fountains of tears: but to those my chamber is witness, and my hours of solitude.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:36
verses.text: For believe me I have (at times) despaired of my own salvation, but from my mourning on your account, I have not even leisure to bemoan my own evils: so entirely are ye all in all to me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:37
verses.text: And whether I perceive you to be advancing, then, for very delight, I am not sensible of my own evils: or whether I see you not advancing, such is my grief, I again dismiss my own cares from my thoughts: brightening up on account of your good things, though I myself have evils without number, and saddened on account of your painful things, though my own successes are without number.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:38
verses.text: For what hope is there for the teacher, when his flock is destroyed? What kind of life, what kind of expectation is there for him? With what sort of confidence will he stand up before God? what will he say? For grant that he has nothing laid to his charge, has no punishment to suffer, but is "pure from the blood of all men:" yet even so will he suffer a grief incurable: since fathers also though they be not liable to be called to account for their children's sins, nevertheless have grief and vexation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:39
verses.text: And this profits them nothing, nor shields them (προίσταται).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:40
verses.text: "For it is they that watch for our souls, as those that must give account".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:41
verses.text: (Heb.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:42
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:43
verses.text: ) This seems to be a fearful thing: to me this gives no concern after your destruction.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:44
verses.text: For whether I give account, or not, it is no profit to me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:45
verses.text: Might it be, that ye were saved, and I to give account because of you: ye saved, and I charged with not having fulfiled my part! For my anxiety is not that you should be saved through me as the means, but only that you should be saved, no matter by what person as the instrument.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:46
verses.text: Ye know not the pangs of spiritual childbirth, how overpowering they are; how he who is in travail with this birth, would rather be cut into ten thousand pieces, than see one of those to whom he has given birth perishing and undone.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:47
verses.text: Whence shall we persuade you? By no other argument indeed, but by what has been done, in all that regards you we shall clear ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:48
verses.text: We too shall be able to say, that in nothing have we "shrunk from declaring" to you the whole truth: nevertheless we grieve: and that we do grieve, is manifest from the numberless plans we lay and contrivances we devise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:49
verses.text: And yet we might say to ourselves, What matters it to me? I have done my part, "I am pure from" (their) "blood:" but this is not enough for comfort.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:50
verses.text: If we could tear open our heart, and show it to you, ye would see with what largeness it holds (you) within it, both women and children and men; for such is the power of love, that it makes the soul more spacious than the heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:51
verses.text: "Receive us," says (Paul): "we have wronged no man, ye are not straitened in us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:52
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:53
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:54
verses.text: ; vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:55
verses.text: ) He had all Corinth in his heart, and says, "Ye are not straitened: be ye also enlarged" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:56
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:57
verses.text: ); but I myself could not say this, for I well know, that ye both love me and receive me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:58
verses.text: But what is the profit either from my love or from yours, when the things pertaining to God thrive not in us? It is a ground for greater sorrow, an occasion of worse mischief (λύμης, al.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:59
verses.text: λύπης).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:60
verses.text: I have nothing to lay to your charge: "for I bear you record, that, if it had been possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:61
verses.text: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:62
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:63
verses.text: ) "We yearn not only to give you the Gospel, but also our own souls".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:64
verses.text: ( Thess.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:65
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:66
verses.text: ) We are loved and we love (you): but this is not the question.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:67
verses.text: But let us love Christ, "for the first commandment is, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God: and the second is like unto it, And thy neighbor as thyself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:68
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:69
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:70
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:71
verses.text: ) We have the second, we need the first: need the first, exceedingly, both I and you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:72
verses.text: We have it, but not as we ought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 125:73
verses.text: Let us love Him: ye know how great a reward is laid up for them that love Christ: let us love Him with fervor of soul, that, enjoying his goodwill, we may escape the stormy waves of this present life, and be found worthy to obtain the good things promised to them that love Him, through the grace and mercy of His only-begotten Son, with whom to the Father, together with the Holy Ghost, be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:1
verses.text: Homily XLV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:2
verses.text: Acts XX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:3
verses.text: "And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of His grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them that are sanctified".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:4
verses.text: What he does when writing in an Epistle, this he does also when speaking in council: from exhorting, he ends with prayer: for since he had much alarmed them by saying, "Grievous wolves shall enter in among you" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:5
verses.text: ), therefore, not to overpower them, and make them lose all self-possession, observe the consolation (he gives).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:6
verses.text: "And now," he says, as always, "I commend you, brethren, to God, and to the word of His grace:" that is, to His grace: it is grace that saveth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:7
verses.text: He constantly puts them in mind of grace, to make them more earnest as being debtors, and to persuade them to have confidence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:8
verses.text: "Which is able to build you up".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:9
verses.text: He does not say, to build, but, "to build up," showing that they had (already) been built.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:10
verses.text: Then he puts them in mind of the hope to come; "to give you an inheritance," he says, "among all them which are sanctified".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:11
verses.text: Then exhortation again: "I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:12
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:13
verses.text: ) He takes away that which is the root of evils, the love of money.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:14
verses.text: "Silver, or gold," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:15
verses.text: He says not, I have not taken, but, not even "coveted".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:16
verses.text: No great thing this, but what follows after is great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:17
verses.text: "Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:18
verses.text: I have showed you all things, how that so laboring, ye ought to support the weak".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:20
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:21
verses.text: ) Observe him employed in work and not simply that, but toiling.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:22
verses.text: "These hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me:" so as to put them to shame.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:23
verses.text: And see how worthily of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:24
verses.text: For he says not, Ye ought to show yourselves superior to money, but what? "to support the weak"—not all indiscriminately—"and to hear the word of the Lord which He spake, It is more blessed to give than to receive".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:25
verses.text: For lest any one should think that it was spoken with reference to them, and that he gave himself for an ensample, as he elsewhere says, "giving an ensample to you" (Phil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:26
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:27
verses.text: ), he added the declaration of Christ, Who said, "It is more blessed to give than to receive".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:28
verses.text: He prayed over them while exhorting them: he shows it both by action,—"And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:29
verses.text: )—he did not simply pray, but with much feeling: (κατανύξεως): great was the consolation—and by his saying, "I commend you to the Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:30
verses.text: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck and kissed him, sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:32
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:33
verses.text: ) He had said, that "grievous wolves should enter in;" had said, "I am pure from the blood of all men:" and yet the thing that grieved them most of all was this, "that they should see him no more:" since indeed it was this that made the war grievous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:34
verses.text: "And they accompanied them," it says, "unto the ship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:35
verses.text: And it came to pass, that after we had torn ourselves from them"—so much did they love him, such was their affection towards him—"and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara: and finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:36
verses.text: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre" (Acts xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:37
verses.text: –): he came to Lycia, and having left Cyprus, he sailed down to Tyre—"for there the ship was to unlade her burden.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:38
verses.text: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:40
verses.text: ) They too prophesy of the afflictions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:41
verses.text: It is so ordered that they should be spoken by them also, that none might imagine that Paul said those things without cause, and only by way of boasting.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:42
verses.text: And there again they part from each other with prayer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:43
verses.text: "And when we had accomplished those days, we departed, and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:44
verses.text: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:45
verses.text: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:46
verses.text: And the next day we that were of Paul's company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:48
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:49
verses.text: ) Having come to Caesarea, it says, we abode with Philip, which was one of the seven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:50
verses.text: "And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:51
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:52
verses.text: ) But it is not these that foretell to Paul, though they were prophetesses; it is Agabus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:53
verses.text: "And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judea a certain prophet, named Agabus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:54
verses.text: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul's girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:55
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:56
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:57
verses.text: ) He who formerly had declared about the famine, the same says, This "man, who owneth this girdle, thus shall they bind".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:58
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:59
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:60
verses.text: ) The same that the prophets used to do, representing events to the sight, when they spoke about the captivity—as did Ezekiel—the same did this (Agabus).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:61
verses.text: "And," what is the grievous part of the business, "deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:62
verses.text: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:63
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:64
verses.text: ) Many even besought him not to depart, and still he would not comply.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:65
verses.text: "Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:66
verses.text: ) Do you mark? Lest, having heard that saying, "I go bound in the Spirit" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:67
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:68
verses.text: ), you should imagine it a matter of necessity, or that he fell into it ignorantly, therefore these things are foretold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:69
verses.text: But they wept, and he comforted them, grieving at their tears.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:70
verses.text: For, "what mean ye," he says, "to weep and to break my heart?" Nothing could be more affectionate: because he saw them weeping, he grieved, he that felt no pain at his own trials.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:71
verses.text: "For I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:72
verses.text: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:73
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:74
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:75
verses.text: ) Ye do me wrong in doing this: for do I grieve? Then they ceased, when he said, "to break my heart".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:76
verses.text: I weep, he says, for you, not on account of my own sufferings: as for those (men), I am willing even to die for them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:77
verses.text: But let us look over again what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:78
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:79
verses.text: ) "Silver, or gold, or apparel," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:80
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:81
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:82
verses.text: , ;  Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:83
verses.text: ix;  Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:84
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:85
verses.text: ) So then, it was not in Corinth only that they did this—they that corrupted the disciples, but in Asia as well.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:86
verses.text: But he nowhere casts this up as a reproach to the Ephesians, when writing to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:87
verses.text: And why? Because he did not fall upon any subject that obliged him to speak of this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:88
verses.text: But to the Corinthians he says, "My boasting has not been stopped in the regions of Achaia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:89
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:90
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:91
verses.text: ) And he does not say, Ye did not give to me; but, "Silver, or gold, or apparel, I coveted not," that it might not seem to be their doing, that they had not given.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:92
verses.text: And he does not say, From no man have I coveted the necessaries of life, that again it might not look like accusing them: but he covertly hints as much, seeing that he provided subsistence for others as well as himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:93
verses.text: See how he worked with earnestness, "night and day" discoursing (to others), "with tears warning each one of them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:94
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:95
verses.text: ) (Here) again he puts them in fear: "I have showed you all things," he says: ye cannot take refuge in the plea of ignorance: "have shown you" by works "how that so laboring ye ought to work".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:96
verses.text: And he does not say, that to receive is bad, but that not to receive is better.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:97
verses.text: For, "remember," he says, "the words of the Lord which he spake: It is more blessed to give than to receive".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:98
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:99
verses.text: ) And where said He this? Perhaps the Apostles delivered it by unwritten tradition; or else it is plain from (recorded sayings, from) which one could infer it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:100
verses.text: For in fact here he has shown both boldness in meeting dangers, sympathy with those over whom he ruled, teaching with (unshrinking) boldness, humility, (voluntary) poverty: but, what we have here is even more than that poverty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:101
verses.text: For if He says there (in the Gospel), "If thou wilt be perfect, sell what thou hast and give to the poor" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:102
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:103
verses.text: ), when, besides receiving nothing himself, he provides sustenance for others also, what could equal this? It is one degree to fling away one's possessions; a second, to be sufficient for the supply of one's own necessities: a third, to provide for others also; a fourth, for one (to do all this) who preaches and has a right to receive.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:104
verses.text: So that here is a man far better than those who merely forego possessions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:105
verses.text: "Thus it is right to support the weak:" this is (indeed) sympathy with the weak; for to give from the labors of others, is easy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:106
verses.text: "And they fell on his neck," it says, "and wept".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:107
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:108
verses.text: ) He shows their affection also by saying, "Upon his neck," as taking a last and yet a last embrace, such was the love they conceived from his discourse, such the spell of love that bound them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:109
verses.text: For if we groan when simply parting from each other, although we know that we shall receive one another back again, what a tearing away of themselves it must have been to them! Methinks Paul also wept.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:110
verses.text: "Having torn ourselves away," he says: he shows the violence of it by saying, "having torn ourselves away from them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:111
verses.text: And with reason: otherwise they could never have got to sea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:112
verses.text: What means, "We came with a straight course unto Coos?" Instead of saying, "we did not go round nor make stay in other places".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:113
verses.text: Then "unto Rhodes".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:114
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:115
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:116
verses.text: ) See how he hastes on.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:117
verses.text: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:118
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:119
verses.text: ) Possibly that ship (in which they had come) was making a stay there: wherefore they shifted to another, and not having found one going to Caesarea, but (finding this) for Phenice, they embarked in it (and pursued their voyage), having left Cyprus also and Syria: but the expression, "having left it on the left hand," is not said simply (in that meaning), but that they made speed not to get to Syria either.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:120
verses.text: "We landed at Tyre".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:121
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:122
verses.text: ) Then they tarry with the brethren seven days.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:123
verses.text: Now that they were come near to Jerusalem, they no longer run.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:124
verses.text: (b) "Who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:125
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:126
verses.text: ) Observe how, when the Spirit does not forbid, he complies.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:127
verses.text: They said, "Adventure not thyself into the theatre, and he did not adventure" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:128
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:129
verses.text: ): often they bore him off (from dangers), and he complied: again he escaped by a window: and now, though numberless persons, so to say, beseech him, both those at Tyre and those at Caesarea, weeping also and predicting numberless dangers, he refuses to comply.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:130
verses.text: And yet it is not (merely), they predicted the dangers, but "said by the Spirit".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:131
verses.text: If then the Spirit bade, why did he gainsay? "By the Spirit," that is, they knowing "by the Spirit" (what would be the consequences, said to him): for of course it does not mean that the exhortation they made was by the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:132
verses.text: For they did not simply foretell to him the dangers (through the Spirit), but (added of themselves) that it behooved him not to go up—sparing him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:133
verses.text: But "after we had accomplished the days," i-e: had fulfilled the appointed days, "we separated, and went on our way: they all bringing us on our way with wives and children".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:134
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:135
verses.text: )—See how great was the entreaty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:136
verses.text: And again they part with prayer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:137
verses.text: Also in Ptolemais they stay one day, but in Caesarea many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:138
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:139
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:140
verses.text: ) (a) Now that they are near to Jerusalem, they no longer hurry.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:141
verses.text: For observe, I pray you, all the days.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:142
verses.text: "After the day of unleavened bread" they came "to Troas in five days" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:143
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:144
verses.text: ); then they there spent "seven;" in all, twelve: then to "Thasos," to "Mytilene," to "Trogylium" and "over against Chios," and to "Samos" and "Miletus" (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:145
verses.text: –); eighteen in all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:146
verses.text: Then to "Cos," to "Rhodes," to "Patara," twenty-one: then say five to "Tyre;" twenty-six: there "seven;" thirty-three; "Ptolemais," thirty-four; then to "Caesarea, many days" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:147
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:148
verses.text: –); and then, thereafter, the prophet puts them up thence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:149
verses.text: (c) When Paul has heard that he has to suffer numberless perils, then he is in haste, not flinging himself upon the dangers but accounting it to be the command of the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:150
verses.text: (e) And Agabus does not say, "They shall bind" Paul, that he may not seem to speak upon agreement (with Paul), but "the man that owneth this girdle" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:151
verses.text: )—so then he had a girdle also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:152
verses.text: But when they could not persuade him—this was why they wept—then they "held their peace".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:153
verses.text: Do you mark the resignation? do you mark the affection? "They held their peace," it says, "saying, The will of the Lord be done".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:154
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:155
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:156
verses.text: ) (g) The Lord, say they, Himself will do that which is pleasing in his sight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:157
verses.text: For they perceived that it was the will of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:158
verses.text: Else Paul would not be so bent (upon going)—he that on all (other occasions delivers himself out of dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:159
verses.text: (d) "And after these, days," it says, "having taken up our baggage"—i-e: having received the (supplies) necessary for the journey—"we went up to Jerusalem".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:160
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:161
verses.text: ) "And there went with us also certain of the disciples from Caesarea, bringing us to one with whom we should lodge, one Mnason, an ancient disciple of Cyprus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:162
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:163
verses.text: ) "And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:164
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:165
verses.text: ) (f) "Bringing us," it says, "(to him) with whom we should lodge"—not to the church: for on the former occasion (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:166
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:167
verses.text: ), when they went up concerning the decrees, they lodged with the Church, but now with a certain "ancient disciple".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:168
verses.text: (The expression) shows that the preaching had been going on a long time: whence it seems to me that this writer in the Acts epitomizes the events of many years, relating (only) the matters of chief importance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:169
verses.text: (h) So unwilling were they to burthen the Church, when there was another to lodge them; and so little did they stand upon their dignity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:170
verses.text: "The brethren," it says, "received us gladly".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:171
verses.text: Affairs among the Jews were now full of peace: there was not much warfare (among them).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:172
verses.text: "Bringing us," it says, "to one with whom we should lodge".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:173
verses.text: Paul was the guest he entertained.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:174
verses.text: Perchance some one of you says: Aye, if it were given me to entertain Paul as a guest, I readily and with much eagerness would do this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:175
verses.text: Lo! it is in thy power to entertain Paul's Master for thy guest, and thou wilt not: for "he that receiveth one of these least," he saith, "receiveth Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:176
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:177
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:178
verses.text: ; Luke ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:179
verses.text: ) By how much the brother may be least, so much the more does Christ come to thee through him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:180
verses.text: For he that receives the great, often does it from vainglory also; but he that receives the small, does it purely for Christ's sake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:181
verses.text: It is in thy power to entertain even the Father of Christ as thy guest, and thou will not: for, "I was a stranger," He says, "and ye took me in" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:182
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:183
verses.text: ): and again, "Unto one of the least of these the brethren that believe on Me, ye have done it unto Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:184
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:185
verses.text: ) Though it be not Paul, yet if it be a believer and a brother, although the least, Christ cometh to thee through him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:186
verses.text: Open thine house, take Him in.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:187
verses.text: "He that receiveth a prophet," He saith, "shall receive a prophet's reward".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:188
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:189
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:190
verses.text: ) Therefore too he that receives Christ, shall receive the reward of him who has Christ for his guest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:191
verses.text: Do not thou disbelieve His words, but be believing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:192
verses.text: Himself hath said, Through them I come to thee: and that thou mayest not disbelieve, He lays down both punishments for those who do not receive, and honors for those who do receive; since He would not have done this, unless both the person honored and the person insulted were Himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:193
verses.text: "Thou receivedst Me," He saith, "into thy lodging, I will receive thee into the Kingdom of My Father; thou tookest away My hunger, I take away thy sins; thou sawest Me bound, I see thee loosed; thou sawest Me a stranger, I make thee a citizen of heaven; thou gavest Me bread, I give thee an entire Kingdom, that thou mayest inherit and possess it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:194
verses.text: He saith not, "Receive," but, "Inherit," the word which is spoken of those who have possession by right of ownership; as when we say, "This have I inherited".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:195
verses.text: Thou didst it to Me in secret, I will proclaim it openly: and of thine acts indeed I say, that they were of free gift, but Mine are of debt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:196
verses.text: "For since thou," He saith, "didst begin, I follow and come after: I am not ashamed to confess the benefits conferred on Me, nor from what things thou didst free Me, hunger and nakedness and wandering.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:197
verses.text: Thou sawest Me bound, thou shalt not behold the fire of hell; thou sawest Me sick, thou shalt not behold the torments nor the punishments".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:198
verses.text: O hands, truly blessed, which minister in such services as these, which are accounted worthy to serve Christ! Feet which go into prisons for Christ's sake, with ease defy the fire: no trial of bonds have they, (the hands) which saw Him bound! Thou clothedst Him with a garment, and thou puttest on a garment of salvation: thou wast in prison with Him, and with Him thou findest thyself in the Kingdom, not ashamed, knowing that thou visitedst Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:199
verses.text: The Patriarch knew not that he was entertaining Angels, and he did entertain them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:200
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:201
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:202
verses.text: ) Let us take shame to ourselves, I beseech you: he was sitting in mid-day, being in a foreign land, where he had none inheritance, "not so much as to set his foot on" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:203
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:204
verses.text: ): he was a stranger, and the stranger entertained strangers: for he was a citizen of heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:205
verses.text: Therefore, not even while he was on earth was he a stranger (to Him).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:206
verses.text: We are rather strangers than that stranger, if we receive not strangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:207
verses.text: He had no home, and his tent was his place of reception.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:208
verses.text: And mark his liberality—he killed a calf, and kneaded fine meal: mark his ready mind—by himself and his wife: mark the unassuming manner—he worships and beseeches them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:209
verses.text: For all these qualities ought to be in that man who entertains strangers—readiness, cheerfulness, liberality.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:210
verses.text: For the soul of the stranger is abashed, and feels ashamed; and unless (his host) show excessive joy, he is as (if) slighted, and goes away, and it becomes worse than not to have received him, his being received in this way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:211
verses.text: Therefore he worships them, therefore he welcomes them with speech, therefore with a seat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:212
verses.text: For who would have hesitated, knowing that this work was done unto Him? "But we are not in a foreign land".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:213
verses.text: If we will, we shall be able to imitate him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:214
verses.text: How many of the brethren are strangers? There is a common apartment, the Church, which we call the "Xenon".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:215
verses.text: Be inquisitive (περιεργάζεσθε), sit before the doors, receive those who come yourselves; though you may not wish to take them into your houses, at any rate in some other way (receive them), by supplying them with necessaries.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:216
verses.text: "Why, has not the Church means" you will say? She has: but what is that to you? that they should be fed from the common funds of the Church, can that benefit you? If another man prays, does it follow that you are not bound to pray? Wherefore do you not say, "Do not the priests pray? then why should I pray?" "But I," you will say, "give to him who cannot be received there".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:217
verses.text: Give, though it be to that one: for what we are anxious for is this, that you should give at any rate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:218
verses.text: Hear what Paul says: "That it may relieve them that are widows indeed, and that the Church be not burdened".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:219
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:220
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:221
verses.text: ) Be it how you will, only do it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:222
verses.text: But I put it, not, "that the Church be not burdened," but, "that thou be not burdened;" for at this rate thou wilt do nothing, leaving all to the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:223
verses.text: This is why there is a common room set apart by the Church, that you may not say these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:224
verses.text: "The Church," say you, "has lands, has money, and revenues".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:225
verses.text: And has she not charges? I ask; and has she not a daily expenditure? "No doubt," you will say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:226
verses.text: Why then do you not lend aid to her moderate means? I am ashamed indeed to say these things: however, I compel no man, if any one imagines what I am saying to be for gain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:227
verses.text: Make for yourself a guest-chamber in your own house: set up a bed there, set up a table there and a candlestick.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:228
verses.text: (comp.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:229
verses.text: Kings iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:230
verses.text: ) For is it not absurd, that whereas, if soldiers should come, you have rooms set apart for them, and show much care for them, and furnish them with everything, because they keep off from you the visible war of this world, yet strangers have no place where they might abide? Gain a victory over the Church.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:231
verses.text: Would you put us to shame? This do: surpass us in liberality: have a room, to which Christ may come; say, "This is Christ's cell; this building is set apart for Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:232
verses.text: Be it but an underground chamber, and mean, He disdains it not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:233
verses.text: "Naked and a stranger," Christ goes about, it is but a shelter He wants: afford it, though but this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:234
verses.text: Be not uncompassionate, nor inhuman; be not so earnest in worldly matters, so cold in spiritual.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:235
verses.text: Let also the most faithful of thy servants be the one entrusted with this office, and let him bring in the maimed, the beggars, and the homeless.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:236
verses.text: These things I say to shame you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:237
verses.text: For ye ought indeed to receive them in the upper part of your house; but if ye will not do this, then though it be below, though but where thy mules are housed, and thy servants, there receive Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:238
verses.text: Perchance ye shudder at hearing this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:239
verses.text: What then, when ye do not even this? Behold, I exhort, behold, I bid you; let this be a matter to be taken up in earnest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:240
verses.text: But ye do not wish it thus, perhaps? Do it some other way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:241
verses.text: There are many poor men and poor women: set apart some one (of these) constantly to remain there: let the poor man be (thine inmate) though but as a guard to thy house: let him be to thee wall and fence, shield and spear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:242
verses.text: Where alms are, the devil dares not approach, nor any other evil thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:243
verses.text: Let us not overlook so great a gain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:244
verses.text: But now a place is set apart for a chariot, and for litters (βαστερνίοις) another; but for Christ Who is wandering, not even one! Abraham received the strangers in the place where he abode himself; his wife stood in the place of a servant, the guests in the place of masters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:245
verses.text: He knew not that he was receiving Christ; knew not that he was receiving Angels; so that had he known it, he would have lavished his whole substance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:246
verses.text: But we, who know that we receive Christ, show not even so much zeal as he did who thought that he was receiving men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:247
verses.text: "But they are impostors," you will say, "many of them, and unthankful".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:248
verses.text: And for this the greater thy reward, when thou receivest for the sake of Christ's name.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:249
verses.text: For if thou knowest indeed that they are impostors, receive them not into thy house: but if thou dost not know this, why dost thou accuse them lightly? "Therefore I tell them to go to the receiving house".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:250
verses.text: But what kind of excuse is there for us, when we do not even receive those whom we know, but shut our doors against all? Let our house be Christ's general receptacle: let us demand of them as a reward, not money, but that they make our house the receptacle for Christ; let us run about everywhere, let us drag them in, let us seize our booty: greater are the benefits we receive than what we confer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:251
verses.text: He does not bid thee kill a calf: give thou bread to the hungry, raiment to the naked, shelter to the stranger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:252
verses.text: But that thou mayest not make this thy pretext, there is a common apartment, that of the Church; throw thy money into that, and then thou hast received them: since (Abraham) there had the reward of those things also which were done by his servants.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:253
verses.text: "He gave the calf to a young man, and he hasted to dress it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:254
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:255
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:256
verses.text: ) So well trained were his servants also! They ran, and murmured not as ours do: for he had made them pious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:257
verses.text: He drew them out to war, and they murmured not: so well disciplined were they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:258
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:259
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:260
verses.text: ) For he had equal care for all as for himself: he all but said as Job did, "We were alike formed in the same womb".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:261
verses.text: (Job xxxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:262
verses.text: ) Therefore let us also take thought for their salvation, and let us make it our duty to care for our servants, that they may be good; and let our servants also be instructed in the things pertaining to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:263
verses.text: Then will virtue not be difficult to us, if we train them orderly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:264
verses.text: Just as in war, when the soldiers are well-disciplined, the general carries on war easily, but the contrary happens, when this is not so; and when the sailors too are of one mind, the pilot easily handles the rudder-strings; so here likewise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:265
verses.text: For say now, if thy servants have been so schooled, thou wilt not be easily exasperated, thou wilt not have to find fault, wilt not be made angry, wilt not need to abuse them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:266
verses.text: It may be, thou wilt even stand in awe of thy servants, if they are worthy of admiration, and they will be helpers with thee, and will give thee good counsel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 126:267
verses.text: But from all these shall all things proceed that are pleasing to God, and thus shall the whole house be filled with blessing, and we, performing things pleasing to God, shall enjoy abundant succor from above, unto which may we all attain, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost, together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:1
verses.text: Homily XLVI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:2
verses.text: Acts XXI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:3
verses.text: ,  "And the day following Paul went in with us unto James: and all the elders were present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:4
verses.text: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:5
verses.text: This was the Bishop of Jerusalem; and to him (Paul) is sent on an earlier occasion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:6
verses.text: This (James) was brother of the Lord; a great and admirable man.
