verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:7
verses.text: (To him, it says,) "Paul entered in with us".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:8
verses.text: Mark the (Bishop's) unassuming behavior: "and the elders" (were present).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:9
verses.text: Again Paul relates to them the things relating to the Gentiles, not indulging in vainglory, God forbid, but wishing to show forth the mercy of God, and to fill them with great joy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:10
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:11
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:12
verses.text: ) See accordingly: "when they heard it," it says, "they glorified God,"—not praised nor admired Paul: for in such wise had he narrated, as referring all to Him—"and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:13
verses.text: Observe with what modest deference they too speak: "they said to him:" not (James) as Bishop discourses authoritatively, but they take Paul as partner with them in their view; "Thou seest, brother:" as though immediately and at the outset apologizing for themselves, and saying, "We did not wish this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:14
verses.text: Seest thou the necessity of the thing? 'how many thousands,' say they, 'of Jews there are which' have come together".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:15
verses.text: And they say not, "how many thousands we have made catechumens," but, "there are.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:16
verses.text: And these," say they, "are all zealous for the law".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:17
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:18
verses.text: ) Two reasons—the number of them, and their views.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:19
verses.text: For neither had they been few, would it have been right to despise them: nor, if they were many and did not all cling to the law, would there have been need to make much account of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:20
verses.text: Then also a third cause is given: "And they all," it says, "have been informed of thee"—they say not,"have heard," but κατηχήθησαν, that is, so they have believed, and have been taught, "that thou teachest apostasy from Moses to all the Jews which are among the Gentiles, by telling them not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:22
verses.text: ) "What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:23
verses.text: Do therefore this that we say to thee" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:24
verses.text: , ): they say these things as advising, not as commanding.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:25
verses.text: "We have four men which have a vow on them; them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:26
verses.text: Make thy defence in act, not in word—"that they may shave themselves," it says, "and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:27
verses.text: , ): they say not, "teachest," but, of superabundance, "that thou thyself also keepest the law".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:28
verses.text: For of course not this was the matter of chief interest, whether he did not teach others, but, that he did himself observe the law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:29
verses.text: "What then" (he might say), "if the Gentiles should learn it? I shall injure them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:30
verses.text: How so? say they, seeing that even we, the teachers of the Jews, have sent unto them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:31
verses.text: "As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:32
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:33
verses.text: ) Here with a kind of remonstrance (ἐντρεπτικὥς), As "we," say they, commanded them, although we are preachers to the Jews, so do thou, although a preacher to the Gentiles, cooperate with us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:34
verses.text: Observe Paul: he does not say, "Well, but I can bring forward Timothy, whom I circumcised: well, but I can satisfy them by what I have to say (of myself):" but he complied, and did all: for in fact thus was it expedient (to do).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:35
verses.text: For it was one thing to take (effectual) measures for clearing himself, and another to have done these things without the knowledge of any (of the parties).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:36
verses.text: It was a step open to no suspicion, the fact of his even bearing the expenses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:37
verses.text: "Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, signifying the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:39
verses.text: ) "Signifying," διαγγέλλων, i-e: καταγγέλλων, publicly notifying: so that it was he who made himself conspicuous.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:40
verses.text: "And when the seven days were about to be completed, the Jews from Asia"—for (his arrival) most keeps times with theirs—"when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him, crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:42
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:43
verses.text: ) Mark their habitual conduct, how turbulent we everywhere find it, how men who with or without reason make a clamor in the midst.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:44
verses.text: "For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:45
verses.text: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple and forthwith the doors were shut".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:48
verses.text: ) "Men of Israel," it says, "help: this is the man that (teaches) against the people, and the law, and this place".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:49
verses.text: —the things which most trouble them, the Temple and the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:50
verses.text: And Paul does not tax the Apostles with being the cause of these things to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:51
verses.text: "And they drew him," it says, "out of the Temple: and the doors were shut".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:52
verses.text: For they wished to kill him; and therefore were dragging him out, to do this with greater security.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:53
verses.text: "And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the tribune of the cohort, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:54
verses.text: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the tribune and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:55
verses.text: Then the tribune came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:56
verses.text: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:57
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:59
verses.text: ) But the tribune having come down delivered him, and "commanded him to be bound with two chains:" (hereby) appeasing the anger of the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:60
verses.text: "And when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:61
verses.text: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:62
verses.text: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him!" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:63
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:64
verses.text: ) What means, "Away with him?" that is, what they say with us according to the Roman custom, To the standards with him! "And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the tribune, May I speak unto thee?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:65
verses.text: ) In the act of being borne along up the stairs, he requests to say something to the tribune: and observe how quietly he does it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:66
verses.text: "May I speak unto thee?" he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:67
verses.text: "Who said, Canst thou speak Greek? Art thou not then that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:68
verses.text: ) For (this Egyptian) was a revolutionary and seditious person.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 127:69
verses.text: With regard to this then Paul clears himself, and.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:1
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:2
verses.text: ) "Do therefore this that we say unto thee," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:3
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:4
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:5
verses.text: ) He shows that it was not necessary to do this upon principle (προηγουμένως)—whence also they obtain his compliance—but that it was economy and condescension.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:6
verses.text: "As touching the Gentiles," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:7
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:8
verses.text: ) Why, then, this was no hindrance to the preaching, seeing they themselves legislated for them to this effect.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:9
verses.text: Why, then, in his taking Peter to task he does not absolutely (ἁπλὥς) charge him with doing wrong: for precisely what he does on this occasion himself, the same does Peter on that occasion, (merely) holding his peace, and establishing his doctrine.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:10
verses.text: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:11
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:12
verses.text: ) And he says not, For why? it is not right to teach those among the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:13
verses.text: "It is not enough to have not (so) preached there, but there was need also to do something more, that those may be persuaded that thou observest the law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:14
verses.text: The affair is one of condescension, be not alarmed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:15
verses.text: They do not advise him (to this course) sooner, until they have first spoken of the economy and the gain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:16
verses.text: "And besides, the doing this in Jerusalem, is a thing to be borne.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:17
verses.text: 'Do thou this thing therefore' here, that it may be in thy power abroad to do the other".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:18
verses.text: (b) "The next day," it says, "he took them" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:19
verses.text: ): he deferred it not; for when there is economy in the case, this is the way of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:20
verses.text: (a) "Jews from Asia having seen him," for it was natural that they were spending some days there, "in the Temple".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:22
verses.text: ) (c) Mark the economy (of Providence) that appeared (in this).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:23
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:24
verses.text: , note ) After the (believing) Jews had been persuaded (concerning him), then it is that those (Jews of Asia) set upon him in order that those (believing Jews) may not also set upon him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:25
verses.text: Help, say they, "ye men of Israel!" as though it were some (monster) difficult to be caught, and hard to be overcome, that has fallen into their hands.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:26
verses.text: "All men," they say, "everywhere, he ceaseth not to teach;" not here only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:27
verses.text: And then the accusation (is) more aggravated by the present circumstances.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:28
verses.text: "And yet more," say they, "he has polluted the temple, having brought into it men who are Greeks".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:29
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:30
verses.text: ) And yet in Christ's time there "came up (Greeks) to worship" (John xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:31
verses.text: ): true, but here it speaks of Greeks who had no mind to worship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:32
verses.text: "And they seized Paul," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:35
verses.text: ) They no longer wanted laws nor courts of justice: they also beat him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:36
verses.text: But he forbore to make his defence then; he made it afterward: with reason; for they would not even have heard him then.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:37
verses.text: Pray, why did they cry, "Away with him?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:38
verses.text: ) They feared he might escape them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:39
verses.text: Observe how submissively Paul speaks to the tribune.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:40
verses.text: "May I speak unto thee? Then art not thou that Egyptian?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:42
verses.text: ) This Egyptian, namely, was a cheat and impostor, and the devil expected to cast a cloud over (the Gospel) through him, and implicate both Christ and His Apostles in the charges pertaining to those (imposters): but he prevailed nothing, nay the truth became even more brilliant, being nothing defeated by the machinations of the devil, nay rather shining forth all the more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:43
verses.text: Since if there had not been impostors, and then these (Christ and His Apostles) had prevailed, perhaps some one might have laid hold upon this: but when those impostors did actually appear, this is the wonder.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:44
verses.text: "In order," says (the Apostle), "that they which are approved may be made manifest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:45
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:46
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:47
verses.text: ) And Gamaliel says, "Before these days stood up Theudas".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:48
verses.text: Then let us not grieve that heresies exist, seeing that false Christs wished to attack even Christ both before this and after; with a view to throw Him into the shade, but on every occasion we find the truth shining out transparent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:49
verses.text: So it was with the Prophets: there were false prophets, and by contrast with these they shone the more: just as disease enhances health, and darkness light, and tempest calm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:50
verses.text: There is no room left for the Greeks to say that (our teachers) were impostors and mountebanks: for those (that were such) were exposed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:51
verses.text: It was the same in the case of Moses: God suffered the magicians, on purpose that Moses might not be suspected to be a magician: He let them teach all men to what length magic can go in making a fantastic show: beyond this point they deceived not, but themselves confessed their defeat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:52
verses.text: Impostors do us no harm, rather do us good, if we will apply our mind to the matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:53
verses.text: What then, you will say, if we are partners with them in common estimation? The estimation is not among us, but with those who have no judgment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:54
verses.text: Let not us greatly care for the estimation of the many, nor mind it more than needs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:55
verses.text: To God we live, not to men: in heaven we have our conversation, not on earth: there lie the awards and the prizes of our labors, thence we look for our praises, thence for our crowns.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:56
verses.text: Thus far let us trouble ourselves about men—that we do not give and afford them a handle against us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:57
verses.text: But if, though we afford none, those choose to accuse us thoughtlessly and without discrimination, let us laugh, not weep.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:58
verses.text: "Provide" thou "things honest before the Lord and before men" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:59
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:60
verses.text: ): if, though thou provide things honest, that man derides, give thyself no more concern (for that).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:61
verses.text: Thou hast thy patterns in the Scriptures.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:62
verses.text: For, saith he, "do I now persuade men or God?" (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:63
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:64
verses.text: ) and again, "We persuade men, but we are made manifest unto God".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:65
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:66
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:67
verses.text: ) And Christ (spoke) thus of them that take offence: "Let them alone, they be blind guides of the blind" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:68
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:69
verses.text: ); and again, "Woe unto you, when all men speak well of you" (Luke vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:70
verses.text: ): and again, "Let your works shine, that men may see, and glorify your Father which is in heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:71
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:72
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:73
verses.text: ) And, "Whoso shall offend one of these little ones, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were drowned in the depths of the sea".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:74
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:75
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:76
verses.text: )  These sayings are not contrary, nay, they are exceedingly in accord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:77
verses.text: For when the offence is with us, then woe unto us, but when not with us, not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:78
verses.text: And again, Woe to (that man) through whom "the name of God is blasphemed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:79
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:80
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:81
verses.text: ) How then if I do what is right in anything, but another blasphemes? That is nothing to me, but only to him: for through him (God) was blasphemed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:82
verses.text: "And how is it possible to do what is right in anything, and yet give a handle to the rest?" Whence will ye that I bring examples—from present, or from old times? Not to be easily scared (ψοφοδεεἵς), shall we speak to the very point now in hand? Paul judaized in Jerusalem, but in Antioch not so: he judaized, and they were offended (p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:83
verses.text: , note ), but those had no right to be offended.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:84
verses.text: He is said to have saluted both Nero's cupbearer and his concubine: what, think ye, must they have said against him because of this? But they had no right to do so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:85
verses.text: Since, if he drew them to him for loose living or any wicked acts, one might well be offended: but if in order to right living, what is there to be offended at? Let me mention something that happened to one of my acquaintance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:86
verses.text: The wrath of God once fell upon (a city), and he being very young (was) in the order of deacon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:87
verses.text: The bishop was absent at the time, and of the presbyters none took thought for the matter, but indiscriminately they caused in one night immense numbers of people to be baptized all at once, and they did indiscriminately receive baptism, all of them ignorant of everything: these he took apart by a hundred or two hundred together, and discoursed to them, not upon any other subject, but only on the sacraments, so that the unbaptized also were not allowed to be present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:88
verses.text: Many thought he did this because he coveted rule.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:89
verses.text: But he cared not for that: neither however did he continue the thing for a (longer) time, but immediately desisted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:90
verses.text: When then? Was he the cause of the scandal? I think not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:91
verses.text: For if indeed he had done this without cause, they might with reason have ascribed it to him: and so again, if he had continued to do so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:92
verses.text: For when aught of what is pleasing to God is hindered by another's taking offence, it is right to take no notice: but then is the time to mind it, when we are not forced because of him to offend God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:93
verses.text: For, say, if, while we are discoursing and putting drunkards to shame (σκωπτόντων), any one take offence—am I to give over speaking? Hear Christ say, "Will ye also go away?" (John vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:94
verses.text: ) So then, the right thing is, neither to take no notice, nor to take too much, of the weakness of the many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:95
verses.text: Do we not see the physicians acting thus: how, when it may be done, they humor the whims of their patients, but when the gratification does harm, then they will not spare? Always it is good to know the right mean.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:96
verses.text: Many reviled, because a certain beautiful virgin stayed, and they railed upon those who catechised (her).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:97
verses.text: What then? Was it their duty to desist for that? By no means.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:98
verses.text: For let us not look to this only, whether some be offended, but whether they are justly offended, and so that it is no hurt to ourselves (to give way).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:99
verses.text: "If meat," saith (Paul), "offend my brother, I will eat no meat as long as the world lasts".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:100
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:101
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:102
verses.text: ) With reason: for the not eating did (him) no harm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:103
verses.text: If however it offend him, that I wish to renounce (ἀποτάξασθαι) (the world), it is not right to mind him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:104
verses.text: And whom, you will ask, does this offend? Many, to my knowledge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:105
verses.text: When therefore the hindrance is a thing indifferent, let (the thing) be done.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:106
verses.text: Else, if we were to look only to this, many are the things we have to desist from: just as, on the other hand, if we should despise (all objections), we have to destroy many (brethren).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:107
verses.text: As in fact Paul also took thought beforehand concerning offence: "Lest," he says, "in this liberality which is administered by us:" for it was attended with no loss (to him) to obviate an ill surmise.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:108
verses.text: But when we fall into such a necessity as that great evils should ensue through the other's taking offence let us pay no heed to that person.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:109
verses.text: He has to thank himself for it, and we are not now accountable, for it was not possible to spare him without hurt (to ourselves).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:110
verses.text: Some were offended, because certain believers sat down to meat in (heathen) temples.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:111
verses.text: It was not right to sit down: for no harm came of this (their not doing it).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:112
verses.text: They were offended, because Peter ate with the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:113
verses.text: But he indeed spared them, but (Paul) not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 129:114
verses.text: On all occasions it behooves us in following the laws of God to take great pains that we give no matter of offence; that both ourselves may not have to answer for it, and may have mercy vouchsafed us from God, by the grace and loving-kindness of His only-begotten Son, with Whom to the Father and Holy Ghost together be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:1
verses.text: Homily XLVII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:2
verses.text: Acts XXI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:3
verses.text: ,  "But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:4
verses.text: And when he had given him license, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:5
verses.text: And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:6
verses.text: Observe how, when he discourses to those that are without, he does not decline availing himself of the aids afforded by the laws.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:7
verses.text: Here he awes the tribune by the name of his city.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:8
verses.text: And again, elsewhere he said, "Openly, uncondemned, Romans as we are, they have cast us into prison".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:9
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:10
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:11
verses.text: ) For since the tribune said, "Art thou that Egyptian?" he immediately drew him off from that surmise: then, that he may not be thought to deny his nation, he says at once, "I am a Jew:" he means his religion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:12
verses.text: (b) What then? he did not deny (that he was a Christian): God forbid: for he was both a Jew and a Christian, observing what things he ought: since indeed he, most of all men, did obey the law: (a) as in fact he elsewhere calls himself, "Under the law to Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:13
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:14
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:15
verses.text: ) What is this, I pray? (c) The man that believes in Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:16
verses.text: And when discoursing with Peter, he says: "We, Jews by nature.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:17
verses.text: —But I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:18
verses.text: (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:19
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:20
verses.text: ) And this is a proof, that he does not speak lies, seeing he takes all as his witnesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:21
verses.text: Observe again how mildly he speaks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:22
verses.text: This again is a very strong argument that he is chargeable with no crime, his being so ready to make his defence, and his wishing to come to discourse with the people of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:23
verses.text: See a man well-prepared (τεταγμένον ἄνδρα)!—Mark the providential ordering of the thing: unless the tribune had come, unless he had bound him, he would not have desired to speak for his defence, he would not have obtained the silence he did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:24
verses.text: "Standing on the stairs".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:25
verses.text: Then there was the additional facility afforded by the locality, that he should have a high place to harangue them from—in chains too! What spectacle could be equal to this, to see Paul, bound with two chains, and haranguing the people! (To see him,) how he was not a whit perturbed, not a whit confused; how, seeing as he did so great a multitude all hostility against him, the ruler standing by, he first of all made them desist from their anger: then, how prudently (he does this).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:26
verses.text: Just what he does in his Epistle to the Hebrews, the same he does here: first he attracts them by the sound of their common mother tongue: then by his mildness itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:27
verses.text: "He spake unto them," it says, "in the Hebrew tongue, saying, Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:28
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:29
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:30
verses.text: ) Mark his address, at once so free from all flattery, and so expressive of meekness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:31
verses.text: For he says not, "Masters," nor "Lords," but, "Brethren," just the word they most liked: "I am no alien from.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:32
verses.text: you," he says, nor "against you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:33
verses.text: "Men," he says, "brethren, and fathers:" this, a term of honor, that of kindred.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:34
verses.text: "Hear ye," says he, "my"—he says not, "teaching," nor "harangue," but, "my defence which I now make unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:35
verses.text: He puts himself in the posture of a suppliant.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:36
verses.text: "And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:38
verses.text: ) Do you observe how the using the same tongue subdued them? In fact, they had a sort of awe for that language.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:39
verses.text: Observe also how he prepares the way for his discourse, beginning thus: "I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:41
verses.text: ) "I am a man," he says, "which am a Jew:" which thing they liked most of all to hear; "born in Tarsus, a city of Cilicia".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:42
verses.text: That they may not again think him to be of another nation, he adds his religion: "but brought up in this city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:43
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:44
verses.text: , note.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:45
verses.text: ) He shows how great was his zeal for the worship, inasmuch as having left his native city, which was so great and so remote too, he chose to be brought up here for the Law's sake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:46
verses.text: See how from the beginning he attached himself to the law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:47
verses.text: But this he says, not only to defend himself to them, but to show that not by human intent was he led to the preaching of the Gospel, but by a Divine power: else, having been so educated, he would not have suddenly changed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:48
verses.text: For if indeed he had been one of the common order of men, it might have been reasonable to suspect this: but if he was of the number of those who were most of all bound by the law, it was not likely that he should change lightly, and without strong necessity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:49
verses.text: But perhaps some one may say: "To have been brought up here proves nothing: for what if thou camest here for the purpose of trading, or for some other cause?" Therefore he says, "at the feet of Gamaliel:" and not simply, "by Gamaliel," but "at his feet," showing his perseverance, his assiduity, his zeal for the hearing, and his great reverence for the man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:50
verses.text: "Taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:51
verses.text: Not simply, "the law," but "the law of the fathers;" showing that he was such from the beginning, and not merely one that knew the Law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:52
verses.text: All this seems indeed to be spoken on their side, but in fact it told against them, since he, knowing the law, forsook it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:53
verses.text: "Yes: but what if thou didst indeed know the law accurately, but dost not vindicate it, no, nor love it?" "Being a zealot," he adds: not simply (one that knew it).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:54
verses.text: Then, since it was a high encomium he had passed upon himself, he makes it theirs as well as his, adding, "As ye all are this day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:55
verses.text: For he shows that they act not from any human object, but from zeal for God; gratifying them, and preoccupying their minds, and getting a hold upon them in a way that did no harm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:56
verses.text: Then he brings forward proofs also, saying, "and I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:57
verses.text: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:58
verses.text: , ): "How does this appear".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:59
verses.text: As witnesses he brings forward the high-priest himself and the elders.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:60
verses.text: He says indeed, "Being a zealot, as ye" (Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:61
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:62
verses.text: p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:63
verses.text: ): but he shows by his actions, that he went beyond them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:64
verses.text: "For I did not wait for an opportunity of seizing them: I both stirred up the priests, and undertook journeys: I did not confine my attacks, as ye did, to men, I extended them to women also: "both binding, and casting into prisons both men and women".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:65
verses.text: This testimony is incontrovertible; the (unbelief) of the Jews (is left) without excuse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:66
verses.text: See how many witnesses he brings forward, the elders, the high-priest, and those in the city.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:67
verses.text: Observe his defence, how it is not of cowardly fear (for himself, that he pleads), no, but for teaching and indoctrination.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:68
verses.text: For had not the hearers been stones, they would have felt the force of what he was saying.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:69
verses.text: For up to this point he had themselves as witnesses: the rest, however, was without witnesses: "From whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:70
verses.text: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:71
verses.text: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me? And I answered, Who are Thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, Whom thou persecutest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:72
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:73
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:74
verses.text: ) Why then, these very things ought to have been held worthy of credit, from those that went before: otherwise he would not have undergone such a revolution.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:75
verses.text: How if he is only making a fine story of it, say you? Answer me, Why did he suddenly fling away all this zeal? Because he looked for honor? And yet he got just the contrary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:76
verses.text: But an easy life, perhaps? No, nor that either.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:77
verses.text: Well but something else? Why it is not in the power of thought to invent any other object.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:78
verses.text: So then, leaving it to themselves to draw the inference, he narrates the facts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:79
verses.text: "As I came nigh," he says, "unto Damascus, about noonday".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:80
verses.text: See how great was the excess of the light.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:81
verses.text: What if he is only making a fine story, say you? Those who were with him are witnesses, who led him by the hand, who saw the light.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:82
verses.text: "And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of Him that spake to me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:83
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:84
verses.text: ) But in another place he says, "Hearing the voice, but seeing no man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:85
verses.text: (Acts ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:86
verses.text: ) It is not at variance: no, there were two voices, that of Paul and the Lord's voice: in that place, the writer means Paul's voice (Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:87
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:88
verses.text: p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:89
verses.text: , note ); as in fact (Paul) here adds, "The voice of Him that spake unto me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:90
verses.text: Seeing no man:" he does not say, that they did not see the light: but, "no man," that is, "none speaking".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:91
verses.text: And good reason that it should be so, since it behooved him alone to have that voice vouchsafed unto him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:92
verses.text: For if indeed they also had heard it, (the miracle) would not have been so great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:93
verses.text: Since persons of grosser minds are persuaded more by sight, those saw the light, and were afraid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:94
verses.text: In fact, neither did the light take so much effect on them, as it did on him: for it even blinded his eyes: by that which befel him, (God) gave them also an opportunity of recovering their sight, if they had the mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:95
verses.text: It seems to me at least, that their not believing was providentially ordered, that they might be unexceptionable witnesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:96
verses.text: "And he said unto me" it says, "I am Jesus of Nazareth, Whom thou persecutest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:97
verses.text: (comp.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:98
verses.text: ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:99
verses.text: ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:100
verses.text: ) Well is the name of the city (Nazareth) also added, that they might recognize (the Person): moreover, the Apostles also spoke thus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:101
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:102
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:103
verses.text: ; iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:104
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:105
verses.text: ) And Himself bore witness, that they were persecuting Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:106
verses.text: "And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid, but they heard not the voice of Him that spake to me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:107
verses.text: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:108
verses.text: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:109
verses.text: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there, came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:110
verses.text: And the same hour I looked up upon him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:111
verses.text: Enter into the city," it says, "and there it shall be spoken to thee of all that is appointed for thee to do".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:112
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:113
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:114
verses.text: ) Lo! again another witness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:115
verses.text: And see how unexceptionable he makes him also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:116
verses.text: "And one Ananias," he says, "a devout man according to the law,"—so far is it from being anything alien!—"having a good report of all the Jews that dwelt" (there).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:117
verses.text: "And I in the same hour received sight".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:118
verses.text: Then follows the testimony borne by the facts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:119
verses.text: Observe how it is interwoven, of persons and facts; and the persons, both of their own and of aliens: the priests, the elders, and his fellow-travellers: the facts, what he did and what was done to him: and facts bear witness to facts, not persons only.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:120
verses.text: Then Ananias, an alien; then the fact itself, the recovery of sight; then a great prophecy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:121
verses.text: "And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know His will, and see That Just One".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:122
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:123
verses.text: ) It is well said, "Of the fathers," to show that they were not Jews, but aliens from the law, and that it was not from zeal (for the law) that they were acting.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:124
verses.text: "That thou shouldest know His will".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:125
verses.text: Why then His will is this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:126
verses.text: See how in the form of narrative it is teaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:127
verses.text: "And see That Just One, and hear the voice of His mouth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:128
verses.text: For thou shalt be His witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:129
verses.text: And see," he says, "that Just One".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:130
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:131
verses.text: ) For the present he says no more than this: if He is Just, they are guilty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:132
verses.text: "And hear the voice of His mouth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:133
verses.text: See how high he raises the fact! "For thou shalt be His witness—for this, because thou wilt not betray the sight and hearing (i-e: "prove false to")—"both of what thou hast seen, and of what thou hast heard:" by means of both the senses he claims his faith, fulness—"to all men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:134
verses.text: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on His name".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:135
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:136
verses.text: ) Here it is a great thing he has uttered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:137
verses.text: For he said not, "Be baptized in His name:" but, "calling on the name of Christ".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:138
verses.text: It shows that He is God: since it is not lawful to "call upon" any other, save God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:139
verses.text: Then he shows also, that he himself was not compelled: for, "I said," says he, "What must I do?" Nothing is (left) without witness: no; he brings forward the witness of a whole city, seeing they had beheld him led by the hand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:140
verses.text: But see the prophecy fulfilled.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:141
verses.text: "To all men," it is said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:142
verses.text: For he did become a witness to Him, and a witness as it ought to be; by what he suffered, by what he did, and by what he said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:143
verses.text: Such witnesses ought we also to be, and not to betray the things we have been entrusted withal: I speak not only of doctrines, but also of the manner of life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:144
verses.text: For observe: because he had seen, because he had heard, he bears witness to all men, and nothing hindered him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:145
verses.text: We too bear witness (Mod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:146
verses.text: text "have heard") that there is a Resurrection and numberless good things: we are bound to bear witness of this to all men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:147
verses.text: "Yes, and we do bear witness," you will say, "and do believe".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:148
verses.text: How; when ye act the contrary? Say now: if any one should call himself a Christian, and then having apostatized should hold with the Jews, would this testimony suffice? By no means: for men would desire the testimony which is borne by the actions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:149
verses.text: Just so, if we say that there is a Resurrection and numberless good things, and then despise those things and prefer the things here, who will believe us? Not what we say, but what we do, is what all men look to.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:150
verses.text: "Thou shalt be a witness," it says, "unto all men:" not only to the friendly, but also to the unbelievers: for this is what witnesses are for; not to persuade those who know, but those who know not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:151
verses.text: Let us be trustworthy witnesses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:152
verses.text: But how shall we be trustworthy? By the life we lead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:153
verses.text: The Jews assaulted him: our passions assault us, bidding us abjure our testimony.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:154
verses.text: But let us not obey them: we are witnesses from God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:155
verses.text: (Christ) is judged that He is not God: He has sent us to bear witness to Him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:156
verses.text: Let us bear witness and persuade those who have to decide the point: if we do not bear witness, we have to answer for their error also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:157
verses.text: But if in a court of justice, where worldly matters come in question, nobody would receive a witness full of numberless vices, much less here, where such (and so great) are the matters to be considered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:158
verses.text: We say, that we have heard Christ, and that we believe the things which He has promised: Show it, say they, by your works: for your life bears witness of the contrary—that ye do not believe.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:159
verses.text: Say, shall we look at the money-getting people, the rapacious, the covetous? the people that mourn and wail, that build and busy themselves in all sorts of things, as though they were never to die? "Ye do not believe that ye shall die, a thing so plain and evident: and how shall we believe you when ye bear witness?" For there are, there are many men, whose state of mind is just as if they were not to die.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:160
verses.text: For when in a lengthened old age they set about building and planting, when will they take death into their calculations? It will be no small punishment to us that we were called to bear witness, but were not able to bear witness of the things that we have seen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:161
verses.text: We have seen Angels with our eyes, yea, more clearly than those who have (visibly) beheld them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:162
verses.text: We shall be (Mod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:163
verses.text: text "Then let us be") witnesses to Christ: for not those only are "martyrs," (or witnesses, whom we so call), but ourselves also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:164
verses.text: This is why they are called martyrs, because when bidden to abjure (the faith), they endure all things, that they may speak the truth: and we, when we are bidden by our passions to abjure, let us not be overcome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:165
verses.text: Gold saith: Say that Christ is not Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:166
verses.text: Then listen not to it as to God, but despise its biddings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:167
verses.text: The evil lusts "profess that they know God, but in works they deny Him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:168
verses.text: (Tit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:169
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:170
verses.text: ) For this is not to witness, but the contrary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:171
verses.text: And indeed that others should deny (Him) is nothing wonderful: but that we who have been called to bear witness should deny Him, is a grievous and a heinous thing: this of all things does the greatest hurt to our cause.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:172
verses.text: "It shall be to (your)selves for a testimony".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:173
verses.text: (Luke xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:174
verses.text: ), He saith: but (this is) when we ourselves stand to it firmly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:175
verses.text: If we would all bear witness to Christ, we should quickly persuade the greater number of the heathen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:176
verses.text: It is a great thing, my beloved, the life (one leads).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:177
verses.text: Let a man be savage as a beast, let him openly condemn thee on account of thy doctrine, yet he secretly approves, yet he will praise, yet he will admire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:178
verses.text: For say, whence can an excellent life proceed? From no source, except from a Divine Power working in us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:179
verses.text: "What if there be heathen also of such a character?" If anywhere any of them be such, it is partly from nature, partly from vainglory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:180
verses.text: Wilt thou learn what a brilliancy there is in a good life, what a force of persuasion it has? Many of the heretics have thus prevailed, and while their doctrines are corrupt, yet the greater part of men out of reverence for their (virtuous) life did not go on to examine their doctrine: and many even condemning them on account of their doctrine, reverence them on account of their life: not rightly indeed, but still so it is, that they do thus feel (towards them).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:181
verses.text: This has brought slanders on the awful articles of our creed, this has turned everything upside down, that no one takes any account of good living: this is a mischief to the faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:182
verses.text: We say that Christ is God; numberless other arguments we bring forward, and this one among the rest, that He has persuaded all men to live rightly: but this is the case with few.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:183
verses.text: The badness of the life is a mischief to the doctrine of the Resurrection, to that of the immortality of the soul, to that of the Judgment: many other (false doctrines) too it draws on with itself, fate, necessity, denial of a Providence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:184
verses.text: For the soul being immersed in numberless vices, by way of consolations to itself tries to devise these, that it may not be pained in having to reflect that there is a Judgment, and that virtue and vice lie in our own power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:185
verses.text: (Such a) life works numberless evils, it makes men beasts, and more irrational than beasts: for what things are in each several nature of the beasts, these it has often collected together in one man, and turned everything upside down.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:186
verses.text: This is why the devil has brought in the doctrine of Fate: this is why he has said that the world is without a Providence (Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:187
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:188
verses.text: p.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:189
verses.text: ): this is why he advances his hypothesis of good natures, and evil natures, and his hypothesis of evil (uncreated and) without beginning, and material (in its essence): and, in short, all the rest of it, that he may ruin our life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:190
verses.text: For it is not possible for a man who is of such a life either to recover himself from corrupt doctrines, or to remain in a sound faith: but of inevitable necessity he must receive all this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:191
verses.text: For I do not think, for my part, that of those who do not live aright, there could be easily found any who do not hold numberless satanical devices—as, that there is a nativity (or birth-fate) (γένεσις), that things happen at random, that all is hap-hazard and chance-medley.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:192
verses.text: Wherefore I beseech you let us have a care for good living, that we may not receive evil doctrines.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:193
verses.text: Cain received for punishment that he should be (ever) groaning and trembling.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:194
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:195
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:196
verses.text: ) Such are the wicked, and being conscious within themselves of numberless bad things, often they start out of their sleep, their thoughts are full of tumult, their eyes full of perturbation; everything is fraught for them with misgivings, everything alarms them, their soul is replete with grievous expectation and cowardly apprehension, contracted with impotent fear and trembling.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:197
verses.text: Nothing can be more effeminate than such a soul, nothing more inane.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:198
verses.text: Like madmen, it has no self-possession.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:199
verses.text: For it were well for it that in the enjoyment of calm and quiet it were enabled to take knowledge of its proper nobility.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:200
verses.text: But when all things terrify and throw it into perturbation, dreams, and words, and gestures, and forebodings, indiscriminately, when will it be able to look into itself, being thus troubled and amazed? Let us therefore do away with its fear, let us break asunder its bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 130:201
verses.text: For were there no other punishment, what punishment could exceed this—to be living always in fear, never to have confidence, never to be at ease? Therefore knowing these things assuredly, let us keep ourselves in a state of calm and be careful to practise virtue, that maintaining both sound doctrines and an upright life, we may without offence pass through this life present, and be enabled to attain unto the good things which God hath promised to them that love Him, through the grace and mercy of His only-begotten Son, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:1
verses.text: Homily XLVIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:2
verses.text: Acts XXII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:3
verses.text: –  "And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance; and saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:4
verses.text: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee: and when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:5
verses.text: See how he thrusts himself (into danger), I came, he says, after that vision, "to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:6
verses.text: I was in a trance," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:7
verses.text: Again, this is without witness: but observe, the witness follows from the result.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:8
verses.text: He said, "They will not receive thy testimony:" they did not receive it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:9
verses.text: And yet from calculations of reason the surmise should have been this, that they would assuredly receive him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:10
verses.text: For I was the man that made war upon the Christians: so that they ought to have received him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:11
verses.text: Here he establishes two things: both that they are without excuse, since they persecuted him contrary to all likelihood or calculation of reason; and, that Christ was God, as prophesying things contrary to expectation, and as not looking to past things, but fore-knowing the things to come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:12
verses.text: How then does He say, "He shall bear My name before the Gentiles and kings and children of Israel?" (Acts ix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:13
verses.text: ) Not, certainly persuade.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:14
verses.text: Besides which, on other occasions we find the Jews were persuaded, but here they were not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:15
verses.text: Where most of all they ought to have been persuaded, as knowing his former zeal (in their cause), here they were not persuaded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:16
verses.text: "And when the blood of Thy martyr Stephen," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:17
verses.text: See where again his discourse terminates, namely, in the forcible main point (εἰς τὸ ἱσχυρὸν κεφάλαιον): that it was he that persecuted, and not only persecuted but killed, nay, had he ten thousand hands (μυρίαις χερσὶν ἀναιρὥν) would have used them all to kill Stephen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:18
verses.text: He reminded them of the murderous spirit heinously indulged (by him and them).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:19
verses.text: Then of course above all they would not endure him, since this convicted them; and truly the prophecy was having its fulfilment: great the zeal, vehement the accusation, and the Jews themselves witnesses of the truth of Christ! "And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:20
verses.text: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:23
verses.text: ) The Jews would not endure to hear out all his harangue, but excessively fired by their wrath, they shouted, it says, "Away with him; for it is not fit that he should live.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:24
verses.text: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air, the tribune commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:25
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:27
verses.text: ) Whereas both the tribune ought to have examined whether these things were so—yes, and the Jews themselves too—or, if they were not so, to have ordered him to be scourged, he "bade examine him by scourging, that he might know for what cause they so clamored against him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:28
verses.text: And yet he ought to have learnt from those clamorers, and to have asked whether they laid hold upon aught of the things spoken: instead of that, without more ado he indulges his arbitrary will and pleasure, and acts with a view to gratify them: for he did not look to this, how he should do a righteous thing, but only how he might stop their rage unrighteous as it was.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:29
verses.text: "And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman and uncondemned?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:30
verses.text: ) Paul lied not, God forbid: for he was a Roman: if there was nothing else, he would have been afraid (to pretend this), lest he should be found out, and suffer a worse punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:31
verses.text: (See Sueton.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:32
verses.text: Vit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:33
verses.text: Claud.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:35
verses.text: ) And observe he does not say it peremptorily (ἁπλὥς), but, "Is it lawful for you?" The charges brought are two, both its being without examination, and his being a Roman.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:36
verses.text: They held this as a great privilege, at that time: for they say that (it was only) from the time of Hadrian that all were named Romans, but of old it was not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:37
verses.text: He would have been contemptible had he been scourged: but as it is, he puts them into greater fear (than they him).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:38
verses.text: Had they scourged him, they would also have dismissed the whole matter, or even have killed him; but as it is, the result is not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:39
verses.text: See how God permits many (good results) to be brought about quite in a human way, both in the case of the Apostles and of the rest (of mankind).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:40
verses.text: Mark how they suspected the thing to be a pretext, and that in calling himself a Roman, Paul lied: perhaps surmising this from his poverty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:41
verses.text: "When the centurion heard that, he went and told the tribune, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:42
verses.text: Then the tribune came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:43
verses.text: And the tribune answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:44
verses.text: And Paul said, But I was free born.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:45
verses.text: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the tribune also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:47
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:48
verses.text: )—"But I," he says, "was free born".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:49
verses.text: So then his father also was a Roman.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:50
verses.text: What then comes of this? He bound him, and brought him down to the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:51
verses.text: "On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty whereof he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:52
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:53
verses.text: ) He discourses not now to the multitude, nor to the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:54
verses.text: "And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:55
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:56
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:57
verses.text: ) What he means is this: I am not conscious to myself of having wronged you at all, or of having done anything worthy of these bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:58
verses.text: What then said the high priest? Right justly, and ruler-like, and mildly: "And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:59
verses.text: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law? And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:60
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:61
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:62
verses.text: ) Because "I knew not that he was high priest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:63
verses.text: Some say, Why then does he defend himself as if it was matter of accusation, and adds, "Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people?" For if he were not the ruler, was it right for no better reason than that to abuse (him or any) other? He says himself, "Being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:64
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:65
verses.text: ); but here he does the contrary, and not only reviles, but curses.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:66
verses.text: They are the words of boldness, rather than of anger; he did not choose to appear in a contemptible light to the tribune.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:67
