verses.text: For suppose the tribune himself had spared to scourge him, only as he was about to be delivered up to the Jews, his being beaten by their servants would have more emboldened him: this is why Paul does not attack the servant, but the person who gave the order.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:68
verses.text: But that saying, "Thou whited wall, and dost thou sit to judge me after the law?" (is) instead of, Being (thyself) a culprit: as if he had said, And (thyself) worthy of stripes without number.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:69
verses.text: See accordingly how greatly they were struck with his boldness; for whereas the point was to have overthrown the whole matter, they rather commend him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:70
verses.text: (infra, v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:71
verses.text: ) "For it is written," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:72
verses.text: He wishes to show that he thus speaks, not from fear, nor because (Ananias) did not deserve to be called this, but from obedience to the law in this point also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:73
verses.text: And indeed I am fully persuaded that he did not know that it was the high priest, since he had returned now after a long interval, and was not in the habit of constant intercourse with the Jews; seeing him too in the midst among many others: for the high priest was no longer easy to be seen at a glance, there being many of them and diverse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:74
verses.text: So, it seems to me, in this also he spoke with a view to his plea against them: by way of showing that he does obey the law; therefore he (thus) exculpates himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:75
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:76
verses.text: ) (b) But let us review what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:77
verses.text: (a) "And when I was came again to Jerusalem," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:78
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:79
verses.text: ) How was it, that being a Jew, and there brought up and taught, he did not stay there? Nor did he abide there, unless he had a mind to furnish numberless occasions against him: everywhere just like an exile, fleeing about from place to place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:80
verses.text: (c) "While I prayed in the temple," he says, "it came to pass that I was in a trance".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:81
verses.text: (To show) that it was not simply a phantom of the imagination, therefore "while he prayed" (the Lord) stood by him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:82
verses.text: And he shows that it was not from fear of their dangers that he fled, but because they would "not receive" his "testimony".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:83
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:84
verses.text: ) But why said he "They know I imprisoned?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:85
verses.text: ) Not to gainsay Christ, but because he wished to learn this which was so contrary to all reasonable expectation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:86
verses.text: Christ, however, did not teach him (this), but only bade him depart, and he obeys: so obedient is he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:87
verses.text: "And they lifted up their voices," it says, "and said, Away with him: it is not fit that this fellow should live".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:88
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:89
verses.text: ) Nay, ye are the persons not fit to live; not he, who in everything obeys God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:90
verses.text: O villains and murderers! "And shaking out their clothes," it says, "they threw dust into the air" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:91
verses.text: ), to make insurrection more fierce, because they wished to frighten the governor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:92
verses.text: And observe; they do not say what the charge was, as in fact they had nothing to allege, but only think to strike terror by their shouting.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:93
verses.text: "The tribune commanded," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:94
verses.text: and yet he ought to have learnt from the accusers, "wherefore they cried so against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:95
verses.text: And as they bound him, etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:96
verses.text: And the chief captain was afraid, after he learnt that he was a Roman".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:97
verses.text: Why then it was no falsehood.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:98
verses.text: "On the morrow, because he would know the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:99
verses.text: , he brought him down before the council".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:101
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:102
verses.text: ) This he should have done at the outset.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:103
verses.text: He brought him in, loosed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:104
verses.text: This above all the Jews would not know what to make of.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:105
verses.text: "And Paul," it says, "earnestly beholding them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:106
verses.text: It shows his boldness, and how it awed them (τὸ ἐντρεπτικόν).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:107
verses.text: "Then the high priest Ananias".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:108
verses.text: etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:109
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:110
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:111
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:112
verses.text: ) Why, what has he said that was affronting? What is he beaten for? Why what hardihood, what shamelessness! Therefore (Paul) set him down (with a rebuke): "God shall smite thee thou whited wall".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:113
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:114
verses.text: ) Accordingly (Ananias) himself is put to a stand, and dares not say a word: only those about him could not bear Paul's boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 131:115
verses.text: They saw a man ready to die.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:1
verses.text: for if this was the case, (Paul) had but to hold his peace, and the tribune would have taken him, and gone his way; he would have sacrificed him to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:2
verses.text: He both shows that he suffers willingly what he suffers, and thus excuses himself before them, not that he wished to excuse himself to them—since as for those, he even strongly condemns them—but for the sake of the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:3
verses.text: "Violating the law, commandest thou me to be beaten?" Well may he say so: for to kill a man who had done (them) no injury, and that an innocent person, was a violating of the law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:4
verses.text: For neither was it abuse that was spoken by him, unless one would call Christ's words abusive, when He says, "Woe unto you, Scribes and Pharisees, for ye are like unto whited walls".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:5
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:6
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:7
verses.text: ) True, you will say: but if he had said it before he had been beaten, it would have betokened not anger, but boldness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:8
verses.text: But I have mentioned the reason of this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:9
verses.text: And (at this rate) we often find Christ Himself "speaking abusively" to the Jews when abused by them; as when He says, "Do not think that I will accuse you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:10
verses.text: (John v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:11
verses.text: ) But this is not abuse, God forbid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:12
verses.text: See, with what gentleness he addresses these men: "I wist not," he says, "that he was God's high priest" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:13
verses.text: , ): and, (to show) that he was not dissembling (εἰρωνεύεται) he adds, "Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:14
verses.text: He even confesses him to be still ruler.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:15
verses.text: Let us also learn the gentleness also, that in both the one and the other we may be perfect.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:16
verses.text: For one must look narrowly into them, to learn what the one is and what the other: narrowly, because these virtues have their corresponding vices hard by them: mere forwardness passing itself off for boldness, mere cowardice for gentleness: and need being to scan them, lest any person possessing the vice should seem to have the virtue: which would be just as if a person should fancy that he was cohabiting with the mistress, and not know that it was the servant-maid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:17
verses.text: What then is gentleness, and what mere cowardice? When others are wronged, and we do not take their part, but hold our peace, this is cowardice: when we are the persons ill-treated, and we bear it, this is gentleness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:18
verses.text: What is boldness? Again the same, when others are the persons for whom we contend.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:19
verses.text: What forwardness? When it is in our own cause that we are willing to fight.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:20
verses.text: So that magnanimity and boldness go together, as also (mere) forwardness and (mere) cowardice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:21
verses.text: For he that (does not) resent on his own behalf, will hardly but resent on behalf of others: and he that does not stand up for his own cause, will hardly fail to stand up for others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:22
verses.text: For when our habitual disposition is pure from passion, it admits virtue also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:23
verses.text: Just as a body when free from fever admits strength, so the soul, unless it be corrupted by the passions, admits strength.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:24
verses.text: It betokens great strength, this gentleness; it needs a generous and a gallant soul, and one of exceeding loftiness, this gentleness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:25
verses.text: Or, think you, is it a small thing to suffer ill, and not be exasperated? Indeed one would not err if in speaking of the disposition to stand up for our neighbors, one should call it the spirit of manly courage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:26
verses.text: For he that has had the strength to be able to overcome so strong a passion (as this of selfishness), will have the strength to dare the attack on another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:27
verses.text: For instance, these are two passions, cowardice and anger: if thou have overcome anger, it is very plain that thou overcomest cowardice also: but thou gettest the mastery over anger, by being gentle: therefore (do so) with cowardice also, and thou wilt be manly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:28
verses.text: Again, if thou hast not got the better of anger, thou art become forward (and pugnacious); but not having got the better of this, neither canst thou get the better of fear; consequently, thou wilt be a coward too: and the case is the same as with the body; if it be weak, it is quickly overcome both by cold and heat: for such is the ill temperament, but the good temperament is able to stand all (changes).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:29
verses.text: Again, greatness of soul is a virtue, and hard by it stands prodigality: economy is a virtue, the being a good manager; hard by it stands parsimony and meanness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:30
verses.text: Come, let us again collate and compare the virtues (with their vices).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:31
verses.text: Well, then, the prodigal person is not to be called great-minded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:32
verses.text: How should he? The man who is overcome by numberless passions, how should he be great of soul? For this is not despising money; it is only the being ordered about by other passions: for just as a man, if he were at the beck and bidding of robbers to obey their orders, could not be free (so it is here).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:33
verses.text: His large spending does not come of his contempt of money, but simply from his not knowing how to dispose of it properly: else, were it possible both to keep it and to lay it out on his pleasure, this is what he would like.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:34
verses.text: But he that spends his money on fit objects, this is the man of high soul: for it is truly a high soul, that which is not in slavery to passion, which accounts money to be nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:35
verses.text: Again, economy is a good thing: for thus that will be the best manager, who spends in a proper manner, and not at random without management.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:36
verses.text: But parsimony is not the same thing with this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:37
verses.text: For the former indeed, not even when an urgent necessity demands, touches the principal of his money: but the latter will be brother to the former.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:38
verses.text: Well, then, we will put together the man of great soul, and the prudent economist, as also the prodigal and the mean man: for both of these are thus affected from littleness of soul, as those others are (from the opposite).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:39
verses.text: Let us not then call him high-souled, who simply spends, but him who spends aright: nor let us call the economical manager mean and parsimonious, but him who is unseasonably sparing of his money.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:40
verses.text: What a quantity of wealth that rich man spent, "who was clothed in purple and fine linen?" (Luke xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:41
verses.text: ) But he was not high-souled: for his soul was possessed by an unmerciful disposition and by numberless lusts: how then should it be great? Abraham had a great soul, spending as he did for the reception of his guests, killing the calf, and, where need was, not only not sparing his property, but not even his life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:42
verses.text: If then we see a person having his sumptuous table, having his harlots and his parasites, let us not call him a man of a great mind, but a man of an exceedingly little mind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:43
verses.text: For see how many passions he is enslaved and subject to—gluttony, inordinate pleasure, flattery: but him who is possessed by so many, and cannot even escape one of them, how can any one call magnanimous? Nay, then most of all let us call him little-minded, when he spends the most: for the more he spends, the more does he show the tyranny of those passions: for had they not excessively got the mastery over him, he would not have spent to excess.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:44
verses.text: Again, if we see a person, giving nothing to such people as these, but feeding the poor, and succoring those in need, himself keeping a mean table—him let us call an exceedingly high-souled man: for it is truly a mark of a great soul, to despise one's own comfort, but to care for that of others.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:45
verses.text: For tell me, if you should see a person despising all tyrants, and holding their commands of no account, but rescuing from their tyranny those who are oppressed and evil entreated; would you not think this a great man? So let us account of the man in this case also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:46
verses.text: The passions are the tyrant: if then we despise them, we shall be great: but if we rescue others also from them, we shall be far greater, as being sufficient not only for ourselves, but for others also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:47
verses.text: But if any one, at a tyrant's bidding, beat some other of his subjects, is this greatness of soul? No, indeed: but the extreme of slavery, in proportion as he is great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:48
verses.text: And now also there is set before us (πρόκειται) a soul that is a noble one and a free: but this the prodigal has ordered to be beaten by his passions: the man then that beats himself, shall we call high-souled? By no means.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 134:49
verses.text: Well then.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 136

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 136:1
verses.text: , but let us see what is greatness of soul, and what prodigality; what is economy, and what meanness; what is gentleness, and (what) dulness and cowardice; what boldness, and what forwardness: that having distinguished these things from each other, we may be enabled to pass (this life) well-pleasing to the Lord, and to attain unto the good things promised, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, to Whom be the glory for ever and ever, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:1
verses.text: Homily XLIX.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:2
verses.text: Acts XXIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:3
verses.text: –  "But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:4
verses.text: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:5
verses.text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:6
verses.text: Again he discourses simply as man, and he does not on all occasions alike enjoy the benefit of supernatural aid.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:7
verses.text: "I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee:" both in this, and in what comes after it, he wished to divide the multitude, which had an evil unanimity against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:8
verses.text: And he does not speak a falsehood here either: for he was a Pharisee by descent from his ancestors.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:9
verses.text: "Of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:10
verses.text: For since they would not say for what reason they arraigned him, he is compelled therefore to declare it himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:11
verses.text: "But the Pharisees," it says, "confess both".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:12
verses.text: And yet there are three things: how then does he say both? "Spirit and Angel" is put as one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:13
verses.text: When he is on their side, then they plead for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:14
verses.text: "And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees' part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but" (what) "if a spirit has spoken to him, or an angel?"  (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:15
verses.text: ) Why did they not plead for him before this? Do you observe, how, when the passions give way, the truth is discovered? Where is the crime, say they, if an angel has spoken to him, or a spirit? Paul gives them no handle against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:16
verses.text: "And when there arose a great dissension, the tribune, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:17
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:18
verses.text: ) The tribune is afraid of his being pulled in pieces, now that he has said that he is a Roman: and the matter was not without danger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:19
verses.text: Do you observe that Paul had a right to profess himself a Roman? Else, neither would (the tribune) have been afraid now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:20
verses.text: So it remains that the soldiers must bear him off by force.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:21
verses.text: But when the wretches saw all to be without avail, they take the whole matter into their own hands, as they would fain have done before, but were prevented: and their wickedness stops nowhere, though it received so many checks: and yet how many things were providentially ordered, on purpose that they might settle down from their rage, and learn those things through which they might possibly recover themselves! But none the less do they set upon him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:22
verses.text: Sufficient for proof of his innocence was even this, that the man was saved when at the point to be pulled in pieces, and that with these so great dangers about him, he escaped them all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:23
verses.text: "And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of Me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:24
verses.text: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:25
verses.text: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:28
verses.text: ) "They bound themselves under a curse," it says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:29
verses.text: See how vehement and revengeful they are in their malice! What means, "bound under a curse?" Why then those men are accused forever, seeing they did not kill Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:30
verses.text: And forty together.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:31
verses.text: For such is the nature of that nation: when there needs concerting together for a good object, not even two concur with each other: but when it is for an evil object, the entire people does it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:32
verses.text: And they admit the rulers also as accomplices.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:33
verses.text: "And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:34
verses.text: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the tribune that he bring him down unto you to-morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:35
verses.text: And when Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:36
verses.text: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the tribune: For he hath a certain thing to tell him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:37
verses.text: So he took him, and brought him to the tribune, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:38
verses.text: Then the tribune took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me? And he said, the Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to-morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:39
verses.text: But do not thou yield unto them for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:40
verses.text: So the tribune then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast showed these things to me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:42
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:43
verses.text: Again he is saved by man's forethought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:44
verses.text: And observe: Paul lets no man learn this, not even the centurion, that the matter might not become known.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:45
verses.text: And the centurion having come, reported to the tribune.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:46
verses.text: And it is well done of the tribune also, that he bids him keep it secret, that it might not become known: moreover he gives his orders to the centurions only, at the time when the thing was to be done: and so Paul is sent into Caesarea, that there too he might discourse in a greater theatre and before a more splendid audience: that so the Jews may not be able to say, "If we had seen Paul, we would have believed—if we had heard him teaching".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:47
verses.text: Therefore this excuse too is cut off from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:48
verses.text: "And the Lord," it said, "stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer: for as thou hast testified of Me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:49
verses.text: (Yet) even after He has appeared to him, He again suffers him to be saved by man's means.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:50
verses.text: And one may well be astonished at Paul; he was not taken aback, neither said, "Why, what is this? Have I then been deceived by Christ?" but he believed: yet, because he believed, he did not therefore sleep: no; what was in his own power by means of human wisdom, he did not abandon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:51
verses.text: "Bound themselves by a curse:" it was a kind of necessity that those men fastened on themselves by the curse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:52
verses.text: "That they would neither eat nor drink".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:53
verses.text: Behold fasting the mother of murder! Just as Herod imposed on himself that necessity by his oath, so also do these.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:54
verses.text: For such are the devil's (ways): under the pretext forsooth of piety he sets his traps.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:55
verses.text: "And they came to the chief priests," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:56
verses.text: And yet they ought to have come (to the tribune), ought to have laid a charge, and assembled a court of justice: for these are not the doings for priests, but for captains of banditti, these are not the doings for rulers, but for ruffians.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:57
verses.text: They endeavor also to corrupt the ruler: but it was providentially ordered, to the intent that he also should learn of their plot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:58
verses.text: For not (only) by their having nothing to say, but also by their secret attempt, they convicted themselves that they were naught.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:59
verses.text: It is likely too that after (Paul was gone) the chief priests came to (the tribune) making their request, and were put to shame.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:60
verses.text: For of course he would not have liked either to deny or to grant their request.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:61
verses.text: How came he to believe (the young man's tale)? He did so in consequence of what had already taken place; because it was likely they would do this also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:62
verses.text: And observe their wickedness: they as good as laid a necessity on the chief priests also: for if they undertook so great a thing themselves, and engaged themselves in the whole risk, much more ought those to do thus much.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:63
verses.text: Do you observe, how Paul is held innocent by those that are without, as was also Christ by Pilate? See their malice brought to naught: they delivered him up, to kill and condemn him: but the result is just the contrary; he is both saved, and held innocent.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:64
verses.text: For had it not been so, he would have been pulled in pieces: had it not been so, he would have perished, he would have been condemned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:65
verses.text: And not only does (the tribune) rescue him from the rush (made upon him), but also from much other (violence): see how he becomes a minister to him, insomuch that without risk he is carried off safe with so large a force.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:66
verses.text: "And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night; and provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:67
verses.text: And he wrote a letter after this manner: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:68
verses.text: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:69
verses.text: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council: whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:70
verses.text: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:71
verses.text: Fare ye well".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:72
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:73
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:74
verses.text: See how the letter speaks for him as a defence—for it says, "I found nothing worthy of death," but as accusation against them (rather) than against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:75
verses.text: "About to have been killed of them:" so set upon his death were they.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:76
verses.text: First, "I came with the army, and rescued him:" then also "I brought him down unto them:" and not even so did they find anything to lay to his charge: and when they ought to have been stricken with fear and shame for the former act, they again attempt to kill him, insomuch that again his cause became all the more clear.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:77
verses.text: "And his accusers," he says, "I have sent unto thee:" that at the tribunal where these things are more strictly examined, he may be proved guiltless.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:78
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:79
verses.text: ) Let us look then to what has been said above.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:80
verses.text: "I," he says, "am a Pharisee:" then, that he may not seem to pay court, he adds, "Of the hope and resurrection of the dead it is, that I am called in question".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:81
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:82
verses.text: ) From this charge and calumny he commends himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:83
verses.text: "For the Sadducees indeed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:84
verses.text: The Sadducees have no knowledge of anything incorporeal, perhaps not even God; so gross (παχεἵς) are they: whence neither do they choose to believe that there is a Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:85
verses.text: "And the scribes," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:86
verses.text: Look; the tribune also hears that the Pharisees have acquitted him of the charges, and have given sentence (mss.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:87
verses.text: and Edd.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:88
verses.text: ἐψηφίσατο, "he gave sentence") in his favor, and with greater confidence carries him off by force.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:89
verses.text: Moreover all that was spoken (by Paul) was full of right-mindedness (φιλοσοφίας).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:90
verses.text: "And the night following the Lord stood by him," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:91
verses.text: See what strong consolation! First he praises him, "As thou hast testified to My cause in Jerusalem;" then He does not leave him to be afraid for the uncertain issue of his journey to Rome: for thither also, He saith, thou shalt not depart alone (μόνος, Cat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:92
verses.text: and Edd.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:93
verses.text: μόνον), but thou shalt also have all this boldness of speech.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:94
verses.text: Hereby it was made manifest, not (only) that he should be saved, but that (he should be so) in order to great crowns in the great city.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:95
verses.text: But why did He not appear to him before he fell into the danger? Because it is evermore in the afflictions that God comforts us; for He appears more wished-for, while even in the dangers He exercises and trains us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:96
verses.text: Besides, he was then at ease, when free from bonds; but now great perils were awaiting him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:97
verses.text: "We have bound ourselves," they say, "under a curse, that we will not eat nor drink".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:98
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:99
verses.text: ) What is all this zeal? "That he may bring him down," it says, "unto you, as though ye would enquire into his case more perfectly".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:100
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:101
verses.text: ) Has he not twice made a speech unto you? has he not said that he is a Pharisee? What (would ye have) over and above this? So reckless were they and afraid of nothing, not tribunals, not laws: such their hardihood which shrunk from nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:102
verses.text: They both declare their purpose, and announce the way of carrying it into effect.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:103
verses.text: "Paul's sister's son heard of it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:104
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:105
verses.text: ) This was of God's providence, their not perceiving that it would be heard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:106
verses.text: What then did Paul? he was not alarmed, but perceived that this was God's doing: and casting all upon Him, so he acquits himself (from further concern about it:) "having called one of the centurions," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:107
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:108
verses.text: ) He told of the plot, he was believed; he is saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:109
verses.text: If he was acquitted of the charge, why did (the tribune) send the accusers? That the enquiry might be more strict: that the man might be the more entirely cleared.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:110
verses.text: Such are God's ways of ordering: the very things by which we are hurt, by these same are we benefited.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:111
verses.text: Thus it was with Joseph: his mistress sought to ruin him: and she seemed indeed to be contriving his ruin, but by her contriving she placed him in a state of safety: for the house where that wild beast (of a woman) was kept was a den in comparison with which the prison was gentle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:112
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:113
verses.text: xxxix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:114
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:115
verses.text: ) For while he was there, although he was looked up to and courted, he was in constant fear, lest his mistress should set upon him, and worse than any prison was the fear that lay upon him: but after the accusation he was in security and peace, well rid of that beast, of her lewdness and her machinations for his destruction: for it was better for him to keep company with human creatures in miserable plight, than with a maddened mistress.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:116
verses.text: Here he comforted himself, that for chastity's sake he had fallen into it: there he had been in dread, lest he should receive a death-blow to his soul: for nothing in the world is more annoying than a woman in love can be to a young man who will not (meet her advances): nothing more detestable (than a woman in such case), nothing more fell: all the bonds in the world are light to this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:117
verses.text: So that the fact was not that he got into prison, but that he got out of prison.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:118
verses.text: She made his master his foe, but she made God his friend: brought him into closer relation to Him Who is indeed the true Master; she cast him out of his stewardship in the family, but made him a familiar friend to that Master.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:119
verses.text: Again, his brethren sold him (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:120
verses.text: xxxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:121
verses.text: ); but they freed him from having enemies dwelling in the same house with him, from envy and much ill will, and from daily machinations for his ruin: they placed him far aloof from them that hated him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:122
verses.text: For what can be worse than this, to be compelled to dwell in the same house with brethren that envy one; to be an object of suspicion, to be a mark for evil designs? So that while they and she were severally seeking to compass their own ends, far other were the mighty consequences working out by the Providence of God for that just man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:123
verses.text: When he was in honor, then was he in danger; when he was in dishonor, then was he in safety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:124
verses.text: The eunuchs did not remember him, and right well it was that they did not, that the occasion of his deliverance might be more glorious: that the whole might be ascribed, not to man's favor, but to God's Providence (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:125
verses.text: xl.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:126
verses.text: ): that at the right moment, Pharaoh, reduced to need, might bring him out; that not as conferring but as receiving a benefit, the king might release him from the prison.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:127
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:128
verses.text: xli.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:129
verses.text: ) It behooved to be no servile gift, but that the king should be reduced to a necessity of doing this: it behooved that it should be made manifest what wisdom was in him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:130
verses.text: Therefore it is that the eunuch forgets him, that Egypt might not forget him, that the king might not be ignorant of him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:131
verses.text: Had he been delivered at that time, it is likely he would have desired to depart to his own country: therefore he is kept back by numberless constraints, first by subjection to a master, secondly by being in prison, thirdly by being over the kingdom, to the end that all this might be brought about by the Providence of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:132
verses.text: Like a spirited steed that is eager to bound off to his fellows, did God keep him back there, for causes full of glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:133
verses.text: For that he longed to see his father, and free him from his distress, is evident from his calling him thither.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:134
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:135
verses.text: xlv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:136
verses.text: )  Shall we look at other instances of evil designing, how they turn out to our good, not only by having their reward, but also by their working at the very time precisely what is for our good? This (Joseph's) uncle (Esau) had ill designs against his father (Jacob), and drove him out of his native land: what then? (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:137
verses.text: xxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:138
verses.text: ) He too set him (thereby) aloof from the danger; for he too got (thereby) to be in safety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:139
verses.text: He made him a wiser and a better man (φιλοσοφώτερον); he was the means of his having that dream (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:140
verses.text: xxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:141
verses.text: ) But, you will say, he was a slave in a foreign land? Yes, but he arrives among his own kindred, and receives a bride, and appears worthy to his father-in-law.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:142
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:143
verses.text: xxix.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:144
verses.text: ) But he too cheated him? Yes, but this also turned out to his good, that he might be the father of many children.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:145
verses.text: But it was in his mind to design evil against him? True, but even this was for his good, that he might thereupon return to his own country; for if he had been in good circumstances, he would not have so longed for home.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:146
verses.text: But he defrauded him of his hire? Aye, but he got more by the means.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:147
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:148
verses.text: xxxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:149
verses.text: ) Thus, in every point of these men's history, the more people designed their hurt, the more their affairs flourished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:150
verses.text: If (Jacob) had not received the elder daughter, he would not soon have been the father of so many children; he would have dragged out a long period in childlessness, he would have mourned as his wife did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:151
verses.text: For she indeed had reason to mourn, as not having become a mother (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:152
verses.text: xxx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:153
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:154
verses.text: ); but he had his consolation: whence also he gives her a repulse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:155
verses.text: Again, had not (Laban) defrauded him of his hire, he would not have longed to see his own country; the higher points (φιλοσοφία) of the man's character would not have come to light, (his wives) would not have become more closely attached to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:156
verses.text: For see what they say: "With devouring hath he devoured us and our money".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:157
verses.text: (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:158
verses.text: xxxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:159
verses.text: ) So that this became the means of riveting their love to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:160
verses.text: After this he had in them not merely wives, but (devoted) slaves; he was beloved by them: a thing that no possession can equal: for nothing, nothing whatever, is more precious than to be thus loved by a wife and to love her.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:161
verses.text: "And a wife," Scripture says, "that agrees with her husband".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:162
verses.text: (Ecclus.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:163
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:164
verses.text: ) "A man and a wife that agree together".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:165
verses.text: E.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:166
verses.text: V.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:167
verses.text: ) One thing this, as the Wise Man puts it, of the things for which a man is to be counted happy; for where this is, there all wealth, all prosperity abounds: as also, where it is not, there all besides profits nothing, but all goes wrong, all is mere unpleasantness and confusion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:168
verses.text: Then let us seek this before all things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:169
verses.text: He that seeks money, seeks not this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:170
verses.text: Let us seek those things which can remain fixed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:171
verses.text: Let us not seek a wife from among the rich, lest the excess of wealth on her side produce arrogance, lest that arrogance be the means of marring all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:172
verses.text: See you not what God did? how He put the woman in subjection? (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:173
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:174
verses.text: ) Why art thou ungrateful, why without perception? The very benefit God has given thee by nature, do not thou mar the help it was meant to be.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:175
verses.text: So that it is not for her wealth that we ought to seek a wife: it is that we may receive a partner of our life, for the appointed order of the procreation of children.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:176
verses.text: It was not that she should bring money, that God gave the woman; it was that she might be an helpmate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:177
verses.text: But she that brings money, becomes, instead of a wife, a setter up of her own will (ἐπίβουλος), a mistress—it may be a wild beast instead of a wife—while she thinks she has a right to give herself airs upon her wealth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:178
verses.text: Nothing more shameful than a man who lays himself out to get riches in this way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:179
verses.text: If wealth itself is full of temptations, what shall we say to wealth so gotten? For you must not look to this, that one or another as a rare and unusual case, and contrary to the reason of the thing, has succeeded: as neither ought we in other matters to fix our regards upon the good which people may enjoy, or their chance successes, out of the common course: but let us look to the reason of the thing as it is in itself, and see whether this thing be not fraught with endless annoyance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:180
verses.text: Not only you bring yourself into a disreputable position; you also disgrace your children by leaving them poor, if it chance that you depart this life before the wife: and you give her incomparably more occasions for connecting herself with a second bridegroom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:181
verses.text: Or do you not see that many women make this the excuse for a second marriage—that they may not be despised; that they want to have some man to take the management of their property? Then let us not bring about so great evils for the sake of money; but let us dismiss all (such aims), and seek a beautiful soul, that we may also succeed in obtaining love.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 137:182
verses.text: This is the exceeding wealth, this the great treasure, this the endless good things: whereunto may we all attain by the grace and loving kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, dominion, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:1
verses.text: Homily L.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:2
verses.text: Acts XXIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:3
verses.text: , ,  "Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:4
verses.text: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle: who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:5
verses.text: Like some king whom his body-guards escort, so did these convey Paul; in such numbers too, and by night, for fear of the wrath of the people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:6
verses.text: Now then you will say that they have got him out of the city, they desist from their violence? No indeed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:7
verses.text: But (the tribune) would not have sent him off with such care for his safety, but that while he himself had found nothing amiss in him, he knew the murderous disposition of his adversaries.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:8
verses.text: "And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:9
verses.text: And when he understood that he was of Cilicia; I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:10
verses.text: Already Lysias has spoken for his exculpation; (but the Jews seek to) gain the hearer beforehand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:11
verses.text: "And he ordered him to be kept in custody in Herod's praetorium" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:12
verses.text: , ): again Paul is put in bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:13
verses.text: "And after five days came down the high priest Ananias with the elders".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:14
verses.text: See how for all this they do not desist; hindered as they were by obstacles without number, nevertheless they come, only to be put to shame here also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:15
verses.text: "And with an orator, one Tertullus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:16
verses.text: And what need was there of "an orator? Which (persons) also informed the governor against Paul".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:17
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:18
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:19
verses.text: ) See how this man also from the very outset (b) with his praises seeks to gain the judge beforehand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:20
verses.text: "And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence, we accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:21
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:22
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:23
verses.text: ) Then as having much to say, he passes by the rest: "Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:24
verses.text: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:25
verses.text: (a) As a revolutionary and seditious person he wishes to deliver him up.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:26
verses.text: And yet, it might be answered, it is ye that have done this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:27
verses.text: (c) And see how he would put up the judge to a desire of punishing, seeing he had here an opportunity to coerce the man that turned the world upside down! As if they had achieved a meritorious action, they make much of it: "Having found this fellow," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:28
verses.text: , "a mover of sedition," say they, "among all the Jews throughout the world".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:29
verses.text: (Had he been such), they would have proclaimed him as a benefactor and saviour of the nation! "And a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:30
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:32
verses.text: ) They thought this likely to tell as a reproach—"of the Nazarenes:" and by this also they seek to damage him—for Nazareth was a mean place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:33
verses.text: And, "we have found him," say they: see how maliciously they calumniate him: (found him), as if he had been always giving them the slip, and with difficulty they had succeeded in getting him: though he had been seven days in the Temple! "Who also hath gone about to profane the temple; whom we took, and would have judged according to our law".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:35
verses.text: ) See how they insult even the Law; it was so like the Law, forsooth, to beat, to kill, to lie in wait! And then the accusation against Lysias: though he had no right, say they, to interfere, in the excess of his confidence he snatched him from us: "But the tribune Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands, commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, where of we accuse him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:36
verses.text: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:37
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:38
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:39
verses.text: What then says Paul? "Then Paul; after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a just judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:41
verses.text: ) This is not the language of flattery, his testifying to the judge's justice: no, the adulation was rather in that speech of the orator, "By thee we enjoy great quietness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:42
verses.text: If so, then why are ye seditious? What Paul sought was justice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:43
verses.text: "Knowing thee to be a just judge, I cheerfully," says he, "answer for myself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:44
verses.text: Then also he enforces this by the length of time: that (he had been judge) "of many years.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:45
verses.text: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:47
verses.text: ) And what is this? (It means), "that I could not immediately have raised a commotion".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:48
verses.text: Because the accuser had nothing to show (as done) in Jerusalem, observe what he said: "among all the Jews throughout the world".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:49
verses.text: Therefore it is that Paul here forcibly attracts him—"to worship," he says, "I came up," so far am I from raising sedition—and lays a stress upon this point of justices being the strong point.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:50
verses.text: "And they neither found me in the Temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:51
verses.text: ); which in fact was the truth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:52
verses.text: And the accusers indeed use the term "ringleader," as if it were a case of fighting and insurrection; but see how mildly Paul here answers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:53
verses.text: "But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the Law and the Prophets: and have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:55
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:56
verses.text: ) The accusers were separating him (as an alien), but he identifies himself with the Law, as one of themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:57
verses.text: "And in this," says he, "do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God and toward men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:58
verses.text: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:59
verses.text: In which they found me purified in the temple, not with multitude, neither with tumult".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:60
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:61
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:62
verses.text: ) Why then camest thou up? What brought thee hither? To worship, says he; to do alms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:63
verses.text: This was not the act of a factious person.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:64
verses.text: Then also he casts out their person: "but," says he, (they that found me, were) "certain Jews from Asia, who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:65
verses.text: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me while I stood before the council, except it be for this one voice, that I cried, standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:66
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:67
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:68
verses.text: ) For this is justification in superabundance, not to flee from his accusers, but to be ready to give account to all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:69
verses.text: "Of the resurrection of the dead," says he, "am I this day called in question".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:70
verses.text: And not a word said he of what he had to say, how they had conspired against him, had violently kept him, had laid wait for him—for these matters are course spoken of by the tribune—but by Paul, though there was danger, not so: no, he is silent, and only defends himself, though he had very much to say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:71
verses.text: (b) "In which" (alms), says he, "they found me in course of purifying in the Temple".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:72
verses.text: Then how did he profane it? For it was not the part of the same man both to purify himself and worship and come for this purpose, and then to profane it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:73
verses.text: This has with it a surmise of the justice of his cause, that he does not fall into a long discourse.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:74
verses.text: And he gratifies the judge, I suppose, by that also (namely, by), making his defence compendious: (d) seeing that Tertullus before him did make a long harangue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:75
verses.text: (f) And this too is a proof of mildness, that when one has much to say, in order not to be troublesome one says but few words.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:76
verses.text: (c) But let us look again at what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:77
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:78
verses.text: ) "Then the soldiers," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:79
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:80
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:81
verses.text: ) (a) This also made Paul famous in Caesarea, his coming with so large a force.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:82
verses.text: —"But," says Tertullus, "that I be not further tedious," (e) showing that (Felix) does find him tedious (ἐγκόπτεται): "I beseech thee," he does not say, Hear the matter, but, "hear us of thy clemency".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:83
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:84
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:85
verses.text: ) Probably it is to pay court, that he thus lays out his speech.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:86
verses.text: (g) "For having found this man, a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:87
verses.text: ): how then, it might be said, if he did this elsewhere (and not here)? No, says he; among us also he has profaned the Temple; "attempted," says he, "to profane it:" but the how, he leaves untold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:88
verses.text: "Whom also we took".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:89
verses.text: etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:90
verses.text: "But the tribune," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:91
verses.text: And while he thus exaggerates what relates to the tribune, see how he extenuates the part of the accusers themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:92
verses.text: "We took him," he says, "and would have judged him according to our Law".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:93
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:94
verses.text: ) He shows that it is a hardship to them that they have to come to foreign tribunals, and that they would not have troubled him had not the tribune compelled them, and that he, having no concern in the matter, had seized the man by force: for in fact the wrongs done were against us, and with us the tribunal ought to have been.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:95
verses.text: For that this is the meaning, see what follows: "with great violence" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:96
verses.text: ), he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:97
verses.text: For this conduct is violence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:98
verses.text: "From whom thou mayest know".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:99
verses.text: He neither dares to accuse him (the tribune)—for the man was indulgent (forsooth)—nor does he wholly pass it by.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:100
verses.text: Then again, lest he should seem to be lying, he adduces Paul himself as his own accuser.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:101
verses.text: "From whom, by examining him, thou mayest take knowledge of all these things".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:102
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:103
verses.text: ) Next, as witnesses also of the things spoken, the accusers, the same persons themselves both witnesses and accusers: "And the Jews also assented," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:104
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:105
verses.text: ) But Paul, "Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a just judge".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:106
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:107
verses.text: ) Why then, he is no stranger or alien or revolutionary person, seeing he had known the judge for many years.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:108
verses.text: And he does well to add the epithet "just," that he (Felix) might not look to the chief priest, nor to the people, nor the accuser.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:109
verses.text: See, how he did not let himself be carried away into abuse, although there was strong provocation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:110
verses.text: "Believing," he says, "that there will be a resurrection:" now a man who believed a resurrection, would never have done such things—"which" (resurrection) "they themselves also allow".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:111
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:112
verses.text: ) He does not say it of them, that they believe "all things written in the Prophets:" it was he that believed them all, not they: but how "all," it would require a long discourse to show.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:113
verses.text: And he nowhere makes mention of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:114
verses.text: Here by saying, "Believing," he does (virtually) introduce what relates to Christ; for the present he dwells on the subject of the resurrection, which doctrine was common to them also, and removed the suspicion of any sedition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:115
verses.text: And for the cause of his going up, "I came," he says, "to bring alms to my nation and offerings".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:116
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:117
verses.text: ) How then should I have troubled those, for the bringing offerings to whom I had come so long a journey? "Neither with multitude, nor with tumult".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:118
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:119
verses.text: ) Everywhere he does away the charge of sedition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:120
verses.text: And he also does well to challenge his accusers who were from Asia, "Who ought to accuse before thee," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:121
verses.text: , but he does well also not to reject this either; "or else," says he, "let these same here say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:122
verses.text: Touching the resurrection of the dead," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:123
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:124
verses.text: , , ): for in fact it was on this account they were sore troubled from the first, because he preached the Resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:125
verses.text: This being proved, the things relating to Christ also were easily introduced, that He was risen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:126
verses.text: "What evil doing," he says, "they found in me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:127
verses.text: In the council" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:128
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:129
verses.text: ) he says: the examination not having taken place in private.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:130
verses.text: That these things which I say are true, those witness who bring this charge against me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:131
verses.text: "Having," he says, "a conscience void of offence both toward God, and toward men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:132
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:133
verses.text: ) This is the perfection of virtue, when even to men we give no handle against us, and are careful to be void of offence with God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:134
verses.text: "That I cried," he says, "in the council".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:135
verses.text: He also shows their violence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:136
verses.text: They have it not to say, Thou didst these things under the pretext of alms: for (it was) "not with multitude, nor with tumult:" especially as upon enquiry made concerning this thing, nothing further was found.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:137
verses.text: Do you observe his moderation, though there were dangers? do you observe how he keeps his tongue from evil-speaking, how he seeks only one thing, to free himself from the charges against himself, not that he may criminate them, except so far as he might be obliged to do so while defending himself? Just as Christ also said: "I have not a devil, but I honor My Father: but ye do dishonor Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:138
verses.text: (John viii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:139
verses.text: )  Let us imitate him, since he also was an imitator of Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:140
verses.text: If he, with enemies, who went even to the length of murder and slaughter, said nothing offensive to them, what pardon shall we deserve, who in reviling and abuse become infuriated, calling our enemies villains, detestable wretches? what pardon shall we deserve, for having enemies at all? Hear you not, that to honor (another) is to honor one's self? So it is: but we disgrace ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:141
verses.text: You accuse (some one) that he has abused you: then why do you bring yourself under the same accusation? Why inflict a blow on yourself? Keep free from passion, keep unwounded: do not, by wishing to smite another, bring the hurt upon yourself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:142
verses.text: What, is the other tumult of our soul not enough for us, the tumult that is stirred up, though there be none to stir it up—for example, its outrageous lusts, its griefs and sorrows, and such like—but we must needs heap up a pile of others also? And how, you will say, is it possible, when one is insulted and abused, to bear this? And how is it not possible, I ask? Is a wound got from words; or do words inflict bruises on our bodies? Then where is the hurt to us? So that, if we will, we can bear it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:143
