verses.text: Let us lay down for ourselves a law not to grieve, and we shall bear it: let us say to ourselves, "It is not from enmity; it is from infirmity"—for it is indeed owing to an infirmity, since, for proof that it comes not from enmity nor from malignity of disposition, but from infirmity, the other also would fain have restrained (his anger), although he had suffered numberless wrongs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:144
verses.text: If we only have this thought in our minds, that it is from infirmity, we shall bear it, and while we forgive the offending person, we shall try not to fall into it ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:145
verses.text: For I ask all you who are present: would ye have wished to be able to exercise such a philosophic temper, as to bear with those who insult you? I think so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:146
verses.text: Well, then, he insulted unwillingly; he would rather not have done so, but he did it, forced by his passion: refrain thyself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:147
verses.text: Do you not see (how it is with) the demoniacs (in their fits)? Just then as it is with them, so with him: it is not so much from enmity, as from infirmity (that he behaves as he does): endure it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:148
verses.text: And as for us—it is not so much from the insults as they are in themselves that we are moved, as from our own selves: else how is it that when madmen offer us the same insults, we bear it? Again, if those who insult us be our friends, in that case too we bear it: or also our superiors, in that case also we bear it: how then is it not absurd, that in the case of these three, friends, madmen, and superiors, we bear it, but where they are of the same rank or our inferiors, we do not bear it? I have oftentimes said: It is but an impulse of the moment, something that hurries us away on the sudden: let us endure it for a little, and we shall bear the whole thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:149
verses.text: The greater the insults, the more weak the offender.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:150
verses.text: Do you know when it behooves us to grieve? When we have insulted another, and he keeps silence: for then he is strong, and we weak: but if the contrary be the case, you must even rejoice: you are crowned, you are proclaimed conqueror, without having even entered into the contest, without having borne the annoyance of sun, and heat, and dust, without having grappled with an antagonist and let him close with you; nothing but a mere wish on your part, sitting or standing, and you have got a mighty crown: a crown far greater than those (combatants earn): for to throw an enemy standing to the encounter, is nothing like so great as to overcome the darts of anger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:151
verses.text: You have conquered, without having even let him close with you, you have thrown down the passion that was in you, have slain the beast that was roused, have quelled the anger that was raging, like some excellent herdsman.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:152
verses.text: The fight was like to have been an intestine one, the war a civil war.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:153
verses.text: For, as those who sit down to besiege from without (endeavor to), embroil (the besieged) in civil discords, and then overcome them; so he that insults, unless he rouse the passion within us, will not be able to overcome us: unless we kindle the flame in ourselves, he has no power.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:154
verses.text: Let the spark of anger be within us, so as to be ready for lighting at the right moment, not against ourselves, nor so as to involve us in numberless evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:155
verses.text: See ye not how the fire in houses is kept apart, and not thrown about at random everywhere, neither among straw, nor among the linen, nor just where it may chance, that so there may not be danger, if a wind blow on it, of its kindling a flame: but whether a maid-servant have a lamp, or the cook light a fire, there is many an injunction given, not to do this in the draught of the wind, nor near a wooden panel, nor in the night-time: but when the night has come on, we extinguish the fire, fearing lest perchance while we are asleep and there is none to help, it set fire, and burn us all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:156
verses.text: Let this also be done with regard to anger; let it not be scattered everywhere up and down in our thoughts, but let it be in some deep recess of the mind, that the wind arising from the words of him who is opposing us may not easily reach to it, but that it receive the wind (which is to rouse it) from ourselves, who know how to rouse it in due measure and with safety.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:157
verses.text: If it receive the wind from without, it knows no moderation; it will set everything on fire: oftentimes when we are asleep this wind will come upon it, and will burn up all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:158
verses.text: Let it therefore be with us (in safe keeping) in such sort as only to kindle a light: for anger does kindle a light when it is managed as it ought to be: and let us have torches against those who wrong others, against the devil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:159
verses.text: Let not the spark lie anywhere as it may chance, nor be thrown about; let us keep it safe under ashes: in lowly thoughts let us keep it slumbering.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:160
verses.text: We do not want it at all times, but when there is need to subdue and to make tender, to mollify obduracy, and convict the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:161
verses.text: What evils have angry and wrathful passions wrought! And what makes it grievous indeed is, that when we have parted asunder, we have no longer the power to come together again, but we wait for others (to do this): each is ashamed, and blushes to come back himself and reconcile the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:162
verses.text: See, he is not ashamed to part asunder and to be separated; no, he takes the lead as author of the evil: but to come forward and patch that which is rent, this he is ashamed to do: and the case is just the same, as if a man should not shrink from cutting off a limb, but should be ashamed to join it together again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:163
verses.text: What sayest thou, O man? Hast thou committed great injuries, and thyself been the cause of the quarrel? Why, then, thou wouldest justly be the first to go and be reconciled, as having thyself furnished the cause.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:164
verses.text: But he did the wrong, he is the cause of the enmity? Why then, for this reason also thou must do it, that men may the more admire thee, that in addition to the former, thou mayest get the first prize in the latter also: as thou wast not the cause of the enmity, so neither of its being extended further.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:165
verses.text: Perhaps also the other, as conscious within himself of numberless evils, is ashamed and blushes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:166
verses.text: But he is haughty? On this account above all, do not thou hesitate to run and meet him: for if the ailment in him be twofold, both haughtiness and anger, in this thou hast mentioned the very reason why thou oughtest to be the first to go to him, thou that art the one in sound health, the one who is able to see: as for him, he is in darkness: for such is anger and false pride.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:167
verses.text: But do thou, who art free from these and in sound health, go to him—thou the physician, go to the sick.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:168
verses.text: Does any of the physicians say, Because such an one is sick, I do not go to him? No, this is the very reason above all why they do go, when they see that he is not able to come to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:169
verses.text: For of those who are able (to come) they think less, as of persons not extremely ill, but not so of those who lie at home sick.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:170
verses.text: Or are not pride and anger, think you, worse than any illness? is not the one like a sharp fever, the other like a body swollen with inflammation? Think what a thing it is to have a fever and inflammation: go to him, extinguish the fire, for by the grace of God thou canst: go, assuage the heat as it were with water.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:171
verses.text: "But," you will say, "how if he is only the more set up by my doing this very thing?" This is nothing to thee: thou hast done thy part, let him take account for himself: let not our conscience condemn us, that this thing happens in consequence of any omission of what ought to have been done on our part.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:172
verses.text: "In so doing," says the Scripture, "thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:173
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:174
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:175
verses.text: , cf.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:176
verses.text: Hom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:177
verses.text: in l.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:178
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:179
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:180
verses.text: ) And yet, for all that this is the consequence, it bids us go and be reconciled and do good offices—not that we may heap coals of fire, but that (our enemy) knowing that future consequence, may be assuaged by the present kindness, that he may tremble, that he may fear our good offices rather than our hostilities, and our friendships rather than our ill designs.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:181
verses.text: For one does not so hurt his hater by showing his resentment as an enemy, as by doing him good and showing kindness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:182
verses.text: For by his resentment, he has hurt both himself and perhaps the other also in some little degree: but by doing good offices, he has heaped coals of fire on his head.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:183
verses.text: "Why then," you will say, "for fear of thus heaping coals one ought not to do this (b) but to carry on the enmity to greater lengths".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:184
verses.text: By no means: it is not you that cause this, but he with his brutish disposition.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:185
verses.text: For if, when you are doing him good, and honoring him, and offering to be reconciled, he persists in keeping up the enmity, it is he has kindled the fire for himself, he has set his own head on fire; you are guiltless.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:186
verses.text: Do not want to be more merciful than God (b), or rather, if you wish it, you will not be able, not even in the least degree.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:187
verses.text: How should you? "As far as the heaven is from the earth," Scripture says, "so far are My counsels from your counsels" (Isa.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:188
verses.text: xlv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:189
verses.text: ): and again, "If ye," He says, "being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more your heavenly Father" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:190
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:191
verses.text: )? But in fact this talk is mere pretext and subterfuge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:192
verses.text: Let us not prevaricate with God's commandments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:193
verses.text: "And how do we prevaricate," you will say? He has said, "In so doing, thou wilt heap coals of fire on his head:" and you say, I do not like to do this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:194
verses.text: (a) But are you willing to heap coals after another fashion, that is upon your own head? For in fact this is what resentment does: (c) since you shall suffer evils without number.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:195
verses.text: (e) You say, "I am afraid for my enemy, because he has done me great injuries:" in reality is it this you say? But how came you to have an enemy? But how came you to hate your enemy? You fear for him that has injured you, but do you not fear yourself? Would that you had a care for yourself! Do not act (the kindness) with such an aim as this: or rather do it, though it be but with such an aim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:196
verses.text: But you do it not at all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:197
verses.text: I say not to you, "thou wilt heap coals of fire:" no, I say another and a greater thing: only do it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:198
verses.text: For Paul says this only by way of summoning thee (if only), in hope of the vengeance, to put an end to the enmity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:199
verses.text: Because we are savage as wild beasts in disposition, and would not otherwise endure to love our enemy, unless we expected some revenge, he offers this as a cake, so to say, to a wild beast.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:200
verses.text: For to the Apostles (the Lord) says not this, but what says He? "That ye may be like to your Father which is in heaven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:201
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:202
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:203
verses.text: ) And besides, it is not possible that the benefactor and the benefited should remain in enmity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:204
verses.text: This is why Paul has put it in this way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:205
verses.text: Why, affecting a high and generous principle in thy words, why in thy deeds dost thou not even observe (common) moderation? (It sounds) well; thou dost not feed him, for fear of thereby heaping upon him coals of fire: well then, thou sparest him? well then, thou lovest him, thou actest with this object in view? God knows, whether thou hast this object in so speaking, and are not palming this talk upon us as a mere pretence and subterfuge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:206
verses.text: Thou hast a care for thine enemy, thou fearest lest he be punished, then wouldest thou not have extinguished thine anger? For he that loves to that degree that he overlooks his own interest for the sake of the other's advantage, that man has no enemy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:207
verses.text: (Then indeed) thou mightest say this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 138:208
verses.text: How long shall we trifle in matters that are not to be trifled with, and that admit of no excuse? Wherefore I beseech you, let us cut off these pretexts; let us not despise God's laws: that we may be enabled with well-pleasing to the Lord to pass this life present, and attain unto the good things promised, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:1
verses.text: Homily LI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:2
verses.text: Acts XXIV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:3
verses.text: ,  "And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them and said, When Lysias the tribune shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:4
verses.text: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:5
verses.text: See how much close investigation is made by the many in a long course of time, that it should not be said that the trial was hurried over.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:6
verses.text: For, as the orator had made mention of Lysias, that he took "him away with violence, Felix," he says, "deferred them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:7
verses.text: Having knowledge of that way:" that is, he put them off on purpose: not because he wanted to learn, but as wishing to get rid of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:8
verses.text: On their account, he did not like to let him go: to punish him was not possible; that would have been (too) barefaced.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:9
verses.text: "And to let him have liberty, and to forbid none of his acquaintance to minister to him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:10
verses.text: So entirely did he too acquit him of the charges.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:11
verses.text: Howbeit, to gratify them, he detained him, and besides, expecting to receive money, he called for Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:12
verses.text: "And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:13
verses.text: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance (i-e: self-control or chastity), and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:14
verses.text: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him; wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:15
verses.text: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix's room: and Felix, willing to show the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:16
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:17
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:18
verses.text: ) See how close to the truth are the things written.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:19
verses.text: But he sent for him frequently, not that he admired him, nor that he praised the things spoken, nor that he wished to believe, but why? "Expecting," it says, "that money should have been given him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:20
verses.text: Observe how he does not hide here the mind of the judge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:21
verses.text: "Wherefore he sent for him," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:22
verses.text: And yet if he had condemned him, he would not have done this, nor have wished to hear a man, condemned and of evil character.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:23
verses.text: And observe Paul, how, though reasoning with a ruler, he says nothing of the sort that was likely to amuse and entertain, but ("he reasoned," it says,) "of righteousness, and of the coming judgment," and of the resurrection.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:24
verses.text: And such was the force of his words, that they even terrified the governor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:25
verses.text: This man is succeeded in his office by another, and he leaves Paul a prisoner: and yet he ought not to have done this; he ought to have put an end to the business: but he leaves him, by way of gratifying them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:26
verses.text: They however were so urgent, that they again besought the judge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:27
verses.text: Yet against none of the Apostles had they set themselves thus pertinaciously; there, when they had attacked, anon they desisted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:28
verses.text: So providentially is he removed from Jerusalem, having to do with such wild beasts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:29
verses.text: And they nevertheless request that he might be brought again there to be tried.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:30
verses.text: "Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:31
verses.text: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him, and desired favor against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:32
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:33
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:34
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:35
verses.text: ) Here now God's providence interposed, not permitting the governor to do this: for it was natural that he having just come to the government would wish to gratify them: but God suffered him not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:36
verses.text: "But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:37
verses.text: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:38
verses.text: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:39
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:41
verses.text: ) But after they came down, they forthwith made their accusations shamelessly and with more vehemence: and not having been able to convict him on grounds relating to the Law, they again according to their custom stirred the question about Caesar, being just what they did in Christ's case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:42
verses.text: For that they had recourse to this is manifest by the fact, that Paul defends himself on the score of offences against Caesar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:43
verses.text: "And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:44
verses.text: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended anything at all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:45
verses.text: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me"? (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:46
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:47
verses.text: ) Wherefore he too gratifies the Jews, the whole people, and the city.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:48
verses.text: Such being the case, Paul terrifies him also, using a human weapon for his defence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:49
verses.text: "Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged; to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:50
verses.text: For if I be an offender, or have committed anything worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:51
verses.text: I appeal unto Caesar".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:52
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:54
verses.text: ) Some one might say, How is it, that having been told, "Thou must also bear witness of Me in Rome," (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:55
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:56
verses.text: ), he, as if unbelieving, did this? God forbid: nay, he did it, because he so strongly believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:57
verses.text: For it would have been a tempting of God to be bold on account of that declaration, and to cast himself into numberless dangers, and to say: "Let us see if God is able even thus to deliver me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:58
verses.text: But not so does Paul; no, he does his part, all that in him lies, committing the whole to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:59
verses.text: Quietly also he reproves the governor: for, "If, says he, I am an offender, thou doest well: but if not, why dost thou give me up?" "No man," he says, "may sacrifice me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:60
verses.text: He put him in fear, so that even if he wished, he could not sacrifice him to them; while also as an excuse to them he had Paul's appeal to allege.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:61
verses.text: "Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:62
verses.text: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:63
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:64
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:65
verses.text: ) Observe, he communicates the matter to Agrippa, so that there should be other hearers once more, both the king, and the army, and Bernice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:66
verses.text: Thereupon a speech in his exculpation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:67
verses.text: "And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:68
verses.text: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have license to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:69
verses.text: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:70
verses.text: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed: but had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:71
verses.text: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:72
verses.text: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:73
verses.text: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:74
verses.text: Tomorrow, said he, thou shalt hear him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:75
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:76
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:77
verses.text: ) And observe a crimination of the Jews, not from Paul, but also from the governor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:78
verses.text: "Desiring," he says, "to have judgment against him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:79
verses.text: To whom I said, to their shame, that "it is not the manner of the Romans," before giving an opportunity to speak for himself, "to sacrifice a man".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:80
verses.text: But I did give him (such opportunity), and I found no fault in him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:81
verses.text: "Because I doubted," says he, of "such manner of questions:" he casts a veil also over his own wrong.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:82
verses.text: Then the other desires to see him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:83
verses.text: (b) But let us look again at what has been said.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:84
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:85
verses.text: ) "And when Felix," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:86
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:87
verses.text: ) Observe on all occasions how the governors try to keep off from themselves the annoyance of the Jews, and are often compelled to act contrary to justice, and seek pretexts for deferring: for of course it was not from ignorance that he deferred the cause, but knowing it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:88
verses.text: And his wife also hears, together with the governor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:89
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:90
verses.text: ) This seems to me to show great honor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:91
verses.text: For he would not have brought his wife to be present with him at the hearing, but that he thought great things of him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:92
verses.text: It seems to me that she also longed for this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:93
verses.text: And observe how Paul immediately discourses not only about faith, nor about remission of sins, but also about practical points of duty.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:94
verses.text: "Go thy way," he says, "for this time: when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:95
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:96
verses.text: ) Observe his hardness of heart: hearing such things, "he hoped that he should receive money from him!" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:97
verses.text: ) And not only so, but even after conversing with him—for it was towards the end of his government—he left him bound, "willing to show the Jews a pleasure" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:98
verses.text: ): so that he not only coveted money, but also glory.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:99
verses.text: How, O wretch, canst thou look for money from a man who preaches the contrary? But that he did not get it, is evident from his leaving him bound; he would have loosed him, had he received it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:100
verses.text: "Of temperance," it says, he reasoned; but the other was hankering to receive money from him who discoursed these things! And to ask indeed he did not dare: for such is wickedness: but he hoped it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:101
verses.text: "And when two years were completed," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:102
verses.text: , so that it was but natural that he showed them a pleasure, as he had been so long governor there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:103
verses.text: "Now when Festus was come into the province," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:104
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:105
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:106
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:107
verses.text: ) At the very beginning, the priests came to him, who would not have hesitated to go even to Caesarea, unless he had been seen immediately coming up, since immediately on his arrival they come to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:108
verses.text: And he spends ten days, in order, I suppose, to be open to those who wished to corrupt him with bribes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:109
verses.text: But Paul was in the prison.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:110
verses.text: "They besought him," it says, "that he would send for him:" why did they desire it as a favor, if he was deserving of death? But thus their plotting became evident even to him, so that discoursing of it (to Agrippa), he says, "desiring to have judgment against him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:111
verses.text: They wanted to induce him to pass sentence now immediately, being afraid of Paul's tongue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:112
verses.text: What are ye afraid of? What are ye in such a hurry? In fact, that expression, "that he should be kept" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:113
verses.text: ), shows this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:114
verses.text: Does he want to escape? "Let them therefore," he says, "which among you are able, accuse him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:115
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:116
verses.text: ) Again accusers, again at Caesarea, again Paul is brought forth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:117
verses.text: And having come, immediately "he sat on the judgment-seat" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:118
verses.text: ); with all his haste: they so drove, so hurried him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:119
verses.text: While as yet he had not got acquainted with the Jews, nor experienced the honor paid to him by them, he answered rightly: but now that he had been in Jerusalem ten days, he too wants to pleasure them (by sacrificing Paul to them): then, also to receive Paul, "Wilt thou," says he, "be judged there of these things by me?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:120
verses.text: ) I am not giving thee up to them—but this was the fact—and he leaves the point to his own choice, that by this mark of respect he might get him to yield: since his was the sentence, and it would have been too barefaced, when he had been convicted of nothing here, to take him back thither.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:121
verses.text: "But Paul said, At Caesar's tribunal am I standing," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:122
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:123
verses.text: ): he did not say, I will not, lest he should make the judge more vehement, but (here) again is his great boldness: They cast me out once for all, themselves, and by this they think to condemn me, by their showing that I have offended against Caesar: at his bar I choose to be judged, at the bar of the injured person himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:124
verses.text: "To the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou also very well knowest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:125
verses.text: Here now he reproved him, that he too wished to sacrifice him to the Jews: then, on the other hand, he relaxes (the sternness of) his speech: "if then I be an offender, or have committed anything worthy of death, I refuse not to die".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:126
verses.text: I utter sentence against myself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:127
verses.text: For along with boldness of speech there must be also justness of cause, so as to abash (the hearer).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:128
verses.text: "But if there be nothing in the things whereof these accuse me, no man"—however he may wish it—"no man may sacrifice me to please them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:129
verses.text: He said, not, I am not worthy of death, nor, I am worthy to be acquitted, but, I am ready to take my trial before Caesar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:130
verses.text: At the same time too, remembering the dream, he was the more confident to appeal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:131
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:132
verses.text: xxiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:133
verses.text: ) And he said not, Thou (mayest not), but, neither any other man may sacrifice me, that it might be no affront to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:134
verses.text: "Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council"—do you observe how he seeks to gratify them? for this is favor—"having conferred," it says, "with the council, he said, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:135
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:136
verses.text: ) See how his trial is again lengthened out, and how the plot against him becomes an occasion for the preaching: so that with ease and in safe custody he should be taken away to Rome, with none to plot evil against him: for it was not the same thing his simply coming there, and his coming on such a cause.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:137
verses.text: For, in fact this was what made the Jews come together there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:138
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:139
verses.text: xxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:140
verses.text: ) Then again, some time passes while he tarries at Jerusalem, that you may learn, that, though some time passed, the evil design against him prevails nothing, God not permitting it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:141
verses.text: But this king Agrippa, who was also a Herod, was a different Agrippa, after him of James' time, so that this is the fourth (Herod).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:142
verses.text: See how his enemies coöperate with him against their will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:143
verses.text: To make the audience large, Agrippa falls into a desire of hearing: and he does not simply hear, but with much parade.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:144
verses.text: And see what a vindication (απολογιαν)! So writes Festus, and the ruthlessness of the Jews is openly made a show of: for when it is the governor that says these things, he is a witness above all suspicion: so that the Jews are condemned by him also.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:145
verses.text: For, when all had pronounced sentence against them, then, and not sooner, God brings upon them the punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:146
verses.text: But observe: Lysias gave it against them, Felix against them, Festus against them—although he wished to gratify them—Agrippa against them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:147
verses.text: What further? The Pharisees—even they gave it against themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:148
verses.text: No evil, says Festus, "of such things as I supposed: no accusation did they bring against him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:149
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:150
verses.text: ) And yet they did bring it: true, but they did not prove it: for their evil design and daring plot against him gave cause to surmise this, but the examination brought out nothing of the kind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:151
verses.text: "And of one Jesus," he says, "which was dead".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:152
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:153
verses.text: ) He says naturally enough, "of one" (Jesus), as being a man in office, and not caring for these things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:154
verses.text: "And not knowing, for my part, what to make of the enquiry concerning these things" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:155
verses.text: )—of course, it went beyond a judge's hearing, the examining into these matters.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:156
verses.text: If thou art at a loss, why dost thou drag him to Jerusalem? But the other would not deign this: no, "To Caesar" (says he); as in fact it was touching Caesar that they accused him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:157
verses.text: Do you hear the appeal? hear the plotting of the Jews? hear their factious spirit? All these things provoked him to a desire (of hearing him): and he gives them the gratification and Paul becomes more renowned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:158
verses.text: For such as I said, are the ill designs (of enemies).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:159
verses.text: Had not these things been so, none of these rulers would have deigned to hear him, none would have heard with such quietness and silence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:160
verses.text: And he seems indeed to be teaching, he seems to be making a defence; but he rather makes a public harangue with much orderliness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:161
verses.text: Then let us not think that ill designs against us are a grievous thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:162
verses.text: So long as we do not make ill designs against ourselves, no one will be able to have ill designs against us: or rather, people may do this, but they do us no hurt; nay, even benefit us in the highest degree: for it rests with ourselves, whether we shall suffer evil, or not suffer evil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:163
verses.text: Lo! I testify, and proclaim with a loud voice, more piercing even than the sound of a trumpet—and were it possible to ascend on high and cry aloud, I would not shrink from doing it—him that is a Christian, none of all the human beings that inhabit the earth will have power to hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:164
verses.text: And why do I say, human beings? Not even the Evil Spirit himself, the tyrant, the Devil, can do this, unless the man injure himself; be what it may that any one works, in vain he works it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:165
verses.text: For even as no human being could hurt an angel, if he were on earth, so neither can one human being hurt another human being.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:166
verses.text: But neither again will he himself be able to hurt another, so long as he is good.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:167
verses.text: What then can be equal to this, when neither to be hurt is possible, nor to hurt another? For this thing is not less than the former, the not wishing to hurt another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:168
verses.text: Why, that man is a kind of angel, yea, like God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:169
verses.text: For such is God; only, He indeed (is such) by nature, but this man, by moral choice: neither to be hurt is possible (for either), nor to hurt another.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:170
verses.text: But this thing, this "not possible," think not that it is for any want of power—for the contrary to this is want of power—no, I speak of the morally incompatible (τὸ ἀνενδεκτόν).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:171
verses.text: For the (Divine) Nature is neither Itself susceptible of hurt, nor capable of hurting another: since this very thing in itself is a hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:172
verses.text: For in no other way do we hurt ourselves, than by hurting another, and our greatest sins become such from our doing injury to ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:173
verses.text: So that for this reason also the Christian cannot be hurt, namely, because neither can he hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:174
verses.text: But how in hurting others we hurt ourselves, come, let us take this saying in hand for examination in detail.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:175
verses.text: Let a man wrong another, insult, overreach; whom then has he hurt? Is it not himself first? This is plain to every one.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:176
verses.text: For to the one, the damage is in money, to himself, it is in the soul; to destruction, and to punishment.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:177
verses.text: Again, let another be envious: is it not himself he has injured? For such is the nature of injustice: to its own author first it does incalculable hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:178
verses.text: "Yes, but to another also?" True, but nothing worth considering: or rather, not even a little—nay, it even benefits him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:179
verses.text: For let there be,—as the whole matter lies most in these examples,—let there be some poor man, having but little property and (barely) provided with necessary food, and another rich and wealthy, and having much power, and then let him take the poor man's property, and strip him naked, and give him up to starvation, while he shall luxuriate in what he has unjustly taken from the other: not only has he not hurt that man at all—he has even benefited him, while himself he has not only not benefited, but even hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:180
verses.text: For how should it be otherwise? In the first place, harassed by an evil conscience, and day by day condemning himself and being condemned by all men: and then, secondly, in the judgment to come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:181
verses.text: But the other, how is he benefited? Because to suffer ill and bear it nobly, is great gain: for it is a doing away of sins, this suffering of ill, it is a training to philosophy, it is a discipline of virtue.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:182
verses.text: Let us see which of the two is in evil case, this man or that.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:183
verses.text: For the one, if he be a man of well-ordered mind, will bear it nobly: the other will be every day in a constant tremor and misgiving: which then is hurt, this man or that? "You talk idly," say you: "for when a man has nothing to eat, and is forced to bewail himself and to feel himself very wretched, or comes and begs, and gets nothing, is not that a ruining of both soul and body?" No, it is you that talk idly: for I show facts in proof.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:184
verses.text: For say, does none of the rich feel himself wretched? What then? Is poverty the cause of his wretchedness? "But he does not starve".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:185
verses.text: And what of that? The greater is the punishment, when having riches he does this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:186
verses.text: For neither does wealth make a man strong-minded, nor poverty make him weak: otherwise none of those living in wealth would pass a wretched life, nor would any of those in poverty (not) curse his fate.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:187
verses.text: But that yours is indeed the idle talk, I will make manifest to you from hence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:188
verses.text: Was Paul in poverty or in wealth? did he suffer hunger, or did he not? You may hear himself saying, "In hunger and thirst".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:189
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:190
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:191
verses.text: ) Did the prophets suffer hunger, or did they not? They too had a hard time of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:192
verses.text: "Again, you fetch up Paul to me, again the prophets, some ten or twenty men".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:193
verses.text: But whence shall I bring examples? "Show me from the many some who bear ills nobly".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:194
verses.text: But the rare is ever such: however, if you will, let us examine the matter as it is in itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:195
verses.text: Let us see whose is the greater and sharper care, whose the more easy to be borne.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:196
verses.text: The one is solicitous about his necessary food, the other about numberless matters, freed from that care.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:197
verses.text: The rich man is not afraid on the score of hunger, but he is afraid about other things: oftentimes for his very life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:198
verses.text: The poor man is not free from anxiety about food, but he is free from other anxieties, he has safety, has quietness, has security.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:199
verses.text: If to injure another is not an evil, but a good, wherefore are we ashamed? wherefore do we cover our faces? Wherefore, being reproached, are we vexed and disconcerted? If the being injured is not a good thing, wherefore do we pride ourselves, and glory in the thing, and justify ourselves on its account? Would you learn how this is better than that? Observe those who are in the one condition, and those who are in the other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:200
verses.text: Wherefore are laws? Wherefore are courts of justice? Wherefore punishments? Is it not, on account of those men, as being diseased and unsound? But the pleasure lies great, you will say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:201
verses.text: Let us not speak of the future: let us look into the present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:202
verses.text: What is worse than a man who is under such a suspicion as this? what more precarious? what more unsound? is he not always in a state of shipwreck? Even if he do any just thing, he is not credited, condemned as he is by all on account of his power (of injuring): for in all who dwell with him he has accusers: he cannot enjoy friendship: for none would readily choose to become the friend of a man who has such a character, for fear of becoming implicated with him in the opinion held of him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:203
verses.text: As if he were a wild beast, all men turn away from him; as from a pest, a foe, a man-slayer, and an enemy of nature, so they shrink from the unjust man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:204
verses.text: If he who has wronged another happen to be brought into a court of justice, he does not even need an accuser, his character condemns him in place of any accuser.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:205
verses.text: Not so he who is injured; he has all men to take his part, to condole with him, to stretch out the hand of help: he stands on safe ground.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:206
verses.text: If to injure another be a good and a safe thing, let any one confess that he is unjust: but if he dares not do this, why then does he pursue it as a good thing? But let us see in our own persons, if his same be done there, what evils come of it: (I mean,) if any of the parts or functions within us having overstepped its proper bounds, grasp at the office of some other.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:207
verses.text: For let the spleen, if it will, have left its proper place, and seize on the part belonging to some other organ along with its own, is not this disease? The moisture within us, let it fill every place, is it not dropsy and gout? is not this to ruin itself, along with the other? Again, let the bile seek for a wide room, and let the blood be diffused throughout every part.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:208
verses.text: But how is it in the soul with anger, lust, and all the rest, if the food exceed its proper measure? Again in the body, if the eye wish to take in more, or to see more than is allotted to it, or admit a greater light than is proper.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:209
verses.text: But if, when the light is good, yet the eye is ruined, if it choose to see more than is right: consider what it must be in the case of an evil thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:210
verses.text: If the ear take in a (too) loud voice, the sense is stunned: the mind, if it reason about things above itself, it is overpowered: and whatever is in excess, mars all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:211
verses.text: For this is πλεονεξία, the wanting to have more than what is marked off and allotted.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:212
verses.text: So too in respect of money; when we will needs put upon (us) more burdens (than is meet), although we do not perceive it, to our sore hurt we are nourishing within ourselves a wild beast; much having, yet much wanting, numberless the cares we entangle ourselves withal, many the handles we furnish the devil against ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:213
verses.text: In the case of the rich, however, the devil has not even need of labor, so surely do their very concerns of business of themselves ruin them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 139:214
verses.text: Wherefore I beseech you to abstain from the lust of these things, that we may be enabled to escape the snares of the evil one, and having taken hold of virtue, to attain unto the good things eternal, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory forever, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:1
verses.text: Homily LII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:2
verses.text: Acts XXV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:3
verses.text: "And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus' commandment Paul was brought forth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:4
verses.text: See what an audience is gathered together for Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:5
verses.text: Having collected all his guards, the governor is come, and the king, and the tribunes, "with the principal men," it says, "of the city".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:6
verses.text: Then Paul being brought forth, see how he is proclaimed as conqueror.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:7
verses.text: Festus himself acquits him from the charges, for what says Festus? "And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:8
verses.text: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:9
verses.text: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:10
verses.text: Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and especially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:11
verses.text: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:12
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:13
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:14
verses.text: ) Mark how he accuses them, while he acquits him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:15
verses.text: O what an abundance of justifications! After all these repeated examinations, the governor finds not how he may condemn him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:16
verses.text: They said he was worthy of death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:17
verses.text: On this account he said also: "When I found," says he "that he had committed nothing worthy of death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:18
verses.text: —Of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:19
verses.text: This too is a proof of Paul's spotlessness, that the judge found nothing to say concerning him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:20
verses.text: "Therefore I have brought him forth," he says, "before you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:21
verses.text: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crime laid against him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:22
verses.text: Such were the great straits into which the Jews brought themselves and their rulers! What then? "Agrippa said to Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:23
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:24
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:25
verses.text: ) From his great desire to hear, the king permits him to speak.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:26
verses.text: But Paul speaks out forthwith with boldness, not flattering, but for this reason saying that he is happy, namely, because (Agrippa) knew all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:27
verses.text: "Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:28
verses.text: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:29
verses.text: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:30
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:32
verses.text: ) And yet, had he been conscious of guilt, he should have feared at being tried in the presence of one who knew all the facts: but this is a mark of a clear conscience, not to shrink from a judge who has an accurate knowledge of the circumstances, but even to rejoice, and to call himself happy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:33
verses.text: "I beseech thee," he says, "to hear me patiently".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:34
verses.text: Since he is about to lengthen out his speech, and to say something about himself, on this account, he premises an entreaty, and (then) says: "My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews: which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:35
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:36
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:37
verses.text: ) Then how should I have become a seditious person, who when young was (thus) testified of by all? Then too from his sect: "after the most straitest sect" says he, "of our religion I lived".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:38
verses.text: "What then, if though the sect indeed be worthy of admiration, thou art evil?" Touching this also I call all to witness—touching my life and conversation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:39
verses.text: "And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers: unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:40
verses.text: For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:41
verses.text: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:42
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:43
verses.text: ) Two arguments he lays down for the Resurrection: one, the argument from the prophets: and he does not bring forward any prophet (in particular,) but the doctrine itself as held by the Jews: the other and stronger one, the argument from the facts—(especially from this,) that Christ Himself held discourse with him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:44
verses.text: And he lays the ground for this by (other) arguments, relating accurately his former madness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:45
verses.text: Then too, with high commendation of the Jews, he says, "Night and day," says he, "serving (God) look to attain unto".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:46
verses.text: So that even if I had not been of unblemished life, it is not for this (doctrine) that I ought to be brought to trial:—"for which hope, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:47
verses.text: And then another argument "Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?" Since, if such an opinion had not existed, if they had not been brought up in these dogmas, but they were now for the first time brought in, perhaps some one might not have received the saying.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:48
verses.text: Then he tells, how he persecuted: this also helps the proof: and he brings forward the chief priests as witnesses, and the "strange cities," and that he heard Him saying to him, "It is hard for thee to kick against the pricks," and shows the mercifulness of God, that, though being persecuted He appeared (to men), and did that benefit not to me only, but also sent me as teacher to others: and shows also the prophecy, now come to pass, which he then heard, "Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom I send thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:49
verses.text: Showing all this, he says: "I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:50
verses.text: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:51
verses.text: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:52
verses.text: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests, at midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:53
verses.text: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:54
verses.text: And I said, Who art Thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest; but rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee: delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee, to open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:55
verses.text: –):—observe how mildly he discourses—God, he says, said (this) to me, "that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in Me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:56
verses.text: By these things, says he, I was persuaded, by this vision He drew me to Himself, and so persuaded me, that I made no delay.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:57
verses.text: "Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision: but showed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:59
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:60
verses.text: ) I therefore, who instructed others also concerning the most excellent way of living, how should I myself have become the author of sedition and contention? "For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:61
verses.text: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:62
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:63
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:64
verses.text: ) See how free from flattery his speech is, and how he ascribes the whole to God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:65
verses.text: Then his boldness—but neither do I now desist: and the sure grounds—for it is from the prophets that I urge the question, "Whether the Christ was to suffer:" then the Resurrection and the promise, "Whether He, as the first to rise from the dead, should show light unto the people and to the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:66
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:67
verses.text: ) Festus saw the boldness, and what says he? For Paul was all along addressing himself to the king—he was in a manner annoyed, and says to him, "Thou art beside thyself, Paul:" for, "while he thus discoursed, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself: much learning doth make thee mad".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:68
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:69
verses.text: ) What then says Paul? With gentleness, "I am not mad," says he, "most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:70
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:71
verses.text: ) Then too he gives him to understand why, turning from him, he addressed his speech to the king: "For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him: for this thing was not done in a corner".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:72
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:73
verses.text: ) He shows, that (the king) knows all perfectly; at the same time, all but saying to the Jews, And ye indeed ought to have known these things—for this is the meaning of that which he adds, "For this thing was not done in a corner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:74
verses.text: And Agrippa, said to Paul, ᾽Εν ὀλίγῳ thou persuadest me to be a Christian".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:75
verses.text: What is ἐν ὀλίγῳ? "Within a little, παρὰ μικρόν.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:76
verses.text: "And Paul said, I could pray to God," καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ καὶ ἐν πολλᾥ, (that is) "I could pray to God," for my part, not "in little" (but "in much"): he does not simply pray, he prays (not briefly, but) with largeness—"that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were such as I am".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:77
verses.text: Then he adds, "except these bonds;" and yet it was matter of glory; true, but looking to their notion of it, therefore says he, "except these bonds".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:78
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:79
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:80
verses.text: )  (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:81
verses.text: ) "And on the morrow," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:82
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:83
verses.text: ) The Jews desisted ever since Paul exercised his right of appeal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:84
verses.text: Then also for him the theatre becomes a splendid one: "with great pomp" they were present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:85
verses.text: "And Festus said," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:86
verses.text: "The whole multitude of the Jews—"not some of them only, and others not so—"both at Jerusalem, and also here," they said "that he ought not to live any longer".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:87
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:88
verses.text: ) "And I having found," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:89
verses.text: It shows that he did right in appealing to Caesar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:90
verses.text: For if though they had no great matter to allege against him, yet those (at Jerusalem) were mad against him, with good reason may he go to Caesar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:91
verses.text: "That after examination had by you," he says, "I may get somewhat to write".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:92
verses.text: Observe how the matter is repeatedly put to the test.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:93
verses.text: The Jews therefore may thank themselves for this vindication (of Paul), which would come to the ears of those also who were at Rome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:94
verses.text: See how they become the unwilling heralds both of their own wickedness and of Paul's virtue, even to the emperor himself: so that Paul was carried away (to Rome) with more renown than if he had gone thither without bonds: for not as an impostor and a deceiver, after so many judges had acquitted him, was he now carried thither.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:95
verses.text: Quit therefore of all charges, among those with whom he was bred and born, and not only so, (but) thus free from all suspicion, he makes his appearance at Rome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:96
verses.text: "Then Paul," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:97
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:98
verses.text: xxvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:99
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:100
verses.text: ) And he said not, Why is this? once for all I have appealed to Caesar: I have been tried many times: when will there be an end of this? but what did he? Again he is ready to render an account, and that, before the man who was the best informed on the subject; and with much boldness, seeing they were not his judges to condemn him: but still, though they were not his judges, since that declaration was in force, "Unto Caesar shalt thou go, he renders an account and gives full answers, "touching all the things," and not merely on one and another here and there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:101
verses.text: They accuse me of sedition, accuse me of heresy, accuse me that I have profaned the temple: "touching all these things I answer for myself:" now that these are not things in accordance with my ways, my accusers themselves are witnesses: "my manner of life from my youth," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:102
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:103
verses.text: ) which is what he says on a former occasion "Being a zealot".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:104
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:105
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:106
verses.text: ) And when the whole people was present, then he challenges their testimony: not before the tribunal, but before Lysias, and again here, when more were present: whereas in that hearing there needed not much vindication of himself, since Lysias' letter exculpated him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:107
verses.text: "Know all the Jews," he says, "which knew me from the beginning".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:108
verses.text: And he does not say what kind of life his was, but leaves it to their own conscience, and lays the whole stress on his sect, as he would not have chosen that sect, if he had been a man of evil disposition and bad character (πονηρὸς καὶ μοχθηρός).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:109
verses.text: "But, for this hope" (mss.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:110
verses.text: and Edd.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:111
verses.text: αἱρέσεως) he says, "I stand and am judged".
