verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:112
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:113
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:114
verses.text: ) This hope is honored among themselves also, because of this they pray, because of this they worship, that unto this they may attain: this same do I show forth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:115
verses.text: Why then, it is acting like madmen, to be doing all things for the sake of attaining to this, and yet to persecute him who believes in the same.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:116
verses.text: "I indeed thought with myself," that is, I determined, "to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:117
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:118
verses.text: ) I was not one of Christ's disciples: among those who fought against Him, was I.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:119
verses.text: Whence also he is a witness who has a right to be believed, because he, a man who was doing numberless things, makes war on the believers, persuading them to blaspheme, stirring up all against them, cities, rulers, and by himself doing all this of his own accord, was thus suddenly changed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:120
verses.text: Then again the witnesses, those who were with him: next he shows what just cause he had to be persuaded, both from the light, and from the prophets, and from the results, and from the things which have now taken place.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:121
verses.text: See accordingly, how both from the prophets, and from these particulars, he confirms the proof to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:122
verses.text: For that he may not seem to be broaching some novelty, although he had great things to say, yet he again takes refuge with the prophets, and puts this as a question for discussion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:123
verses.text: Now this had a stronger claim upon belief, as having actually come to pass: but since he alone saw (Christ), he again fetches proof of it from the prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:124
verses.text: And see how he does not discourse alike in the court of justice, and in the assembly (of his own people); there indeed he says, "ye slew Him:" but here no such thing, that he might not kindle their anger more: but he shows the same thing, by saying, "Whether the Christ was to suffer".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:125
verses.text: He so frees them from accusations: for the prophets, he says, say this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:126
verses.text: Therefore receive ye also the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:127
verses.text: Since he has mentioned the vision, he then without fear goes on to speak also of the good wrought by it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:128
verses.text: "To turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:129
verses.text: For to this end have I appeared unto thee" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:130
verses.text: –), not to punish, but to make thee an Apostle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:131
verses.text: He shows the evils which possess unbelievers, "Satan, darkness;" the good things belonging to believers, light, God, "the inheritance of the saints.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:132
verses.text: Whereupon, O king Agrippa," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:133
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:134
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:135
verses.text: ) He not only exhorts them to repent, but also to show forth a life worthy of admiration.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:136
verses.text: And see how everywhere the Gentiles are admitted into connection with the people (Israel): for those who were present were of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:137
verses.text: "Testifying," he says, "both to great and small," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:138
verses.text: ) that is, both to distinguished and undistinguished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:139
verses.text: This is also for the soldiers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:140
verses.text: Observe: having left the post of defendant, he took up that of teacher—and therefore also it is that Festus says to him, "Thou art beside thyself"—but then, that he may not seem to be himself the teacher, he brings in the prophets, and Moses: "Whether the Christ was to suffer, whether He as the first to rise from the dead should show light both to the people, and to the Gentiles".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:141
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:142
verses.text: ) "And Festus said with a loud voice"—in such anger and displeasure (did he speak)—"Paul, thou art beside thyself".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:143
verses.text: What then said Paul? "I am not mad," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:144
verses.text: "For this thing," he says, "was not done in a corner".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:145
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:146
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:147
verses.text: ) Here he speaks of the Cross, of the Resurrection: that the doctrine was come to every part of the world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:148
verses.text: "King Agrippa," he says, "believest thou"—he does not say, the Resurrection, but—"the prophets?" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:149
verses.text: ) Then he forestalls him, and says: "I know that thou believest".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:150
verses.text: ᾽Εν ὀλίγῳ (i-e: within a little,) "almost thou persuadeth the to be a Christian".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:151
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:152
verses.text: ) Paul did not understand what the phrase ἐν ὀλίγῳ meant: he thought it meant ἐξ ὀλιγου (i-e: with little cost or trouble), wherefore also he answers (as) to this: so unlearned was he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:153
verses.text: And he said not, I do not wish (that), but, "I pray that not only thou, but also all that hear".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:154
verses.text: Mark how free from flattery his speech is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:155
verses.text: —"I pray that this day they may be all such as I am, except these bonds".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:156
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:157
verses.text: ) He, the man that glories in his bonds, that puts them forth as a golden chain, deprecates them for these men: for they were as yet too weak in their minds, and it was rather in condescension that he so spake.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:158
verses.text: For what could be better than those bonds which always in his Epistles he prefers (to all things else), saying, "Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ:" (Eph.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:159
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:160
verses.text: ) and again, "On this account I am bound with this chain" (Acts xxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:161
verses.text: ), "but the word of God is not bound;" and, "Even unto bonds, as an evil-doer".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:162
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:163
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:164
verses.text: ) The punishment was twofold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:165
verses.text: For if indeed he had been so bound, as with a view to his good, the thing would have carried with it some consolation: but now (he is bound) both "as an evil-doer," and as with a view to very ill consequences; yet for none of these things cared he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:166
verses.text: Such is a soul winged with heavenly love.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:167
verses.text: For if those who cherish the foul (earthly passion which men call) love, think nothing either glorious of precious, but those things alone which tend to gratify their lust, they think both glorious and honorable, and their mistress is everything to them; much more do those, who have been taken captive by this heavenly love, think nothing of the cost (τὰ ἐπιτίμια).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:168
verses.text: But if we do not understand what I am saying, it is no marvel, while we are unskilled in this Divine Wisdom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:169
verses.text: For if any one be caught with the fire of Christ's love, he becomes such as a man would become who dwelt alone upon the earth, so utterly careless is he for glory or disgrace: but just as if he dwelt alone, he would care for nothing, no more does he in this case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:170
verses.text: As for trials, he so despises them, both scourges and imprisonments, as though the body in which he suffers these things were another's and not his own, or as though he had got a body made of adamant: while as for the sweet things of this life, he so laughs them to scorn, is so insensible to them, as we are insensible of dead bodies, being ourselves dead.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:171
verses.text: He is as far from being taken captive by any passion, as the gold refined in the fire and purified is free from alloy.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:172
verses.text: For even as flies would not dart into the midst of a flame, but fly from it, so the passions dare not even to come near this man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:173
verses.text: Would that I could bring forward examples of all this from among ourselves: but since we are at a loss for such, we must needs betake ourselves to this same Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:174
verses.text: Observe him then, how he felt towards the whole world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:175
verses.text: "The world is crucified unto me," he says, "and I unto the world" (Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:176
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:177
verses.text: ): I am dead to the world, and the world is dead to me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:178
verses.text: And again: "It is no longer I that live, but Christ liveth in me".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:179
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:180
verses.text: Gal.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:181
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:182
verses.text: ) And, to show you that he was as it were in solitude, and so looked upon the things present, hear himself saying, "While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:183
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:184
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:185
verses.text: ) What sayest thou? Answer me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:186
verses.text: And yet what thou sayest is the contrary; thou seest the things invisible, and the visible thou seest not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:187
verses.text: Such eyes as thou hadst gotten, such are the eyes which are given by Christ: for as these bodily eyes see indeed the things that are seen, but things unseen they see not: so those (heavenly eyes) do the contrary: none that beholds the invisible things, beholds the visible: no one beholding the things seen, beholds the invisible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:188
verses.text: Or is not this the case with us also? For when having turned our mind inwards we think of any of the unseen things, our views become raised above the things on earth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:189
verses.text: Let us despise glory: let us be willing to be laughed at rather than to be praised.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:190
verses.text: For he indeed who is laughed at is nothing hurt: but he who is praised is much hurt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:191
verses.text: Let us not think much of those things which terrify men, but as we do in the case of children, this let us do here: namely, if we see any one terrifying children, we do not hold that man in admiration: since in fact whoever does frighten, only frightens children; for were it a man, he could not frighten him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:192
verses.text: Just as those who frighten (children in sport), do this either by drawing up their eyelids, or by otherwise distorting their face, but with the eye looking naturally and mild they would not be able to do this: so these others do this, by distorting their mental vision (τὸ διορατικὸν τἥς διανοίας).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:193
verses.text: So that of a mild man and beautiful in soul nobody would be afraid; on the contrary, we all respect him, honor and venerate him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:194
verses.text: See ye not, how the man who causes terror is also an object of hatred and abhorrence to us all? For of those things which are only able to terrify what do we not turn away from? Is it not so with wild beasts, with sounds, with sights, with places, with the air, such as darkness? Let us not therefore think it a great thing, if men fear us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:195
verses.text: For, in the first place, no man indeed is frightened at us: and, secondly, it is no great thing (if they were).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:196
verses.text: Virtue is a great good: and see how great.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:197
verses.text: However wretched we may deem the things by means of which it consists, yet we admire virtue itself, and count them blessed (that have it).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:198
verses.text: For who would not count the patient sufferer blessed, although poverty and such like things seem to be wretched? When therefore it shines forth through those things which seem to be wretched, see how surpassingly great this is! Thinkest thou much, O man, because thou art in power? And what sort of power? say, was it conferred by appointment? (If so,) of men thou hast received power: appoint thyself to it from within.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:199
verses.text: For the ruler is not he who is so called, but he who is really so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:200
verses.text: For as a king could not make a physician or an orator, so neither can he make a ruler: since it is not the (imperial) letters nor the name that makes a ruler.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:201
verses.text: For, if you will, let any man build a medicine-shop, let him also have pupils, let him have instruments too and drugs, and let him visit those who are sick: are these things sufficient to make a physician? By no means: but there is need of art, and without that, not only do these things profit nothing, but they even hurt: since it were better that he who is not a physician should not even possess medicines.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:202
verses.text: He that possesses them not, neither saves nor destroys: but he that possesses them, destroys, if he knows not how to use them: since the healing power is not only in the nature of the medicines, but also in the art of the person applying them: where this is not, all is marred.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:203
verses.text: Such also is the ruler: he has for instruments, his voice, anger, executioners, banishments, honors, gifts, and praises; he has also for medicines, the law; has also for his patients, men; for a place to practise in, the court of justice; for pupils, he has the soldiers: if then he know not the science of healing, all these profit him nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:204
verses.text: The judge is a physician of souls, not of bodies: but if this art of healing the bodies needs so much care, much more that of healing the soul, since the soul is of more importance than the body.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:205
verses.text: Then not the mere having the name of ruler is to be a ruler: since others also are called by great names: as Paul, Peter, James, and John: but the names do not make them that which they are called, as neither does my name make me (to be that which John was); I bear indeed the same name with that blessed man, but I am not the same thing (ὁμώνυμος, οὐ μὴν συνώνυμος), I am not John, but am called so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:206
verses.text: In the same way they are not rulers, but are called so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:207
verses.text: But those others are rulers even without these adjuncts, just as also a physician, though he may not actually practise his science, yet if he have it in his soul, he is a physician.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:208
verses.text: Those are rulers, who bear rule over themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:209
verses.text: For there are these four things, soul, family; city, world: and the things form a regular progression (ὁδᾥ προβαίνει).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:210
verses.text: He therefore that is to superintend a family, and order it well, must first bring his own soul into order; for it is his family: but if he cannot order his own family, where there is but one soul, where he himself is master, where he is always along with himself, how shall he order others? He that is able to regulate his own soul, and makes the one part to rule, the other to be subject, this man will be able to regulate a family also: but he that can do this by a family, can do it by a city also: and if by a city, then also by the world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:211
verses.text: But if he cannot do this for his own soul, how then shall he be able to do it for the world? These things have been spoken by me, that we may not be excited about offices of rule; that we may know what ruling is: for this (which is so called) is not ruling, but a there object of derision, mere slavery, and many other names one might call it by.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:212
verses.text: Tell me, what is proper to a ruler? is it not to help one's subjects, and to do them good? What then, if this be not the case? how shall he help others, who has not helped himself? he who has numberless tyrannies of the passions in his own soul, how shall he root out those of others? Again, with respect to "luxury" or delightful living: the true luxury or delight is not this (which is so called), but quite another thing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:213
verses.text: For as we have shown that the ruler is not he who is so called, but another (who has something more than the name), so the person who lives indeed in delight is another sort of person (than he whom we so describe).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:214
verses.text: For "luxury" or delightful living seems indeed to be, the enjoying pleasure and the gratifying the belly: yet it is not this thing, but the contrary: it is, to have a soul worthy of admiration, and to be in a state of pleasure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:215
verses.text: For let there be a man eating, drinking, and wantoning; then let him suffer cares and loss of spirits: can this man be said to be in a state of delight? Therefore, it is not eating and drinking, it is the being in pleasure, that makes true luxury or delightful living.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:216
verses.text: Let there be a man who gets only dry bread, and let him be filled with gladness: is not this pleasure? Well then, it is the true luxury.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:217
verses.text: Let us see then, to whom this befalls—whether to the rich, or to those who are not rich? Neither to the one part altogether, nor to the other, but to those who so order their own souls, that they may not have many grounds for sorrows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:218
verses.text: And where is such a life as this to be found? for I see you all eager and wishing to hear what this life is which has no sorrows.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:219
verses.text: Well then, let this be acknowledged first by you, that this is pleasure, this the true luxury, to have no sorrow to cause annoyance; and ask not of me meats, and wine, and sauces, and silken robes, and a sumptuous table.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:220
verses.text: But if I shall show that apart from all these such a life as that is present (within our reach), then welcome thou this pleasure, and this life: for the most part of painful things happen to us from our not calculating things as we ought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:221
verses.text: Who then will have the most sorrows—he that cares for none of these things, or he that cares for them? He that fears changes, or he that does not fear? He that is in dread of jealousy, of envy, of false accusations, of plottings, of destruction, or he that stands aloof from these fears? He that wants many things, or he that wants nothing? He that is a slave to masters without number, or he that is a slave to none? He that has need of many things, or he that is free? He that has one lord to fear, or he that fears despots innumerable? Well then, greater is the pleasure here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 140:222
verses.text: This then let us pursue, and not be excited about the things present: but let us laugh to scorn all the pomp of life, and everywhere practise moderation, that we may be enabled so to pass through this life, that it may be without pain, and to attain unto the good things promised, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:1
verses.text: Homily LIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:2
verses.text: Acts XXVI.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:3
verses.text: –  "And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them: and when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:4
verses.text: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:5
verses.text: See how again also they pass sentence in his favor, and after having said, "Thou art beside thyself," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:6
verses.text: ) they acquit him, as undeserving not only of death, but also of bonds, and indeed would have released him entirely, if he had not appealed to Caesar.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:7
verses.text: But this was done providentially, that he should also depart with bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:8
verses.text: "Unto bonds," he says, "as an evil doer".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:9
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:10
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:11
verses.text: ) For if his Lord "was reckoned among the transgressors" (Mark xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:12
verses.text: ), much more he: but as the Lord did not share with them in their character, so neither did Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:13
verses.text: For in this is seen the marvellous thing, the being mixed up with such, and yet receiving no harm from them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:14
verses.text: "And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:15
verses.text: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:16
verses.text: And the next day we touched at Sidon".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:17
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:18
verses.text: xxvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:20
verses.text: ) See how far Aristarchus also accompanies Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:21
verses.text: To good and useful purpose is Aristarchus present, as he would take back the report of all to Macedonia.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:22
verses.text: "And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:23
verses.text: Julius gave Paul liberty," it says, acting "courteously, that he might refresh himself;" as it was but natural that he should be much the worse from his bonds and the fear, and the being dragged hither and thither.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:24
verses.text: See how the writer does not hide this either, that Paul wished "to refresh himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:25
verses.text: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:27
verses.text: ) Again trials, again contrary winds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:28
verses.text: See how the life of the saints is thus interwoven throughout: escaped from the court of justice, they fall in with shipwreck and storm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:29
verses.text: "And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:30
verses.text: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:31
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:32
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:33
verses.text: ) "A ship of Alexandria," it says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:34
verses.text: It is likely that both those (in the former ship) would bear to Asia the report of what had befallen Paul, and that these would do the same in Lycia.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:35
verses.text: See how God does not innovate or change the order of nature, but suffers them to sail into the unfavorable winds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:36
verses.text: But even so the miracle is wrought.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:37
verses.text: That they may sail safely, He did not let them go out in the (open) sea, but they always sailed near the land.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:38
verses.text: "And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone; and, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called the fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:39
verses.text: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:42
verses.text: ) By "the fast" here, I suppose he means that of the Jews.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:43
verses.text: For they departed thence a long time after the Pentecost, so that it was much about midwinter that they arrived at the coasts of Crete.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:44
verses.text: And this too was no slight miracle, that they also should be saved on his account.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:45
verses.text: "Paul admonished them, and said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:46
verses.text: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:47
verses.text: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the southwest and northwest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:48
verses.text: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close to Crete.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:49
verses.text: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:50
verses.text: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive" (R.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:51
verses.text: V.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:52
verses.text: "were driven".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:53
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:54
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:55
verses.text: ) Paul therefore advised them to remain, and he foretells what would come of it: but they, being in a hurry, and being prevented by the place, wished to winter at Phenice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:56
verses.text: Mark then the providential ordering of the events: first indeed, "when the south wind blew softly, supposing they had obtained their purpose," they loosed the vessel, and came forth; then when the wind bore down upon them, they gave way to it driving them, and were with difficulty saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:57
verses.text: "And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat: which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:58
verses.text: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship; and the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:59
verses.text: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:60
verses.text: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:61
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:62
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:63
verses.text: ) Then after so great a storm he does not speak as insultingly over them, but as wishing that at any rate he might be believed for the future.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:64
verses.text: Wherefore also he alleges what had taken place for a testimony of the truth of what was about to be said by him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:65
verses.text: "And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:66
verses.text: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:67
verses.text: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer, for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:68
verses.text: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:69
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:70
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:71
verses.text: ) And he foretells two things; both that they must be cast upon an island, and that though the ship would be lost, those who were in it should be saved—which thing he spoke not of conjecture, but of prophecy—and that he "must be brought before Caesar".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:72
verses.text: But this that he says, "God hath given thee all," is not spoken boastfully, but in the wish to win those who were sailing in the ship: for (he spoke thus), not that they might feel themselves bound to him, but that they might believe what he was saying.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:73
verses.text: "God hath given thee;" as much (as to say), They are worthy indeed of death, since they would not listen to thee: however, this is done out of favor to thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:74
verses.text: "But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country; and sounded, and found it twenty fathoms; and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:75
verses.text: Then fearing lest they should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:76
verses.text: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under color as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship, Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:77
verses.text: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:78
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:79
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:80
verses.text: ) The sailors however, were about to escape, having no faith in what was said: but the centurion does believe Paul, For he says, If these flee, "ye cannot be saved:" so saying, not on this account, but that he might restrain them, and the prophecy might not fall to the ground.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:81
verses.text: See how as in a church they are instructed by the calmness of Paul's behavior, how he saved them out of the very midst of the dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:82
verses.text: And it is of providential ordering that Paul is disbelieved, that after proof of the facts, he might be believed: which accordingly was the case.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:83
verses.text: And he exhorts them again to take some meat, and they do as he bids them, and he takes some first, to persuade them not by word, but also by act, that the storm did them no harm, but rather was a benefit to their souls.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:84
verses.text: "And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting having taken nothing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:85
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:86
verses.text: ) (b) And how, say you, did they go without food, having taken nothing? how did they bear it? Their fear possessed them, and did not let them fall into a desire of food, being, as they were, at the point of extreme jeopardy; (f) but they had no care for food.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:87
verses.text: "Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:88
verses.text: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:89
verses.text: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:90
verses.text: –) seeing that there was no question about their lives being saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:91
verses.text: (d) "And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:92
verses.text: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:93
verses.text: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:94
verses.text: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoisted up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:95
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:96
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:97
verses.text: ) "They made towards shore," having given the rudder-handles to the wind: for oftentimes they do it not in this way.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:98
verses.text: They were borne along, having loosed the rigging, i-e: the sails.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:99
verses.text: "And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmovable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves;" for when there is a strong wind, this is the consequence, the stern bearing the brunt (of the storm).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:100
verses.text: (a) "And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:101
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:102
verses.text: ) Again the devil tries to hinder the prophecy, and they had a mind to kill some, but the centurion suffered them not, that he might save Paul, so much was the centurion attached to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:103
verses.text: "But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land: and the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:104
verses.text: And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:105
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:106
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:107
verses.text: ) "And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:108
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:109
verses.text: xxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:110
verses.text: ) Do you mark what good came of the storm? Why then it was no mark of their being forsaken, that the storm came upon them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:111
verses.text: (c) Now this that happened was in consequence of the season of the year; but the wonder is greater, that at such a season they were saved from the midst of the dangers, both he, and for his sake the rest, (e) and this too in the Hadriatic.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:112
verses.text: There were two hundred and seventy-six souls in all: no small matter this also, if indeed they believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:113
verses.text: The voyage was at an unseasonable time.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:114
verses.text: (g) It is natural to suppose they would ask the reason why they were sailing, and would learn all.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:115
verses.text: Nor was it for nothing that the voyage was so protracted; it afforded Paul an opportunity for teaching.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:116
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:117
verses.text: ) And Paul says, "I perceive that (this voyage will be) with hurt and loss".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:118
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:119
verses.text: ) And observe how unassuming the expression is.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:120
verses.text: That he may not seem to prophesy, but to speak as of conjecture, "I perceive," says he.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:121
verses.text: For they would not have received it, had he said this at the outset.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:122
verses.text: In fact he does prophesy on this former occasion, as he does afterward, and says (there), "The God whom I serve," leading them on.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:123
verses.text: Then how comes it that it was not "with loss" (of any) "of their lives?" It would have been so, but that God brought them safe through it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:124
verses.text: For as far as depended on the nature of the thing, they had perished, but God prevented it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:125
verses.text: Then, to show that it was not from conjecture that he so spake, the master of the ship said the contrary (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:126
verses.text: ), and he a man of experience in the matter: so far was it from being the case that Paul's advice was given from conjecture.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:127
verses.text: Moreover, the place suggested this same (which the master said), "being not commodious;" and it was evident that from conjecture "the more part advised" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:128
verses.text: ) as they did, rather than Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:129
verses.text: Then, severe the storm (that ensued), deep the darkness: and that they may not forget, the vessel also goes to pieces, and the corn is flung out and all beside, that they may not have it in their power after this to be shameless.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:130
verses.text: For this is why the vessel goes to pieces, and their souls are tightly braced.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:131
verses.text: Moreover, both the storm and the darkness contributed not a little to his obtaining the hearing he did.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:132
verses.text: Accordingly observe how the centurion does as he bids him, insomuch that he even let the boat go, and destroyed it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:133
verses.text: And if the sailors did not as yet comply with his bidding, yet afterwards they do so: for in fact this is a reckless sort of people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:134
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:135
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:136
verses.text: ) "Sirs, ye should have hearkened to me," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:137
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:138
verses.text: ) One is not likely to have a good reception, when he chides in the midst of calamity; but when he tells them what more there is (to come) of the calamity, and then predicts the good, then he is acceptable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:139
verses.text: Therefore he attacks them then first, when "all hope that they should be saved was taken away:" that none may say, Nothing has come of it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:140
verses.text: And their fear also bears witness.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:141
verses.text: Moreover, the place is a trying one, for it was in the Adriatic, and then their long abstinence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:142
verses.text: They were in the midst of death.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:143
verses.text: It was now the fourteenth day that they were going without food, having taken nothing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:144
verses.text: "Wherefore," said he, "I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:145
verses.text: ), that ye should eat, lest ye perish of hunger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:146
verses.text: Observe, his giving thanks after all that had happened strengthened them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:147
verses.text: For this showed an assured mind that they would be saved.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:148
verses.text: (b) "Then were they all of good cheer; and they also took some meat".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:149
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:150
verses.text: ) And not only so, but henceforth they so cast all their care upon Paul, that they even cast out the corn (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:151
verses.text: ), being so many.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:152
verses.text: (a) Two hundred and seventy-six souls (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:153
verses.text: ): whence had they victuals? (c) See how they do their part as men, and how Paul does not forbid them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:154
verses.text: "And when it was day," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:155
verses.text: , "they loosed the rudder-bands".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:156
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:157
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:158
verses.text: ) And the vessel goes to pieces in the daytime, that they may not be clean dissolved with the terror: that you may see the prophecy brought out as fact.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:159
verses.text: "And the soldiers' counsel," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:160
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:161
verses.text: ) Do you mark that in this respect also they were given to Paul? since for his sake the centurion suffered them not to be slain.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:162
verses.text: So confessedly wicked do those men seem to me to have been: insomuch that they would have chosen even to slay them: but some swam on shore, others were borne on boards, and they all were thus saved, and the prophecy received accomplishment; (a prophecy,) although not solemn from length of time, since he did not deliver it a number of years before, but keeping close to the nature of the things themselves: (still a prophecy it was,) for all was beyond the reach of hope.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:163
verses.text: And (so) it was through themselves being saved that they learnt who Paul was.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:164
verses.text: But some one may say: why did he not save the ship? That they might perceive how great a danger they had escaped: and that the whole matter depended, not on the help of man, but on God's hand saving them independently of a ship.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:165
verses.text: So that righteous men, though they may be in a tempest, or on the sea, or in the deep, suffer nothing dreadful, but even save others together with themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:166
verses.text: If (here was) a ship in danger and suffering wreck, and prisoners were saved for Paul's sake, consider what a thing it is to have a holy man in a house: for many are the tempests which assail us also, tempests far more grievous than these (natural ones), but He can also give us to be delivered, if only we obey holy men as those (in the ship) did, if we do what they enjoin.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:167
verses.text: For they are not simply saved, but themselves also contributed to other men's believing (πίστιν εἰσήνεγκαν).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:168
verses.text: Though the holy man be in bonds, he does greater works than those who are free.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:169
verses.text: And look how this was the case here.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:170
verses.text: The free centurion stood in need of his bound prisoner: the skilful pilot was in want of him who was no pilot—nay rather, of him who was the true pilot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:171
verses.text: For he steered as pilot not a vessel of this (earthly) kind, but the Church of the whole world, having learnt of Him Who is Lord also of the sea; (steered it,) not by the art of man, but by the wisdom of the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:172
verses.text: In this vessel are many shipwrecks, many waves, spirits of wickedness, "from within are fightings, from without are fears" ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:173
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:174
verses.text: ): so that he was the true pilot.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:175
verses.text: Look at our whole life: it is just such (as was this voyage).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:176
verses.text: For at one time we meet with kindliness, at another with a tempest; sometimes from our own want of counsel, sometimes from our idleness, we fall into numberless evils; from our not hearkening to Paul, when we are eager to go somewhither, where he bids us not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:177
verses.text: For Paul is sailing even now with us, only not bound as he was then: he admonishes us even now, and says to those who are (sailing) on this sea, "take heed unto yourselves: for after my departing grievous wolves shall enter in among you" (Acts xx.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:178
verses.text: ): and again, "In the last times perilous times shall come: and men shall be lovers of their own selves, lovers of money, boasters".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:179
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:180
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:181
verses.text: ) This is more grievous than all storms.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:182
verses.text: Let us therefore abide where he bids us—in faith, in the safe haven: let us hearken unto him rather than to the pilot that is within us, that is, our own reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:183
verses.text: Let us not straightway do just what this may suggest; not what the owner of the ship: no, but what Paul suggests: he has passed through many such tempests.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:184
verses.text: Let us not learn (to our cost) by experience, but before the experience let us "avoid both harm and loss".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:185
verses.text: Hear what he says: "They that will be rich fall into temptation".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:186
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:187
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:188
verses.text: ) Let us therefore obey him; else, see what they suffered, because they did not take his counsel.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:189
verses.text: And again he tells in another place what causes shipwrecks: "Who," he says, "have made shipwreck concerning the faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:190
verses.text: But do thou continue in the things which thou hast learned and wast assured of".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:191
verses.text: ( Tim.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:192
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:193
verses.text: ) Let us obey Paul: though we be in the midst of a tempest, we shall surely be freed from the dangers: though we remain without food fourteen days, though hope of safety may have left us, though we be in darkness and mist, by doing his bidding, we shall be freed from the dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:194
verses.text: Let us think that the whole world is a ship, and in this the evildoers and those who have numberless vices, some rulers, others guards, others just men, as Paul was, others prisoners, those bound by their sins: if then we do as Paul bids us, we perish not in our bonds, but are released from them: God will give us also to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:195
verses.text: Or think you not that sins and passions are grievous bonds? for it is not the hands only that are bound, but the whole man.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:196
verses.text: For tell me, when any one possessed of much money uses it not, nor spends it, but keeps it close, is he not bound more grievously than any prisoner by his miserliness, a bond that cannot be broken? What again, when a man gives himself up to (the belief in) Fate, is not he too bound with other fetters? What, when he gives himself up to observations (of times)? What, when to omens? are not these more grievous than all bonds? What again, when he gives himself up to an unreasonable lust and to love? Who shall break in pieces these bonds for you? There is need of God's help that they may be loosed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:197
verses.text: But when there are both bonds and tempest, think how great is the amount of dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:198
verses.text: For which of them is not enough to destroy? The hunger, the tempest, the wickedness of those on board, the unfitness of the season? But against all these, Paul's glory stood its ground.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:199
verses.text: So is it now: let us keep the saints near us, and there will be no tempest: or rather, though there be a tempest, there will be great calm and tranquillity, and freedom from dangers: since that widow had the saint for her friend, and the death of her child was loosed, and she received back her son alive again.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:200
verses.text: ( Kings xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:201
verses.text: ) Where the feet of saints step, there will be nothing painful; and if such should happen, it is for proving us and for the greater glory of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:202
verses.text: Accustom the floor of thy house to be trodden by such feet, and an evil spirit will not tread there.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:203
verses.text: For as where a sweet odor is, there a bad odor will not find place: so where the holy unguent is, there the evil spirit is choked, and it gladdens those who are near it, it delights, it refreshes the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:204
verses.text: Where thorns are, there are wild beasts: where hospitality is, there are no thorns: for almsgiving having entered in, more keenly than any sickle it destroys the thorns, more violently than any fire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:205
verses.text: Be not thou afraid: (the wicked one) fears the tracks of saints, as foxes do lions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:206
verses.text: For "the righteous," it says, "is as bold as alion".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:207
verses.text: (Prov.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:208
verses.text: xxviii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:209
verses.text: ) Let us bring these lions into our house, and all the wild beasts are put to flight, the lions not needing to roar, but simply to utter their voice.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:210
verses.text: For not so much does the roaring of a lion put the wild beasts to flight, as the prayer of a righteous man puts to flight evil spirits: let him but speak, they cower.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:211
verses.text: And where are such men now to be found, you will say? Everywhere, if we believe, if we seek, if we take pains.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:212
verses.text: Where hast thou sought, tell me? When didst thou take this work in hand? When didst thou make this thy business? But if thou seekest not, marvel not that thou dost not find.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:213
verses.text: For "he that seeketh findeth" (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:214
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:215
verses.text: ), not he that seeketh not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:216
verses.text: Listen to those who live in deserts: away with thy gold and silver: (such holy men) are to be found in every part of the world.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:217
verses.text: Though thou receive not such an one in thy house, yet go thou to him, live with the man, be at his dwelling-place, that thou mayest be able to obtain and enjoy his blessing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 141:218
verses.text: For a great thing it is to receive a blessing from the saints: which let us be careful to obtain, that being helped by their prayers we may enjoy mercy from God, through the grace and loving-kindness of His only-begotten Son, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:1
verses.text: Homily LIV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:2
verses.text: Acts XXVIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:3
verses.text: "And the barbarous people showed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:4
verses.text: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:5
verses.text: "Showed," he says, "no little kindness to us—barbarians" (as they were)—"having kindled a fire:" else it were of no use that their lives be saved, if the wintry weather must destroy them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:6
verses.text: Then Paul having taken brushwood, laid it on the fire.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:7
verses.text: See how active he is; observe how we nowhere find him doing miracles for the sake of doing them, but only upon emergency.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:8
verses.text: Both during the storm when there was a cause he prophesied, not for the sake of prophesying, and here again in the first instance he lays on brushwood:—nothing for vain display, but (with a simple view) to their being preserved, and enjoying some warmth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:9
verses.text: Then a viper "fastened on his hand.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:10
verses.text: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:11
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:12
verses.text: ) Well also was this permitted, that they should both see the thing and utter the thought, in order that, when the result ensued, there might be no disbelieving the miracle.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:13
verses.text: Observe their good feeling (towards the distressed), in saying this (not aloud, but) among themselves—observe (also) the natural judgment clearly expressed even among barbarians, and how they do not condemn without assigning a reason.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:14
verses.text: And these also behold, that they may wonder the more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:15
verses.text: "And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:16
verses.text: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:17
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:19
verses.text: ) They expected him, it says, to fall down dead: and again, having seen that nothing of the kind happened to him, they said, He is a god.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:20
verses.text: Again (viz.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:21
verses.text: as in ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:22
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:23
verses.text: ), another excess on the part of these men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:24
verses.text: "In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:25
verses.text: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:28
verses.text: ) Behold again another hospitable man, Publius, who was both rich and of great possessions: he had seen nothing, but purely out of compassion for their misfortune, he received them, and took care of them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:29
verses.text: So that he was worthy to receive kindness: wherefore Paul as a requital for his receiving them, "healed him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:30
verses.text: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed: who also honored us with many honors; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:31
verses.text: , ), both us and the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:32
verses.text: See how when they were quit of the storm, they did not become more negligent, but what a liberal entertainment was given to them for Paul's sake: and three months were they there, all of them provided with sustenance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:33
verses.text: See how all this is done for the sake of Paul, to the end that the prisoners should believe, and the soldiers, and the centurion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:34
verses.text: For if they were very stone, yet from the counsel they heard him giving, and from the prediction they had heard him making, and from the miracles they knew him to have wrought, and from the sustenance they by his means enjoyed, they must have got a very high notion of him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:35
verses.text: See, when the judgment is right, and not preoccupied by some passion, how immediately it gets right judgings, and gives sound verdicts.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:36
verses.text: "And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:37
verses.text: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:38
verses.text: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli: where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:39
verses.text: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and the Three Taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:40
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:41
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:42
verses.text: ) Already the preaching has reached to Sicily: see how it has run through (even to those lands): at Puteoli also they found some: others also came to meet them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:43
verses.text: Such was the eagerness of the brethren, it nothing disconcerted them, that Paul was in bonds.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:44
verses.text: But observe also how Paul himself also was affected after the manner of men.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:45
verses.text: For it says, "he took courage, when he saw the brethren".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:46
verses.text: Although he had worked so many miracles, nevertheless even from sight he received an accession (of confidence).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:47
verses.text: From this we learn, that he was both comforted after the manner of men, and the contrary.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:48
verses.text: "And when we came to Rome, Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:49
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:50
verses.text: ) Leave was given him to dwell by himself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:51
verses.text: No slight proof this also of his being held in much admiration: it is clear they did not number him among the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:52
verses.text: "And it came to pass, that after three days he called together them that were the chief of the Jews".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:53
verses.text: After three days he called the chief of the Jews, that their ears might not be preoccupied.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:54
verses.text: And what had he in common with them? for they would not (else) have been like to accuse him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:55
verses.text: Nevertheless, it was not for this that he cared; it was for the teaching that he was concerned, and that what he had to say might not offend them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:56
verses.text: (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:57
verses.text: ) "And the barbarians," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:58
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:59
verses.text: ) The Jews then, beholding all the many miracles they did, persecuted and harassed (Paul); but the barbarians, who had seen none, merely on the ground of his misfortune, were kind to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:60
verses.text: —"No doubt," say they, "this man is a murderer:" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:61
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:62
verses.text: They do not simply pronounce their judgment, but say, "No doubt," (i-e:) as any one may see "and vengeance," say they, "suffereth him not to live".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:63
verses.text: Why then, they held also the doctrine of a Providence, and these barbarians were far more philosophic than the philosophers, who allow not the benefit of a Providence to extend to things "below the moon:" whereas (these barbarians) suppose God to be present everywhere, and that although a (guilty) man may escape many (a danger), he will not escape in the end.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:64
verses.text: And they do not assail him forthwith, but for a time respect him on account of his misfortune: nor do they openly proclaim their surmise, but speak it "among themselves: a murderer;" for the bonds led them to suspect this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:65
verses.text: "They showed no small kindness," and yet (some of them) were prisoners.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:66
verses.text: Let those be ashamed that say, Do not do good to those in prison: let these barbarians shame us; for they knew not who these men were, but simply because they were in misfortune (they were kind): thus much they perceived, that they were human beings, and therefore they considered them to have a claim upon their humanity.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:67
verses.text: "And for a great while," it says, "they expected that he would die".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:68
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:69
verses.text: ) But when he shook his hand, and flung off the beast, then they saw and were astonished.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:70
verses.text: And the miracle did not take place suddenly, but the men went by the length of time, "after they had looked a great while," so plainly was there no deceit, no haste here (συναρπαγή).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:71
verses.text: "Publius," it says, "lodged them courteously" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:72
verses.text: ): two hundred and seventy-six persons.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:73
verses.text: Consider how great the gain of his hospitality: not as of necessity, not as unwilling, but as reckoning it a gain he lodged them for three days: thereafter having met with his requital, he naturally honored Paul much more, when the others also received healing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:74
verses.text: "Who also," it says, "honored us with many honors" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:75
verses.text: ): not that he received wages, God forbid; but as it is written, "The workman is worthy of his meat.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:76
verses.text: And when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:77
verses.text: (Matt.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:78
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:79
verses.text: ) It is plain that having thus received them, they also received the word of the preaching: for it is not to be supposed, that during an entire three months they would have had all this kindness shown them, had these persons not believed strongly, and herein exhibited the fruits (of their conversion): so that from this we may see a strong proof of the great number there was of those that believed.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:80
verses.text: Even this was enough to establish (Paul's) credit with those (his fellow-voyagers).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:81
verses.text: Observe how in all this voyage they nowhere touched at a city, but (were cast) on an island, and passed the entire winter (there, or) sailing—those being herein under training for faith, his fellow-voyagers, I mean.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:82
verses.text: (a) "And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:83
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:84
verses.text: ) Probably this was painted on it: so addicted were they to their idols.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:85
verses.text: (d) "And when the south wind blew, we came the next day to Puteoli: where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:86
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:87
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:88
verses.text: ) (b) Observe them tarrying a while, and again hasting onwards.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:89
verses.text: (e) "And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and the Three Taverns" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:90
verses.text: ): not fearing the danger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:91
