verses.text: (c) Paul therefore was now so much respected, that he was even permitted to be by himself: for if even before this they used him kindly, much more would they now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:92
verses.text: (g) "He was suffered," it says, "to dwell by himself, with a soldier that kept him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:93
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:94
verses.text: ) That it might not be possible for any plot to be laid against him there either—for there could be no raising of sedition now.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:95
verses.text: So that in fact they were not keeping Paul in custody, but guarding him, so that nothing unpleasant should happen: for it was not possible now, in so great a city, and with the Emperor there, and with Paul's appeal, for anything to be done contrary to order.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:96
verses.text: So surely is it the case, that always through the things which seem to be against us, all things turn out for us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:97
verses.text: "With the soldier"—for he was Paul's guard.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:98
verses.text: "And having called together the chief of the Jews" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:99
verses.text: ), he discourses to them, who both depart gainsaying, and are taunted by him, yet they dare not say anything: for it was not permitted them to deal with his matter at their own will.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:100
verses.text: For this is a marvellous thing, that not by the things which seem to be for our security, but by their very opposites, all comes to be for us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:101
verses.text: And that you may learn this—Pharaoh commanded the infants to be cast into the river.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:102
verses.text: (Exod.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:103
verses.text: i.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:104
verses.text: ) Unless the infants had been cast forth, Moses would not have been saved, he would not have been brought up in the palace.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:105
verses.text: When he was safe, he was not in honor; when he was exposed, then he was in honor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:106
verses.text: But God did this, to show His riches of resource and contrivance.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:107
verses.text: The Jew threatened him, saying, "Wouldest thou kill me?" (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:108
verses.text: ) and this too was of profit to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:109
verses.text: It was of God's providence, in order that he should see that vision in the desert, in order that the proper time should be completed, that he should learn philosophy in the desert, and there live in security.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:110
verses.text: And in all the plottings of the Jews against him the same thing happens: then he becomes more illustrious.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:111
verses.text: As also in the case of Aaron; they rose up against him, and thereby made him more illustrious (Num.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:112
verses.text: xvi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:113
verses.text: , xvii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:114
verses.text: ): that so his ordination should be unquestionable, that he might be held in admiration for the future also from the plates of brass (τὥν πετάλων τοὕ χαλκοὕ).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:115
verses.text: Of course you know the history: wherefore I pass over the narration.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:116
verses.text: And if ye will, let us go over the same examples from the beginning.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:117
verses.text: Cain slew his brother, but in this he rather benefited him: for hear what Scripture says, "The voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto Me" (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:118
verses.text: iv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:119
verses.text: ): and again in another place, "To the blood that speaketh better things than that of Abel".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:120
verses.text: (Heb.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:121
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:122
verses.text: ) He freed him from the uncertainty of the future, he increased his reward: we have all learnt hereby what love God had for him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:123
verses.text: For what was he injured? Not a whit, in that he received his end sooner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:124
verses.text: For say, what do they gain, who die more slowly? Nothing: for the having good days does not depend on the living many years or few years, but in the using life properly.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:125
verses.text: The Three Children were thrown into the furnace, and through this they became more illustrious: Daniel was cast into the pit, and thence was he made more renowned.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:126
verses.text: (Dan.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:127
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:128
verses.text: and vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:129
verses.text: ) You see that trials in every case bring forth great good even in this life, much more in the life to come: but as to malice, the case is the same, as if a man having a reed should set himself to fight with the fire: it seems indeed to beat the fire, but it makes it brighter, and only consumes itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:130
verses.text: For the malice of the wicked becomes food and an occasion of splendor to virtue: for by God's turning the unrighteousness to good account, our character shines forth all the more.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:131
verses.text: Again, when the devil works anything of this kind, he makes those more illustrious that endure.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:132
verses.text: How then, you will say, was this not the case with Adam, but, on the contrary, he became more disgraced? Nay, in this case of all others God turned (the malice of) that (wicked one) to good account: but if (Adam) was the worse for it, it was he that injured himself: for it is the wrongs that are done to us by others that become the means of great good to us, not so the wrongs which are done by ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:133
verses.text: As indeed, because the fact is that when hurt by others, we grieve, but not so when hurt by ourselves, therefore it is that God shows, that he who suffers unjustly at the hands of another, gets renown, but he who injures himself, receives hurt: that so we may bear the former courageously, but not the latter.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:134
verses.text: And besides, the whole thing there was Adam's own doing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:135
verses.text: Wherefore didst thou the woman's bidding? (Gen.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:136
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:137
verses.text: ) Wherefore when she counselled thee contrary (to God), didst thou not repel her? Thou wast assuredly thyself the cause.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:138
verses.text: Else, if the devil was the cause, at this rate all that are tempted ought to perish: but if all do not perish, the cause (of our destruction) rests with ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:139
verses.text: "But," you will say, "all that are tempted ought (at that rate) to succeed".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:140
verses.text: No: for the cause is in ourselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:141
verses.text: "At that rate it ought to follow that (some) perish without the devil's having anything to do with it".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:142
verses.text: Yes: and in fact many do perish without the devil's being concerned in it: for surely the devil does not bring about all (our evil doings); no, much comes also from our own sluggishness by itself alone: and if he too is anywhere concerned as a cause, it is from our offering the occasion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:143
verses.text: For say, why did the devil prevail in Judas' case? When "Satan entered into him" (John xiii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:144
verses.text: ), you will say.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:145
verses.text: Yes, but hear the cause: it was because "he was a thief, and bare what was put in the bag".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:146
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:147
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:148
verses.text: ) It was he that himself gave the devil a wide room for entering into him: so that it is not the devil who puts into us the beginning, it is we that receive and invite him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:149
verses.text: "But," you will say, "if there were no devil, the evils would not have become great".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:150
verses.text: True, but then our punishment would admit of no plea for mitigation: but as it is, beloved, our punishment is more mild, whereas if we had wrought the evils of ourselves, the chastisements would be intolerable.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:151
verses.text: For say, if Adam, without any counsel, had committed the sin he did, who would have snatched him out of the dangers? "But he would not have sinned," you will say? What right hast thou to say this? For he who had so little solidity, that was so inert and so ready for folly as to receive such advice as this, much more would he without any counsel have become this (that he did become).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:152
verses.text: What devil incited the brethren of Joseph to envy? If then we be watchful brethren, the devil becomes to us the cause even of renown.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:153
verses.text: Thus, what was Job the worse for his falling into such helplessness of distress? "Speak not of this instance," you will say: "(Job was not the worse,) but the weak person is the worse".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:154
verses.text: Yes, and the weak person is the worse, even if there be no devil.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:155
verses.text: "But in a greater degree," you will say, "when there is the devil's power working along with him".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:156
verses.text: True, but he is the less punished, when he has sinned through the devil's working with him; for the punishments are not the same for all sins.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:157
verses.text: Let us not deceive ourselves: the devil is not the cause of our taking harm, if we be watchful: rather what he does, is to awake us out of our sleep; what he does, is to keep us on the alert.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:158
verses.text: Let us for a while examine these things: suppose there were no wild beasts, no irregular states of the atmosphere; no sicknesses, no pains, no sorrows, nor anything else of the kind: what would not man have become? A hog rather than a man, revelling in gluttony and drunkenness, and troubled by none of those things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:159
verses.text: But as it is, cares and anxieties are an exercise and discipline of philosophy, a method for the best of training.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:160
verses.text: For say, let a man be brought up in a palace, having no pain, nor care, nor anxiety, and having neither cause for anger nor failure, but whatever he sets his mind upon, that let him do, in that let him succeed, and have all men obeying him: (see whether) such a man would not become more irrational than any wild beast.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:161
verses.text: But as it is, our reverses and our afflictions are as it were a whetstone to sharpen us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:162
verses.text: For this reason the poor are for the most part wiser than the rich, as being driven about and tost by many waves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:163
verses.text: Thus a body also, being idle and without motion, is sickly and unsightly: but that which is exercised, and suffers labor and hardships, is more comely and healthy: and this we should find to hold also in the case of the soul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:164
verses.text: Iron also, lying unused, is spoilt, but if worked it shines brightly; and in like manner a soul which is kept in motion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:165
verses.text: Now these reverses are precisely what keeps the soul in motion.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:166
verses.text: Arts again perish, when the soul is not active: but it is active when it has not everything plain before it: it is made active by adverse things.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:167
verses.text: If there were no adverse things, there would be nothing to stir it: thus, if everything existed ready-made in beautiful sort, art would not have found wherein to exercise itself.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:168
verses.text: So, if all things were level to our understanding, the soul would not find wherein to exert itself: if it had to be carried about everywhere, it would be an unsightly object.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:169
verses.text: See you not, that we exhort nurses not to make a practice of carrying children always, that they may not bring them into a habit (of wanting to be carried) and so make them helpless? This is why those children which are brought up under the eyes of their parents are weak, in consequence of the indulgence, which by sparing them too much injures their health.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:170
verses.text: It is a good thing, even pain in moderation; a good thing, care; a good thing, want; for they make us strong: good also are their opposites: but each of these when in excess destroys us; and the one relaxes, but the other (by overmuch tension) breaks us.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:171
verses.text: Seest thou not, that Christ also thus trains His own disciples? If they needed these things, much more do we.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:172
verses.text: But if we need them, let us not grieve, but even rejoice in our afflictions.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:173
verses.text: For these are remedies, answering to our wounds, some of them bitter, others mild; but either of them by itself would be useless.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:174
verses.text: Let us therefore return thanks to God for all these things: for He does not suffer them to happen at random, but for the benefit of our souls.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 142:175
verses.text: Therefore, showing forth our gratitude, let us return Him thanks, let us glorify Him, let us bear up courageously, considering that it is but for a time, and stretching forward our minds to the things future, that we may both lightly bear the things present, and be counted worthy to attain unto the good things to come, through the grace and mercy of His only begotten Son, with Whom to the Father and the Holy Ghost together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:1
verses.text: Homily LV.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:2
verses.text: Acts XXVIII.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:3
verses.text: –  "And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:4
verses.text: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:5
verses.text: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had aught to accuse my nation of.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:6
verses.text: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:7
verses.text: He wished to exculpate both himself and others; himself, that they might not accuse him, and by so doing hurt themselves; and those (others), that it might not seem that the whole thing was of their doing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:8
verses.text: For it was likely that a report was prevalent, that he had been delivered up by the Jews; and this was enough to alarm them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:9
verses.text: He therefore addresses himself to this, and defends himself as to his own conduct.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:10
verses.text: "How then is it reasonable," it might be said, "that they should deliver thee up without a cause?" The Roman governors, he says, bear me witness, who wished to let me go.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:11
verses.text: "How was it then that they did not let (thee) go?" "When the Jews spake against it," he says.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:12
verses.text: Observe how he extenuates (in speaking of) their charges against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:13
verses.text: Since if he had wished to aggravate matters, he might have used them so as to bear harder upon them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:14
verses.text: Wherefore, he says, "I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar:" so that his whole speech is of a forgiving nature.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:15
verses.text: What then? didst thou this, that thou mightest accuse them? No, he says: "Not that I had aught to accuse my nation of:" but that I might escape the danger.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:16
verses.text: For it is for your sakes "that I am bound with this chain".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:17
verses.text: So far am I, he says, from any hostile feeling towards you.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:18
verses.text: Then they also were so subdued by his speech, that they too apologized for those of their own nation: "And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came showed or spake any harm of thee".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:19
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:20
verses.text: ) Neither through letters, nor through men, have they made known any harm of thee.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:21
verses.text: Nevertheless, we wish to hear from thyself: "But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:22
verses.text: ): and then forestalled him by showing their own sentiments.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:23
verses.text: "For as concerning this sect, it is known to us, that everywhere it is spoken against.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:24
verses.text: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the Law of Moses and out of the Prophets, from morning till evening.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:25
verses.text: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:26
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:27
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:28
verses.text: ) They said not, we speak against it, but "it is spoken against".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:29
verses.text: Then he did not immediately answer, but gave them a day, and they came to him, and he discoursed, it says, "both out of the Law of Moses, and out of the Prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:30
verses.text: And some believed, and some believed not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:31
verses.text: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers, saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive: for the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:32
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:33
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:34
verses.text: ) But when they departed, as they were opposed to each other, then he reproaches them, not because he wished to reproach those (that believed not), but to confirm these (that believed).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:35
verses.text: "Well said Esaias," says he to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:36
verses.text: So that to the Gentiles it is given to know this mystery.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:37
verses.text: No wonder then, if they did gainsay: this was foretold from the first.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:38
verses.text: Then again he moves their jealousy (on the score) of them of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:39
verses.text: "Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:40
verses.text: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:41
verses.text: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him, preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him, Amen".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:42
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:43
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:44
verses.text: ) It shows the freedom he had now: without hindrance in Rome, he who had been hindered in Judea; and he remained teaching there for two years.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:45
verses.text: What of the (years) after these?  (Recapitulation.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:46
verses.text: ) (d) "Who having examined me," says he, "found nothing in me" (v.

Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 143:48
verses.text: When those ought to have rescued, they "delivered (him) into the hands of the Romans".

verses.text: And such the superabundance,.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:1
verses.text: because those had not power to condemn but delivered him prisoner.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:2
verses.text: "Not as having aught to accuse my nation of," (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:3
verses.text: ) am I come.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:4
verses.text: See what friendliness of expression "my nation:" he does not hold them as aliens.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:5
verses.text: He does not say, I do not accuse, but, "I have not (whereof) to accuse:" although he had suffered so many evils at their hands.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:6
verses.text: But nothing of all this does he say, nor make his speech offensive: neither does he seem to be sparing them as matter of favor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:7
verses.text: For this was the main point, to show that they delivered him prisoner to the Romans, when those ought to have condemned him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:8
verses.text: (a) "For this cause," he says, "I wished to see you" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:9
verses.text: ): that it might not be in any man's power to accuse me, and to say what (naturally) might suggest itself (τὰ παριστάμενα), that having escaped their hands I have come for this: not to bring evils upon others, but myself fleeing from evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:10
verses.text: "I was compelled to appeal unto Caesar".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:11
verses.text: Observe them also speaking more mildly to him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:12
verses.text: "We beg," say they: and wish to speak in exculpation of those (at Jerusalem).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:13
verses.text: (e) Whereas they ought to accuse them, they plead for them: by the very fact of their exonerating them, they do in fact accuse them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:14
verses.text: (b) For this very thing was a proof that they knew themselves exceedingly in the wrong.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:15
verses.text: Had they been confident, they would at any rate have done this, so that he should not have it in his power to make out his story in his own way, and besides they shrank from coming.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 144:16
verses.text: And by their many times attempting they showed.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:1
verses.text: (f) "As for this sect, it is known to us," say    they, "that it is everywhere spoken against".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:2
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:3
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:4
verses.text: ) True, but (people) are also everywhere persuaded (as, in fact, here), "some were persuaded, and some believed not.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:5
verses.text: And when they had appointed him a day," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:6
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:7
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:8
verses.text: ) See again how not by miracles but by Law and Prophets he puts them to silence, and how we always find him doing this.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:9
verses.text: And yet he might also have wrought signs; but then it would no longer have been matter of faith.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:10
verses.text: In fact, this (itself) was a great sign, his discoursing from the Law and the Prophets.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:11
verses.text: Then that you may not deem it strange (that they believed not), he introduces the prophecy which saith, "Hearing ye shall hear and not understand," more now than then: "and ye shall see and not perceive" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:12
verses.text: ) more now than then.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:13
verses.text: This is not spoken for the former sort, but for the unbelievers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:14
verses.text: How then? Was it contrary to the prophecy, that those believed? ("Go,") it says, "unto this people" (that is), to the unbelieving people.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:15
verses.text: He did not say this to insult them, but to remove the offence.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:16
verses.text: "Be it known then," he says, "unto you, that unto the Gentiles is sent the salvation of God.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:17
verses.text: They," says he, "will hear it too".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:19
verses.text: ) Then why dost thou discourse to us? Didst thou not know this? Yes, but that ye might be persuaded, and that I might exculpate myself, and give none a handle (against me).

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:20
verses.text: (c) The unbelieving were they that withdrew.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:21
verses.text: But see how they do not now form plots against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:22
verses.text: For in Judea they had a sort of tyranny.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:23
verses.text: Then wherefore did the Providence of God order that he should go thither, and yet the Lord had said, "Get thee out quickly from Jerusalem?" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:24
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:25
verses.text: ) That both their wickedness might be shown and Christ's prophecy made good, that they would not endure to hear him: and so that all might learn that he was ready to suffer all things, and that the event might be for the consolation of those in Judea: for there also (the brethren) were suffering many grievous evils.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:26
verses.text: But if while preaching the Jewish doctrines, he suffered thus, had he preached the doctrines of the glory of Christ, how would they have endured him? While "purifying himself" (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:27
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:28
verses.text: ) he was intolerable, and how should he have been tolerable while preaching? What lay ye to his charge? What have ye heard? He spoke nothing of the kind.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:29
verses.text: He was simply seen, and he exasperated all against him.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:30
verses.text: Well might he then be set apart for the Gentiles: well might he be sent afar off: there also destined to discourse to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:31
verses.text: First he calls the Jews, then having shown them the facts he comes to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:32
verses.text: (ch.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:33
verses.text: xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:34
verses.text: ) "Well spake the Holy Ghost," etc.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:35
verses.text: But this saying, "The Spirit said," is nothing wonderful: for an angel also is said to say what the Lord saith: but He (the Spirit) not so.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:36
verses.text: When one is speaking of the things said by the angel, one does not say, Well said the angel, but, Well said the Lord.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:37
verses.text: "Well said the Spirit:" as much as to say, It is not me that ye disbelieve.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:38
verses.text: But God foreknew this from the first.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:39
verses.text: "He discoursed," it says, "with boldness, unhindered" (v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:40
verses.text: ): for it is possible to speak with boldness, yet hindered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:41
verses.text: His boldness nothing checked: but in fact he also spoke unhindered.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:42
verses.text: (c) "Discoursed," it says, "the things concerning the kingdom of God:" mark, nothing of the things of sense, nothing of the things present.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:43
verses.text: (f) But of his affairs after the two years, what say we? (b) (The writer) leaves the hearer athirst for more: the heathen authors do the same (in their writings), for to know everything makes the reader dull and jaded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:44
verses.text: Or else he does this, (e) not having it in his power to exhibit it from his own personal knowledge.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:45
verses.text: (a) Mark the order of God's Providence, "I have been much hindered from coming unto you…having a great desire these many years to come unto you".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:46
verses.text: (Rom.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:47
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:48
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:49
verses.text: ) (d) But he fed them with hopes.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:50
verses.text: (g) I am in haste to go to Spain, and "I hope," says he, "to see you in my journey, and to be brought thitherward on my journey by you, if first I be filled with your company in some measure".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:51
verses.text: (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:52
verses.text: ) (i) Of this he says, I will come and rest together with you "in the fulness of the blessing of the Gospel" (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:53
verses.text: ): and again "I am going to Jerusalem to minister to the saints" (ib.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:54
verses.text: ): this is the same that he has said here, "To do alms to my nation I came".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:55
verses.text: (Acts xxiv.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:56
verses.text: ) (h) Do you mark how he did not foresee everything—that sacred and divine head, the man higher than the heavens, that had a soul able to grasp all at once, the holder of the first place—Paul? The man whose very name, to them that know him, suffices for rousing of the soul, for vigilance, for shaking off all sleep! Rome received him bound, coming up from the sea, saved from a ship-wreck—and was saved from the shipwreck of error.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:57
verses.text: Like an emperor that has fought a naval battle and overcome, he entered into that most imperial city.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:58
verses.text: (k) He was nearer now to his crown.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:59
verses.text: Rome received him bound, and saw him crowned and proclaimed conqueror.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:60
verses.text: There he had said, I will rest together with you: but this was the beginning of a course once more, and he added trophies to trophies, a man not to be overcome.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:61
verses.text: Corinth kept him two years, and Asia three, and this city two for this time; a second time he again entered it, when also he was consummated.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:62
verses.text: Thus he escaped then, and having filled the whole world, he so brought his life to a close.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:63
verses.text: Why didst thou wish to learn what happened after these two years? Those too are such as these: bonds, tortures, fightings, imprisonments, lyings in wait, false accusations, deaths, day by day.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:64
verses.text: Thou hast seen but a small part of it? How much soever thou hast seen, such is he for all the rest.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:65
verses.text: As in the case of the sky, if thou see one part of it, go where thou wilt thou shalt see it such as this: as it is with the sun, though thou see its rays but in part, thou mayest conjecture the rest: so is it with Paul.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:66
verses.text: His Acts thou hast seen in part; such are they all throughout, teeming with dangers.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:67
verses.text: He was a heaven having in it the Sun of Righteousness, not such a sun (as we see): so that that man was better than the very heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:68
verses.text: Think you that this is a small thing—when you say "The Apostle," immediately every one thinks of him (as), when you say "The Baptist," immediately they think of John? To what shall one compare his words? To the sea, or even to the ocean? But nothing is equal to them.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:69
verses.text: More copious than this (sea) are (his) streams; purer and deeper; so that one would not err in calling Paul's heart both a sea and a heaven, the one for purity, the other for depth.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:70
verses.text: He is a sea, having for its voyagers not those who sail from city to city, but those from earth to heaven: if any man sail in this sea, he will have a prosperous voyage.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:71
verses.text: On this sea, not winds, but instead of winds the Holy and Divine Spirit wafts the souls which sail thereon: no waves are here, no rock, no monsters: all is calm.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 145:72
verses.text: It is a sea which is more calm and secure than a haven, having no bitter brine, but a pure fountain both sweeter than.

chapters.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:1
verses.text: , and brighter and more transparent than the sun: a sea it is, not having precious stones, nor purple dye as ours, but treasures far better than those.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:2
verses.text: He who wishes to descend into this sea, needs not divers, needs not oil, but much loving-kindness (φιλανθρωπίας): he will find in it all the good things that are in the kingdom of Heaven.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:3
verses.text: He will even be able to become a king, and to take the whole world into his possession, and to be in the greatest honor; he who sails on this sea will never undergo shipwreck, but will know all things well.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:4
verses.text: But as those who are inexpert in this (our visible sea) are suffocated (in attempting to dive therein), so is it in that other sea: which is just the case with the heretics, when they attempt things above their strength.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:5
verses.text: It behooves therefore to know the depth, or else not to venture.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:6
verses.text: If we are to sail on this sea, let us come well-girded.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:7
verses.text: "I could not," he says, "speak unto you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:8
verses.text: ( Cor.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:9
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:10
verses.text: ) Let no one who is without endurance sail on this sea.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:11
verses.text: Let us provide for ourselves ships, that is, zeal, earnestness, prayers, that we may pass over the sea in quiet.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:12
verses.text: For indeed this is the living water.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:13
verses.text: Like as if one should get a mouth of fire, such a mouth does that man get who knows Paul well: like as if one should have a sharp sword, so again does such an one become invincible.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:14
verses.text: And for the understanding of Paul's words there is needed also a pure life.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:15
verses.text: For therefore also he said: "Ye are become such as have need of milk, seeing ye are dull of hearing".

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:16
verses.text: (Heb.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:17
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:18
Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:19
verses.text: ) For there is, there is an infirmity of hearing.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:20
verses.text: For as a stomach which is infirm could not take in wholesome food (which it finds) hard of digestion, so a soul which is become tumid and heated, unstrung and relaxed, could not receive the word of the Spirit.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:21
verses.text: Hear the disciples saying, "This is a hard saying: who can hear it" (John vi.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:22
verses.text: )? But if the soul be strong and healthy, all is most easy, all is light: it becomes more lofty and buoyant: it is more able to soar and lift itself on high.

verses.name: Chrysostom: Homilies on Acts of the Apostles 147:23
verses.text: Knowing then these things, let us bring our soul into a healthy state: let us emulate Paul,and imitate that noble, that adamantine soul: that, advancing in the steps of his life, we may be enabled to sail through the sea of this present life, and to come unto the haven wherein are no waves, and attain unto the good things promised to them that love Him, through the grace and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, with Whom to the Father and Holy Ghost together be glory, might, honor, now and ever, world without end, Amen.
